## XIV Concerning Face-of-god and the Mountain / 十四 面神与山

===Original===
But it must be told of Gold-mane that what had befallen him was in this wise. His skid-strap brake in good sooth, and he stayed to mend it; but when he had done what was needful, he looked up and saw no man nigh, what for the drift, and that they had gone on somewhat; so he rose to his feet, and without more delay, instead of keeping on toward the elk-ground and the way his face had been set, he turned himself north-and-by-east, and went his ways swiftly towards that airt, because he deemed that it might lead him to the Mountain-hall where he had guested. He abode not for the storm to clear, but swept off through the thick of it; and indeed the wind was somewhat at his back, so that he went the swiftlier. But when the drift was gotten to its very worst, he sheltered himself for a little in a hollow behind a thorn-bush he stumbled upon. As soon as it began to abate he went on again, and at last when it was quite clear, and the sun shone out, he found himself on a long slope of the fells covered deep with smooth white snow, and at the higher end a great crag rising bare fifty feet above the snow, and more rocks, but none so great, and broken ground as he judged (the snow being deep) about it on the hither side; and on the further, three great pine-trees all bent down and mingled together by their load of snow.

Thitherward he made, as a man might, seeing nothing else to note before him; but he had not made many strides when forth from behind the crag by the pine-trees came a man; and at first Face-of-god thought it might be one of his hunting-fellows gone astray, and he hailed him in a loud voice, but as he looked he saw the sun flash back from a bright helm on the newcomer’s head; albeit he kept on his way till there was but a space of two hundred yards between them; when lo! the helm-bearer notched a shaft to his bent bow and loosed at Face-of-god, and the arrow came whistling and passed six inches by his right ear. Then Face-of-god stopped perplexed with his case; for he was on the deep snow in his skids, with his bow unbent, and he knew not how to bend it speedily. He was loth to turn his back and flee, and indeed he scarce deemed that it would help him. Meanwhile of his tarrying the archer loosed again at him, and this time the shaft flew close to his left ear. Then Face-of-god thought to cast himself down into the snow, but he was ashamed; till there came a third shaft which flew over his head amidmost and close to it. “Good shooting on the Mountain!” muttered he; “the next shaft will be amidst my breast, and who knows whether the Alderman’s handiwork will keep it out.”

===Chinese===
至于金鬃（Gold-mane），其所遭之事，原是这般。他那雪板的绑带确乎断了，他便停下来修理；待修好该修之处，抬头一看，四下并无人影——一则风雪迷眼，二则众人已前行了一段路；于是他立起身来，不再耽搁，并不照原定方向继续往猎鹿之地去，反而转身向北偏东，急急朝那一处方位奔去，因为他想那条路或许能引他到他曾作过客的山厅（Mountain-hall）。他不等风雪放晴，便径自冲入风雪最浓处；好在风势略在背后，倒使他走得更快。及至飞雪最为狂暴之时，他在一处洼地里、一丛他撞见的荆棘背后，稍稍躲避片刻。雪势一减，他便重新上路；末了，待风雪全消、阳光普照，他发觉自己已在一道长长的山岭斜坡之上，满覆深厚而光滑的白雪；坡之高处，一方巨崖自雪中拔起，足有五十尺光秃秃高出雪面；近处还有些乱石，但都不甚大，他料想（因雪深之故）崖之这一侧乃是一片崎岖破碎之地；而那一侧，立着三株大松，俱被积雪压得弯折、纠缠作一处。

他朝那边走去，也是势所必然——眼前别无可注意之物；然而他没走几步，便见从松树旁那方巨崖背后走出一个人来；面神起初以为是同行猎手中走失的一员，便高声呼喝；但定睛一看，却见阳光从来人头上的一顶明亮头盔上闪回；虽然如此，他仍继续前行，直至两人之间只剩二百步之距；忽然！那戴盔之人将一支箭搭上弯弓，朝面神便射，箭矢呼啸而至，擦着他右耳六寸飞过。面神当下站住，进退两难：他脚踏雪板、立于深雪之上，弓未上弦，又不知如何能迅速上弦。他不愿转身逃走，而且也几乎觉得逃亦无益。就在他迟疑之际，那弓手又朝他射来一箭，这一回箭矢紧贴他左耳飞过。面神心想索性扑倒在雪中，却又觉羞惭；直到第三箭飞来，正从他头顶中央、贴着头皮掠过。"山上好箭法！"他低声咕哝，"下一箭可要射进我胸口了，谁知道长老的手艺挡不挡得住。"

===Original===
So he cried aloud: “Thou shootest well, brother; but art thou a foe? If thou art, I have a sword by my side, and so hast thou; come hither to me, and let us fight it out friendly if we must needs fight.”

A laugh came down the wind to him clear but somewhat shrill, and the archer came swiftly towards him on his skids with no weapon in his hand save his bow; so that Face-of-god did not draw his sword, but stood wondering.

As they drew nearer he beheld the face of the newcomer, and deemed that he had seen it before; and soon, for all that it was hooded close by the ill-weather raiment, he perceived it to be the face of Bow-may, ruddy and smiling.

She laughed out loud again, as she stopped herself within three feet of him, and said:

===Chinese===
于是他高声喊道："兄弟，你箭法不错；可你是敌人么？若是敌人，我腰间有剑，你也有；请到我跟前来，倘若非打不可，咱们就痛痛快快地较量一番。"

一阵笑声顺风传来，清亮而略带尖细；那弓手踏着雪板飞速朝他而来，手中除了弓之外再无别样兵器；面神因此并未拔剑，只站在那里纳罕。

两人渐近，他端详来人的脸，觉得似曾相识；不多时，纵然那张脸被御寒的兜帽严严裹住，他已辨出那是弓女（Bow-may）的面孔，红润而含笑。

她又放声大笑，在距他三尺之内收住脚步，说道：

===Original===
“Yea, friend Yellow-hair, we heard of the elks and looked to see thee hereabouts, and I knew thee at once when I came out from behind the crag and saw thee stand bewildered.”

Said Gold-mane: “Hail to thee, Bow-may! and glad am I to see thee. But thou liest in saying that thou knewest me; else why didst thou shoot those three shafts at me? Surely thou art not so quick as that with all thy friends: these be sharp greetings of you Mountain-folk.”

“Thou lad with the sweet mouth,” she said, “I like to see thee and hear thee talk, but now must I hasten thy departure; so stand we here no longer. Let us get down into the wood where we can do off our skids and sit down, and then will I tell thee the tidings. Come on!”

And she caught his hand in hers, and they went speedily down the slopes toward the great oak-wood, the wind whistling past their ears.

===Chinese===
"是啊，黄发（Yellow-hair）朋友，我们听说了那些鹿的事，料定你会在这一带；我从崖后走出来、看见你一脸茫然站在那里，便立刻认出了你。"

金鬃道："弓女，向你问好！见到你我很欢喜。可你说认得我，这话却是假的；不然你为何朝我连射三箭？你对所有的朋友未必都这般手快吧：你们山中之民（the Mountain-folk）的见面礼，可真够锋利的。"

"你这嘴甜的小子，"她说，"我喜欢见你、喜欢听你说话，可眼下我得催你动身了；咱们别在这里站着了。且下到林子里去，在那里脱下雪板、坐下，到时我再把消息告诉你。来吧！"

她便一把握住他的手，两人一同飞快地顺坡而下，朝那片大柞林奔去，风从他们耳畔呼啸而过。

===Original===
“Whither are we going?” said he.

Said she: “I am to show thee the way back home, which thou wilt not know surely amidst this snow. Come, no words! thou shalt not have my tale from me till we are in the wood: so the sooner we are there the sooner shalt thou be pleased.”

So Face-of-god held his peace, and they went on swiftly side by side. But it was not Bow-may’s wont to be silent for long, so presently she said:

“Thou art good so do as I bid thee; but see thou, sweet playmate, for all thou art a chieftain’s son, thou wert but featherbrained to ask me why I shot at thee. I shoot at thee! that were a fine tale to tell her this even! Or dost thou think that I could shoot at a big man on the snow at two hundred paces and miss him three times? Unless I aimed to miss.”

===Chinese===
"我们去哪里？"他问。

她答道："我要给你指一条回家的路，这漫天大雪之中你自己定然认不得。来，别多话！不到林子里，我决不把话告诉你：所以咱们越早到那里，你便越早称心。"

面神便不再言语，两人并肩疾行。然弓女素来不是久默之人，不多时她便开口道：

"你这般听话、由我差遣，很好；可是你瞧，好性儿的玩伴，你虽是首领之子，却来问我为何朝你射箭，未免太过轻率了。我朝你射箭！这事今儿晚上要是讲给她听，倒是一桩好故事！难不成你以为，我能在大雪之上、二百步外朝一条大汉连射三箭都射不中？除非我本就存心射偏。"

===Original===
“Yea, Bow-may,” said he, “art thou so deft a Bow-may? Thou shalt be in my company whenso I fare to battle.”

“Indeed,” she said, “therein thou sayest but the bare truth: nowhere else shall I be, and thou shalt find my bow no worse than a good shield.”

He laughed somewhat lightly; but she looked on him soberly and said: “Laugh in that fashion on the day of battle, and we shall be well content with thee!”

So on they sped very swiftly, for their way was mostly down hill, so that they were soon amongst the outskirting trees of the wood, and presently after reached the edge of the thicket, beyond which the ground was but thinly covered with snow.

===Chinese===
"好一个弓女，"他说，"你箭术竟如此了得？今后我但凡上阵杀敌，你须得与我同行。"

"可不是么，"她说，"你这话说得半点不差：我别处不去，定在你身旁；我的弓在你手下，决不亚于一面好盾。"

他略略轻笑；她却正色看着他，说道："到了上阵那日，你若还这般笑法，我们便很满意你了！"

于是他们飞快前行，因一路大半是下坡，不多时便到了林子外缘的树间，又过片刻便到了丛林边上，自那以远，地上的积雪便已很薄。

===Original===
There they took off their skids, and went into the thick wood and sat down under a hornbeam tree; and ere Gold-mane could open his mouth to speak Bow-may began and said:

“Well it was that I fell in with thee, Dalesman, else had there been murders of men to tell of; but ever she ordereth all things wisely, though unwisely hast thou done to seek to her. Hearken! dost thou think that thou hast done well that thou hast me here with my tale? Well, hadst thou busied thyself with the slaying of elks, or with sitting quietly at home, yet shouldest thou have heard my tale, and thou shouldest have seen me in Burgstead in a day or two to tell thee concerning the flitting of the token. And ill it is that I have missed it, for fain had I been to behold the House of the Face, and to have seen thee sitting there in thy dignity amidst the kindred of chieftains.”

And she sighed therewith. But he said: “Hold up thine heart, Bow-may! On the word of a true man that shall befall thee one day. But come, playmate, give me thy tale!”

“Yea,” she said, “I must now tell thee in the wildwood what else I had told thee in the Hall. Hearken closely, for this is the message:”

> “Seek not to me again till thou hast the token; else assuredly wilt thou be slain, and I shall be sorry for many a day. Thereof as now I may not tell thee more. Now as to the token: When March is worn two weeks fail not to go to and fro on the place of the Maiden Ward for an hour before sunrise every day till thou hear tidings.”

===Chinese===
他们便在那里脱下雪板，走入密林，在一株鹅耳枥树下坐定；金鬃还没来得及张口说话，弓女便抢先说道：

"幸亏我撞见了你，谷民，不然这会儿怕要闹出人命来；凡事她都安排得妥妥帖帖，唯独你这样去找她，却是行事莽撞。听着！你以为把我和我的消息一同讨到手里，便是做了件聪明事么？哼，你或去忙着猎鹿、或安安稳稳坐在家里，照样会听到我的消息，再过一两日你便会在堡镇见到我，由我告诉你信物（the token）易手之事。只可惜我错过了那一幕，因为我本极想亲眼看一看面神之宅，看一看你端坐于诸位首领亲族之间、一派尊严的模样。"

她说着便叹了口气。他却说："弓女，且提起精神来！凭一个真汉子的话，那一日定会到来的。来吧，伙伴，把你的话讲给我听！"

"好，"她说，"我如今只得在这荒林之中，把本该在厅堂里告诉你的话告诉你了。仔细听着，这便是那口信："

> "在你取得信物之前，切勿再来寻我；否则你定会被杀，而我也将为此伤心多日。此事眼下我不便多讲。至于信物：待三月已过两周，你务必每日在日出之前一个时辰，到少女岗（the Maiden Ward）那地方来回行走，直到听见消息为止。"

===Original===
“Now,” quoth Bow-may, “hast thou hearkened and understood?”

“Yea,” said he.

She said: “Then tell me the words of my message concerning the token.” And he did so word for word. Then she said:

“It is well, there is no more to say. Now must I lead thee till thou knowest the wood; and then mayst thou get on to the smooth snow again, and so home merrily. Yet, thou grey-eyed fellow, I will have my pay of thee before I do that last work.”

Therewith she turned about to him and took his head between her hands, and kissed him well favouredly both cheeks and mouth; and she laughed, albeit the tears stood in her eyes as she said: “Now smelleth the wood sweeter, and summer will come back again. And even thus will I do once more when we stand side by side in battle array.”

===Chinese===
"好了，"弓女说，"你可听明白了？"

"听明白了。"他说。

她说："那你把信物之事的那几句口信复述给我听。"他便一字不差地复述了一遍。她又说：

"很好，别无他话了。眼下我须领你走到你认得路之处；然后你便可再上光滑的雪面，欢欢喜喜回家了。不过，你这灰眼睛的家伙，在做这最后一桩事之前，我得先向你讨些酬劳。"

说着她便转过身来面对他，双手捧住他的头，大大方方地亲了他两颊和嘴；她笑了起来，尽管眼中含着泪，说道："如今这林子闻起来更香了，夏日也终会再回来。待到有一日我们并肩列于战阵之上，我还要这般再做一次。"

===Original===
He smiled kindly on her and nodded as they both rose up from the earth: she had taken off her foul-weather gloves while they spake, and he kissed her hand, which was shapely of fashion albeit somewhat brown, and hard of palm, and he said in friendly wise:

“Thou art a merry faring-fellow, Bow-may, and belike shalt be withal a true fighting-fellow. Come now, thou shalt be my sister and I thy brother, in despite of those three shafts across the snow.”

He laughed therewith; she laughed not, but seemed glad, and said soberly:

“Yea, I may well be thy sister; for belike I also am of the people of the Gods, who have come into these Dales by many far ways. I am of the House of the Ragged Sword of the Kindred of the Wolf. Come, brother, let us toward Wildlake’s Way.”

===Chinese===
他和颜悦色地朝她笑了笑，点点头，两人一齐从地上起身：方才说话间她已脱下御寒的手套，他便吻了她的手——那手模样姣好，虽则肤色微褐、掌心粗硬——他亲热地说：

"弓女，你是个快活的同行伴侣，多半还会是个忠实的战友。来，你便做我的妹妹，我做你的哥哥，那雪地上的三箭，就此一笔勾销。"

他说着便笑了起来；她却没有笑，但似乎很是欢喜，正色说道：

"是啊，我确可做你的妹妹；因为多半我也是诸神之族的血脉，他们由许多遥远之路来到这些谷中。我出身于狼族（the Kindred of the Wolf）的残剑之宅（the House of the Ragged Sword）。来吧，哥哥，咱们往野湖径去吧。"

===Original===
Therewith she went before him and led through the thicket as by an assured and wonted path, and he followed hard at heel; but his thought went from her for a while; for those words of brother and sister that he had spoken called to his mind the Bride, and their kindness of little children, and the days when they seemed to have nought to do but to make the sun brighter, and the flowers fairer, and the grass greener, and the birds happier each for the other; and a hard and evil thing it seemed to him that now he should be making all these things nought and dreary to her, now when he had become a man and deeds lay before him. Yet again was he solaced by what Bow-may had said concerning battle to come; for he deemed that she must have had this from the Friend’s foreseeing; and he longed sore for deeds to do, wherein all these things might be cleared up and washen clean as it were.

So passed they through the wood a long way, and it was getting dark therein, and Gold-mane said:

===Chinese===
说罢她便走在他前头，领他穿过丛林，仿佛走在一条熟稳常走之路，他紧随其后；但他的心思有一阵子从她身上飘开了；因为他方才所说的"哥哥""妹妹"那几句话，唤起了他对新娘的回忆——他们自幼小时的情谊，那些仿佛除了彼此便无事可做、只为使太阳更明、花朵更艳、青草更绿、鸟儿更欢的日子；而眼下他已成了男子汉、面前已有当作之事，却要把这一切都化作她的乌有与凄凉，他只觉这是一桩残酷而不美的事。然而弓女方才所讲将来之战事，又使他心生宽慰；因为他想这话必是出于那位友人（the Friend）的先见之明；他渴望着有事功可为，好让这一切纠葛，仿佛在水中洗净一般、一一涤清。

他们就这样穿过林子走了好一大段，林中渐渐暗了下来，金鬃说道：

===Original===
“Hold now, Bow-may, for I am at home here.”

She looked around and said: “Yea, so it is: I was thinking of many things. Farewell and live merrily till March comes and the token!”

Therewith she turned and went her ways and was soon out of sight, and he went lightly through the wood, and then on skids over the hard snow along the Dale’s edge till he was come to the watchtower, when the moon was bright in heaven.

Thus was he at Burgstead and the House of the Face betimes, and before the hunters were gotten back.

===Chinese===
"且停下吧，弓女，到这里我认得路了。"

她四下里看了看，说道："是啊，正是如此：方才我正想着许多事。再会吧，好好活着，等到三月来、信物到！"

说罢她转身自去，转眼便不见身影；他便轻快地穿过林子，又踏上雪板、沿着谷沿在坚硬的雪面上滑行，直到望楼下，其时月已高悬、清辉满天。

他就这样早早地回到了堡镇、回到面神之宅，比猎手们归来得更早。

## XLIX Dallach Fareth to Rosedale: Crow Telleth of His Errand: The Kindreds Eat Their Meat in Silverdale / 四十九 达拉赫奔赴玫瑰谷：克劳禀报使命：诸族于银谷用肉食

===Original===
Now Dallach, who had gone away for a while, came back again into the Hall; and at his back were a half score of men who bore ladders with them: they were stout men, clad in scanty and ragged raiment, but girt with swords and bearing axes, those of them who were not handling the ladders. Men looked on them curiously, because they saw them to be of the roughest of the thralls. They were sullen and fierce-eyed to behold, and their hands and bare arms were flecked with blood; and it was easy to see that they had been chasing the fleers, and making them pay for their many torments of past days.

But when Face-of-god beheld this he cried out: “Ho, Dallach! is it so that thou hast bethought thee to bring in hither men to fall to the cleansing of the Hall, and to do away the defiling of the Dusky Men?”

===Chinese===
先前离去了一阵的达拉赫（Dallach）此刻又回到厅堂里来；身后跟着十个汉子，扛着梯子：都是些壮硕之辈，衣衫褴褛短窄，腰间却佩着剑，凡未扛梯子的手里还提着斧头。众人好奇地打量他们，因为看得出这些都是奴隶中最粗豪的一类。他们面容阴沉、目光凶狠，手与裸臂之上还斑斑沾着血迹；一望便知他们方才一直在追杀逃敌，正要他们为昔日所受的种种酷刑偿命。

面神见此情景，高声呼道："喂，达拉赫！莫非你已想起带人进来清扫这座厅堂、清除黝暗人所留的污秽？"

===Original===
“Even so, War-leader,” said Dallach; “also ye shall know that all battle is over in Silverstead; for the thralls fell in numbers not to be endured on the Dusky Men who had turned their backs to us, and hindered them from fleeing north. But though they have slain many, they have not slain all, and the remnant have fled by divers ways westaway, that they may gain the wood and the ways to Rosedale; and the stoutest of the thralls are at their heels, and ever as they go fresh men from the fields join in the chase with great joy. I have gathered together of the best of them two hundreds and a half well-armed; and if thou wilt give me leave, I will get to me yet more, and follow hard on the fleers, and so get me home to Rosedale; for thither will these runaways to meet whatso of their kind may be left there. Also I would fain be there to set some order amongst the poor folk of mine own people, whom this day’s work hath delivered from torment. And if thou wilt suffer a few men of the Dalesmen to come along with me, then shall all things be better done there.”

===Chinese===
"正是如此，战首，"达拉赫说，"还有，你们当知道：银镇之内战事已全部了结；因为那些黝暗人背向我们、欲向北逃窜，奴隶们便成群结队扑将上去，其数之众、势不可挡，挡住了他们北逃之路。然而他们虽杀了大批，却未杀尽，余下的从各路向西逃去，意欲钻入林地、夺路奔往玫瑰谷；那些最强壮的奴隶正紧追其后，一路之上，田间的壮丁不断欢欢喜喜地加入追击。我已从其中精选了二百五十名装备齐整之人；你若允准，我还要再招揽些人，紧紧咬住那些逃敌，就此取道回家、直奔玫瑰谷；因为这些逃敌必往那里去，好与彼处可能尚存的同伙会合。再者，今日这一战已将我那些穷苦的族人从苦刑之中解救出来，我也很想赶回去为他们略作安排。你若肯让几位堡谷人随我同去，那边的事便能办得更为妥帖。"

===Original===
“Luck go with thine hands!” said Face-of-god. “Take whomso thou wilt of the Burgdalers that have a mind to fare with thee to the number of five score; and send word of thy thriving to Folk-might, the chieftain of the Dale; as for us, meseemeth that we shall abide here no long while. How sayest thou, Folk-might, shall Dallach go?”

Then Folk-might, who stood close beside him, looked up and reddened somewhat, as a man caught heedless when he should be heedful; but he looked kindly on Face-of-god, and said:

===Chinese===
"愿好运伴你双手！"面神说，"堡谷人中凡愿随你去的，你尽可挑选，至多一百人；并将你的进展差人告知谷中首领民强；至于我们，我看我们在此地也待不了多久。民强，你以为如何？达拉赫可以去么？"

站在他身旁的民强闻言抬起头来，脸上微微一红，像是该用心时却走了神、被人撞见一般；但他和颜悦色地望着面神，说道：

===Original===
“War-leader, so long as thou art in the Dale which ye kindreds have won back for us, thou art the chieftain, and no other, and I bid thee do as thou wilt in this matter, and in all things; and I hereby give command to all my kindred to do according to thy will everywhere and always, as they love me; and indeed I deem that thy will shall be theirs; since it is only fools who know not their well-wishers. How say ye, kinsmen?”

Then those about cried out: “Hail to Face-of-god! Hail to the Dalesmen! Hail to our friends!”

===Chinese===
"战首，只要你还在诸族为我们夺回的这山谷之中，首领便只有你、不是别人；此事以及一切事务，我都请你随心处置；我在此传令全体族人——他们若爱我，便当无论何时何地都照你的意思去做；其实我也料定，你的意思必会成为他们的意思；因为唯有蠢人方认不出自己的善意之友。亲族们，你们意下如何？"

周围的人便齐声高呼："向面神致敬！向堡谷人致敬！向我们的朋友致敬！"

===Original===
But Folk-might went up to Face-of-god, and threw his arms about him and kissed him, and he said therewithal, so that most men heard him:

“Herewith I kiss not only thee, thou goodly and glorious warrior! but this kiss and embrace is for all the men of the kindreds of the Dale and the Shepherds; since I deem that never have men more valiant dwelt upon the earth.”

===Chinese===
民强随即走到面神跟前，张开双臂抱住他、亲吻他，同时说道——声音之高，使在场大多数人都听得见：

"我此处所吻的，不止你这英武辉煌的勇士一人！这一吻、这一抱，乃是献给堡谷诸族与牧羊之民全体男儿的；因为我想，世上再未曾住过比他们更英勇的人。"

===Original===
Therewith all men shouted for joy of him, and were exceeding glad; but Folk-might spake apart to Face-of-god and said:

“Brother, I suppose that thou wilt deem it good to abide in this Hall or anigh it; for hereabouts now is the heart of the Host. But as for me, I would have leave to depart for a little; since I have an errand, whereof thou mayest wot.”

===Chinese===
众人为他欢呼雀跃，欢喜异常；民强却把面神拉到一旁，单独对他说：

"兄弟，我想你会觉得留在这座厅堂里、或在它近旁才妥当；因为眼下大军的中枢就在这一带。至于我，想告假离开片刻；因为我有一桩差事，你大约是明白的。"

===Original===
Then Face-of-god smiled on him, and said: “Go, and all good go with thee; and tell my father that I would have tidings, since I may not be there.” So he spake; yet in his heart was he glad that he might not go to behold the Bride lying sick and sorry. But Folk-might departed without more words; and in the door of the Hall he met Crow the Shaft-speeder, who would have spoken to him, and given him the tidings; but Folk-might said to him: “Do thine errand to the War-leader, who is within the Hall.” And so went on his way.

===Chinese===
面神便对他微笑，说道："去吧，愿一切善事与你同行；并告诉我父亲，说我想知道消息，因为我自己离不开。"他这样说；然而他心里却暗自庆幸，因为不必去探望那卧病忧伤的新娘。民强不多言语便离去了；在厅堂门口，他撞见疾箭者克劳（Crow the Shaft-speeder），克劳正要与他说话、向他禀报消息；民强却对他说："你的差事去禀报战首吧，他就在厅堂里头。"说罢径自去了。

===Original===
Then came Crow up the Hall, and stood before Face-of-god and said: “War-leader, we have done that which was to be done, and have cleared all the houses about the Marketstead. Moreover, by the rede of Dallach we have set certain men of the poor folk of the Dale, who are well looked to by the others, to the burying of the slain felons; and they be digging trenches in the fields on the north side of the Marketstead, and carry the carcasses thither as they may. But the slain whom they find of the kindreds do they array out yonder before this Hall. In all wise are these men tame and biddable, save that they rage against the Dusky Men, though they fear them yet. As for us, they deem us Gods come down from heaven to help them. So much for what is good: now have I an ill word to say; to wit, that in the houses whereas we have found many thralls alive, yet also have we found many dead; for amongst these murder-carles were some of an evil sort, who, when they saw that the battle would go against them, rushed into the houses hewing down all before them﻿—man, woman, and child; so that many of the halls and chambers we saw running blood like to shambles. To be short: of them whom they were going to hew to the Gods, we have found thirteen living and three dead, of which latter is one woman; and of the living, seven women; and all these, living and dead, with the leaden shackles yet on them wherein they should be burned. To all these and others whom we have found, we have done what of service we could in the way of victual and clothes, so that they scarce believe that they are on this lower earth. Moreover, I have with me two score of them, who are men of some wits, and who know of the stores of victual and other wares which the felons had, and these will fetch and carry for you as much as ye will. Is all done rightly, War-leader?”

===Chinese===
克劳便走上厅堂，立在面神面前说道："战首，该办的事我们都已办妥，集市坪四周的房屋都已清扫一空。再者，依达拉赫之谋，我们已派了谷中穷苦之民里几名为众人所敬重者，去掩埋那些被杀恶徒的尸首；他们正在集市坪北边的田里挖沟，将尸首尽力搬运过去。至于所发现的诸族阵亡者，则陈列于那边、厅堂之前。这些人处处驯顺听命，唯独对黝暗人恨之入骨——尽管他们至今仍畏惧他们。至于我们，他们把我们当作从天而降、来救助他们的神灵。好消息便是这些；如今我还有一桩坏消息要禀报：即在我们寻见许多活奴隶的屋子里，同样也寻见许多死者；原来那些凶徒之中，有几个最为穷凶极恶之辈，一见战局将败，便冲进屋里见人就砍——无论男女老幼；以至许多厅堂、内室之中，血水横流、宛如屠场。简而言之：那些他们正要砍了献祭诸神的人，我们发现十三人尚活、三人已死，后者之中有一名女子；活着的里面有七个女子；这些无论死活，身上都还带着铅制的镣铐——他们原是要带着这些镣铐被活活烧死的。对所有这些人以及我们寻见的其他受难者，我们都在饮食、衣物质料上尽力周济，使他们简直不敢相信自己还在尘世之上。再者，我身边还有他们之中四十名颇有机灵之人，他们知道那些恶徒所屯的粮食及其他货物的下落，你们要多少、他们便能搬运多少。战首，这一切办得可妥当？"

===Original===
“Right well,” said Face-of-god, “and we give thee our thanks therefor. And now it were well if these thy folk were to dight our dinner for us in some green field the nighest that may be, and thither shall all the Host be bidden by sound of horn. Meantime, let us void this Hall till it be cleansed of the filth of the Dusky Ones; but hereafter shall we come again to it, and light a fire on the Holy Hearth, and bid the Gods and the Fathers come back and behold their children sitting glad in the ancient Hall.”

===Chinese===
"再妥当不过，"面神说，"我们为此向你致谢。如今，最好让你这些手下在最近的草地上为我们备好正餐，并吹响号角，邀全军都去入席。眼下且让我们撤出这座厅堂，待清除黝暗人所留的污秽之后再说；此后我们还要再回到这里，在圣灶之上燃起火，请诸神与列祖回来，看他们的儿女欢然端坐于这座古老的厅堂之中。"

===Original===
Then men shouted and were exceeding joyous; but Face-of-god said once more: “Bear ye a bench out into the Marketplace over against the door of this Hall: thereon will I sit with other chieftains of the kindreds, that whoso will may have recourse to us.”

So therewith all the men of the kindreds made their ways out of the Hall and into the Marketstead, which was by this time much cleared of the slaughtered felons; and the bale for the burnt-offering was now but smouldering, and a thin column of blue smoke was going up wavering amidst the light airs of the afternoon. Men were somewhat silent now; for they were stiff and weary with the morning’s battle; and a many had been hurt withal; and on many there yet rested the after-grief of battle, and sorrow for the loss of friends and well-wishers.

===Chinese===
众人欢呼，欢喜异常；面神又说道："你们抬一条长凳出去，放到集市之中、正对这厅堂门的地方：我要与诸族的其他首领同坐其上，好让凡有需要的，都能来找我们。"

于是诸族之人纷纷走出厅堂、进入集市坪，此时坪中被杀的恶徒尸首已大半被清走；燔祭的柴堆此刻只剩余烬暗燃，一缕细细的青烟在午后微风中摇曳直上。众人此刻都有些沉默；因为晨间一战，他们浑身僵硬疲乏；许多人还带着伤；更多人心中仍压着战后的余哀，为失去朋友与善意之友而悲伤。

===Original===
For in the battle had fallen one long hundred and two of the men of the Host; and of these were two score and five of the kindreds of the Steer, the Bull, and the Bridge, who had made such valiant onslaught by the southern road. Of the Shepherds died one score save three; for though they scattered the foe at once, yet they fell on with such headlong valour, rather than wisely, that many were trapped in the throng of the Dusky Men. Of the Woodlanders were slain one score and nine; for hard had been the fight about them, and no man of them spared himself one whit. Of the men of the Wolf, who were but a few, fell sixteen men, and all save two of these in Face-of-god’s battle. Of the Burgdale men whom Folk-might led, to wit, them of the Face, the Vine, and the Sickle, were but seven men slain outright. In this tale are told all those who died of their hurts after the day of battle. Therewithal many others were sorely hurt who mended, and went about afterwards hale and hearty.

===Chinese===
原来此战之中，大军阵亡者共一长百又二；其中属犍牛族、公牛族与桥族的，有四十五人之多——他们沿南路发起了那般英勇的冲杀。牧羊之民阵亡十七人；因为他们虽将敌军一举冲散，却一味奋不顾身地猛冲、不顾轻重，结果许多人在黝暗人的重围中被困。林中汉子阵亡二十九人；因为他们那一处的战斗极为惨烈，他们之中无一人稍稍爱惜自己。狼族之人本就不多，阵亡十六人，其中除两人之外，皆死于面神所指挥的那一场战斗。民强所率的堡谷人——即面族、葡藤族与镰族之人——仅七人当场阵亡。此数之中，已包括决战之后因伤而死的全部死者。此外尚有许多人伤势虽重，却渐痊愈，事后仍能健步行走、精神康健。

===Original===
So as the folk abode in the Marketplace, somewhat faint and weary, they heard horns blow up merrily, and Crow the Shaft-speeder came forth and stood on the mound of the altar, and bade men fare to dinner, and therewith he led the way, bearing in his hand the banner of the Golden Bushel, of which House he was; and they followed him into a fair and great mead on the southwest of Silverstead, besprinkled about with ancient trees of sweet chestnut. There they found the boards spread for them with the best of victual which the poor downtrodden folk knew how to dight for them; and especially was there great plenty of good wine of the sun-smitten bents.

===Chinese===
众人正有些委顿疲倦地立在集市之中，忽听得号角欢快地吹起，疾箭者克劳走出来，站在祭坛土台之上，招呼众人去用饭；他便领头前行，手中擎着金斗之旗——他正是金斗族之人；众人随他走到银镇西南一片宽广秀美的草地上，那里疏疏落落地点缀着几株古老的甜栗树。草坪之上，桌案已为他们铺开，摆满了那些穷苦受压之民所能精心备办的最佳肴馔；尤其是向阳山坡所产的佳酿，格外丰足。

===Original===
So they fell to their meat, and the poor folk, both men and women, served them gladly, though they were somewhat afeard of these fierce sword-wielders, the Gods who had delivered them. The said thralls were mostly not of those who had fallen so bitterly on their fleeing masters, but were men and women of the households, not so roughly treated as the others, that is to say, those who had been wont to toil under the lash in the fields and the silver-mines, and were as wild as they durst be.

As for these waiting-thralls, the men of the kindreds were gentle and blithe with them, and often as they served them would they stay their hands (and especially if they were women), and would draw down their heads to put a morsel in their mouths, or set the wine-cup to their lips; and they would stroke them and caress them, and treat them in all wise as their dear friends. Moreover, when any man was full, he would arise and take hold of one of the thralls, and set him in his place, and serve him with meat and drink, and talk with him kindly, so that the poor folk were much bewildered with joy. And the first that arose from table were the Sun-beam and Bow-may and Hall-face, with many of the swains and the women of the Woodlanders; and they went from table to table serving the others.

===Chinese===
于是众人落座用肉食，那些穷苦之民——无论男女——都欢喜地在一旁伺候，尽管他们对这些挥剑的猛士、这些解救他们的神灵尚有几分畏怯。这些奴隶大多并非方才痛击逃亡主人的那一类，而是内宅的男女仆役，不像别人那般受尽苛待——所谓别人，指的是那些常年在田间、银矿之中受鞭笞苦役的奴隶，他们不过是胆敢野到何处、便野到何处罢了。

至于这些伺候用饭的奴隶，诸族之人都待他们亲切和悦；他们上前伺候时，诸族之人常常按住他们的手（尤其是女子），扳下他们的头、把一口菜送进他们嘴里，或将酒杯凑到他们唇边；又抚摸他们、亲热他们，处处把他们当作挚友看待。再者，谁一吃饱，便起身拉过一名奴隶，让在自己位子上坐下，布他肉食、敬他酒浆，和颜悦色地与他攀谈，使这些穷苦之民欢喜得不知所措。最先离席的，是日光、弓娥与厅面，还有许多少年郎与林中汉子的女子；他们逐桌走去，伺候旁人。

===Original===
The Sun-beam had done off her armour, and went about exceeding fair and lovely in her kirtle; but Bow-may yet bore her hauberk, for she loved it, and indeed it was so fine and well-wrought that it was no great burden. Albeit she had gone down with the Sun-beam and other women to a fair stream thereby, and there had they bathed and washed themselves; and Bow-may’s hurts, which were not great, had been looked to and bound up afresh, and she had come to table unhelmed, with a wreath of windflowers round her head.

===Chinese===
日光已卸下甲胄，一袭长裙，四处走动，容光焕发、娇美不可方物；弓娥却仍穿着锁子甲，因为她喜爱它，况且那甲精细考究，穿在身上也并不怎样累赘。不过她方才已与日光及其他女子一同下到近旁一条清溪里，沐浴浣洗过；弓娥的伤——都不甚重——也已被重新察看、包扎停当；她未戴盔入席，头上绕着一圈银莲花编的花环。

===Original===
There then they feasted; and their hearts were strengthened by the meat and drink; and if sorrow were blended with their joy, yet were they high-hearted through both joy and sorrow, looking forward to the good days to be in the Dales at the Roots of the Mountains, and the love and fellowship of Folks and of Houses.

===Chinese===
他们便在那里设起盛宴；酒肉下肚，心头又有了力气；纵然悲伤与欢乐交织，他们无论悲喜，心境都依然高昂——他们期盼着群山之根诸谷之中将要到来的美好岁月，期盼着诸部族、诸宅第之间的情谊与同心。

===Original===
But as for Face-of-god, he went not to the meadow, but abode sitting on the bench in the Marketplace, where were none else now of the kindreds save the appointed warders. They had brought him a morsel and a cup of wine, and he had eaten and drunk; and now he sat there with Dale-warden lying sheathed across his knees, and seeming to gaze on the thralls of Silverdale busied in carrying away the bodies of the slain felons, after they had stripped them of their raiment and weapons. Yet indeed all this was before his eyes as a picture which he noted not. Rather he sat pondering many things; wondering at his being here in Silverdale in the hour of victory; longing for the peace of Burgdale and the bride-chamber of the Sun-beam. Then went his thought out toward his old playmate lying hurt in Silverdale; and his heart was grieved because of her, yet not for long, though his thought still dwelt on her; since he deemed that she would live and presently be happy﻿—and happy thenceforward for many years. So pondered Face-of-god in the Marketplace of Silverdale.

===Chinese===
至于面神，他没有去那片草地，仍坐在集市里的长凳之上，此刻那里除指定的守卫之外，再无别的诸族之人。有人给他送来一口食物、一杯酒，他已吃喝过了；此刻他坐在那里，谷卫横陈于膝、尚在鞘中，仿佛凝望着银谷的奴隶们忙着搬运那些被杀恶徒的尸首——他们已剥去尸首的衣物和兵器。然而这一切在他眼前不过如一幅画，他并未真个留意。他其实坐在那里沉思许多事；惊异于自己竟在胜利之时身处银谷；又渴想堡谷的太平、日光的洞房。随后他的心思又飘向那位卧伤在银谷的旧日玩伴；他为此心痛，然而并不长久——纵然心思仍停留在她身上；因为他想她必将活下去，不久便会快乐——此后许多年都将快乐。面神便这样在银镇的集市之中沉思。

## LV Departure from Silverdale / 五十五 离银谷

===Original===
On morrow of the morrow were the Burgdale men and they of the Shepherds gathered together in the Marketstead early in the morning, and they were all ready for departure; and the men of the Wolf and the Woodlanders, and of the delivered thralls a great many, stood round about them grieving that they must go. There was much talk between the folk of the Dale and the Guests, and many promises were given and taken to come and go betwixt the two Dales. There also were the men of the thrall-folk who were to wend home with the Burgdalers; and they had been stuffed with good things by the men of the kindreds, and were as fain as might be.

===Chinese===
到了第三日清晨，堡谷之人与牧羊之民齐集于集市坪（Marketstead），皆已整装待发；狼族之人、林中汉子，以及获释的奴隶之中也有许多，围立四周，为他们即将离去而依依不舍。谷中之人与宾客之间言谈甚多，彼此许下来往两谷的诸多诺言。那些要随堡谷人归去的原奴隶之民也在其中；他们被诸族之人赠了满身好物，个个喜不自胜。

===Original===
As for the Sun-beam, she was somewhat out of herself at first, being eager and restless beyond her wont, and yet at whiles weeping-ripe when she called to mind that she was now leaving all those things, the gain whereof had been a dream to her both waking and sleeping for these years past. But at last, as she stood in the door of the Mote-house, and beheld all the throng of folk happy and friendly, it came over her that she herself had done her full share to bring all this about, and that all those pleasant places of Silverdale now full of the goodly life of man would be there even as she had striven for them, and that they would be a part of her left behind, though she were dwelling otherwhere.

Therewithal she said to herself that it was now her part to wield the life of men in Burgdale, and begin once more her days of a chieftain and a swayer of the Folk, and the life of a stirring woman, which the edge of the sword and the need of the hard handplay had taken out of her hands for a while, making her as a child in the hands of the strong wielders of the blades.

So now she became calm once more, and her face was clad again with the full measure of that majesty of beauty which had once overawed Face-of-god amidst his love of her; and folk beheld her and marvelled at her fairness, and said: “She hath an inward sorrow at leaving the fair Dale wherein her Fathers dwelt, and where her mother’s ashes lie in earth.” Albeit now was her sorrow but little, and much was her hope, and her foresight of days to be; though all the Dale, yea, every leaf and twig of it whereby her feet had ever passed, and each stone of the fair houses, was to her as a picture that she could look on from henceforth forever.

===Chinese===
至于日光，初时神色颇有失常，焦灼浮躁，远异平素；然而每念及自己如今要离弃这一切——这些东西，数年来她醒时梦中所求的，如今都已成真——又时时欲泣。但终于，当她立于议事堂之门，望着这一大群欢悦友善之人，心中忽然有所感悟：这一切之所以成就，她自己也尽了全力；银谷所有那些悦人之处，如今充满了人之美善生活，将来仍会如她所力争的那般存留；纵使她身居他乡，这些地方也将是她留在此地的一部分。

她随即想道：如今她当治理堡谷人之生活，重又开始她身为族中首领与主事者的日子，重过那操劳女子之生活——而这生活，前些时因刀剑之锋、苦战之需，曾一度离她而去，使她如同孩童一般，任凭那些执刃壮士摆布。

于是她又复归平静，面容重又披上那份美的威严之全体——这威严曾使面神在爱慕她之时不禁心生敬畏；众人望着她，惊异于她的美，说道："她离弃这先祖所居、母亲骨灰所埋的佳谷，心中必有难言之恸。"然而此时她的悲伤已甚微，而希望与对来日的预见却甚多；尽管整条山谷——是的，她足踪所及的每一片叶、每一根枝，那些美屋的每一块石头——对她而言都如同一幅画卷，从此可以永远凝望。

===Original===
Of the Bride it is to be said that she was now much mended, and she caused men bear her on a litter out into the Marketplace, that she might look on the departure of her folk. She had seen Face-of-god once and again since the Day of Battle, and each time had been kind and blithe with him; and for Iron-face, she loved him so well that she was ever loth to let him depart from her, save when Folk-might was with her.

And now was the Alderman standing beside her, and she said to him: “Friend and kinsman, this is the day of departure, and though I must needs abide behind, and am content to abide, yet doth mine heart ache with the sundering; for tomorrow when I wake in the morning there will be no more sending of a messenger to fetch thee to me. Indeed, great hath been the love between me and my people, and nought hath come between us to mar it. Now, kinsman, I would see Gold-mane, my cousin, that I may bid him farewell; for who knoweth if I shall see him again hereafter?”

===Chinese===
至于新娘，要说的是她如今伤势已大好，命人抬她坐轿椅出到集市之中，好目送她的族人启程。自决战之日（the Day of Battle）以来，她已与面神见过一两面，每次都待他亲切和悦；至于铁面，她爱他极深，总是舍不得让他离去——除非民强在旁陪伴。

此刻长老正立在她身旁，她对他说："朋友兼亲人，今日便是离别之日；我虽不得不留在此地，也甘愿留下，然而这分离仍令我心痛；因为明日清晨醒来，再也不能差人去请你到我这里来了。我与我的族人之间，情谊确实深厚，从未有任何事从中作梗、损害这份情。亲人啊，我想见一见金鬃，我的表弟，好与他道别；因为谁能知道，此后我是否还能再见到他呢？"

===Original===
Then went Iron-face and found Face-of-god where he was speaking with Folk-might and the chieftains, and said to him:

“Come quickly, for thy cousin the Bride would speak with thee.”

Face-of-god reddened, and paled afterwards, but he went along with his father silently; and his heart beat as he came and stood before the litter whereas the Bride lay, clad all in white and propped up on fair cushions of red silk. She was frail to look on, and worn and pale yet; but he deemed that she was very happy.

She smiled on him, and reached out her hand and said:

“Welcome once more, cousin!” And he held her hand and kissed it, and was nigh weeping, so sore was he beset by a throng of memories concerning her and him in the days when they were little; and he bethought him of her loving-kindness of past days, beyond that of most children, beyond that of most maidens; and how there was nothing in his life but she had a share in it, till the day when he found the Hall on the Mountain.

===Chinese===
于是铁面走去，在面神正与民强及诸首领说话之处找到了他，对他说道：

"快来，你的表姐新娘要与你说话。"

面神先是一红，随即又转白，却默默随父亲而去；他走到轿椅之前站定，心跳不止——新娘便躺在那轿椅之上，通身白衣，靠在精美的红绸软垫之上。她看起来娇弱，形容憔悴而苍白；但他觉得她是极快乐的。

她朝他微笑，伸出手来，说道：

"欢迎再来，表弟！"他握住她的手吻了吻，几乎要落下泪来——太多关于他们二人幼时之日的回忆一齐涌上心头，将他重重围困；他想起她昔日那份情义，胜过大多数孩童，胜过大多数少女；又想起他一生之中，无一事她不曾有份——直到他在山上发现那座厅堂的那一日为止。

===Original===
So he said to her: “Kinswoman, is it well with thee?”

“Yea,” she said, “I am now nigh whole of my hurts.”

He was silent a while; then he said:

“And otherwise art thou merry at heart?”

“Yea, indeed,” said she; “yet thou wilt not find it hard to deem that I am sorry of the sundering betwixt me and Burgdale.”

Again was he silent, and said in a while: “Dost thou deem that I wrought that sundering?”

She smiled kindly on him and said: “Gold-mane, my playmate, thou art become a mighty warrior and a great chief; but thou art not so mighty as that. Many things lay behind the sundering which were neither thou nor I.”

“Yet,” said he, “it was but such a little time agone that all things seemed so sure; and we﻿—to both of us was the outlook happy.”

“Let it be happy still,” she said, “now begrudging is gone. Belike the sundering came because we were so sure, and had no defence against the wearing of the days; even as it fareth with a folk that hath no foes.”

He smiled and said: “Even as it hath befallen *thy* folk, O Bride, a while ago.”

She reddened, and reached her hand to him, and he took it and held it, and said: “Shall I see thee again as the days wear?”

Said she: “O chieftain of the Folk, thou shalt have much to do in Burgdale, and the way is long. Yet would I have thee see my children. Forget not the token on my hand which thou holdest. But now get thee to thy folk with no more words; for after all, playmate, the sundering is grievous to me, and I would not spin out the time thereof. Farewell!”

He said no more, but stooped down and kissed her lips, and then turned from her, and took his ways to the head of the Host, and fell to asking and answering, and bidding and arraying; and in a little time was his heart dancing with joy to think of the days that lay before him, wherein now all seemed happy.

===Chinese===
于是他对她说："表姐，你身子可好？"

"嗯，"她说，"我的伤如今已快痊愈了。"

他沉默了一阵，然后说道：

"那你的心境呢，可还舒畅？"

"确实舒畅，"她说，"然而你不难想到，我与堡谷这番分离，心中是惆怅的。"

他又沉默了，过了一阵说道："你以为这分离是我造成的么？"

她和善地朝他微笑，说道："金鬃，我的玩伴，你已成了英勇的武士、伟大的首领；然而你还没伟大到那个地步。这分离背后有许多缘由，既非因你，也非因我。"

"然而，"他说，"不过是多久以前的事，一切还显得那么笃定；我们——我们两人眼前的前景都是那般美满。"

"就让那美满仍存吧，"她说，"如今妒意既已消去。这分离之来，多半正因为我们太过笃定，对岁月的侵蚀全无防备；正如一个没有仇敌的部族一般。"

他微笑道："正如不久前你族人所遭遇的那样，新娘。"

她红了脸，把手伸向他，他接过来握住，说道："岁月流转，我还能再见到你么？"

她说："族人的首领啊，你在堡谷有许多事要做，路途又遥远。然而我愿你来见见我的孩子们。别忘了你手中所握的、我手上这信物。但如今你莫再多言，回到你族人那里去吧；因为玩伴啊，这分离毕竟令我伤怀，我不愿将它拖延。珍重！"

他不再多言，俯身吻了她的嘴唇，然后转身离去，径往大军（the Host）之前列走去，开始问询应答、发号施令、整顿队伍；不多时，他的心便因想到眼前的日子而欢跃起舞——在那日子里，如今一切似乎都美满了。

===Original===
So was all arrayed for departure when it lacked three hours of noon. As Folk-might had promised, there were certain light wains drawn by bullocks abiding the departure of the Host, and of sumpter bullocks and horses no few; and all these were laden with fair gifts of the Dale, as silver, and raiment, and weapons. There were many things fair-wrought in the time of the Sorrow, that henceforth should see but little sorrow. Moreover, there was plenty of provision for the way, both meal and wine, and sheep and neat; and all things as fair as might be, and well-arrayed.

It was the Shepherds who were to lead the way; and after them were arrayed the men of the Vine and the Sickle; then they of the Steer, the Bridge, and the Bull; and lastly the House of the Face, with old Stone-face leading them. The Sun-beam was to journey along with the House of the Steer, which had taken her in as a maiden of their blood; and though she had so much liefer have fared with the House of the Face, yet she went meekly as she was bidden, as one who has gotten a great thing, and will make no stir about a small one.

Along with her were Wood-father and Wood-mother, and Wood-wise, now whole of his hurt, and Wood-wont, and Bow-may. Save Bow-may, they were not very joyous; for they were fain of Silverdale, and it irked them to leave it; moreover, they also had liefer have gone along with the House of the War-leader.

Last of all went those people of the once thralls of the Dusky Men who had cast in their lot with the Burgdalers, and they were exceeding merry; and especially the women of them, they were chattering like the stares in the autumn evening, when they gather from the fields in the tall elm-trees before they go to roost.

===Chinese===
于是一切整备停当，只待启程，其时距正午尚差三个时辰。正如民强所许诺的，有数辆由犍牛牵引的轻便辎车，等候大军出发；驮货的犍牛和马匹也不在少数；这些全载满了山谷所赠的精美礼物，如白银、衣物、兵器。其中有许多是苦难之世（the Sorrow）精心所制之物，此后再不必见什么忧愁了。此外，路上的粮草也丰足得很，既有米面酒浆，也有牛羊牲口；一切物什都尽可能精美，安排得妥妥当当。

打头阵的是牧羊之民；其后是葡藤族与镰族之人；再后是犍牛族、桥族与公牛族之人；殿后的则是面神之宅，由年迈的石面率领。日光要随犍牛族同行——那一族已收她作本族血脉中的少女；虽说她极愿与面神之宅同行，却仍温顺地听从安排，正如一个已得到大恩之人，不愿为小事再起波澜。

与她同行的有林父、林母，还有如今伤已痊愈的林智，以及林习和弓娥。除了弓娥之外，他们都不甚欢悦；因为他们喜爱银谷，离弃它令他们心绪难平；况且他们也情愿随战首之族同行。

最后是那些从前为黝暗人所奴、如今已决意随堡谷人而去的人，他们欢喜异常；尤其是其中的女子们，叽叽喳喳，宛如秋暮的椋鸟——它们从田间飞来，聚在参天榆树之上，待到栖宿之时。

===Original===
Now all the men of the Dale, both of the kindreds and of the thrall-folk, made way for the Host and its havings, that they might go their ways down the Dale; albeit the Woodlanders clung close to the line of their ancient friends, and with them, as men who were sorry for the sundering, were Wolf-stone and God-swain and Spear-fist. But the chiefs, they drew around Folk-might a little beside the way.

Now Red-coat of Waterless, who had been hurt, and was now whole again, cast his arms about Folk-might and kissed him, and said:

“All the way hence to Burgdale will I sow with good wishes for thee and thine, and especially for my dear friend God-swain of the Silver Arm; and I would wish and long that they might turn into spells to draw thy feet to usward; for we love thee well.”

In like wise spake other of the Burgdalers; and Folk-might was kind and blithe with them, and he said:

“Friends, forget ye not that the way is no longer from you to us than it is from us to you. One half of this matter it is for you to deal with.”

“True is that,” said Red-beard of the Knolls, “but look you, Folk-might, we be but simple husbandmen, and may not often stir from our meadows and acres; even now I bethink me that May is amidst us, and I am beginning to be drawn by the thought of the haysel. Whereas thou﻿—” (and therewith he reddened) “I doubt that thou hast little to do save the work of chieftains, and we know that such work is but little missed if it be undone.”

Thereat Folk-might laughed; and when the others saw that he laughed, they laughed also, else had they foreborne for courtesy’s sake.

But Folk-might answered: “Nay, chief of the Sickle, I am not altogether a chieftain, now we have gotten us peace; and somewhat of a husbandman shall I be. Moreover, doubt ye not that I shall do my utmost to behold the fair Dale again; for it is but mountains that meet not.”

===Chinese===
此刻谷中之所有人——无论诸族之人还是原奴隶之民——都为大军及其辎重让开道路，好让他们沿山谷而下；然而林中汉子们仍紧随着旧日好友的队伍，与他们同行的还有狼石（Wolf-stone）、神仆（God-swain）和枪拳（Spear-fist），这几人也为分离而伤感。但首领们却走到路旁，围拢到民强身边。

那无水地（Waterless）的红衣——他先前受了伤，如今已痊愈——张开双臂抱住民强吻了他，说道：

"从这儿一直到堡谷，我一路都要为你和你的族人撒下祝福，尤其为我的好友银臂族的神仆；我愿这些祝福化作咒语，吸引你的脚步转向我们这边；因为我们深爱着你。"

其余堡谷人也说了类似的话；民强对他们亲切和悦，说道：

"朋友们，别忘了这条路：从你们到我们这里，并不比从我们到你们那里更远。这事的一半，是要由你们来操持的。"

"这话不错，"丘冈（the Knolls）的红胡子（Red-beard）说，"但是你瞧，民强，我们不过是些老实庄稼人，不常离开我们的草场和田亩；即便此刻，我想到五月已至，心里已开始被割草之候（haysel）的念头牵动了。而你呢——"（说到这里他红了脸）"我猜想你除了首领的事务之外，几乎无事可做；而我们知道，这种事若搁着不做，也没人会怎么惦记。"

民强听了大笑；旁人见他笑了，便也跟着笑，否则出于礼貌本会忍住的。

民强却答道："不然，镰族的首领啊，如今我们既已得享太平，我便不完全是个首领了，多少也要做个庄稼人。况且，你们不必怀疑，我必竭尽全力再来看看这美丽的山谷；因为唯有山与山不会相会。"

===Original===
Now spake Face-of-god to Folk-might, smiling and somewhat softly, and said: “Is all forgiven now, since the day when we first felt each other’s arms?”

“Yea, all,” said Folk-might; “now hath befallen what I foretold thee in Shadowy Vale, that thou mightest pay for all that had come and gone, if thou wouldest but look to it. Indeed thou wert angry with me for that saying on that eve of Shadowy Vale; but see thou, in those days I was an older man than thou, and might admonish thee somewhat; but now, though but few days have gone over thine head, yet many deeds have abided in thine hand, and thou art much aged. Anger hath left thee, and wisdom hath waxed in thee. As for me, I may now say this word: May the Folk of Burgdale love the Folk of Silverdale as well as I love thee; then shall all be well.”

Then Face-of-god cast his arms about him and kissed him, and turned away toward Stone-face and Hall-face his brother, where they stood at the head of the array of the Face; and even therewith came up the Alderman somewhat sad and sober of countenance, and he pushed by the War-leader roughly and would not speak with him.

And now blew up the horns of the Shepherds, and they began to move on amidst the shouting of the men of Silverdale; yet were there amongst the Woodlanders those who wept when they saw their friends verily departing from them.

===Chinese===
这时面神微笑着、语调柔和地对民强说道："自从我们初次交手那一日起，如今一切恩怨可都化解了？"

"是的，全都化解了，"民强说，"我在幽谷曾对你预言过的事如今已经应验——你若肯留意，便能弥补一切已往之事。当日幽谷那个傍晚，你因我这番话恼了我；但是你瞧，那些日子里我比你年长，可以稍稍规劝你几句；而如今，虽不过寥寥数日从你头上过去，却有许多大事经了你的手，你已老成许多。怒气已离你而去，智慧已在心中滋长。至于我，如今可以说出这一句话：愿堡谷之民爱银谷之民，如同我爱你一般；如此则一切皆安。"

面神张开双臂抱住他吻了他，然后转身走向石面和他的兄弟厅面——他们正站在面族阵列之首；正在此时，长老走了过来，面容颇有几分黯然凝重，他从战首身边粗鲁地挤了过去，不肯与他说话。

此时牧羊之民的号角吹响，他们在银谷人的欢呼声中开始前行；然而林中汉子之中，有人见他们的好友真的离他们而去，不禁落下泪来。

===Original===
But when they of the foremost of the Host were gotten so far forward that the men of the Face could begin to move, lo! there was Redesman with his fiddle amongst the leaders; and he had done a man’s work in the day of battle, and all looked kindly on him. About him on this morn were some who had learned the craft of singing well together, and knew his minstrelsy, and he turned to these and nodded as their array moved on, and he drew his bow across the strings, and straightway they fell a-singing, even as it might be thus:

> Back again to the dear Dale where born was the kindred,
> Here wend we all living, and liveth our mirth.
> Here afoot fares our joyance, whatever men hindred,
> Through all wrath of the heavens, all storms of the earth.

> O true, we have left here a part of our treasure,
> The ashes of stout ones, the stems of the shield;
> But the bold lives they spended have sown us new pleasure,
> Fair tales for the telling in fold and on field.

> For as oft as we sing of their edges’ upheaving,
> When the yellowing windows shine forth o’er the night,
> Their names unforgotten with song interweaving
> Shall draw forth dear drops from the depths of delight.

> Or when down by our feet the grey sickles are lying,
> And behind us is curling the supper-tide smoke,
> No whit shall they grudge us the joyance undying,
> Remembrance of men that put from us the yoke.

> When the huddle of ewes from the fells we have driven,
> And we see down the Dale the grey reach of the roof,
> We shall tell of the gift in the battle-joy given,
> All the fierceness of friends that drave sorrow aloof.

> Once then we lamented, and mourned them departed;
> Once only, no oftener. Henceforth shall we fling
> Their names up aloft, when the merriest hearted
> To the Fathers unseen of our life-days we sing.

===Chinese===
但当大军前队已前行到面族之人可以开始移动之时，看哪！雷德斯曼正带着他的提琴站在前队之中；他在决战之日曾立下壮士之功，众人都和善地看着他。这日清晨，他身边聚着几个善于和声合唱、熟悉他曲谱之人；队伍前行之际，他转向他们点了点头，将琴弓一拉掠过琴弦，他们便齐声唱了起来，其辞大略如此：

> 归矣，归于亲族诞育之爱谷，
> 生者尽偕行于此，欢乐长存其中。
> 欢欣徒步而行，任凭世人横加阻挠，
> 历尽诸天之盛怒、大地之风雨。

> 诚然，吾辈留下一份珍宝于此：
> 勇者之灰烬、盾牌之残柄；
> 然彼等倾尽之壮命，已播下新的欢愉，
> 化作羊栏、田野之间可传之佳谭。

> 盖每当吾辈歌颂其利刃之高举，
> 当昏黄之窗于夜色中透出光华，
> 其名永不忘，与歌声交织相融，
> 必从欢愉之深渊汲出珍贵之泪。

> 抑或足畔横陈灰色镰刀之时，
> 身后袅袅升起晚餐之炊烟，
> 彼等必不吝留予吾辈不朽之欢颜——
> 对那为吾辈卸去枷锁者之怀念。

> 待吾辈将母羊之群自山岭驱归，
> 遥见谷底连绵之灰色屋顶，
> 吾辈当讲述战之欢中所赐之礼，
> 挚友驱远愁苦之那份刚猛。

> 彼时吾辈曾哀恸，为逝者举哀；
> 唯此一度，断无再有。自此以后，
> 吾辈当扬其名于九天——每逢心怀至欢，
> 向吾辈生年所未见之冥冥列祖歌唱。

===Original===
Then was there silence in the ranks of men; and many murmured the names of the fallen as they fared on their way from out the Marketplace of Silverstead. Then once more Redesman and his mates took up the song:

> Come tell me, O friends, for whom bideth the maiden
> Wet-foot from the river-ford down in the Dale?
> For whom hath the goodwife the ox-wagon laden
> With the babble of children, brown-handed and hale?

> Come tell me for what are the women abiding,
> Till each on the other aweary they lean?
> Is it loitering of evil that thus they are chiding,
> The slow-footed bearers of sorrow unseen?

> Nay, yet were they toiling if sorrow had worn them,
> Or hushed had they bided with lips parched and wan.
> The birds of the air other tidings have borne them﻿—
> How glad through the wood goeth man beside man.

> Then fare forth, O valiant, and loiter no longer
> Than the cry of the cuckoo when May is at hand;
> Late waxeth the spring-tide, and daylight grows longer,
> And nightly the star-street hangs high o’er the land.

> Many lives, many days for the Dale do ye carry;
> When the Host breaketh out from the thicket unshorn,
> It shall be as the sun that refuseth to tarry
> On the crown of all mornings, the Midsummer morn.

===Chinese===
于是人丛之中归于寂静；许多人从银镇集市而出、一路前行之际，低声念诵着阵亡者的名字。随后雷德斯曼与他的同伴们再度唱起：

> 来吧告诉我，朋友们，少女为谁而待，
> 她湿足涉过谷中河上之渡口？
> 主妇又为谁将牛车装满，
> 满载棕手健壮孩童之喧哗？

> 来吧告诉我，女人们为谁而候，
> 直至彼此倦极相倚？
> 可是恶人迁延，令她们如此嗔怪，
> 那慢足的、暗携忧愁的背负者？

> 不然，若是忧愁磨耗了她们，她们必在劳作，
> 必缄默枯坐，唇焦而面惨。
> 空中飞鸟却已捎来别样消息——
> 人与人之并肩过林，何等欢然。

> 那么前行吧，勇者，莫再迁延，
> 唯趁杜鹃啼鸣、五月将至之时；
> 春时虽迟来，白昼渐渐长了，
> 夜夜星街高悬于大地上空。

> 多少生命、多少时日，你们为山谷而承载；
> 待大军从未剪之密林中破围而出，
> 那必将如不肯稍驻的日轮，
> 临于众清晨之冠冕——仲夏之晨。

===Original===
Again the song fell down till they were well on the western way down Silverdale; and then Redesman handled his fiddle once more, and again the song rose up, and suchlike were the words which were borne back into the Marketplace of Silverstead:

> And yet what is this, and why fare ye so slowly,
> While our echoing halls of our voices are dumb,
> And abideth unlitten the hearth-brand the holy,
> And the feet of the kind fare afield till we come?

> For not yet through the wood and its tangle ye wander;
> Now skirt we no thicket, no path by the mere;
> Far aloof for our feet leads the Dale-road out yonder;
> Full fair is the morning, its doings all clear.

> There is nought now our feet on the highway delaying
> Save the friend’s loving-kindness, the sundering of speech;
> The well-willer’s word that ends words with the saying,
> The loth to depart while each looketh on each.

> Fare on then, for nought are ye laden with sorrow;
> The love of this land do ye bear with you still.
> In two Dales of the earth for today and tomorrow
> Is waxing the oak-tree of peace and goodwill.

Thus then they departed from Silverdale, even as men who were a portion thereof, and had not utterly left it behind. And that night they lay in the wildwood not very far from the Dale’s end; for they went softly, faring amongst so many friends.

===Chinese===
歌声再度低落，直到他们走上银谷西行之路甚远；雷德斯曼再度操起提琴，歌声又起，那随风飘回银镇集市的歌辞，大略如此：

> 然则这是为何，你们行得如此迟缓？
> 吾辈回声缭绕之厅堂此刻寂然无声，
> 神圣之灶火尚待点燃，
> 亲族之足犹在田间相候，直至吾辈来归。

> 此刻你们尚未穿行于林木荆棘之间；
> 吾辈不傍丛林，不经湖畔小径；
> 远远在前方，山谷之路引吾辈之足；
> 晨光何等明媚，诸事皆朗然分明。

> 如今大道之上，再无一物留滞吾辈之足，
> 唯有友人之深情、言语之将别；
> 善意者一言既出，遂尽止余辞，
> 彼此相顾，依依不忍离去。

> 那么前行吧，你们未尝为忧愁所累；
> 此地之热爱，你们仍随身携行。
> 今日与明日，于大地之两谷之中，
> 和平与善意之橡树正日益长成。

他们便这样离开了银谷，仿佛自身原是此地之一部分，并未将它全然抛在身后。是夜，他们宿于距谷口不远的野林之中；因为他们走得从容——在这么多友人之间穿行。

===Original===
> Whiles carried o’er the iron road,
 

 We hurry by some fair abode;
 

 The garden bright amidst the hay,
 

 The yellow wain upon the way,
 

 The dining men, the wind that sweeps
 

 Light locks from off the sun-sweet heaps﻿—
 

 The gable grey, the hoary roof,
 

 Here now﻿—and now so far aloof.
 

 How sorely then we long to stay
 

 And midst its sweetness wear the day,
 

 And ’neath its changing shadows sit,
 

 And feel ourselves a part of it.
 

 Such rest, such stay, I strove to win
 

 With these same leaves that lie herein.

===Chinese===
> 正当乘着铁道之车疾驶而过，
 
 我们匆匆掠过一处佳美之宅：
 
 干草之间那明丽的花园，
 
 路上那黄色的禾车，
 
 就食之人，那掠过的长风
 
 卷起轻柔禾束，自沐日甘美之禾堆——
 
 灰色山墙，苍然屋顶，
 
 方才犹在眼前——转瞬已远在天边。
 
 尔时我等何等切切欲停留，
 
 欲于其甜美之中度过此日，
 
 欲坐于其流转之荫下，
 
 觉我自身亦为其一分。
 
 此般歇息，此般停留，我曾力求以得，
 
 所凭惟此册中所藏之数叶而已。

## VIII Face-of-God Cometh Home Again to Burgstead / 八 面神重归堡镇

===Original===
Face-of-god went back through the wood by the way he had come, paying little heed to the things about him. For whatever he thought of strayed not one whit from the image of the Fair Woman of the Mountainside.

He went through the wood swiftlier than yesterday, and made no stay for noon or aught else, nor did he linger on the road when he was come into the Dale, either to speak to any or to note what they did. So he came to the House of the Face about dusk, and found no man within the hall either carle or queen. So he cried out on the folk, and there came in a damsel of the house, whom he greeted kindly and she him again. He bade her bring the washing-water, and she did so and washed his feet and his hands. She was a fair maid enough, as were most in the Dale, but he heeded her little; and when she was done he kissed not her cheek for her pains, as his wont was, but let her go her ways unthanked. But he went to his shut-bed and opened his chest, and drew fair raiment from it, and did off his wood-gear, and did on him a goodly scarlet kirtle fairly broidered, and a collar with gems of price therein, and other braveries. And when he was so attired he came out into the hall, and there was old Stone-face standing by the hearth, which was blazing brightly with fresh brands, so that things were clear to see.

===Chinese===
面神循来路穿过林莽归去，沿途事物全不留心。盖因他心之所思，丝毫不能偏离那山颜美妇人（the Fair Woman of the Mountainside）的影像。

这一日穿林较昨日更为迅疾，正午亦不停歇，余事更不必论；及至入了堡谷，路上亦不逗留，既不与任何人搭话，亦不察看他人所务。约近黄昏时分，他回到面神之宅，厅中空无一人，无论男女。他便高声呼唤仆从，有一侍女入内，他和颜以待，侍女亦还礼。他命她取盥洗之水来，侍女依言，为他洗足、洗手。此女容貌颇为姣好——堡谷中女子多半如此——他却几乎未曾留意；侍女侍奉既毕，他竟不如往常那般吻她脸颊以酬其劳，连谢也不谢一声，便任她自去。他自己却走到封闭木榻卧间，打开箱箧，自内取出华美衣裳，脱下林中行装，换上一件绣工精美之大红长袍，又戴上一条嵌有珍贵宝石之项圈，并其他诸般华饰。装束既毕，他步出厅堂，只见老石面正立于炉畔，炉中新柴烈焰熊熊，照得满室通明。

===Original===
Stone-face noted Gold-mane's gay raiment, for he was not wont to wear such attire, save on the feasts and high days when he behoved to. So the old man smiled and said:

"Welcome back from the Wood! But what is it? Hast thou been wedded there, or who hath made thee Earl and King?"

Said Face-of-god: "Foster-father, sooth it is that I have been to the wood, but there have I seen nought of manfolk worse than myself. Now as to my raiment, needs must I keep it from the moth. And I am weary withal, and this kirtle is light and easy to me. Moreover, I look to see the Bride here again, and I would pleasure her with the sight of gay raiment upon me."

"Nay," said Stone-face, "hast thou not seen some woman in the wood arrayed like the image of a God? and hath she not bidden thee thus to worship her tonight? For I know that such wights be in the wood, and that such is their wont."

Said Gold-mane: "I worship nought save the Gods and the Fathers. Nor saw I in the wood any such as thou sayest."

===Chinese===
石面留心到金鬃这一身华服——他平日并不穿这等衣裳，唯有节庆大日理当穿着之时方才一著。于是老人含笑说道：

"自林中归来，欢迎欢迎！可这是怎么一回事？你在那边成了亲么，还是有谁封你作了伯爵与国王？"

面神道："义父，我确是去了林中，但在那边并未遇见什么比我更险恶之人。至于这身衣裳嘛，总须拿出来晾一晾，免为蠹虫所蛀。况且我亦疲倦，这件长袍于我轻便舒适。再者，我盼着新娘今夜再来此间，愿以一身华服博她一欢。"

"不然，"石面道，"你莫非在林中遇见了什么女子，衣饰如同神像一般？她岂不是命你今夜如此供奉她么？盖因我深知林中确有这等精怪，而此乃其惯技。"

金鬃道："我所崇奉者，唯诸神与列祖而已。林中亦未见你所言那等人物。"

===Original===
Therewith Stone-face shook his head; but after a while he said:

"Art thou for the wood tomorrow?"

"Nay," said Gold-mane angrily, knitting his brows.

"The morrow of tomorrow," said Stone-face, "is the day when we look to see the Westland merchants: after all, wilt thou not go hence with them when they wend their ways back before the first snows fall?"

"Nay," said he, "I have no mind to it, fosterer; cease egging me on hereto."

Then Stone-face shook his head again, and looked on him long, and muttered: "To the wood wilt thou go tomorrow or next day; or some day when doomed is thine undoing."

===Chinese===
说罢石面摇了摇头；过一会儿又道：

"你明日还要去林中么？"

"不去，"金鬃怒道，双眉紧皱。

"明日之后那一日，"石面道，"便是我们盼望西土商人（Westland merchants）到来之日：说到底，待他们初雪降前启程归去之时，你难道不与他们一同离此而去么？"

"不，"他道，"我无意于此，义父；休要再怂恿我。"

于是石面又摇了摇头，久久凝视着他，喃喃道："明日也好，后日也好，你总要再去林中；要不然，便是你劫数已到的那一日。"

===Original===
Therewith entered the service and torches, and presently after came the Alderman with Hall-face; and Iron-face greeted his son and said to him: "Thou hast not hit the time to do on thy gay raiment, for the Bride will not be here tonight; she bideth still at the Feast at the Apple-tree House: or wilt thou be there, son?"

"Nay," said Face-of-god, "I am overweary. And as for my raiment, it is well; it is for thine honour and the honour of the name."

So to table they went, and Iron-face asked his son of his ways again, and whether he was quite fixed in his mind not to go down to the Plain and the Cities: "For," said he, "the morrow of tomorrow shall the merchants be here, and this were great news for them if the son of the Alderman should be their faring-fellow back."

But Face-of-god answered without any haste or heat: "Nay, father, it may not be: fear not, thou shalt see that I have a good will to work and live in the Dale."

And in good sooth, though he was a young man and loved mirth and the ways of his own will, he was a stalwarth workman, and few could mow a match with him in the hay-month and win it; or fell trees as certainly and swiftly, or drive as straight and clean a furrow through the stiff land of the lower Dale; and in other matters also was he deft and sturdy.

===Chinese===
正说间，仆役执火炬鱼贯而入，俄顷长老偕厅面亦至；铁面问候其子，对他说道："你这身华服穿得不是时候，新娘今夜不来此间；她尚在苹果树之宅（the Apple-tree House）的宴席上未散：儿啊，你莫非也要去那边么？"

"不去，"面神道，"我太过疲倦。至于我这身衣裳，倒也无妨；这是为你的体面，也是为家族名声的体面。"

于是众人入席。铁面又问其子近来行止，问他是否当真下定决心不下平原、不入诸城："盖因，"他说，"明日之后那一日商人便到此地，若长老之子肯做他们归程的同路人，于他们实乃天大的喜讯。"

面神却不慌不忙、不愠不怒地答道："父亲，不可如此：你放心，你将看到我有心于堡谷之中劳作、安居。"

且说句实在话，他虽年少之人、性好游乐任性，却是一把干活的好手：割草之月能与他比试镰刀而取胜者寥寥无几；伐木亦少有人能如他那般稳当利落；在堡谷下端那片硬土上犁田，也少有人能如他那般犁出又直又净的沟垄；至于旁的活计，他亦无一不巧、无一不强健。

## XXII Face-of-God Cometh Home to Burgstead / 二十二 面神归堡镇

===Original===
But Face-of-god with Bow-may and Wood-wise fared over the waste, going at first alongside the cliffs of the Shivering Flood, and then afterwards turning somewhat to the west. They soon had to climb a very high and steep bent going up to a mountain-neck; and the way over the neck was rough indeed when they were on it, and they toiled out of it into a barren valley, and out of the valley again on to a rough neck; and suchlike their journey the day long, for they were going athwart all those great dykes that went from the ice-mountains toward the lower dales like the outspread fingers of a hand or the roots of a great tree. And the ice-mountains they had on their left hands and whiles at their backs.

They went very warily, with their bows bended and spear in hand, but saw no man, good or bad, and but few living things. At noon they rested in a valley where was a stream, but no grass, nought but stones and sand; but where they were at least sheltered from the wind, which was mostly very great in these high wastes; and there Bow-may drew meat and wine from a wallet she bore, and they ate and drank, and were merry enough; and Bow-may said:

===Chinese===
且说面神与弓娥（Bow-may）、林智（Wood-wise）一同越过荒原，起初沿战栗川（the Shivering Flood）之崖而行，继而稍向西转。不多时便须攀上一道极高极陡的坡，直上一道山颈；那山颈之上的路一旦踏上去，便崎岖异常；他们好容易翻过山颈，进入一片荒谷，又出荒谷、再上一道崎岖山颈；如此这般，竟是一整日的路程——原来他们一路横切那些巨大的山脊，那些山脊自冰山蜿蜒而下、直趋下方诸谷，犹如一只张开五指的手掌，又如一棵大树的根须。冰山一路在他们的左手边，有时又转至身后。

三人一路十分戒备，弓上弦、枪在手，然而无论善恶，连一个人影也未曾撞见，活物也不过寥寥。正午时分，他们在一条有溪流的谷中歇息，那里没有一根草，唯有碎石与沙砾；但至少可以遮风——这些高处荒原之上，风往往极大。弓娥从随身的褡裢里取出酒肉，三人吃喝一通，倒也快活；弓娥说道：

===Original===
“I would I were going all the way with thee, Gold-mane; for I long sore to let my eyes rest a while on the land where I shall one day live.”

“Yea,” said Face-of-god, “art thou minded to dwell there? We shall be glad of that.”

“Whither are thy wits straying?” said she; “whether I am minded to it or not, I shall dwell there.”

And Wood-wise nodded a yea to her. But Face-of-god said:

“Good will be thy dwelling; but wherefore must it be so?”

Then Wood-wise laughed and said: “I shall tell thee in fewer words than she will, and time presses now: Wood-father and Wood-mother, and I and my two brethren and this woman have ever been about and anigh the Sun-beam; and we deem that war and other troubles have made us of closer kin to her than we were born, whether ye call it brotherhood or whatnot, and never shall we sunder from her in life or in death. So when thou goest to Burgdale with her, there shall we be.”

Then was Face-of-god glad when he found that they deemed his wedding so settled and sure; but Wood-wise fell to making ready for the road. And Face-of-god said to him:

“Tell me one thing, Wood-wise; that whoop that thou gavest forth when we were at handy-strokes e’en now—is it but a cry of thine own or is it of thy Folk, and shall I hear it again?”

“Thou may’st look to hear it many a time,” said Wood-wise, “for it is the cry of the Wolf. Seldom indeed hath battle been joined where men of our blood are, but that cry is given forth. Come now, to the road!”

===Chinese===
"我恨不得与你同行一路，金鬃（Gold-mane）；因为我太想让我这双眼睛，在你那一日将要居住的土地上歇息片刻了。"

面神道："是了，你是有意要迁居到那里去么？那我们可高兴。"

她道："你的心思飞到哪里去了？不管我有意无意，我总归是要住在那里的。"

林智朝她点头称是。面神却道：

"你们住过去，那是好事；可是为何非如此不可呢？"

林智便笑道："我用比她更少的话告诉你吧，眼下时候紧：林父（Wood-father）、林母（Wood-mother），还有我和我两个兄弟，以及这位女子，一向都在日光（Sun-beam）身前身后；我们觉得，战争和种种患难，已使我们与她比生来更近了一层——你唤它作兄弟之情也好，随你怎么说——生死我们都不与她分离。所以你随她往堡谷（Burgdale）去时，我们也要在那里。"

面神见他们竟把他这桩亲事看得如此笃定、如此十拿九稳，心里自是欢喜；林智却已着手打点行装。面神对他道：

"你且告诉我一件事，林智；方才我们短兵相接之时，你高声喊出的那一声呼哨——是你自家的喊法呢，还是你们一族都这么喊？我日后还能再听见么？"

"你日后有的是听的，"林智道，"因为那是狼之呼号。但凡有我们血脉之人参与交锋，这一声几乎从未少过。来吧，上路！"

===Original===
So they went their ways and the road worsened upon them, and toilsome was the climbing up steep bents and the scaling of doubtful paths in the cliff-sides, so that the journey, though the distance of it were not so long to the fowl flying, was much eked out for them, and it was not till near nightfall that they came on the ghyll of the Weltering Water some six miles above Burgstead. Forsooth Wood-wise said that the way might be made less toilsome though far longer by turning back eastward a little past the vale where they had rested at midday; and that seemed good to Gold-mane, in case they should be wending hereafter in a great company between Burgdale and Shadowy Vale.

But now those two went with Face-of-god down a path in the side of the cliff whereby him-seemed he had gone before; and they came down into the ghyll and sat down together on a stone by the waterside, and Face-of-god spake to them kindly, for he deemed them good and trusty faring-fellows.

“Bow-may,” said he, “thou saidst a while ago that thou wouldst be fain to look on Burgdale; and indeed it is fair and lovely, and ye may soon be in it if ye will. Ye shall both be more than welcome to the house of my father, and heartily I bid you thither. For night is on us, and the way back is long and toilsome and beset with peril. Sister Bow-may, thou wottest that it would be a sore grief to me if thou camest to any harm, and thou also, fellow Wood-wise. Daylight is a good faring-fellow over the waste.”

Said Bow-may: “Thou art kind, Gold-mane, and that is thy wont, I know; and fain were I tonight of the candles in thine hall. But we may not tarry; for thou wottest how busy we be at home; and Sun-beam needeth me, if it were only to make her sure that no Dusky Man is bearing off thine head by its lovely locks. Neither shall we journey in the mirk night; for look you, the moon yonder.”

===Chinese===
于是三人上路，路愈发难行，攀陡坡、登崖壁间那些吉凶难料的险径，无不艰辛；因此这一程路，虽说飞禽掠空而过并不算远，于他们却足足绕长了许多，直到将近日落，方才抵达翻滚河（the Weltering Water）的一道深涧——已在堡镇之上约六英里处。林智倒说，这条路若从他们正午歇息的那条谷再向东回转少许，虽远了许多，却没那么辛苦；金鬃觉得此言有理——以备日后他们大队人马在堡谷与幽谷（Shadowy Vale）之间往来行走。

如今那两人随面神沿崖壁间一条小径而下——面神仿佛觉得自己从前曾走过此路；三人下到涧底，在溪边一块石头上并肩坐下，面神好言相待——他觉得这二人乃是又好又靠得住的旅伴。

"弓娥，"他道，"你方才说巴不得瞧一瞧堡谷；那地方果然秀美可人，你们只要愿意，少刻便到。我父之宅，你二人去作客再欢迎不过，我诚心邀你们过去。夜色已至，回路漫长艰险、祸患重重。弓娥妹子，你是知道的，你若有个三长两短，我心里要多难过有多难过，林智兄弟也是一样。白昼才是过荒原的好旅伴。"

弓娥道："你这人就是心善，金鬃，我知道你向来如此；今夜你厅上点起的烛光，我也很想凑一份。可我们不能再耽搁了；你晓得家里有多少事要忙；日光缺不得我，哪怕只为叫她放心：没有一个黝暗人（Dusky Man）正揪着你那头可爱鬈发提着你的脑袋跑呢。再者我们也不在漆黑夜里赶路；你瞧，那边的月亮。"

===Original===
“Well,” said Face-of-god, “parting is ill at the best, and I would I could give you twain a gift, and especially to thee, my sister Bow-may.”

Said Wood-wise: “Thou may’st well do that; or at least promise the gift; and that is all one as if we held it in our hands.”

“Yea,” said Bow-may, “Wood-wise and I have been thinking in one way belike; and I was at point to ask a gift of thee.”

“What is it?” said Gold-mane. “Surely it is thine, if it were but a guerdon for thy good shooting.”

She laughed and handled the skirts of his hauberk as she said:

“Show us the dint in thine helm that the steel axe made this morning.”

“There is no such great dint,” said he; “my father forged that helm, and his work is better than good.”

“Yea,” said Bow-may, “and might I have hauberk and helm of his handiwork, and Wood-wise a good sword of the same, then were I a glad woman, and this man a happy carle.”

Said Gold-mane: “I am well pleased at thine asking, and so shall Iron-face be when he heareth of thine archery; and how that Hall-face were now his only son but for thy close shooting. But now must I to the way; for my heart tells me that there may have been tidings in Burgstead this while I have been aloof.”

So they rose all three, and Bow-may said:

“Thou art a kind brother, and soon shall we meet again; and that will be well.”

Then he put his hands on her shoulders and kissed both her cheeks; and he kissed Wood-wise, and turned and went his ways, threading the stony tangle about the Weltering Water, which was now at middle height, and running clear and strong; so turning once he beheld Wood-wise and Bow-may climbing the path up the side of the ghyll, and Bow-may turned to him also and waved her bow as token of farewell. Then he went upon his way, which was rough enough to follow by night, though the moon was shining brightly high aloft. Yet as he knew his road he made but little of it all, and in somewhat more than an hour and a half was come out of the pass into the broken ground at the head of the Dale, and began to make his way speedily under the bright moonlight toward the Gate, still going close by the water. But as he went he heard of a sudden cries and rumour not far from him, unwonted in that place, where none dwelt, and where the only folk he might look to see were those who cast an angle into the pools and eddies of the Water. Moreover, he saw about the place whence came the cries torches moving swiftly hither and thither; so that he looked to hear of new tidings, and stayed his feet and looked keenly about him on every side; and just then, between his rough path and the shimmer of the dancing moonlit water, he saw the moon smite on something gleaming; so, as quietly as he could, he got his target on his arm, and shortened his spear in his right hand, and then turned sharply toward that gleam. Even therewith up sprang a man on his right hand, and then another in front of him just betwixt him and the water; an axe gleamed bright in the moon, and he caught a great stroke on his target, and therewith drave his left shoulder straight forward, so that the man before him fell over into the water with a mighty splash; for they were at the very edge of the deepest eddy of the Water. Then he spun round on his heel, heeding not that another stroke had fallen on his right shoulder, yet ill-aimed, and not with the full edge, so that it ran down his byrny and rent it not. So he sent the thrust of his spear crashing through the face and skull of the smiter, and looked not to him as he fell, but stood still, brandishing his spear and crying out, “For the Burg and the Face! For the Burg and the Face!”

===Chinese===
"也好，"面神道，"离别之事，再好也是难堪；我恨不得送你二人一件礼物，尤其是你，弓娥妹子。"

林智道："这你大可做得到；至少可以先把礼物许下；那与我们已拿在手里，原是一样。"

"正是，"弓娥道，"林智和我怕是一条心；我正要向你讨一件礼物呢。"

"什么？"金鬃道。"只要你说出口，便是你的，哪怕只算你射得好箭的一份赏钱。"

她笑了起来，一面伸手摸了摸他锁子甲的下摆，道：

"给我们瞧瞧你头盔上今早那柄钢斧砍出的凹痕。"

"凹得并不怎样深，"他道，"这顶盔是我父亲打造的，他的活计比'好'还好。"

"是啊，"弓娥道，"若是能得他亲手打造一副锁子甲和一顶盔给我，再给林智一口好剑，也是同一手艺，那我这女子可就快活了，这条汉子也欢喜了。"

金鬃道："你这一讨，我满心欢喜，铁面（Iron-face）听见你那射术也要欢喜；还要多亏你那一箭射得准，否则厅面（Hall-face）如今便是他仅存的独子了。可现在我得赶路了；我心底有个预感，我离堡镇的这些时日，镇上怕是出了什么消息。"

三人一齐起身，弓娥道：

"你是个好兄长，我们不久便可再见；那是好事。"

于是他两手按住她双肩，吻了她两颊；又吻了林智，转身而去，一路穿过翻滚河一带乱石丛生的纠缠之地——河水此时正值中水位，流得清而有力；他回头一望，只见林智与弓娥正攀上涧壁的小径，弓娥也回过头来，挥了挥手中的弓作别。他继续赶路，那路夜里走起来够崎岖的，虽说一轮明月高高悬于天上。然他既认得路，这些都不在话下，一个半小时多一点，便已穿过隘口，踏入谷首那片高低破碎的地面，在皎洁月色之下，紧贴河岸，疾向堡门而去。正走之间，忽然听见离自己不远传来叫喊与嘈杂之声，此地素无人居，殊不寻常——这地方平日所能指望见到的，不过是些在水潭漩涡边垂钓之人。况且他看见那叫喊之处，有火把四面飞快地来回移动；他便料定必有新的消息，于是收住脚步，机警地四下张望；就在此时，在他那条崎岖小径与波光粼粼的月下流水之间，他望见月光击在一样闪闪发亮的东西上；他便尽可能悄悄地将圆盾套上左臂，右手将长枪握短，随即猛地转向那道闪光之处。就在此时，他右手边跃起一人，前方水边又冒出一人，正拦在他与河水之间；一柄斧头在月光下亮得耀眼，他一盾挡住狠狠劈来的一斧，随即左肩直顶向前，面前那人扑通一声翻进水里——原来他们正站在全河最深那道漩涡的边沿上。他猛地旋身，不顾又一斧已落在自己右肩——那一斧却未砍准，又非以全刃落下，故而顺着锁子甲滑了下去，未曾砍破。他一枪刺出，正中那挥斧之人的面门与头骨，直贯而入，也不看那人倒下，只立定身躯，挥舞长枪，高声呼喊："为堡、为面！为堡、为面！"

===Original===
No other foe came against him, but like to the echo of his cry rose a clear shout not far aloof, “For the Face, for the Face! For the Burg and the Face!” He muttered, “So ends the day as it begun,” and shouted loud again, “For the Burg and the Face!” And in a minute more came breaking forth from the stone-heaps into the moonlit space before the water the tall shapes of the men of Burgstead, the red torchlight and the moonlight flashing back from their war-gear and weapons; for every man had his sword or spear in hand.

Hall-face was the first of them, and he threw his arms about his brother and said: “Well met, Gold-mane, though thou comest amongst us like Stone-fist of the Mountain. Art thou hurt? With whom hast thou dealt? Where be they? Whence comest thou?”

“Nay, I am not hurt,” said Face-of-god. “Stint thy questions then, till thou hast told me whom thou seekest with spear and sword and candle.”

“Two felons were they,” said Hall-face, “even such as ye saw lying dead at Wood-grey’s the other day.”

“Then may ye sheathe your swords and go home,” said Gold-mane, “for one lieth at the bottom of the eddy, and the other, thy feet are well-nigh treading on him, Hall-face.”

Then arose a rumour of praise and victory, and they brought the torches nigh and looked at the fallen man, and found that he was stark dead; so they even let him lie there till the morrow, and all turned about toward the Thorp; and many looked on Face-of-god and wondered concerning him, whence he was and what had befallen him. Indeed, they would have asked him thereof, but could not get at him to ask; but whoso could, went as nigh to Hall-face and him as they might, to hearken to the talk between the brothers.

===Chinese===
再无别个敌人上来，然而宛似呼应他那声呼喊一般，离此不远处又响起一声清亮的呐喊："为面！为面！为堡、为面！"他低声道："这一日如何起始，便如何收场。"随即又高呼："为堡、为面！"不到一分钟，堡镇众人高大的身影便从石堆中冲出，奔入水前那片月光之地，红色火光与皎洁月色自他们的甲胄兵器上交相辉映——人人手中都执剑或持枪。

厅面一马当先，张开双臂抱住兄长，道："幸会，金鬃，虽说你像山中的石拳（Stone-fist of the Mountain）那般冷不防插到我们中间来。你受伤没有？你和谁交了手？人在哪里？你从何处来？"

"没有，我未受伤。"面神道。"你且收住这一连串问话，先告诉我，你执剑持枪、举着火把，要找的是谁。"

"是两名恶徒（felons），"厅面道，"就跟前几日你们在林灰（Wood-grey）家所见横尸在地的那两个一个模样。"

"那你们大可收剑回家了，"金鬃道，"因为一个已沉在漩涡底上，另一个——厅面，你的脚几乎就要踩到他身上了。"

顿时响起一片赞叹与胜利之声，众人将火把移近，细看那倒地之人，见他早已气绝；便索性将他留在原处，待明日再理会，一齐转身朝村子（the Thorp）而去；许多人望着面神，心中纳罕：他从何处来，又遭了什么事。他们本想问他，却挤不拢他身前发问；但凡挤得过去的，都尽量靠近厅面与他两兄弟，好偷听兄弟俩的交谈。

===Original===
So as they went along Hall-face did verily ask him whence he came: “For was it not so,” said he, “that thou didst enter into the wood seeking some adventure early in the morning the day before yesterday?”

“Sooth is that,” said Face-of-god, “and I came to Shadowy Vale, and thence am I come this morning.”

Said Hall-face: “I know not Shadowy Vale, nor doth any of us. This is a new word. How say ye, friends, doth any man here know of Shadowy Vale?”

They all said, “Nay.”

Then said Hall-face: “Hast thou been amongst mere ghosts and marvels, brother, or cometh this tale of thy minstrelsy?”

“For all your words,” said Gold-mane, “to that Vale have I been; and, to speak shortly (for I desire to have your tale, and am waiting for it), I will tell thee that I found there no marvels or strange wights, but a folk of valiant men; a folk small in numbers, but great of heart; a folk come, as we be, from the Fathers and the Gods. And this, moreover, is to be said of them, that they are the foes of these felons of whom ye were chasing these twain. And these same Dusky Men of Silverdale would slay them every man if they might; and if we look not to it they will soon be doing the same by us; for they are many, and as venomous as adders, as fierce as bears, and as foul as swine. But these valiant men, who bear on their banner the image of the Wolf, should be our fellows in arms, and they have good will thereto; and they shall show us the way to Silverdale by blind paths, so that we may fall upon these felons while they dwell there tormenting the poor people of the land, and thus may we destroy them as lads a hornet’s nest. Or else the days shall be hard for us.”

The men who hung about them drank in his words greedily. But Hall-face was silent a little while, and then he said: “Brother Gold-mane, these be great tidings. Time was when we might have deemed them but a minstrel’s tale; for Silverdale we know not, of which thou speakest so glibly, nor the Dusky Men, any more than the Shadowy Vale. Howbeit, things have befallen these two last days so strange and new, that putting them together with the murder at Wood-grey’s, and thy words which seem somewhat wild, it may well seem to us that tidings unlooked for are coming our way.”

===Chinese===
于是路上厅面当真问起他从何处来："事情难道不是这样么？"他道，"前日一早，你为寻一场奇遇而入了林子？"

"正是如此，"面神道，"我到了幽谷，今早才从那里动身。"

厅面道："我不知道什么幽谷，我们这里谁也不知道。这倒是头一回听见的词。诸位朋友，你们这里可有人晓得幽谷的？"

众人皆道："不曾晓得。"

厅面又道："兄弟，莫非你与一班鬼魂异事打了一回交道，还是这故事出自你那吟游的口才？"

"随你们怎么说，"金鬃道，"那谷我确确实实是去过了；长话短说吧（因为我更想听你们这边的事，正等着呢），我只告诉你：我在那里没见着什么妖异怪诞之物，倒遇见了一族勇武之人；人数虽少，胆气却大；和我们一样，是祖先与诸神（the Fathers and the Gods）所传的后人。再者，还有一句要说：他们正是你们方才追赶的那两个恶徒所从出那一族的仇敌。银谷（Silverdale）那帮黝暗人恨不得把他们斩尽杀绝；我们若不提防，转眼也要轮到我们头上——他们人多势众，毒如蝮蛇，猛如恶熊，脏如蠢豕。而那一族勇武之人，旗上绣着狼之造像，正该是我们同袍同仇的盟友，他们也极有此意；他们能领我们走隐僻小径直抵银谷，好叫我们趁那帮恶徒盘踞彼处、虐害当地可怜百姓之时，出其不意地杀将过去，犹如孩童之捣马蜂窝，把他们一并了结。否则，我们往后的日子就要难熬了。"

围在他们身边的众人，贪婪地把这番话一字不漏地吞进耳中。厅面却沉默了片刻，才道："金鬃兄弟，这是了不起的大事。换作从前，我们大可把它当作吟游诗人的故事；你口中滔滔讲来的银谷也好、黝暗人也罢，我们一概不知，正如不知什么幽谷一样。然而这两日所发生之事，如此新奇离奇，再连同林灰家那桩命案，加上你这番听来有些骇人的话——我们简直不能不觉得，未曾料到的消息，正向我们这边涌来了。"

===Original===
“Come, then,” said Face-of-god, “give me what thou hast in thy scrip, and trust me, I shall not jeer at thy tale.”

Said Hall-face: “I also will be short with the tale; and that the more, as meseemeth it is not yet done, and that thou thyself shalt share in the ending of it. It was the day before yesterday, that is the day when thou departedst into the woods on that adventure whereof thou shalt one day tell me more, wilt thou not?”

“Yea, in good time,” said Face-of-god.

“Well,” quoth Hall-face, “we went into the woods that day and in the morning, but after sunrise, to the number of a score: we looked to meet a bear and a she-bear with cubs in a certain place; for one of the Woodlanders, a keen hunter, had told us of their lair. Also we were wishful to slay some of the wild-swine, the yearlings, if we might. Therefore, though we had no helms or shields or coats of fence, we had bowshot a plenty, and good store of casting-weapons, besides our wood-knives and an axe or so; and some of us, of whom I was one, bore our battle-swords, as we are wont ever to do, be the foe beast or man.

“Thus armed we went up Wildlake’s Way and came to Carlstead, where half-a-score Woodlanders joined themselves to us, so that we became a band. We went up the half-cleared places past Carlstead for a mile, and then turned east into the wood, and went I know not how far, for the Woodlanders led us by crooked paths, but two hours wore away in our going, till we came to the place where they looked to find the bears. It is a place that may well be noted, for it is unlike the wood round about. There is a close thicket some two furlongs about of thorn and briar and ill-grown ash and oak and other trees, planted by the birds belike; and it stands as it were in an island amidst of a wide-spreading wood-lawn of fine turf, set about in the most goodly fashion with great tall straight-boled oak-trees, that seem to have been planted of set purpose by man’s hand. Yea, dost thou know the place?”

“Methinks I do,” said Gold-mane, “and I seem to have heard the Woodlanders give it a name and call it Boars-bait.”

“That may be,” said Hall-face.

===Chinese===
"那么，"面神道，"你把你袋里的东西拿出来给我吧，信我，我断不会笑话你那番话。"

厅面道："我这故事也要长话短说；况且我看这事尚未了结，它的结局你自己也要有一份。那是在前日，也就是你为一桩奇遇入林的那一日——那一桩，你改日总要把详情细细告诉我，可好？"

"好，待到方便之时。"面神道。

"也罢，"厅面道，"那一日我们入林，时在清晨，日已出而未高，一伙人足二十之数：我们原指望在某处寻一头公熊、一头带崽的母熊；因为林中汉子（Woodlanders）里一个好事的猎手，已将他探得的熊窝告诉了我们。我们还想着，若有可能，也猎几头一岁的小野猪。因此，我们虽未带盔、盾、护身的甲衣，箭矢却带得足足的，投掷的兵刃也颇不少，此外还有林中砍刀和一两柄斧头；我们之中有些人——我也是其中一个——按我们向来不论对手是兽是人都不肯离身的规矩，随身佩着战剑。

"我们这般武装，上野湖径（Wildlake's Way），到汉子镇（Carlstead），又有十名林中汉子加入我们，于是结成一队。我们沿汉子镇以上那些半开垦之地走了一英里，便转东入林，走了多远我不知道——林中汉子领我们走的都是些曲折小径——只在途中耗去了足两个时辰，才到他们要寻熊之处。那地方颇值得记认，因为与四周林地大不相同。有一片密密匝匝的灌木丛，方圆约莫两浪（furlong），尽是荆棘、野蔷薇，以及生得猥琐的白蜡树、橡树之类，多半是鸟雀种下的；这片灌木丛宛如一座小岛，立于一片开阔的林中草场之上，草场细草如茵，四周整整齐齐地长着一圈高大笔直的橡树，那排列竟似出自人手、有意栽种一般。是了，你可知道这地方？"

"我想我知道，"金鬃道，"我还好像听林中汉子给那地方起过名字，唤作野猪饵（Boars-bait）。"

"也许正是。"厅面道。

===Original===
“Well, there we were, the dogs and the men, and we drew nigh the thicket and beset it, and doubted not to find prey therein: but when we would set the dogs at the thicket to enter it, they were uneasy, and would not take up the slot, but growled and turned about this way and that, so that we deemed that they winded some fierce beast at our flanks or backs.

“Even so it was, and fierce enough and deadly was the beast; for suddenly we heard bowstrings twang, and shafts came flying; and Iron-shield of the Upper Dale, who was close beside me, leapt up into the air and fell down dead with an arrow through his back. Then I bethought me in the twinkling of an eye, and I cried out, ‘The foe are on us! take the cover of the tree-boles and be wary! For the Burg and the Face! For the Burg and the Face!’

“So we scattered and covered ourselves with the oak-boles, but besides Iron-shield, who was slain outright, two goodmen were sorely hurt, to wit Bald-face, a man of our house, and Stonyford of the Lower Dale.

“I looked from behind my tree-bole, a great one; and far off down the glades I saw men moving, clad in gay raiment; but nearer to me, not a hundred yards from my cover, I saw an arm clad in scarlet come out from behind a tree-bole, so I loosed at it, and missed not; for straight there tottered out from behind the tree one of those dusky foul-favoured men like to those that were slain by Wood-grey. I had another shaft ready notched, so I loosed and set the shaft in his throat, and he fell.

“Straightway was a yelling and howling about us like the cries of scalded curs, and the oak-wood swarmed thick with these felons rushing on us; for it seems that the man whom I had slain was a chief amongst them, or we judged so by his goodly raiment.

“Methought then our last day was come. What could we do but run together again after we had loosed at a venture, and so withstand them sword and spear in hand? Some fell beneath our shot, but not many, for they came on very swiftly.

“So they fell on us; but for all their fierceness and their numbers they might not break our array, and we slew four and hurt many by sword-hewing and spear-casting and push of spear; and five of us were hurt and one slain by their dart-casting. So they drew off from us a little, and strove to spread out and fall to shooting at us again; but this we would not suffer, but pushed on as they fell back, keeping as close together as we might for the trees. For we said that we would all die together if needs must; and verily the stour was hard.

===Chinese===
"也罢，我们便在那里，人狗俱备，便逼近灌木丛，将其四面合围，深信其中必有猎物；可是当我们要放狗钻进灌木丛时，那些狗却焦躁不安，不肯循踪而进，只管低吼，东张西望地乱转，我们便以为它们在侧翼或身后嗅到了什么猛兽。

"果然如此，那猛兽也够凶够毒；因为猛然间只听弓弦嘣的一响，箭矢飞来；上谷（the Upper Dale）的铁盾（Iron-shield）——他正紧挨着我——猛地腾空而起，又重重摔下，一箭穿透后背，当场毙命。电光石火之间，我心中已有计较，高呼：'敌人来犯！快借树身掩蔽，小心在意！为堡、为面！为堡、为面！'

"我们便四散开来，借橡树身掩蔽，只是除铁盾当场阵亡之外，还有两名壮丁重伤：一个是我们本宅的秃面（Bald-face），一个是下谷（the Lower Dale）的石渡（Stonyford）。

"我藏身的那棵橡树极粗，自树身之后望去，只见远处林间空地上有身披鲜丽衣裳之人影移动；而离我较近处——离我藏身之地不足百码——我瞧见一条裹在猩红衣里的手臂自一棵树身后伸出来，我便放了一箭，未落空；那人当即自树后踉跄而出，正是黝黑丑陋的汉子，与林灰所杀的那一类人一模一样。我早又搭好一支箭，便再一箭，正中其喉，那人便倒了。

"霎时间，四下里呼号惨叫，犹如烫了水的癞皮狗一般；橡林之中密密麻麻全是这帮恶徒，直扑上来；看来我所杀的那人是他们一头首领，至少我们从他那身讲究衣裳上如此推断。

"我心想，今日怕是我们最后一日了。除了乱箭放出一阵之后再合拢一处、以剑以枪硬抗，我们还能怎样？他们之中也有几个中箭倒下，但不多，因为他们扑得太快。

"他们便扑上来；然而尽管凶猛、尽管人多，却冲不开我们的阵势；我们以剑砍、以枪掷、以枪刺，杀了他们四个，伤了许多；我们这边也有五人受伤、一人被他们的飞镖投杀。他们稍退一些，便试图散开，再来放箭；我们却不肯容他们如此，他们一退我们便压上，借着林木之便，尽量紧紧抱成一团。因为我们都拿定主意，若无可避免，便一同死在一处；这一场恶战实是惨烈。

===Original===
