“Yet hearken! In that nick of time rose up a strange cry not far from us, Ha! ha! ha! ha! How-ow-ow! ending like the howl of a wolf, and then another and another and another, till the whole wood rang again.

“At first we deemed that here were come fresh foemen, and that we were undone indeed; but when they heard it, the foemen before us faltered and gave way, and at last turned their backs and fled, and we followed, keeping well together still: thereby the more part of these men escaped us, for they fled wildly here and there from those who bore that cry with them; so we knew that our work was being done for us; therefore we stood, and saw tall men clad in sheep-brown weed running through the glades pursuing those felons and smiting them down, till both fleers and pursuers passed out of our sight like men in a dream, or as when ye roll up a pictured cloth to lay it in the coffer.

“But to Stone-face’s mind those brown-clad men were the Wights of the Wood that be of the Fathers” blood, and our very friends; and when some of us would yet have gone forward and foregathered with them, and followed the chase along with them, Stone-face gainsaid it, bidding us not to run into the arms of a second death, when we had but just escaped from the first. Sooth to say, moreover, we had divers hurt men that needed looking to.

“So what with one thing, what with another, we turned back: but War-cliff’s brother, a tall man, had felled two of those felons with an oak sapling which he had torn from the thicket; but he had not slain them, and by now they were just awakening from their swoon, and were sitting up looking round them with fierce rolling eyes, expecting the stroke, for Raven of Longscree was standing over them with a naked war-sword in his hand. But now that our blood was cool, we were loth to slay them as they lay in our hands; so we bound them and brought them away with us; and our own dead we carried also on such biers as we might lightly make there, and with them three that were so grievously hurt that they might not go afoot, these we left at Carlstead: they were Tardy the Son of the Untamed, and Swan of Bull-meadow, both of the Lower Dale, and a Woodlander, Undoomed to wit. But the dead were Iron-shield aforesaid, and Wool-sark, and the Hewer, a Woodlander.

===Chinese===
"且听！正在这紧要关头，离我们不远之处，忽然响起一种古怪的呼号：哈！哈！哈！哈！嗷——呜——，结尾如狼嗥一般；接着又是一声、又一声、又一声，最后整座林子都震响起来。

"起初我们以为又来了一拨生力之敌，心想这回是真完了；然而前方的敌人一听此声，便踟蹰退却，终于转身败逃，我们便在后面追，仍紧紧抱成一团：正因如此，这帮人倒有大半从我们手下逃脱了——他们被那带着此声之人追得四散乱窜；我们便知道已经有人代我们动手了；于是我们站定，只见一群身着羊褐衣裳的高大汉子穿过一道道林间空地，追赶那帮恶徒，将他们一一砍翻，直到逃的追的都从我们眼前消失，犹如梦中之人，又像卷起一幅画图收进箱子一般。

"然而在石面（Stone-face）看来，那些羊褐衣人乃是林之灵（the Wights of the Wood），与我等同一祖先血脉，是我们真正的朋友；我们之中有人还想上前去与他们相会、一同追击，石面却坚不答应，说我们刚刚逃过一劫，切莫又去自投第二道死路。再者说老实话，我们也有好几个伤员须得照看。

"这么一来二去，我们便折返了：只是战崖（War-cliff）的兄弟——一个高大汉子——已经从灌木丛里连根拔起一棵橡树幼树，抽倒了那两个恶徒；他并未取他们性命，此时他们刚刚从昏迷中醒转，坐起身来，凶眼乱转，四下张望，只等那一刀落下来——长崖的雷文（Raven of Longscree）正手执出鞘的战剑立于其上。可此刻我们血气既冷，便不忍将到手之人就地处决；于是把他们捆了，一并带走；自家的阵亡者也以当地所能草草做成的担架抬上，连同三名伤重不能步行的，一并安置：此三人留在汉子镇——他们是下谷的不驯者之子迟行（Tardy the Son of the Untamed）和公牛甸之天鹅（Swan of Bull-meadow），以及一名林中汉子，名唤未判者（Undoomed）。而死者则是前面说过的铁盾，还有羊衫（Wool-sark），以及一名林中汉子，名唤伐木者（the Hewer）。

===Original===
“So came we sadly at eventide to Burgstead with the two dead Burgdalers, and the captive felons, and the wounded of us that might go afoot; and ye may judge that they of Burgdale and our father deemed these tidings great enough, and wotted not what next should befall. Stone-face would have had those two felons slain there and then; for no true tale could we get out of them, nor indeed any word at all. But the Alderman would not have it so; and he deemed they might serve our turn as hostages if any of our folk should be taken: for one and all we deemed, and still deem, that war is on us and that new folk have gathered on our skirts.

“So the captives were shut up in the red out-bower of our house; and our father was minded that thou mightest tell us somewhat of them when thou wert come home. But about dusk today the word went that they had broken out and gotten them weapons and fled up the Dale; and so it was.

“But tomorrow morning will a Gate-thing be holden, and there it will be looked for of thee that thou tell us a true tale of thy goings. For it is deemed, and it is my deeming especially, that thou may’st tell us more of these men than thou hast yet told us. Is it not so?”

“Yea, surely,” said Gold-mane, “I can make as many words as ye will about it; yet when all is said, it will come to much the same tale as I have already told thee. Yet belike, if ye are minded to take up the sword to defend you, I may tell you in what wise to lay hold on the hilts.”

“And that is well,” said Hall-face, “and no less do I look for of thee. But lo! here are we come to the Gate of the Burg that abideth battle.”

===Chinese===
"于是我们一行在薄暮时分凄然回到堡镇，带着两名堡谷人的尸首、两名被擒的恶徒，还有我们之中尚能步行的伤者；你们可想而知，堡谷众人与我父都视此为天大的事，且不知下一步还会有什么变故。石面本想当下便把那两个恶徒就地正法；因为我们从他们口中问不出半句实话，甚至连一句话也问不出来。然而长老（the Alderman）不允；他以为，倘若我们的人被对方捉去，这两个倒可作人质派上用场：因为我们众人一致觉得——如今仍如此觉得——战事已临头，另有新人已聚到了我们边上。

"于是那两个被擒之人被关在我们宅子的红色外厢里；我父原指望你回家之后，能告诉我们一些他们的来历。可是今日黄昏时分，消息传来，说他们已经破牢而出，夺了兵器，沿谷上游逃去了；果然如此。

"但明日清晨要开一场门前议事（Gate-thing），大家都指望你在那里把你这些日子的行踪如实相告。因为众人以为——我更是如此以为——你关于这帮人，还能告诉我们一些尚未说出口的事。是不是？"

"是，自然，"金鬃道，"你们要我说多少话，我便能说多少话；只是说完之后，仍与我方才所讲大同小异。不过，倘若你们当真有意拔剑自卫，我倒可以告诉你们该怎样握住剑柄。"

"那很好，"厅面道，"我对你所指望的，也正是这些。可瞧！我们已经到了候战之堡（the Burg that abideth battle）的堡门了。"

## V Face-of-God Falls in with Menfolk on the Mountain / 五 面神于山中邂逅众人

===Original===
Now he plodded on steadily, and for a long time the forest changed but little, and of wild things he saw only a few of those that love the close covert. The ground still went up and up, though at whiles were hollows, and steeper bents out of them again, and the half-blind path or slot still led past the close thickets and fallen trees, and he made way without let or hindrance. At last once more the wood began to thin, and the trees themselves to be smaller and gnarled and ill-grown: therewithal the day was waning, and the sky was quite clear again as the afternoon grew into a fair autumn evening.

Now the trees failed altogether, and the slope grown steeper was covered with heather and ling; and looking up, he saw before him quite near by seeming in the clear even (though indeed they were yet far away) the snowy peaks flushed with the sinking sun against the frosty dark-grey eastern sky; and below them the dark rock-mountains, and below these again, and nigh to him indeed, the fells covered with pinewoods and looking like a wall to the heaths he trod.

He stayed a little while and turned his head to look at the way whereby he had come; but that way a swell of the oak-forest hid everything but the wood itself, making a wall behind him as the pinewood made a wall before. There came across him then a sharp memory of the boding words which Stone-face had spoken last night, and he felt as if he were now indeed within the trap. But presently he laughed and said: “I am a fool: this comes of being alone in the dark wood and the dismal waste, after the merry faces of the Dale had swept away my foolish musings of yesterday and the day before. Lo! here I stand, a man of the Face, sword and axe by my side; if death come, it can but come once; and if I fear not death, what shall make me afraid? The Gods hate me not, and will not hurt me; and they are not ugly, but beauteous.”

===Chinese===
且说他稳步趱行，久之森林殊无甚变化，至于走兽，他也只瞧见几只喜藏密荫之类。地势仍是一路攀升，虽间或有低洼之处，复又陡斜而上；那条半隐半现的小径或兽径，仍沿着密丛与倒木穿行而过，他一路行来，并无阻拦。终于林木复又渐疏，树木本身亦变得矮小，虬结畸形：与此同时，日色渐沉，天穹重又澄澈，午后遂化为一个明丽的秋夕。

继而林木尽绝，坡势愈陡，满覆石楠与帚石楠；他抬头望去，只见眼前——在这清明的夕照之中看去似已极近（实则尚远）——那雪峰为西沉之日映得绯红，衬着寒意料峭的深灰东方天穹；雪峰之下是乌黑的岩山，岩山之下——这才是真正离他不远的——则是苍松覆被之山峦，望去宛如一道墙，挡在他所踏的这片石楠荒原之前。

他驻足片刻，回头望去，看来时之路；然而那一头，一道柞林的隆起将林以外一切尽数遮蔽，在他身后成了一道墙，恰如松林在他身前亦成一道墙。于是石面昨夜那番不祥之言忽地锐然涌上心头，他只觉自己如今当真已落入陷阱之中。但他随即笑道："我是个痴人：这都是孤身处于幽暗之林、凄清之野所致——盖因谷中那一张张欢颜，早将我前日、昨日的种种胡思乱想一扫而空，如今离群独行，旧念复萌。看哪！我立于此处，乃面族之汉子，腰悬剑、胯挂斧；死若来寻，不过一死而已；我既不畏死，更有何物能令我惧？诸神并不恨我，亦不害我；它们并不丑陋，乃是华美的。"

===Original===
Therewith he strode on again, and soon came to a place where the ground sank into a shallow valley and the ling gave place to grass for a while, and there were tall old pines scattered about, and betwixt them grey rocks; this he passed through, climbing a steep bent out of it, and the pines were all about him now, though growing wide apart, till at last he came to where they thickened into a wood, not very close, wherethrough he went merrily, singing to himself and swinging his spear. He was soon through this wood, and came on to a wide well-grassed wood-lawn, hedged by the wood aforesaid on three sides, but sloping up slowly toward the black wall of the thicker pinewood on the fourth side, and about half a furlong overthwart and endlong. The sun had set while he was in the last wood, but it was still broad daylight on the wood-lawn, and as he stood there he was ware of a house under the pinewood on the other side, built long and low, much like the houses of the Woodland-Carles, but rougher fashioned and of unhewn trees. He gazed on it, and said aloud to himself as his wont was:

“Marvellous! here is a dwelling of man, scarce a day’s journey from Burgstead; yet have I never heard tell of it: may happen some of the Woodland-Carles have built it, and are on some errand of hunting peltries up in the mountains, or maybe are seeking copper and tin among the rocks. Well, at least let us go see what manner of men dwell there, and if they are minded for a guest tonight; for fain were I of a bed beneath a roof, and of a board with strong meat and drink on it.”

===Chinese===
说罢他大步又向前，不久便行至一处——地势陷作一道浅谷，帚石楠暂让位给青草，散生着几株高大古松，松间杂以灰色岩石；他穿行而过，攀上一道陡坡走出浅谷，此时四周皆是松树，虽株距颇宽，渐渐却愈聚愈密，终成一片林子，林并不甚密，他快活地穿行其中，边走边自哼小曲，手中挥弄着长矛。不多时他便穿过此林，来到一片宽阔、青草丰美之林间草甸，三面为前述之林所围，第四面则缓缓上斜，直抵一片更密松林所成之黑墙，其纵横各约半浪。他穿过最后那片林子时太阳已经落山，然而林间草甸上仍是一片大白昼光；他立于其间，便瞧见对面松林之下有一座屋，长而低矮，形制颇似林中汉子之居屋，只是造得更为粗糙，所用乃是未加斧凿之原木。他凝视片刻，依其惯习，朗声自语道：

"奇哉！此地距堡镇不及一日之程，竟有人居；我却从未听闻：或许是林中汉子中有人在此造屋，为上山猎取皮张之事，又或在岩间寻觅铜与锡。也罢，且过去看看所居者是何等之人，今夜可愿留一客人；盖因我甚盼得一榻于屋檐之下，得一案而有丰美酒肉。"

===Original===
Therewith he set forward, not heeding much that the wood he had passed through was hard on his left hand; but he had gone but twenty paces when he saw a red thing at the edge of the wood, and then a glitter, and a spear came whistling forth, and smote his own spear so hard close to the steel that it flew out of his hand; then came a great shout, and a man clad in a scarlet kirtle ran forth on him. Face-of-god had his axe in his hand in a twinkling, and ran at once to meet his foe; but the man had the hill on his side as he rushed on with a short-sword in his hand. Axe and sword clashed together for a moment of time, and then both the men rolled over on the grass together, and Face-of-god as he fell deemed that he heard the shrill cry of a woman. Now Face-of-god found that he was the nethermost, for if he was strong, yet was his foe stronger; the axe had flown out of his hand also, while the strange man still kept a hold of his short-sword; and presently, though he still struggled all he could, he saw the man draw back his hand to smite with the said sword; and at that nick of time the foeman’s knee was on his breast, his left hand was doubled back behind him, and his right wrist was gripped hard in the stranger’s left hand. Even therewith his ears, sharpened by the coming death, heard the sound of footsteps and fluttering raiment drawing near; something dark came between him and the sky; there was the sound of a great stroke, and the big man loosened his grip and fell off him to one side.

Face-of-god leapt up and ran to his axe and got hold of it; but turning round found himself face to face with a tall woman holding in her hand a stout staff like the limb of a tree. She was calm and smiling, though forsooth it was she who had stricken the stroke and stayed the sword from his throat. His hand and axe dropped down to his side when he saw what it was that faced him, and that the woman was young and fair; so he spake to her and said:

===Chinese===
说罢他便举步向前，也不甚在意刚才所穿之林紧贴他左手；然才行得二十步，便见林边有一抹红，继而一道闪光，一杆长矛嗖然飞出，正中他手中长矛近钢尖处，力大势沉，他矛顿时脱手飞去；继之一声大喝，一个身着猩红短袍之汉子向他扑来。面神顷刻之间便把斧握在手中，立时迎上会敌；然那汉子居高临下，手持短剑冲来。斧与剑只交击了一瞬，二人便一同滚倒在草上，面神在跌倒之际，仿佛听得一声妇人尖锐的呼喝。面神发觉自己被压在下面，因他纵然强壮，对手却更胜一筹；他的斧也已脱手，那陌生汉子却仍紧握短剑；不多时，尽管他拼命挣扎，只见那人抽回手臂，欲以短剑劈下；就在这千钧一发之际，敌人的膝盖压在他胸口，他的左手被反折到身后，右手腕被那人左手死死攥住。恰在此时，他那为将至之死磨得敏锐的耳朵，听得一阵脚步声与衣袂飘拂之声逼近；一团阴影遮在他与天空之间；只听得重重一击之声，那大汉便松了手，歪向一边倒下。

面神一跃而起，奔去拾斧，握在手中；然一转身，却发现自己与一个高挑妇人正面相对，那人手持一根粗壮如树枝之木棍。她神色从容、面带微笑，虽说方才那一击实系她所下、那剑之所以不曾加于他喉间也正是她所阻。待看清面前是何人、又见这妇人年轻貌美，他握斧之手便垂落身侧；于是他向她开口道：

===Original===
“What aileth, maiden? is this man thy foe? doth he oppress thee? shall I slay him?”

She laughed and said: “Thou art openhanded in thy proffers: he might have asked the like concerning thee but a minute ago.”

“Yea, yea,” said Gold-mane, laughing also, “but he asked it not of thee.”

“That is sooth,” she said, “but since thou hast asked me, I will tell thee that if thou slay him it will be my harm as well as his; and in my country a man that taketh a gift is not wont to break the giver’s head with it straightway. The man is my brother, O stranger, and presently, if thou wilt, thou mayst be eating at the same board with him. Or if thou wilt, thou mayst go thy ways unhurt into the wood. But I had liefer of the twain that thou wert in our house tonight; for thou hast a wrong against us.”

===Chinese===
"姑娘，这是怎么了？这汉子是你仇人么？他可欺凌于你？要我杀了他么？"

她笑道："你这般出言便慷慨相许：换作片刻之前，他倒也可以就你问出同一番话来。"

"是极，是极，"金鬃也笑道，"但他并未曾就你问出这话。"

"这倒是实话，"她说，"然你既问了我，我便告诉你：你若杀了他，于他固有大损，于我亦复有损；在我乡里，凡受人之物者，并不曾循例立即以所受之物砸破赠者之头。这汉子是我兄长，外乡客，少顷你若愿意，便可与他同案而食。你若不愿，亦可安然无恙地自去林中。但二者之间，我宁愿你今夜宿于我家；因我们有亏于你。"

===Original===
Her voice was sweet and clear, and she spake the last words kindly, and drew somewhat nigher to Gold-mane. Therewithal the smitten man sat up, and put his hand to his head, and quoth he:

“Angry is my sister! good it is to wear the helm abroad when she shaketh the nut-trees.”

“Nay,” said she, “it is thy luck that thou wert bareheaded, else had I been forced to smite thee on the face. Thou churl, since when hath it been our wont to thrust knives into a guest, who is come of great kin, a man of gentle heart and fair face? Come hither and handsel him self-doom for thy fool’s onset!”

The man rose to his feet and said: “Well, sister, least said, soonest mended. A clout on the head is worse than a woman’s chiding; but since ye have given me one, ye may forbear the other.”

===Chinese===
她声音清甜明亮，末了几句话说得很是和善，并向金鬃略略走近了些。就在此时，那挨了打的汉子坐起身来，伸手摸了摸头，说道：

"我这妹子好生气恼！她摇撼胡桃树的时候，出门在外还是戴头盔为妙。"

"住口，"她说，"算你运气好没戴头盔，否则我非得打在你脸上不可。你这粗坯，我们何时有了把刀子捅进客人身体里的规矩？何况他是名门望族出身，心性温文、容貌俊朗之汉子！过来，为你这场胡乱偷袭，将自断之权（self-doom）交予他！"

那汉子站起身来，说道："罢了，妹子，话越少越好，事好得最快。头上挨一下，可比挨妇人一顿骂还难受；既然你已经给了我前者，那后者便可以免了。"

===Original===
Therewith he drew near to them. He was a very big-made man, most stalwarth, with dark red hair and a thin pointed beard; his nose was straight and fine, his eyes grey and well-opened, but somewhat fierce withal. Yet was he in nowise evil-looking; he seemed some thirty summers old. He was clad in a short scarlet kirtle, a goodly garment, with a hood of like web pulled off his head on to his shoulders: he bore a great gold ring on his left arm, and a collar of gold came down on to his breast from under his hood.

As for the woman, she was clad in a long white linen smock, and over it a short gown of dark blue woollen, and she had skin shoes on her feet.

Now the man came up to Face-of-god, and took his hand and said: “I deemed thee a foe, and I may not have over-many foes alive: but it seems that thou art to be a friend, and that is well and better; so herewith I handsel thee self-doom in the matter of the onslaught.”

===Chinese===
说罢他向二人走近。此人生得极为魁梧，最为雄健，一头暗红发，下巴上一撮尖细之须；鼻梁直而秀挺，两眼灰色、睁得大大，却略带几分凶气。然其相貌绝无凶恶之态；看年纪约莫三十个夏天。他身着一袭猩红短袍，乃是一件华美之衣，同料之风兜自头上褪下，搭在肩上：他左臂戴一只粗大金环，颈间自风兜之下垂下一领金项圈，直抵胸前。

至于那妇人，则内着一袭白色长身亚麻衬衣，外罩一件深蓝毛料短袍，足下一双皮履。

那汉子走到面神跟前，握住他的手，说道："我原当你是个仇敌，而活着的仇敌，我不能任其太多：但看来你将成为一位朋友，这便好，且更好；故而我于此番偷袭之事，将自断之权交予你。"

===Original===
Then Face-of-god laughed and said: “The doom is soon given forth; against the tumble on the grass I set the clout on the head; there is nought left over to pay to any man’s son.”

Said the scarlet-clad man: “Belike by thine eyes thou art a true man, and wilt not bewray me. Now is there no foeman here, but rather maybe a friend both now and in time to come.” Therewith he cast his arms about Face-of-god and kissed him. But Face-of-god turned about to the woman and said: “Is the peace wholly made?”

She shook her head and said soberly: “Nay, thou art too fair for a woman to kiss.”

===Chinese===
面神笑道："裁断立时可下：拿你头上挨的那一下，抵我二人一同滚倒在草上那一跤；此外再无半文该赔给任何人之子。"

那身着猩红袍之汉子道："凭你一双眼睛，想必你是个诚实之人，不会出卖我。此地如今再无仇敌，倒可能是一位朋友，今时、日后皆是。"说罢他便张开双臂，抱住面神，与他亲吻。面神却转身向那妇人道："和好算是全然达成了么？"

她摇了摇头，正色道："不然，你生得这般俊美，妇人若吻你一下，所求岂止于此。"

===Original===
He flushed red, as his wont was when a woman praised him; yet was his heart full of pleasure and well-liking. But she laid her hand on his shoulder and said: “Now is it for thee to choose betwixt the wildwood and the hall, and whether thou wilt be a guest or a wayfarer this night.”

As she touched him there took hold of him a sweetness of pleasure he had never felt erst, and he answered: “I will be thy guest and not thy stranger.”

“Come then,” she said, and took his hand in hers, so that he scarce felt the earth under his feet, as they went all three together toward the house in the gathering dusk, while eastward where the peaks of the great mountains dipped was a light that told of the rising of the moon.

===Chinese===
他顿时涨红了脸，凡有妇人夸他，他向来如此；然他心下却满是欢喜与惬意。她却把手按在他肩上，说道："如今任你抉择：是野林，还是厅堂；今夜你是做客人，还是过路客。"

她这一触，一种前所未有的甜美欢愉便攫住了他，他答道："我愿做你的客人，不作你的生客。"

"那便来吧，"她说，便握住他的手，三人一同向那屋子走去；暮色四合之间，他几乎不觉足下之土。东面那大山群峰低伏之处，一抹微光正预告着月亮将升。

## IV Face-of-God Fareth to the Wood Again / 四 面神再赴林中

===Original===
When it was the earliest morning and dawn was but just beginning, Face-of-god awoke and rose up from his bed, and came forth into the hall naked in his shirt, and stood by the hearth, wherein the piled-up embers were yet red, and looked about and could see nothing stirring in the dimness: then he fetched water and washed the night-tide off him, and clad himself in haste, and was even as he was yesterday, save that he left his bow and quiver in their place and took instead a short casting-spear; moreover he took a leathern scrip and went therewith to the buttery, and set therein bread and flesh and a little gilded beaker; and all this he did with but little noise; for he would not be questioned, lest he should have to answer himself as well as others.

Thus he went quietly out of doors, for the door was but latched, since no bolts or bars or locks were used in Burgstead, and through the town-gate, which stood open, save when rumours of war were about. He turned his face straight towards Wildlake’s Way, walking briskly, but at whiles looking back over his shoulder toward the East to note what way was made by the dawning, and how the sky lightened above the mountain passes.

===Chinese===
最清早，天色方才破晓，面神便即醒转，自榻上起身，只穿一件衬衫便步入厅堂，立于炉畔。炉中余烬堆叠犹红，他四下张望，朦胧之中不见一丝动静：于是取水盥洗，洗去一夜之气，匆匆披挂穿戴，打扮得与昨日一般无二，只是将弓与箭袋留在原处，另取一杆短投枪；又取一只皮囊，去到酒食房中，装入面包、肉食，并一只镀金小杯；凡此种种，皆做得极是轻手轻脚；盖因他不愿被人盘问，免得到时候既要为自己、又要替别人作答。

他便如此悄悄出了门——门只是虚掩着，堡镇之中向不用门闩、横木、铁锁；又穿过城门，城门也是大开着的，除非风闻兵祸将至。他径直面朝野湖径而去，步履轻捷，却时时回头望东，看那晨曦如何推进，山隘之上天色怎样放明。

===Original===
By then he was come to the place where the Maiden Ward was held in the summer the dawn was so far forward that all things had their due colours, and were clear to see in the shadowless day. It was a bright morning, with an easterly air stirring that drave away the haze and dried the meadows, which had otherwise been rimy; for it was cold. Gold-mane lingered on the place a little, and his eyes fell on the road, as dusty yet as in Redesman’s song; for the autumn had been very dry, and the strip of green that edged the outside of the way was worn and dusty also. On the edge of it, half in the dusty road, half on the worn grass, was a long twine of briony red-berried and black-leaved; and right in the midst of the road were two twigs of great-leaved sturdy pollard oak, as though they had been thrown aside there yesterday by women or children a-sporting; and the deep white dust yet held the marks of feet, some bare, some shod, crossing each other here and there. Face-of-god smiled as he passed on, as a man with a happy thought; for his mind showed him a picture of the Bride as she would be leading the Maiden Ward next summer, and singing first among the singers, and he saw her as clearly as he had often seen her verily, and before him was the fashion of her hands and all her body, and the little mark on her right wrist, and the place where her arm whitened, because the sleeve guarded it against the sun, which had long been pleasant unto him, and the little hollow in her chin, and the lock of red-brown hair waving in the wind above her brow, and shining in the sun as brightly as the Alderman’s cunningest work of golden wire. Soft and sweet seemed that picture, till he almost seemed to hear her sweet voice calling to him, and desire of her so took hold of the youth, that it stirred him up to go swiftlier as he strode on, the day brightening behind him.

Now was it nigh sunrise, and he began to meet folk on the way, though not many; since for most their way lay afield, and not towards the Burg. The first was a Woodlander, tall and gaunt, striding beside his ass, whose panniers were laden with charcoal. The carle’s daughter, a little maiden of seven winters, riding on the ass’s back betwixt the panniers, and prattling to herself in the cold morning; for she was pleased with the clear light in the east, and the smooth wide turf of the meadows, as one who had not often been far from the shadow of the heavy trees of the wood, and their dark wall round about the clearing where they dwelt. Face-of-god gave the twain the sele of the day in merry fashion as he passed them by, and the sober dark-faced man nodded to him but spake no word, and the child stayed her prattle to watch him as he went by.

Then came the sound of the rattle of wheels, and, as he doubled an angle of the rock-wall, he came upon a wain drawn by four dun kine, wherein lay a young woman all muffled up against the cold with furs and cloths; beside the yoke-beasts went her man, a well-knit trim-faced Dalesman clad bravely in holiday raiment, girt with a goodly sword, bearing a bright steel helm on his head, in his hand a long spear with a gay red and white shaft done about with copper bands. He looked merry and proud of his wain-load, and the woman was smiling kindly on him from out of her scarlet and fur; but now she turned a weary happy face on Gold-mane, for they knew him, as did all men of the Dale.

===Chinese===
待他走到夏日里举行少女仪（the Maiden Ward）的那处地方时，天已大明，万物各还其本色，在无影的晨光中清晰可见。那是个晴朗的早晨，东风习习，驱散薄雾，吹干草甸——否则草甸上本该凝着一层白霜；因为天气很冷。金鬃在那地方稍作徘徊，目光落到路上——果然仍如雷德斯曼（Redesman）歌中所唱的那般尘土飞扬；原来这个秋天干旱得很，路边外侧那一道绿草带也已被踏得斑驳、积满尘土。路缘之上，半在尘土之路、半在践踏之草间，缠绕着一长缕牛尾菜，红果黑叶；路正中则横着两大枝阔叶壮实的截头柞枝，好像是昨日妇孺嬉戏时随手抛在那里的；厚厚的白尘上还留着脚印，有的赤足、有的穿履，处处交错。面神一路走过，不禁微微含笑，犹如心中生出一个愉快的念头；原来他心里浮现出一幅图景：新娘明年夏天领着少女仪的队伍、在众歌者之中领唱的模样；他看得清清楚楚，就像他平日里常真切见到她那样——她双手的姿态、全身的体段、右腕上那颗小痣、衣袖遮日因而格外白皙的那段小臂（这景致久已令他心悦）、下巴上那个小酒窝、额前在风中飘动的那缕赤褐色发丝，在阳光下亮得如同长老手艺最精的金丝之作。那图景温柔而甜蜜，他几乎仿佛听得她甜美的声音在唤他；对她的渴慕如此攫住这少年，催着他大步流星越走越快，身后天色也越走越亮。

其时将近日出，他开始在路上遇见行人，虽则不多；因为大多数人的路在田间，并不朝向山堡。第一个遇见的是个林中之民，瘦高个儿，大步走在一头驴旁，驴两边驮篮里满满装着炭。那汉子的女儿，一个七岁的小丫头，骑在驴背上、夹在两只驮篮之间，在清冷的早晨自顾自地呀呀呢喃；她见了东边那一片清明天光、那一平如砥的广阔草甸，满心欢喜——她是个不常远离林中那些沉重树影、远离环绕他们居所空地那道黑墙的孩子。面神走过他们父女俩身边时，快快活活地向二人道了日安；那面色黝黑、神色凝重的汉子朝他点了点头，却不出声；那孩子倒停了喃喃，看着他走过去。

接着传来车轮辚辚之声，他绕过石墙一角，便撞见一辆由四头灰褐之牛拉的大车，车中躺着一位少妇，为御寒用裘皮和布帛将自头到脚裹得严严实实；驾辕的牛旁走着她的汉子，一个体格结实、眉目清秀的谷民，一身节日盛装，打扮得颇为神气，腰间佩一口好剑，头戴亮钢盔，手执一杆长枪，枪杆红白相间、甚是鲜亮，外箍铜箍。他满脸喜气、以车中人为傲，那妇人从一身猩红裘皮之中含笑温颜望着他；这时她却把一张疲惫而幸福的脸转向金鬃——他们认得他，全谷之人都认得他。

===Original===
So he stopped when they met, for the goodman had already stayed his slow beasts, and the goodwife had risen a little on her cushions to greet him, yet slowly and but a little, for she was great with child, and not far from her time. That knew Gold-mane well, and what was toward, and why the goodman wore his fine clothes, and why the wain was decked with oak-boughs and the yoke-beasts with their best gilded bells and copper-adorned harness. For it was a custom with many of the kindreds that the goodwife should fare to her father’s house to lie in with her first babe, and the day of her coming home was made a great feast in the house. So then Face-of-god cried out: “Hail to thee, O Warcliff! Shrewd is the wind this morning, and thou dost well to heed it carefully, this thine orchard, this thy garden, this thy fair apple-tree! To a good hall thou wendest, and the Wine of Increase shall be sweet there this even.”

Then smiled Warcliff all across his face, and the goodwife hung her head and reddened. Said the goodman: “Wilt thou not be with us, son of the Alderman, as surely thy father shall be?”

“Nay,” said Face-of-god, “though I were fain of it: my own matters carry me away.”

===Chinese===
于是相遇之时他便停下，那汉子早已勒住迟缓的牛，那妇人也在软垫上略略欠身招呼他——只是缓缓欠了欠，因为腹中已是沉重，临盆之日不远。这事金鬃心里明白得很：他知道正有什么事要发生，知道那汉子为何穿戴齐整，知道车为何用橡枝装饰、驾辕的牛为何挂上最好的镀金铃铛、套上铜饰辔头。原来许多氏族都有这么个习俗：妇人头胎将养，要回娘家去坐蓐；归宁之日，家中便大排筵席。于是面神扬声道："战崖（Warcliff），你好啊！今晨风头凌厉，你这般悉心护着她，做得对——你这片果园，这座花园，这棵佳美的苹果树！你去的是一座好厅堂，今夕那增衍酒（the Wine of Increase）在那儿定是甘美的。"

战崖听了，满脸绽出笑容，那妇人则垂首红了脸。那汉子道："长老之子，你父定然会来，你难道不来么？"

"不去，"面神道，"虽则我很想赴席：我自家的事将我带往他处。"

===Original===
“What matters?” said Warcliff; “perchance thou art for the cities this autumn?”

Face-of-god answered somewhat stiffly: “Nay, I am not;” and then more kindly, and smiling, “All roads lead not down to the Plain, friend.”

“What road then farest thou away from us?” said the goodwife.

“The way of my will,” he answered.

===Chinese===
"什么事？"战崖问，"莫非今秋你要往诸城去？"

面神答得有几分生硬："并不。"继而语气缓和下来，含笑道，"朋友，条条大路并不尽通平原。"

"那你走哪条路离我们而去呢？"那妇人问。

"随我心意之路。"他答。

===Original===
“And what way is that?” said she; “take heed, lest I get a longing to know. For then must thou needs tell me, or deal with the carle there beside thee.”

“Nay, goodwife,” said Face-of-god, “let not that longing take thee; for on that matter I am even as wise as thou. Now good speed to thee and to the newcomer!”

Therewith he went close up to the wain, and reached out his hand to her, and she gave him hers and he kissed it, and so went his ways smiling kindly on them. Then the carle cried to his kine, and they bent down their heads to the yoke; and presently, as he walked on, he heard the rumble of the wain mingling with the tinkling of their bells, which in a little while became measured and musical, and sounded above the creaking of the axles and the rattle of the gear and the roll of the great wheels over the road: and so it grew thinner and thinner till it all died away behind him.

===Chinese===
"那是什么路？"她道，"当心些，莫惹得我非要打听不可。到那时你不告诉我也不成，否则就要与身边那汉子理论一番。"

"不至于此，大嫂，"面神道，"你且莫生那心思；那一桩事上，我所知并不比你多。愿你一路顺遂，也祝那位将至的小客人平安！"

说罢便走到大车跟前，伸手向她；她也将手伸来，他低头一吻，便含笑向二人告辞而去。那汉子一声吆喝，几头牛便低头承辕；面神一路前行，不多时便听见大车的辚辚声与铃铛的叮当声混作一处，渐渐变得齐整而有韵律，盖过了车轴的吱呀、挽具的碰撞、大轮在路上的滚动之声：那声响越来越细，终于在他身后渐渐消隐。

===Original===
He was now come to where the river turned away from the sheer rock-wall, which was not so high there as in most other places, as there had been in old time long screes from the cliff, which had now grown together, with the waxing of herbs and the washing down of the earth on to them, and made a steady slope or low hill going down riverward. Over this the road lifted itself above the level of the meadows, keeping a little way from the cliffs, while on the other side its bank was somewhat broken and steep here and there. As Face-of-god came up to one of these broken places, the sun rose over the eastern pass, and the meadows grew golden with its long beams. He lingered, and looked back under his hand, and as he did so heard the voices and laughter of women coming up from the slope below him, and presently a young woman came struggling up the broken bank with hand and knee, and cast herself down on the roadside turf laughing and panting. She was a long-limbed light-made woman, dark-faced and black-haired: amidst her laughter she looked up and saw Gold-mane, who had stopped at once when he saw her; she held out her hands to him, and said lightly, though her face flushed withal:

“Come hither, thou, and help the others to climb the bank; for they are beaten in the race, and now must they do after my will; that was the forfeit.”

He went up to her, and took her hands and kissed them, as was the custom of the Dale, and said:

===Chinese===
这时他已走到大河折离绝壁之处；此处绝壁不若他处那般高峻，原来古时崖下本有一道道长长的碎石坡，日久天长，草木滋生、泥土冲积其上，遂连成一片，化作一道平缓的山坡或低丘，向河一方倾下。路便自此高出草甸之面，离崖壁不远不近，另一侧的路岸却处处高低崎岖、颇为陡峭。面神走到一处这般崩缺之地时，太阳正从东隘升起，长长光线将草甸染成金黄。他停下脚步，以手遮阳回头一望，正这当口，便听得身下坡上传来妇人说笑之声，旋即一个少妇手脚并用地自崩岸攀爬上来，笑着喘着，扑倒在路边的草皮上。她身长肢长、体态轻盈，面色黝黑、头发乌黑：笑声之中她抬头一见金鬃——金鬃早已看见她、当即站住——她便向他伸出双手，轻佻地说，脸上却同时飞起红晕：

"你过来，帮帮后头那几个爬上岸来；她们赛跑输了，如今须得听我吩咐行事——这便是赌注。"

他走到她跟前，握住她的双手一吻——这是堡谷的礼俗——说道：

===Original===
“Hail to thee, Long-coat! who be they, and whither away this morning early?”

She looked hard at him, and fondly belike, as she answered slowly: “They be the two maidens of my father’s house, whom thou knowest; and our errand, all three of us, is to Burgstead, the Feast of the Wine of Increase which shall be drunk this even.”

As she spake came another woman half up the bank, to whom went Face-of-god, and, taking her hands, drew her up while she laughed merrily in his face: he saluted her as he had Long-coat, and then with a laugh turned about to wait for the third; who came indeed, but after a little while, for she had abided, hearing their voices. Her also Gold-mane drew up, and kissed her hands, and she lay on the grass by Long-coat, but the second maiden stood up beside the young man. She was white-skinned and golden-haired, a very fair damsel, whereas the last-comer was but comely, as were well-nigh all the women of the Dale.

Said Face-of-god, looking on the three: “How comes it, maidens, that ye are but in your kirtles this sharp autumn morning? or where have ye left your gowns or your cloaks?”

===Chinese===
"你好啊，长衣（Long-coat）！她们是谁？一大清早要往哪里去？"

她定定地看着他，眼神中似有几分情意，缓缓答道："她们是我家的两个丫头，你都认得；我们三人此去堡镇，为的是今夕那增衍酒宴。"

她说话间，又一个妇人已爬到半坡；面神走过去，握住她的双手将她拉上来，那妇人当着他的面笑得欢畅：他与她见礼如前，随即笑着转身等候第三人；那人果然也来了，只是稍迟片刻，因为她听见人声便有意在后面磨蹭。金鬃也把她拉上来，吻了她的手，她便在草地上、长衣身旁躺下；而方才第二个爬上来的少女则站在少年身旁。这少女肤白如雪、金发灿灿，是个极美的姑娘；而后到的那位不过清秀而已——堡谷的妇人本就几乎个个都是这般清秀。

面神看着三人道："姑娘们，这么冷的秋天早晨，你们怎么只穿贴身长裙？你们的外袍斗篷都丢到哪里去了？"

===Original===
For indeed they were clad but in close-fitting blue kirtles of fine wool, embroidered about the hems with gold and coloured threads.

The last-comer laughed and said: “What ails thee, Gold-mane, to be so careful of us, as if thou wert our mother or our nurse? Yet if thou must needs know, there hang our gowns on the thorn-bush down yonder; for we have been running a match and a forfeit; to wit, that she who was last on the highway should go down again and bring them up all three; and now that is my day’s work: but since thou art here, Alderman’s son, thou shalt go down instead of me and fetch them up.”

But he laughed merrily and outright, and said: “That will I not, for there be but twenty-four hours in the day, and what between eating and drinking and talking to fair maidens, I have enough to do in every one of them. Wasteful are ye women, and simple is your forfeit. Now will I, who am the Alderman’s son, give forth a doom, and will ordain that one of you fetch up the gowns yourselves, and that Long-coat be the one; for she is the fleetest-footed and ablest thereto. Will ye take my doom? for later on I shall not be wiser.”

===Chinese===
原来她们身上只穿着紧身的蓝色细呢长裙，裙边用金线彩线绣着花纹。

那后到之人笑道："金鬃，你是怎么了，这般操心我们，活像我们的娘或奶娘？不过你既然非要打听——我们的外袍就挂在下面那丛荆棘上；我们方才赛跑赌东道，约好谁最后上到大路，谁就要再下去把三人的袍子都拿上来；如今这便是我今日的活计了：不过既然你这位长老之子在此，就替我下去拿上来吧。"

他却是哈哈一笑，说道："我才不干。一天不过十二个时辰，吃喝之外还要陪美貌姑娘说话，每个时辰我都忙得很。你们妇人家真是糟蹋人力，你们的东道也定得蠢。如今我以长老之子之名下一道判语：你们当中须有一人亲自下去拿袍子，而此人便是长衣；因为她脚程最快、最为能干。你们服不服我的判决？再晚我可也聪明不起来了。"

===Original===
“Yea,” said the fair woman, “not because thou art the Alderman’s son, but because thou art the fairest man of the Dale, and mayst bid us poor souls what thou wilt.”

Face-of-god reddened at her words, and the speaker and the last-comer laughed; but Long-coat held her peace: she cast one very sober look on him, and then ran lightly down the bent; he drew near the edge of it, and watched her going; for her light-foot slimness was fair to look on: and he noted that when she was nigh the thorn-bush whereon hung the bright-broidered gowns, and deemed belike that she was not seen, she kissed both her hands where he had kissed them erst.

Thereat he drew aback and turned away shyly, scarce looking at the other twain, who smiled on him with somewhat jeering looks; but he bade them farewell and departed speedily; and if they spoke, it was but softly, for he heard their voices no more.

===Chinese===
"服，"那美貌姑娘道，"不是因为你是长老之子，而是因为你是全堡谷最俊的男子，尽可随意支使我们这些可怜人。"

面神闻言脸上一红，那发话之人以及后到之人都笑起来；长衣却不出声：她极凝重地看了他一眼，随即轻盈地奔下山坡；他走到坡缘，看着她去——她那轻捷苗条的身段赏心悦目：他留意到，当她走到挂着鲜亮绣袍的荆棘丛旁、自以为无人瞧见之时，她将双手都贴上唇去，吻了他方才吻过的那处。

他见状便退后一步，羞答答地转身，几乎不敢看另外两人——那二人含笑看着他，目光里颇有几分揶揄；他与她们匆匆作别，赶紧上路；她们若还有话说，也只是低声，因为他再也听不见她们的声音了。

===Original===
He went on under the sunlight which was now gilding the outstanding stones of the cliffs, and still his mind was set upon the Bride; and his meeting with the mother of the yet unborn baby, and with the three women with their freshness and fairness, did somehow turn his thought the more upon her, since she was the woman who was to be his amongst all women, for she was far fairer than any one of them; and through all manner of life and through all kinds of deeds would he be with her, and know more of her fairness and kindness than any other could: and him-seemed he could see pictures of her and of him amidst all these deeds and ways.

Now he went very swiftly; for he was eager, though he knew not for what, and he thought but little of the things on which his eyes fell. He met none else on the road till he was come to Wildlake’s Way, though he saw folk enough down in the meadows; he was soon amidst the first of the trees, and without making any stay set his face east and somewhat north, that is, toward the slopes that led to the great mountains. He said to himself aloud, as he wended the wood: “Strange! yestereven I thought much of the wood, and I set my mind on not going thither, and this morning I thought nothing of it, and here am I amidst its trees, and wending towards its innermost.”

His way was easy at first, because the wood for a little space was all of beech, so that there was no undergrowth, and he went lightly betwixt the tall grey and smooth boles; albeit his heart was nought so gay as it was in the dale amidst the sunshine. After a while the beechwood grew thinner, and at last gave out altogether, and he came into a space of rough broken ground with nought but a few scrubby oaks and thorn-bushes growing thereon here and there. The sun was high in the heavens now, and shone brightly down on the waste, though there were a few white clouds high up above him. The rabbits scuttled out of the grass before him; here and there he turned aside from a stone on which lay coiled an adder sunning itself; now and again both hart and hind bounded away from before him, or a sounder of wild swine ran grunting away toward closer covert. But nought did he see but the common sights and sounds of the woodland; nor did he look for aught else, for he knew this part of the woodland indifferent well.

===Chinese===
他继续前行，阳光此刻正把崖壁上突出的石块镀上一层金；他心里仍念着新娘；方才遇见那位尚未分娩的母亲、又遇见那三位清新明媚的姑娘，反倒愈发将他的心思牵到她身上——因为她是众妇之中将属于他的那一位，她又比她们中任何一个都美得多；他将与她同历种种人生、共行种种事业，比任何旁人都更深知她的美与好：他恍惚能看见一幅幅图景，她与他同在那些事业与道路之间。

此时他走得极快；因为心头火热，虽则不知为了什么，眼里落到的种种他几乎都不甚在意。在到野湖径之前，他再没遇见别的行人，虽然下边草甸上人影绰绰；不多时他便已置身于头一片树木之间，一刻不停，便面朝东偏北而去——也就是说，朝那通向大山的一道道山坡而去。他穿行林间，自言自语道："奇哉！昨夜我满心想这林子，打定主意不去；今早我把它丢在脑后，人却在它的树木之中，向它最深处走去。"

起初路倒好走，因为林中有一小段尽是山毛榉，并无灌丛，他便在那些高大灰白光滑的树干之间轻快穿行；只是他的心在林中远不如在谷中阳光之下那般畅快。行不多时，山毛榉林渐渐稀疏，终于绝尽，他来到一片崎岖坎坷之地，其间只零零落落生着几株矮柞和几丛荆棘。此刻日已高悬，朗朗照在这片荒地上，虽则头顶高处尚有几片白云。野兔在他面前的草里东奔西窜；他时时绕开某块盘着一条蝮蛇晒太阳的石头；不时又有公鹿母鹿自他跟前跃开，或是一群野猪哼哼唧唧奔向更密的隐蔽处。但所见所闻，无非林中寻常景物声响而已；他也不指望别的，因为这片林地他原不算生疏。

===Original===
He held on over this treeless waste for an hour or more, when the ground began to be less rugged, and he came upon trees again, but thinly scattered, oak and ash and hornbeam not right great, with thickets of holly and blackthorn between them. The set of the ground was still steadily up to the east and northeast, and he followed it as one who wendeth an assured way. At last before him seemed to rise a wall of trees and thicket; but when he drew near to it, lo! an opening in a certain place, and a little path as if men were wont to thread the tangle of the wood thereby; though hitherto he had noted no slot of men, nor any sign of them, since he had plunged into the deep of the beechwood. He took the path as one who needs must, and went his ways as it led. In sooth it was well-nigh blind, but he was a deft woodsman, and by means of it skirted many a close thicket that had otherwise stayed him. So on he went, and though the boughs were close enough overhead, and the sun came through but in flecks, he judged that it was growing towards noon, and he wotted well that he was growing aweary. For he had been long afoot, and the more part of the time on a rough way, or breasting a slope which was at whiles steep enough.

At last the track led him skirting about an exceeding close thicket into a small clearing, through which ran a little woodland rill amidst rushes and dead leaves: there was a low mound near the eastern side of this wood-lawn, as though there had been once a dwelling of man there, but no other sign or slot of man was there.

So Face-of-god made stay in that place, casting himself down beside the rill to rest him and eat and drink somewhat. Whatever thoughts had been with him through the wood (and they been many) concerning his House and his name, and his father, and the journey he might make to the cities of the Westland, and what was to befall him when he was wedded, and what war or trouble should be on his hands﻿—all this was now mingled together and confused by this rest amidst his weariness. He laid down his scrip, and drew his meat from it and ate what he would, and dipping his gilded beaker into the brook, drank water smacking of the damp musty savour of the woodland; and then his head sank back on a little mound in the short turf, and he fell asleep at once. A long dream he had in short space; and therein were blent his thoughts of the morning with the deeds of yesterday; and other matters long forgotten in his waking hours came back to his slumber in unordered confusion: all which made up for him pictures clear, but of little meaning, save that, as oft befalls in dreams, whatever he was a-doing he felt himself belated.

===Chinese===
他在这一片无树的荒地上又走了一个时辰有余，地势方始渐缓，重又见到树木，只是疏疏落落，柞、梣、鹅耳枥都不甚高大，树与树之间杂生着冬青与黑刺李的灌丛。地势仍一路缓缓向东、向东北抬升，他便循势而行，犹如走在一条胸有成竹的路上。到得后来，只见面前仿佛升起一道林木灌丛之墙；待走近一看，嗬！某一处竟有一个豁口，一条小径蜿蜒其间，似乎常有人借此穿行林莽纠缠之处；然而自他深入山毛榉林腹地以来，并不曾见到人的足印，也不曾见到半点人迹。他便上了这条小径，一路循径而行，仿佛不得不然。这条路其实近乎湮没难辨，但他是个精于林事的汉子，借它绕过一道又一道本来会挡住去路的浓密灌丛。他继续前行，头顶枝柯虽密、阳光仅成斑驳漏下，他仍判断时辰将近正午，自己也分明疲倦起来。因为徒步已久，且大半时候走的是崎岖之路，或是在攀越有时颇为陡峭的山坡。

终于，小径引着他绕过一道极密之灌丛，来到一小片空地，一道林间细流穿行于灯心草与败叶之间：这片林中草地的东侧有一座低矮的土阜，似乎曾有人居于此处，除此之外再无人迹。

于是面神就在此处歇下，倒在细流旁休息，吃点东西、喝口水。方才穿林而来时那些念头（实在不少）——关于他的宗族与名号、关于他父亲、关于他或可西行诸城之旅、关于他成亲之后将有何事降临、关于他肩上或将担起何种战事或纷扰——凡此种种，此刻在这倦极之歇中，全都混作一团、糊里糊涂。他放下皮囊，取出肉食，随心吃了一些，又拿那只镀金小杯舀了溪水喝下——水味里带着林间那种潮湿霉旧的气息；随即他的头一歪，枕在短草地上一个小土阜上，立时沉沉睡去。片刻之间他做了一个长长的梦；梦中晨间的心绪与昨日的种种事迹交织一处；另有清醒时早已忘却的诸般往事，也零乱无序地回到他这眠中：这一切为他拼出一幅幅清晰却意义寥寥的图景——唯有这一点，正如梦中常有之事：无论他正在做什么，他总觉得自己来得太迟。

===Original===
When he awoke, smiling at something strange in his gone-by dream, he looked up to the heavens, thinking to see signs of the even at hand, for he seemed to have been dreaming so long. The sky was thinly overcast by now, but by his wonted woodcraft he knew the whereabouts of the sun, and that it was scant an hour after noon. He sat there till he was wholly awake, and then drank once more of the woodland water; and he said to himself, but out loud, for he was fain of the sound of a man’s voice, though it were but his own:

“What is mine errand hither? Whither wend I? What shall I have done tomorrow that I have hitherto left undone? Or what manner of man shall I be then other than I am now?”

Yet though he said the words he failed to think the thought, or it left him in a moment of time, and he thought but of the Bride and her kindness. Yet that abode with him but a moment, and again he saw himself and those two women on the highway edge, and Long-coat lingering on the slope below, kissing his kisses on her hands; and he was sorry that she desired him overmuch, for she was a fair woman and a friendly. But all that also flowed from him at once, and he had no thought in him but that he also desired something that he lacked: and this was a burden to him, and he rose up frowning, and said to himself, “Am I become a mere sport of dreams, whether I sleep or wake? I will go backward﻿—or forward, but will think no more.”

Then he ordered his gear again, and took the path onward and upward toward the Great Mountains; and the track was even fainter than before for a while, so that he had to seek his way diligently.

===Chinese===
待他醒来，因方才那怪梦而含着笑，抬头望天，以为必是黄昏将至的景象了——他仿佛睡了那么久。此刻天上薄薄地覆着一层云，但凭他素来的林事经验，他晓得太阳大约在何处，时辰不过刚过正午不到一个时辰。他坐在那里直坐到完全清醒，又喝了一口林中溪水；便自言自语起来——只是出声说的，因为他爱听人声，纵然只是自己的声音：

"我到此地来所为何事？我要往何处去？我明日将做成何事、是至今未曾做的？又或者，我将变成怎样一个与今日不同之人？"

然而话虽出口，那念头却未跟上，或者才起即灭，他心里所想的不过是新娘、是她的好处。然而这也不过停了一瞬，他又看见自己与大路边的两个妇人、看见长衣在坡下流连、将他吻过之处贴到唇上；他为她如此过度地思慕自己而觉得抱歉，因为她原是个美貌而和善的妇人。但这一切也立时自他心中流走，他脑中只剩一念：他自己也在渴求一样他所欠缺之物。这念头成了他的重负，他皱眉起身，自语道："难道我已成了梦的玩物，无分睡与醒？我往后退也好——往前去也好，总之不再想了。"

于是他重新收拾行装，循小径继续向大山、向上行去；那条径有一段比先前更难辨认，他不得不一路用心寻路。

## XXIV Face-of-God Giveth That Token to the Bride / 二十四 面神将那信物付与新娘

===Original===
Now on the morrow, when Face-of-god arose and other men with him, and the Hall was astir and there was no little throng therein, the Bride came up to him; for she had slept in the House of the Face by the bidding of the Alderman; and she spake to him before all men, and bade him come forth with her into the garden, because she would speak to him apart. He yeasaid her, though with a heavy heart; and to the folk about that seemed meet and due, since those twain were deemed to be troth-plight, and they smiled kindly on them as they went out of the Hall together.

So they came into the garden, where the pear-trees were blossoming over the spring lilies, and the cherries were showering their flowers on the deep green grass, and everything smelled sweetly on the warm windless spring morning.

She led the way, going before him till they came by a smooth grass path between the berry bushes, to a square space of grass about which were barberry trees, their first tender leaves bright green in the sun against the dry yellowish twigs. There was a sundial amidmost of the grass, and betwixt the garden-boughs one could see the long grey roof of the ancient hall; and sweet familiar sounds of the nesting birds and men and women going on their errands were all about in the scented air. She turned about at the sundial and faced Face-of-god, her hand lightly laid on the scored brass, and spake with no anger in her voice:

===Chinese===
次日清晨，面神起身，众人亦起，大厅之中一片忙乱，人来人往颇为拥挤，新娘便走到他跟前；原来她昨夜奉长老之命，宿于面神之宅中；她当着众人的面对他说话，请他随她出到花园里去，因她要与他单独一谈。他虽然心事沉重，仍应允了她；旁人看了，也觉得这是理所当然、合乎礼数的事，因为两人已被视作定了亲的，见他俩一同步出大厅，都和颜悦色地含笑相送。

于是二人来到花园之中。其时梨花盛开，掩映于春日百合之上；樱桃花纷纷扬扬，洒落在深绿的草地上；这温暖无风的春日清晨，万物都散发着甜香。

她在前引路，走在他的前头，二人沿着浆果丛间一条平整的草径，来到一片方形的草地；草地四周种着小檗树，初生的嫩叶在日光中碧绿可爱，映着枯黄微褐的枝条。草地正中立着一座日晷，透过园中的枝叶，可以望见古厅那长长的灰色屋脊；筑巢鸟儿的啼鸣、男女各忙各事的种种亲切声响，在这香气氤氲的空气里四处可闻。她在日晷前转过身来，面对着面神，一只手轻轻按在那刻有纹路的铜盘上，语声中不带一丝怒意：

===Original===
“I ask thee if thou hast brought me the token whereon thou shalt swear to give me that gift.”

“Yea,” said he; and therewith drew the ring from his bosom, and held it out to her. She reached out her hand to him slowly and took it, and their fingers met as she did so, and he noted that her hand was warm and firm and wholesome as he well remembered it.

She said: “Whence hadst thou this fair finger-ring?”

Said Face-of-god: “My friend there in the mountain-valley drew it from off her finger for thee, and bade me bear thee a message.”

Her face flushed red: “Yea,” she said, “and doth she send me a message? Then doth she know of me, and ye have talked of me together. Well, give the message!”

Said Face-of-god: “She saith, that thou shalt bear in mind, That tomorrow is a new day.”

===Chinese===
「我问你，你可曾将那信物带来？你须凭它立誓，将那件礼物赐予我。」

「带来了。」他说，随即从怀中取出那枚戒指，向她递去。她缓缓伸出手来接过，接时两人的手指相触，他觉察到她的手温暖、结实而康健，一如他所熟记的那般。

她说：「这枚精美的戒指，你是从何处得来的？」

面神说：「我那位山中之谷的朋友，从自己指上褪下它来给你，并托我带一句话与你。」

她的脸涨得通红：「好啊，」她说，「她还带话给我？这么说来，她已经知道了我，你们两个也已在一起谈论过我。也罢，把话传给我吧！」

面神说：「她说，你须记住：明天又是新的一天。」

===Original===
“Yea,” she said, “for her it is so, and for thee; but not for me. But now I have brought thee here that thou mightest swear thine oath to me; lay thine hand on this ring and on this brazen plate whereby the sun measures the hours of the day for happy folk, and swear by the spring-tide of the year and all glad things that find a mate, and by the God of the Earth that rejoiceth in the life of man.”

Then he laid his hand on the finger-ring as it lay on the dial-plate and said:

“By the spring-tide and the live things that long to multiply their kind; by the God of the Earth that rejoiceth in the life of man, I swear to give to my kinswoman the Bride the second man-child that I beget; to be hers, to leave or cherish, to love or hate, as her will may bid her.” Then he looked on her soberly and said: “It is duly sworn; is it enough?”

“Yea,” she said; but he saw how the tears ran out of her eyes and wetted the bosom of her kirtle, and she hung her head for shame of her grief. And Gold-mane was all abashed, and had no word to say; for he knew that no word of his might comfort her; and he deemed it ill done to stay there and behold her sorrow; and he knew not how to get him gone, and be glad elsewhere, and leave her alone.

===Chinese===
「是啊，」她说，「对她而言是如此，对你而言也是如此；于我却不然。但我既把你带到此处，是要你向我立下誓言：将你的手按在这枚戒指上，按在这块铜盘上——太阳借它为幸福之人丈量白昼的时辰——以一年之春、以一切得以结偶的欢乐之物、以乐见人世生命的地神之名立誓。」

于是他把手按在搁于晷盘之上的戒指上，说道：

「以春之时节与渴望繁衍其类的活物；以乐见人世生命的地神之名，我誓将我所生之第二个男儿赐予族亲新娘；归她所有，任她弃之或抚之、爱之或恶之，一凭其意。」说罢他神色郑重地看着她，又道：「誓已按礼立下；可够了？」

「够了。」她说；他却看见泪水如何夺眶而出，沾湿了她衣裙的胸前，她因自己这番哀伤而羞惭地低下了头。金鬃则窘迫万分，无话可说；因为他知道自己的任何言语都安慰不了她；他觉得自己若留在此处目睹她的悲伤，实在于心难安；却又不知如何抽身而去、到别处去寻欢，将她独自撇下。

===Original===
Then, as if she had read his thought, she looked up at him and said smiling a little amidst of her tears:

“I bid thee stay by me till the flood is over; for I have yet a word to say to thee.”

So he stood there gazing down on the grass in his turn, and not daring to raise his eyes to her face, and the minutes seemed long to him: till at last she said in a voice scarcely yet clear of weeping:

“Wilt thou say anything to me, and tell me what thou hast done, and why, and what thou deemest will come of it?”

===Chinese===
这时，仿佛看穿了他的心思一般，她抬起头来望着他，在泪痕之中微微笑道：

「我求你留在我身边，等这阵潮水退去；因为我还有一句话要对你说。」

于是这回轮到他站在那里，垂眼凝视着草地，不敢抬眼去看她的脸，只觉一刻一刻都漫长得难熬：直到最后她开口说道，声音里还带着未曾褪尽的哽咽：

「你可愿对我说些什么，告诉我你做了什么、为何要做、又料想这事会有怎样的结局？」

===Original===
He said: “I will tell the truth as I know it, because thou askest it of me, and not because I would excuse myself before thee. What have I done? Yesterday I plighted my troth to wed the woman that I met last autumn in the wood. And why? I wot not why, but that I longed for her. Yet I must tell thee that it seemed to me, and yet seemeth, that I might do no otherwise—that there was nothing else in the world for me to do. What do I deem will come of it, sayest thou? This, that we shall be happy together, she and I, till the day of our death.”

She said: “And even so long shall I be sorry: so far are we sundered now. Alas! who looked for it? And whither shall I turn to now?”

Said Gold-mane: “She bade me tell thee that tomorrow is a new day: meseemeth I know her meaning.”

“No word of hers hath any meaning to me,” said the Bride.

===Chinese===
他说：「我愿将我所知的实情相告，因这是你所求于我的，而非我欲在你面前为自己开脱。我做了什么？昨日我与去年秋日在林中遇见的那个女子立下了婚誓。为何如此？我不知道为何，只知我渴慕她。然而我必须告诉你：在我看——至今仍然如此看——我别无选择，这世上再没有别的事可做。你问我料想此事会有何结局？是这个：我和她将一同幸福度日，直到我二人生命的终了。」

她说：「即便到了那时，我也仍将如此悲伤：如今你我竟已相隔如此之远。唉！谁曾料到这一日？我又该转向何处去呢？」

金鬃说：「她让我告诉你，明天又是新的一天：我想我懂得她的用意。」

新娘说：「她的话，于我没有任何意义。」

===Original===
“Nay,” said he, “but hast thou not heard these rumours of war that are in the Dale? Shall not these things avail thee? Much may grow out of them; and thou with the mighty heart, so faithful and compassionate!”

She said: “What sayest thou? What may grow out of them? Yea, I have heard those rumours as a man sick to death heareth men talk of their business down in the street while he lieth on his bed; and already he hath done with it all, and hath no world to mend or mar. For me nought shall grow out of it. What meanest thou?”

Said Gold-mane: “Is there nought in the fellowship of Folks, and the aiding of the valiant, and the deliverance of the hapless?”

“Nay,” she said, “there is nought to me. I cannot think of it today nor yet tomorrow belike. Yet true it is that I may mingle in it, though thinking nought of it. But this shall not avail me.”

===Chinese===
「不，」他说，「你可曾听见谷中流传的那些战争的风声？这些事难道不能为你所用？其中能生出许多事来；而你又是这般刚毅的心肠，如此忠贞而富于怜悯！」

她说：「你说什么？能生出什么事来？是啊，我听见过那些风声，就像一个病入膏肓的人躺在床上，听见下面街上人们谈论各自的营生；他对这一切早已了无干系，再没有一个世界可供他修补或破坏。于我而言，其中什么也生不出来。你是什么意思？」

金鬃说：「诸族携手同盟、扶助勇者、解救困厄之人——这一切于你便全无意义么？」

「不，」她说，「于我毫无意义。今日我无法去想这事，明日只怕也不能。然而我确有可能卷入其中，尽管我心不在此。但这于我终究无益。」

===Original===
She was silent a little, but presently spake and said: “Thou sayest right; it is not thou that hast done this, but the woman who sent me the ring and the message of an old saw. O that she should be born to sunder us! How hath it befallen that I am now so little to thee and she so much?”

And again she was silent; and after a while Face-of-god spake kindly and softly and said: “Kinswoman, wilt thou forever begrudge our love? this grudge lieth heavy on my soul, and it is I alone that have to bear it.”

She said: “This is but a light burden for thee to bear, when thou hast nought else to bear! But do I begrudge thee thy love, Gold-mane? I know not that. Rather meseemeth I do not believe in it—nor shall do ever.”

===Chinese===
她沉默了一阵，随即又开口说道：「你说得对；做下这事的不是你，而是那个送我戒指、又以一句老话传讯与我的人。唉，她竟生来就要拆散你我！怎会落到这步田地——我如今在你心中竟如此微不足道，而她竟如此举足轻重？」

她再度沉默；过了一会儿，面神温言款款地说道：「族亲，难道你要永远记恨我们的相好么？这份记恨重重压在我的心上，而须独自承受它的，又偏偏只是我一人。」

她说：「在你别无负担之时，这不过是一副轻担子罢了！可是我当真记恨你的相好么，金鬃？我不知道。倒不如说，我根本不信有这回事——日后也永远不会信。」

===Original===
Then she held her peace a long while, nor did he speak one word: and they were so still, that a robin came hopping about them, close to the hem of her kirtle, and a starling pitched in the apple-tree hard by and whistled and chuckled, turning about and about, heeding them nought. Then at last she lifted up her face from looking on the grass and said: “These are idle words and avail nothing: one thing only I know, that we are sundered. And now it repenteth me that I have shown thee my tears and my grief and my sickness of the earth and those that dwell thereon. I am ashamed of it, as if thou hadst smitten me, and I had come and shown thee the stripes, and said, See what thou hast done! hast thou no pity? Yea, thou pitiest me, and wilt try to forget thy pity. Belike thou art right when thou sayest, Tomorrow is a new day; belike matters will arise that will call me back to life, and I shall once more take heed of the joy and sorrow of my people. Nay, it is most like that this I shall feign to do even now. But if tomorrow be a new day, it is today now and not tomorrow, and so shall it be for long. Hereof belike we shall talk no more, thou and I. For as the days wear, the dealings between us shall be that thou shalt but get thee away from my life, and I shall be nought to thee but the name of a kinswoman. Thus should it be even wert thou to strive to make it otherwise; and thou shalt *not* strive. So let all this be; for this is not the word I had to say to thee. But hearken! now are we sundered, and it irketh me beyond measure that folk know it not, and are kind, and rejoice in our love, and deem it a happy thing for the folk; and this burden I may bear no longer. So I shall declare unto men that I will not wed thee; and belike they may wonder why it is, till they see thee wedded to the Woman of the Mountain. Art thou content that so it shall be?”

Said Face-of-god: “Nay, thou shalt not take this all upon thyself; I also shall declare unto the Folk that I will wed none but her, the Mountain-Woman.”

She said: “This shalt thou not do; I forbid it thee. And I *will* take it all upon myself. Shall I have it said of me that I am unmeet to wed thee, and that thou hast found me out at last and at latest? I lay this upon thee, that wheresoever I declare this and whatsoever I may say, thou shalt hold thy peace. This at least thou may’st do for me. Wilt thou?”

“Yea,” he said, “though it shall put me to shame.”

===Chinese===
于是她长久地住了口，他也不发一言：两人静得连一只知更鸟都跳到他们身旁来，几乎挨到了她衣裙的下摆，一只椋鸟落在近处的苹果树上，啾啾唧唧地鸣叫着，转来转去，全不把他们放在眼里。末了她终于从凝视草地中抬起脸来，说道：「这些都是废话，毫无用处：我只知道一件事——我们已被拆散。如今我后悔让你看见了我的眼泪、我的悲伤、我对这大地及居于其上之人的厌倦。我为此感到羞愧，仿佛你打了我，我却跑来把伤痕指给你看，说：看你所做的事！你竟毫无怜悯之心么？是的，你是怜悯我的，而且会设法忘掉你的怜悯。你说『明天又是新的一天』，只怕你说得对；只怕会有一些事把我重新唤回人世，让我再度去关切我族人的悲欢。不，多半连眼下这事，我也只是装作去做罢了。纵然明天是新的一天，此刻却仍是今日，不是明日，而且长久之内都将如此。这件事，你我大概不会再提了。因为随着日子一天天过去，你我之间将只剩下：你从我生命中抽身而去，而我在你心中不过是一个族亲的名字而已。即便你竭力想改写它，结局仍会如此；况且你也并*不会*竭力。那么，就让这一切都过去吧；因为我要对你说的话，并不是这一桩。且听我说！如今我们既已分开，最让我难以忍受的是，众人对此一无所知，仍待我们亲切，为我们的相爱而欢喜，以为这是全族的一桩幸事；这副担子我再也挑不动了。所以我将当众宣布，我不愿嫁你；只怕众人要纳罕其中缘故，直到看见你娶了那山中女子。这样办，你可愿意？」

面神说：「不，你不该把这一切都揽到自己身上；我也要当众向族人宣告，除了她——那山中女子——我谁也不娶。」

她说：「你不可以这样做；我不许。我*一定*要把这一切揽到自己身上。难道要让人说我配不上嫁你，说你终归到底还是看穿了我么？我以此相求于你：无论我在何处宣布此事，也无论我说些什么，你都要保持缄默。这至少是你能为我做的。你可愿意？」

「我愿意，」他说，「纵然这会使我蒙羞。」

===Original===
Again she was silent for a little; then she said:

“O Gold-mane, this would I take upon myself not soothly for any shame of seeming to be thy cast-off; but because it is I who needs must bear all the sorrow of our sundering; and I have the will to bear it greater and heavier, that I may be as the women of old time, and they that have come from the Gods, lest I belittle my life with malice and spite and confusion, and it become poisonous to me. Be at peace! be at peace! And leave all to the wearing of the years; and forget not that which thou hast sworn!”

===Chinese===
她又沉默了一阵；然后说道：

「金鬃啊，我之所以要把这一切揽到自己身上，并非真为了所谓被你抛弃的那种羞耻；而是因为我们的离散之痛，本就该由我来承受全部；我立意要将这痛担得更重更深，好让自己像古时的女子、像那班自神灵而出的人一样，免得我因怨毒、嫉恨与纷乱而看轻了自己的生命，使它变得如毒物一般反噬自身。安心吧！安心吧！把一切交给岁月去消磨；也别忘了你所立下的誓言！」

===Original===
Therewith she turned and went from that green place toward the House of the Face, walking slowly through the garden amongst the sweet odours, beneath the fair blossoms, a body most dainty and beauteous of fashion, but the casket of grievous sorrow, which all that goodliness availed not.

But Face-of-god lingered in that place a little, and for that little while the joy of his life was dulled and overworn; and the days before his wandering on the mountain seemed to him free and careless and happy days that he could not but regret. He was ashamed, moreover, that this so unquenchable grief should come but of him, and the pleasure of his life, which he himself had found out for himself, and which was but such a little portion of the Earth and the deeds thereof. But presently his thought wandered from all this, and as he turned away from the sundial and went his ways through the garden, he called to mind his longing for the day of the spring market, when he should see the Sun-beam again and be cherished by the sweetness of her love.

===Chinese===
说罢她转过身，从那片绿草地走向面神之宅，缓缓穿行于花园之中，行过阵阵甜香之间，行过繁花之下；那身姿本是极其曼妙美好的，却如同一只盛满沉痛哀伤的匣子，而那一切美好，于这哀伤都无能为力。

面神却在原地稍作逗留，就在这片刻之间，他生命中的欢愉被磨钝了、消磨尽了；而他在山上漫游之前的日子，在他看来竟是那般自在、无忧而幸福，叫他不能不心生追悔。况且他也惭愧：这般无法平息的悲伤，竟全由他一人而起，全由他自己所寻得的、生命中那份欢愉而起——而那份欢愉，不过是这大地及其万千行事之中极其微小的一粟罢了。但不久他的心思便从这一切上游离开去，当他转身离开日晷、穿过花园走自己的路时，他又想起了自己对春日集市之日的渴盼——到了那一日，他将再次见到日光（Sun-beam），并在她那甜蜜的爱意里被珍视呵护。

## XXVII Face-of-God Leadeth a Band Through the Wood / 二十七 面神率一队人穿过林莽

===Original===
Next morning tryst was held faithfully, and an hundred and a half were gathered together on Wildlake’s Way; and Face-of-god ordered them into three companies. He made Hall-face leader over the first one, and bade him hold on his way northward, and then to make for Boars-bait and see if he should meet with anything thereabout where the battle had been. Red-coat of Waterless he made captain of the second band; and he had it in charge to wend eastward along the edge of the Dale, and not to go deep into the wood, but to go as far as he might within the time appointed, toward the Mountains. Furthermore, he bade both Hall-face and Red-coat to bring their bands back to Wildlake’s Way by the morrow at sunset, where other goodmen should be come to take the places of their men; and then if he and his company were back again, he would bid them further what to do; but if not, as seemed likely, then Hall-face’s band to go west toward the Shepherd country half a day’s journey, and so back, and Red-coat’s east along the Dale’s lip again for the like time, and then back, so that there might be a constant watch and ward of the Dale kept against the Felons.

===Chinese===
次日清晨，众人依约准时赴会，共一百五十人齐聚于野湖径（Wildlake's Way）之上；面神（Face-of-god）将他们编作三队。他命厅面（Hall-face）统领第一队，嘱咐他一路北行，再转向野猪饵（Boars-bait），到前番交战之地附近查看有无动静。他又任无水地（Waterless）的红衣（Red-coat）为第二队之长，令其沿谷之边缘东行，不必深入林中，唯于限定之时辰内、朝群山方向尽可能探进。此外，面神又嘱咐厅面与红衣二人，须于次日日落之前率队返回野湖径，届时自有别家好汉前来接替其部下；若他与其本队已归，再行吩咐下一步行止；若未归——此事看来极有可能——则厅面之队往西朝牧羊之民之地行半日之程再折返，红衣之队则再沿谷之口缘东行同样时辰再折返，如此轮番往来，使谷中常有守望，以防恶徒（the Felons）来犯。

===Original===
All being ordered Gold-mane led his own company northeast through the thick wood, thinking that he might so fare as to come nigh to Silverdale, or at least to hear tidings thereof. This intent he told to Stone-face, but the old man shook his head and said:

“Good is this if it may be done; but it is not for everyone to go down to Hell in his lifetime and come back safe with a tale thereof. However, whither thou wilt lead, thither will I follow, though assured death waylayeth us.”

And the old carle was joyous and proud to be on this adventure, and said, that it was good indeed that his foster-son had with him a man well stricken in years, who had both seen many things, and learned many, and had good rede to give to valiant men.

===Chinese===
一切部署既定，金鬃（Gold-mane，即面神）便率自家那一队穿过密林朝东北而去，心下盘算：如此行去，或可逼近银谷（Silverdale），至少也能探得些银谷的消息。他把此意告知石面（Stone-face），老汉却摇头说道：

“这事若能办到，自然甚好；然而活人活着下黄泉，又全须全尾地回来讲说一番，却不是人人都能做得的。话虽如此，你往哪里带，我便往哪里跟，纵然必死之祸埋伏于前，也在所不辞。”

这老汉以此番历险为乐、为荣，说道：他的义孙身边带着一个年事已长之人，实在是一桩好事——这老人既见过许多世面，又学过许多本事，正可为勇士们进上一言良策。

===Original===
So they went on their ways, and fared very warily when they were gotten beyond those parts of the wood which they knew well. By this time they were strung out in a long line; and they noted their road carefully, blazing the trees on either side when there were trees, and piling up little stone-heaps where the trees failed them. For Stone-face said that oft it befell men amidst the thicket and the waste to be misled by wights that begrudged men their lives, so that they went round and round in a ring which they might not depart from till they died; and no man doubted his word herein.

All day they went, and met no foe, nay, no man at all; nought but the wild things of the wood; and that day the wood changed little about them from mile to mile. There were many thickets across their road which they had to go round about; so that to the crow flying over the treetops the journey had not been long to the place where night came upon them, and where they had to make the wood their bedchamber.

That night they lighted no fire, but ate such cold victual as they might carry with them; nor had they shot any venison, since they had with them more than enough; they made little noise or stir therefore and fell asleep when they had set the watch.

===Chinese===
于是众人启程，待走出素来熟稔的那片林地之后，便步步格外小心。此时他们已拉开一字长蛇阵；沿途留意记认道路，两旁有树处便在树皮上砍出记号，无树处便垒起一个个小石堆。盖因石面说过：人在密林荒原之中，常为那些嫉恨人活命的荒原之灵（wights）所迷，绕着圈子打转，再也走不出去，直至困死其中；此话众人深信不疑。

整整一日他们穿行不停，未遇一敌，甚至连一个人影也未曾撞见；所遇无非林中野兽罢了。这一日，林地里里外外几乎一成不变。沿途横亘着许多灌丛，他们不得不绕道而行；所以若是乌鸦掠过树梢俯瞰，飞到他们当夜歇息之处并不算远——他们只得在林中权作寝室。

那夜他们不生火，只就随身所带干粮冷食；也未猎取鹿肉，因所带口粮早已富足有余；故而动静极小，安好哨卫便各自睡下。

===Original===
On the morrow they arose betimes, and broke their fast and went their ways till noon: by then the wood had thinned somewhat, and there was little underwood betwixt the scrubby oak and ash which were pretty nigh all the trees about: the ground also was broken, and here and there rocky, and they went into and out of rough little dales, most of which had in them a brook of water running west and southwest; and now Face-of-god led his men somewhat more easterly; and still for some while they met no man.

At last, about four hours after noon, when they were going less warily, because they had hitherto come across nothing to hinder them, rising over the brow of a somewhat steep ridge, they saw down in the valley below them a half score of men sitting by the brook-side eating and drinking, their weapons lying beside them, and along with them stood a woman with her hands tied behind her back.

===Chinese===
次日众人早早起身，用过朝食便启程，直行到正午：此时林木已稍见稀疏，矮柞与梣树之间几乎再无下木矮丛——这两种树几乎是此地仅见之树：地面也起伏不平，处处乱石，他们穿进穿出一道道粗陋的小谷，这些小谷大多有一条溪水自其中向西、向西南流去；这时面神引部众略略偏向东方；此后好一段时辰，他们仍未遇见一人。

末了，午后约莫四个钟点，因一路并无阻拦、众人戒备渐松之际，他们攀上一道稍陡山脊之巅，忽见下方谷中溪畔有十来个人坐着饮食，兵器都搁在身旁，其中还立着一个妇人，双手被反缚于后。

===Original===
They saw at once that these men were of the Felons, so they that had their bows bent, loosed at them without more ado, while the others ran in upon them with sword and spear. The felons leapt up and ran scattering down the dale, such of them as were not smitten by the shafts; but he who was nighest to the woman, ere he ran, turned and caught up a sword from the ground and thrust it through her, and the next moment fell across the brook with an arrow in his back.

No one of the felons was nimble enough to escape from the fleet-foot hunters of Burgdale, and they were all slain there to the number of eleven.

===Chinese===
众人一看便知这些人乃恶徒之流，于是弯弓在手者不及多想便放箭，余下的人挺剑举矛直扑上去。那些恶徒纵身跃起，未被箭中所中者四散奔逃下谷；然而离那妇人最近的一个，临逃之前，却回身从地上抄起一柄剑，一剑将那妇人刺穿，随即背上一箭，扑倒在溪对岸。

恶徒中无一矫捷得能逃脱堡谷（Burgdale）健步猎手之追击，尽被诛于此处，共计十一人。

===Original===
But when they came back to the woman to tend her, she breathed her last in their hands: she was a young and fair woman, black-haired and dark-eyed. She had on her body a gown of rich web, but nought else: she had been bruised and sore mishandled, and the Burgdale carles wept for pity of her, and for wrath, as they straightened her limbs on the turf of the little valley. They let her lie there a little, whilst they searched round about, lest there should be any other poor soul needing their help, or any felon lurking thereby; but they found nought else save a bundle wherein was another rich gown and divers woman’s gear, and sundry rings and jewels, and therewithal the weapons and war-gear of a knight, delicately wrought after the Westland fashion: these seemed to them to betoken other foul deeds of these murder-carles. So when they had abided a while, they laid the dead woman in mould by the brook-side, and buried with her the other woman’s attire and the knight’s gear, all but his sword and shield, which they had away with them: then they cast the carcasses of the felons into the brake, but brought away their weapons and the silver rings from their arms, which they wore like all the others of them whom they had fallen in with; and so went on their way to the northeast, full of wrath against those dastards of the Earth.

It was hard on sunset when they left the valley of murder, and they went no long way thence before they must needs make stop for the night; and when they had arrayed their sleepingstead the moon was up, and they saw that before them lay the close wood again, for they had made their lair on the top of a little ridge.

There then they lay, and nought stirred them in the night, and betimes on the morrow they were afoot, and entered the abovesaid thicket, wherein two of them, keen hunters, had been aforetime, but had not gone deep into it. Through this wood they went all day toward the northeast, and met nought but the wild things therein. At last, when it was near sunset, they came out of the thicket into a small plain, or shallow dale rather, with no great trees in it, but thorn-brakes here and there where the ground sank into hollows; a little river ran through the midst of it, and winded round about a height whose face toward the river went down sheer into the water, but away from it sank down in a long slope to where the thick wood began again: and this height or burg looked well-nigh west.

===Chinese===
然而待他们回到那妇人身畔施救时，她已在他们怀中咽了气：她是个年轻貌美的女子，黑发黑眸。身上只穿一件华贵料子所制的衣裳，此外再无他物：遍体鳞伤，受尽凌辱。堡谷的汉子们一面怜悯、一面愤恨，流泪将她四肢在小谷的草皮上理顺。他们让她就地躺了一会儿，同时四下搜索，恐尚有别的苦命人待救，或有恶徒潜伏于旁；却别无所获，唯得一个包袱，里头是另一件华贵衣裳及各色女子用物，若干指环珠宝，还有一副骑士的兵器甲胄，皆按西土（the Westland）式样精工细制：在众人看来，这都是这伙杀人汉子另造孽案的明证。于是又守候片刻，他们将死去的妇人埋于溪畔土中，把那另一名女子的衣物及骑士的甲胄一并随葬，唯独留下骑士的剑与盾带走；又将那些恶徒的尸体抛入荆棘丛中，却取走他们的兵器，并剥下他们臂上的银环——这些银环与他们前番所遇那批人臂上所戴一模一样；随后便满怀愤恨，继续朝东北进发，深恨这世上竟有这等卑劣之徒。

他们离开那凶杀之谷时已近日落，走出去不远便不得不就地过夜；待铺好寝处，月亮已然升起，只见前面又是密林——原来他们的卧处正是一道小山脊之顶。

众人就此躺下，一夜并无动静相扰，次日一早便又起身上路，钻入前文所说的那片密林。林中有两名眼尖的猎手昔年曾至此处，却未曾深入。他们整日在林中朝东北穿行，所遇无非林中野兽。将近日落时分，他们终于钻出密林，来到一片小平地——或者说一道浅谷之中，谷中没有大树，唯有随地势低洼处长出的一处处荆棘丛；一条小河从正中穿过，绕着一处高地蜿蜒，那高地临河的一面陡直入水，背河的一面则以一道长坡缓缓低伏，直至密林复又重新展开：而这处高地——或者说山堡（burg）——几乎正面向西方。

===Original===
Thitherward they went; but as they were drawing nigh to the river, and were on the top of a bent above a bushy hollow between them and the water, they espied a man standing in the river near the bank, who saw them not, because he was stooping down intent on something in the bank or under it: so they gat them speedily down into the hollow without noise, that they might get some tidings of the man.

Then Face-of-god bade his men abide hidden under the bushes and stole forward quietly up the further bank of the hollow, his target on his arm and his spear poised. When he was behind the last bush on the top of the bent he was within half a spear-cast of the water and the man; so he looked on him and saw that he was quite naked except for a clout about his middle.

Face-of-god saw at once that he was not one of the Dusky Men; he was a black-haired man, but white-skinned, and of fair stature, though not so tall as the Burgdale folk. He was busied in tickling trouts, and just as Face-of-god came out from the bush into the westering sunlight, he threw up a fish on to the bank, and looked up therewithal, and beheld the weaponed man glittering, and uttered a cry, but fled not when he saw the spear poised for casting.

===Chinese===
他们便朝那处进发；然而将到河边之际，正立在他们与河水之间一道灌木丛生之空谷上方的土阜之巅时，他们瞥见河中近岸处立着一个人，那人并未发觉他们，因为他正俯身专注地查看岸上或岸下某物：于是他们连忙悄然下到空谷之中，以便探听此人的一些消息。

面神命部下伏在灌木下隐匿不动，自己则挽盾于臂、横执长矛，悄然从空谷的另一侧岸上潜行而上。当他身处土阜之巅最后一丛灌木之后时，离水、离那人都不过半矛之遥；他便打量那人，只见那人通体赤裸，腰间只围了一块遮羞布。

面神一看便知此人并非黝暗人（the Dusky Men）：他虽是黑发，肤色却白，身量也算魁梧，只是不及堡谷之人高大。他正忙于摸钓鳟鱼，恰好面神从灌木后步入西斜的日光之中时，他将一条鱼甩上岸来，随之一抬头，便瞧见那披坚执锐之人熠熠生光，惊呼一声，却见长矛引而待发，并不逃窜。

===Original===
Then Face-of-god spake to him and said: “Come hither, Woodsman! we will not harm thee, but we desire speech of thee: and it will not avail thee to flee, since I have bowmen of the best in the hollow yonder.”

The man put forth his hands towards him as if praying him to forbear casting, and looked at him hard, and then came dripping from out the water, and seemed not greatly afeard; for he stooped down and picked up the trouts he had taken, and came towards Face-of-god stringing the last-caught one through the gills on to the withy whereon were the others: and Face-of-god saw that he was a goodly man of some thirty winters.

Then Face-of-god looked on him with friendly eyes and said:

===Chinese===
面神便开口对他道：“过来，林中人！我们不会加害于你，只是要与你攀谈几句：你要逃也是逃不掉的，我那边空谷里正埋伏着最上乘的弓手。”

那人向他伸出双手，似在求他莫要投矛，又定定地打量他一番，这才浑身滴水地从水中走出来，似乎并不怎么害怕；只见他俯身拾起所捕的鳟鱼，把最后一条穿过鳃串到一根柔柳条上——其余几条已串在上头——朝面神走来：面神看出这是个三十来岁、相貌堂堂的汉子。

面神以友善之色看着他，说道：

===Original===
“Art thou a foemen? or wilt thou be helpful to us?”

He answered in the speech of the kindreds with the hoarse voice of a much weather-beaten man:

“Thou seest, lord, that I am naked and unarmed.”

“Yet may’st thou bewray us,” said Face-of-god. “What man art thou?”

===Chinese===
“你是仇敌？还是肯助我们一臂之力？”

那人用诸宗族之语答道，嗓音粗哑，是一副饱经风霜之人的嗓门：

“大人请看，我赤身裸体，手无寸铁。”

“那你也可能出卖我们，”面神道，“你是什么人？”

===Original===
Said the man: “I am the runaway thrall of evil men; I have fled from Rosedale and the Dusky Men. Hast thou the heart to hurt me?”

“We are the foemen of the Dusky Men,” said Face-of-god; “wilt thou help us against them?”

The man knit his brows and said: “Yea, if ye will give me your word not to suffer me to fall into their hands alive. But whence art thou, to be so bold?”

Said Face-of-god: “We are of Burgdale; and I will swear to thee on the edge of the sword that thou shalt not fall alive into the hands of the Dusky Men.”

===Chinese===
那人道：“我是恶人的逃奴，是从玫瑰谷（Rosedale）和黝暗人那里逃出来的。你忍心害我么？”

面神道：“我们正是黝暗人的仇敌；你可愿助我们对付他们？”

那人皱眉道：“愿意，只要你们肯立誓，不让我活着落入他们之手。不过你们是何处人，胆敢如此？”

面神道：“我们是堡谷之人；我愿以剑刃向你立誓——你绝不会活着落入黝暗人之手。”

===Original===
“Of Burgdale have I heard,” said the man; “and in sooth thou seemest not such a man as would bewray a hapless man. But now had I best bring you to some lurking-place where ye shall not be easily found of these devils, who now ofttimes scour the woods hereabout.”

Said Face-of-god: “Come first and see my fellows; and then if thou thinkest we have need to hide, it is well.”

So the man went side by side with him towards their lair, and as they went Gold-mane noted marks of stripes on his back and sides, and said: “Sorely hast thou been mishandled, poor man!”

Then the man turned on him and said somewhat fiercely: “Said I not that I had been a thrall of the Dusky Men? how then should I have escaped tormenting and scourging, if I had been with them for but three days?”

===Chinese===
那人道：“堡谷之名我曾听闻；你瞧着也不像会出卖苦命人的那种人。不过眼下我最好领你们到一个藏身之处，叫这些魔鬼不易寻获——他们如今常常在这一带林中巡查。”

面神道：“且先去见见我的伙伴；你若以为我们确需藏匿，那也好。”

于是那人与他并肩朝众人藏身处走去。一路行去，金鬃留意到他腰背之上伤痕累累，便道：“可怜人，你被折磨得好苦！”

那人闻言转过身来，颇带几分狠色道：“我岂不曾说过，我曾是黝暗人的奴隶？纵然只与他们同处三日，又怎能免受酷刑鞭挞？”

===Original===
As he spake they came about a thorn-bush, and there were the Burgdale men down in the hollow; and the man said: “Are these thy fellows? Call to mind that thou hast sworn by the edge of the sword not to hurt me.”

“Poor man!” said Face-of-god; “these are thy friends, unless thou bewrayest us.”

Then he cried aloud to his folk: “Here is now a good hap! this is a runaway thrall of the Dusky Men; of him shall we hear tidings; so cherish him all ye may.”

So the carles thronged about him and bestirred themselves to help him, and one gave him his surcoat for a kirtle, and another cast a cloak about him; and they brought him meat and drink, such as they had ready to hand: and the man looked as if he scarce believed in all this, but deemed himself to be in a dream.

===Chinese===
正说话间，两人绕过一丛荆棘，堡谷之人尽在下方空谷之中；那人道：“这些便是你的伙伴？须记你曾以剑刃立誓不加害我。”

面神道：“可怜的人！除非你出卖我们，否则他们都是你的朋友。”

便扬声对部下道：“天大的好运！这是黝暗人手下一名逃奴；我们要打听的消息正可问问他；大伙儿尽心待他。”

众汉子便围上前来争相照料，有人解下自己的罩袍权作里衣给他穿上，有人把一件斗篷披在他肩头；又把手边现成的饮食端到他面前：那人神色之间竟似不敢置信，只当自己是在梦中。

===Original===
“Now I see so many men and weapons I deem that ye have no need to skulk in caves tonight, though I know of good ones: yet shall ye do well not to light a fire till moon-setting; for the flame ye may lightly hide, but the smoke may be seen from far aloof.”

But they bade him to meat, and he needed no second bidding but ate lustily, and they gave him wine, and he drank a great draught and sighed as for joy. Then he said in a trembling voice, as though he feared a naysay:

“If ye are from Burgdale ye shall be faring back again presently; and I pray you to take me with you.”

===Chinese===
“如今我见你们人多械精，今夜倒不必钻进山洞藏身——虽说我知道几处好洞子：不过你们最好等月落之后再生火；火苗尚易遮掩，烟子却老远便能被人望见。”

众人却先请他入席用饭，他也不用让第二回，便狼吞虎咽地吃起来；众人又给他酒，他痛饮一大口，欢喜得叹了一声。然后他才以颤巍巍的嗓音开口，似怕讨个没趣：

“你们既从堡谷来，不日便要回去；我求你们带我一同走。”

===Original===
Said Face-of-god: “Yea surely, friend, that will we do, and rejoice in thee.”

Then he drank another cup which Warcliff held out to him, and spake again: “Yet if ye would abide here till about noon tomorrow, or mayhappen a little later, I would bring other runaways to see you; and them also might ye take with you: ye may think when ye see them that ye shall have small gain of their company; for poor wretched folk they be, like to myself. Yet since ye seek for tidings, herein might they do you more service than I; for amongst them are some who came out of the hapless Dale within this moon; and it is six months since I escaped. Moreover, though they may look spent and outworn now, yet if ye give them a little rest, and feed them well, they shall yet do many a day’s work for you: and I tell you that if ye take them for thralls, and put collars on their necks, and use them no worse than a goodman useth his oxen and his asses, beating them not save when they are idle or at fault, it shall be to them as if they were come to heaven out of hell, and to such goodhap as they have not thought of, save in dreams, for many and many a day. And thus I entreat you to do because ye seem to me to be happy and merciful men, who will not begrudge us this happiness.”

===Chinese===
面神道：“自然，朋友，这事我们一定办，得了你这样的人，我们欢喜还来不及。”

那人接过战崖（Warcliff）递来的一杯酒又饮了一杯，乃再开口道：“然而你们若愿在此耽到明日午时前后，或者再稍晚一些，我便去将别的逃奴引来见你们；他们几位，你们也可一并带走：你们见着他们时，或会以为留他们在身边没什么用处；因为他们都是和我一样的可怜苦命人。然你们既要打听消息，这一层上他们能帮的忙却比我更大；他们中间有几个人，是这个月才从那不幸之谷逃出来的；而我脱身已是六个月前的事了。再者，他们眼下虽然形容枯槁、精疲力竭，只要稍加歇息、好好将养，日后仍能为你们做许多日的活计：我且告诉你们，纵然把他们收作奴隶，给他们颈上套上项圈，只要待他们不比一个正经主人待自家牛驴更差——除了他们偷懒或出差错时才打——在他们便如同从地狱升入天堂，是这许多许多日子以来做梦才敢想的好运。我如此恳求你们，是因为我看你们是快乐而仁慈之人，必不至于舍不得这一点福分给我们。”

===Original===
The carles of Burgdale listened eagerly to what he said, and they looked at him with great eyes and marvelled; and their hearts were moved with pity towards him; and Stone-face said:

“Herein, O War-leader, need I give thee no rede, for thou mayst see clearly that all we deem that we should lose our manhood and become the dastards of the Warrior if we did not abide the coming of these poor men, and take them back to the Dale, and cherish them.”

“Yea,” said Wolf of Whitegarth, “and great thanks we owe to this man that he biddeth us this: for great will be the gain to us if we become so like the Gods that we may deliver the poor from misery. Now must I needs think how they shall wonder when they come to Burgstead and find out how happy it is to dwell there.”

===Chinese===
堡谷的汉子们屏息凝神听他说话，都睁大了眼睛望着他，啧啧称奇；心中都不禁生出怜悯；石面说道：

“战首（War-leader），此事我何必再给你出主意，你自能看得明明白白：我们都以为，若不去等这些可怜人来、不把他们带回谷中好生抚养，便是丢了男儿气节，沦为辱没武神（the Warrior）的懦夫。”

白院（Whitegarth）的狼（Wolf）道：“正是，我们还须多谢此人相邀：因为我们若能像诸神那样，把穷苦之人从苦难中救拔出来，所得之大实在无可估量。我此刻不禁在想：他们到了堡镇（Burgstead），发觉在那儿安居竟如此快乐，不知要怎样惊奇呢。”

===Original===
“Surely,” said Face-of-god, “thus shall we do, whatever cometh of it. But, friend of the wood, as to thralls, there be none such in the Dale, but therein are all men friends and neighbours, and even so shall ye be.”

And he fell a-musing, when he bethought him of how little he had known of sorrow.

But that man, when he beheld the happy faces of the Burgdalers, and hearkened to their friendly voices, and understood what they said, and he also was become strong with the meat and drink, he bowed his head adown and wept a long while; and they meddled not with him, till he turned again to them and said:

“Since ye are in arms, and seem to be seeking your foemen, I suppose ye wot that these tyrants and man-quellers will fall upon you in Burgdale ere the summer is well worn.”

===Chinese===
面神道：“一定如此，不管日后如何，我们都照此办理。只是，林中之友，至于奴隶——谷中并无此物，谷中人人皆为朋友邻里，你们也将一样。”

说罢便堕入沉思，想起自己从前对忧患之味竟所知甚少。

那人却不同，他望着堡谷众人欢快的脸、听着他们友善的声音、听明白他们的话，加之饮食下肚、气力渐复，竟低下头去，哭了许久；众人也不去搅他，直到他重新转向他们，说道：

“你们既全副武装、似在寻觅仇敌，我想你们必已知晓：这些暴虐嗜杀之徒，在今年夏未过尽之前，便要发兵来犯堡谷。”

===Original===
“So much we deem indeed,” said Face-of-god, “but we were fain to hear the certainty of it, and how thou knowest thereof.”

Said the man: “It was six moons ago that I fled, as I have told you; and even then it was the common talk amongst our masters that there were fair dales to the south which they would overrun. Man would say to man: We were over many in Silverdale, and we needed more thralls, because those we had were lessening, and especially the women; now are we more at ease in Rosedale, though we have sent thralls to Silverdale; but yet we can bear no more men from thence to eat up our stock from us: let them fare south to the happy dales, and conquer them, and we will go with them and help therein, whether we come back to Rosedale or no. Such talk did I hear then with mine own ears: but some of those whom I shall bring to you tomorrow shall know better what is doing, since they have fled from Rosedale but a few days. Moreover, there is a man and a woman who have fled from Silverdale itself, and are but a month from it, journeying all the time save when they must needs hide; and these say that their masters have got to know the way to Burgdale, and are minded for it before the winter, as I said; and nought else but the ways thither do they desire to know, since they have no fear.”

By then was night come, and though the moon was high in heaven, and lighted all that waste, the Burgdalers must needs light a fire for cooking their meat, whatsoever that woodsman might say; moreover, the night was cold and somewhat frosty. A little before they had come to that place they had shot a fat buck and some smaller deer, but of other meat they had no great store, though there was wine enough. So they lit their fire in the thickest of the thorn-bush to hide it all they might, and thereat they cooked their venison and the trouts which the runaway had taken, and they fell to, and ate and drank and were merry, making much of that poor man till him-seemed he was gotten into the company of the kindest of the Gods.

===Chinese===
面神道：“我们也是这般猜测，只是愿听个确凿，并问问你是从何处得知。”

那人道：“我逃出来是六个月前的事了，方才已说过；彼时便是我们的主子之间也常常谈及：南边有几处丰饶山谷，他们要发兵去侵占。人与人之间彼此说道：我们在银谷人太多了，需要更多的奴隶，因为我们手头的奴隶越来越少，尤其是女奴；如今我们在玫瑰谷宽松了些，虽然也往银谷送过奴隶；但即便如此，我们再不能从那里往外抽人，来吃我们的存粮了：让他们南下到那些安乐之谷去，征服那些地方，我们随他们同去、助一臂之力便是，回不回玫瑰谷再说。这些话我当时是亲耳听见的：但明日我要引到你们面前的几个人，会更清楚眼下的情势，因为他们几天前才从玫瑰谷逃出来。再者，有一男一女是从银谷本身逃出来的，离开那里才一个月，一路奔波，只有不得不藏匿时才停下；这两人说，他们的主子已经探明了通往堡谷的路，打算在入冬之前下手，正如我方才所说；他们除了去堡谷的路径之外，旁的一概无心打听，因为他们全无畏惧之心。”

其时夜已降临，虽说明月高悬、照彻那片荒野，堡谷之人却不能不生火煮食，不管那林中猎人怎么说；况且夜里寒凉，颇有霜气。在他们到此之前不久，刚刚射获一头肥鹿和几只小鹿，然而除了鹿肉之外别无多少荤腥，酒倒充足。于是他们在那荆棘丛最密处生了火，尽可能遮掩，在火上烤起鹿肉和那逃奴所捕的鳟鱼，众人便大吃大喝、十分快活，对那可怜人百般照拂，直教他觉得自己仿佛落到了最仁慈的诸神之中。

===Original===
But when they were full, Face-of-god spake to him, and asked him his name; and he named himself Dallach; but said he: “Lord, this is according to the naming of men in Rosedale before we were enthralled: but now what names have thralls? Also I am not altogether of the blood of them of Rosedale, but of better and more warrior-like kin.”

===Chinese===
众人吃饱之后，面神开口问他姓名；他自报名为达拉赫（Dallach）；却又说道：“大人，这是玫瑰谷之人未被贬为奴之前的叫法：如今奴隶还有什么名字呢？况且我也并非全是玫瑰谷人的血脉，而是出自更高贵、更尚武的宗族。”

===Original===
Said Face-of-god: “Thou hast named Silverdale; knowest thou it?”

Dallach answered: “I have never seen it. It is far hence; in a week’s journey, making all diligence, and not being forced to hide and skulk like those runaways, ye shall come to the mouth thereof lying west, where its rock-walls fall off toward the plain.”

“But,” said Face-of-god, “is there no other way into that Dale?”

“Nay, none that folk wot of,” said Dallach, “except to bold cragsmen with their lives in their hands.”

“Knowest thou aught of the affairs of Silverdale?” said Face-of-god.

===Chinese===
面神道：“你提到了银谷；你可到过那里？”

达拉赫答道：“我从未见过。离这里很远；以全速赶路、又不必像那些逃奴那样躲躲藏藏来算，要走一个星期的路，方能抵达它那朝西的谷口，那里的石壁向平原低伏下去。”

面神道：“不过，难道没有别的路可入那谷吗？”

达拉赫道：“没有，凡人所知的一条也无，除非是那种把性命攥在手里的胆大攀崖客。”

面神道：“银谷的近况，你可晓得些什么？”

===Original===
Said Dallach: “Somewhat I know: we wot that but a few years ago there was a valiant folk dwelling therein, who were lords of the whole dale, and that they were vanquished by the Dusky Men: but whether they were all slain and enthralled we wot not; but we deem it otherwise. As for me it is of their blood that I am partly come; for my father’s father came thence to settle in Rosedale, and wedded a woman of the Dale, who was my father’s mother.”
