For now he doubted whether the other folk were aught save shows and shadows, and she the Goddess who had fashioned them out of nothing for his bewilderment, presently to return to nothing.

Yet whatever he might fear or doubt, he went up the hall towards her till he was quite nigh to her, and there he stood silent, wondering at her beauty and desiring her kindness.

===Chinese===
于是他起身穿衣，走进厅堂四下张望，起初只当厅中空无一人。但后来他抬头望见大厅上首的山墙，墙下挂着一幅极华美的帷幔，帷幔前一条覆着金银织锦的长凳上，端坐着一位光彩照人的女子。他看了又看，想看那女子会不会动弹、是不是个活人；她却转过头来朝他一望——啊，正是那位朋友。他又惊又惧又生渴慕，一颗心几乎要跳到嗓子眼儿。此刻他不禁怀疑，先前那些人是不是不过是幻影虚形，而她才是那位女神，专为使他神魂颠倒而凭空造出那些幻象，转眼便要复归于虚无。

然而无论他心怀怎样的疑惧，他仍沿着大厅向她走去，直到离她极近，默默站着，惊叹她的美丽，渴慕她的温存。

===Original===
Grey-eyed she was like her brother; but her hair the colour of red wheat: her lips full and red, her chin round, her nose fine and straight. Her hands and all her body fashioned exceeding sweetly and delicately; yet not as if she were an image of which the like might be found if the craftsman were but deft enough to make a perfect thing, but in such a way that there was none like to her for those that had eyes to behold her as she was; and none could ever be made like to her, even by such a master-craftsman as could fashion a body without a blemish.

She was clad in a white smock, whose hems were broidered with gold wire and precious gems of the Mountains, and over that a gown woven of gold and silver: scarce hath the world such another. On her head was a fillet of gold and gems, and there were wondrous gold rings on her arms: her feet lay bare on the dark grey wolf-skin that was stretched before her.

===Chinese===
她同她兄弟一样生着一双灰色的眼睛，头发却是红麦的颜色：嘴唇丰润朱红，下巴圆润，鼻梁秀挺。她的双手与全身都生得极其甜美精巧；然而并非那种"只要工匠巧到极致、便能照样复制出第二件完美造像"的模样，而是如此：凡有幸亲眼目睹她真容的人，便知世上再无与她相仿者；即便有能工巧匠可雕琢出一具毫无瑕疵的身躯，也永远造不出第二个她来。

她身穿一件白色罩衫，衣边以金线与山中宝石绣成，外罩一件金银织就的长袍：普天之下怕是再找不出第二件。头上束一条嵌宝金发带，臂上戴着奇巧的金钏；那双赤足搁在面前铺着的一张深灰色狼皮上。

===Original===
She smiled kindly upon his solemn and troubled face, and her voice sounded strangely familiar to him coming from all that loveliness, as she said: “Hail, Face-of-god! here am I left alone, although I deemed last night that I should be gone with the others. Therefore am I fain to show myself to thee in fairer array than yesternight; for though we dwell in the wildwood, from the solace of folk, yet are we not of thralls’ blood. But come now, I bid thee break thy fast and talk with me a little while; and then shalt thou depart in peace.”

===Chinese===
她对着他那张凝重而惶惑的脸和蔼地微笑着。在那样一位绝代佳人身上听见她的声音，他竟有一种奇异的熟悉之感。她说道："面神，你好。他们全都走了，只留下我一个人在此，虽然昨夜我还以为我会随众人一同离去。所以我乐意以比昨夜更齐整的装束来见你；因为我们虽然居住在荒林之中、远避人境，却并非奴婢之种。来罢，我请你用些早餐，与我略谈片刻；然后你便可安然离去。"

===Original===
Spake Face-of-god, and his voice trembled as he spake: “What art thou? Last night I deemed at whiles once and again that thou wert of the Gods; and now that I behold thee thus, and it is broad daylight, and of those others is no more to be seen than if they had never lived, I cannot but deem that it is even so, and that thou comest from the City that shall never perish. Now if thou be a goddess, I have nought to pray thee, save to slay me speedily if thou hast a mind for my death. But if thou art a woman—”

She broke in: “Gold-mane, stay thy prayer and hold thy peace for this time, lest thou repent when repentance availeth not. And this I say because I am none of the Gods nor akin to them, save far off through the generations, as art thou also, and all men of goodly kindred. Now I bid thee eat thy meat, since ’tis ill talking betwixt a full man and a fasting; and I have dight it myself with mine own hands; for Bow-may and the Wood-mother went away with the rest three hours before dawn. Come sit and eat as thou hast a hardy heart; as forsooth thou shouldest do if I were a very goddess. Take heed, friend, lest I take thee for some damsel of the lower Dale arrayed in Earl’s garments.”

===Chinese===
面神开口了，说话时声音发颤："你究竟是什么人？昨夜我曾一而再、再而三地觉得你是神祇之属；如今我这样看着你，又分明是大白天，那些旁人则消失得一干二净，仿佛从未存在过一般，我不能不认定事情正是如此——你乃是从那座永不倾覆之城来的。你若真是女神，我别无所求，只求你若要取我性命，便快快杀了我。但你若是一个女子——"

她打断他道："金鬃，且住，收回你的祷告，这一回先别作声，免得日后追悔却已不及。我这般说，是因为我并非诸神之一，也非神族近亲，不过是隔着无数世代、才与神有那一点远的渊源罢了——你也一样，一切出身高贵的良家男子都是如此。我劝你吃你的饭罢，一人空腹、一人饱腹地说话，总是不妥；这饭菜是我亲手为你备下的，因为弓娘（Bow-may）与林母（the Wood-mother）已于黎明前三个时辰随众人一同离去。来，坐下吃罢，要拿出一条硬汉的心肠来；便是我真是一位女神，你也理当如此。当心啊，朋友，免得我把你当作下谷来的哪位小娘子，穿戴着伯爵的衣裳。"

===Original===
She laughed therewith, and leaned toward him and put forth her hand to him, and he took it and caressed it; and the exceeding beauty of her body and of the raiment which was as it were a part of her and her loveliness, made her laughter and her friendly words strange to him, as if one did not belong to the other; as in a dream it might be. Nevertheless he did as she bade him, and sat at the board and ate, while she leaned forward on the arm of her chair and spake to him in friendly wise. And he wondered as she spake that she knew so much of him and his: and he kept saying to himself: “She drew me hither; wherefore did she so?”

===Chinese===
她说着笑了起来，向他探过身去，伸出手给他。他接过她的手轻轻抚弄。她身上那种惊人之美，连同那仿佛与她本人及她的可爱融为一体的衣裳，使她的笑语与亲切的话语在他听来都显得奇异，仿佛一头与另一头并不相称；如同梦中光景一般。然而他还是照她的吩咐做了，在桌前坐下进食，她则俯身在椅臂上，以友善之态同他说话。她说话时他很惊讶，她对他和他的家人竟知道得这么多；他不停地在心里念叨："是她把我引到这儿来的；她为什么要这样呢？"

===Original===
But she said: “Gold-mane, how fareth thy father the Alderman? is he as good a wright as ever?”

He told her: Yea, that ever was his hammer on the iron, the copper, and the gold, and that no wright in the Dale was as deft as he.

Said she: “Would he not have had thee seek to the Cities, to see the ways of the outer world?”

“Yea,” said he.

She said: “Thou wert wise to naysay that offer; thou shalt have enough to do in the Dale and round about it in twelve months’ time.”

“Art thou foresighted?” said he.

===Chinese===
她却问："金鬃，你父亲长老可好？他还是像从前那样，是一位好匠人么？"

他告诉她：是的，他的铁锤总在铁上、铜上、金上敲个不停，堡谷里再没有哪个匠人比他更巧了。

她道："他没劝你去各处城邦走走，见识见识外面的世界么？"

"劝过。"他说。

她道："你回绝了，倒也明智；不出十二个月，你在堡谷之内、堡谷四周，便有的是事要做。"

"你能未卜先知？"他问。

===Original===
“Folk have called me so,” she said, “but I wot not. But thy brother Hall-face, how fareth he?”

“Well;” said he, “to my deeming he is the Sword of our House, and the Warrior of the Dale, if the days were ready for him.”

“And Stone-face, that stark ancient,” she said, “doth he still love the Folk of the Dale, and hate all other folks?”

“Nay,” he said, “I know not that, but I know that he loveth as, and above all me and my father.”

===Chinese===
"世人有这般说过，"她答道，"可我自己也不甚了然。但你兄弟厅面可好？"

"很好，"他说，"依我看，若时世相须，他必是我家的宝剑、堡谷的勇士。"

"那石面呢，那位严峻的古稀老人，"她道，"他可仍只爱谷中之民，而仇视一切他族么？"

"不然，"他说，"这我可不清楚；我只知他爱谷民之心一如既往，而其中最爱的，便是我和我父亲。"

===Original===
Again she spake: “How fareth the Bride, the fair maid to whom thou art affianced?”

As she spake, it was to him as if his heart was stricken cold; but he put a force upon himself, and neither reddened nor whitened, nor changed countenance in any way; so he answered:

“She was well the eve of yesterday.” Then he remembered what she was, and her beauty and valour, and he constrained himself to say: “Each day she groweth fairer; there is no man’s son and no daughter of woman that does not love her; yea, the very beasts of field and fold love her.”

The Friend looked at him steadily and spake no word, but a red flush mounted to her cheeks and brow and changed her face; and he marvelled thereat; for still he misdoubted that she was a Goddess. But it passed away in a moment, and she smiled and said:

===Chinese===
她又问："那新娘呢——你那位已许聘的美丽未婚妻，她可好？"

她说话之时，他只觉心口像被冰水击中；但他强自按捺，既不脸红，也不脸白，神色丝毫不变，于是答道：

"前天傍晚她还很好。"随即他想起她是谁，想起她的美貌与才德，便强逼着自己说："她一日比一日更美；天底下没有一个男子、一个女子不爱她；便是田野里、栏圈里的牲畜，也都爱她。"

那位朋友定定地看着他，一言不发，一抹红晕却涌上她的双颊与额头，变了她的脸色。他对此深感诧异，因为他心中仍怀疑她是一位女神。但这红晕一闪即逝，她微笑道：

===Original===
“Guest, thou seemest to wonder that I know concerning thee and the Dale and thy kindred. But now shalt thou wot that I have been in the Dale once and again, and my brother oftener still; and that I have seen thee before yesterday.”

===Chinese===
"客人，你似乎奇怪我怎会知道你、知道堡谷、知道你的亲族。但如今你该知道，我不止一次到过堡谷，我兄弟去的次数更多；而且早在昨天以前，我便见过你了。"

===Original===
“That is marvellous,” quoth he, “for sure am I that I have not seen thee.”

“Yet thou hast seen me,” she said; “yet not altogether as I am now;” and therewith she smiled on him friendly.

“How is this?” said he; “art thou a skin-changer?”

“Yea, in a fashion,” she said. “Hearken! dost thou perchance remember a day of last summer when there was a market holden in Burgstead; and there stood in the way over against the House of the Face a tall old carle who was trucking deer-skins for diverse gear; and with him was a queen, tall and dark-skinned, somewhat well-liking, her hair bound up in a white coif so that none of it could be seen; by the token that she had a large stone of mountain blue set in silver stuck in the said coif?”

===Chinese===
"这就奇了，"他说，"因为我敢肯定，我从未见过你。"

"可是你确实见过我，"她道，"只是不像我现在这般模样罢了。"说着又对他亲切地笑了笑。

"这是怎么回事？"他问，"你是换形者么？"

"可算是罢，不过是其中一种而已。"她道，"你听着！你可还记得去年夏天堡镇逢集的那一日？面神之宅对面的路上，站着一个高大的老汉，正拿鹿皮换各样物件；他身边有一位贵妇模样的妇人，身材高挑、肤色黝黑，略略丰腴，头发包在一条白头巾里，一根也露不出来——凭一个记号便可认出她来：那条头巾上，别着一颗大颗的镶银山蓝宝石。"

===Original===
As she spoke she set her hand to her bosom and drew something from it, and held forth her hand to Gold-mane, and lo amidst the palm the great blue stone set in silver.

“Wondrous as a dream is this,” said Face-of-god, “for these twain I remember well, and what followed.”

===Chinese===
她一边说，一边伸手入怀，从怀中取出一件物事，朝金鬃伸出手来——只见她掌心之中，正是那颗大颗镶银的山蓝宝石。

"这事简直如梦一般，"面神道，"这两个人我记得清清楚楚，后来所发生的事，我也记得。"

===Original===
She said: “I will tell thee that. There came a man of the Shepherd-Folk, drunk or foolish, or both, who began to chaffer with the big carle; but ever on the queen were his eyes set, and presently he put forth his hand to her to clip her, whereon the big carle hove up his fist and smote him, so that he fell to earth noseling. Then ran the folk together to hale off the stranger and help the shepherd, and it was like that the stranger should be mishandled. Then there thrust through the press a young man with yellow hair and grey eyes, who cried out, ‘Fellows, let be! The stranger had the right of it; this is no matter to make a quarrel or a court case of. Let the market go on! This man and maid are true folk.’ So when the folk heard the young man and his bidding, they forebore and let the carle and the queen be, and the shepherd went his ways little hurt. Now then, who was this young man?”

===Chinese===
她道："我这就告诉你。来了一个牧羊之民的男人，醉了也罢、蠢了也罢，或者二者兼有，开始同那大汉讨价还价；可他一双眼睛一刻不离地盯着那贵妇，不久便伸出手去要搂抱她。那大汉便抡起拳头一拳打去，打得他嘴啃泥一般摔倒在地。于是众人围拢上来，要拖走那外乡人、扶起那牧人，看样子那外乡人免不了要挨一顿好打。这时一个黄头发灰眼睛的年轻人挤过人群，高声喊道：'伙计们，住手！外乡人理直气壮；这点事，犯不着打架，也犯不着闹到堂上去。让集市照常进行罢！这一男一女，都是正经人。'众人听了那年轻人的话与他这一番劝导，便住了手，不再为难那大汉与贵妇；那牧人也只受了点轻伤，自去了。那么请问，这个年轻人是谁？"

===Original===
Quoth Gold-mane: “It was even I, and meseemeth it was no great deed to do.”

“Yea,” she said, “and the big carle was my brother, and the tall queen, it was myself.”

===Chinese===
金鬃道："正是我。我看这也不是什么了不起的事。"

"是了，"她道，"那大汉便是我兄弟，那位高挑的贵妇，就是我自己。"

===Original===
“How then,” said he, “for she was as dark-skinned as a dwarf, and thou so bright and fair?”

She said: “Well, if the woods are good for nothing else, yet are they good for the growing of herbs, and I know the craft of simpling; and with one of these herbs had I stained my skin and my brother’s also. And it showed the darker beneath the white coif.”

===Chinese===
"那怎么可能，"他说，"她肤色黑得像个矮人，你却如此明艳白皙？"

她道："这个嘛，林子就算别的好处没有，倒长得出好草药来，我懂得采药的本领；我便用其中一种草药，把自己的皮肤染了色，连我兄弟的也一并染了。那肤色衬在白头巾之下，便显得更黑了。"

===Original===
“Yea,” said he, “but why must ye needs fare in feigned shapes? Ye would have been welcome guests in the Dale howsoever ye had come.”

“I may not tell thee hereof as now,” said she.

===Chinese===
"是了，"他说，"可你们又何必乔装打扮前来呢？无论以何种模样，你们在堡谷都会是受欢迎的客人。"

"此事我此刻还不能告诉你。"她道。

===Original===
Said Gold-mane: “Yet thou mayst belike tell me wherefore was that thy brother desired to slay me yesterday, if he knew me, who I was.”

“Gold-mane,” she said, “thou art not slain, so little story need be made of that: for the rest, belike he knew thee not at that moment. So it falls with us, that we look to see foes rather than friends in the wildwoods. Many uncouth things are therein. Moreover, I must tell thee of my brother that whiles he is as the stalled bull late let loose, and nothing is good to him save battle and onset; and then is he blind and knows not friend from foe.”

===Chinese===
金鬃道："不过你或许可以告诉我，令兄昨日既要杀我，他若认得我是谁，却又所为何来？"

"金鬃，"她道，"你并未被杀，这点事便不必多提了；至于其余，他当时多半没认出你来。我们在荒林中谋生，便是如此——宁可把人当作仇敌，也不敢把人当作朋友。林中怪事多得很。此外，我还须替我兄弟说一句：他有时就像一头久关栏中、刚被放出来的牡牛，唯有厮杀冲杀才合他的意；那时他便瞎了眼，认不清敌友了。"

===Original===
Said Face-of-god: “Thou hast asked of me and mine; wilt thou not tell me of thee and thine?”

“Nay,” she said, “not as now; thou must betake thee to the way. Whither wert thou wending when thou happenedst upon us?”

He said: “I know not; I was seeking something, but I knew not what—meseemeth that now I have found it.”

===Chinese===
面神道："你问了我、问了我家中之人；你可愿把你自己、你家中之人，也说与我听听？"

"不，"她道，"此刻不能；你须得上路了。你撞见我们之前，是要往何处去？"

他说："我不知道；我在找寻一样东西，却不知是什么——如今看来，我已找到了。"

===Original===
“Art thou for the great mountains seeking gems?” she said. “Yet go not thither today: for who knoweth what thou shalt meet there that shall be thy foe?”

He said: “Nay, nay; I have nought to do but to abide here as long as I may, looking upon thee and hearkening to thy voice.”

Her eyes were upon his, but yet she did not seem to see him, and for a while she answered not; and still he wondered that mere words should come from so fair a thing; for whether she moved foot, or hand, or knee, or turned this way or that, each time she stirred it was a caress to his very heart.

===Chinese===
"你是要上大山里去找宝石么？"她问。"只是今日别往那里去：谁知你会碰上什么东西，竟会是你对头的？"

他说："不，不；我别无他事，只想尽可能久地留在这里，看着你，听你的声音。"

她的双眼望着他的双眼，却又仿佛没看见他，有一会儿她没有作答；他始终惊奇，如此美丽的一件造物，竟会吐出寻常的话语来；因为她无论动一动脚、动一动手、动一动膝盖，或转向这一边、那一边，每一次动作，都仿佛是对他心底的抚慰。

===Original===
He spake again: “May I not abide here a while? What scathe may be in that?”

“It is not so,” she said; “thou must depart, and that straightway: lo, there lieth thy spear which the Wood-mother hath brought in from the waste. Take thy gear to thee and wend thy ways. Have patience! I will lead thee to the place where we first met and there give thee farewell.”

===Chinese===
他又道："我不能在此再盘桓片刻么？这能有什么妨害？"

"不行，"她道，"你必须离去，而且要立刻就走：瞧，那儿放着你的那杆长矛，是林母从荒野里替你带回来的。收拾好你的物件上路罢。耐着性子！我会带你到我们初次相遇之处，在那里与你作别。"

===Original===
Therewith she arose and he also perforce, and when they came to the doorway she stepped across the threshold and then turned back and gave him her hand and so led him forth, the sun flashing back from her golden raiment. Together they went over the short grey grass of that hillside till they came to the place where he had arisen from that wrestle with her brother. There she stayed him and said:

===Chinese===
说罢她站起身来，他也只得跟着起身。两人来到门口，她迈过门槛，又回过头把手伸给他，引他出去；阳光自她那一身金色的衣裳上反射出耀眼的光华。两人并肩走过山坡上那片短短的灰草，直到他昨夜与她兄弟角力之后爬起来的地方。她让他停下，说道：

===Original===
“This is the place; here must we part.”

But his heart failed him and he faltered in his speech as he said:

“When shall I see thee again? Wilt thou slay me if I seek to thee hither once more?”

===Chinese===
"就是此地了；我们须在此分别。"

他却壮不起胆气，说话也发起结来：

"我何时才能再见到你？若我再寻到这里来找你，你会杀了我么？"

===Original===
“Hearken,” she said, “autumn is now a-dying into winter: let winter and its snows go past: nor seek to me hither; for me thou should’st not find, but thy death thou mightest well fall in with; and I would not that thou shouldest die. When winter is gone, and spring is on the land, if thou hast not forgotten us thou shalt meet us again. Yet shalt thou go further than this Woodland Hall. In Shadowy Vale shalt thou seek to me then, and there will I talk with thee.”

===Chinese===
"你听着，"她道，"如今秋将尽、冬将至：你且让冬日与其冰雪自行过去：莫要到这里来寻我；你来寻我也寻我不着，倒很可能撞上你自己的死期；我可不愿你死。待冬天过去、春天来到大地之上，你若没有忘了我们，自会与我们再见。只是那时你要走得比这处林中之堂更远。到时你当往幽谷（Shadowy Vale）来寻我，我会在那里与你说话。"

===Original===
“And where,” said he, “is Shadowy Vale? for thereof have I never heard tell.”

She said: “The token when it cometh to thee shall show thee thereof and the way thither. Art thou a babbler, Gold-mane?”

He said: “I have won no prize for babbling hitherto.”

She said: “If thou listest to babble concerning what hath befallen thee on the Mountain, so do, and repent it once only, that is, thy life long.”

“Why should I say any word thereof?” said he. “Dost thou not know the sweetness of such a tale untold?”

===Chinese===
"可是，"他说，"幽谷在何处？我从未听人说起过。"

她道："那信物到了你手中，自会告诉你幽谷之所在、与通往之路。金鬃，你是个多嘴的人么？"

他说："我至今未曾因多嘴得过什么奖赏。"

她道："你若爱把山上这番遭遇拿去说嘴，只管去说，但只许后悔一次——也就是说，懊悔一辈子。"

"我为何要对人提起半个字？"他说，"你难道不知，这样一段事，不说出来，才最有甘味么？"

===Original===
He spake as one who is somewhat wrathful, and she answered humbly and kindly:

“Well is that. Bide thou the token that shall lead thee to Shadowy Vale. Farewell now.”

===Chinese===
他说这话时带着几分恼意。她却谦和而亲切地回答：

"这样便好。你且等那引你去幽谷的信物罢。就此别过了。"

===Original===
She drew her hand from his, and turned and went her ways swiftly to the house: he could not choose but gaze on her as she went glittering-bright and fair in that grey place of the mountains, till the dark doorway swallowed up her beauty. Then he turned away and took the path through the pinewoods, muttering to himself as he went:

“What thing have I done now that hitherto I had not done? What manner of man am I today other than the man I was yesterday?”

===Chinese===
她从他的掌中抽回手，转身快步朝屋子走去。在这灰蒙蒙的山间之地，她浑身光彩夺目、明艳动人，他不由自主地目送她，直到那幽暗的门口将她那一份美丽吞没。然后他转过身，踏上穿过松林的小径，一边走一边自言自语：

"我如今做了什么事，是以前不曾做过的？今日的我，与昨日的我，究竟有何不同？"

## XXXV Face-of-God Talketh with the Sun-Beam / 三十五 面神与日光相语

===Original===
Face-of-god was at the Bridge on the morrow before sun-rising, and as he turned about at the Bridge-foot he saw the Sun-beam coming down the street; and his heart rose to his mouth at the sight of her, and he went to meet her and took her by the hand; and there were no words between them till they had kissed and caressed each other, for there was no one stirring about them. So they went over the Bridge into the meadows, and eastward of the beaten path thereover.

The grass was growing thick and strong, and it was full of flowers, as the cowslip and the oxlip, and the chequered daffodil, and the wild tulip: the blackthorn was well-nigh done blooming, but the hawthorn was in bud, and in some places growing white. It was a fair morning, warm and cloudless, but the night had been misty, and the haze still hung about the meadows of the Dale where they were wettest, and the grass and its flowers were heavy with dew, so that the Sun-beam went barefoot in the meadow. She had a dark cloak cast over her kirtle, and had left her glittering gown behind her in the House.

===Chinese===
次日日出之前，面神已在大桥之上；他在桥头转过身来，便见日光正沿街而来。一见她，他那颗心直提到口边。他迎上前去，执住她的手；二人之间并无一言，直至彼此亲吻抚慰方休——因四周并无他人走动。于是他们过了桥，走入草甸，并自桥上踏出的小径偏东而行。

草长得既密且壮，其中繁花满布：如立金花、如报春花、如格子水仙、如野郁金香，皆是。黑刺李的花已开得差不多尽了，山楂却已含苞，有几处更已泛白。那是个美好的清晨，温暖而无云；然夜里曾起薄雾，谷中草甸最湿之处，仍缭绕着轻霭；草与花皆被露水压得低垂，于是日光便赤足行于草甸之上。她在长裙外披了一件深色斗篷，那件光华闪烁的袍子则留在了宅中。

===Original===
They went along hand in hand exceeding fain of each other, and the sun rose as they went, and the long beams of gold shone through the tops of the tall trees across the grass they trod, and a light wind rose up in the north, as Face-of-god stayed a moment and turned toward the Face of the Sun and prayed to Him, while the Sun-beam’s hand left the War-leader’s hand and stole up to his golden locks and lay amongst them.

Presently they went on, and the feet of Face-of-god led him unwitting toward the chestnut grove by the old dyke where he had met the Bride such a little while ago, till he bethought whither he was going and stopped short and reddened; and the Sun-beam noted it, but spake not; but he said: “Hereby is a fair place for us to sit and talk till the day’s work beginneth.”

So then he turned aside, and soon they came to a hawthorn brake out of which arose a great tall-stemmed oak, showing no green as yet save a little on its lower twigs; and anigh it, yet with room for its boughs to grow freely, was a great bird-cherry tree, all covered now with sweet-smelling white blossoms. There they sat down on the trunk of a tree felled last year, and she cast off her cloak, and took his face between her two hands and kissed him long and fondly, and for a while their joy had no word. But when speech came to them, it was she that spake first and said:

===Chinese===
二人执手而行，彼此满怀欣悦；正行之间，太阳升起，金色长光穿过高树之巅，照在他们所踏的草地之上；北面起了一阵微风。面神驻足片刻，转身朝向太阳之容，向他祈祷；日光的那只手便从战帅（War-leader）手中抽离，悄然伸上去，落入他金色的发卷之间。

不多时他们又往前走，面神的双脚不知不觉引着他，朝那旧堤边的栗林而去——就在不久之前，他还在那里与新娘相会。他猛然想起自己所往何处，顿时止步，脸上一红；日光看在眼里，却不开口；他便说道："此处附近倒有个好去处，正可容我们坐下闲谈，等白日的活计开始。"

于是他转开去路，不多时他们便走到一片山楂丛前，丛中拔起一棵高大挺拔的橡树，枝头尚未吐绿，唯最下的几根细枝略有绿意；紧挨着它——又留出余地让它枝条自由舒展——是一棵大稠李，此时满树覆盖着芬芳的白花。二人便在去年所伐的一段树干上坐下；她褪下斗篷，双手捧住他的脸，长长而深情地亲他；一时之间，他们的喜悦无以言表。及至言语回到唇边，先开口的却是她：

===Original===
“Gold-mane, my dear, sorely I wonder at thee and at me, how we are changed since that day last autumn when I first saw thee. Whiles I think, didst thou not laugh when thou wert by thyself that day, and mock at me privily, that I must needs take such wisdom on myself, and lesson thee standing like a stripling before me. Dost thou not call it all to mind and make merry over it, now that thou art become a great chieftain and a wise warrior, and I am yet what I always was, a young maiden of the kindred; save that now I abide no longer for my love?”

Her face was exceeding bright and rippled with joyous smiles, and he looked at her and deemed that her heart was overflowing with happiness, and he wondered at her indeed that she was so glad of him, and he said:

“Yea, indeed, oft do I see that morning in the woodland hall and thee and me therein, as one looketh on a picture; yea verily, and I laugh, yet is it for very bliss; neither do I mock at all. Did I not deem thee a God then? and am I not most happy now when I can call it thus to mind? And as to thee, thou wert wise then, and yet art thou wise now. Yea, I thought thee a God; and if we are changed, is it not rather that thou hast lifted me up to thee, and not come down to me?”

===Chinese===
"金鬃，我的爱人，我着实惊异于你和我——自去年秋日我初次见你那天起，我们变化何其之大。我有时不禁想：那一天你独处之时，岂不曾暗自好笑，私下里嘲弄我，说我竟非要摆出一副老成的智者模样，训诫着立在我面前宛如少年郎的你？如今你已成了一位大酋领、一位明智的武士，我却仍是向来那个样子——宗族中一名年轻少女；所不同者，唯如今我不再为我的爱而等候罢了——这一切，你岂不在心中一一追忆，引为乐事？"

她的脸庞明亮非常，涟漪般荡漾着欢快的笑意；他看着她，只觉她的心正溢出幸福。他着实惊异她竟能为他如此欣喜，便说道：

"正是，正是——林中厅堂里那个清晨，还有其中的你和我，我常常恍若看一幅画般看见它；是啊，我真的会笑，但那是极度幸福的笑；我绝无半点嘲弄。当年我岂不曾视你为神？如今我能将此事如此唤回心头，岂非最为幸福？至于你，那时你是明智的，如今你也仍明智。是的，那时我以为你是神；若说我们之间有了变化，岂不是你反倒把我提升到你身边，而非你屈身就我？"

===Original===
Yet therewithal he knit his brows somewhat and said:

“Yet thou hast not to tell me that all thy love for thy Folk, and thy yearning hope for its recoverance, was but a painted show. Else why shouldst thou love me the better now that I am become a chieftain, and therefore am more meet to understand thy hope and thy sorrow? Did I not behold thee as we stood before the Wolf of the Hall of Shadowy Vale, how the tears stood in thine eyes as thou beheldest him, and thine hand in mine quivered and clung to me, and thou wert all changed in a moment of time? Was all this then but a seeming and a beguilement?”

“O young man,” she said, “hast thou not said it, that we stood there close together, and my hand in thine and desire growing up in me? Dost thou not know how this also quickeneth the story of our Folk, and our goodwill towards the living, and remembrance of the dead? Shall they have lived and desired, and we deny desire and life? Or tell me: what was it made thee so chieftain-like in the Hall yesterday, so that thou wert the master of all our wills, for as self-willed as some of us were? Was it not that I, whom thou deemest lovely, was thereby watching thee and rejoicing in thee? Did not the sweetness of thy love quicken thee? Yet because of that was thy warrior’s wisdom and thy foresight an empty show? Heedest thou nought the Folk of the Dale? Wouldest thou sunder from the children of the Fathers, and dwell amongst strangers?”

===Chinese===
然而说到此处，他微微皱眉，又道：

"然而你总不至于要对我说：你对族人全部的爱，以及你期盼他们复兴的那种渴慕之情，不过是一场画出来的假象。否则为何如今我成了酋领——因而也更配理解你的希望与哀愁——你便更加爱我了呢？我们站在幽谷之厅那尊狼像前之时，我岂不曾看着你么？你望着它时，眼中如何噙满泪水，你在我掌中的手又如何颤抖着紧攀着我，你整个人如何在那一刹那间都变了样？这一切，难道都不过是一场假相、一场欺蒙？"

"年轻人啊，"她说，"你自己方才不是说了——我们紧挨着站在那里，我的手在你手中，欲求在我心中生发？你难道不知，这也使我族的故事、我们对生者的善意、对死者的追忆，都一并更加生动起来？他们既已活过、爱过，我们难道就要背弃爱与生？或者你告诉我：昨日厅堂之上，是什么使你如此酋领气度，使我们众人——尽管有几个人执拗不改——的意志都受你驾驭？岂不正是因你所钟爱的我，正注视着你、为你而欣悦？你爱的甜蜜岂不曾令你更加机敏？然则因这缘故，你那武士的明智、那先见之明，便成了空洞的虚饰么？你难道对谷中之民毫不在意？你竟要脱离先祖的子嗣，去与陌生人同居？"

===Original===
He kissed her and smiled on her and said: “Did I not say of thee that thou wert wiser than the daughters of men? See how wise thou hast made me!”

She spake again: “Nay, nay, there was no feigning in my love for my people. How couldest thou think it, when the Fathers and the kindred have made this body that thou lovest, and the voice of their songs is in the speech thou deemest sweet?”

He said: “Sweet friend, I deemed not that there was feigning in thee: I was but wondering what I am and how I was fashioned, that I should make thee so glad that thou couldst for a while forget thy hope of the days before we met.”

She said: “O how glad, how glad! Yet was I nought hapless. In despite of all trouble I had no down-weighing grief, and I had the hope of my people before me. Good were my days; but I knew not till now how glad a child of man may be.”

===Chinese===
他亲她，对她笑，说道："我岂不曾说过，你比人间的女儿都更明智？瞧你把我变得多明智！"

她又道："不，不，我对族人之爱绝无虚假。你怎么能这般想呢？这具你所爱的身躯，本就是先祖与宗族所造就的；你所觉得甜美的话语之中，本就有他们歌声的余响。"

他说："甜美的朋友，我并非以为你有虚假：我只是惊异自己是什么、又是如何被造就的，竟能令你如此欣喜，乃至一时忘却我们相遇之前那些日子里的希望。"

她说："啊，何等欣喜，何等欣喜！然而我也并非不幸。无论多少艰难，我从未有过压得我抬不起头的悲愁；我眼前还有我族人的希望。我的日子原是好的；只是直至此刻，我才知道生而为人竟能如此欣喜。"

===Original===
Their words were hushed for a while amidst their caresses. Then she said:

“Gold-mane, my friend, I mocked not my past self because I deem that I was a fool then, but because I see now that all that my wisdom could do, would have come about without my wisdom; and that thou, deeming thyself something less than wise, didst accomplish the thing I craved, and that which thou didst crave also; and withal wisdom embraced thee, along with love.”

Therewith she cast her arms about him and said:

“O friend, I mock myself of this: that erst thou deemedst me a God and fearedst me, but now thou seemest to me to be a God, and I fear thee. Yea, though I have longed so sore to be with thee since the day of Shadowy Vale, and though I have wearied of the slow wearing of the days, and it hath tormented me; yet now that I am with thee, I bless the torment of my longing; for it is but my longing that compelleth me to cast away my fear of thee and caress thee, because I have learned how sweet it is to love thee thus.”

He wound his arms about her, and sweeter was their longing than mere joy; and though their love was beyond measure, yet was therein no shame to aught, not even to the lovely Dale and that fair season of spring, so goodly they were among the children of men.

===Chinese===
一时之间，在彼此的温存里，他们的话音归于沉寂。然后她说道：

"金鬃，我的朋友，我方才嘲弄过去的自己，并非以为那时我是个傻子，而是因为我如今才看清：我那点智慧所能做成的事，没有我的智慧也都会自然成就；而你呢——自以为算不上明智——却做成了我所渴求之事，也做成了你所渴求之事；并且智慧也与爱一道，将你拥入怀中。"

说着，她伸出双臂抱住他，说道：

"朋友啊，我之所以嘲弄自己，是为这一桩：从前你视我为神，敬畏我；如今在我眼中，你倒像是一位神，我便敬畏你。是啊，自幽谷（Shadowy Vale）那一日之后，我是何等苦苦地盼着与你相守；那些日子拖沓难熬，叫我备受折磨；然而此刻既与你相守，我却反过来感激那相思之苦；因为唯有这相思逼着我抛开对你的敬畏，去亲近你、抚慰你——因为我已尝到如此爱你是何等甜美。"

他双臂环绕着她；他们的相思比寻常的喜悦更加甘美；他们的爱虽无可度量，却于万物无所亏欠，便是对这秀美的山谷、对这美好的春日，亦无所惭愧——他们在世人之子中，便是这般美好。

===Original===
In a while they arose and turned homeward, and went over the open meadow, and it was yet early, and the dew was as heavy on the grass as before, though the wide sunlight was now upon it, glittering on the wet blades, and shining through the bells of the chequered daffodils till they looked like gouts of blood.

“Look,” said Sun-beam, as they went along by the same way whereas they came, “deemest thou not that other speech-friends besides us have been abroad to talk together apart on this morning of the eve of battle. It is nought unwonted, that we do, even though we forget the trouble of the people to think of our own joy for a while.”

The smile died out of her face as she spoke, and she said:

“O friend, this much may I say for myself in all sooth, that indeed I would die for the kindred and its good days, nor falter therein; but if I am to die, might I but die in thine arms!”

He looked very lovingly on her, and put his arm about her and kissed her and said: “What ails us to stand in the doom-ring and bear witness against ourselves before the kindred? Now I will say, that whatsoever the kindred may or can call upon me to do, that will I do, nor grudge the deed: I am sackless before them. But that is true which I spake to thee when we came together up out of Shadowy Vale, to wit, that I am no strifeful man, but a peaceful; and I look to it to win through this war, and find on the other side either death, or life amongst a happy folk; and I deem that this is mostly the mind of our people.”

===Chinese===
过了一阵，他们起身往回走，越过空旷的草甸。其时仍早，草上露水仍与先前一般沉重，虽说这时已洒满阳光——湿漉漉的草叶反光闪烁，阳光穿透格子水仙钟形的花冠，那花便红得像一滴滴鲜血。

"你看，"日光道——他们正沿着来时的路往回走——"在这大战前夜的清晨，你以为除了我们，便没有别的言谈之友也走出来私下相会么？我们所做的，原不算什么稀奇事，哪怕我们一时忘了众人的烦难，只顾念自己的喜悦。"

说话之间，她脸上的笑意褪去，又道：

"朋友啊，这一句我能为自己诚诚实实地说：我确愿为宗族、为他们美好的日子而死，决不退缩；但若我当真要死，唯愿能死在你怀中！"

他满眼怜爱地看着她，伸手揽住她，亲她，说道："我们这是怎么了，竟仿佛站在判决环（the Doom-ring）中，在宗族面前为自己作证定罪？如今我要说的是：无论宗族能叫我做什么、有什么可叫我做的，我都会去做，绝无怨言：在他们面前我无可指摘。然而我们自幽谷一同上来时我对你说的话，也是真话——那就是：我本不是好斗之人，而是好和之人；我指望从这场战事中得胜而过，在那一头所遇见的，不是死，便是与一族快乐之民共生；我想我们族中多数人的心意，也是如此。"

===Original===
She said: “Thou shalt not die, thou shalt not die!”

“Mayhappen not,” he said; “yet yesterday I could not but look into the slaughter to come, and it seemed to me a grim thing, and darkened the day for me; and I grew acold as a man walking with the dead. But tell me: thou sayest I shall not die; dost thou say this only because I am become dear to thee, or dost thou speak it out of thy foresight of things to come?”

She stopped and looked silently a while over the meadows towards the houses of the Thorp: they were standing now on the border of a shallow brook that ran down toward the Weltering Water; it had a little strand of fine sand like the seashore, driven close together, and all moist, because that brook was used to flood the meadow for the feeding of the grass; and the last evening the hatches which held up the water had been drawn, so that much had ebbed away and left the strand aforesaid.

After a while the Sun-beam turned to Face-of-god, and she was become somewhat pale; she said:

“Nay, I have striven to see, and can see nought save the picture of hope and fear that I make for myself. So it oft befalleth foreseeing women, that the love of a man cloudeth their vision. Be content, dear friend; it is for life or death; but whichso it be, the same for me and thee together?”

===Chinese===
她说："你不会死的，你不会死的！"

"也许不会，"他说，"然而昨日我忍不住去想那将至的厮杀，那景象于我十分可怖，把那一整日都罩上了阴霾；我冷得就像一个与死人同行的人。但你且告诉我：你说我不会死，是只因我已在你心中珍重，还是凭着你对将来之事的先见之明而说？"

她停下脚步，默然向草甸那头、屯子的房屋望了一会儿：此时他们正站在一道浅溪边，那溪水向翻滚河（the Weltering Water）流去；溪边有一小片细沙的小滩，像海滩一般，沙粒挤得很紧，又全湿润——因为这条溪水往常被用来漫灌草甸以养青草；昨夜傍晚，挡水的闸板已被提起，大半水流退去，便留下了前述这片沙滩。

过了一会儿，日光转过身来面向面神，脸色微微发白；她说道：

"不，我曾竭力去看，可是什么也看不见——只看见我自己为自己描出的一幅希望与恐惧交织的图景。能预见的女子往往如此：一个男子的爱，遮蔽了她的目光。安心吧，亲爱的朋友；这便是生与死之事了；但无论生死，你与我同担，好么？"

===Original===
“Yea,” he said, “and well content I am; so now let each of us trust in the other to be both good and dear, even as I trusted in thee the first hour that I looked on thee.”

“It is well,” she said; “it is well. How fair thou art; and how fair is the morn, and this our Dale in the goodly season; and all this abideth us when the battle is over.”

Once more her voice became sweet and wheedling, and the smile lit up her face again, and she pointed down to the sand with her finger, and said:

“See thou! Here indeed have other lovers passed by across the brook. Shall we wish them good luck?”

===Chinese===
"好，"他说，"我十分安心；那么就让我们彼此信赖对方是善良而可珍的——正如我初次见你那一时辰里，便信赖了你一样。"

"这便好，"她说，"这便好。你是何等俊美；这清晨是何等美好；时令正佳，我们的山谷又是何等秀美——这一切，等战事完结，便都在那边等着我们。"

她的声音重又变得甜美婉转，笑意再次照亮了她的脸；她伸手指着下面的沙地，说道：

"你瞧！果真有别的恋人，也从这溪上走过。我们可要祝他们好运？"

===Original===
He laughed and looked down on the sand, and said:

“Thou art in haste to make a story up. Indeed I see that these first footprints are of a woman, for no carle of the Dale has a foot as small; for we be tall fellows; and these others withal are a man’s footprints; and if they showed that they had been walking side by side, simple had been thy tale; but so it is not. I cannot say that these two pairs of feet went over the brook within five minutes of each other; but sure it is that they could not have been faring side by side. Well, belike they were lovers bickering, and we may wish them luck out of that. Truly it is well seen that Bow-may hath done thine hunting for thee, dear friend; or else wouldest thou have lacked venison; for thou hast no hunter’s eye.”

“Well,” she said, “but wish them luck, and give me thine hand upon it.”

He took her hand, and fondled it, and said: “By this hand of my speech-friend, I wish these twain all luck, in love and in leisure, in faring and fighting, in sowing and samming, in getting and giving. Is it well enough wished? If so it be, then come thy ways, dear friend; for the day’s work is at hand.”

“It is well wished,” she said. “Now hearken: by the valiant hand of the War-leader, by the hand that shall unloose my girdle, I wish these twain to be as happy as we be.”

He made as if to draw her away, but she hung aback to set the print of her foot beside the woman’s foot, and then they went on together, and soon crossed the Bridge, and came home to the House of the Face.

===Chinese===
他笑了起来，低头看那沙地，说道：

"你倒急着要编一个故事出来。我确能看出：先印下的这串脚印是个女子的，因为谷里没有哪个汉子的脚有这么小——我们都是大个子；旁边这些则是男子的脚印；倘若它们显示二人并肩同行，那你这个故事便寡淡无味了；然而并非如此。我不能断言这两双脚过溪前后相隔在五分钟之内；但可以肯定的是，他们绝非并肩而行。罢了，大约是一对拌了嘴的恋人，我们正好可以借此祝他们好运。明眼可见——亲爱的朋友——必是弓女（Bow-may）替你打猎的；否则你便要缺鹿肉吃了——你到底没有一双猎人的眼睛。"

"好罢，"她说，"可是祝他们好运，并把你的手放在我手上，就此一言为定。"

他执住她的手，轻轻抚弄，说道："凭我言谈之友这只手，我祝这两人诸般顺遂——于恋爱、于闲暇、于行旅、于战阵、于播种、于收成、于获取、于施与。祝得可够周全？若已够了，那么来罢，亲爱的朋友——白日的活计到了。"

"祝得好，"她说，"如今你听好：凭着战帅那只英勇的手，凭着那只将解我腰带的手，我愿这两人与我们一样幸福。"

他作势要拉她走，她却落后一步，把自己的脚印踏在那女子的脚印旁，然后二人一同前行，不多时便过了桥，回到面神之宅（the House of the Face）。

===Original===
When they had broken their fast, Face-of-god would straight get to his business of ordering matters for the warfare, and was wishful to speak with Folk-might; but found him not, either in the House or the street. But a man said:

“I saw the tall Guest come abroad from the House and go toward the Bridge very early in the morning.”

The Sun-beam, who was anigh when that was spoken, heard it and smiled, and said: “Gold-mane, deemest thou that it was my brother whom we blessed?”

===Chinese===
二人用过早饭，面神便要立即着手料理战阵之事，意欲与民强商议；然宅中、街上皆寻他不见。一个人说道：

"我见那位高个子客人清晨极早从宅中出来，朝桥那边去了。"

日光当时就在旁边，闻言笑了起来，说道："金鬃，你以为我们方才所祝福的那一对里，可有一位是我哥哥？"

===Original===
“I wot not,” he said; “but I would he were here, for this gear must speedily be looked to.”

Nevertheless it was nigh an hour before Folk-might came home to the House. He strode in lightly and gaily, and shaking the crest of his war-helm as he went. He looked friendly on Face-of-god, and said to him:

“Thou hast been seeking me, War-leader; but grudge it not that I have caused thee to tarry. For as things have gone, I am twice the man for thine helping that I was yester-eve; and thou art so ready and deft, that all will be done in due time.”

He looked as if he would have had Face-of-god ask of him what made him so fain, but Face-of-god said only:

“I am glad of thy gladness; but now let us dally no longer, for I have many folk to see today and much to set a-going.”

So therewith they spake together a while, and then went their ways together toward Carlstead and the Woodlanders.

===Chinese===
"我不知晓，"他说，"但我愿他在此，因这桩事须得赶紧料理。"

然而几乎过了一个时辰，民强才回到宅中。他步履轻快欢欣地大步而入，一路走，头顶战盔上的盔缨随之晃动。他友好地看着面神，对他说：

"你一直在找我，战帅；但请勿见怪我让你久等。因为事情既已如此，得你相助，我比昨晚更加强了一倍；而你又是这般手脚利落、心思敏捷，凡事自会按时就绪。"

他神色之间，似乎很想让面神追问一句是什么让他如此欣喜，然而面神只说道：

"你的欢喜便是我的欢喜；不过如今我们再不可耽搁，因我今日要见的人不少，要着手的事也多。"

于是他们又交谈了一会儿，便一同动身，朝汉子镇（Carlstead）与林中之民那边去了。

## L Folk-Might Seeth the Bride and Speaketh with Her / 五十 民强见新娘并与之交谈

===Original===
Now tells the tale of Folk-might, that he went his ways from the Hall to the house where the Bride lay; and the swain who had brought the message went along with him, and he was proud of walking beside so mighty a warrior, and he talked to Folk-might as they went; and the sound of his voice was irksome to the chieftain, but he made as though he hearkened. Yet when they came to the door of the house, which was just out of the Place on the Southern road (for thereby had the Bride fallen to earth), he could withhold his grief no longer, but turned on the threshold and laid his head on the doorjamb, and sobbed and wept till the tears fell down like rain. And the boy stood by wondering, and wishing that Folk-might would forbear weeping, but durst not speak to him.

In a while Folk-might left weeping and went in, and found a fair hall sore befouled by the felons, and in the corner on a bed covered with furs the wounded woman; and at first sight he deemed her not so pale as he looked to see her, as she lay with her long dark-red hair strewed over the pillow, her head moving about wearily. A linen cloth was thrown over her body, but her arms lay out of it before her. Beside her sat the Alderman, his face sober enough, but not as one in heavy sorrow; and anigh him was another chair as if someone had but just got up from it. There was no one else in the hall save two women of the Woodlanders, one of whom was cooking some potion on the hearth, and another was sweeping the floor anigh of bran or some such stuff, which had been thrown down to sop up the blood.

===Chinese===
今且说民强之事：他自厅中而出，往新娘所卧之屋而去；那传信的少年与他同行，因能与如此威武之勇士并肩而行，颇以为荣，一路上向民强絮絮叨叨；其声之于这位首领，本甚聒噪，他却装作倾听之状。然待行至那屋门前——其屋恰在广场（the Place）之外、南行大路旁（盖新娘即于彼处倒地也）——他再也按捺不住心中之痛，便于门槛上回过身来，将头抵住门柱，抽噎哀泣，泪落如雨。那少年立在一旁，心中诧异，唯愿民强莫再哭泣，却不敢开口劝他。

过了一会儿，民强止泪入内，只见一座本甚华美之厅堂，被那些凶徒糟蹋得不成样子；角落里一张盖着毛皮之床上，卧着那位受伤之妇人；初看之下，她并不如他所预想的那般苍白——她卧在那里，一头深红长发披散枕上，头颅无力地来回晃动。她身上搭着一块亚麻布，双臂却伸在布外，垂于身前。长老（the Alderman）坐于她身旁，面色颇为凝重，却不像怀有深哀之人；他近旁另有一椅，似乎方才有人刚刚起身离座。厅中除两名林中汉子（the Woodlanders）部族之妇人外，再无他人——一名在炉前煎熬药汤，另一名正在扫地，扫的是麸皮之类物事，乃撒在地上以吸渍血迹。

===Original===
So Folk-might went up to the Bride, sorely dreading the image of death which she had grown to be, and sorely loving the woman she was and would be.

He knelt down by the bedside, heeding Iron-face little, though he nodded friendly to him, and he held his face close to hers; but she had her eyes shut and did not open them till he had been there a little while; and then they opened and fixed themselves on his without surprise or change. Then she lifted her right hand (for it was in her left shoulder and side that she had been hurt) and slowly laid it on his head, and drew his face to hers and kissed it fondly, as she both smiled and let the tears run over from her eyes. Then she spake in a weak voice:

===Chinese===
于是民强走向新娘，心中既深惧她如今已成的那副将死之相，又深爱她此刻所是、将来所仍是的那位女子。

他在床前跪下，对铁面（Iron-face）几乎未加理会——虽则向他友善地颔首——便将自己的脸凑近她的脸；然她双目紧闭，直至他在那里待了一阵之后方才睁开；那双眼一睁开，便直直凝注于他脸上，既无惊讶之色，亦无变化之容。于是她抬起右手（盖受伤之处乃在左肩与左胁），缓缓置于他头上，引他的脸贴向自己，深情一吻，面上既是微笑，眼中又任泪水盈盈而下。随即她以虚弱之声说道：

===Original===
"Thou seest, chieftain and dear friend, that I may not stand by thy victorious side today. And now, though I were fain if thou wouldst never leave me, yet needs must thou go about thy work, since thou art become the Alderman of the Folk of Silverdale. Yea, and even if thou wert not to go from me, yet in a manner should I go from thee. For I am grievously hurt, and I know by myself, and also the leeches have told me, that the fever is a-coming on me; so that presently I shall not know thee, but may deem thee to be a woman, or a hound, or the very Wolf that is the image of the Father of thy kindred; or even, it may be, someone else—that I have played with time agone."

===Chinese===
「首领，挚友啊，尔今可见，今日我已不能立于尔凯旋之侧了。如今，虽我甚愿尔永不离我，然尔既已成银谷（Silverdale）之民的长老，自须去料理尔之事务。便算尔不离我而去，在某种意义上，亦将是我要离尔而去。盖我伤势沉重，我自己心知，医师们也已言明，热度即将发作；故不多时我便要认不得尔了，或将尔当作一名妇人、一条猎犬，甚至当作那头狼（the Wolf）——那乃是尔族之祖（the Father of thy kindred）的形相；甚或，也许，当作别的什么人——是我昔日曾一同嬉戏过的。」

===Original===
Her voice faltered and faded out here, and she was silent a while; then she said:

"So depart, kind friend and dear love, bearing this word with thee, that should I die, I call on Iron-face my kinsman to bear witness that I bid thee carry me to bale in Silverdale, and lay mine ashes with the ashes of thy Fathers, with whom thine own shall mingle at the last, since I have been of the warriors who have helped to bring thee aback to the land of thy folk."

===Chinese===
她说至此处，声音断续渐低，终至不可闻，遂沉默了一阵；然后又道：

「故去罢，仁慈之友、亲爱之人，携此言而去：倘若我死，我请我之族人铁面作证——我嘱尔扶柩至银谷行火葬之礼，将我之骨灰与尔先祖之骨灰合葬，尔自己之骨灰最终亦必与之相融——因我亦是助尔重返尔族故土之诸战士中的一员。」

===Original===
Then she smiled and shut her eyes and said: "And if I live, as indeed I hope, and how glad and glad I shall be to live, then shalt thou bring me to thy house and thy bed, that I may not depart from thee while both our lives last."

And she opened her eyes and looked at him; and he might not speak for a while, so ravished as he was betwixt joy and sorrow. But the Alderman arose and took a gold ring from off his arm, and spake:

===Chinese===
她随即一笑，闭上了眼睛，说道：「若我活下来——我亦正如此想，活下来我当何等欢欣、何等欢欣——那时尔便须引我入尔之宅、尔之榻，使我于我二人一生之期内，再不与尔分离。」

她又睁开双眼，望着他；他半晌说不出话来，盖其心正为悲喜二者所攫。此时长老起身，自臂上褪下一枚金戒，开口说道：

===Original===
"This is the gold ring of the God of the Face, and I bear it on mine arm betwixt the Folk and the God in all man-motes, and I bore it through the battle today; and it is as holy a ring as may be; and since ye are plighting troth, and I am the witness thereof, it were good that ye held this ring together and called the God to witness, who is akin to the God of the Earth, as we all be. Take the ring, Folk-might, for I trust thee; and of all women now alive would I have this woman happy."

===Chinese===
「此乃面之神（the God of the Face）之金戒；凡遇民人大会（man-motes），我皆戴之于臂，以介于民众与神明之间；今日血战之中，我亦戴着它。此戒乃世间至圣之戒；尔等既在订盟立誓，而我又是见证之人，尔等便当同握此戒，请此神作证——此神与地神（the God of the Earth）同源一体，正如我众人皆然。民强，将戒拿去罢，我信得过尔；当今在世之诸妇人之中，我最愿此女得享安乐。」

===Original===
So Folk-might took the ring and thrust his hand through it, and took her hand, and said:

"Ye Fathers, thou God of the Face, thou Earth-god, thou Warrior, bear witness that my life and my body are plighted to this woman, the Bride of the House of the Steer!"

===Chinese===
于是民强接过那戒，将手穿过其中，又握住她的手，说道：

「列位先祖！面之神！地神！武士（the Warrior）！请共鉴之：我之性命、我之身躯，已许此女——犍牛之宅（the House of the Steer）之新娘！」

===Original===
His face was flushed and bright as he spoke, but as his words ceased he noted how feebly her hand lay in his, and his face fell, and he gazed on her timidly. But she lay quiet, and said softly and slowly:

"O Fathers of my kindred! O Warrior and God of the Earth! bear witness that I plight my troth to this man, to lie in his grave if I die, and in his bed if I live."

===Chinese===
说话之时，他面色潮红、神采焕发；然言语既毕，他便察觉她的手何等无力地躺在自己掌中，脸色随之一黯，怯怯地望着她。她却静静地卧着，轻而缓地说道：

「噫，我族之列位先祖！武士与地神啊！请共鉴之：我以此身许此人——死则同其坟茔，生则同其卧榻。」

===Original===
And she smiled on him again, and then closed her eyes; but opened them presently once more, and said:

"Dear friend, how fared it with Gold-mane today?"

===Chinese===
她又对他一笑，随又合上双目；然不多时复又睁开，说道：

「挚友，金鬃（Gold-mane）今日战况如何？」

===Original===
Said Folk-might: "So well he did, that none might have done better. He fared in the fight as if he had been our Father the Warrior: he is a great chieftain."

She said: "Wilt thou give him this message from me, that in no wise he forget the oath which he swore upon the finger-ring as it lay on the sundial of the Garden of the Face? And say, moreover, that I am sorry that we shall part, and have between us such breadth of wildwood and mountain-neck."

===Chinese===
民强答道：「他战得极好，无人能出其右。他在阵中厮杀，宛如我等之父、那位武士亲临：他诚然是位大首领。」

她道：「尔可愿替我传一句话给他——千万莫要忘了他在面神之园（the Garden of the Face）日晷之上、对着那枚指环所立之誓？再告诉他，我甚憾我们将要分离，你我之间隔着如此辽阔之林莽山颈。」

===Original===
"Yea, surely will I give thy message," said Folk-might; and in his heart he rejoiced, because he heard her speak as if she were sure of life. Then she said faintly:

"It is now thy work to depart from me, and to do as it behoveth a chieftain of the people and the Alderman of Silverdale. Depart, lest the leeches chide me: farewell, my dear!"

===Chinese===
「是，我必替尔传话，」民强道；他心中暗喜，盖听她说话之态，似已确信自己能活。她遂又虚弱地说道：

「尔今当去作尔之事，行一民之首领、银谷之长所当为之事。去罢，免得医师们怪罪于我：再会了，我亲爱的！」

===Original===
So he laid his face to hers and kissed her, and rose up and embraced Iron-face, and went his ways without looking back.

But just over the threshold he met old Hall-ward of the House of the Steer, who was at point to enter, and he greeted him kindly. The old man looked on him steadily, and said: "Tomorrow or the day after I will utter a word to thee, O Chief of the Wolf."

===Chinese===
他便把脸贴上她的脸，吻了她，起身与铁面相拥，径自去了，不再回顾。

然方出门槛，便撞见犍牛之宅的老厅卫（Hall-ward）正欲入门，民强殷勤向他致意。老人定定地端详着他，说道：「明日或后日，我有一言要告尔，狼之首领（O Chief of the Wolf）。」

===Original===
"In a good hour," said Folk-might, "for all thy words are true." Therewith he gat him away from the house, and came to Face-of-god, where he sat before the altar of the Crooked Sword; and now were the chiefs come back from their meat, and were sitting with him; there also were Wood-father and Wood-wont; but Bow-may was with the Sun-beam, who was resting softly in the fair meadow after all the turmoil.

So men made place for Folk-might beside the War-leader, who looked upon his face, and saw that it was sober and unsmiling, but not heavy or moody with grief. So he deemed that all was as well as it might be with the Bride, and with a good heart fell to taking counsel with the others; and kindly and friendly were the redes which they held there, with no gainsaying of man by man, for the whole folk was glad at heart.

===Chinese===
「正逢吉时，」民强道，「盖尔所言皆是真话。」说罢他便离了此屋，来到面神（Face-of-god）跟前——面神正坐于曲剑祭坛（the altar of the Crooked Sword）之前；此时众首领已用罢饭食回来，与他同坐；在座者尚有林父（Wood-father）与林习（Wood-wont）；然弓姝（Bow-may）却在日光（Sun-beam）之处——日光历经那一番惊扰之后，正于那片芳草地之上恬然歇息。

众人为民强在战首（the War-leader）身侧让出一席；战首观其面色，见其凝重不笑，却并未为悲愁所压、郁郁不乐。他遂以为新娘之事已是不幸中之大幸，便欣然与众计议；他们在那里所议之事，皆甚和气友善，无人彼此驳难，盖全族上下心怀欢欣。

===Original===
So there they ordered all matters duly for that present time, and by then they had made an end, it was past sunset, and men were lodged in the chief houses about the Marketstead.

Albeit, though they ate their meat with all joy of heart, and were merry in converse one with the other, the men of the Wolf would by no means feast in their Hall again till it had been cleansed and hallowed anew.

===Chinese===
他们便在那里将当下诸事一一安排妥帖；待到议毕，日已西沉，众人皆被安顿歇宿于市坪（the Marketstead）四周那些主要屋宇之中。

然则，他们虽满怀欢欣地用饭，彼此交谈甚乐，狼族（the Wolf）之人却无论如何不肯再于他们那厅中设宴，须得等那厅重新洒扫洁净、重新祝圣之后方可。

## XXXVI Folk-Might Speaketh with the Bride / 三十六 民强与新娘相语

===Original===
It must be told that those footprints which Face-of-god and the Sun-beam had blessed betwixt jest and earnest had more to do with them than they wotted of. For Folk-might, who had had many thoughts and longings since he had seen the Bride again, rose up early about sunrise, and went out-a-doors, and wandered about the Burg, letting his eyes stray over the goodly stone houses and their trim gardens, yet noting them little, since the Bride was not there.

At last he came to where there was an open place, straight-sided, longer than it was wide, with a wall on each side of it, over which showed the blossomed boughs of pear and cherry and plum-trees: on either hand before the wall was a row of great lindens, now showing their first tender green, especially on their lower twigs, where they were sheltered by the wall. At the nether end of this place Folk-might saw a grey stone house, and he went towards it betwixt the lindens, for it seemed right great, and presently was but a score of paces from its door, and as yet there was no man, carle or queen, stirring about it.

===Chinese===
且说面神（Face-of-god）与日光（the Sun-beam）半戏半真之间所祝福过的那些脚印，其干系之大，远非他们所能知晓。原来民强（Folk-might）自重见新娘（the Bride）之后，心思百转、渴慕方深，这一日日出之际便早早起身，出门来，在堡镇（Burgstead）之中信步闲游，任目光掠过那些华美的石屋与齐整的花园，却无心细看——只因新娘并不在那里。

终于他来到一处空地，四四方方，长过于宽，两边各有一道墙，墙头露出梨、樱、李树正盛开的花枝：墙前两侧各立着一排高大的椴树，此时方吐嫩绿新芽，尤以低处枝条更显青翠——那是因有墙遮蔽之故。民强在这空地的一端看见一座灰色石屋，便自椴树之间向它走去，因那屋看来颇为宏大，不多时便距其门不过二十步之遥，而此时屋之四周尚无一人走动，无论男女。

===Original===
It was a long low house with a very steep roof; but belike the hall was built over some undercroft, for many steps went up to the door on either hand; and the doorway was low, with a straight lintel under its arch. This house, like the House of the Face, seemed ancient and somewhat strange, and Folk-might could not choose but take note of it. The front was all of good ashlar work, but it was carven all over, without heed being paid to the joints of the stones, into one picture of a flowery meadow, with tall trees and bushes in it, and fowl perched in the trees and running through the grass, and sheep and kine and oxen and horses feeding down the meadow; and over the door at the top of the stair was wrought a great steer bigger than all the other neat, whose head was turned toward the sun-rising and uplifted with open mouth, as though he were lowing aloud. Exceeding fair seemed that house to Folk-might, and as though it were the dwelling of some great kindred.

But he had scarce gone over it with his eyes, and was just about to draw nigher yet to it, when the door at the top of those steps opened, and a woman came out of the house clad in a green kirtle and a gown of brazil, with a golden-hilted sword girt to her side. Folk-might saw at once that it was the Bride, and drew aback behind one of the trees so that she might not see him, if she had not already seen him, as it seemed not that she had, for she stayed but for a moment on the top of the stair, looking out down the tree-rows, and then came down the stair and went soberly along the road, passing so close to Folk-might that he could see the fashion of her beauty closely, as one looks into the work of some deftest artificer. Then it came suddenly into his head that he would follow her and see whither she was wending. "At least," said he to himself, "if I come not to speech with her, I shall be nigh unto her, and shall see somewhat of her beauty."

===Chinese===
这是一座长而低矮之屋，屋顶极陡；但或许正厅是建在某处地窖之上，因为两侧都有许多级台阶通至门口；门道低矮，拱下横一道直楣。此屋如同面神之宅（the House of the Face）一般，显得古老而略带奇诡，民强不由得对它注目。屋之正面全是上好方石砌就，然而其上满布雕饰，并不顾及石缝之所在，浑然作一幅繁花草甸之图：图中有高树、有矮丛，有飞禽栖于枝头、穿行草间，有绵羊、母牛、阉牛、马匹散布草甸之上啃食；门之上、阶之顶，又雕有一头大公牛，比其余所有的牛（neat）都更大，牛首朝向日出之方，昂然而张其口，仿佛正高声哞叫。此屋在民强眼中是极美的，仿佛是某个显赫氏族之所居。

然而他目光方将此屋一一览遍、正欲再近前去看，阶顶那扇门忽然开了，一名妇人自屋中走出，身穿一件绿色短袍，外罩一件深红长裙，腰间佩一口金柄宝剑。民强一眼便认出那是新娘，当即退到一棵椴树背后，免得被她看见——倘若她尚未看见他的话；看她模样，似乎并未看见，因为她不过在那阶顶停了片刻，向树列尽头望去，便走下台阶，沿着路端庄而行，从民强身畔经过，离得极近，使他能细细端详她那美貌的形貌，宛如审视某位至巧匠人的一件手笔一般。这时他忽然心生一念：要跟着她，看她往何处去。"至少，"他自语道，"纵然不能与她交谈，我也能近在她身畔，多少一睹她的容颜。"

===Original===
So he came out quietly from behind the tree, and followed her softly; and he was clad in no garment save his kirtle, and bare no weapons to clash and jingle, though he had his helm on his head for lack of a softer hat. He kept her well in sight, and she went straight onward and looked not back. She went by the way whereas he had come, till they were in the main street, wherein as yet was no one afoot; she made her way to the Bridge, and passed over it into the meadows; but when she had gone but a few steps, she stayed a little and looked on the ground, and as she did so turned a little toward Folk-might, who had drawn back into the last of the refuges over the upstream buttresses. He saw that there was a half-smile on her face, but he could not tell whether she were glad or sorry. A light wind was beginning to blow, that stirred her raiment and raised a lock of hair that had strayed from the golden fillet round about her head, and she looked most marvellous fair.

Now she looked along the grass that glittered under the beams of the newly-risen sun, and noted belike how heavy the dew lay on it; and the grass was high already, for the spring had been hot, and haysel would be early in the Dale. So she put off her shoes, that were of deerskin and broidered with golden threads, and turned somewhat from the way, and hung them up amidst the new green leaves of a hawthorn bush that stood nearby, and so went thwart the meadow somewhat eastward straight from that bush, and her feet shone out like pearls amidst the deep green grass.

===Chinese===
于是他悄悄自树后出来，蹑足随她而行；他身上除短袍外别无衣着，又不曾带什么兵器叮当作响，只因没有更软的帽子，头上仍戴着盔。他始终将她收于眼底，她则一路笔直前行，并不回头。她所走之路，正是他来时之路，直到二人来到大街之上——此时街上尚无一人行走；她径向桥而去，过桥走入草甸之中；然而她才行了几步，便稍作停留，低头看着地上，趁此时稍稍侧身朝向民强——民强已退入上游桥墩之上最后一处壁龛之中。他看见她脸上有半丝笑意，却辨不出她是喜是悲。一阵微风渐起，吹动她的衣袂，扬起她自头上一圈金发带中散出的一缕秀发；她那模样，美得不可思议。

此时她放眼向那在初升日光下闪烁的草地望去，大约也留意到草上露水何其浓重；草已长得很高了，因为这个春天颇为炎热，谷中割草之期（haysel）将至得早。于是她脱下那双鹿皮所制、绣着金线的鞋子，略略离开小路，将鞋挂在一株近旁山楂丛的新绿嫩叶之间，然后稍稍偏东、直自那丛灌木横穿草甸而去，她的双足在深绿的草丛中莹然如珠。

===Original===
Folk-might followed presently, and she stayed not again, nor turned, nor beheld him; he recked not if she had, for then would he have come up with her and hailed her, and he knew that she was no foolish maiden to start at the sight of a man who was the friend of her Folk.

So they went their ways till she came to the strand of the water-meadow brook aforesaid, and she went through the little ripples of the shallow without staying, and on through the tall deep grass of the meadow beyond, to where they met the brook again; for it swept round the meadow in a wide curve, and turned back toward itself; so it was some half furlong over from water to water.

She stood a while on the brink of the brook here, which was brimful and nigh running into the grass, because there was a dam just below the place; and Folk-might drew nigher to her under cover of the thorn-bushes, and looked at the place about her and beyond her. The meadow beyond stream was very fair and flowery, but not right great; for it was bounded by a grove of ancient chestnut trees, that went on and on toward the southern cliffs of the Dale: in front of the chestnut wood stood a broken row of blackthorn bushes, now growing green and losing their blossom, and he could see betwixt them that there was a grassy bank running along, as if there had once been a turf-wall and ditch round about the chestnut trees. For indeed this was the old place of tryst between Gold-mane and the Bride, whereof the tale hath told before.

===Chinese===
民强随即跟上，她不再停留，不转身，也不看他；他并不在乎她是否回头看他——因为倘若她看了，他便会上前与她招呼；况且他深知她不是那种见了本族友人便要大惊小怪的愚蠢少女。

二人如此各走各路，直到她来到前述那条水草甸之溪的岸边；她不停步地蹚过浅水中一道道细小涟漪，又走过对岸高大茂密的深草，直走到草地与那溪再度相会之处；因为那溪绕着草甸划出一道宽阔的弧线，又转回向自身；所以从此水到彼水，约莫半浪（furlong）之遥。

她在此处溪畔立了片刻——此处溪水满满当当、几乎要漫入草中，因为下游不远处正有一道堰；民强借着荆棘丛的掩护向她靠近，端详她身周及其背后的地势。溪对岸那片草甸极美、繁花点点，却不算很大；因为它的尽头是一片古老的栗树林，那林子向南谷的崖壁延展而去，绵绵不绝：栗林之前立着一排参差不齐的黑刺李丛，此时正抽出新绿、花事将尽，他透过丛间缝隙可以看见，沿林缘有一道长满青草的土堤，仿佛曾有一道草皮墙与壕沟环绕着那些栗树。原来此处正是金鬃（Gold-mane）与新娘从前幽会的旧地，前文已曾叙及。

===Original===
The Bride stayed scarce longer than gave him time to note all this; but he deemed that she was weeping, though he could not rightly see her face; for her shoulders heaved, and she hung her face adown and put up her hands to it. But now she went a little higher up the stream, where the water was shallower, and waded the stream and went up over the meadow, still weeping, as he deemed, and went between the blackthorn bushes, and sat her down on the grassy bank with her back to the chestnut trees.

Folk-might was ashamed to have seen her weeping, and was half-minded to turn him back again at once; but love constrained him, and he said to himself, "Where shall I see her again privily if I pass by this time and place?" So he waited a little till he deemed she might have mastered the passion of tears, and then came forth from his bush, and went down to the water and crossed it, and went quietly over the meadow straight towards her. But he was not halfway across, when she lifted up her face from between her hands and beheld the man coming. She neither started nor rose up; but straightened herself as she sat, and looked right into Folk-might's eyes as he drew near, though the tears were not dry on her cheeks.

===Chinese===
新娘停留的时间，几乎只够他将这一切看个分明；但他觉得她正在垂泪，虽则不能清楚看见她的脸；因为她的双肩起伏，把脸垂下，双手举到脸上。然而此刻她稍向上游走去，那里水更浅，便蹚过溪水，走上草甸——他揣度她仍在哭泣——穿过黑刺李丛之间，背靠栗树，在草堤之上坐了下来。

民强因窥见她落泪而心下抱愧，几乎想立刻转身回去；然而情之所驱，使他不能自已，便自忖道："若错过此时此地，我何处再能私下与她相见？"于是他又稍候片刻，待他觉得她那一阵泪潮或已平伏，便自灌木后走出，下到水边、蹚过溪水，安安静静地横穿草甸，径直向她而去。但他尚未走到一半，她便自双手之间抬起脸来，看见来人。她既不惊跳，也不起身；只是在坐中挺直了身子，在民强走近时直直望入他的眼中——尽管她颊上的泪痕未干。

===Original===
Now he stood before her, and said: "Hail to the Daughter of a mighty House! Mayst thou live happy!"

She answered: "Hail to thee also, Guest of our Folk! Hast thou been wandering about our meadows, and happened on me perchance?"

"Nay," he said; "I saw thee come forth from the House of the Steer, and I followed thee hither."

She reddened a little, and knit her brow, and said:
"Thou wilt have something to say to me?"

"I have much to say to thee," he said; "yet it was sweet to me to behold thee, even if I might not speak with thee."

She looked on him with her deep simple eyes, and neither reddened again, nor seemed wroth; then she said:
"Speak what thou hast in thine heart, and I will hearken without anger whatsoever it may be; even if thou hast but to tell me of the passing folly of a mighty man, which in a month or two he will not remember for sorrow or for joy. Sit here beside me, and tell me thy thought."

===Chinese===
此时他立于她面前，开口道："强族之女，向你问好！愿你一生安乐！"

她答道："也向你问好，我族之客！你是在我等草甸上闲游，偶然撞见我的么？"

"不然，"他说，"我见你自公牛之宅（the House of the Steer）出来，便一路随你来此。"

她微微脸红，蹙起眉，说道：
"你有话要对我讲？"

"我有许多话要对你讲，"他说，"纵然不能与你交谈，得见你一面也是甜美的。"

她用那深沉清澈的双目看着他，不再脸红，也不见恼怒；然后说道：
"你心中有什么话，便说什么罢；无论是什么，我都会不带怒气地聆听；哪怕你不过是要告诉我一位壮士一时的痴愚——这事一两月后，不论悲喜，他自己都将不复记起。请在我身旁坐下，把你的心思讲来。"

===Original===
So he sat him adown and said: "Yea, I have much to say to thee, but it is hard to me to say it. But this I will say: today and yesterday make the third time I have seen thee. The first time thou wert happy and calm, and no shadow of trouble was on thee; the second time thine happy days were waning, though thou scarce knewest it; but today and yesterday thou art constrained by the bonds of grief, and wouldest loosen them if thou mightest."

She said: "What meanest thou? How knowest thou this? How may a stranger partake in my joy and my sorrow?"

He said: "As for yesterday, all the people might see thy grief and know it. But when I beheld thee the first time, I saw thee that thou wert more fair and lovely than all other women; and when I was away from thee, the thought of thee and thine image were with me, and I might not put them away; and oft at such and such a time I wondered and said to myself, what is she doing now? though god wot I was dealing with tangles and troubles and rough deeds enough. But the second time I beheld thee, when I had looked to have great joy in the sight of thee, my heart was smitten with a pang of grief; for I saw thee hanging on the words and the looks of another man, who was light-minded toward thee, and that thou wert troubled with the anguish of doubt and fear. And he knew it not, nor saw it, though I saw it."

===Chinese===
于是他坐了下来，说道："是，我有许多话要对你讲，却难以启齿。但这一点我要说：今日与昨日，是我第三次见你。第一次你安乐恬静，身上没有一丝愁云；第二次你那些快乐的日子已开始凋零，你自己却几乎不曾察觉；而今日与昨日，你已被愁苦之索所缚，恨不得能挣脱它才好。"

她说："你这话怎讲？你怎么知道这些？一个外人怎能与我的悲欢相与？"

他说："至于昨日，全体百姓都能看出你的愁苦，都晓得。然而我第一次见你之时，我看你比一切女子都更美、更可爱；当我离开你之后，对你的思念与你的影子始终伴我左右，挥之不去；我常常在某些时刻出神，自问道：她此刻在做什么？——虽然皇天在上，我手头所办之事已是纠葛、麻烦、粗豪之举够多的了。可是我第二次见你之时，本指望见你一面而大喜，我的心却被一记愁痛击中；因为我看见你正系恋于另一个男子的言语和眼色之上，而那男子对你却心思轻浮；又看见你被疑惧之苦所折磨。那人自己并不知道，也看不见，我却看得见。"

===Original===
Her face grew troubled, and the tearful passion stirred within her. But she held it aback, and said, as anyone might have said it:
"How wert thou in the Dale, mighty man? We saw thee not."

He said: "I came hither hidden in other semblance than mine own. But meddle not therewith; it availeth nought. Let me say this, and do thou hearken to it. I saw thee yesterday in the street, and thou wert as the ghost of thine old gladness; although belike thou hast striven with sorrow; for I see thee with a sword by thy side, and we have been told that thou, O fairest of women, hast given thyself to the Warrior to be his damsel."

"Yea," she said, "that is sooth."

He went on: "But the face which thou bearedst yesterday against thy will, amidst all the people, that was because thou hadst seen my sister the Sun-beam for the first time, and Face-of-god with her, hand clinging to hand, lip longing for lip, desire unsatisfied, but glad with all hope."

===Chinese===
她面色转忧，泪潮又在心中翻涌。但她强自按捺，平淡说道——平淡得几乎人人都能那般说：
"壮士，你是怎么进到谷中来的？我们并未看见你。"

他说："我是改头换面、隐姓埋名而来。但此事不必深究；说了也无益。容我说这一桩，你且听好：昨日我在街上见你，你已如旧日欢乐的鬼魂；虽然你大约曾与愁苦抗争过；因为我看见你腰间佩着剑，又有人告诉我们说，你这最美的女子，已将自己许给了那位武士（the Warrior），做他的侍女。"

"是啊，"她说，"那是真的。"

他继续说道："然而你昨日当着众人之面所勉强摆出的那副脸色，却是因为你第一次见到了我妹妹日光，又见面神与她在一起——手恋着手，唇盼着唇，欲求未足，却满怀希望而欢喜。"

===Original===
She laid hand upon hand in the lap of her gown, and looked down, and her voice trembled as she said:
"Doth it avail to talk of this?"

He said: "I know not: it may avail; for I am grieved, and shall be whilst thou art grieved; and it is my wont to strive with my griefs till I amend them."

She turned to him with kind eyes and said:
"O mighty man, canst thou clear away the tangle which besetteth the soul of her whose hope hath bewrayed her? Canst thou make hope grow up in her heart? Friend, I will tell thee that when I wed, I shall wed for the sake of the kindred, hoping for no joy therein. Yea, or if by some chance the desire of man came again into my heart, I should strive with it to rid myself of it, for I should know of it that it was but a wasting folly, that should but beguile me, and wound me, and depart, leaving me empty of joy and heedless of life."

===Chinese===
她把双手交叠在裙裾之上，垂下眼，声音微颤地说道：
"说这些可有用么？"

他说："我不知道：也许有用；因为我心忧愁，你一日忧愁，我便一日不得宽解；遇有忧愁之事，我总要与之相争、直到把它化解，此乃我的性子。"

她转过身来，目光柔和地看着他，说道：
"壮士啊，你能否解开那纠缠着一个被自己希望所辜负之女子灵魂的乱麻？你能否在她心里重新种出希望来？朋友，我告诉你：我若出嫁，必是为亲族而嫁，不指望其中有任何欢乐。是啊，纵或偶然间，男欢女爱之心又回到我心里来，我也要竭力与之相争、把它驱除；因为我会知道那不过是徒耗精神的痴愚，只会哄骗我、伤我，然后离去——留我空无欢乐、对生命再不在意。"

===Original===
He shook his head and said: "Even so thou deemest now; but one day it shall be otherwise. Or dost thou love thy sorrow? I tell thee, as it wears thee and wears thee, thou shalt hate it, and strive to shake it off."

"Nay, nay," she said; "I love it not; for not only it grieveth me, but also it beateth me down and belittleth me."

"Good is that," said he. "I know how strong thine heart is. Now, wilt thou take mine hand, which is verily the hand of thy friend, and remember what I have told thee of my grief which cannot be sundered from thine? Shall we not talk more concerning this? For surely I shall soon see thee again, and often; since the Warrior, who loveth me belike, leadeth thee into fellowship with me. Yea, I tell thee, O friend, that in that fellowship shalt thou find both the seed of hope, and the sun of desire that shall quicken it."

===Chinese===
他摇头说道："你此刻是这般想；但终有一日会不一样。莫非你爱你的忧愁不成？我告诉你，当它日复一日地消磨你，你终会恨它，竭力要把它甩脱。"

"不，不，"她说，"我并不爱它；因为它不仅使我痛苦，更将我打倒、使我卑微。"

"那就好，"他说，"我知道你的心有多坚强。如今，你愿不愿意握我的手——这手确确实实是你朋友的手——并记着我对你所说的、那与你忧愁不可分离的我的忧愁？我们何不再多谈谈此事？因为我相信不久便又能见到你，而且会常常相见；因为那位武士——他大约是爱我的——正领着你与我结为同伴。是啊，朋友，我告诉你，正是在这同伴之谊中，你将寻到希望的种子，以及能催它发芽的欲求之阳光。"

===Original===
Therewith he arose and stood before her, and held out to her his hand all hardened with the sword-hilt, and she took it, and stood up facing him, and said:
"This much will I tell thee, O friend; that what I have said to thee this hour, I thought not to have said to any man; or to talk with a man of the grief that weareth me, or to suffer him to see my tears; and marvellous I deem it of thee, for all thy might, that thou hast drawn this speech from out of me, and left me neither angry nor ashamed, in spite of these tears; and thou whom I have known not, though thou knewest me!

"But now it were best that thou depart, and get thee home to the House of the Face, where I was once so frequent; for I wot that thou hast much to do; and as thou sayest, it will be in warfare that I shall see thee. Now I thank thee for thy words and the thought thou hast had of me, and the pain which thou hast taken to heal my hurt: I thank thee, I thank thee, for as grievous as it is to show one's hurts even to a friend."

He said: "O Bride, I thank thee for hearkening to my tale; and one day shall I thank thee much more. Mayest thou fare well in the Field and amidst the Folk!"

Therewith he kissed her hand, and turned away, and went across the meadow and the stream, glad at heart and blithe with everyone; for kindness grew in him as gladness grew.

===Chinese===
说罢他起身立在她面前，向她伸出手去——那手因久握剑柄而已满是硬茧——她接住，面对他站起身来，说道：
"朋友，这一点我要告诉你：我这一时辰对你所说的话，原想不到会对任何男子说起；也想不到会与一个男子讲那消磨我的忧愁，更想不到会让一个男子看见我的眼泪；我觉得你真是奇妙——纵然有这等本事，竟能从我口中引出这些话来，又留下我既不恼怒也不羞惭——尽管有这些泪；你原本是我所不识之人，虽然你却识得我！

"但如今你最好离去，回面神之宅去罢——那里我曾出入频仍；因为我知道你事务繁多；而正如你所说，日后我见你，必是在战阵之中。现在我多谢你的话，多谢你对我的挂念，也多谢你为医治我的伤痛所费的苦心：我谢你，谢你——虽然把伤口给人看，纵然给朋友看，也一样地痛。"

他说："新娘啊，多谢你听我这一番话；终有一日我会更加感激你。愿你在田野之间、在族人之中，一切顺遂！"

说罢他吻了她的手，转身而去，横穿草甸与溪流，满心欢喜，待一切人都和悦；因为欢喜愈增，仁慈也随之愈增。

## XXX Hall-Face Goeth Toward Rosedale / XXX 厅面赴玫瑰谷

===Original===
On the morrow Face-of-god took counsel with Hall-face and Stone-face as to what were best to be done, and they sat on the dais in the Hall to talk it over.

Short was the time that had worn since that day in Shadowy Vale, for it was but eight days since then; yet so many things had befallen in that time, and, to speak shortly, the outlook for the Burgdalers had changed so much, that the time seemed long to all the three, and especially to Face-of-god.

It was yet twenty days till the Great Folk-mote should beholden, and to Hall-face the time seemed long enough to do somewhat, and he deemed it good to gather force and fall on the Dusky Men in Rosedale, since now they had gotten men who could lead them the nighest way and by the safest passes, and who knew all the ways of the foemen. But to Stone-face this rede seemed not so good; for they would have to go and come back, and fight and conquer, in less time than twenty days, or be belated of the Folk-mote, and meanwhile much might happen.

===Chinese===
次日，面神与厅面、石面商议当以何策为善，三人坐于厅中高台之上，细细筹度。

自幽谷那一日至今，为时其实未久，前后不过八日；然此八日之间所历之事甚多，且简而言之，堡谷之民处境之大局已大为改观——故三人皆觉时日迁延甚久，面神之感尤甚。

距民众大会之期尚有二十日；厅面以为此段时间足以有所作为，遂力主聚兵突袭玫瑰谷之黝暗人，因如今他们已得向导，能引众人取最近之路、过最稳妥之隘，且尽知敌人之路径。然石面以为此计未善：盖出兵往返、厮杀取胜，须在二十日之内了结，否则便要错过民众大会之期；而此期间，变故殊多。

===Original===
“For,” said Stone-face, “we may deem the fighting-men of Rosedale to be little less than one thousand, and however we fall on them, even if it be unawares at first, they shall fight stubbornly; so that we may not send against them many less than they be, and that shall strip Burgdale of its fighting-men, so that whatever befalls, we that be left shall have to bide at home.”

Now was Face-of-god of the same mind as Stone-face; and he said moreover: “When we go to Rosedale we must abide there a while unless we be overthrown. For if ye conquer it and come away at once, presently shall the tidings come to the ears of the Dusky Men in Silverdale, and they shall join themselves to those of Rosedale who have fled before you, and between them they shall destroy the unhappy people therein; for ye cannot take them all away with you: and that shall they do all the more now, when they look to have new thralls in Burgdale, both men and women. And this we may not suffer, but must abide till we have met all our foemen and have overcome them, so that the poor folk there shall be safe from them till they have learned how to defend their dale. Now my rede is, that we send out the War-arrow at once up and down the Dale, and to the Shepherds and Woodlanders, and appoint a day for the Muster and Weapon-show of all our Folk, and that day to be the day before the Spring Market, that is to say, four days before the Great Folk-mote, and meantime that we keep sure watch about the border of the wood, and now and again scour the wood, so as to clear the Dale of their wandering bands.”

===Chinese===
石面道：“玫瑰谷之能战之丁，料来不下千人；纵我军突袭、初时出其不意，他们亦必顽抗到底；故我军所遣，不可较敌少了多少，如此则堡谷精壮尽出，一旦有变，我等留守之人唯有困守家中。”

面神之意与石面相同；又道：“我等若赴玫瑰谷，除非兵败，否则必得在那驻扎一段时日。因为若攻下其地旋即撤回，则消息很快便会传入银谷黝暗人之耳，他们必将与玫瑰谷溃逃之敌合流，合力残害当地苦命之民——因汝等不能将他们尽数携走：而如今他们正盘算在堡谷再掳男女新奴，此种恶行必将更甚。此事实不可忍，我等必须留下，与众敌一一交锋并尽行击败，好让那里穷苦之民得免荼毒，直到他们学会如何守卫自家山谷。我的主意是：即刻向谷中上下、向牧羊之民与林中之民传发战箭，择定全族集结受阅之期——即春市前一日，亦即民众大会之前四日——同时于林缘严加巡逻，并不时扫荡林中，以肃清谷内游窜之敌队。”

===Original===
“Yea,” said Hall-face; “and I pray thee, brother, let me have an hundred of men and thy Dallach, and let us go somewhat deep into the wood towards Rosedale, and see what we may come across; peradventure it might be something better than hart or wild-swine.”

Said Face-of-god: “I see no harm therein, if Dallach goeth with thee freely; for I will have no force put on him or any other of the Runaways. Yet meseemeth it were not ill for thee to find the road to Rosedale; for I have it in my mind to send a company thither to give those Rosedale man-quellers somewhat to do at home when we fall upon Silverdale. Therefore go find Dallach, and get thy men together at once; for the sooner thou art gone on thy way the better. But this I bid thee, go no further than three days out, that ye may be back home betimes.”

At this word Hall-face’s eyes gleamed with joy, and he went out from the Hall straightway and sought Dallach, and found him at the Gate. Iron-face had given him a new sword, a good one, and had bidden him call it Thicket-clearer, and he would not leave it any moment of the day or night, but would lay it under his pillow at night as a child does with a new toy; and now he was leaning against a buttress and drawing the said sword half out of the scabbard and poring over its blade, which was indeed fair enough, being wrought with dark grey waving lines like the eddies of the Weltering Water.

===Chinese===
厅面道：“正是；并请吾兄允我领壮士一百、并借汝之达拉赫一用，让我等往玫瑰谷方向深入林中一行，看看有何机缘；说不定所遇比猎鹿、猎野猪更为可观。”

面神道：“此事无妨，但须达拉赫自愿随行；我定不加逼迫于他或其他逃亡者。然我想，汝能识得赴玫瑰谷之路，亦非坏事；因我心有所算——攻打银谷之时，当遣一队人马赴玫瑰谷，让那些嗜杀之徒在自家也忙上一阵。故汝且去寻达拉赫，速速点齐人马；动身越早越好。但有一言相嘱：此去勿过三日，以便及早归家。”

闻此言，厅面双目顿生光彩，立即辞出厅堂，去寻达拉赫，于城门处找到他。铁面曾赠他一柄新剑，剑甚精良，并嘱其名为“辟丛”；他日夜片刻不离此剑，夜间便置于枕下，犹如孩童得了新玩具一般；此刻他正倚在一处撑壁之上，将这柄剑自鞘中抽出一半，端详剑身——剑身确也精良，镌有暗灰色水波纹，正如翻滚河之回旋。

===Original===
So Hall-face greeted him, and smiled and said:
“Guest, if thou wilt, thou may’st take that new blade of my father’s work which thou lovest so, a journey which shall rejoice it.”
“Yea,” said Dallach, “I suppose that thou wouldest fare on thy brother’s footsteps, and deemest that I am the man to lead thee on the road, and even farther than he went; and though it might be thought by some that I have seen enough of Rosedale and the parts thereabout for one while, yet will I go with thee; for now am I a man again, body and soul.”

And therewith he drew Thicket-clearer right out of his sheath and waved him in the air. And Hall-face was glad of him and said he was well apaid of his help. So they went away together to gather men, and on the morrow Hall-face departed and went into the Wildwood with Dallach and an hundred and two score men.

===Chinese===
厅面上前见礼，含笑说道：
“客人，汝若愿意，不妨带着这柄汝所钟爱的、家父所制之新剑，去走一遭，也好让它开个欢心。”
达拉赫道：“正是。我猜汝是欲步汝兄之后尘，以为我是能引汝上路之人，且要走得比他更远；虽或有人以为，我于玫瑰谷及其一带一时之间所见已够多了，然我仍愿随汝同去；因为如今我已重新是个男子汉了——身心皆是。”

说罢，他将“辟丛”剑整个抽出鞘来，在空中一挥。厅面见他如此，心中欢喜，言道有他相助，甚为满意。于是二人同去点齐人马，次日厅面便启程，带着达拉赫与一百四十名壮士进入野林。

===Original===
But as for Face-of-god, he fared up and down the Dale following the War-arrow, and went into all houses, and talked with the folk, both young and old, men and women, and told them closely all that had betid and all that was like to betide; and he was well pleased with that which he saw and heard; for all took his words well, and were nought afeard or dismayed by the tidings; and he saw that they would not hang aback. Meantime the days wore, and Hall-face came not back till the seventh day, and he brought with him twelve more Runaways, of whom five were women. But he had lost four men, and had with him Dallach and five others of the Dalesmen borne upon litters sore hurt; and this was his story:

They got to the Burg of the Runaways on the forenoon of the third day, and thereby came on five carles of the Runaways—men who had missed meeting Dallach that other day, but knew what had been done; for one of them had been sick and could not come with him, and he had told the others: so now they were hanging about the Burg of the Runaways hoping somewhat that he might come again; and they met the Burgdalers full of joy, and brought them trouts that they had caught in the river.

As for the other runaways, namely, five women and two more carles—they had gotten them close to the entrance into Silverdale, where by night and cloud they came on a campment of the Dusky Men, who were leading home these seven poor wretches, runaways whom they had caught, that they might slay them most evilly in Rosestead. So Hall-face fell on the Dusky Men, and delivered their captives, but slew not all the foe, and they that fled brought pursuers on them who came up with them the next day, so near was Rosedale, though they made all diligence homeward. The Burgdalers must needs turn and fight with those pursuers, and at last they drave them aback so that they might go on their ways home. They let not the grass grow beneath their feet thereafter, till they were assured by meeting a band of the Woodlanders, who had gone forth to help them, and with whom they rested a little. But neither so were they quite done with the foemen, who came upon them next day a very many: these however they and the Woodlanders, who were all fresh and unwounded and very valiant, speedily put to the worse; and so they came on to Burgstead, leaving those of them who were sorest hurt to be tended by the Woodlanders at Carlstead, who, as might be looked for, deal with them very lovingly.

===Chinese===
至于面神，他则奔走于谷中上下，循战箭所传之处，挨门挨户登门，与男女老少一一相谈，将已发生之事、将发生之事，原原本本告诉他们；他于所见所闻颇为满意：众人皆能虚心听受其言，对消息既不畏惧，亦不气馁；他看得出众人不会退缩。期间时日推移，厅面直至第七日方归，又带回十二名逃亡者，其中五人为女子。但他折损了四名部下，随行的达拉赫与另外五名谷民则身受重伤，以担架抬回；他所禀报如下：

第三日上午，他们抵达逃亡者之堡，在那里遇见五名逃亡之男子——这些人那一日错过了与达拉赫的会合，然已知事情经过；因其中一人当时染病，未能随行，他将始末告诉了其余人：故此刻他们在逃亡者之堡附近徘徊，仍盼着达拉赫或会再来；见到堡谷之人，欢欣莫名，并将河中所捕之鳟鱼献上。

至于其余逃亡者——即五名女子与另外两名男子——他们已逼近银谷入口，在那里，借夜色与阴云之掩护，他们撞见黝暗人的一队营帐，这些黝暗人正将这七个可怜人押回老家——这都是他们捕获的逃亡者，预备带到玫瑰镇极其残酷地处死。于是厅面率众突袭黝暗人，救出俘虏，但未能将敌兵尽数诛杀；逃脱之人引来追兵，次日便追上他们——玫瑰谷离此之近如此——虽然堡谷之人全力赶路回家，亦所不免。堡谷之人不得不回头迎战追兵，最终将追兵击退，方能继续赶路归家。此后他们片刻不敢耽搁，直到遇见一队出林接应的林中之民，方才放心，与他们略作歇息。但即便如此，敌人仍未罢休，次日又大举来攻，人数甚众：然堡谷之人与林中之民合力应战——林中之民气力正盛、一无伤损、勇悍异常——顷刻便将敌军击溃；他们这才回到堡镇，其中伤势最重者留在汉子镇由林中之民照看——果不其然，林中之民待他们极尽亲厚。

===Original===
It was in the first fight that they suffered that loss of slain and wounded; and therein the newly delivered thralls fought valiantly against their masters: as for Dallach, it was no marvel, said Hall-face, that he was hurt; but rather a marvel that he was not slain, so little he recked of point and edge, if he might but slay the foemen.

Such was Hall-face’s-tale; and Face-of-god deemed that he had done unwisely to let him go that journey; for the slaying of a few Dusky Men was but a light gain to set against the loss of so many Burgdalers; yet was he glad of the deliverance of those Runaways, and deemed it a gain indeed. But henceforth would he hold all still till he should have tidings of Folk-might; so nought was done thereafter save the warding of the Dale, from the country of the Shepherds to the Waste above the Eastern passes.

But Face-of-god himself went up amongst the Shepherds, and abode with a goodman hight Hound-under-Greenbury, who gathered to him the folk from the countryside, and they went up on to Greenbury, and sat on the green grass while he spoke with them and told them, as he had told the others, what had been done and what should be done. And they heard him gladly, and he deemed that there would be no blenching in them, for they were all in one tale to live and die with their friends of Burgdale, and they said that they would have no other word save that to bear to the Great Folk-mote.

===Chinese===
阵亡与伤损皆出在那第一场恶战之中；那一战里，新获救之奴隶奋不顾身，与旧主厮杀至烈：至于达拉赫，厅面说，他受了伤并不奇怪，倒是他能保住性命才是奇事——他全然不顾刀枪剑戟，只要能多杀几个敌人。

厅面所禀便是如此；面神自悔当时允他此行，实为不智——杀几个黝暗人，比之折损这许多堡谷之人，所得实在太轻；然他亦为那些逃亡者获救而喜，以为此亦确是收获。但此后他决意按兵不动，直到有民强的消息传来；于是除了自牧羊之民之地至东面隘口之上荒原一路守备山谷之外，别无他事。

面神则亲自前往牧羊之民之间，投宿于一位名叫“绿堡下之猎犬”的家长家中；那人将四乡之人召集到他这里，众人登上绿堡，坐在青草地上，由他向众人讲说——如同对其他人讲的一样——已经做了什么、还须做什么。众人皆欣然倾听，他相信众人不会畏缩，因他们都同心同德，誓与堡谷之友人同生共死；他们表示，赴民众大会之时所要带的话，唯此一语，别无他言。

===Original===
So he went away well-pleased, and he fared on thence to the Woodlanders, and guested at the house of a valiant man hight War-grove, who on the morrow morn called the folk together to a green lawn of the Wildwood, so that there was scarce a soul of them that was not there. Then he laid the whole matter before them; and if the Dalesmen had been merry and ready, and the Shepherds stouthearted and friendly, yet were the Woodlanders more eager still, so that every hour seemed long to them till they stood in their war-gear; and they told him that now at last was the hour drawing nigh which they had dreamed of, but had scarce dared to hope for, when the lost way should be found, and the crooked made straight, and that which had been broken should be mended; that their meat and drink, and sleeping and waking, and all that they did were now become to them but the means of living till the day was come whereon the two remnants of the children of the Wolf should meet and become one Folk to live or die together.

Then went Face-of-god back to Burgstead again, and as he stood anigh the Thingstead once more, and looked down on the Dale as he had beheld it last autumn, he bethought him that with all that had been done and all that had been promised, the earth was clearing of her trouble, and that now there was nought betwixt him and the happy days of life which the Dale should give to the dwellers therein, save the gathering hosts of the battlefield and the day when the last word should be spoken and the first stroke smitten. So he went down on to the Portway well content.

Thereafter till the day of the Weapon-show there is nought to tell of, save that Dallach and the other wounded men began to grow whole again; and all men sat at home, or went on the woodland ward, expecting great tidings after the holding of the Folk-mote.

===Chinese===
于是他心满意足地离去，自此前往林中之民处，投宿于一位名叫“战林”的勇士家中；次日清晨，那人将众人召集到野林一片青草地上，几乎无人不到。他便将整件事的原委向众人陈述：若说谷民踊跃乐意、牧羊之民坚毅热诚，则林中之民尤有过之——盼着披甲执兵之时，每一刻都觉得漫长；他们告诉他，他们梦寐以求、却几乎不敢企盼的那一刻，终于临近了——迷失之路将被寻回，弯曲之物将被掰直，破碎之物将被修补；他们如今衣食起居、一切所行，皆不过是为了活到那一天——狼之子孙的两支遗民将相会合流，成为一个民族，同生共死。

于是面神又回到堡镇，当他再次立于议事坪近旁，俯瞰这山谷——一如去年秋天他所见的那样——他想到，所有已经做成的、所有已经许下的承诺，都使大地的苦痛逐渐消散；如今他与山谷将赐予居者的安乐岁月之间，唯有集结大军于战场、最后通牒说尽、第一击挥下的那一日。于是他满怀欣慰地走下港路。

此后直到受阅之期，再无可叙之事，唯有达拉赫与其他伤者逐渐痊愈；众人皆闲坐家中，或赴林中守卫，静候民众大会之后的重大消息。

## LVII How the Host Came Home Again / 五十七 大军归乡

===Original===
It was fourteen days before they came to Rosedale; for they had much baggage with them, and they had no mind to weary themselves, and the wood was nothing loathsome to them, whereas the weather was fair and bright for the more part. They fell in with no mishap by the way. But a score and three of runaways joined themselves to the Host, having watched their goings and wotting that they were not foemen. Of these, some had heard of the overthrow of the Dusky Men in Silverdale, and others not. The Burgdalers received them all, for it seemed to them no great matter for a score or so of newcomers to the Dale.

But when the Host was come to Rosedale, they found it fair arid lovely; and there they met with those of their folk who had gone with Dallach. But Dallach welcomed the kindreds with great joy, and bade them abide; for he said that they had the less need to hasten, since he had sent messengers into Burgdale to tell men there of the tidings. Albeit they were mostly loth to tarry; yet when he lay hard on them not to depart as men on the morrow of a gild-feast, they abode there three days, and were as well guested as might be, and on their departure they were laden with gifts from the wealth of Rosedale by Dallach and his folk.

===Chinese===
他们走了十四日方才抵达玫瑰谷；因随军辎重繁多，又无意赶路劳累，且一路天气多半晴朗明丽，林莽于他们并不令人生厌。途中未遭任何祸患。但有二十三名逃亡之人归附了大军——他们一路窥伺其行迹，已知这些人并非敌寇。这些人中，有的已听闻黝暗人在银谷覆灭之事，有的则未有所闻。堡谷之民将他们尽数收留，因多来二十来个新人入谷，在他们看来并非什么了不起的大事。

及至大军抵达玫瑰谷，只见其地秀美可爱；在那里他们遇见了先前随达拉赫同去的本族之人。达拉赫满心欢喜地迎接诸宗族，坚请他们驻留；因他说他们无须急于赶路，他早已派出信使前往堡谷，向彼处之人通报消息。他们虽多半不愿久留，然达拉赫苦苦相劝，谓不可如行会盛宴翌晨之人那般匆匆散去；他们遂在此盘桓三日，受尽上宾之待，临行之际，达拉赫及其族人又将玫瑰谷的珍宝礼物装了他们满载。

===Original===
Before they went their ways Dallach spake with Face-of-god and the chiefs of the Dalesmen, and said:

“Ye have given me much from the time when ye found me in the wood a naked wastrel; yet now I would ask you a gift to lay on the top of all that ye have given me.”
