Said Face-of-god: “Name the gift, and thou shalt have it; for we deem thee our friend.”

===Chinese===
临行之前，达拉赫与面神及谷民诸首领交谈，说道：

「自尔等于林中寻得我这赤身露体的流浪汉之时起，尔等已赐我良多；然今我仍欲向尔等再求一桩馈赠，置于尔等所赐一切之上。」

面神道：「说出此馈赠为何，你便可得着；因我们视你为友。」

===Original===
“I am no less,” said Dallach, “as in time to come I may perchance be able to show you. But now I am asking you to suffer a score or two of your men to abide here with me this summer, till I see how this folk newborn again is like to deal with me. For pleasure and a fair life have become so strange to them, that they scarce know what to do with them, or how to live; and unless all is to go awry, I must needs command and forbid; and though belike they love me, yet they fear me not; so that when my commandment pleaseth them, they do as I bid, and when it pleaseth them not, they do contrary to my bidding; for it hath got into their minds that I shall in no case lift a hand against them, which indeed is the very sooth. But your folk they fear as warriors of the world, who have slain the Dusky Men in the Marketplace of Silverstead; and they are of alien blood to them, men who will do as their friend biddeth (think our folk) against them who are neither friends or foes. With such help I shall be well holpen.”

===Chinese===
达拉赫道：「我所求不亚于此，来日我或许能向尔等证之。然今我所求者，是请尔等容许二三十名部下于此留驻一夏，直至我看清这群重获新生之民将如何与我相处。因欢乐与美好的生活于他们已变得如此陌生，他们几乎不知如何消受，不知如何度日；除非任一切尽归败坏，我势必发号施令、有所禁断；然他们虽多半爱戴我，却不畏惧我；故我所发命令合其心意时，他们便照办，不合心意时，便反其道而行之；因他们心中已认定我绝不会向他们动手，而这确是实情。然尔等之人，他们则视作当世武士而畏惧之——这些人曾在银镇的市集上斩杀黝暗人；且与他们血统殊异，是些（我们的人如此想）会照朋友之命行事、去对付那些对他们而言既非友亦非敌之人。有此臂助，我便大有依靠了。」

===Original===
In such wise spake Dallach; and Face-of-god and the chiefs said that so it should be, if men could be found willing to abide in Rosedale for a while. And when the matter was put abroad, there was no lack of such men amongst the younger warriors, who had noted that the dale was fair amongst dales and its women fairer yet amongst women.

===Chinese===
达拉赫如此说道；面神与众首领皆言此事当允，只要能寻得愿意暂留玫瑰谷之人。此事一传开，年轻武士之中便不乏应募者——他们早已留意到，此谷于诸谷之中最为秀美，而其女子于众女之中更为姣好。

===Original===
So two score and ten of the Burgdale men abode in Rosedale, no one of whom was of more than twenty and five winters. Forsooth divers of them set up house in Rosedale, and never came back to Burgdale, save as guests. For a half score were wedded in Rosedale before the year’s ending; and seven more, who had also taken to them wives of the goodliest of the Rosedale women, betook them the next spring to the Burg of the Runaways, and there built them a stead, and drew a garth about it, and dug and sowed the banks of the river, which they called Inglebourne. And as years passed, this same stead throve exceedingly, and men resorted thither both from Rosedale and Burgdale; for it was a pleasant place; and the land, when it was cured, was sweet and good, and the wood thereabout was full of deer of all kinds. So their stead was called Inglebourne after the stream; and in latter days it became a very goodly habitation of men.

===Chinese===
于是堡谷之人中有五十名留驻玫瑰谷，无一超过二十五冬之龄。其中确有数人在玫瑰谷安家立业，此后除作客外再未回归堡谷。因岁末之前，便有十人在玫瑰谷成婚；又有七人，亦娶了玫瑰谷女子中最姣好者为妻，于次年春前往逃奴堡，在那里筑起一处宅院，围以院墙，并于河两岸掘土播种——他们称此河为炉火溪（Inglebourne）。随着岁月流逝，这处宅院日渐繁盛，玫瑰谷与堡谷之人皆来聚居；因此地宜人；其土一经整治，便肥美丰饶，周围林中百兽群游。故其宅院因溪而得名，亦唤作炉火溪；日后成为一处极其美好的人居之所。

===Original===
Moreover, some of the once-enthralled folk of Rosedale, when they knew that men of their kindred from Silverdale were going home with the men of Burgdale to dwell in the Dale, prayed hard to go along with them; for they looked on the Burgdalers as if they were new Gods of the Earth. The Burgdale chiefs would not gainsay these men either, but took with them three score and ten from Rosedale, men and women, and promised them dwelling and livelihood in Burgdale.

===Chinese===
此外，玫瑰谷昔日为奴之人中，有知其在银谷的同族之人将随堡谷之人归去、居于谷中者，苦苦恳求同往；因他们视堡谷之人如同新生的地神一般。堡谷诸首领也不忍回绝这些人，便从玫瑰谷带走七十人，男女皆有，许他们在堡谷安身立命。

===Original===
So now with good hearts the Host of Burgdale turned their faces toward their well-beloved Dale; and they made good diligence, so that in three days’ time they were come anigh the edge of the woodland wilderness. Thither in the eventide, as they were making ready for their last supper and bed in the wood, came three men and two women of their folk, who had been abiding their coming ever since they had had the tidings of Silverdale and the battles from Dallach. Great was the joy of these messengers as they went from company to company of the warriors, and saw the familiar faces of their friends, and heard their wonted voices telling all the story of battle and slaughter. And for their part the men of the Host feasted these stay-at-homes, and made much of them. But one of them, a man of the House of the Face, left the Host a little after nightfall, and bore back to Burgstead at once the tidings of the coming home of the Host. Albeit since Dallach’s tidings of victory had come to the Dale, the dwellers in the steads of the countryside had left Burgstead and gone home to their own houses; so that there was no great multitude abiding in the Thorp.

===Chinese===
于是堡谷大军满怀欣悦，转身奔赴他们挚爱的山谷；他们赶路甚勤，三日之后便已抵近林莽荒野之边缘。彼处暮色之中，他们正备办林中最后一顿晚餐、安最后一次床铺之际，来了他们族中三男二女——这些人自打从达拉赫处闻知银谷及诸战消息之后，便一直在此守候大军驾临。这些信使穿行于一队一队武士之间，看见故友熟识的面容，听见他们熟悉的声音讲述着厮杀战伐的全本故事，心中之喜无以言表。而大军这边也将这些居家之人奉为上宾，殷勤款待。其中一人，是面神之宅的人，入夜不久便离了大军，连夜将大军归来的消息送回堡镇。然自达拉赫的捷报传至谷中之后，乡间农舍之人已纷纷离开堡镇、各回自家；故屯中所留之人已无多。

===Original===
So early on the morrow was the Host astir; but ere they came to Wildlake’s Way, the Shepherd-folk turned aside westward to go home, after they had bidden farewell to their friends and fellows of the Dale; for their souls longed for the sheepcotes in the winding valleys under the long grey downs; and the garths where the last year’s ricks shouldered up against the old stone gables, and where the daws were busy in the tall unfrequent ash-trees; and the green flowery meadows adown along the bright streams, where the crowfoot and the paigles were blooming now, and the harebells were in flower about the thorn-bushes at the down’s foot, whence went the savour of their blossom over sheepwalk and water-meadow.

===Chinese===
次日清晨，大军便已起身赶路；然未至野湖径，牧羊之民便辞别谷中之亲友同伴，折向西行归家去了；因他们的心魂早已向往那蜿蜒山谷中、绵长灰冈之下的羊栏；向往那去年草垛挨挤在旧石山墙边、高大疏落的白蜡树上寒鸦忙碌的院落；向往那沿着明丽溪流而下的一片片绿茵繁花之甸——此时毛茛与黄花九轮草正当盛开，冈脚荆棘丛畔蓝铃花正吐蕊，花香弥漫过牧羊之地与水边草甸。

===Original===
So these went their ways with many kind words; and two hours afterwards all the rest of the Host stood on the level ground of the Portway; but presently were the ranks of war disordered and broken up by the joy of the women and children, as they fell to drawing goodman or brother or lover out of the throng to the way that led speediest to their homesteads and halls. For the War-leader would not hold the Host together any longer, but suffered each man to go to his home, deeming that the men of Burgstead, and chiefly they of the Face and the Steer, would suffice for a company if any need were, and they would be easily gathered to meet any hap.

===Chinese===
这些人说着无数温言话语，各自上路；两个时辰之后，大军余众尽数立于港路之平地之上；然顷刻之间，战阵便被妇人孩童之喜乐冲散打乱——她们纷纷从人群里将自己的男人、或兄弟、或情郎拉出来，拽向通往自家农舍厅堂最快捷的那条路。因战首不愿再将大军拘作一处，任凭众人各自归家；他以为堡镇之人，尤其是面族与犍牛族之人，若遇何需用，足可成一队之用，且容易召集以应对任何变故。

===Original===
So now the men of the Middle and Lower Dale made for their houses by the road and the lanes and the meadows, and the men of the Upper Dale and Burgstead went their ways along the Portway toward their halls, with the throng of women and children that had come out to meet them. And now men came home when it was yet early, and the long day lay before them; and it was, as it were, made giddy and cumbered with the exceeding joy of return, and the thought of the day when the fear of death and sundering had been ever in their hearts. For these new hours were full of the kissing and embracing of lovers, and the sweetness of renewed delight in beholding the fair bodies so sorely desired, and hearkening the soft wheedling of longed-for voices. There were the cups of friends beneath the chestnut trees, and the talk of the deeds of the fighting-men, and of the heavy days of the home-abiders; many a tale told oft and o’er again. There was the singing of old songs and of new, and the beholding the well-loved nook of the pleasant places, which death might well have made nought for them; and they were sweet with the fear of that which was past, and in their pleasantness was fresh promise for the days to come.

===Chinese===
于是中谷与下谷之人沿大路、小径、草甸奔自家屋舍而去，上谷与堡镇之人则携着一群群出来迎接的妇人孩童，沿港路归向各自的厅堂。此时众人归家尚早，漫长一日仍铺展于前；这一日仿佛因归来之极度喜乐而令人目眩神摇、不胜负荷，又因忆起那段死亡离散之忧常驻心头的日子而百感交集。因这些崭新的时辰里满是情人们的亲吻与拥抱，满是重新得见那朝思暮想的美好身躯所涌起之甜蜜欢愉，满是聆听那梦萦魂牵之温柔嗓音所唤起之欣慰。栗树之下，故交举杯；谈说武士之功勋、居家者之艰难岁月；一段故事，反复传讲，不厌其烦。有旧曲新歌的吟唱，有重睹那些心爱角落、宜人之地——那些死亡本可轻易使之化为乌有之处；往昔之恐惧反使眼前愈发甘甜，而这甘美之中，又蕴着来日崭新的期许。

===Original===
So amid their joyance came evening and nightfall; and though folk were weary with the fullness of delight, yet now for many their weariness led them to the chamber of love before the rest of deep night came to them to make them strong for the happy life to be begun again on the morrow.

House by house they feasted, and few were the lovers that sat not together that even. But Face-of-god and the Sun-beam parted at the door of the House of the Face; for needs must she go with her new folk to the House of the Steer, and needs must Face-of-god be amongst his own folk in that hour of high-tide, and sit beside his father beneath the image of the God with the ray-begirt head.

===Chinese===
于是在他们的欢庆之中，暮色降临，夜幕四合；众人虽因欢愉之满溢而疲惫，然此时对许多人而言，这份疲惫反将他们引向了爱之密室——待到深夜酣眠来临，使他们养足精神，好在明日重启那幸福的生活。

他们挨家挨户地设宴欢庆，那一晚情人们鲜有不并肩而坐者。然面神与日光在面神之宅门前依依惜别；因她必须随她的新族人前往犍牛之宅，而面神也必须在这欢庆高潮之时刻与自家族人同在，坐在父亲身旁，在那尊首级环绕光芒的神像之下。

## LVIII How the Maiden Ward Was Held in Burgdale / 五十八 堡谷中少女守如何举行

===Original===
Now May was well worn when the Host came home to Burgdale; and on the very morrow of men’s homecoming they began to talk eagerly of the Midsummer Weddings, and how the Maiden Ward would be the greatest and fairest of all yet seen, whereas battle and the deliverance from battle stir up the longing and love both of men and maidens; much also men spake of the wedding of Face-of-god and the Sun-beam; and needs must their wedding abide to the time of the Maiden Ward at Midsummer, and needs also must the Sun-beam go on the Ward with the other Brides of the Folk. So then must Face-of-god keep his soul in patience till those few days were over, doing what work came to hand; and he held his head high among the people, and was well looked to of every man.

===Chinese===
大军归堡谷之时，五月已将阑矣；众人归来的次日，便急切地谈论起仲夏婚礼（Midsummer Weddings），又说此番少女守（the Maiden Ward）必为历来所见最为盛大、最为繁丽的一回——盖因战事及战事之解脱，皆足以激发男子与少女之情思爱恋；众人亦多谈及面神与日光之婚事；而他们的婚礼须待仲夏少女守之时方可举行，日光亦须与众族之新娘一同上守。于是面神只得按捺心神，耐过这几日，手边何事来便做何事；他在众人之中昂首挺胸，人人都对他另眼相看。

===Original===
In all matters the Sun-beam helped him, both in doing and in forbearing; and now so wonderful and rare was her beauty, that folk looked on her with somewhat of fear, as though she came from the very folk of the Gods.

===Chinese===
凡事日光都从旁助他，应做者为之，应忍者忍之；此时她的美貌已奇妙罕异至于极点，众人看她时，竟带几分敬畏，仿佛她是自诸神之族中而来。

===Original===
Indeed she seemed somewhat changed from what she had been of late; she was sober of demeanour during these last days of her maidenhood, and sat amongst the kindred as one communing with herself: of few words she was and little laughter; but her face clear, not overcast by any gloom or shaken by passion: soft and kind was she in converse with others, and sweet were the smiles that came into her face if others’ faces seemed to crave for them. For it must be said that as some folk eat out their hearts with fear of the coming evils, even so was she feeding her soul with the joy of the days to be, whatever trouble might fall upon them, whereof belike she foreboded some.

===Chinese===
诚然她似乎比近来略有不同；在少女时代这最后几日里，她举止端庄沉静，坐在亲族之间，如一人在心中默默对语：言语寥寥，笑声亦稀；然其面容清朗，不为任何阴霾所遮，亦不为激情所动：与人交谈时温柔和蔼，若旁人面容似有所渴盼，她面上便现出甜美的微笑。须知有些人因惧怕将临之祸患而憔悴其心，她却恰相反，正以将来日子之乐滋养其灵魂——任凭那些日子会遭何等忧患，其中一些她或许已有所预感。

===Original===
So wore the days toward Midsummer, when the wheat was getting past the blossoming, and the grass in the mown fields was growing deep green again after the shearing of the scythe; when the leaves were most and biggest; when the roses were beginning to fall; when the apples were reddening, and the skins of the grape-berries gathering bloom. High aloft floated the light clouds over the Dale; deep blue showed the distant fells below the ice-mountains; the waters dwindled; all things sought the shadow by daytime, and the twilight of even and the twilight of dawn were but sundered by three hours of half-dark night.

===Chinese===
日子便如此向仲夏推移，彼时麦已过花期，割过的草场经镰刀一剪之后又生出深绿的新草；树叶最密最盛；玫瑰开始凋落；苹果渐渐转红，葡萄果皮上凝起一层霜粉。淡云高悬于谷之上空；冰山之下远处的峰峦显出深蓝；水势渐瘦；白昼间万物皆趋就阴凉，而黄昏之暮色与黎明之曙光之间，不过隔了三个时辰的半明之夜。

===Original===
So in the bright forenoon were seventeen brides assembled in the Gate of Burgstead (but of the rest of the Dale were twenty and three looked for), and with these was the Sun-beam, her face as calm as the mountain lake under a summer sunset, while of the others many were restless, and babbling like April throstles; and not a few talked to her eagerly, and in their restless love of her dragged her about hither and thither.

No men were to be seen that morning; for such was the custom, that the carles either departed to the fields and the acres, or abode within doors on the morn of the day of the Maiden Ward; but there was a throng of women about the Gate and down the street of Burgstead, and it may well be deemed that they kept not silence that hour.

===Chinese===
于是在明亮的上午，十七位新娘齐聚于堡镇城门（而自谷中其他各处盼望而来的还有二十三位），日光也在其中，她的面容沉静如夏日夕阳下的山中之湖，而其余诸人多焦躁不安，叽叽喳喳如四月之画眉；更有不少人与她热切交谈，因爱她爱得按捺不住，拉着她东奔西跑。

那日早晨不见一个男子；因为风俗如此：少女守之日的清晨，汉子们或下田野，或留在屋中不出；但城门四周及堡镇街上满是妇人，可以想见，她们那一刻绝不会安静。

===Original===
So fared the Brides of Burgstead to the place of the Maiden Ward on the causeway, whereto were come already the other brides from steads up and down the Dale, or were even then close at hand on the way; and among them were Long-coat and her two fellows, with whom Face-of-god had held converse on that morning whereon he had followed his fate to the Mountain.

There then were they gathered under the cliff-wall of the Portway; and by the roadside had their grooms built them up bowers of green boughs to shelter them from the sun’s burning, which were thatched with bulrushes, and decked with garlands of the fairest flowers of the meadows and the gardens.

===Chinese===
堡镇的新娘们便如此行至大堤上的少女守之地，谷中各处农庄来的其他新娘或已先到，或已近在咫尺、正在路上；其中还有长衣（Long-coat）和她的两名同伴——正是面神追随命运往高山而去的那天早晨，与之交谈的那几位。

她们便聚集在港路（the Portway）的崖壁之下；路旁她们的新郎已为她们搭起绿枝凉棚，以遮烈日，棚顶以蒲草苫盖，并以草甸花园中最美的鲜花编成的花环加以装饰。

===Original===
Forsooth they were a lovely sight to look on, for no fairer women might be seen in the world; and the eldest of them was scant of five and twenty winters. Every maiden was clad in as goodly raiment as she might compass; their sleeves and gown-hems and girdles, yea, their very shoes and sandals were embroidered so fairly and closely, that as they shifted in the sun they changed colour like the kingfisher shooting from shadow to sunshine. According to due custom every maiden bore some weapon. A few had bows in their hands and quivers at their backs; some had nought but a sword girt to their sides; some bore slender-shafted spears, so as not to overburden their shapely hands; but to some it seemed a merry game to carry long and heavy thrust-spears, or to bear great war-axes over their shoulders. Most had their flowing hair coifed with bright helms; some had burdened their arms with shields; some bore steel hauberks over their linen smocks: almost all had some piece of war-gear on their bodies; and one, to wit, Steed-linden of the Sickle, a tall and fair damsel, was so arrayed that no garment could be seen on her but bright steel war-gear.

===Chinese===
她们诚然是一道赏心悦目的景象，世间再也见不到比她们更美的女子了；其中年最长者也不过堪堪二十五岁。每一位少女都尽力穿戴上她所能办到的最华美的衣裳；她们的衣袖、裙摆、腰带，乃至鞋子和凉履，都绣得极为精细华美，在阳光下移动时，色泽变幻如翠鸟自阴影中掠入阳光。按照习俗，每一位少女都带有某种兵器。少数人手持弓、背挎箭囊；有些人腰间只佩一把剑；有些人执杆身纤细的长矛，以免累赘她们秀美的双手；但有些人觉得手执又长又重的刺矛，或肩负大战斧，是一场欢乐的游戏。大多数人那飘垂的长发上都戴着明亮的头盔；有些人臂上挎着盾牌；有些人在亚麻罩衣外披着钢制锁子甲：几乎每个人身上都有某件战具；其中一位，即镰刀氏之驹楯（Steed-linden of the Sickle），一位高挑美貌的少女，装束如此：身上只见明亮的钢制战具，别无他衣。

===Original===
As for the Sun-beam, she was clad in a white kirtle embroidered from throat to hem with work of green boughs and flowers of the goodliest fashion, and a garland of roses on her head. Dale-warden himself was girt to her side by a girdle fair-wrought of golden wire, and she bore no other weapon or war-gear; and she let him lie quiet in his scabbard, nor touched the hilts once; whereas some of the other damsels would be ever drawing their swords out and thrusting them back. But all noted that goodly weapon, the yoke-fellow of so many great deeds.

===Chinese===
至于日光，她身穿一袭白袍，自领口至下摆皆绣以绿枝繁花之最美纹样，头戴玫瑰花环。谷卫（Dale-warden）本身由一条以金丝精工编成的腰带佩在她腰间，此外她不带任何其他兵器或战具；她任它静卧鞘中，一次也不去碰剑柄；而其他少女中有些人却总是不停地拔剑出鞘、又插回去。但众人都注意到那把华美的兵器，它是诸多丰功伟绩的同侪伴侣。

===Original===
There then on the Portway, between the water and the rock-wall, rose up plenteous and gleeful talk of clear voices shrill and soft; and whiles the maidens sang, and whiles they told tales of old days, and whiles they joined hands and danced together on the sweet summer dust of the highway. Then they mostly grew aweary, and sat down on the banks of the road or under their leafy bowers.

Noon came, and therewithal goodwives of the neighbouring Dale, who brought them meat and drink, and fruit and fresh flowers from the teeming gardens; and thereafter for a while they nursed their joy in their bosoms, and spake but little and softly while the day was at its hottest in the early afternoon.

===Chinese===
于是在港路之上，水与石壁之间，响起了欢快热闹的交谈，嗓音清亮，或尖或柔；少女们时而歌唱，时而讲述旧日的故事，时而又手拉手在公路上甘甜的夏日尘土之上翩翩起舞。后来大多数人倦了，便坐在路坡上或绿叶凉棚下。

正午到了，邻处的村妇们也来了，给她们带来饮食，以及硕果累累的园中采来的鲜果与鲜花；此后的一段时间里，她们将喜悦珍藏在胸中，言语不多而轻柔——此时正值午后初时、一日中最热的时候。

===Original===
Then came out of Burgstead men making semblance of chapmen with a wain bearing wares, and they made as though they were wending down the Portway westward to go out of the Dale. Then arose the weaponed maidens and barred the way to them, and turned them back amidst fresh-springing merriment.

Again in a while, when the sun was westering and the shadows growing long, came herdsmen from down the Dale driving neat, and making as though they would pass by into Burgstead, but to them also did the maidens gainsay the road, so that needs must they turn back amidst laughter and mockery, they themselves also laughing and mocking.

===Chinese===
随后从堡镇中走出一伙人，扮作商贩模样，赶着一辆载货的车，装作要沿港路向西出谷的样子。执兵器的少女们便起而拦路，将他们挡回，一时间又涌起新的欢笑。

又过一会儿，太阳西斜、影子拉长之时，谷中下游来了牧人赶着牛群，装作要经过此地进堡镇去；但少女们也同样不许他们通行，弄得他们只得在嬉笑嘲谑中转身回去，他们自己也跟着又笑又嘲。

===Original===
And so at last, when the maidens had been all alone a while, and it was now hard on sunset, they drew together and stood in a ring, and fell to singing; and one Gold-may of the House of the Bridge, a most sweet singer, stood amidst their ring and led them. And this is somewhat of the meaning of their words:

> The sun will not tarry; now changeth the light,
 

 Fail the colours that marry the Day to the Night.
> Amid the sun’s burning bright weapons we bore,
 

 For this eve of our earning comes once and no more.
> For today hath no brother in yesterday’s tide,
 

 And tomorrow no other alike it doth hide.
> This day is the token of oath and behest
 

 That ne’er shall be broken through ill days and best.
> Here the troth hath been given, the oath hath been done,
 

 To the Folk that hath thriven well under the sun.
> And the gifts of its giving our troth-day shall win
 

 Are the Dale for our living and dear days therein.
> O Sun, now thou wanest! yet come back and see
 

 Amidst all that thou gainest how gainful are we.
> O witness of sorrow wide over the earth,
 

 Rise up on the morrow to look on our mirth!
> Thy blooms art thou bringing back ever for men,
 

 And thy birds are a-singing each summer again.
> But to men little-hearted what winter is worse
 

 Than thy summers departed that bore them the curse?
> And e’en such art thou knowing where thriveth the year,
 

 And good is all growing save thralldom and fear.
> Nought such be our lovers’ hearts drawing anigh,
 

 While yet thy light hovers aloft in the sky.
> Lo the seeker, the finder of Death in the Blade!
 

 What lips shall be kinder on lips of mine laid?
> La he that hath driven back tribes of the South!
 

 Sweet-breathed is thine even, but sweeter his mouth.
> Come back from the sea then, O sun! come aback,
 

 Look adown, look on me then, and ask what I lack!
> Come many a morrow to gaze on the Dale,
 

 And if e’er thou seest sorrow remember its tale!
> For ’twill be of a story to tell how men died
 

 In the garnering of glory that no man may hide.
> O sun sinking under! O fragrance of earth!
 

 O heart! O the wonder whence longing has birth!

===Chinese===
如此到了最后，少女们独处了一会儿，此时已近日落，她们聚拢成一圈，开始歌唱；桥宅之金娘（Gold-may of the House of the Bridge），一位歌喉最甜美的歌手，站在圈中领唱。以下是她们歌辞大意：

> 太阳不肯留驻；光明正在变迁，
 

 使昼与夜相为婚配的诸色，渐渐凋残。
> 烈日灼照之中，我们曾执明晃晃的兵刃，
 

 我们挣来的此夕，一来再不来。
> 今日之于昨日的光阴，并无兄弟，
 

 明日之中，也未藏有与之相同的别一日。
> 此日是誓言与嘱托的凭证，
 

 任凭日子顺逆，永不破毁。
> 忠信已经许下，誓约已经立成，
 

 为那在太阳之下繁盛的族民。
> 我们订盟之日所将赢得的、它所赐的馈赠，
 

 便是此谷供我们安身，以及其中珍贵的时辰。
> 太阳啊，你今正西沉！然而回来吧，且看一看，
 

 在你所得的一切之中，我们是何等丰盈。
> 辽阔大地之上忧患的见证者啊，
 

 明日升起来看看我们的欢情吧！
> 你总是把花朵再带回来给人间，
 

 你的鸟儿每逢夏天都来歌唱。
> 然而对于心胸狭小之人，何等严冬更糟，
 

 胜过那曾给他们带来诅咒、业已逝去的夏天？
> 你便是这般知晓：一年之中何处兴旺，
 

 凡有所生长皆是善，除了奴役与恐惧。
> 愿我们爱人之心，当他们走近之时，
 

 不至如此——趁你的光犹在高空徘徊。
> 看哪，那寻觅者，那在刀锋之中寻得死亡之人！
 

 有何嘴唇能比这更温柔地贴在我唇上？
> 啊！他击退了南方诸部族！
 

 你的黄昏气息香甜，他的口更甜。
> 那么从海上回来吧，太阳啊！回来吧，
 

 俯首看看我，问我缺少什么！
> 愿你日复一日的清晨，都来看看此谷，
 

 若你曾见忧患，请记取它的故事！
> 因为那将是一个值得讲述的故事：人们如何死去，
 

 在那无人能遮掩的、荣耀的收获里。
> 沉落的太阳啊！大地的芬芳啊！
 

 心啊！那渴望由之而生的奇奥啊！

===Original===
So they sang, and the sun sank indeed; and amidst their singing the eve was still about them, though there came a happy murmur from the face of the meadows and the houses of the Thorp aloof. But as their song fell they heard the sound of footsteps a many on the road; so they turned and stood with beating hearts in such order as when a band of the valiant draw together to meet many foes coming on them from all sides, and they stand back to back to face all comers. And even therewith, their raiment gleaming amidst the gathering dusk, came on them the young men of the Dale newly delivered from the grief of war.

Then in very deed the fierce mouths of the raisers of the war-shout were kind on the faces of tender maidens. Then went spear and axe and helm and shield clattering to the earth, as the arms of the newcomers went round about the bodies of the Brides, weary with the long day of sunshine, and glee and loving speech, and the maidens suffered the young men to lead them whither they would, and twilight began to draw round about them as the Maiden Band was sundered.

===Chinese===
她们如此歌唱，太阳确实也落了下去；在她们的歌声中，四周的黄昏一片静谧，虽然远处草甸之上和屯中屋宇之间传来一阵欢快的呢喃。但当她们的歌声落下时，她们听见路上传来许多脚步声；于是她们转过身来，心跳如鼓，列成一种阵势——正如一队勇士被四面围来的众敌所逼时聚拢一处，背靠背地面对一切来者。就在此时，在渐浓的暮色中衣衫闪亮，向她们走来的，是堡谷中刚刚从战事的忧伤中解脱出来的年轻人。

于是当真地，那些惯于呐喊发战吼的粗豪之口，此刻贴在娇柔少女的面庞上，落下的尽是温柔。长矛、战斧、头盔、盾牌，叮叮当当落了一地，新来者的双臂环上了新娘们的身躯——她们已因一整日的阳光、欢笑和柔情蜜语而倦怠了——少女们任由年轻男子牵着她们，欲往何处便往何处；当少女之队解散之时，暮色便开始笼罩住他们。

===Original===
Some, they were led away westward down the Portway to the homesteads thereabout; and for divers of these the way was long to their halls, and they would have to wend over long stretches of dewy meadows, and hear the night-wind whisper in many a tree, and see the east begin to lighten with the dawn before they came to the lighted feast that awaited them. But some turned up the Portway straight towards Burgstead; and short was their road to the halls where even now the lights were being kindled for their greeting.

===Chinese===
有些人被领着向西，沿港路下行到附近的农庄去；其中几位还要走很长的路才能到自家的厅堂，她们得穿过大片沾露的草甸，听见夜风在许多树间低语，看见东方天色因破晓而渐白，方能到达那灯火通明、等待她们的宴席。但有些人径直沿港路折回堡镇；他们去往厅堂的路很短，那里的灯火此刻正在为他们点燃，以作迎接。

===Original===
As for the Sun-beam, she had been very quiet the day long, speaking as little as she might do, laughing not at all, and smiling for kindness’ sake rather than for merriment; and when the grooms came seeking their maidens, she withdrew herself from the band, and stood alone amidst the road nigher to Burgstead than they; and her heart beat hard, and her breath came short and quick, as though fear had caught her in its grip; and indeed for one moment of time she feared that he was not coming to her. For he had gone with the other grooms to that gathered band, and had passed from one to the other, not finding her, till he had got him through the whole company, and beheld her awaiting him. Then indeed he bounded toward her, and caught her by the hands, and then by the shoulders, and drew her to him, and she nothing loth; and in that while he said to her:

===Chinese===
至于日光，她整日极其安静，能不说便不说，完全不笑，即便微笑也是出于和善而非欢欣；当新郎们来寻找他们的少女时，她从队伍中退出来，独自站在路上，比他们离堡镇更近一些；她的心跳得很厉害，呼吸又短又急，仿佛被恐惧攫住了一般；确实，在某一刹那间，她害怕他不会来找她。因为他已随其他新郎到了那聚拢的一群人那里，从一个走到另一个，没有找到她，直到他把整队人都走遍了，才看见她在等着他。那时他便朝她奔过去，先抓住她的双手，继而抓住她的双肩，将她拉向自己，她丝毫没有抗拒；在这一刻他对她说：

===Original===
“Come then, my friend; lo thou! they go each their own way toward the halls of their houses; and for thee have I chosen a way﻿—a way over the footbridge yonder, and over the dewy meadows on this best even of the year.”

“Nay, nay,” she said, “it may not be. Surely the Burgstead grooms look to thee to lead them to the gate; and surely in the House of the Face they look to see thee before any other. Nay, Gold-mane, my dear, we must needs go by the Portway.”

===Chinese===
“那么来吧，我的朋友；你看！他们各自走各自的路，往自家的厅堂去；至于你，我已为你选了一条路——走过那边那座小木桥，再走过沾露的草甸，在这全年最好的傍晚里。”

“不，不，”她说，“这怎么行。堡镇的新郎们一定指望你领他们到城门去；面神之宅（the House of the Face）里的人也一定等着你比谁都先到。不，金鬃（Gold-mane），我的亲爱，我们必须走港路。”

===Original===
He said: “We shall be home but a very little while after the first, for the way I tell of is as short as the Portway. But hearken, my sweet! When we are in the meadows we shall sit down for a minute on a bank under the chestnut trees, and thence watch the moon coming up over the southern cliffs. And I shall behold thee in the summer night, and deem that I see all thy beauty; which yet shall make me dumb with wonder when I see it indeed in the house amongst the candles.”

“O nay,” she said, “by the Portway shall we go; the torchbearers shall be abiding thee at the gate.”

===Chinese===
他说：“我们只会比最先到的人晚一点点到家，因为我说的这条路和港路一样近。可是听我说，我的心肝！到了草甸之上，我们要在栗树下的一处土坡上坐一会儿，从那里看月亮从南边悬崖上升起。我将在夏夜中端详你，自以为已尽见你的美貌；然而这美貌将来在屋中烛光之下真个看见时，仍将使我惊奇得说不出话来。”

“啊，不行，”她说，“我们走港路吧；擎火把的人一定在城门处等你了。”

===Original===
Spake Face-of-god: “Then shall we rise up and wend first through a wide treeless meadow, wherein amidst the night we shall behold the kine moving about like odorous shadows; and through the greyness of the moonlight thou shalt deem that thou seest the pink colour of the eglantine blossoms, so fragrant they are.”

“O nay,” she said, “but it is meet that we go by the Portway.”

===Chinese===
面神说：“然后我们便起身，先走过一片宽阔无树的草甸，夜里我们会在其中看见牛群走动，犹如散发气味的阴影；在苍白的月光中，你会以为自己看见了野蔷薇花朵的粉色，它们是如此芬芳。”

“啊，不行，”她说，“我们理当走港路才是。”

===Original===
But he said: “Then from the wide meadow come we into a close of corn, and then into an orchard-close beyond it. There in the ancient walnut-tree the owl sitteth breathing hard in the nighttime; but thou shalt not hear him for the joy of the nightingales singing from the apple-trees of the close. Then from out of the shadowed orchard shall we come into the open town-meadow, and over its daisies shall the moonlight be lying in a grey flood of brightness.

“Short is the way across it to the brim of the Weltering Water, and across the water lieth the fair garden of the Face; and I have dight for thee there a little boat to waft us across the night-dark waters, that shall be like wavering flames of white fire where the moon smites them, and like the void of all things where the shadows hang over them. There then shall we be in the garden, beholding how the hall-windows are yellow, and hearkening the sound of the hall-glee borne across the flowers and blending with the voice of the nightingales in the trees. There then shall we go along the grass paths whereby the pinks and the cloves and the lavender are sending forth their fragrance, to cheer us, who faint at the scent of the overworn roses, and the honey-sweetness of the lilies.

“All this is for thee, and for nought but for thee this even; and many a blossom whereof thou knowest nought shall grieve if thy foot tread not thereby tonight; if the path of thy wedding which I have made, be void of thee, on the even of the Chamber of Love.

“But lo! at last at the garden’s end is the yew-walk arched over for thee, and thou canst not see whereby to enter it; but I, I know it, and I lead thee into and along the dark tunnel through the moonlight, and thine hand is not weary of mine as we go. But at the end shall we come to a wicket, which shall bring us out by the gable-end of the Hall of the Face. Turn we about its corner then, and there are we blinking on the torches of the torchbearers, and the candles through the open door, and the hall ablaze with light and full of joyous clamour, like the balefire in the dark night kindled on a ness above the sea by fisher-folk remembering the Gods.”

===Chinese===
但是他说：“然后从那片宽阔草甸出来，我们便走进一片麦田，再走进麦田那边的一片果园。那棵古老的核桃树上，夜里猫头鹰坐在那里喘着粗气；可是你不会听得见它，因为果园中苹果树上的夜莺唱得正欢。然后从那阴影笼罩的果园中出来，我们便走进开阔的镇上草甸，月光会如一道灰白的明亮洪流，铺洒在雏菊之上。

“从那里穿过草甸到翻滚河（the Weltering Water）的岸边，路很短；河对面便是面神家那美丽的花园；我已在花园里为你备下一只小舟，把我们渡过夜色漆黑的水面——那水在月亮照射之处，会像摇曳的白色火焰；在阴影笼罩之处，则像万物皆空的虚无。然后我们便到了花园里，看见厅堂的窗子一片金黄，听见厅堂中的欢笑声越过花丛传来，与树上夜莺的歌声交融在一起。然后我们便沿着草径走去，径旁的石竹、康乃馨和薰衣草吐出芬芳，为我们提神——我们闻着那已开败的玫瑰之气、百合之蜜甜，已觉昏然欲醉了。

“这一切都是为你准备的，今夜只为你一人而设；许多你尚不知晓的花朵，今夜若你的脚不从旁经过，它们将会悲伤；我所为你铺就的婚路，若在这爱之阁（the Chamber of Love）之夜少了你，便会落空。

“看哪！终于在花园的尽头，是为你在紫杉夹道、拱覆成廊之处；你看不见从何处可以进去；可是我，我知道，我领着你走进这条穿过月光的暗黑隧道，走着走着，你的手也不曾厌倦我的手。但走到尽头，我们会来到一道小门，它会把我们带到面神之厅（the Hall of the Face）的山墙尽头。绕过它的墙角，我们便迎着擎火把者的火光眨眼，迎着敞开的门里透出的烛光眨眼——厅中灯火辉煌，充满了欢腾的喧闹，犹如渔人在夜里于海岬之上、为追念诸神而点燃的篝火。”

===Original===
“O nay,” she said, “but by the Portway must we go; the straightest way to the Gate of Burgstead.”

In vain she spake, and knew not what she said; for even as he was speaking he led her away, and her feet went as her will went, rather than her words; and even as she said that last word she set her foot on the first board of the footbridge; and she turned aback one moment, and saw the long line of the rock-wall yet glowing with the last of the sunset of midsummer, while as she turned again, lo! before her the moon just beginning to lift himself above the edge of the southern cliffs, and betwixt her and him all Burgdale, and Face-of-god moreover.

===Chinese===
“啊，不行，”她说，“我们必须走港路；那才是去堡镇城门最直的路。”

她说也徒然，自己也不知道说了什么；因为他说着话便已牵着她走开，她的脚是随她的心走的，而非随她的话；正当她说出最后一个字时，她的一只脚已踏上了小木桥的第一块板；她回头一望，只见那一道长长的石壁仍在仲夏夕阳的最后一抹余晖中发亮；再转回头时，看哪！她面前，月亮正从南边悬崖的边缘刚刚升起，而她与月亮之间，是整个堡谷，还有面神。

===Original===
Thus then they crossed the bridge into the green meadows, and through the closes and into the garden of the Face and unto the Hall-door; and other brides and grooms were there before them (for six grooms had brought home brides to the House of the Face); but none deemed it amiss in the War-leader of the folk and the love that had led him. And old Stone-face said: “Too many are the rows of bee-skeps in the gardens of the Dale that we should begrudge wayward lovers an hour’s waste of candlelight.”

So at last those twain went up the sun-bright Hall hand in hand in all their loveliness, and up on to the dais, and stood together by the middle seat; and the tumult of the joy of the kindred was hushed for a while as they saw that there was speech in the mouth of the War-leader.

===Chinese===
他们便如此过了桥，走进青青草甸，穿过一块块田亩，走进面神家之花园，直抵厅门；在他们之前已有了别的新娘新郎（因为有六位新郎把新娘领回了面神之宅）；但没有人觉得族民的战首（War-leader）以及引领着他的那份爱这样做有何不妥。老石面（Stone-face）说：“谷中花园里的蜂巢一排接一排，那么多，我们何至于吝惜一对任性恋人虚掷的一两个时辰烛光呢。”

于是这一对终于手牵手、带着他们的万种风华，走上阳光灿烂的厅堂，走上高台，并肩站在中间的座旁；亲族们欢乐的喧腾暂时安静下来，因为他们看见战首口中有话要说。

===Original===
Then he spread his hands abroad before them all and cried out: “How then have I kept mine oath, whereas I swore on the Holy Boar to wed the fairest woman of the world?”

A mighty shout went rattling about the timbers of the roof in answer to his word; and they that looked up to the gable of the Hall said that they saw the ray-ringed image of the God smile with joy over the gathered folk.

But spake Iron-face unheard amidst the clamour of the Hall: “How fares it now with my darling and my daughter, who dwelleth amongst strangers in the land beyond the wildwood?”

===Chinese===
他便在众人面前张开双手，高声喊道：“我既在圣猪（the Holy Boar）之前发誓娶世间最美的女子为妻，我这誓守得如何？”

一声震天的呐喊回荡在屋梁之间，作为对他这句话的回答；仰头望向厅堂山墙的人说，他们看见那位光芒环绕的神像，因喜悦而对济济一堂的族民露出了微笑。

但铁面（Iron-face）在厅堂的喧腾中，说了一句谁也没听见的话：“我心爱的、我的女儿，如今在那野林之外的异乡、在陌生人之中，可过得好么？”

## XI Men Make Oath at Burgstead on the Holy Boar / 十一 众人于堡镇对圣猪立誓

===Original===
A week after the ransacking at Greentofts the snow and the winter came on in earnest, and all the Dale lay in snow, and men went on skids when they fared up and down the Dale or on the Mountain.
All was now tidingless till Yule over, and in Burgstead was there feasting and joyance enough; and especially at the House of the Face was high-tide holden, and the Alderman and his sons and Stone-face and all the kindred and all their men sat in glorious attire within the hall; and many others were there of the best of the kindreds of Burgstead who had been bidden.

===Chinese===
绿冢（Greentofts）遭劫之后又过一周，大雪与严冬果然而至，全谷皆没于雪，人若上下于谷中、或入于山中，皆须踩着雪橇而行。
自此直到岁末冬至节（Yuletide）既过，一切太平无事；堡镇之中盛宴欢娱，尽堪受用；尤以面神之宅（the House of the Face）大行盛节之礼，长老（the Alderman）及其诸子、石面（Stone-face）、合族上下并所有部曲，皆盛服坐于厅中；此外又有应邀而来的堡镇诸族中诸多贵人。

===Original===
Face-of-god sat between his father and Stone-face; and he looked up and down the tables and the hall and saw not the Bride, and his heart misgave him because she was not there, and he wondered what had befallen and if she were sick of sorrow.
But Iron-face beheld him how he gazed about, and he laughed; for he was exceeding merry that night and fared as a young man. Then he said to his son: “Whom seekest thou, son? is there someone lacking?”
Face-of-god reddened as one who lies unused to it, and said:

===Chinese===
面神（Face-of-god）坐于其父与石面之间；他上下打量几案、环顾厅堂，竟不见新娘（the Bride），心中便老大不安，不知她究竟出了何事，又疑她莫非因愁成疾。
铁面（Iron-face）却看在眼里，见他四处张望，不禁大笑；原来他今夜兴致极高，举止全如少年人一般。遂对其子道：“儿啊，你在寻谁？可是少了什么人？”
面神登时面红过耳，一如不惯撒谎之人被当场说破，道：

===Original===
“Yea, kinsman, so it is that I was seeking the Bride my kinswoman.”
“Nay,” said Iron-face, “call her not kinswoman: therein is ill-luck, lest it seem that thou art to wed one too nigh thine own blood. Call her the Bride only: to thee and to me the name is good. Well, son, desirest thou sorely to see her?”
“Yea, yea, surely,” said Face-of-god; but his eyes went all about the hall still, as though his mind strayed from the place and that home of his.
Said Iron-face: “Have patience, son, thou shalt see her anon, and that in such guise as shall please thee.”

===Chinese===
“正是，父亲，我方才确在寻我的族妹新娘。”
“不然，”铁面道，“莫叫她族妹：此中颇有晦气，恐显得你欲娶血脉过近之女。只唤她‘新娘’便好——此名于你于我皆相宜。罢了，儿啊，你可想见她想得紧？”
“正是，正是，自然想的，”面神道；然而他两目仍不住扫视全厅，恍如心神早已离此地去、离了自家宅院。
铁面道：“且忍耐片刻，儿啊，你即刻便可见她，且是以令你赏心悦目之姿相见。”

===Original===
Therewithal came the maidens with the ewers of wine, and they filled all horns and beakers, and then stood by the endlong tables on either side laughing and talking with the carles and the older women; and the hall was a fair sight to see, for the many candles burned bright and the fire on the hearth flared up, and those maids were clad in fair raiment, and there was none of them but was comely, and some were fair, and some very fair: the walls also were hung with goodly pictured cloths, and the image of the God of the Face looked down smiling terribly from the gable-end above the high-seat.
Thus as they sat they heard the sound of a horn winded close outside the hall door, and the door was smitten on. Then rose Iron-face smiling merrily, and cried out:

===Chinese===
正说话间，众少女捧着酒壶鱼贯而入，将所有角杯、酒盏一一斟满，然后分立长桌两旁，与那些汉子及年长妇人有说有笑；此时厅中景象煞是可观：烛光通明、炉火熊熊，众少女皆着盛装，无一不貌美，其中有几分姿色者，有容貌出众者，更有甚是姝丽者：四壁又悬满精美之画幔，那面之神（the God of the Face）的神像，自高座上方之屋山墙处，含笑俯瞰，威容可畏。
正这般坐着，忽听厅门之外近处传来一声号角，紧接着门上砰然遭人捶打。铁面欣然含笑起身，高声呼道：

===Original===
“Enter ye, whether ye be friends or foes: for if ye be foemen, yet shall ye keep the holy peace of Yule, unless ye be the foes of all kindreds and nations, and then shall we slay you.”
Thereat some who knew what was toward laughed; but Gold-mane, who had been away from Burgstead some days past, marvelled and knit his brows, and let his right hand fall on his sword-hilt. For this folk, who were of merry ways, were wont to deal diversely with the Yuletide customs in the manner of shows; and he knew not that this was one of them.

===Chinese===
“请进罢，任凭是友是敌：纵是仇敌，亦须守这岁末冬至节之圣安，除非尔等乃天下万族万邦之公敌——若果如此，我们便要取尔等性命。”
在座有些知情之人听了皆笑；独有金鬃（Gold-mane）——他前几日不在堡镇——闻言一头雾水，皱紧眉头，右手已按上剑柄。盖因此族生性乐天，每于岁末冬至节之风俗，好作种种戏耍变通；他不知眼前这一桩便是其中之一。

===Original===
Now was the Outer door thrown open, and there entered seven men, whereof two were all-armed in bright war-gear, and two bore slug-horns, and two bore up somewhat on a dish covered over with a piece of rich cloth, and the seventh stood before them all wrapped up in a dark fur mantle.
Thus they stood a moment; and when he saw their number, back to Gold-mane’s heart came the thought of those folk on the Mountain: for indeed he was somewhat out of himself for doubt and longing, else would he have deemed that all this was but a Yuletide play.
Now the men with the slug-horns set them to their mouths and blew a long blast; while the first of the newcomers set hand to the clasps of the fur cloak and let it fall to the ground, and lo! a woman exceeding beauteous, clad in glistering raiment of gold and fine web; her hair wreathed with bay, and in her hand a naked sword with goodly-wrought golden hilt and polished blue-gleaming blade.

===Chinese===
此时外门大开，进来七人，其中两名披挂鲜明战甲、全身武装，两名手执长号角，两名共捧一盘、上覆一块锦缎、盘中隐约盛着何物，第七人立于众人之前，周身裹着一件深色毛皮斗篷。
众人如此静立片刻；金鬃一见其人数，心中忽又念及山上所遇之人：实则他此刻为疑虑与渴慕所扰，神魂已非其所有，否则必会看出眼前这一切不过是一出岁末冬至之戏罢了。
此时执长号角之二人将号角凑至唇边，吹出一声长音；那为首的新客则伸手解开毛皮斗篷的搭扣，任其滑落地上——呀！只见一位极美之女子，身披金线与细纱织就之闪闪衣裳；其发以月桂缠束，手执一柄出鞘之剑，剑柄精工镂金，剑身打磨得泛出幽蓝寒光。

===Original===
Face-of-god started up in his sear, and stared like a man new-wakened from a strange dream: because for one moment he deemed verily that it was the Woman of the Mountain arrayed as he had last seen her, and he cried aloud “The Friend, the Friend!”
His father brake out into loud laughter thereat, and clapped his son on the shoulder and said: “Yea, yea, lad, thou mayst well say the Friend; for this is thine old playmate whom thou hast been looking round the hall for, arrayed this eve in such fashion as is meet for her goodliness and her worthiness. Yea, this is the Friend indeed!”
Then waxed Face-of-god as red as blood for shame, and he sat him down in his place again: for now he wotted what was toward, and saw that this fair woman was the Bride.
But Stone-face from the other side looked keenly on him.

===Chinese===
面神从座上一跃而起，瞪目直视，宛如方从一场异梦中惊醒：原来一刹那间，他竟以为眼前之人正是那位山中女子（the Woman of the Mountain），穿着与他末次相见时一般无二；他不由得高声呼道：“友伴！友伴（the Friend）！”
其父闻言放声大笑，在子肩上一拍，道：“正是，正是，孩子，你唤她友伴倒也恰切；因为这位正是你那旧日玩伴——你方才正满厅寻她——今夜如此盛装，正配得上她的容颜与身份。哈，这确确实实是位友伴呢！”
面神顿时羞得面红过耳、宛如血染，复又颓然坐下归于本座：原来他这才明白是怎么回事，看清眼前这位绝色女子正是新娘。
石面在另一侧，却目光锐利地打量着他。

===Original===
Then blew the horns again, and the Bride stepped daintily up the hall, and the sweet odour of her raiment went from her about the fire-warmed dwelling, and her beauty moved all hearts with love. So stood she at the high-table; and those two who bore the burden set it down thereon and drew off the covering, and lo! there was the Holy Boar of Yule on which men were wont to make oath of deeds that they would do in the coming year, according to the custom of their forefathers. Then the Bride laid the goodly sword beside the dish, and then went round the table and sat down betwixt Face-of-god and Stone-face, and turned kindly to Gold-mane, and was glad; for now was his fair face as its wont was to be. He in turn smiled upon her, for she was fair and kind and his fellow for many a day.
Now the men-at-arms stood each side the Boar, and out from them on each side stood the two hornsmen: then these blew up again, whereon the Alderman stood up and cried:

===Chinese===
号角再鸣，新娘袅袅婷婷穿过厅堂而行，她衣裳之幽香随火暖之气温溢满室，其美貌令满座皆生爱慕之心。她步至高桌之前立定；那两名捧物之人将所捧之物安放桌上，揭去覆盖之锦——呀！正是岁末冬至之圣猪（the Holy Boar of Yule）：按先祖之俗，众人每于其上立誓，誓说来年所欲行之诸事。新娘遂将那柄宝剑置于盘旁，然后绕过桌案，在面神与石面之间坐下，和颜悦色转向金鬃，心中欢喜；因为此刻他那俊美容颜已复如平常。他也含笑望她，因为她既美且亲，与他实是多年的同伴。
此时两名兵士分立圣猪两旁，再往外两侧各立一名号手：号手再度吹响号角，长老遂起身高呼：

===Original===
“Ye sons of the brave who have any deed that ye may be desirous of doing, come up, come lay your hand on the sword, and the point of the sword to the Holy Beast, and swear the oath that lieth on your hearts.”
Therewith he sat down, and there strode a man up the hall, strong-built and sturdy, but short of stature; black-haired, red-bearded, and ruddy-faced: and he stood on the dais, and took up the sword and laid its point on the Boar, and said:
“I am Bristler, son of Brightling, a man of the Shepherds. Here by the Holy Boar I swear to follow up the ransackers of Penny-thumb and the slayers of Rusty. And I take this feud upon me, although they be no good men, because I am of the kin and it falleth to me, since others forbear; and when the Court was hallowed hereon I was away out of the Dale and the Downs. So help me the Warrior, and the God of the Earth.”

===Chinese===
“尔等勇者之裔，凡心存欲为之事者，上前来，将手按在此剑之上，剑尖指向这头圣兽，把压在你们心头的誓言说出来罢。”
言罢坐下。只见一人大步穿过厅堂走上前来，骨健筋强、甚是壮实，却生得矮小；黑发、红须、面膛赤红：他立于高台之上，抄起那剑，将剑尖搭在圣猪之上，说道：
“我乃鬃汉（Bristler），亮生（Brightling）之子，牧羊之民（the Shepherds）中的一员。今在此圣猪之前我立誓：定要追剿劫掠便士拇（Penny-thumb）之贼，与杀害锈皮（Rusty）之仇人。我虽知他们并非什么了得之人，仍将此仇揽于己身，因为我与他们同族、此仇当落于我身，而旁人皆袖手不管；况且昔日判决庭就此事行圣仪之时，我正离谷出丘、不在其地。愿武神（the Warrior）佑我，愿地神（the God of the Earth）佑我。”

===Original===
Then the Alderman nodded his head to him kindly, and reached him out a cup of wine, and as he drank there went up a rumour of praise from the hall; and men said that his oath was manly and that he was like to keep it; for he was a good man-at-arms and a stout heart.
Then came up three men of the Shepherds and two of the Dale and swore to help Bristler in his feud, and men thought it well sworn.
After that came a braggart, a man very gay of his raiment, and swore with many words that if he lived the year through he would be a captain over the men of the Plain, and would come back again with many gifts for his friends in the Dale. This men deemed foolishly sworn, for they knew the man; so they jeered at him and laughed as he went back to his place ashamed.
Then swore three others oaths not hard to be kept, and men laughed and were merry.

===Chinese===
长老遂和颜点头，递过一杯酒去；他饮罢，满厅响起一片称善之声；众人皆道他此誓颇有丈夫气，料他必能践言；因为他本是精强之兵士、壮胆之汉子。
随后又有牧羊之民三人、谷民两人上前，立誓助鬃汉复此仇，众人皆以为此誓立得好。
其后又上来一个浮夸之徒，衣着甚是华艳，口若悬河地立誓道：若能活过此年，必能做平原之民的统帅，归来时必为谷中故人携来厚礼无数。众人皆以为此誓糊涂，深知其人底细；于是他羞惭归座之际，满座皆起哄嘲笑。
接着又有三人立下不难践行之誓，众人皆笑、其乐融融。

===Original===
At last uprose the Alderman, and said: “Kinsmen, and good fellows, good days and peaceable are in the Dale as now; and of such days little is the story, and little it availeth to swear a deed of derring-do: yet three things I swear by this Beast; and first to gainsay no man’s asking if I may perform it; and next to set right above law and mercy above custom; and lastly, if the days change and war cometh to us or we go to meet it, I will be no backwarder in the onset than three fathoms behind the foremost. So help me the Warrior, and the God of the Face and the Holy Earth!”
Therewith he sat down, and all men shouted for joy of him, and said that it was most like that he would keep his oath.

===Chinese===
末了，长老起身道：“诸位族人，诸位好兄弟，目下谷中正是太平好光阴；这般日子并无多少事迹可述，也犯不着起什么惊世骇俗之誓：然而我仍借此圣兽立下三事：其一，凡有人有所求，只要我力所能及，绝不推辞；其二，将公道置于律法之上，将仁慈置于成规之上；其三，若时局有变、战祸临头——无论敌来或我往——冲锋之际，我必不落人后，至多在最先那人之后三丈之内。愿武神佑我，愿面之神与神圣大地佑我！”
言罢归座，满堂皆为之欢呼，众人皆道他必能践行此誓。

===Original===
Last of all uprose Face-of-god and took up the sword and looked at it; and so bright was the blade that he saw in it the image of the golden braveries which the Bride bore, and even some broken image of her face. Then he handled the hilt and laid the point on the Boar, and cried:
“Hereby I swear to wed the fairest woman of the Earth before the year is worn to an end; and that whether the Dalesmen gainsay me or the men beyond the Dale. So help me the Warrior, and the God of the Face and the Holy Earth!”
Therewith he sat down; and once more men shouted for the love of him and of the Bride, and they said he had sworn well and like a chieftain.

===Chinese===
最后，面神起身，抄起那剑端详；只见剑身明如秋水，竟映出新娘身上所佩金饰之影，乃至她容颜之一斑亦隐约可见。他握住剑柄，将剑尖搭在圣猪之上，朗声道：
“我在此立誓：此年未尽之前，必娶大地之上最美之女子为妻；任凭谷民反对，任凭谷外之人反对，我必行此事。愿武神佑我，愿面之神与神圣大地佑我！”
言罢归座；众人因疼爱他与新娘之故，再度齐声欢呼，皆道他此誓立得好，大有首领之风。

===Original===
But the Bride noted him that neither were his eyes nor his voice like to their wont as he swore, for she knew him well; and thereat was she ill at ease, for now whatever was new in him was to her a threat of evil to come.
Stone-face also noted him, and he knew the young man better than all others save the Bride, and he saw withal that she was ill-pleased, and he said to himself: “I will speak to my fosterling tomorrow if I may find him alone.”
So came the swearing to an end, and they fell to on their meat and feasted on the Boar of Atonement after they had duly given the Gods their due share, and the wine went about the hall and men were merry till they drank the parting cup and fared to rest in the shut-beds, and whereso else they might in the Hall and the House, for there were many men there.

===Chinese===
新娘却注意到：他立誓之时，目光与声音皆异于平日，因为她对他知之甚深；她因此心生不安，因为此刻他身上任何异样，在她看来皆预示来日之凶险。
石面也注意到他——除了新娘之外，石面比谁都更了解这个年轻人——同时又看出新娘心中不悦，遂暗自盘算：“明日若能寻他独处，我须与我这养子谈一谈。”
立誓既毕，众人遂就席大啖，先依礼将诸神应得之分献上，然后享用那赎罪之猪（the Boar of Atonement）；酒在厅中流转，众人尽欢，直至饮过散席之杯，方才就寝——或睡于封闭木榻之中，或厅内宅中凡可容身之处皆已卧满，因为今夜在此之人实在太多。

## XLVI Men Meet in the Market of Silverstead / 四十六 银镇集市中众人相会

===Original===
So sang they; but Face-of-god went with Red-wolf, who was hurt sorely, but not deadly, and led him back toward the place just under the break of the bent; and there he found Bow-may in the hands of the women who were tending her hurts. She smiled on him from a pale face as he drew nigh, and he looked kindly at her, but he might not abide there, for haste was in his feet. He left Red-wolf to the tending of the women, and clomb the bent hastily, and when he deemed he was high enough, he looked about him; and somewhat more than half an hour had worn since Bow-may had sped the first shaft against the Dusky Men.

He looked down into the Marketstead, and deemed he could see that nigh the Mote-house the Dusky Men were gathering into some better order; but they were no longer drifting toward the southern bents, but were standing round about the altar as men abiding somewhat; and he deemed that they had gotten more bowshot than before, and that most of them bare bows. Though so many had been slain in the battles of the southern bents, yet was the Marketstead full of them, so to say, for others had come thereto in place of those that had fallen.

But now as he looked arose mighty clamour amongst them; and a little west of the Altar was a stir and a hurrying onward and around as in the eddies of a swift stream. Face-of-god wotted not what was betiding there, but he deemed that they were now ware of the onfall of Folk-might and Hall-face and the men of Burgdale, for their faces were all turned to where that was to be looked for.

So he turned and looked on the road to the east of him, where had been the battle of the Steer, but now it was all gone down toward the Marketplace, and he could but hear the clamour of it; but nought he saw thereof, because of the houses that hid it.

Then he cast his eyes on the road that entered the Marketstead from the north, and he saw thereon many men gathered; and he wotted not what they were; for though there were weapons amongst them, yet were they not all weaponed, as far as he could see.

===Chinese===
众人如此唱罢；面神（Face-of-god）却陪着红狼（Red-wolf）——红狼伤得不轻，却未伤及要害——将他领回山坡断口正下方之处；在那里，他看见弓娥（Bow-may）正由几名妇人家照看着伤。他走近时，弓娥自一张苍白的脸上向他微笑，他也温颜看她一眼，却不能在那里逗留，因他脚下心急如焚。他将红狼交与妇人家照料，自个儿匆匆攀上山坡，待觉着已攀得够高，便四下眺望；自弓娥向黝暗人（the Dusky Men）射出第一箭以来，已过了小半个时辰。

他俯瞰集市坪（the Marketstead），只见议事堂（the Mote-house）近旁，黝暗人正重整队形，略见齐整；他们已不再向南面山坡涌去，而是围着祭坛站立，像在等候什么；他看得分明，他们的弓箭较先前为多，多半都拿着弓。虽说南面山坡诸战中已毙敌甚众，然这集市坪之中仍可说是黑压压挤满了他们，盖因倒下之处又有旁人补上。

正看间，敌阵中忽起一片惊天喧声；祭坛稍西之处，一阵骚动，人潮前涌后回，犹如急流中之漩涡。面神不知那里出了何事，却揣想他们此刻已发觉民强（Folk-might）、厅面（Hall-face）与堡谷（Burgdale）之众来攻，因其面孔尽皆转向那一路当来之方位。

于是他转身望向东面那条路——犍牛旗昔日鏖战之处；然此刻战事已尽数压向集市，他只能闻其喧声，却因房屋遮蔽而一无所见。

随后他将目光投向自北面进入集市坪的那条路，见路上聚着好些人；他辨不清那是些什么人；因其中虽有持兵刃者，然就他目力所及，并非人人皆持兵刃。

===Original===
Now as he looked this way and that, and deemed that he must tarry no longer, but must enter into the courts of the houses before him and make his way into the Marketstead, lo! a change in the throng of Dusky Warriors nigh the Mote-house, and the ordered bands about the Altar fell to drifting toward the western way with one accord, with great noise and hurry and fierce cries of wrath. Then made Face-of-god no delay, but ran down the bent at once, and at the break of it came upon Bow-may standing upright and sword in hand; and as he passed, she joined herself to him, and said: “What new tidings now, Gold-mane?”

“Tidings of battle!” he cried; “tidings of victory! Folk-might hath fallen on, and the Dusky Men run hastily to meet him. Hark, hark!”

For as he spoke came a great noise of horns, and Bow-may said: “What horn is that blowing?”

He stayed not, but shouted aloud: “For the Face, for the Face! Now will we fall upon their backs!”

===Chinese===
他正左顾右盼、自觉再不可耽搁，须进入眼前那些屋宇的庭院、由此杀入集市坪——忽然！议事堂近旁那一群黝暗武士骚然有变：祭坛四周原本齐整的队伍，齐齐向西路移去，喧嚷纷乱、怒声猛厉。面神不再迟疑，当即奔下山坡，至断口处迎面遇见弓娥挺身而立、手执长剑；他掠过之际，她便与他合为一处，问道：“金鬃（Gold-mane），如今又有何新消息？”

“战事之讯！”他呼道，“得胜之讯！民强已然杀到，黝暗人正急急迎上去。听啊，听啊！”

原来正说话间，传来一片号角之声，弓娥问道：“那是何处的号角在响？”

他并不停步，只高声呼喝：“为了面旗！为了面旗！我们如今要从他们背后掩杀！”

===Original===
Therewith was he come to his company, and he cried out to them: “Heard ye the horn, heard ye the horn? Now follow me into the Marketplace; much is yet to do!”

Even therewith came the sound of other horns, and all men were silent a moment, and then shouted all together, for the Woodlanders knew it for the horn of the Shepherds coming on by the eastward way.

But Face-of-god waved his sword aloft and set on at once, and they followed and gat them through the courts of the houses and their passages into the Marketplace. There they found more room than they looked to find; for the foemen had drawn away on the left hand toward the battle of Folk-might, and on the right hand toward the battle of the Steer; and great was the noise and cry that came thence.

===Chinese===
说话间他已奔回自己那一队人马之中，向他们高呼：“你们可曾听见号角，可曾听见号角？如今随我杀入集市，尚有许多事要做！”

正在此际，又传来旁的号角之声，众人一时默然，继而齐声欢呼——盖因林中之民（the Woodlanders）听出那是牧羊之民（the Shepherds）自东路杀到的号角。

面神却已将剑高高挥起，当即杀出，众人紧随其后，穿过那些屋宇的庭院与夹道，杀入集市。到了那里，他们发觉比预想宽敞得多；因敌人已向左趋去应对民强那一路的战事，向右趋去应对犍牛族的战事；自那两处传来的喊杀之声甚是鼎沸。

===Original===
Now stood Face-of-god under the two banners of the Wolf in the Marketplace of Silverstead, and scarce had he time to be high-hearted, for needs must he ponder in his mind what thing were best to do. For on the left hand he deemed the foe was the strongest and best ordered; but there also were the kindreds the doughtiest, and it was little like that the felons should overcome the spear-casters of the Face and the glaive-bearers of the Sickle, and the bowmen of the Vine: there also were the wisest leaders, as the stark elder Stone-face, and the tall Hall-face, and his father of the unshaken heart, and above all Folk-might, fierce in his wrath, but his anger burning steady and clear, like the oaken butt on the hearth of the hall.

Then as his mind pictured him amongst the foe, it made therewith another picture of the slender warrior Sun-beam caught in the tangle of battle, and longing for him and calling for him amidst the hard handplay. And thereat his face flushed, and all his body waxed hot, and he was on the very point of leading the onset against the foe on the left. But therewith he bethought him of the bold men of the Steer and the Bridge and the Bull weary with much fighting; and he remembered also that the Bride was amongst them and fighting, it might be, amidst the foremost, and if she were slain how should he ever hold up his head again. He bethought him also that the Shepherds, who had fallen on by the eastern road, valiant as they were, were scarce so well armed or so well led as the others. Therewithal he bethought him (and again it came like a picture into his mind) of falling on the foemen by whom the southern battle was beset, and then the twain of them meeting the Shepherds, and lastly, all those three companies joined together clearing the Marketplace, and meeting the men under Folk-might in the midst thereof.

===Chinese===
此刻面神立于银镇（Silverstead）集市之中、两面狼旗之下，几乎无暇意气风发，因他心中必须盘算何为上策。盖因在他看来，左路之敌最为强悍、阵形最为严整；然那里诸族之勇士也最为刚猛，那群恶徒（the Felons）断难压倒面族的掷矛手、镰族的长刀手，以及葡藤族的弓手：那里也有最睿智的首领——如刚毅的长者石面（Stone-face），高大的厅面，他那心志不摇之父，而尤为民强，其怒凶猛，却烧得稳而明澈，一如厅堂炉畔那段橡木根桩。

当他心中描摹出民强身在敌阵之状，紧接着又浮现另一幅图景：那纤秀的武士日光（Sun-beam）陷于战阵的纠葛之中，正苦苦盼他、唤他来援于这场惨烈的白刃之间。他不由面颊发热，通身滚烫，几乎便要率众向左路之敌发起冲锋。然而他随即又想起犍牛族、桥族、公牛族那些勇武之士已鏖战多时、疲惫不堪；他又记起新娘（the Bride）也在他们中间，说不定正冲在最前，若她阵亡了，自己日后如何还能抬起头来做人。他又想到，那些自东路杀来的牧羊之民虽然英勇，却未必像旁人那般装备精良、指挥得宜。于是他又盘算（这念头又如一幅图景浮上心头）：先去掩杀围困南面那一路战事的敌人，然后两路会合牧羊之民，最后这三支人马联为一体、扫清集市，在集市正中与民强所领之众会师。

===Original===
Therefore, scant had he been pondering these things in his mind for a minute ere he cried out: “Blow up horns, blow up! forward banners, and follow me, O valiant men! to the helping of the Steer, the Bridge, and the Bull; deep have they thrust into the Dusky Throng, and belike are hard pressed. Hark how the clamour ariseth from their besetters! On now, on!”

Therewith hung a star of sunlight on his sword as he raised it aloft, and the Wolf-whoop rang out terribly in the Marketplace, for now had the Woodlanders also learned it, and the hearts of the foemen sank as they heard the might and the mass thereof. Then the battle of the Woodlanders swept round and fell upon the flank of them who were besetting the kindreds, as an iron bar smiteth the soft fir-wood; and they of the kindreds heard their cry, but faintly and confusedly, so great was the turmoil of battle about them.

===Chinese===
因此，他在心头将此事盘算了不到片刻，便高声呼喝：“吹起号角，吹起来！旗帜向前，众位勇士随我来！去援救犍牛族、桥族、公牛族；他们已深深杀入黝暗人丛中，想必正吃紧。听那围攻他们之人所发的喧声多盛！上啊，上啊！”

他举剑过顶之际，剑上一簇日光犹如明星高悬；狼嗥（the Wolf-whoop）之声在集市中惊天动地地响起——盖因林中之民如今也已学会此声——敌人闻其浩大雄沉之声势，无不胆落。于是林中之民这一阵横扫而回，直扑围困诸族之敌的侧翼，一如铁杖横扫松软杉木；诸族人等虽听见了他们的呐喊，却听得不甚分明、隐隐约约，只因身遭战事正混乱得厉害。

===Original===
Now once more was Bow-may by the side of Face-of-god; and if she had not the might of the mightiest, yet had she the deftness of the deftest. And now was she calm and cool, shielding herself with a copper-bossed target, and driving home the point of her sharp sword; white was her face, and her eyes glittered amidst it, and she seemed to men like to those on whose heads the Warrior hath laid the Holy Bread.

As to Wood-wise, he had given the Banner of the red-jawed Wolf to Stone-wolf, a huge and dreadful warrior some forty winters old, who had fought in the Great Overthrow, and now hewed down the Dusky Men, wielding a heavy short-sword left-handed. But Wood-wise himself fought with a great sword, giving great strokes to the right hand and the left, and was no more hasty than is the hewer in the winter wood.

Face-of-god fought wisely and coldly now, and looked more to warding his friends than destroying his foes, and both to Bow-may and Wood-wise his sword was a shield; for oft he took the life from the edge of the upraised axe, and stayed the point of the foeman in midair.

===Chinese===
此刻弓娥又到了面神身旁；她纵无最强者之力，却有最巧者之巧。此刻她沉静冷峻，以一面镶铜钉的圆盾护身，将她那柄利剑的锋尖直刺入敌；她面色苍白，双目于其中灼灼生辉，在众人看来，她恰似那些被武神（the Warrior）在头上放过圣饼（the Holy Bread）之人。

至于林智（Wood-wise），他已将那面血红巨颚的狼旗交与石狼（Stone-wolf）——一个年约四十、魁梧可畏的武士，曾经历大倾覆（the Great Overthrow）之战，此刻左手挥一柄沉重的短剑，将黝暗人逐一砍倒。而林智本人则使一口大剑，左右大开大阖，其从容不迫，一如隆冬伐木之樵夫。

面神此刻迎战得既沉静又冷峻，更重护卫同伴，而不甚着意杀敌；对弓娥与林智而言，他手中之剑便是一面盾牌；因他往往能将那一柄柄高举之斧锋刃上的劲力卸去，又能将敌人刺来之枪尖生生止于半空。

===Original===
Even so wisely fought the whole band of the Woodlanders and the Wolves, who got within smiting space of the foe; for they had no will to cast away their lives when assured victory was so nigh to them. Sooth to say, the handplay was not so hard to them as it had been betwixt the bent and the houses; for the Dusky Men were intent on dealing with the men of the kindreds from the southern road, who stood war-wearied before them; and they were hewing and casting at them, and baying and yelling like dogs; and though they turned about to meet the storm of the Woodlanders, yet their hearts failed them withal, and they strove to edge away from betwixt those two fearful scythes of war, fighting as men fleeing, not as men in onset. But still the Woodlanders and the Wolves came on, hewing and thrusting, smiting down the foemen in heaps, till the Dusky Throng grew thin, and the staves of the Dalesmen and their bright banners in the morning sun were clear to see, and at last their very faces, kindly and familiar, worn and strained with the stress of battle, or laughing wildly, or pale with the fury of the fight. Then rose up to the heavens the blended shout of the Woodlanders and the Dalesmen, and now there was nought of foemen betwixt them save the dead and the wounded.

===Chinese===
凡进入杀得到敌人之距的林中之民与狼族众人，人人皆这般沉稳应战；因既见胜券近在眼前、确凿可握，谁也不肯白白送了性命。实话实说，这场肉搏远不似山坡与屋宇之间那般吃力；盖因黝暗人一心要对付自南路而来的诸族人马——那些立于他们面前、久战疲惫的战士；他们正朝其乱砍乱掷，如群犬般狂吠嗥叫；虽则他们转身应付林中之民这阵风暴，心中却已先自气馁，只图从那两扇可畏的战争之镰之间脱身，其战法有如逃命之卒，而非冲锋之师。然而林中之民与狼族众人仍步步推进，砍的砍、刺的刺，将敌人一堆堆砍倒，直杀得黝暗人丛渐渐稀薄，谷民（the Dalesmen）的枪杆和他们在朝阳下鲜明的旗帜渐渐看得清了，末了连他们的面庞也看得清了——那些和蔼熟稔的面庞，因战事紧张而疲惫紧绷，或狂笑不止，或因厮杀之怒而苍白。于是林中之民与谷民汇成一片呐喊，直冲云霄，此刻两者之间再无一个活着的敌人，唯余死者和伤者。

===Original===
Then Face-of-god thrust his sword into its sheath all bloody as it was, and strode over the dead men to where Hall-ward stood under the banner of the Steer, and cast his arms about the old carle, and kissed him for joy of the victory. But Hall-ward thrust him aback and looked him in the face, and his cheeks were pale and his lips clenched, and his eyes haggard and staring, and he said in a harsh voice:

“O young man, she is dead! I saw her fall. The Bride is dead, and thou hast lost thy troth-plight maiden. O death, death to the Dusky Men!”

Then grew Face-of-god as pale as a linen sleeve, and all the newcomers groaned and cried out. But a bystander said: “Nay, nay, it is nought so bad as that; she is hurt, and sorely; but she liveth yet.”

===Chinese===
于是面神将那柄血迹未干的剑推回鞘中，大步踏过尸首，走到犍牛旗下厅卫（Hall-ward）所立之处，伸臂抱住这位老汉，为得胜之喜而吻他。厅卫却一把将他推开，直视他的脸——只见老汉双颊苍白、双唇紧咬，双目失神瞪视——以沙哑之声说道：

“小哥啊，她没了！我亲眼看着她倒下的。新娘没了，你那誓约相许的未婚之人没了。死啊，黝暗人统统去死罢！”

面神登时白得如一只麻布袖子，新来众人也都一片哀号惊呼。却有一个在旁之人说道：“不，不，没到那般地步；她受了伤，且伤得不轻；可她还活着。”

===Original===
Face-of-god heard him not. He forgot Dale-warden lying in his sheath, and he saw that the last speaker had a great wood-axe broad and heavy in his hand, so he cried: “Man, man, thine axe!” and snatched it from him, and turned about to the foe again, and thrust through the ranks, suffering none to stay him till all his friends were behind and all his foes before him. And as he burst forth from the ranks waving his axe aloft, bareheaded now, his yellow hair flying abroad, his mouth crying out, “Death, death, death to the Dusky Men!” fear of him smote their hearts, and they howled and fled before him as they might; for they said that the Dalesmen had prayed their Gods into the battle. But not so fast could they flee but he was presently amidst them, smiting down all about him, and they so terror-stricken that scarce might they raise a hand against him. All that blended host followed him mad with wrath and victory, and as they pressed on, they heard behind them the horns and war-cries of the Shepherds falling on from the east. Nought they heeded that now, but drave on a fearful storm of war, and terrible was the slaughter of the Felons.

===Chinese===
面神却没听见他这话。他全然忘了还卧在鞘中的谷卫（Dale-warden），只见方才说话之人手里有一柄又宽又重的伐木大斧，便叫道：“汉子，汉子，你的斧头！”一把夺了过来，复又转身朝向敌人，直透阵中，任谁也拦他不住，直至所有同伴都落到他身后、所有敌人都在他前头。当他挥斧高举、自阵中一跃而出之时——此刻已光着头，一头黄发四散飞扬，口中高呼“死罢，死罢，黝暗人统统去死罢！”——对他的恐惧直击敌心，他们嗥叫着，拼尽全力在他前头四散逃命；因他们都说，谷民已将他们的神祇祈入了战阵。然而他们逃得再快，也快不过他转眼杀入其中，前后左右一路砍倒，而敌人惊怖万分，几乎连一只手也举不起来还击。那一整支混成的大军随他而进，人人被愤怒与胜利激得如狂；他们向前压上之际，听见背后传来牧羊之民自东面杀到的号角与战吼。此刻他们全然顾不上这些了，只管推进一场可畏的战争风暴，恶徒们被屠戮之惨，直是骇人。

===Original===
It was but a few minutes ere they had driven them up against that great stack of faggots that had been dight for the burnt-offering of men, and many of the felons had mounted up on to it, and now in their anguish of fear were shooting arrows and casting spears on all about them, heeding little if they were friend or foe. Now were the men of the kindreds at point to climb this twiggen burg; but by this time the fury of Face-of-god had run clear, and he knew where he was and what he was doing; so he stayed his folk, and cried out to them: “Forbear, climb not! let the torch help the sword!” And therewith he looked about and saw the fire-pot which had been set down there for the kindling of the balefire, and the coals were yet red in it; so he snatched up a dry brand and lighted it thereat, and so did divers others, and they thrust them among the faggots, and the fire caught at once, and the tongues of flame began to leap from faggot to faggot till all was in a light low; for the wood had been laid for that very end, and smeared with grease and oil so that the burning to the god might be speedy.

But the fierceness of the kindreds heeded not the fire, nor overmuch the men who leapt down from the stack before it, but they left all behind them, faring straight toward the western outgate from the Marketstead; and Face-of-god still led them on; though by now he was wholly come to his right mind again, albeit the burden of sorrow yet lay heavy on his heart. He had broken his axe, and had once more drawn Dale-warden from his sheath, and many felt his point and edge.

===Chinese===
不过几分钟，他们便将敌人逼到那一大堆原为焚烧活人祭品而备的柴堆跟前，许多恶徒已爬上柴堆，此刻在恐惧的痛楚里向四面八方乱箭齐发、乱枪齐掷，全然不顾是友是敌。诸族之人正欲攀爬这座枝条垒成的山堡（twiggen burg）；然此时面神的怒火已烧得清明，他清楚自己在何处、所为何事；于是他制止部下，向他们高呼：“住手，莫爬！让火把来助剑一臂之力！”随即四下张望，看见那边放着一个原为点燃祭火而设的火盆，盆中炭火尚红；他便抓起一根干柴就其引燃，旁人也有几个照做，他们一同将火把捅入柴堆，火势立时蔓延，火舌自一捆柴跳到另一捆柴，直至整堆化作一片低伏的光焰；盖因这些木柴本就是为此而堆，又涂满油脂膏油，好叫献给神的火燃得迅捷。

然诸族的猛勇既不顾那火，也不甚理会那些趁火自柴堆跳下之人，他们把一切抛在身后，径直奔向集市坪的西出口；面神仍旧率众而进；虽则此刻他已完全恢复清明，只是悲哀的重担依旧沉沉压在心头。他那柄斧头已经折断，他便再度自鞘中拔出谷卫，许多人尝过它的锋尖与利刃。

===Original===
But now, as they chased, came a rush of men upon them again, as though a new onset were at hand. That saw Face-of-god and Hall-ward and War-well, and other wise leaders of men, and they bade their folk forbear the chase, and lock their ranks to meet the onfall of this new wave of foemen. And they did so, and stood fast as a wall; but lo! the onrush that drave up against them was but a fleeing shrieking throng, and no longer an array of warriors, for many had cast away their weapons, and were rushing they knew not whither; for they were being thrust on the bitter edges of Face-of-god’s companies by the terror of the fleers from the onset of the men of the Face, the Sickle, and the Vine, whom Hall-face and Stone-face were leading, along with Folk-might. Then once again the men of Face-of-god gave forth the whoop of victory, and pressed forward again, hewing their way through the throng of fleers, but turning not to chase to the right or the left; while at their backs came on the Shepherd-folk, who had swept down all that withstood them; for now indeed was the Marketstead getting thinner of living men.

So led the War-leader his ordered ranks, till at last over the tangled crowd of runaways he saw the banners of the Burg and the Face flashing against the sun, and heard the roar of the kindreds as they drave the chase towards them. Then he lifted up his sword, and stood still, and all the host behind him stayed and cast a huge shout up to the heavens, and there they abode the coming of the other Dalesmen.

===Chinese===
然而正追杀间，又有一阵人马朝他们涌来，仿佛新一轮攻势将到。面神、厅卫与战井（War-well）等诸位善知兵者都看见了，便命部下停止追击、结紧阵势，以迎这股新的敌潮。众人依令而行，立稳如墙；咦！那冲将上来的，却不过是一群尖声嘶叫的逃命之众，已不再是成阵的武士，许多人已丢了兵刃，正没头没脑地乱窜；因他们被面神一队人马的无情锋刃逼得走投无路——而那群逃人之奔逃，又是因为厅面与石面所领的面族、镰族、葡藤族之众的猛攻，民强亦在其中。于是面神的人马再一次发出得胜的狼嗥，又复向前推进，在逃命人丛中一路砍杀而进，却不向左右追击；而他们背后杀来的，是牧羊之民——他们已将一切阻挡之物一扫而空；盖因集市坪之中，此刻活着的敌人确实越来越稀了。

战首（the War-leader）便这般率着他那齐整的队伍而进，直至越过那一团乱麻似的逃命人丛，望见堡旗与面旗迎着日光熠熠生辉，又听见诸族追杀过来所发的呐喊如雷。于是他将剑高高举起，驻足而立，身后整支大军也随之止步，向苍天迸发出一片惊天动地的欢呼，便在那里等候另一路谷民的到来。

===Original===
But the War-leader sent a message to Hound-under-Greenbury, bidding him lead the Shepherds to the chase of the Dusky Men, who were now all fleeing toward the northern outgate of the Market. Howbeit he called to mind the throng he had seen on the northern road before they were come into the Marketstead, and deemed that way also death awaited the foemen, even if the men of the kindreds forbore them.

But presently the space betwixt the Woodlanders and the men of the Face was clear of all but the dead, so that friend saw the face of friend; and it could be seen that the warriors of the Face were ruddy and smiling for joy, because the battle had been easy to them, and but few of them had fallen; for the Dusky Men who had left the Marketstead to fall on them, had had room for fleeing behind them, and had speedily turned their backs before the spear-casting of the men of the Face and the onrush of the swordsmen.

There then stood these victorious men facing one another, and the banner-bearers on either side came through the throng, and brought the banners together between the two hosts; and the Wolf kissed the Face, and the Sickle and the Vine met the Steer and the Bridge and the Bull: but the Shepherds were yet chasing the fleers.

===Chinese===
然而战首遣人传令与绿堡之犬（Hound-under-Greenbury），命他率领牧羊之民去追杀黝暗人——此刻黝暗人已尽数朝集市的北出口逃去。不过他记起众人尚未杀入集市坪之前、他在北面那条路上所见的那一群人，心想必经此路也照样有死亡等着敌人，纵使诸族之人饶过他们。

然转眼之间，林中之民与面族之众之间的空地便空无一人——除了死者——友朋得以彼此相见；只见面族的武士们红光满面、含笑而喜，盖因这一仗对他们而言甚是轻易，阵亡者寥寥；因那些出集市坪来攻他们的黝暗人，身后本有退路可逃，在面族的掷矛与剑士的冲锋之前，早早便已转身败走了。

于是这些得胜之人相对而立，两边的掌旗手自人丛中走出，将旗帜聚于两军之间；狼旗吻过面旗，镰旗与葡藤旗与犍牛旗、桥旗、公牛旗相会：只是牧羊之民尚在追杀逃敌。

===Original===
There in the forefront stood Hall-face the tall, with the joy of battle in his eyes. And Stone-face, the wise carle in war, stood solemn and stark beside him; and there was the goodly body and the fair and kindly visage of the Alderman smiling on the faces of his friends. But as for Folk-might, his face was yet white and aweful with anger, and he looked restlessly up and down the front of the kindreds, though he spake no word.

Then Face-of-god could no longer forbear, but he thrust Dale-warden into his sheath, and ran forward and cast his arms about his father’s neck and kissed him; and the blood of himself and of the foemen was on him, for he had been hurt in divers places, but not sorely, because of the good hammer-work of the Alderman.

Then he kissed his brother and Stone-face, and he took Folk-might by the hand, and was on the point of speaking some word to him, when the ranks of the Face opened, and lo! the Sun-beam in her bright war-gear, and the sword girt to her side, and she unhurt and unsullied.

Then was it to him as when he met her first in Shadowy Vale, and he thought of little else than her; but she stepped lightly up to him, and unashamed before the whole host she kissed him on the mouth, and he cast his mailed arms about her, and joy made him forget many things and what was next to do, though even at that moment came afresh a great clamour of shrieks and cries from the northern outgate of the Marketstead: and the burning pile behind them cast a great wavering flame into the air, contending with the bright sun of that fair day, now come hard on noontide. But ere he drew away his face from the Sun-beam’s, came memory to him, and a sharp pang shot through his heart, as he heard Folk-might say: “Where then is the Shield-may of Burgstead? where is the Bride?”

===Chinese===
高大的厅面立于最前，眼中犹含战之欢欣。精通兵机的老汉石面，神色冷峻严正地立在他身旁；还有长老（the Alderman）那健全之躯、那和蔼慈祥的面庞，正向着众友朋微笑。至于民强，他的脸仍因愤怒而苍白可畏，在诸族阵前不安地上下张望，虽则一言不发。

面神再也按捺不住，将谷卫推回鞘中，奔上前去，伸臂抱住父亲的颈项吻他；他身上糊着自己与敌人的血，因他身上几处负伤，却都不重——这全赖长老那副好锤工打出的甲胄。

随后他又吻过兄弟与石面，又握住民强的手，正要和他说句什么——忽地面族的阵势一分，哎呀！日光披着她明亮的战甲，腰间佩着剑，安然无恙、纤尘不染。

此刻于他便如初见她在幽谷（Shadowy Vale）之时，心中除她之外再无别念；她却轻盈地走到他跟前，在整支大军之前毫无愧色地吻在他唇上，他伸出披甲的双臂将她抱住，狂喜之中许多事都忘了，连下一步当做什么也忘了——虽说就在这一刻，自集市坪北出口又传来一阵尖嘶惨呼的鼎沸喧声：身后那座熊熊燃烧的柴堆，向空中腾起一道摇曳的大火，与那美好一日里明亮的太阳争辉——此刻已近正午。然而他还没从日光脸上把脸移开，记忆便涌上心头，一阵剧痛直刺入心——因他听见民强说道：“堡镇（Burgstead）的盾娥（Shield-may）在哪里？新娘在哪里？”

===Original===
And Face-of-god said under his breath: “She is dead, she is dead!” And then he stared out straight before him and waited till someone else should say it aloud. But Bow-may stepped forward and said: “Chief of the Wolf, be of good cheer; our kinswoman is hurt, but not deadly.”

The Alderman’s face changed, and he said: “Hast thou seen her, Bow-may?”

“Nay,” she said. “How should I leave the battle? but others have told me who have seen her.”

Folk-might stared into the ranks of men before him, but said nothing. Said the Alderman: “Is she well tended?”

“Yea, surely,” said Bow-may, “since she is amongst friends, and there are no foemen behind us.”

Then came a voice from Folk-might which said: “Now were it best to send good men and deft in arms, and who know Silverdale, from house to house, to search for foemen who may be lurking there.”

===Chinese===
面神低声说道：“她没了，她没了！”随即他便直直瞪着前方，等旁人把它大声说出来。弓娥却上前一步道：“狼族之长，且放宽心；我们这位族姊受了伤，却不致命。”

长老面色一变，说道：“你可曾亲眼见过她，弓娥？”

“不曾，”她道，“我怎能离开战阵？是见过她的人告诉我的。”

民强直瞪着面前的人阵，却一言不发。长老又问：“可有人好好照料她？”

“正是，当然，”弓娥道，“因她如今在朋友中间，我们背后已无一个敌人。”

随后传来民强的声音，说道：“如今最好派些又善战又精通兵刃、又熟识银谷（Silverdale）的好手，挨家挨户去搜索可能潜伏其中的敌人。”

===Original===
The Alderman looked kindly and sadly on him and said:

“Kinsman Stone-face, and Hall-face my son, the brunt of the battle is now over, and I am but a simple man amongst you; therefore, if ye will give me leave, I will go see this poor kinswoman of ours, and comfort her.”

They bade him go: so he sheathed his sword, and went through the press with two men of the Steer toward the southern road; for the Bride had been brought into a house nigh the corner of the Marketplace.

===Chinese===
长老慈和而悲伤地望着他，说道：

“石面兄弟，还有我的儿子厅面，战事的重头如今已过，我在你们中间不过是个寻常之人；故而若蒙见允，我要去看看我们这位可怜的同族女子，宽慰宽慰她。”

他们让他去：于是他将剑推入鞘中，带着两名犍牛族的人穿过人群，朝南路而去；盖因新娘已被抬进集市拐角附近的一所房子里。

===Original===
But Face-of-god looked after his father as he went, and remembrance of past days came upon him, and such a storm of grief swept over him, as he thought of the Bride lying pale and bleeding and brought anigh to her death, that he put his hands to his face and wept as a child that will not be comforted; nor had he any shame of all those bystanders, who in sooth were men good and kindly, and had no shame of his grief or marvelled at it, for indeed their own hearts were sore for their lovely kinswoman, and many of them also wept with Face-of-god. But the Sun-beam stood by and looked on her betrothed, and she thought many things of the Bride, and was sorry, albeit no tears came into her eyes; then she looked askance at Folk-might and trembled; but he said coldly, and in a loud voice:

===Chinese===
面神却目送父亲远去，往昔的种种涌上心头，一阵悲苦的风暴将他卷没——一念及新娘苍白失血、命悬一线地躺在那里——他便双手掩面，哭得像一个任谁也宽慰不了的孩子；他对满旁观的众人并不觉得羞惭——那些人其实皆是善良和蔼之辈，对他的悲哭既不以为耻、也不以为异，因他们自己的心也同样为他们那位可爱的同族女子而痛，其中许多人和面神一同落泪。日光却立在一旁，看着她的未婚夫，心中为新娘转了许多念头，也很是难过，虽则并无眼泪上来；随即她斜睨了民强一眼，身子发抖；他却冷冷地、大声说道：

===Original===
“Needs must we search the houses for the lurking felons, or many a man will yet be murdered. Let Wood-wicked lead a band of men at once from house to house.”

Then said a man of the Wolf hight Hardgrip: “Wood-wicked was slain betwixt the bent and the houses.”

Said Folk-might: “Let it be Wood-wise then.”

But Bow-may said: “Wood-wise is even now hurt in the leg by a wounded felon, and may not go afoot.”

===Chinese===
“我们必须逐屋搜索那些潜伏的恶徒，否则还要有许多人遭毒手。让林恶（Wood-wicked）即刻带领一队人，挨家挨户搜过去。”

便有一个狼族的名叫硬握（Hardgrip）的汉子说道：“林恶已在山坡与屋宇之间阵亡了。”

民强道：“那就让林智去罢。”

弓娥却道：“林智此刻恰好被一个受伤的恶徒伤了腿，走不得路了。”

===Original===
Then said Folk-might: “Is Crow the Shaft-speeder anigh?”

“Yea, here am I,” quoth a tall man of fifty winters, coming from out the ranks where stood the Wolves.

Said Folk-might: “Kinsman Crow, do thou take two score and ten of doughty men who are not too hotheaded, and search every house about the Marketplace; but if ye come on any house that makes a stout defence, send ye word thereof to the Mote-house, where we will presently be, and we shall send you help. Slay every felon that ye fall in with; but if ye find in the houses any of the poor folk crouching and afraid, comfort their hearts all ye may, and tell them that now is life come to them.”

So Crow fell to getting his band together, and presently departed with them on his errand.

===Chinese===
民强便道：“飞矢克劳（Crow the Shaft-speeder）可在近旁？”

“在，我在这儿，”一个年约五十的高大汉子说道，自狼族众人所立的阵列中走出。

民强道：“克劳兄弟，你带五十个好汉——要那些不甚莽撞的——去搜遍集市周围的每一所房子；若遇上哪所房子据守得厉害，便差人去议事堂报信，我们即刻便在那里，会发兵来助你。你们撞见的恶徒，一律格杀；但若在屋中见有那些瑟缩惊恐的可怜百姓，当尽你们所能宽慰他们，告诉他们：如今得生了。”

于是克劳（Crow）着手收拢自己的人马，不多时便带他们去办事了。

## XLVIII Men Sing in the Mote-House / 四十八 人于议事堂中歌吟

===Original===
Then strode the Warriors of the Wolf over the bodies of the slain on to the dais of their own Hall; and Folk-might led the Sun-beam by the hand, and now was his sword in its sheath, and his face was grown calm, though it was stern and sad. But even as he trod the dais comes a slim swain of the Wolves twisting himself through the throng, and so maketh way to Folk-might, and saith to him:

"Chieftain, the Alderman of Burgdale sendeth me hither to say a word to thee; even this, which I am to tell to thee and the War-leader both: It is most true that our kinswoman the Bride will not die, but live. So help me, the Warrior and the Face! This is the word of the Alderman."

===Chinese===
于是狼族的武士们踏过阵亡者的尸身，大步走上自家厅堂的高台；民强牵着日光的手，此时他的剑已归鞘，面色也已平复，唯仍肃穆悲戚。然而他方踏上高台，便有一个狼族的瘦削少年侧身挤过人群，来到民强跟前，对他这样说道：

"首领，堡谷的长老遣我前来向你传一句话；就是这一句，我须向你与战帅二人一同禀明：我们的族人新娘必不致死，必将存活。愿武士与面神助我！这便是长老的话。"

===Original===
When Folk-might heard this, his face changed and he hung his head; and Face-of-god, who was standing close by, beheld him and deemed that tears were falling from his eyes on to the hall-floor. As for him, he grew exceeding glad, and he turned to the Sun-beam and met her eyes, and saw that she could scarce refrain her longing for him; and he was abashed for the sweetness of his love. But she drew close up to him, and spake to him softly and said:

"This is the day that maketh amends; and yet I long for another day. When I saw thee coming to me that first day in Shadowy Vale, I thought thee so goodly a warrior that my heart was in my mouth. But now how goodly thou art! For the battle is over, and we shall live."

"Yea," said Face-of-god, "and none shall begrudge us our love. Behold thy brother, the hard-heart, the warrior; he weepeth because he hath heard that the Bride shall live. Be sure then that she shall not gainsay him. O fair shall the world be tomorrow!"

But she said: "O Gold-mane, I have no words. Is there no minstrelsy amongst us?"

===Chinese===
民强闻言，面色一变，垂下头去；面神正立在近旁，看着他，只道是有泪自他眼中滴落到厅堂地上。至于面神，却欢喜非常，他转向日光，迎上她的目光，见她几乎按捺不住对他的渴慕；他为爱情之甘美所慑，竟有些忸怩。她却挨近他身，轻声对他说道：

"今日便是弥补之日；然而我还期盼着另一日。当初在幽谷，我第一次见你向我走来，便觉得你是那样一位英武的武士，我的心几乎要跳出喉咙。而如今你更显得何等英武！因为战事已了，我们必将活下去。"

"是啊，"面神说，"再无人会妒忌我们的爱情了。你看你的哥哥，那铁石心肠的武士；他之所以落泪，是因为听说新娘将要活下来。那么放心吧，她一定不会拒绝他。啊，明日的世界该多么美好！"

她却说："啊，金鬃，我已经说不出话来了。难道我们中间就没有一点弹唱之乐么？"

===Original===
Now by this time were many of the men of the Wolf and the Woodlanders gathered on the dais of the Hall; and the Dalesmen noting this, and wotting that these men were now in their own Mote-house, withdrew them as they might for the press toward the nether end thereof. That the Sun-beam noted, and that all those about her save the War-leader were of the kindreds of the Wolf and the Woodland, and, still speaking softly, she said to Face-of-god:

"Gold-mane, meseemeth I am now in my wrong place; for now the Wolf raiseth up his head, but I am departing from him. Surely I should now be standing amongst my people of the Face, whereto I am going ere long."

He said: "Beloved, I am now become thy kindred and thine home, and it is meet for thee to stand beside me."

She cast her eyes adown and answered not; and she fell a-pondering of how sorely she had desired that fair dale, and now she would leave it, and be content and more than content.

===Chinese===
此时狼族与林中之民已有许多聚到厅堂的高台之上；谷民见此，又知这些人如今是在自家议事堂中，便尽力穿过拥挤的人群，向厅之下端退去。日光注意到这一点，也注意到身边除了战帅之外，都是狼族与林中氏族之人，便仍轻声对面神说道：

"金鬃，我如今似乎站错了位置；因为此刻狼族正抬起头来，而我却要离开他了。我理应站在我的面神一族的人中间，反正我不久便要归到他们那里去了。"

他说："心爱的，我如今便是你的亲族、你的家了，你理应站在我的身边。"

她垂下目光，不作回答；心中却暗自思量：自己曾怎样苦苦渴慕那片丰美山谷，而如今竟要离它而去，却心甘情愿，且不止于心甘情愿。

===Original===
But now the kindreds had sundered, they upon the dais ranked themselves together there in the House which their fathers had builded; and when they saw themselves so meetly ordered, their hearts being full with the sweetness of hope accomplished and the joy of deliverance from death, song arose amongst them, and they fell to singing together; and this is somewhat of their singing:

===Chinese===
此时诸氏族既已分开，高台之上的人便在那座他们父辈所建的厅堂中，井然整列；他们见自己排列得如此得体，心中满溢着希望成真之甘甜与死里逃生之欢欣，歌声便自他们中间升起，便齐声唱了起来；其所唱略云：

===Original===
> Now raise we the lay
Of the long-coming day!
Bright, white was the sun
When we saw it begun:
O'er its noon now we live;
It hath ceased not to give;
It shall give, and give more
From the wealth of its store.
O fair was the yesterday! Kindly and good
Was the wasteland our guester, and kind was the wood;
Though below us for reaping lay under our hand
The harvest of weeping, the grief of the land;
Dumb cowered the sorrow, nought daring to cry
On the help of tomorrow, the deed drawing nigh.

> All increase throve
In the Dale of our love;
There the ox and the steed
Fed down the mead;
The grapes hung high
'Twixt earth and sky,
And the apples fell
Round the orchard well.
Yet drear was the land there, and all was for nought;
None put forth a hand there for what the year wrought,
And raised it o'erflowing with gifts of the earth.
For man's grief was growing beside of the mirth
Of the springs and the summers that wasted their wealth;
And the birds, the newcomers, made merry by stealth.

> Yet here of old
Abode the bold;
Nor had they wailed
Though the wheat had failed,
And the vine no more
Gave forth her store.
Yea, they found the waste good
For the fearless of mood.
Then to these, that were dwelling aloof from the Dale,
Fared the wild-wind a-telling the worst of the tale;
As men bathed in the morning they saw in the pool
The image of scorning, the throne of the fool.
The picture was gleaming in helm and in sword,
And shone forth its seeming from cups of the board.

> Forth then they came
With the battle-flame;
From the Wood and the Waste
And the Dale did they haste:
They saw the storm rise,
And with untroubled eyes
The war-storm they met;
And the rain ruddy-wet.
O'er the Dale then was litten the Candle of Day,
Night-sorrow was smitten, and gloom fled away.
How the grief-shackles sunder! How many to morn
Shall awaken and wonder how gladness was born!
O wont unto sorrow, how sweet unto you
Shall be pondering tomorrow what deed is to do!

> Fell many a man
'Neath the edges wan,
In the heat of the play
That fashioned the day.
Praise all ye then
The death of men,
And the gift of the aid
Of the unafraid!
O strong are the living men mighty to save,
And good is their giving, and gifts that we have!
But the dead, they that gave us once, never again;
Long and long shall they save us sore trouble and pain.
O Banner above us, O God of the strong,
Love them as ye love us that bore down our wrong!

===Chinese===
> 且扬此歌，
颂那久待之日的来到！
初见其始，朝阳明皎：
吾辈今已行过其中天；
其赐未尝稍减；
它必将再赐，且赐之愈多，
源源乎出于其丰藏。
啊，昨日何其美好！荒原待我以客礼，
慈善而温厚，林木亦怀善意；
纵使我等足下、垂手可刈者，
乃泣涕之庄稼、此土之哀愁；
悲苦默然蜷伏，不敢出声呼求，
唯望明日之援，唯候事机之将至。

> 万物繁滋，
皆在我等所爱之谷；
牛与骏马，
饱食于草甸；
葡萄高悬，
介于天地之间，
苹果纷纷坠落，
绕那园中之井。
然其地仍萧索，一切皆属徒然；
无人伸手，收取岁之所成，
举其满溢大地之赐者。
盖因人之哀愁，
旁生于春夏之欢悦——
那春夏徒耗其丰饶；
而新来之飞鸟，暗自作乐。

> 然古昔之时，
勇者曾居于此；
纵麦稼无收，
彼等亦不悲啼，
葡萄藤亦不再
输其珍藏。
诚哉，于无畏之心，
荒原亦是佳地。
于是野风传至彼等——远居谷外之人，
尽述其事之最恶；
如人晨起沐浴，见于池水之中，
乃嘲弄之影、愚者之座。
其像闪耀于兜鍪与长剑，
其形自席间之杯盏中映出。

> 于是彼等奋然而出，
怀战斗之烈焰；
自林莽、自荒原、
自谷中，皆疾趋而至：
彼等见风暴涌起，
遂以不惊之目，
迎那战之风暴；
迎那血赤之雨。
于是白日之烛照临此谷，
夜之哀愁被击碎，阴霾尽散。
悲苦之枷如何断裂！多少人明朝
将醒而惊异：欢乐如何降生！
啊，素习于悲苦之人，明日之事，
于你将何其甘美——思量当行何举！

> 许多人仆倒，
于苍白刃下，
在那锻造此日的
鏖战炽热之中。
尔等皆当颂赞
人之就死，
并那无惧之人
所赐之援！
啊，生者强健，力能救人，
其赐善哉，其所予我等之礼善哉！
然死者——曾赐我等之人，再不能复赐；
唯久久久久，将为我等免去深重之苦痛。
啊，飘扬我等上方之旆，啊，强者之神，
愿你爱他们，正如爱我们——我们曾推翻冤仇！

===Original===
