So they sang in the Hall; and there was many a man wept, as the song ended, for those that should never see the good days of the Dale, and all the joy that was to be; and men swore, by all that they loved, that they would never forget those that had fallen in the Winning of Silverdale; and that when each year the Cups of Memory went round, they should be no mere names to them, but the very men whom they had known and loved.

===Chinese===
他们便在厅堂中如此歌吟；一曲既终，许多人落下泪来——为了那些再不能见到堡谷好时光、再不能见到一切将临之乐的人；众人凭着所爱之一切起誓，绝不忘却那些在夺取银谷之战中阵亡的人；并誓道：日后每年忆念之杯轮流传饮之时，他们于众人绝非徒具其名，而是众人曾相识、曾相爱的血肉之躯。

## XV Murder Amongst the Folk of the Woodlanders / 十五 林中汉子族中的凶杀

===Original===
So wore away midwinter tidingless. Stone-face spake no more to Face-of-god about the wood and its wights, when he saw that the young man had come back hale and merry, seemed not to crave overmuch to go back thither. As for the Bride, she was sad, and more than misdoubted all; but dauntless as she was in matters that try men’s hardihood, she yet lacked heart to ask of Face-of-god what had befallen him since the autumn-tide, or where he was with her. So she put a force upon herself not to look sad or craving when she was in his company, as full oft she was; for he rather sought her than shunned her. For when he saw her thus, he deemed things were changing with her as they had changed with him, and he bethought him of what he had spoken to Bow-may, and deemed that even so he might speak with the Bride when the time came, and that she would not be grieved beyond measure, and all would be well.

===Chinese===
仲冬便这般风平浪静地过去了。石面见那年轻人回来时安然无恙、神采欢愉，似乎并不十分渴求再赴林中，便不再与面神提起那树林及其中的精怪。至于新娘，她满心忧伤，疑虑重重远逾寻常；然她虽于试炼男儿胆气之事上无畏无惧，到底还是缺少勇气去问面神：自秋时以来他究竟遭遇了什么，他与她之间又到了何等地步。于是她强自克制，每当与他相处——而这样的场合原是极多的——不让自己面露悲戚或渴盼之色；因为他反倒更愿亲近她，而非躲避她。盖因他见她这般，便以为她心中之事亦如他自己一般正在起变化，于是想起曾对弓娥所说之话，暗忖待时机来临，亦可照样向新娘明言，而她必不至伤痛太过，一切终将无恙。

===Original===
Now came on the thaw, and the snow went, and the grass grew all up and down the Dale, and all waters were big. And about this time arose rumours of strange men in the wood, uncouth, vile, and murderous, and many of the feebler sort were made timorous thereby.

But a little before March was born came new tidings from the Woodlanders; to wit: There came on a time to the house of a woodland carle, a worthy goodman well renowned of all, two wayfarers in the first watch of the night; and these men said that they were wending down to the Plain from a faraway dale, Rosedale to wit, which all men had heard of, and that they had strayed from the way and were exceeding weary, and they craved a meal’s meat and lodging for the night.

This the goodman might nowise gainsay, and he saw no harm in it, wherefore he bade them abide and be merry.

===Chinese===
及至春来冰消雪化，积雪褪尽，谷中上下青草遍生，百川皆涨。约莫此时，林中来了陌生人的传言四起，说是有粗野、凶恶、嗜杀之徒出没，许多胆弱之人因此惶惶不安。

然三月将临之际，林中汉子处又传来新的消息：话说某日初夜时分，有两个行路人来到一位林中汉子家中——此汉乃是一位众人皆知、德高望重的好主人——二人自称从远方一处名叫玫瑰谷（Rosedale）的山谷——此谷人人皆知——下来往平原去，因迷了路、疲乏已极，故求一顿饭食、一夜宿处。

好主人自然不好回绝，亦不见有何不妥，于是留他们住下，殷勤相待。

===Original===
These men, said they who told the tidings, were outlanders, and no man had seen any like them before: they were armed, and bore short bows made of horn, and round targets, and coats-of-fence done over with horn scales; they had crooked swords girt to their sides, and axes of steel forged all in one piece, right good weapons. They were clad in scarlet and had much silver on their raiment and about their weapons, and great rings of the same on their arms; and all this silver seemed brand-new.

Now the Woodland Carle gave them of such things as he had, and was kind and blithe to them: there were in his house besides himself five men of his sons and kindred, and his wife and three daughters and two other maids. So they feasted after the Woodlanders’ fashion, and went to bed a little before midnight. Two hours after, the carle awoke and heard a little stir, and he looked and saw the guests on their feet amidst the hall clad in all their war-gear; and they had betwixt them his two youngest daughters, maids of fifteen and twelve winters, and had bound their hands and done clouts over their mouths, so that they might not cry out; and they were just at point to carry them off. Thereat the goodman, naked as he was, caught up his sword and made at these murder-carles, and or ever they were ware of him he had hewn down one and turned to face the other, who smote at him with his steel axe and gave him a great wound on the shoulder, and therewithal fled out at the open door and forth into the wood.

===Chinese===
据报消息之人言道，这两人乃是外乡人，从未有人见过这等模样：他们带着兵器，佩角制短弓、圆盾，身覆角鳞编缀之甲衣；腰间系着弯刀，还有一体锻成之钢斧，皆是上好利器。他们身着大红衣裳，衣上、兵器之上缀银甚多，臂上更套着粗大的银环；而这些银饰看来皆是崭新锃亮。

那林中汉子将自己所有之物尽数款待他们，态度亲切欢愉：他家中除自己外，尚有五个儿子及族中男子、妻子、三个女儿，另有两个使女。于是众人依林中之俗设宴畅饮，将近半夜时便就寝了。过了两个时辰，汉子醒来，听得些许动静，定睛一看，只见那两位客人已披挂齐全、立于厅堂之中；他们二人各挟着他两个最小的女儿——一个十五岁、一个十二岁——已将她们双手反绑、口中塞了布团，使之不能呼救；正要携之遁走。好主人见状，顾不得赤身裸体，抄起佩剑便向这两个杀人恶徒扑去，趁他们尚未察觉，已劈倒一个，转身来迎另一个；那人挥起钢斧向他砍来，在他肩头重重劈了一记，随即夺门而出，窜入林中。

===Original===
The Woodlander made no stay to raise the cry (there was no need, for the hall was astir now from end to end, and men getting to their weapons), but ran out after the felon even as he was; and, in spite of his grievous hurt, overran him no long way from the house before he had gotten into the thicket. But the man was nimble and strong, and the goodman unsteady from his wound, and by then the others of the household came up with the hue and cry he had gotten two more sore wounds and was just making an end of throttling the felon with his bare hands. So he fell into their arms fainting from weakness, and for all they could do he died in two hours’ time from that axe-wound in his shoulder, and another on the side of his head, and a knife-thrust in his side; and he was a man of sixty winters.

But the stranger he had slain outright; and the one whom he had smitten in the hall died before the dawn, thrusting all help aside, and making no sound of speech.

===Chinese===
那林中汉子顾不得呼喊示警（也无需呼喊，因整座大厅此刻已从头到尾骚动起来，众人纷纷抄起兵器），便这般赤身追了出去；虽伤势沉重，仍在那恶徒尚未钻入密林之前不远追上了他。然那人身手矫健、力气甚大，而好主人因伤脚步不稳，待到家中众人闻声呼喝赶来时，他身上又添了两处重伤，正赤手空拳将那恶徒扼至将死。于是他力竭晕厥，倒在众人臂中；众人竭力施救，到底无济于事——两个时辰后他便断了气：肩头那一斧、头侧那一击、胁下那一刀，终送了性命；他已是花甲之年的人了。

至于他赤手扼毙的那名陌生人，早已气绝；而他在厅中劈倒的另一个，则在天亮前也死了——推拒一切救护，不发一言。

===Original===
When these tidings came to Burgstead they seemed great to men, and to Gold-mane more than all. So he and many others took their weapons and fared up to Wildlake’s Way, and so came to the Woodland Carles. But the Woodlanders had borne out the carcasses of those felons and laid them on the green before Wood-grey’s door (for that was the name of the dead goodman), and they were saying that they would not bury such accursed folk, but would bear them a little way so that they should not be vexed with the stink of them, and cast them into the thicket for the wolf and the wildcat and the stoat to deal with; and they should lie there, weapons and silver and all; and they deemed it base to strip such wretches, for who would wear their raiment or bear their weapons after them.

===Chinese===
此消息传至堡镇，众人皆以为大事，金鬃尤甚。于是他与许多人一同带上兵器，取道野湖径而上，来到林中汉子之中。林中之民已将那两个恶徒的尸首抬出，陈于林灰（Wood-grey）——这便是那位死去的男主人之名——门前草地上，并说他们不愿埋葬这种可诅咒之人，只想抬到稍远之处、免得受尸臭之扰，然后丢进密林之中，任狼、野猫、白鼬去处置；尸首连同兵器银饰一并扔在那里；他们以为剥此等恶人之物是卑劣行径，因为谁会去穿他们的衣裳、用他们的兵器呢。

===Original===
There was a great ring of folk round about them when they of Burgstead drew near, and they shouted for joy to see their neighbours, and made way before them. Then the Dalesmen cursed these murderers who had slain so good a man, and they all praised his manliness, whereas he ran out into the night naked and wounded after his foe, and had fallen like his folk of old time.

It was a bright spring afternoon in that clearing of the Wood, and they looked at the two dead men closely; and Gold-mane, who had been somewhat silent and moody till then, became merry and wordy; for he beheld the men and saw that they were utterly strange to him: they were short of stature, crooked-legged, long-armed, very strong for their size: with small blue eyes, snubbed-nosed, wide-mouthed, thin-lipped, very swarthy of skin, exceeding foul of favour. He and all others wondered who they were, and whence they came, for never had they seen their like; and the Woodlanders, who often guested outlanders strayed from the way of divers kindreds and nations, said also that none such had they ever seen. But Stone-face, who stood by Gold-mane, shook his head and quoth he:

“The Wildwood holdeth many marvels, and these be of them: the spawn of evil wights quickeneth therein, and at other whiles it melteth away again like the snow; so may it be with these carcasses.”

And some of the older folk of the Woodlanders who stood by hearkened what he said, and deemed his words wise, for they remembered their ancient lore and many a tale of old time.

===Chinese===
堡镇之人走近时，只见围着一大圈人；众人看见邻人到来，齐声欢呼，为他们让出路来。谷民痛骂这些杀人恶贼——竟害死如此好人；人人称赞那条汉子的壮勇——赤身负伤、连夜追出门外追杀仇敌，正如他先祖当年一般壮烈捐躯。

其时林中空地之上正是一个明媚的春日下午，众人细看那两具尸首；金鬃此前一直沉默寡言、面色郁郁，此时却谈笑风生起来；因为他细看那两人，见其面目全然陌生：身量矮短、罗圈腿、长臂，体型虽小气力却大；蓝眼细小、塌鼻梁、阔口薄唇、肤色黝黑，容貌丑陋至极。他与众人皆纳罕此二人究竟何人、来自何处，因从未见过这等模样的人；林中之民常接待各部各族迷路的外乡人，也说从未见过此等人。但站在金鬃身旁的石面摇头道：

“野林（the Wildwood）之中藏有许多怪事，这便是其中之一：邪恶精怪之种在其中孕育滋生，有时又如雪一般消融殆尽；这两具尸首，恐怕也是如此。”

旁立的几位年长的林中之民闻言，皆觉此言有理——因他们记得古老传说与诸多旧日故事。

===Original===
Thereafter they of Burgstead went into Wood-grey’s hall, or as many of them as might, for it was but a poor place and not right great. There they saw the goodman laid on the dais in all his war-gear, under the last tie-beam of his hall, whereon was carved amidst much goodly work of knots and flowers and twining stems the image of the Wolf of the Waste, his jaws open and gaping: the wife and daughters of the goodman and other women of the folk stood about the bier singing some old song in a low voice, and some sobbing therewithal, for the man was much beloved: and much people of the Woodlanders was in the hall, and it was somewhat dusk within.

So the Burgstead men greeted that folk kindly and humbly, and again they fell to praising the dead man, saying how his deed should long be remembered in the Dale and wide about; and they called him a fearless man and of great worth. And the women hearkened, and ceased their crooning and their sobbing, and stood up proudly and raised their heads with gleaming eyes; and as the words of the Burgstead men ended, they lifted up their voices and sang loudly and clearly, standing together in a row, ten of them, on the dais of that poor hall, facing the gable and the wolf-adorned tie-beam, heeding nought as they sang what was about or behind them.

And this is some of what they sang:

===Chinese===
随后堡镇之人走入林灰的厅堂——或者说是尽可能进去的人，因那屋子简陋、并不甚大。只见好主人全身甲胄停于台上，正在厅堂最后一根脊梁之下；梁上于花结、繁花、缠枝诸般精美雕饰之中，刻着一尊荒原之狼的像，狼口大张、獠牙毕露：好主人之妻女及族中其他妇人环绕灵床，低声唱着某首古老歌谣，其间有人呜咽啜泣——因这汉子深得众人爱戴；厅堂之中林中之民甚多，室内颇为昏暗。

堡镇之人谦和地向他们致以慰问，又再称赞那死者，说他的壮举必将在谷中及远近长久传颂；称他无畏之人、大义之士。妇人们闻言，停下低吟与啜泣，骄傲地站起身来、昂首抬眸、双目灼灼；待堡镇之人话音落下，十人一排立于那简陋厅堂的台上，面朝山墙与那饰狼之脊梁，齐声高歌、嘹亮清澈，全然不顾身前身后有何物事。

她们所唱的，有如下这些：

===Original===
> Why sit ye bare in the spinning-room?
 

 Why weave ye naked at the loom?
> Bare and white as the moon we be,
 

 That the Earth and the drifting night may see.
> Now what is the worst of all your work?
 

 What curse amidst the web shall lurk?
> The worst of the work our hands shall win
 

 Is wrack and ruin round the kin.
> Shall the woollen yarn and the flaxen thread
 

 Be gear for living men or dead?
> The woollen yarn and the flaxen thread
 

 Shall flare ’twixt living men and dead.
> O what is the ending of your day?
 

 When shall ye rise and wend away?
> Our day shall end tomorrow morn,
 

 When we hear the voice of the battle-horn.
> Where first shall eyes of men behold
 

 This weaving of the moonlight cold?
> There where the alien host abides
 

 The gathering on the Mountainsides.
> How long aloft shall the fair web fly
 

 When the bows are bent and the spears draw nigh?
> From eve to morn and morn till eve
 

 Aloft shall fly the work we weave.
> What then is this, the web ye win?
 

 What wood-beast waxeth stark therein?
> We weave the Wolf and the gift of war
 

 From the men that were to the men that are.

===Chinese===
> 尔等为何赤身坐于纺室之中？
 

 尔等为何裸体立于织机之前？
> 我等赤裸皓白如月，
 

 好教大地与漂泊之夜共见。
> 尔等手中所织，最恶为何？
 

 织物之中，有何诅咒潜伏？
> 我等双手所获最恶之果，
 

 乃是环绕亲族之毁亡倾覆。
> 羊毛之线与亚麻之缕，
 

 是活人之物，抑或死人之物？
> 羊毛之线与亚麻之缕，
 

 当于活人与死人之间烈烈而燃。
> 尔等之日将以何终？
 

 何时起身、何时远行？
> 我等之日终于明日清晨，
 

 当闻战角之声。
> 世人之目将先于何处
 

 瞥见此冰冷月光之织物？
> 在异族大军驻留之处，
 

 在群山之侧集结之处。
> 当弓已挽、矛已近，
 

 美丽之织将飘于空中几许？
> 自夕至朝、自朝至夕，
 

 我等所织之物当长飘高空。
> 如此尔等所织者为何物？
 

 何等林兽于中现出狰狞？
> 我等所织乃狼、乃战争之馈，
 

 自往昔之人至今日之人。

===Original===
So sang they: and much were all men moved at their singing, and there was none but called to mind the old days of the Fathers, and the years when their banner went wide in the world.

But the Woodlanders feasted them of Burgstead what they might, and then went the Dalesmen back to their houses; but on the morrow’s morrow they fared thither again, and Wood-grey was laid in mound amidst a great assemblage of the Folk.

Many men said that there was no doubt that those two felons were of the company of those who had ransacked the steads of Penny-thumb and Harts-bane; and so at first deemed Bristler the son of Brightling: but after a while, when he had had time to think of it, he changed his mind; for he said that such men as these would have slain first and ransacked afterwards: and some who loved neither Penny-thumb nor Harts-bane said that they would not have been at the pains to choose for ransacking the two worst men about the Dale, whose loss was no loss to any but themselves.

As for Gold-mane he knew not what to think, except that his friends of the Mountain had had nought to do with it.

So wore the days awhile.

===Chinese===
她们如此唱着：众人闻歌无不激荡，人人忆起先祖之旧日、旌旗远扬于天下的那些岁月。

林中之民竭尽所有款待堡镇之人，随后谷民各自归家；然后日他们又再前来，林灰便在族人云集之中入土安葬。

许多人说，那两个恶徒毫无疑问便是洗劫铜拇指（Penny-thumb）与鹿祸（Harts-bane）宅院的那伙人；布赖特林（Brightling）之子布里斯勒（Bristler）起初也是这般想：然过了一阵，待他细想之后，却改了主意；他说此等人若要动手，必先杀人、后行劫掠：还有些人，既不爱铜拇指、也不爱鹿祸，便说道，那伙人何苦偏偏挑中谷中两个最不堪的人来打劫——此二人之死，于旁人而言并无损失，唯其自家方觉损失罢了。

至于金鬃，他不知该作何想，只知他山中那些朋友与此事无干。

日子便这般过了一阵。

## X New Tidings in the Dale / 十 谷中新消息

===Original===
It was three days thereafter that Gold-mane, leading an ass, went along the highway to fetch home certain fleeces which were needed for the house from a stead a little west of Wildlake; but he had gone scant half a mile ere he fell in with a throng of folk going to Burgstead. They were of the Shepherds; they had weapons with them, and some were clad in coats of fence. They went along making a great noise, for they were all talking each to each at the same time, and seemed very hot and eager about some matter. When they saw Gold-mane anigh, they stopped, and the throng opened as if to let him into their midmost; so he mingled with them, and they stood in a ring about him and an old man more ill-favoured than it was the wont of the Dalesmen to be.

For he was long, stooping, gaunt and spindle-shanked, his hands big and crippled with gout: his cheeks were red after an old man’s fashion, covered with a crimson network like a pippin; his lips thin and not well hiding his few teeth; his nose long like a snipe’s neb. In short, a shame and a laughingstock to the Folk, and a man whom the kindreds had in small esteem, and that for good reasons.

===Chinese===
此后第三日，金鬃（Gold-mane）牵着一头驴，沿着大路去野湖溪（Wildlake）以西不远的一处农舍取些家中需用的羊毛；然而走出尚不足半里，便撞见一伙人正往堡镇（Burgstead）去。那伙人正是牧羊之民（the Shepherds）；他们带着兵器，其中有几个还穿着护身的甲衣。他们一路上大声喧哗，盖因人人都在同时与旁人说话，似乎正因为某事激愤难平、急不可耐。他们看见金鬃走近，便停了下来，人群自行分开，仿佛要请他到最中间去；于是他混入他们之间，他们将他围成一圈，圈中除他之外，还有一位老者，其貌之陋，远过于谷民（the Dalesmen）惯常所见。

盖此人身量瘦长、佝偻、干瘪，两腿细如纺锤，一双大手又为痛风所扭曲残废：双颊照老人之例泛红，上布殷红血丝，恰如一只斑纹苹果；嘴唇薄削，遮不住口中寥寥几颗牙；鼻子长得像鹬鸟的喙。简而言之，此人是全族之耻、众人的笑柄，各氏族都瞧他不起——而且瞧他不起，也是有道理的。

===Original===
Face-of-god knew him at once for a notable close-fist and starve-all fool of the Shepherds; and his name was now become Penny-thumb the Lean, whatever it might once have been.

So Face-of-god greeted all men, and they him again; and he said: “What aileth you, neighbours? Your weapons, are bare, but I see not that they be bloody. What is it, goodman Penny-thumb?”

Penny-thumb did but groan for all answer; but a stout carle who stood by with a broad grin on his face answered and said:

“Face-of-god, evil tidings be abroad; the strong-thieves of the wood are astir; and some deem that the wood-wights be helping them.”

“Yea, and what is the deed they have done?” said Gold-mane.

Said the carle: “Thou knowest Penny-thumb’s abode?”

“Yea surely,” said Face-of-god; “fair are the water-meadows about it; great gain of cheese can be gotten thence.”

“Hast thou been within the house?” said the carle.

“Nay,” said Gold-mane.

===Chinese===
面神（Face-of-god）一见便认得：此人乃是牧羊之民中出了名的吝啬鬼、叫所有人都跟着挨饿的抠门汉；其名如今已被人唤作瘦子拇指钱（Penny-thumb the Lean），至于原本叫什么，已无人知晓。

于是面神与众人互道寒暄，开口说道：「诸位邻人，这是怎么了？你们的兵器虽都出了鞘，我却看不出上面染有血迹。究竟出了何事，当家人拇指钱？」

拇指钱只长叹一声，权作回答；旁边一位宽脸堆笑的壮健汉子却代他答道：

「面神，外面正传着恶讯；林中的悍贼又出来活动了；甚至有人以为那些林精（wood-wights）也在帮他们的忙。」

「是么，他们干了什么事？」金鬃道。

那汉子道：「你可知拇指钱的住处？」

「自然知道，」面神道，「那屋子四周的水草甸子甚是丰美；那里头能得不少好奶酪。」

「你可进过那屋子里头？」那汉子道。

「未曾，」金鬃道。

===Original===
Then spake Penny-thumb: “Within is scant gear: we gather for others to scatter; we make meat for others’ mouths.”

The carle laughed: “Sooth is that,” said he, “that there is little gear therein now; for the strong-thieves have voided both hall and bower and byre.”

“And when was that?” said Face-of-god.

“The night before last night,” said the carle, “the door was smitten on, and when none answered it was broken down.”

“Yea,” quoth Penny-thumb, “a host entered, and they in arms.”

“No host was within,” said the carle, “nought but Penny-thumb and his sister and his sister’s son, and three carles that work for him; and one of them, Rusty to wit, was the worst man of the hill-country. These then the host whereof the goodman telleth bound, but without doing them any scathe; and they ransacked the house, and took away much gear; yet left some.”

“Thou liest,” said Penny-thumb; “they took little and left none.”

Thereat all men laughed, for this seemed to them good game, and another man said: “Well, neighbour Penny-thumb, if it was so little, thou hast done unneighbourly in giving us such a heap of trouble about it.”

===Chinese===
这时拇指钱开口道：「屋里本就没多少家当：我们替别人攒，任别人散；我们做肉，入的是别人的口。」

那汉子大笑：「这话倒是不假，」他道，「如今屋里确实没多少家当了；因为那帮悍贼已把厅堂、闺阁、牛棚扫得一干二净。」

「那是何时的事？」面神道。

「前夜，」那汉子道，「有人敲门，无人应答，门便被砸开了。」

「是啊，」拇指钱道，「进来的是一支人马，人人持械。」

「屋里可没什么人马，」那汉子道，「只有拇指钱、他妹妹、他妹妹的儿子，还有三个给他做工的汉子；其中一个——锈子（Rusty），是山地一带最坏的恶棍。这位当家人所说的人马，便把这些人一一捆了，却没伤他们一根毫毛；他们把屋子搜刮一遍，掠走了不少家当；不过也留下了一些。」

「你胡说，」拇指钱道，「他们拿走的少，留下的更是一件也没有。」

众人闻言皆笑，觉得这话颇有乐子；另有一人接道：「好吧，邻人拇指钱，既然只是这么点东西，你却因此给我们添出这一大堆麻烦来，未免太不够邻里情分了。」

===Original===
And they laughed again, but the first carle said: “True it is, goodman, that thou wert exceeding eager to raise the hue and cry after that little when we happed upon thee and thy housemates bound in your chairs yesterday morning. Well, Alderman’s son, short is the tale to tell: we could not fail to follow the gear, and the slot led us into the wood, and ill is the going there for us shepherds, who are used to the bare downs, save Rusty, who was a good woodsman and lifted the slot for us; so he outwent us all, and ran out of sight of us, so presently we came upon him dead-slain, with the manslayer’s spear in his breast. What then could we do but turn back again, for now was the wood blind now Rusty was dead, and we knew not whither to follow the fray; and the man himself was but little loss: so back we turned, and told goodman Penny-thumb of all this, for we had left him alone in his hall lamenting his gear; so we bided today’s morn, and have come out now, with our neighbour and the spear, and the dead corpse of Rusty. Stand aside, neighbours, and let the Alderman’s son see it.”

They did so, and there was the corpse of a thin-faced tall wiry man, somewhat foxy of aspect, lying on a hand-bier covered with black cloth.

“Yea, Face-of-god,” said the carle, “he is not good to see now he is dead, yet alive was he worser: but, look you, though the man was no good man, yet was he of our people, and the feud is with us; so we would see the Alderman, and do him to wit of the tidings, that he may call the neighbours together to seek a blood-wite for Rusty and atonement for the ransacking. Or what sayest thou?”

===Chinese===
众人又大笑；那第一个汉子却接着道：「当家人，这话倒是真的，昨日清早我们撞见你和你的同屋之人被绑在椅子上，那时你可是急得直跳脚、非要大呼捉贼不可。唉，长老之子，长话短说：我们不能不追那些被掠的家当，踪迹一路引我们进了林子，那里头对我们这些惯于光秃丘陵的牧羊人来说，举步维艰；唯独锈子是个好林客，由他替我们寻踪认路；于是他一马当先超出我们众人，跑出了我们的视线；不多时我们便撞见他已一命呜呼，胸口插着杀人者的矛。事已至此，我们还能怎样，只得掉头回去——锈子一死，林子对我们便成了瞎眼一般，我们不知该循哪条路去追那帮人；况且那家伙本身也死不足惜：于是我们掉头而回，将这一切告知当家人拇指钱，因为我们先前将他一个人留在他那厅堂里哀号他的家当；我们挨到今日清晨，方才一同出来，带着这位邻人，带着那杆矛，还有锈子的尸首。邻人们，让一让，让长老之子瞧一瞧。」

众人依言让开，便见一具瘦面高个子、筋骨如铁的男尸，形容带几分狐色，躺在一副覆着黑布的手抬尸架上。

「是啊，面神，」那汉子道，「他死了这副模样固然不好看，活着的时候还更难看；可是你瞧，这人虽不是什么好人，到底是我们的人，这桩仇得由我们来报；所以我们想见一见长老（the Alderman），把这消息报与他知晓，好让他召集邻里，为锈子讨一笔血金（blood-wite），并为那场洗劫索个赔偿。你以为如何？」

===Original===
“Have ye the spear that ye found in Rusty?” quoth Gold-mane.

“Yea verily,” said the carle. “Hither with it, neighbours; give it to the Alderman’s son.”

So the spear came into his hand, and he looked at it and said:

“This is no spear of the smiths’ work of the Dale, as my father will tell you. We take but little keep of the forging of spearheads here, so that they be well-tempered and made so as to ride well on the shaft; but this head, daintily is it wrought, the blood-trench as clean and trim as though it were an Earl’s sword. See you withal this inlaying of runes on the steel? It is done with no tin or copper, but with very silver; and these bands about the shaft be of silver also. It is a fair weapon, and the owner hath a loss of it greater than his gain in the slaying of Rusty; and he will have left it in the wound so that he might be known hereafter, and that he might be said not to have murdered Rusty but to have slain him. Or how think ye?”

They all said that this seemed like to be; but that if the man who had slain Rusty were one of the ransackers they might have a blood-wite of him, if they could find him. Gold-mane said that so it was, and therewithal he gave the shepherds good-speed and went on his way.

===Chinese===
「你们可有从锈子身上找到的那杆矛？」金鬃道。

「自然有，」那汉子道。「拿过来，邻人们；把它交给长老之子。」

于是那杆矛便到了他手中，他细细端详，说道：

「这不是堡谷（Burgdale）铁匠的手艺，我父亲自会告诉你们。我们这里打造矛头并不甚讲究，只要淬火得当、装在矛杆上吃得住便罢；可是这一枚矛头，打造得极是精巧，那血槽干净利落，竟仿佛一柄伯爵的宝剑。你们再看钢上嵌的这道卢恩文字（runes）？那不是用锡或铜嵌的，而是用十足的银子；矛杆上这几道箍也是银的。这是一件佳兵，其主人失了它，比之杀锈子所得，损失更大；他之所以把它留在伤口里，是想日后被人认出来，想让人说他不是谋杀了锈子，而是光明正大地杀了他。你们以为如何？」

众人都说此言似乎有理；不过，倘若杀锈子的那人正是洗劫者之一，他们或许能向他讨一笔血金——只要找得到他。金鬃道正是如此，随即祝愿牧羊人诸事顺遂，自上路去了。

===Original===
But they came to Burgstead and found the Alderman, and in due time was a Court held, and a finding uttered, and outlawry given forth for the manslaying and the ransacking against certain men unknown. As for the spear, it was laid up in the House of the Face.

But Face-of-god pondered these matters in his mind, for such ransackings there had been none of in late years; and he said to himself that his friends of the Mountain must have other folk, of which the Dalesmen knew nought, whose gear they could lift, or how could they live in that place. And he marvelled that they should risk drawing the Dalesmen’s wrath upon them; whereas they of the Dale were strong men not easily daunted, albeit peaceable enough if not stirred to wrath. For in good sooth he had no doubt concerning that spear, whose it was and whence it came: for that very weapon had been leaning against the panel of his shut-bed the night he slept on the Mountain, and all the other spears that he saw there were more or less of the same fashion, and adorned with silver.

Albeit all that he knew, and all that he thought of, he kept in his own heart and said nothing of it.

===Chinese===
那伙人则径去堡镇，见到了长老；依着规矩，法庭开庭审理，作出裁断，对那桩命案与洗劫，向若干不知姓名之人颁下放逐之令。至于那杆矛，则被收存于面神之宅（the House of the Face）。

面神将这些事在心中反复思量，盖近些年并无此类洗劫之事；他暗自思忖：他在山中的那些朋友，必然另有他族——这些族类是谷民们一无所知的——可被他们掠夺家当，否则他们何以能在那地方存活。他又纳罕他们为何竟敢冒触怒谷民之险；盖谷中之民皆是硬汉，并不轻易被吓倒，虽然若非被激怒，他们倒也颇为爱好和平。盖因对于那杆矛属谁、来自何处，他其实毫无疑虑：就在他睡在山上那一夜，正是那件兵器靠在他封闭式木榻的壁板上；而他在那里所见的一切其他矛，或多或少都是同一形制，俱以银为饰。

纵然这一切他所知的、他所想的，他都深藏于心，半字不吐。

===Original===
So wore the autumn into early winter; and the Westland merchants came in due time, and departed without Face-of-god, though his father made him that offer one last time. He went to and fro about his work in the Dale, and seemed to most men’s eyes nought changed from what he had been. But the Bride noted that he saw her less often than his wont was, and abode with her a lesser space when he met her; and she could not think what this might mean; nor had she heart to ask him thereof, though she was sorry and grieved, but rather withdrew her company from him somewhat; and when she perceived that he noted it not, and made no question of it, then was she the sorrier.

===Chinese===
秋就这样转入初冬；西土（the Westland）商人按例如期而至，又如期而返，并未带面神同去——虽然其父最后一次又向他提过那事。他在谷中照旧来往办事，在大多数人眼中，他与从前并无两样。但新娘（the Bride）却留意到，他来见她的次数比往日少了，即便相遇，停留的时间也更短；她想不出这是为何；她也没有勇气问他，虽然心中难过忧愁，反倒在相处时稍稍疏远了他几分；及至她发觉他对此竟毫无察觉、也不置一词，她便愈发难过了。

===Original===
But the first winter-snow came on with a great storm of wind from the northeast, so that no man stirred abroad who was not compelled thereto, and those who went abroad risked life and limb thereby. Next morning all was calm again, and the snow was deep, but it did not endure long, for the wind shifted to the southwest and the thaw came, and three days after, when folk could fare easily again up and down the Dale, came tidings to Burgstead and the Alderman from the Lower Dale, how a house called Greentofts had been ransacked there, and none knew by whom. Now the goodman of Greentofts was little loved of the neighbours: he was grasping and overbearing, and had often cowed others out of their due: he was very cross-grained, both at home and abroad: his wife had fled from his hand, neither did his sons find it good to abide with him: therewithal he was wealthy of goods, a strong man and a deft man-at-arms. When his sons and his wife departed from him, and none other of the Dalesmen cared to abide with him, he went down into the Plain, and got thence men to be with him for hire, men who were not well seen to in their own land. These to the number of twelve abode with him, and did his bidding whenso it pleased them. Two more had he had who had been slain by good men of the Dale for their masterful ways; and no blood-wite had been paid for them, because of their ill-doings, though they had not been made outlaws. This man of Greentofts was called Harts-bane after his father, who was a great hunter.

===Chinese===
然而第一场冬雪却伴着一场自东北方刮来的狂风骤然而至，凡非万不得已，无人出门，凡出门之人皆冒了身家性命、伤筋断骨之险。次日清晨，一切重归平静，积雪甚深，但并不持久——风转向西南，冰雪消融；三日后，待人们又能往来谷中通行无碍之时，堡镇与长老忽然从下谷（the Lower Dale）得到消息，说那里有一户名叫绿丘（Greentofts）的农舍被人洗劫，无人知是何人所为。这绿丘的当家人素不为邻里所喜：他贪得无厌、性情专横，常以势欺人、夺人应得之物；其人处处与人顶牛，无论在家在外都是这般：他的妻子受不了他的巴掌，逃了出去，几个儿子也不愿与他同住：然而他家产殷实，又是个身强体壮、精通武艺之人。儿子和妻子都离他而去，谷中再无别人愿意与他同住，他便下到平原（the Plain）上去，在那里雇了一批人来做伴——这些人都是其本乡名声不佳、查有案底之辈。这些人共计十二名，留在他那里，高兴时才听他差遣。他原本还有两个，因在谷中横行霸道，被谷中正派之人所杀；因这两人本身作恶在先，虽未被判放逐，那两条命却也没人偿付血金。这绿丘的当家人名叫鹿煞（Harts-bane），袭的是他父亲之名——他父亲当年是一位了不起的猎户。

===Original===
Now the full tidings of the ransacking were these: The storm began two hours before sunset, and an hour thereafter, when it was quite dark, for without none could see because the wind was at its height and the drift of the snow was hard and full, the hall-door flew open; and at first men thought it had been the wind, until they saw in the dimness (for all lights but the fire on the hearth had been quenched) certain things tumbling in which at first they deemed were wolves; but when they took swords and staves against them, lo they were met by swords and axes, and they saw that the seeming wolves were men with wolf-skins drawn over them. So the newcomers cowed them that they threw down their weapons, and were bound in their places; but when they were bound, and had had time to note who the ransackers were, they saw that there were but six of them all told, who had cowed and bound Harts-bane and his twelve masterful men; and this they deemed a great shaming to them, as might well be.

So then the stead was ransacked, and those wolves took away what they would, and went their ways through the fierce storm, and none could tell whether they had lived or died in it; but at least neither the men nor their prey were seen again; nor did they leave any slot, for next morning the snow lay deep over everything.

No doubt had Gold-mane but that these ransackers were his friends of the Mountain; but he held his peace, abiding till the winter should be over.

===Chinese===
至于那场洗劫的详细经过，则是这样：风暴始于日落前两个时辰，又过一个时辰，天便全黑了——外面因风势正烈、雪片又密又猛，什么也看不见——厅堂的大门忽然被推开；起初众人还以为是风吹的，直至他们在昏暗中（因为除炉火之外，所有灯烛皆已被扑灭）看见有东西连滚带爬地翻进来，初看以为是狼；可他们拔剑抡棍迎上去时，迎面却撞上刀斧，这才看清那些貌似野狼的东西，原来是身上披着狼皮的人。来人将他们震慑住，逼得他们抛下兵器、就地被捆；待到被捆之后，才得空看清这些洗劫者究竟是何方神圣——他们统共不过六人，竟将鹿煞和他的十二个悍仆一一镇住、捆翻在地；他们自是引以为奇耻大辱，这也是人之常情。

于是这农舍便遭了洗劫，那些「狼」要什么便拿什么，随后便钻入狂风骤雪之中扬长而去，谁也说不准他们究竟活没活下来；但至少那些人和他们所掠之物再未被人见到；他们也未留下半点踪迹，因为次日清晨，大雪已将一切都厚厚覆盖。

金鬃心中再无疑虑：这些洗劫者必是他山中的朋友；但他默然无语，只待这冬天过去。

## I Of Burgstead and Its Folk and Its Neighbours / 一 堡镇与其子民及其邻人

===Original===
Once upon a time amidst the mountains and hills and falling streams of a fair land there was a town or thorp in a certain valley. This was well-nigh encompassed by a wall of sheer cliffs; toward the East and the great mountains they drew together till they went near to meet, and left but a narrow path on either side of a stony stream that came rattling down into the Dale: toward the river at that end the hills lowered somewhat, though they still ended in sheer rocks; but up from it, and more especially on the north side, they swelled into great shoulders of land, then dipped a little, and rose again into the sides of huge fells clad with pinewoods, and cleft here and there by deep ghylls: thence again they rose higher and steeper, and ever higher till they drew dark and naked out of the woods to meet the snowfields and ice-rivers of the high mountains. But that was far away from the pass by the little river into the valley; and the said river was no drain from the snowfields white and thick with the grinding of the ice, but clear and bright were its waters that came from wells amidst the bare rocky heaths.

The upper end of the valley, where it first began to open out from the pass, was rugged and broken by rocks and ridges of waterborne stones, but presently it smoothed itself into mere grassy swellings and knolls, and at last into a fair and fertile plain swelling up into a green wave, as it were, against the rock-wall which encompassed it on all sides save where the river came gushing out of the strait pass at the east end, and where at the west end it poured itself out of the Dale toward the lowlands and the plain of the great river.

Now the valley was some ten miles of our measure from that place of the rocks and the stone-ridges, to where the faces of the hills drew somewhat anigh to the river again at the west, and then fell aback along the edge of the great plain; like as when ye fare a-sailing past two nesses of a river-mouth, and the main-sea lieth open before you.

===Chinese===
昔在一片丰饶之地，群山逶迤、丘陵起伏、飞瀑流泉之间，某座山谷之中有一城邑，或者说一处处屯。此屯四面几为峭壁绝崖所环绕；东望大山，群崖逼凑，几欲相合，唯于一道乱石潺湲之溪两旁各留一径狭路，那溪水訇然作响，奔下谷中：至于临河那一头，山势虽稍低伏，崖端仍是绝壁；自此往上，尤以北岸为甚，山势鼓作一处一处宽厚之山肩，继而稍伏，复又高起，化为苍松覆被之崇山峻岭，间有深壑幽谷处处劈裂：再往上，山愈高愈险，愈险愈高，直至钻出林表，黝黑裸露，直与高山之雪原冰河相接。然此去河口入谷之隘道已远；且所说之河，并非雪原所泻、含冰磨碾而白浊稠厚之水，其流出自光秃石原间之泉眼，清泠澄澈。

谷之最上端，初自隘口展拓而出之处，崎岖嶙峋，乱石与水冲砾脊交相横斜；然行不多远，便渐趋平缓，化为略有起伏之青草冈阜，终乃舒为一方肥美沃野，宛如一道绿浪，拥向四面围合之石墙——唯东端隘口处河水汩汩涌出、西端谷水倾泻而下去往低地与大河之原处，方有缺豁。

按我们的度量，自乱石砾脊之地至西面山颜复又逼临河岸、复沿大平原之缘向后低伏之处，此谷约长十里；犹如尔等扬帆驶过河口之两岬，便见汪洋大海豁然于前。

===Original===
Besides the river aforementioned, which men called the Weltering Water, there were other waters in the Dale. Near the eastern pass, entangled in the rocky ground was a deep tarn full of cold springs and about two acres in measure, and therefrom ran a stream which fell into the Weltering Water amidst the grassy knolls. Black seemed the waters of that tarn which on one side washed the rocks-wall of the Dale; ugly and aweful it seemed to men, and none knew what lay beneath its waters save black misshapen trouts that few cared to bring to net or angle: and it was called the Death-Tarn.

Other waters yet there were: here and there from the hills on both sides, but especially from the south side, came trickles of water that ran in pretty brooks down to the river; and some of these sprang bubbling up amidst the foot-mounds of the sheer-rocks; some had cleft a rugged and strait way through them, and came tumbling down into the Dale at diverse heights from their faces. But on the north side about halfway down the Dale, one stream somewhat bigger than the others, and dealing with softer ground, had cleft for itself a wider way; and the folk had laboured this way wider yet, till they had made them a road running north along the west side of the stream. Sooth to say, except for the strait pass along the river at the eastern end, and the wider pass at the western, they had no other way (save one of which a word anon) out of the Dale but such as mountain goats and bold cragsmen might take; and even of these but few.

This midway stream was called the Wildlake, and the way along it Wildlake’s Way, because it came to them out of the wood, which on that north side stretched away from nigh to the lip of the valley-wall up to the pine woods and the high fells on the east and north, and down to the plain country on the west and south.

===Chinese===
除前述之人所称翻滚河（the Weltering Water）外，谷中尚有他水。近东端隘口，乱石盘结之间有一深潭，潭底多寒泉，广约二亩，自潭泻出一溪，注入草阜间之翻滚河中。潭水乌黑，一面贴洗谷之石墙；其状狞恶可畏，世人皆谓不祥，水下伏何物无人知晓，唯有乌黑畸形之鳟鱼数尾，少有人肯下网垂钓：故人称之曰死潭（the Death-Tarn）。

此外尚有他水：自两岸山间——尤以南岸为多——处处渗出涓流，汇为玲珑可爱之细涧，下注大河；其中数脉自绝壁根处之土阜间汩汩涌出；数脉则于崖间硬生生劈出一道崎岖狭径，自崖面高低不等处翻滚而下，坠入谷中。然北岸约当谷之半途，有一溪较他水稍大，所经又属土性较软之地，遂自辟出一条较宽之水路；谷中之民复加开凿，更拓其宽，遂沿溪西岸辟出一条北向之路。实话实说，除东端沿河之狭隘、西端之稍宽隘口外，他们再无别路（另有一路，容后补叙）可以出谷，唯有山羊与胆大之攀崖客所能通行者；且即此等险径，亦所余无几。

此中途之溪名曰野湖溪（the Wildlake），沿溪之路名曰野湖径（Wildlake's Way），盖因其自林中而来——北岸那片林莽，自谷壁唇口近旁向北延展，东接松林崇山，北亦接松林崇山，西下抵平原之野，南下亦抵平原之野。

===Original===
Now when the Weltering Water came out of the rocky tangle near the pass, it was turned aside by the ground till it swung right up to the feet of the Southern crags; then it turned and slowly bent round again northward, and at last fairly doubled back on itself before it turned again to run westward; so that when, after its second double, it had come to flowing softly westward under the northern crags, it had cast two thirds of a girdle round about a space of land a little below the grassy knolls and tofts aforesaid; and there in that fair space between the folds of the Weltering Water stood the Thorp whereof the tale hath told.

The men thereof had widened and deepened the Weltering Water about them, and had bridged it over to the plain meads; and athwart the throat of the space left clear by the water they had built them a strong wall though not very high, with a gate amidst and a tower on either side thereof. Moreover, on the face of the cliff which was but a stone’s throw from the gate they had made them stairs and ladders to go up by; and on a knoll nigh the brow had built a watchtower of stone strong and great, lest war should come into the land from over the hills. That tower was ancient, and therefrom the Thorp had its name and the whole valley also; and it was called Burgstead in Burgdale.

So long as the Weltering Water ran straight along by the northern cliffs after it had left Burgstead, betwixt the water and the cliffs was a wide flat way fashioned by man’s hand. Thus was the water again a good defence to the Thorp, for it ran slow and deep there, and there was no other ground betwixt it and the cliffs save that road, which was easy to bar across so that no foemen might pass without battle, and this road was called the Portway. For a long mile the river ran under the northern cliffs, and then turned into the midst of the Dale, and went its way westward a broad stream winding in gentle laps and folds here and there down to the outgate of the Dale. But the Portway held on still underneath the rock-wall, till the sheer-rocks grew somewhat broken, and were cumbered with certain screes, and at last the wayfarer came upon the break in them, and the ghyll through which ran the Wildlake with Wildlake’s Way beside it, but the Portway still went on all down the Dale and away to the Plain-country.

===Chinese===
且说翻滚河自隘口附近乱石丛中涌出之后，为地势所导，径直荡向南岸绝壁之下；继而折回，缓缓北转，末了竟自身回环相叠，方才再转西流；故当其二度折叠、已自徐徐西行于北岸绝壁之下时，便已绕前述草阜土阜稍下之处一方地土，围上整整三分之二道束带；就在翻滚河两道折痕之间那片丰美之地，立着本篇故事所要讲的那个屯子。

屯中之民已将环抱他们的一段翻滚河拓宽挖深，又架桥以通平原之草甸；并于水所留出的那片咽喉之地，筑起一道坚固之城墙，墙虽不高，当中开一门，门之两翼各立一塔。此外，于距城门一箭之遥的崖面之上，又凿级架梯，以便攀援；并于崖畔一处土阜之上，造了一座高大的石筑望楼，以防山外有兵祸来袭。此楼年代久远，屯子与整片山谷之名皆由它而来；是名堡谷之堡镇（Burgstead in Burgdale）。

翻滚河离堡镇之后，沿北岸绝壁笔直流淌之处，水与崖之间，有一条宽阔平夷、人工铺就之路。如此一来，河水又成了堡镇的天然屏障：其处水深流缓，水崖之间别无他地，唯有此路，极易横断设障，来敌非经血战不能通过；此路名曰港路（the Portway）。大河沿北岸绝壁约行一长里，乃折入谷之中枢，化作一条宽阔之流，左回右旋、舒缓蜿蜒，直至谷之西门。港路则依旧沿石墙之下延展，直至绝壁渐破、碎石壅塞之处，行人乃见崖间一豁，野湖溪所流之深壑即在是处，野湖径亦随之并行；而港路仍自沿谷而下，远通平原之野。

===Original===
That road in the ghyll, which was neither wide nor smooth, the wayfarer into the wood must follow, till it lifted itself out of the ghyll, and left the Wildlake coming rattling down by many steps from the east; and now the way went straight north through the woodland, ever mounting higher, (because the whole set of the land was toward the high fells,) but not in any cleft or ghyll. The wood itself thereabout was thick, a blended growth of diverse kinds of trees, but most of oak and ash; light and air enough came through their boughs to suffer the holly and bramble and eglantine and other small wood to grow together into thickets, which no man could pass without hewing a way. But before it is told whereto Wildlake’s Way led, it must be said that on the east side of the ghyll, where it first began just over the Portway, the hill’s brow was clear of wood for a certain space, and there, overlooking all the Dale, was the Motestead of the Dalesmen, marked out by a great ring of stones, amidst of which was the mound for the Judges and the Altar of the Gods before it. And this was the holy place of the men of the Dale and of other folk whereof the tale shall now tell.

For when Wildlake’s Way had gone some three miles from the Motestead, the trees began to thin, and presently afterwards was a clearing and the dwellings of men, built of timber as may well be thought. These houses were neither rich nor great, nor was the folk a mighty folk, because they were but a few, albeit body by body they were stout carles enough. They had not affinity with the Dalesmen, and did not wed with them, yet it is to be deemed that they were somewhat akin to them. To be short, though they were freemen, yet as regards the Dalesmen were they well-nigh their servants; for they were but poor in goods, and had to lean upon them somewhat. No tillage they had among those high trees; and of beasts nought save some flocks of goats and a few asses. Hunters they were, and charcoal-burners, and therein the deftest of men, and they could shoot well in the bow withal: so they trucked their charcoal and their smoked venison and their peltries with the Dalesmen for wheat and wine and weapons and weed; and the Dalesmen gave them main good pennyworths, as men who had abundance wherewith to uphold their kinsmen, though they were but faraway kin. Stout hands had these Woodlanders and true hearts as any; but they were few-spoken and to those that needed them not somewhat surly of speech and grim of visage: brown-skinned they were, but light-haired; well-eyed, with but little red in their cheeks: their women were not very fair, for they toiled like the men, or more. They were thought to be wiser than most men in foreseeing things to come. They were much given to spells, and songs of wizardry, and were very mindful of the old story-lays, wherein they were far more wordy than in their daily speech. Much skill had they in runes, and were exceeding deft in scoring them on treen bowls, and on staves, and doorposts and roof-beams and standing-beds and suchlike things. Many a day when the snow was drifting over their roofs, and hanging heavy on the tree-boughs, and the wind was roaring through the trees aloft and rattling about the close thicket, when the boughs were clattering in the wind, and crashing down beneath the weight of the gathering freezing snow, when all beasts and men lay close in their lairs, would they sit long hours about the house-fire with the knife or the gouge in hand, with the timber twixt their knees and the whetstone beside them, hearkening to some tale of old times and the days when their banner was abroad in the world; and they the while wheedling into growth out of the tough wood knots and blossoms and leaves and the images of beasts and warriors and women.

===Chinese===
深壑中那一条既不宽亦不平之路，入林行人必由之而行，直至其路自壑中拔出，舍野湖溪于东边逐级訇然下泻之处不顾；自此路乃直北穿过林莽，节节升高（盖此地之全势皆倾向崇山也），然不在任何沟裂深壑之中。林中树木至为稠密，杂木并生，而以柞、梣为多；枝间透光透气，足以容冬青、荆棘、野蔷薇及其他矮木丛生纠结，合为灌丛，人不挥斧开路则无以通行。然在未述野湖径所通何处之前，尚有一事须叙：深壑东岸，初起于港路之上处，山颜有一片无林之空地，就在那里，俯瞰全谷，是谷民之议事坪（the Motestead），以一圈大石为记，圈中设判官之土台，台前立诸神之祭坛。此地乃谷民及下文将述之他族之圣地。

盖野湖径自议事坪行约三里，林木渐疏，旋即有一片空地，其中有人家居所，可想而知，皆木所筑。这些屋宇并不富丽、亦不宏大，此族亦非强族，因人丁寡少之故；纵然如此，逐一而论，个个都是壮健汉子。他们与谷民并无姻亲之谊，不相婚娶，然可推想彼此血脉略有相通。长话短说：他们虽是自由之民，对谷民而言却几近仆从；因其家底寒酸，不得不稍借其势以为倚靠。那些参天巨木之下，他们不事耕耘；牲畜则无，唯有山羊几群、驴子数头而已。他们是猎户，又是烧炭之徒，而且皆是此中圣手，弓箭又射得极准：于是以炭、熏鹿肉、皮毛与谷民交换麦、酒、兵器、布帛；谷民所与之物甚是丰厚，因其物产充盈，足以抚恤远亲故旧。这些林中之民双手壮健、心肠忠义，不逊于人；然寡言少语，对于不求他们之人，言语粗率、面色冷峻：肤色棕褐，头发却浅；双目炯炯，双颊少血色；其妇人不算美貌，因其劳作与男子相当，甚或过之。世人以为他们比多数人更善于未卜先知。他们酷好符咒与巫歌，于古老之英雄歌谣记诵极熟，每诵此类，滔滔不绝，远非日常言语之可比。其人精通卢恩文字（runes），极擅以之刻于木碗、杖、门柱、梁栋、固定木榻之类物件之上。多少个冬日，大雪飘过屋脊、压满枝头，长风穿林怒号、撼撼灌丛，枝柯风中哗啦作响、积雪成冰、不堪其重而訇然坠地之时，百兽与人皆蜷伏于巢穴之中，他们却长时围坐炉火之畔，一手执刀或圆凿，膝间夹木、旁侧置磨石，聆一段古老传说、先祖旌旗扬于天下之往事；手底却同时自坚韧之木节中，雕琢催生出花结、繁花、绿叶，以及百兽、武士、妇人之像。

===Original===
They were called nought save the Woodland-Carles in that day, though time had been when they had borne a nobler name: and their abode was called Carlstead. Shortly, for all they had and all they had not, for all they were and all they were not, they were well-beloved by their friends and feared by their foes.

Now when Wildlake’s Way was gotten to Carlstead, there was an end of it toward the north; though beyond it in a right line the wood was thinner, because of the hewing of the Carles. But the road itself turned west at once and went on through the wood, till some four miles further it first thinned and then ceased altogether, the ground going downhill all the way: for this was the lower flank of the first great upheaval toward the high mountains. But presently, after the wood was ended, the land broke into swelling downs and winding dales of no great height or depth, with a few scattered trees about the hillsides, mostly thorns or scrubby oaks, gnarled and bent and kept down by the western wind: here and there also were yew-trees, and whiles the hillsides would be grown over with boxwood, but none very great; and often juniper grew abundantly. This then was the country of the Shepherds, who were friends both of the Dalesmen and the Woodlanders. They dwelt not in any fenced town or thorp, but their homesteads were scattered about as was handy for water and shelter. Nevertheless they had their own stronghold; for amidmost of their country, on the highest of a certain down above a bottom where a willowy stream winded, was a great earthwork: the walls thereof were high and clean and overlapping at the entering in, and amidst of it was a deep well of water, so that it was a very defensible place: and thereto would they drive their flocks and herds when war was in the land, for nought but a very great host might win it; and this stronghold they called Greenbury.

===Chinese===
当世之人只唤他们作林中汉子（the Woodland-Carles），虽则昔日他们曾有一更高贵之名：其所居之处名曰汉子镇（Carlstead）。简而言之，凡其所有所无、所是所非，皆因其友爱之族亲之、仇敌之族畏之。

野湖径既抵汉子镇，其北向之路即尽；然循直线越过镇去，林木渐稀，那是汉子们斫伐所致。但道路本身却当即折而向西，穿过林莽继续延展，约四里之后，林木先疏、继而绝尽，一路地势下行：盖因此处乃是趋向高山的第一道大隆起之较低山麓。林尽之后不久，地势断为一起一伏之丘陵与蜿蜒浅谷，高深皆不甚厉害，山坡之上散生几株树，多是荆棘或矮柞，为西风所扭曲压伏；处处又可见紫杉，有时整面山坡为黄杨所覆，然皆不甚高大；杜松则往往丛生极茂。这便是牧羊之民（the Shepherds）之地——他们与谷民、林中之民皆为友。他们并不居于任何有围墙之城镇屯子之中，其农舍散处各处，唯就水草便易、避风藏风之处而安。然而他们自有其堡垒：其地之正中，某一土阜之最高处，下临一道柳荫溪流蜿蜒之谷底，有一座大土垒：其墙高峻光洁，入口处层层叠套，垒中有一深井，故为一极可坚守之地：一遇兵祸，他们便驱赶牛羊群入此；若无大军，绝难攻取；此堡垒他们唤作绿堡（Greenbury）。

===Original===
These Shepherd-Folk were strong and tall like the Woodlanders, for they were partly of the same blood, but burnt they were both ruddy and brown: they were of more words than the Woodlanders but yet not many-worded. They knew well all those old story-lays, (and this partly by the minstrelsy of the Woodlanders,) but they had scant skill in wizardry, and would send for the Woodlanders, both men and women, to do whatso they needed therein. They were very hale and long-lived, whereas they dwelt in clear bright air, and they mostly went light-clad even in the winter, so strong and merry were they. They wedded with the Woodlanders and the Dalesmen both; at least certain houses of them did so. They grew no corn; nought but a few potherbs, but had their meal of the Dalesmen; and in the summer they drave some of their milch-kine into the Dale for the abundance of grass there; whereas their own hills and bents and winding valleys were not plenteously watered, except here and there as in the bottom under Greenbury. No swine they had, and but few horses, but of sheep very many, and of the best both for their flesh and their wool. Yet were they nought so deft craftsmen at the loom as were the Dalesmen, and their women were not very eager at the weaving, though they loathed not the spindle and rock. Shortly, they were merry folk well-beloved of the Dalesmen, quick to wrath, though it abode not long with them; not very curious in their houses and halls, which were but little, and were decked mostly with the handiwork of the Woodland-Carles their guests; who when they were abiding with them, would oft stand long hours nose to beam, scoring and nicking and hammering, answering no word spoken to them but with aye or no, desiring nought save the endurance of the daylight. Moreover, this shepherd-folk heeded not gay raiment overmuch, but commonly went clad in white woollen or sheep-brown weed.

===Chinese===
这些牧羊之民与林中之民一般强壮高大，因其本有一半相同血脉，只是肤色赤褐相杂：他们比林中之民话多些，却也并非多言之辈。那些古老英雄歌谣他们皆熟知（此半赖林中之民之弹唱），但巫术一道，他们所知甚少，凡有需用之处，便去请林中之民，无论男女，来代为施为。他们极为康健而高寿，因其居于清明朗澈之气中；纵然隆冬，亦多衣衫单薄，其体魄之壮、心性之乐如此。他们与林中之民、谷民皆有婚娶；至少其中几个氏族是如此。他们不种谷物；只种几样菜蔬，口粮全赖谷民供给；夏日则驱一部分乳牛入谷，因谷中牧草丰美；而他们自家之山阜冈岭、蜿蜒谷地，水脉并不充盈，唯处处如绿堡下方之谷底那般为例外。他们不养猪，马也少，但羊极多，无论肉味、羊毛皆是上上之选。然其织造之巧，远不及谷民；其妇人于织布一事也不甚热心，虽则并不厌弃纺锤与卷线杆。简而言之，他们是个乐天之人，深得谷民喜爱，性急易怒，然怒气难久；于居室厅堂并不甚讲究，其屋皆小，所饰大多是座上客林中汉子之手笔；那些汉子作客之时，往往鼻尖贴着梁木，立上良久，或刻或凿或敲，旁人问话只以"是""否"二字作答，所求唯天光不歇而已。再者，此牧羊之民不甚以华服为意，平素多穿白色羊毛或羊褐之布。

===Original===
But beyond this shepherd-folk were more downs and more, scantily peopled, and that after a while by folk with whom they had no kinship or affinity, and who were at whiles their foes. Yet was there no enduring enmity between them; and ever after war and battle came peace; and all blood-wites were duly paid and no long feud followed: nor were the Dalesmen and the Woodlanders always in these wars, though at whiles they were. Thus then it fared with these people.

But now that we have told of the folks with whom the Dalesmen had kinship, affinity, and friendship, tell we of their chief abode, Burgstead to wit, and of its fashion. As hath been told, it lay upon the land made nigh into an isle by the folds of the Weltering Water towards the uppermost end of the Dale; and it was warded by the deep water, and by the wall aforesaid with its towers. Now the Dale at its widest, to wit where Wildlake fell into it, was but nine furlongs over, but at Burgstead it was far narrower; so that betwixt the wall and the wandering stream there was but a space of fifty acres, and therein lay Burgstead in a space of the shape of a sword-pommel: and the houses of the kinships lay about it, amidst of gardens and orchards, but little ordered into streets and lanes, save that a way went clean through everything from the tower-warded gate to the bridge over the Water, which was warded by two other towers on its hither side.

===Chinese===
然而牧羊之民再往外，又是一重接一重的丘陵，人烟稀少；再走一段，所居之民与彼等并无血缘姻亲，时且为仇敌。然彼此之间并无宿怨；每经战伐厮杀之后，旋即复归和好；所有血金皆如期偿付，不生长久仇雠：而此类战事之中，谷民与林中之民亦非每次参与，虽则偶尔也会卷入。这些人之间，便是这般相处的。

既已将谷民有血缘、姻亲、友盟之诸族一一叙过，今且讲其主居之地，即堡镇，并其形制。如前所述，其地位于翻滚河两道折痕所围、几成孤岛之地，处谷之最上端；其地有深水为障，又有所述之墙及墙上之塔为卫。谷之最宽处，即野湖溪汇入之处，亦不过九浪之遥；至堡镇处，则远为狭窄；故墙与曲折之河之间，仅余五十亩之地，堡镇即卧于其间，其形如剑首：诸氏族之屋宇环绕其周，错落于花园果园之间，然街巷并不甚规整，唯有一条大道自塔卫之门笔直穿过一切，直至河上之桥；桥之此岸又另立两塔以为守卫。

===Original===
As to the houses, they were some bigger, some smaller, as the housemates needed. Some were old, but not very old, save two only, and some quite new, but of these there were not many: they were all built fairly of stone and lime, with much fair and curious carved work of knots and beasts and men round about the doors; or whiles a wale of suchlike work all along the house-front. For as deft as were the Woodlanders with knife and gouge on the oaken beams, even so deft were the Dalesmen with mallet and chisel on the face of the hewn stone; and this was a great pastime about the Thorp. Within these houses had but a hall and solar, with shut-beds out from the hall on one side or two, with whatso of kitchen and buttery and out-bower men deemed handy. Many men dwelt in each house, either kinsfolk, or such as were joined to the kindred.

Near to the gate of Burgstead in that street aforesaid and facing east was the biggest house of the Thorp; it was one of the two abovesaid which were older than any other. Its doorposts and the lintel of the door were carved with knots and twining stems fairer than other houses of that stead; and on the wall beside the door carved over many stones was an image wrought in the likeness of a man with a wide face, which was terrible to behold, although it smiled: he bore a bent bow in his hand with an arrow fitted to its string, and about the head of him was a ring of rays like the beams of the sun, and at his feet was a dragon, which had crept, as it were, from amidst of the blossomed knots of the doorpost wherewith the tail of him was yet entwined. And this head with the ring of rays about it was wrought into the adornment of that house, both within and without, in many other places, but on never another house of the Dale; and it was called the House of the Face. Thereof hath the tale much to tell hereafter, but as now it goeth on to tell of the ways of life of the Dalesmen.

===Chinese===
至于那些屋宇，有大有小，全看同居之人所需。其中有些是旧屋，然并不十分古老，唯有两座除外；有些则是新近所造，但这般新的并不算多：皆以石与灰浆垒砌而成，颇为考究，门四周多有精美的花结、走兽、人物的雕饰；有时整道屋前脸都横着一道诸如此类的雕带。盖因林中之民以刀、圆凿施于橡梁之上，其巧如此；谷民以木槌、凿子施于斫石之面，其巧亦然；而这正是全屯之人的一大消遣。屋内不过一厅一堂（厅在明、堂在阁），自厅之一侧或两侧辟出封闭之木榻卧间，外配厨房、酒室、别院之类，凡日常便用者一应俱备。每屋所居之人甚多，或为同族，或为附于宗族之人。

前述那条街上，近堡镇城门、面东而立者，是全屯最大之屋；此屋即前文所说两座最古之屋之一。其门柱与门楣所雕花结缠枝，比镇上他屋都更精美；门侧之墙上，镌于数方大石之上，有一尊人像，作阔面男子之形，虽含笑而威严可畏：他一手持弯弓，弦上搭一矢，头部绕一圈光芒，状如日轮辐条；其足下盘一龙，仿佛刚从门柱繁花结纹之间爬出，龙尾尚与花结缠结未解。这绕以光芒之阔面首级，里里外外镌于该屋多处装饰之上，而全谷他屋再无一处用之；此屋名为面神之宅（the House of the Face）。此事后文尚有许多话讲，眼下且接着讲谷民之日常起居。

===Original===
In Burgstead was no Mote-hall or Town-house or Church, such as we wot of in these days; and their marketplace was wheresoever any might choose to pitch a booth: but for the most part this was done in the wide street betwixt the gate and the bridge. As to a meeting-place, were there any small matters between man and man, these would the Alderman or one of the Wardens deal with, sitting in Court with the neighbours on the wide space just outside the Gate: but if it were to do with greater matters, such as great manslayings and blood-wites, or the making of war or ending of it, or the choosing of the Alderman and the Wardens, such matters must be put off to the Folk-mote, which could but be held in the place aforesaid where was the Doom-ring and the Altar of the Gods; and at that Folk-mote both the Shepherd-Folk and the Woodland-Carles foregathered with the Dalesmen, and duly said their say. There also they held their great casts and made offerings to the Gods for the Fruitfulness of the Year, the ingathering of the increase, and in Memory of their Forefathers. Natheless at Yuletide also they feasted from house to house to be glad with the rest of Midwinter, and many a cup drank at those feasts to the memory of the fathers, and the days when the world was wider to them, and their banners fared far afield.

But besides these dwellings of men in the field between the wall and the water, there were homesteads up and down the Dale whereso men found it easy and pleasant to dwell: their halls were built of much the same fashion as those within the Thorp; but many had a high garth-wall cast about them, so that they might make a stout defence in their own houses if war came into the Dale.

===Chinese===
堡镇之中，并无我们今日所熟知的那种议事厅、公所、或教堂；其集市，则是任人何处愿搭棚摆摊，便在何处：然多半仍设于城门与桥之间那条宽阔大街之上。至于议事之所，凡是人与人之间些许琐碎小事，皆由长老（the Alderman）或一位守事（the Wardens），会同邻里，于城门外那片开阔之地开堂审断：但若事关重大——例如重大命案、血金，或战与和之决断，或长老与守事之推举——此类事必押后至民众大会（the Folk-mote）决断；而民众大会只能于前文所说有判决环（the Doom-ring）与诸神祭坛之处召开；届时牧羊之民与林中汉子皆来与谷民会聚，依礼各陈己见。他们也在那里举行盛大卜占，并向诸神献祭，以求岁物丰成、收纳有余，并追念先祖。然每逢岁末冬至节（Yuletide），他们亦自一家吃到一家，与众人在仲冬（Midwinter）同乐；席间举杯无数，皆祝及先祖，以及那时天地对他们尚宽、他们的旌旗远征四方的旧日。

然除墙与水之间那些人居之外，谷中处处——凡人以为宜居宜乐之地——皆有农舍：其厅堂形制与屯中者大致相同；但许多农舍外围筑有一道高院墙，以便一旦兵祸入谷，可在自家屋中据守力战。

===Original===
As to their work afield; in many places the Dale was fair with growth of trees, and especially were there long groves of sweet chestnut standing on the grass, of the fruit whereof the folk had much gain. Also on the south side nigh to the western end was a wood or two of yew-trees very great and old, whence they gat them bow-staves, for the Dalesmen also shot well in the bow. Much wheat and rye they raised in the Dale, and especially at the nether end thereof. Apples and pears and cherries and plums they had in plenty; of which trees, some grew about the borders of the acres, some in the gardens of the Thorp and the homesteads. On the slopes that had grown from the breaking down here and there of the Northern cliffs, and which faced the South and the Sun’s burning, were rows of goodly vines, whereof the folk made them enough and to spare of strong wine both white and red.

As to their beasts; swine they had a many, but not many sheep, since herein they trusted to their trucking with their friends the Shepherds; they had horses, and yet but a few, for they were stout in going afoot; and, had they a journey to make with women big with babes, or with children or outworn elders, they would yoke their oxen to their wains, and go fair and softly whither they would. But the said oxen and all their neat were exceeding big and fair, far other than the little beasts of the Shepherd-Folk; they were either dun of colour, or white with black horns (and those very great) and black tail-tufts and ear-tips. Asses they had, and mules for the paths of the mountains to the east; geese and hens enough, and dogs not a few, great hounds stronger than wolves, sharp-nosed, long-jawed, dun of colour, shag-haired.

===Chinese===
至于其田亩之业：谷中多处树木葱茏、景致宜人，尤以那一列列立于草地之上的甜栗长林为最，其果为民所获甚丰。又南岸近西端之处，有一两片极其高大古老之紫杉林，他们便从那里取材制作弓背——因谷民弓箭亦射得极准。谷中所种小麦、黑麦甚多，尤以谷之下端为最。苹果、梨、樱桃、李子，应有尽有；其中一些杂生于田亩边界，一些生于屯中及农舍之果园。北岸绝壁处处崩塌所积之山坡，面南而受烈日灼照者，皆成一排排佳美葡萄藤，民以之酿制烈酒，红白俱备，自用有余。

至于牲畜：猪极多，羊却不多，因这一项他们仰仗与朋友牧羊之民的交易；马是有的，却也不多，因为他们步行即是好汉；但凡须携有孕之妇、或孩童、或年迈力衰之长辈出行，他们便驾牛于车，安安稳稳、缓缓而行，欲至何处便至何处。而这些牛以及其他所有牲畜，皆极其肥美高大，与牧羊之民那些矮小牲口判若云泥；其色或为暗褐，或为白身而黑角（角又极大）、黑尾梢、黑耳尖。他们又有驴、有骡，以备东行山路之用；鹅、鸡足用；狗也不少，皆是伟岸之猎犬，气力胜过野狼，鼻尖、颌长、毛色暗褐、毛长而蓬。

===Original===
As to their wares; they were very deft weavers of wool and flax, and made a shift to dye the thrums in fair colours; since both woad and madder came to them good cheap by means of the merchants of the plain country, and of greening weeds was abundance at hand. Good smiths they were in all the metals: they washed somewhat of gold out of the sands of the Weltering Water, and copper and tin they fetched from the rocks of the eastern mountains; but of silver they saw little, and iron they must buy of the merchants of the plain, who came to them twice in the year, to wit in the spring and the late autumn just before the snows. Their wares they bought with wool spun and in the fleece, and fine cloth, and skins of wine and young neat both steers and heifers, and wrought copper bowls, and gold and copper by weight, for they had no stamped money. And they guested these merchants well, for they loved them, because of the tales they told them of the Plain and its cities, and the manslayings therein, and the fall of Kings and Dukes, and the uprising of Captains.

Thus then lived this folk in much plenty and ease of life, though not delicately nor desiring things out of measure. They wrought with their hands and wearied themselves; and they rested from their toil and feasted and were merry: tomorrow was not a burden to them, nor yesterday a thing which they would fain forget: life shamed them not, nor did death make them afraid.

As for the Dale wherein they dwelt, it was indeed most fair and lovely, and they deemed it the Blessing of the Earth, and they trod its flowery grass beside its rippled streams amidst its green tree-boughs proudly and joyfully with goodly bodies and merry hearts.

===Chinese===
至于其百工之物：他们是织造羊毛、亚麻的圣手，又能设法将纱头纱尾染得诸色鲜明；盖因靛蓝、茜草皆可借平原商人之手廉价而至，而可染绿色之草木又处处皆是。他们在一切金工之上皆是良匠：自翻滚河之沙中略可淘出些金，铜与锡则取自东面山中之岩石；但银是难得一见的，铁则必须向平原之商人购买——商人每岁来两次，一在春季，一在大雪将至之深秋。他们用来交易之物，是已纺及未纺之羊毛、精细布匹、整囊之酒、幼牛不论牡牝、铜碗之属，以及以分量计之金与铜——因为他们并无鼓铸之钱。他们待这些商人甚是殷勤，因其爱重他们——爱他们所述平原及其城邑之事、其中的杀伐、诸王公之覆灭与诸将之勃兴。

此族之人便如此生活：丰饶而安乐，然并不奢靡，亦不贪求过度之物。他们以双手劳作、以致筋疲力尽；又自劳顿中歇息、设宴、作乐：明日于他们不是负担，昨日于他们亦非欲忘之物：生不足以使他们羞惭，死亦不足以使他们畏惧。

至于他们所居之谷，诚然是极其秀美可爱之地；他们视之为大地之福泽；他们以健全之躯、欢快之心，昂首欣然踏行于其繁花之草上、其潺潺之溪畔、其青葱之枝下。

## II Of Face-of-god and His Kindred / 二 论面神及其亲族

===Original===
Tells the tale, that on an evening of late autumn when the weather was fair, calm, and sunny, there came a man out of the wood hard by the Motestead aforesaid, who sat him down at the roots of the Speech-mound, casting down before him a roebuck which he had just slain in the wood. He was a young man of three and twenty summers; he was so clad that he had on him a sheep-brown kirtle and leggings of like stuff bound about with white leather thongs; he bore a short-sword in his girdle and a little axe withal; the sword with fair wrought gilded hilts and a dew-shoe of like fashion to its sheath. He had his quiver at his back and bare in his hand his bow unstrung. He was tall and strong, very fair of fashion both of limbs and face, white-skinned, but for the sun’s tanning, and ruddy-cheeked: his beard was little and fine, his hair yellow and curling, cut somewhat close, but for its length so plenteous, and so thick, that none could fail to note it. He had no hat nor hood upon his head, nought but a fillet of golden beads.

As he sat down he glanced at the dale below him with a well-pleased look, and then cast his eyes down to the grass at his feet, as though to hold a little longer all unchanged the image of the fair place he had just seen. The sun was low in the heavens, and his slant beams fell yellow all up the dale, gilding the chestnut groves grown dusk and grey with autumn, and the black masses of the elm-boughs, and gleaming back here and there from the pools of the Weltering Water. Down in the midmost meadows the long-horned dun kine were moving slowly as they fed along the edges of the stream, and a dog was bounding about with exceeding swiftness here and there among them. At a sharply curved bight of the river the man could see a little vermilion flame flickering about, and above it a thin blue veil of smoke hanging in the air, and clinging to the boughs of the willows anear; about it were a dozen menfolk clear to see, some sitting, some standing, some walking to and fro, but all in company together: four of were brown-clad and short-skirted like himself, and from above the hand of one came a flash of light as the sun smote upon the steel of his spear. The others were long-skirted and clad gayer, and amongst them were red and blue and green and white garments, and they were clear to be seen for women. Just as the young man looked up again, those of them who were sitting down rose up, and those that were strolling drew nigh, and they joined hands together, and fell to dancing on the grass, and the dog and another one with him came up to the dancers and raced about and betwixt them; and so clear to see were they all and so little, being far away, that they looked like dainty well-wrought puppets.

===Chinese===
话说晚秋某夕，天朗气清、风息日明，自前述议事坪旁那片林中走出一人，至议事土台之根前坐下，将方才于林中所杀一头獐鹿掷于身前。其人年方二十三岁；所着之衣，乃是一件羊褐短袍，下配同色裤腿，以白皮条缠缚；腰间悬一口短剑，另带一柄小斧；剑柄镌工精美、鎏金为饰，剑鞘口缘亦以同样鎏金之护口（dew-shoe）镶配。背上一壶箭，手中持一张已卸弦之弓。其人身高体壮，肢体与面容皆极俊秀；肤色本白，唯因日晒而微染；双颊红润；须髯稀疏而细，头发金黄卷曲，剪得颇短，然就其长度而言，既丰且密，任谁见了都不能不留意。他头上不戴帽、不披兜帽，唯束一道金珠编成的额带。

他坐下之时，欣然望了一眼脚下之谷，随即将目光垂落足前之草，仿佛要将方才所见那片佳境之影像，原封不动再多留片刻。其时日已西沉，斜晖作金黄色铺满整条山谷，将秋来苍灰之栗林、漆黑成团之榆树枝头，尽镀上一层金色；又自翻滚河（the Weltering Water）各处水潭之中，处处返照而回。下方正中之草甸上，长角暗褐之牛群沿溪边缓缓移牧，一只犬在其间左奔右突，迅捷异常。河流一处急弯之处，那人望见一豆朱红火苗摇曳其上，火上一缕淡蓝炊烟悬于空中，缠附于近旁柳枝之间；其周约有一十二人清晰可辨，或坐、或立、或往来行走，却都聚在一处：其中四人如他一般衣羊褐、着短衣，其中一人之手上方忽有一道闪光，乃日光击于其枪铁之上。其余之人皆衣长裙、装束更鲜，红蓝绿白诸色夹杂其间，一望可知皆是女子。正当那年轻人抬头再看之际，坐着的人纷纷起身，踱步的人也都走近，彼此携手成圈，在草上跳起舞来；那条狗和另一条狗一同跑近舞者，在其间来回穿梭嬉逐；这些人因离得远，个个身形细小，却又望得清清楚楚，宛如一尊尊精巧别致、做工讲究的小傀儡。

===Original===
The young man sat smiling at it for a little, and then rose up and shouldered his venison, and went down into Wildlake’s Way, and presently was fairly in the Dale and striding along the Portway beside the northern cliffs, whose greyness was gilded yet by the last rays of the sun, though in a minute or two it would go under the western rim. He went fast and cheerily, murmuring to himself snatches of old songs; none overtook him on the road, but he overtook divers folk going alone or in company toward Burgstead; swains and old men, mothers and maidens coming from the field and the acre, or going from house to house; and one or two he met but not many. All these greeted him kindly, and he them again; but he stayed not to speak with any, but went as one in haste.

It was dusk by then he passed under the gate of Burgstead; he went straight thence to the door of the House of the Face, and entered as one who is at home, and need go no further, nor abide a bidding.

The hall he came into straight out of the open air was long and somewhat narrow and not right high; it was well-nigh dark now within, but since he knew where to look, he could see by the flicker that leapt up now and then from the smouldering brands of the hearth amidmost the hall under the luffer, that there were but three men therein, and belike they were even they whom he looked to find there, and for their part they looked for his coming, and knew his step.

He set down his venison on the floor, and cried out in a cheery voice: “Ho, Kettel! Are all men gone without doors to sleep so near the winter-tide, that the Hall is as dark as a cave? Hither to me! Or art thou also sleeping?”

A voice came from the further side of the hearth: “Yea, lord, asleep I am, and have been, and dreaming; and in my dream I dealt with the fleshpots and the cake-board, and thou shalt see my dream come true presently to thy gain.”

Quoth another voice: “Kettel hath had out that share of his dream already belike, if the saw sayeth sooth about cooks. All ye have been away, so belike he hath done as Rafe’s dog when Rafe ran away from the slain buck.”

===Chinese===
那年轻人含笑看了片刻，随即起身，将猎得的鹿肉往肩上一扛，下野湖径（Wildlake's Way）而去，不多时便已入谷，大步流星地沿北岸绝壁之下的港路（the Portway）而行；那灰色崖壁犹为最后一缕残阳所镀金，然一二分钟之内，日头便要沉入西山之缘了。他步履轻快、一路欣然，口中低哼着古歌零章；路上无人赶过他，他却赶上了三三两两或独行或结伴往堡镇而去的人：少年与老者、带儿的母亲与闺中少女，或自田间亩中归来，或自一家走往另一家；迎面相逢的也有一两个，却不多。这些人都亲热与他见礼，他也一一回礼；然而他并不停下与任何人搭话，径自匆匆而行。

待他走过堡镇城门之下时，天色已暝；他径直走到面神之宅（the House of the Face）门前，如归家之人一般推门而入——既不必再往别处，也不必等人通报。

他自露天之中径直踏入的那间厅堂，长而稍狭，并不甚高；此时厅内已近乎昏暗，但他知道该往何处看，凭炉火余烬不时跃起之一缕光焰——那炉火正在厅堂中央烟罩（luffer）之下——便可看出其中不过三人，多半正是他要找的那几位；而那几位也在等他前来，一听脚步便知是他。

他将鹿肉往地上一放，朗声笑道："喂，凯特尔（Kettel）！人都到屋外睡觉去了么，冬至在即，厅里竟黑得像个洞穴？过来！莫非你也在打瞌睡？"

炉火那一头传来一个声音："是，少爷，我是在睡觉，已经睡了一阵，还在做梦呢；梦里我正围着肉锅和糕饼案板打转，您马上便能瞧见我这梦应验，叫您占些便宜。"

另一个声音道："若是那句说厨子的俗话不假，凯特尔这梦里他该得的那份怕是已经到手了。你们一个个都出门去了，他多半就像雷夫（Rafe）那条狗——雷夫撇下那头死鹿跑了，狗便——"

===Original===
He laughed therewith, and Kettel with him, and a third voice joined the laughter. The young man also laughed and said: “Here I bring the venison which my kinsman desired; but as ye see I have brought it over-late: but take it, Kettel. When cometh my father from the stithy?”

Quoth Kettel: “My lord hath been hard at it shaping the Yuletide sword, and doth not lightly leave such work, as ye wot, but he will be here presently, for he has sent to bid us dight for supper straightway.”

Said the young man: “Where are there lords in the dale, Kettel, or hast thou made some thyself, that thou must be always throwing them in my teeth?”

“Son of the Alderman,” said Kettel, “ye call me Kettel, which is no name of mine, so why should I not call thee lord, which is no dignity of thine, since it goes well over my tongue from old use and wont? But here comes my mate of the kettle, and the women and lads. Sit down by the hearth away from their hurry, and I will fetch thee the hand-water.”

The young man sat down, and Kettel took up the venison and went his ways toward the door at the lower end of the hall; but ere he reached it it opened, and a noisy crowd entered of men, women, boys, and dogs, some bearing great wax candles, some bowls and cups and dishes and trenchers, and some the boards for the meal.

===Chinese===
他话未说完便笑了起来，凯特尔跟着笑，第三个声音也加入了笑。那年轻人也笑，说道："我把我那位亲戚想要的鹿肉带来了；可你们瞧，我送来得太迟了些：不过你拿去吧，凯特尔。我父亲何时从铁砧回来？"

凯特尔道："老爷正埋头打那柄冬至节（Yuletide）的剑呢，这种活计他向来不肯轻易撒手，您是知道的；不过他马上就到，已经传话下来叫我们即刻备晚膳。"

年轻人道："凯特尔，这谷里哪儿来的'老爷'？还是你自己封了几个，非得成天拿来堵我的嘴？"

凯特尔道："长老（the Alderman）之子啊，您叫我凯特尔，这本不是我的名字；那我为何不能叫您'少爷'，这本也不是您的尊号呢？无非是叫惯了，顺口罢了。不过，我这掌锅的伙计来了，婆子和小厮们也来了。您且在炉旁坐下，离他们忙乱的处所远些，我去给您取洗手水来。"

年轻人坐下，凯特尔扛起鹿肉，径往厅堂下端那道门走去；尚未到门下，门已开了，一伙男女老少、连着几条狗，闹哄哄涌将进来，有的擎着粗大蜡烛，有的捧着碗、杯、碟、木盘，有的扛着搭饭桌用的板子。

===Original===
The young man sat quiet smiling and winking his eyes at the sudden flood of light let into the dark place; he took in without looking at this or the other thing the aspect of his Fathers’ House, so long familiar to him; yet tonight he had a pleasure in it above his wont, and in all the stir of the household; for the thought of the wood wherein he had wandered all day yet hung heavy upon him. Came one of the girls and cast fresh brands on the smouldering fire and stirred it into a blaze, and the wax candles were set up on the dais, so that between them and the mew-quickened fire every corner of the hall was bright. As aforesaid it was long and narrow, overarched with stone and not right high, the windows high up under the springing of the roof-arch and all on the side toward the street; over against them were the arches of the shut-beds of the housemates. The walls were bare that evening, but folk were wont to hang up hallings of woven pictures thereon when feasts and high-days were toward; and all along the walls were the tenterhooks for that purpose, and divers weapons and tools were hanging from them here and there. About the dais behind the thwart-table were now stuck for adornment leavy boughs of oak now just beginning to turn with the first frosts. High up on the gable wall above the tenterhooks for the hangings were carven fair imagery and knots and twining stems; for there in the hewn atone was set forth that same image with the rayed head that was on the outside wall, and he was smiting the dragon and slaying him; but here inside the house all this was stained in fair and lively colours, and the sun-like rays round the head of the image were of beaten gold. At the lower end of the hall were two doors going into the butteries, and kitchen, and other out-bowers; and above these doors was a loft upborne by stone pillars, which loft was the sleeping chamber of the goodman of the house; but the outward door was halfway between the said loft and the hearth of the hall.

So the young man took the shoes from his feet and then sat watching the women and lads arraying the boards, till Kettel came again to him with an old woman bearing the ewer and basin, who washed his feet and poured the water over his hands, and gave him the towel with fair-broidered ends to dry them withal.

===Chinese===
那年轻人静静坐着，含笑眯起眼，任那一股突如其来的光亮泻入这暗处；他不必逐一细看，便将这座父祖之宅的景象——久已习见的一切——尽收眼底；然而今夜他对这一切、对满宅的忙乱，却比平日更多一分喜悦；因为那一整日他所流连的林中之事，仍沉沉压在他心头。一个丫鬟走上前来，把新柴添在将熄的火上，拨旺成熊熊火焰；蜡烛也在高台之上点了起来，烛光与复燃之火交相辉映，厅堂每一个角落都亮堂起来。如前所述，此厅长而狭，以石为拱，并不甚高；窗户高高开在屋顶拱起之处之下，尽在临街那一面；与窗相对的，是同宅人等封闭木榻卧间之拱门。那晚墙上空空的，然每逢盛宴佳节将至，众人惯于在其上张挂织造图画之壁帷（hallings）；为这一用途，沿墙处处钉有张布钩，钩上东一把西一件地挂着各种兵器与器具。高台之后、横案之后，如今为点缀起见，插着几枝橡树枝叶，那些叶子刚刚被初霜染上颜色。山墙高处、张布钩之上，镌刻着精美的人物造像、花结与缠枝；因为就在那里，所斫之石上，正刻画着外墙之上那尊同样的、头部放射光芒的造像：他正在击杀那条恶龙，将其诛灭；只不过在屋内这里，这一切都施以明丽鲜活的色彩，而造像头部那如日之光芒，则以锤打之金箔为之。厅堂下端有两道门，通往酒室、厨房及其他别院；门之上方有一阁楼，以石柱支撑，那阁楼便是此宅主人之卧处；而通往外面的大门，则开在此阁楼与厅中炉火之间，正当其中。

于是那年轻人脱去鞋，坐下看那些婆子和小厮们摆桌板，直看到凯特尔又走来，身后跟着一个老妇，捧着水壶水盆；老妇替他洗了脚，又倒水给他盥手，递上一条两端绣有精美花纹的手巾给他擦干。

===Original===
Scarce had he made an end of this ere through the outer door came in three men and a young woman with them; the foremost of these was a man younger by some two years than the first-comer, but so like him that none might misdoubt that he was his brother; the next was an old man with a long white beard, but hale and upright; and lastly came a man of middle-age, who led the young woman by the hand. He was taller than the first of the young men, though the other who entered with him outwent him in height; a stark carle he was, broad across the shoulders, thin in the flank, long-armed and big-handed; very noble and well-fashioned of countenance, with a straight nose and grey eyes underneath a broad brow: his hair grown somewhat scanty was done about with a fillet of golden beads like the young men his sons. For indeed this was their father, and the master of the House.

His name was Iron-face, for he was the deftest of weapon-smiths, and he was the Alderman of the Dalesmen, and well-beloved of them; his kindred was deemed the noblest of the Dale, and long had they dwelt in the House of the Face. But of his sons the youngest, the newcomer, was named Hall-face, and his brother the elder Face-of-god; which name was of old use amongst the kindred, and many great men and stout warriors had borne it aforetime: and this young man, in great love had he been gotten, and in much hope had he been reared, and therefore had he been named after the best of the kindred. But his mother, who was hight the Jewel, and had been a very fair woman, was dead now, and Iron-face lacked a wife.

Face-of-god was well-beloved of his kindred and of all the Folk of the Dale, and he had gotten a to-name, and was called Gold-mane because of the abundance and fairness of his hair.

===Chinese===
他刚刚盥洗完毕，外门便走进来三个男子，还有一个年轻女子相随；当先一人较先前那年轻人约小两岁，然其相貌与他如此相像，无人会怀疑他们是兄弟；其后是一位长须皓白的老人，却矍铄挺拔；最后是一名中年汉子，手牵着那年轻女子。他的身材比那两个年轻人中年长的一个更高，不过随他一同进门的另一人比他还高；他是一条壮健汉子，肩宽、腰窄、臂长、手大；面容极为高贵俊秀，鼻梁挺直，阔眉之下一双灰眼；头发已见稀疏，也如他那两个儿子一般，束着一道金珠额带。原来这正是他们的父亲，此宅之主。

他的名字叫铁面（Iron-face），因为他是兵器匠中第一圣手；他是谷民（the Dalesmen）的长老，深为众人所爱戴；他的宗族被公认为全谷最尊贵之族，久居面神之宅。他的儿子们，最年幼的——即方才进来的那位——名唤厅面（Hall-face），其兄长则名唤面神（Face-of-god）；这名字乃其宗族中沿用已久的旧名，从前许多伟人壮士都曾用过：而这个年轻人，因其得来出于父母深爱，又寄厚望而抚养长大，故而以族中最优秀者之名名之。至于他的母亲，名唤珠玉（the Jewel），生前是个极其美貌的女子，如今已经故去，铁面再未续弦。

面神深为其宗族所爱，亦为全谷之民所爱；他又得了一个别号，因头发既丰且美，人皆唤他金鬃（Gold-mane）。

===Original===
As for the young woman that was led in by Iron-face, she was the betrothed of Face-of-god, and her name was the Bride. She looked with such eyes of love on him when she saw him in the hall, as though she had never seen him before but once, nor loved him but since yesterday; though in truth they had grown up together and had seen each other most days of the year for many years. She was of the kindred with whom the chiefs and great men of the Face mostly wedded, which was indeed far away kindred of them. She was a fair woman and strong: not easily daunted amidst perils she was hardy and handy and light-foot: she could swim as well as any, and could shoot well in the bow, and wield sword and spear: yet was she kind and compassionate, and of great courtesy, and the very dogs and kine trusted in her and loved her. Her hair was dark red of hue, long and fine and plenteous, her eyes great and brown, her brow broad and very fair, her lips fine and red: her cheek not ruddy, yet nowise sallow, but clear and bright: tall she was and of excellent fashion, but well-knit and well-measured rather than slender and wavering as the willow-bough. Her voice was sweet and soft, her words few, but exceeding dear to the listener. In short, she was a woman born to be the ransom of her Folk.

Now as to the names which the menfolk of the Face bore, and they an ancient kindred, a kindred of chieftains, it has been said that in times past their image of the God of the Earth had over his treen face a mask of beaten gold fashioned to the shape of the image; and that when the Alderman of the Folk died, he to wit who served the God and bore on his arm the gold-ring between the people and the altar, this visor or face of God was laid over the face of him who had been in a manner his priest, and therewith he was borne to mound; and the new Alderman and priest had it in charge to fashion a new visor for the God; and whereas for long this great kindred had been chieftains of the people, they had been, and were all so named, that the word Face was ever a part of their names.

===Chinese===
至于那由铁面携进来的年轻女子，她便是面神的未婚妻，名唤新娘（the Bride）。她在厅堂之中一见他，便以那样的爱慕之眼望着他，仿佛平生只见过他一次、昨日才爱上他一般；虽说事实上他们自幼一同长大，一年之中大多数日子都要相见。她出自一个宗族——面神一族的首领和显贵人物大多与之通婚——彼此血缘其实相去甚远。她是个美貌而强健的女子：身处危难之中不轻易气馁，胆大、手巧、步轻；泅水不输任何人，弓箭又射得准，刀枪也使得来：然而她性情仁慈、富于怜悯，举止极为谦和有礼，连狗和牛都信赖她、喜爱她。她的头发是暗赤色，又长又细又丰密；眼睛大而棕褐；额头宽阔而极美；嘴唇纤秀而红润：双颊虽不红，却也绝无病黄之色，而是清亮明净；她身材高挑，体态极佳，然而骨骼匀称、筋骨结实，而非柳枝一般纤弱摇摆。她声音甜美柔和，言语不多，却令听者格外珍重。简而言之，她生来便是要作她族人的赎价之人。

至于面神一族的男子所取之名——他们是一个古老的宗族，一个首领之族——据说从前他们所奉的地神（the God of the Earth）造像，那木雕面容之上覆有一片锤金打造的面具，形状与造像相合；又说每当一族之长老——即那位侍奉此神、臂上戴着联结族人与祭坛之金环的人——去世之时，这片面具，亦即"神之面"，便要覆在某种意义上曾为其祭司的那人面上，随他一同入冢；而新任长老兼祭司则受命为神另制一片新面；因为这一大宗族长久以来皆为族人之首领，所以他们历来、至今仍皆以"面"字入名，使"面"（Face）永为其名号之一部分。

## VI Of Face-of-God and Those Mountain-Dwellers / 六 面神与那些山中居民

===Original===
A yard or two from the threshold Gold-mane hung back a moment, entangled in some such misgiving as a man is wont to feel when he is just about to do some new deed, but is not yet deep in the story; his new friends noted that, for they smiled each in their own way, and the woman drew her hand away from his. Face-of-god held out his still as though to take hers again, and therewithal he changed countenance and said as though he had stayed but to ask that question:

"Tell me thy name, tall man; and thou, fair woman, tell me thine; for how can we talk together else?"

The man laughed outright and said: "The young chieftain thinks that this house also should be his! Nay, young man, I know what is in thy thought, be not ashamed that thou art wary; and be assured! We shall hurt thee no more than thou hast been hurt. Now as to my name; the name that was born with me is gone: the name that was given me hath been taken from me: now I belike must give myself a name, and that shall be Wild-wearer; but it may be that thou thyself shalt one day give me another, and call me Guest."

His sister gazed at him solemnly as he spoke, and Face-of-god beholding her the while, deemed that her beauty grew and grew till she seemed as aweful as a Goddess; and into his mind it came that this over-strong man and over-lovely woman were nought mortal, and they withal dealing with him as father and mother deal with a wayward child: then for a moment his heart failed him, and he longed for the peace of Burgdale, and even the lonely wood. But therewith she turned to him and let her hand come into his again, and looked kindly on him and said: "And as for me, call me the Friend; the name is good and will serve for many things."

===Chinese===
离门槛一两步远的地方，金鬃迟疑了片刻，心中纠缠着一种人将行未行新事时常有的不安——事在将做未做之间，尚未深陷其中；他的新朋友留意到了，因他们各以各的方式笑了笑，那妇人也将手自他手中抽回。面神仍伸着手，似乎想再握她的，随即面色一变，开口说话，仿佛方才停下只为问那一问：

"高大的汉子，告诉我你的名字；美貌娘子，你也告诉我你的；不然我们怎能在一起说话？"

那男子放声大笑，说道："年轻的头人以为这屋子也该归他所有！不，年轻人，我知道你心里想什么，不必以心存戒备为耻；放心吧！我们伤你，不会重过你已被伤过的。至于我的名字：我生下来就有的名字已经没了；人家给我起的名字也被人夺去了；如今我多半得给自己起一个，就叫荒服者（Wild-wearer）；不过也许有朝一日你亲口会给我另起一个，唤我作客。"

他说话之时，他妹妹庄严地注视着他，面神一面端详她，只觉她的美貌越生越盛，直至她看来威严如一位女神；他心中忽生一念：这过于强壮的男子与过于娇美的妇人，绝非尘世凡人，他们待他，正如父母对待任性的孩童一般：一时间他心生怯意，渴望起堡谷的安宁，甚至那寂寞的树林。但她随即转向他，又将手放入他手中，目光和悦地望着他，说道："至于我，叫我友人（the Friend）便是；这名字不错，许多场合都凑合用得着。"

===Original===
He looked down from her face and his eyes lighted on her hand, and when he noted even amid the evening dusk how fair and lovely it was fashioned, and yet as though it were deft in the crafts that the daughters of menfolk use, his fear departed, and the pleasure of his longing filled his heart, and he drew her hand to him to kiss it; but she held it back. Then he said: "It is the custom of the Dale to all women."

So she let him kiss her hand, heeding the kiss nothing, and said soberly:
"Then art thou of Burgdale, and if it were lawful to guess, I would say that thy name is Face-of-god, of the House of the Face."

"Even so it is," said he, "but in the Dale those that love me do mostly call me Gold-mane."

"It is well named," she said, "and seldom wilt thou be called otherwise, for thou wilt be well-beloved. But come in now, Gold-mane, for night is at hand, and here have we meat and lodging such as an hungry and weary man may take; though we be broken people, dwellers in the waste."

Therewith she led him gently over the threshold into the hall, and it seemed to him as if she were the fairest and the noblest of all the Queens of ancient story.

===Chinese===
他的目光自她脸上移下，落在她手上；纵在暮色苍茫之中，他也看出那只手生得何等纤美可爱，却又像是熟谙人间女子那些手工的巧手，他的惧意顿时消散，渴望之乐充满胸怀，便将她的手拉过来想吻；她却缩了回去。他说道："在我们谷里，对所有妇人都是这等礼数。"

于是她任他吻了她的手，对这一吻浑不在意，郑重说道：
"那么你是堡谷之人了；若容许我猜的话，我要说你的名字是面神，面神之宅的面神。"

"正是如此，"他说，"不过在谷里，爱我的人多半叫我金鬃。"

"这名字起得好，"她说，"你将很少被人用别的名字称呼，因你必为人所深爱。且进来吧，金鬃，夜已将至，我们这里备下了一个又饥又疲之人所能将就的饮食和歇处；虽则我们是个破落之人，荒野中的流寓者。"

说罢她引他轻轻跨过门槛，进入厅堂；在他觉来，她仿佛就是古老传说里所有王后之中最美最高贵的那一位。

===Original===
When he was in the house he looked and saw that, rough as it was without it lacked not fairness within. The floor was of hard-trodden earth strewn with pine-twigs, and with here and there brown bearskins laid on it: there was a standing table near the upper end athwart the hall, and a days beyond that, but no endlong table. Gold-mane looked to the shut-beds, and saw that they were large and fair, though there were but a few of them; and at the lower end was a loft for a sleeping chamber dight very fairly with broidered cloths. The hangings on the walls, though they left some places bare which were hung with fresh boughs, were fairer than any he had ever seen, so that he deemed that they must come from far countries and the City of Cities: therein were images wrought of warriors and fair women of old time and their dealings with the Gods and the Giants, and Wondrous wights; and he deemed that this was the story of some great kindred, and that their token and the sign of their banner must needs be the Wood-wolf, for everywhere was it wrought in these pictured webs. Perforce he looked long and earnestly at these fair things, for the hall was not dark yet, because the brands on the hearth were flaming their last, and when Wild-wearer beheld him so gazing, he stood up and looked too for a moment, and then smote his right hand on the hilt of his sword, and turned away and strode up and down the hall as one in angry thought.

===Chinese===
他进了屋一看，只见此屋外面虽粗糙，里面却并不乏美好之处。地面是夯实的泥土，撒着松针，处处铺着几张棕色熊皮：近上首处有一张横放的固定桌案，再往里有一张长榻，却没有纵放的桌案。金鬃看那封闭式木床，见其又大又精美，虽然为数不多；下首处有一阁楼作寝间，以绣花帷帐布置得非常考究。墙上的挂毯虽然有几处空着，挂上了新鲜树枝，却比他平生所见任何挂毯都更华美，使他以为这些东西必来自远方异国与万城之城（the City of Cities）：其中织有古代武士与美女的形像，以及他们与诸神、巨人及种种奇灵异怪的往来；他心想这必是某个大宗族的故事，其族徽与旗帜之记号必是林狼（the Wood-wolf），因这绣帷之上处处都是它的形象。他不由自主地久久凝视这些美好之物，因厅中尚未昏暗，炉中的柴火正燃着最后的光焰；荒服者见他如此凝望，便站起来也看了一会儿，然后用右手在剑柄上一拍，转过身去，在厅中大步踱来踱去，似在恼怒地思索什么。

===Original===
But the woman, even the Friend, bestirred herself for the service of the guest, and brought water for his hands and feet, and when she had washed him, bore him the wine of Welcome and drank to him and bade him drink; and he all the while was shamefaced; for it was to him as if one of the Ladies of the Heavenly Burg were doing him service.
