Then she went away by a door at the lower end of the hall, and Wild-wearer came and sat down by Gold-mane, and fell a-talking with him about the ways of the Dalesmen, and their garths, and the pastures and growths thereof; and what temper the carles themselves were of; which were good men, which were ill, which was loved and which scorned; no otherwise than if he had been the goodman of some neighbouring dale; and Gold-mane told him whatso he knew, for he saw no harm therein.

After a while the outer door opened, and there came in a woman of some five-and-twenty winters, trimly and strongly built; short-skirted she was and clad as a hunter, with a bow in her hand and a quiver at her back: she unslung a pouch, which she emptied at Wild-wearer's feet of a leash of hares and two brace of mountain grouse; of Face-of-god she took but little heed.

===Chinese===
那妇人——即友人——却忙起来侍候客人，端来供他洗手洗足的水，给他洗过之后，又奉上迎客之酒，向他祝饮，请他同喝；他这一程里满心局促；因在他觉来，仿佛是天宫（the Heavenly Burg）的贵妇们在亲自侍候他。随后她从厅下首的一扇门出去了，荒服者过来坐在金鬃身边，与他攀谈起来，问起谷民的生计、他们的院落、牧场和出产；又问那些汉子们性情如何：谁是好人，谁是坏人，谁受人爱戴，谁被人轻看；活脱脱像是一个邻近山谷的当家汉子。金鬃凡自己所知的都告诉了他，因他看不出其中有什么坏处。

过了一会儿，外门开了，走进一个二十五六岁年纪的妇人，身材匀称结实；她着短裙，一身猎人装束，手中持弓，背上挎箭囊：她解下一只口袋，在荒服者脚边倒空，里头是一串野兔和两对山鹑；对面神她几乎不曾留意。

===Original===
Said Wild-wearer: "This is good for tomorrow, not for today; the meat is well-nigh on the board."

Then Gold-mane smiled, for he called to mind his homecoming of yesterday. But the woman said:
"The fault is not mine; she told me of the coming guest but three hours agone."

"Ay?" said Wild-wearer, "she looked for a guest then?"

"Yea, certes," said the woman, "else why went I forth this afternoon, as wearied as I was with yesterday?"

"Well, well," said Wild-wearer, "get to thy due work or go play; I meddle not with meat! and for thee all jests are as bitter earnest."

"And with thee, chief," she said, "it is no otherwise; surely I am made on thy model."

"Thy tongue is longer, friend," said he; "now tarry if thou wilt, and if the supper's service craveth thee not."

She turned away with one keen look at Face-of-god, and departed through the door at the lower end of the hall.

===Chinese===
荒服者说："这是明日的饭菜，不是今日的；今日的肉快要上桌了。"

金鬃笑了，因他想起自己昨日归家的情景。那妇人却说：
"这不是我的过错；她告诉我有客要来，不过才三个时辰之前的事。"

"哦？"荒服者说，"那么她那时就已盼着有客来了？"

"是啊，当然，"那妇人说，"否则我今日下午何必出门，尽管昨日已累成那样？"

"好了，好了，"荒服者说，"做你该做的活去，要么去玩耍；饭食之事我不掺和！至于你，一切玩笑都当作正经话说。"

"头领，"她说，"你也是一般不差；想必我是照着你的样子造出来的。"

"朋友，你的舌头倒更长些，"他说，"你愿意留下就留下吧，只要晚饭的差事用不着你。"

她向面神投来一道锐利的目光，转身自厅下首的门出去了。

===Original===
By this time the hall was dusk, for there were no candles there, and the hearth-fire was but smouldering. Wild-wearer sat silent and musing now, and Face-of-god spake not, for he was deep in wild and happy dreams. At last the lower door opened and the fair woman came into the hall with a torch in either hand, after whom came the huntress, now clad in a dark blue kirtle, and an old woman yet straight and hale; and these twain bore in the victuals and the table-gear. Then the three fell to dighting the board, and when it was all ready, and Gold-mane and Wild-wearer were set down to it, and with them the fair woman and the huntress, the old woman threw good store of fresh brands on the hearth, so that the light shone into every corner; and even therewith the outer door opened, and four more men entered, whereof one was old, but big and stalwarth, the other three young: they were all clad roughly in sheep-brown weed, but had helms upon their heads and spears in their hands and great swords girt to their sides; and they seemed doughty men and ready for battle. One of the young men cast down by the door the carcass of a big-horned mountain sheep, and then they all trooped off to the out-bower by the lower door, and came back presently fairly clad and without their weapons. Wild-wearer nodded to them kindly, and they sat at table paying no more heed to Face-of-god than to cast him a nod for salutation.

Then said the old woman to them: "Well, lads, have ye been doing or sleeping?"

"Sleeping, mother," said one of the young men, "as was but due after last night was, and tomorrow shall be."

Said the huntress: "Hold thy peace, Wood-wise, and let thy tongue help thy teeth to deal with thy meat; for this is not the talking hour."

"Nay, Bow-may," said another of the swains, "since here is a new man, now is the time to talk to him."

Said the huntress: "'Tis thine hands that talk best, Wood-wont; it is not they that shall bring thee to shame."

Spake the third: "What have we to do with shame here, far away from dooms and doomers, and elders, and wardens, and guarded castles? If the new man listeth to speak, let him speak; or to fight, then let him; it shall ever be man to man."

Then spake the old woman: "Son Wood-wicked, hold thy peace, and forget the steel that ever eggeth thee on to draw."

Therewith she set the last matters on the board, while the three swains sat and eyed Gold-mane somewhat fiercely, now that words had stirred them, and he had sat there saying nothing, as one who was better than they, and contemned them; but now spake Wild-wearer:

===Chinese===
此时厅中已昏暗，因这里不点蜡烛，炉火只剩一缕余烬。荒服者静坐着沉思，面神也不开口，因他正沉浸于狂乱而欢愉的梦境之中。终于下首的门开了，那美貌妇人双手各擎一支火把走入厅中，她身后跟着那女猎手——此刻已换上一袭深蓝长裙——还有一个老妇，身子骨仍挺直硬朗；这两人端进了饭菜和桌上的器具。于是三人动手摆桌，等一切就绪，金鬃与荒服者已入座，与她们同坐的还有那美貌妇人和女猎手，老妇便向炉中添上一大把新柴，使光照亮厅中每个角落；正在此时，外门开了，又进来四个男子，其中一个年迈，却身材魁梧健壮，另外三个年轻：他们都粗粗地穿着羊褐之衣，头上却戴着盔，手中持着矛，腰间佩着大剑；看样子都是骁勇之士，蓄势待战。一个年轻人把一只大角野山羊的尸首丢在门边，随后他们都鱼贯进入下首门边的偏院，不多时换了像样的衣裳出来，兵器也卸下了。荒服者和颜悦色地向他们点点头，他们便在桌边坐下，对面神只是点头致意，并不多加理会。

于是老妇对他们说："怎么样，小伙子们，你们是干活了还是睡觉了？"

"睡觉了，母亲，"一个年轻人说，"昨晚既然那样，明天又要那样，本就该睡嘛。"

女猎手说："住嘴，林慧（Wood-wise），让你的舌头帮着牙齿去对付饭菜吧；现在不是说话的时候。"

"不然，弓女（Bow-may），"另一个小伙子说，"既然这里有位新人，现在正是与他说话的时候。"

女猎手说："最会说话的是你的双手，林习（Wood-wont）；给你招来羞辱的不会是它们。"

第三个开口道："在这里，我们与羞辱有何相干？这里远离裁断与裁断者，远离长老、守事，也没有设防的城堡。那新人若想说话，就让他说；想打架，就让他打；永远是人对人。"

老妇说道："林顽（Wood-wicked）我儿，住嘴，忘了那总是怂恿你拔出来的刀子吧。"

她一边把最后几样饭菜端上桌，那三个小伙子坐着，目光相当凌厉地打量金鬃——方才几句话已把他们撩拨起来，而他坐在那里一言不发，仿佛比他们都强、瞧不起他们似的；此时荒服者开口了：

===Original===
"Whoso hungreth let him eat! Whoso would slumber, let him to bed. But he who would bicker, it must needs be with me. Here is a man of the Dale, who hath sought the wood in peace, and hath found us. His hand is ready and his heart is guileless: if ye fear him, run away to the wood, and come back when he is gone; but none shall mock him while I sit by: now, lads, be merry and blithe with the guest."

Then the young men greeted Gold-mane, and the old man said: "Art thou of Burgstead? then wilt thou be of the House of the Face, and thy name will be Face-of-god; for that man is called the fairest of the Dale, and there shall be none fairer than thou."

Face-of-god laughed and said: "There be but few mirrors in Burgdale, and I have no mind to journey west to the cities to see what manner of man I be: that were ill husbandry. But now I have heard the names of the three swains, tell me thy name, father!"

Spake the huntress: "This is my father's brother, and his name is Wood-father; or ye shall call him so: and I am called Bow-may because I shoot well in the bow: and this old carline is my eme's wife, and now belike my mother, if I need one. But thou, fair-faced Dalesman, little dost thou need a mirror in the Dale so long as women abide there; for their faces shall be instead of mirrors to tell thee whether thou be fair and lovely."

===Chinese===
"谁饿了就吃！谁想睡就去睡。但谁要寻衅，非得跟我较量不可。这里有一位谷中之民，为寻安宁而入林，遇到了我们。他出手在即，心怀坦荡：你们若怕他，就逃到林子里去，等他走了再回来；但我坐在这里时，谁也不许嘲弄他：来吧，小伙子们，与客人一同欢畅。"

年轻人便向金鬃见礼，那老者说："你是堡镇人？那你必是面神之宅的人，你的名字必是面神；因那人被称作全谷最美之男子，而你将是无人能比的美男子。"

面神笑道："堡谷里镜子本就少，我也无心远行西去诸城，看看自己是个什么样的人：那可是不善持家。不过如今我已听到这三个小伙子的名字，老人家，告诉我你的名字吧！"

女猎手说："这是我父亲的兄弟，他的名字是林父（Wood-father）；或者说你们可以这么叫他：我因为弓射得准，唤作弓女：这位老妪是我舅母，如今若是需要，也算我的母亲了。至于你，面容俊美的谷民，只要谷中还有妇人在，你就几乎用不着镜子；因她们的脸便是镜子，足以告诉你，你是不是俊美可爱。"

===Original===
Thereat they all laughed and fell to their victual, which was abundant, of wood-venison and mountain-fowl, but of bread was no great plenty; wine lacked not, and that of the best; and Gold-mane noted that the cups and the apparel of the horns and mazers were not of gold nor gilded copper, but of silver; and he marvelled thereat, for in the Dale silver was rare.

So they ate and drank, and Gold-mane looked ever on the Friend, and spake much with her, and he deemed her friendly indeed, and she seemed most pleased when he spoke best, and led him on to do so. Wild-wearer was but of few words, and those somewhat harsh; yet was he as a man striving to be courteous and blithe; but of the others Bow-may was the greatest speaker.

Wild-wearer called healths to the Sun, and the Moon, and the Hosts of Heaven; to the Gods of the Earth; to the Wood-wights; and to the Guest. Other healths also he called, the meaning of which was dark to Gold-mane; to wit, the Jaws of the Wolf; the Silver Arm; the Red Hand; the Golden Bushel; and the Ragged Sword. But when he asked the Friend concerning these names what they might signify, she shook her head and answered not.

At last Wild-wearer cried out: "Now, lads, the night weareth and the guest is weary: therefore whoso of you hath in him any minstrelsy, now let him make it, for later on it shall be over-late."

Then arose Wood-wont and went to his shut-bed and groped therein, and took from out of it a fiddle in its case; and he opened the case and drew from it a very goodly fiddle, and he stood on the floor amidst of the hall and Bow-may his cousin with him; and he laid his bow on the fiddle and woke up song in it, and when it was well awake she fell a-singing, and he to answering her song, and at the last all they of the house sang together; and this is the meaning of the words which they sang:

===Chinese===
众人都笑了，便大快朵颐。食物丰盛，有林中野味和山禽，只是面包不多；酒不缺，且都是上等好酒；金鬃留意到，那些杯盏和角杯、木碗的配饰，不是金的，也不是镀金的铜，而是银的；他暗暗称奇，因在谷中，银是稀有之物。

于是他们吃着喝着，金鬃目光不离友人，与她说个不停，只觉她确是友善；她说得最高兴的时候，正是他谈吐最精彩之时，便引着他多讲。荒服者话不多，说话时语调略显生硬；却像个极力要做到有礼而和悦的人；至于其他人里，数弓女话最多。

荒服者举杯祝饮，先祝太阳、月亮和天上的万宿；祝诸地神；祝林中精怪（the Wood-wights）；并祝客人。他还祝了别的酒，那些名目金鬃听不出含义：即狼之颚、银臂、红手、金斛、缺锋剑。他问友人这些名字作何解，她只是摇头，并不作答。

终于荒服者高声道："好了，小伙子们，夜渐深，客人也倦了：因此你们当中肚里有点音律的，这就拿出来吧，再迟就来不及了。"

于是林习起身，走到他的封闭式木床边，在里面摸索了一阵，从里头取出一把装在匣中的提琴；他打开匣子，从里头抽出一把极好的提琴，便站在厅堂中央的地板上，他的表妹弓女也与他同立；他把弓搭在琴上，唤醒了琴中之歌，待琴彻底醒转，她便唱了起来，他则以琴音相和，到后来满屋子的人都齐声同唱；他们所唱的歌词，其意如下：

===Original===
Face-of-god thought the song goodly, but to the others it was well known. Then said Wood-father:
"O foster-son, thy foster-brother hath sung well for a wood abider; but we are deeming that his singing shall be but as a starling to a throstle matched against thy new-come guest. Therefore, Dalesman, sing us a song of the Dale, and if ye will, let it be of gardens and pleasant houses of stone, and fair damsels therein, and swains with them who toil not overmuch for a scant livelihood, as do they of the waste, whose heads may not be seen in the Holy Places."

Said Gold-mane: "Father, it is ill to set the words of a lonely man afar from his kin against the song that cometh from the heart of a noble house; yet may I not gainsay thee, but will sing to thee what I may call to mind, and it is called the Song of the Ford."

Therewith he sang in a sweet and clear voice: and this is the meaning of his words:

===Chinese===
面神觉得那歌甚美，其他人却都很熟悉。林父说道：
"义儿啊，你的义兄以一个住林子的人而论，唱得已算不错；但我们要说，他的歌喉与你这位新来的客人相比，不过是椋鸟比鸫鸟罢了。所以，谷民，给我们唱一支谷里的歌吧；你若愿意，不妨唱那花园与悦目的石头宅子，唱其中的美貌少女，以及陪伴她们的小伙子——他们不像荒野中的人那样，为微薄的生计过度劳苦，那些人的头颅，在圣地之中是见不到的。"

金鬃说："老伯，把一个远离亲族的孤身人之歌，去和高门大第发自内心的歌相比，本是不妥；然而我不能驳你，就把我能记起的唱给你听吧，这首歌叫做《渡口之歌》（the Song of the Ford）。"

于是他以清亮悦耳的嗓音唱起来；他所唱的歌词，其意如下：

===Original===
> In hay-tide, through the day newborn,
 
 Across the meads we come;
 
 Our hauberks brush the blossomed corn
 
 A furlong short of home.
> Ere yet the gables we behold
 
 Forth flasheth the red sun,
 
 And smites our fallow helms and cold
 
 Though all the fight be done.
> In this last mend of mowing-grass
 
 Sweet doth the clover smell,
 
 Crushed neath our feet red with the pass
 
 Where hell was blent with hell.
> And now the willowy stream is nigh,
 
 Down wend we to the ford;
 
 No shafts across its fishes fly,
 
 Nor flasheth there a sword.
> But lo! what gleameth on the bank
 
 Across the water wan,
 
 As when our blood the mouse-ear drank
 
 And red the river ran?
> Nay, hasten to the ripple clear,
 
 Look at the grass beyond!
 
 Lo ye the dainty band and dear
 
 Of maidens fair and fond!
> Lo how they needs must take the stream!
 
 The water hides their feet;
 
 On fair kind arms the gold doth gleam,
 
 And midst the ford we meet.
> Up through the garden two and two,
 
 And on the flowers we drip;
 
 Their wet feet kiss the morning dew
 
 As lip lies close to lip.
> Here now we sing; here now we stay:
 
 By these grey walls we tell
 
 The love that lived from out the fray,
 
 The love that fought and fell.

===Chinese===
> 芟草时节新日升，
 
 我等横越草甸行；
 
 锁子甲拂花麦穗，
 
 离家仅余一浪程。
> 山墙未及抬眼望，
 
 红日破云猝然出；
 
 光照暗褐寒铁盔，
 
 纵然干戈全已平。
> 此间刈草地尽头，
 
 三叶草香何芬芳；
 
 踏碎于染血之足下，
 
 彼处地狱与地狱交融。
> 柳荫溪流今已近，
 
 我等下至浅滩前；
 
 箭不越鱼群而飞，
 
 剑不于此而闪光。
> 然则看哪！对岸何物闪亮，
 
 越过那暗淡之流水？
 
 犹如鼠耳草饮我等之血，
 
 当年河水赤红奔流？
> 速速走向清涟旁，
 
 且看彼岸之草地！
 
 看这一队娇美人，
 
 温婉秀丽之少女！
> 看她不得不涉水！
 
 溪水掩过她双足；
 
 秀臂之上金光闪，
 
 渡口中流我等相逢。
> 穿过花园成双对，
 
 水珠滴落繁花上；
 
 湿足亲吻清晨露，
 
 如同嘴唇紧相依。
> 此时此地我等歌吟；此时此地我等驻留：
 
 倚此灰墙，我等讲述
 
 那自战火中存留之爱，
 
 那奋战过、倾覆过之爱。

===Original===
When he was done they all said that he had sung well, and that the song was sweet. Yet did Wild-wearer smile somewhat; and Bow-may said outright: "Soft is the song, and hath been made by lads and minstrels rather than by warriors."

"Nay, kinswoman," said Wood-father, "thou art hard to please; the guest is kind, and hath given us that I asked for, and I give him all thanks therefor."

Face-of-god smiled, but he heeded little what they said, for as he sang he had noted that the Friend looked kindly on him; and he thought he saw that once or twice she put out her hand as if to touch him, but drew it back again each time. She spake after a little and said:
"Here now hath been a stream of song running betwixt the Mountain and the Dale even as doth a river; and this is good to come between our dreams of what hath been and what shall be." Then she turned to Gold-mane, and said to him scarce loud enough for all to hear:
"Herewith I bid thee good night, O Dalesman; and this other word I have to thee: heed not what befalleth in the night, but sleep thy best, for nought shall be to thy scathe. And when thou wakest in the morning, if we are yet here, it is well; but if we are not, then abide us no long while, but break thy fast on the victual thou wilt find upon the board, and so depart and go thy ways home. And yet thou mayst look to it to see us again before thou diest."

Therewith she held out her hand to him, and he took it and kissed it; and she went to her chamber-aloft at the lower end of the hall. And when she was gone, once more he had a deeming of her that she was of the kindred of the Gods. At her departure him-seemed that the hall grew dull and small and smoky, and the night seemed long to him and doubtful the coming of the day.

===Chinese===
他唱完之后，众人都说他唱得好，歌也动听。荒服者却微微一笑；弓女直说道："这歌软绵绵的，是小伙子和吟游诗人所作，而非战士所作。"

"不然，侄女，"林父说，"你可真难讨好；客人厚道，把我所要的给了我，我向他致以全心的感谢。"

面神笑了笑，对他们的话并不甚在意，因他唱歌时已留意到友人慈和地望着他；他仿佛看见她有一两次伸出手来想碰碰他，每次又都缩了回去。过了一会儿她说道：
"此时此地，一道歌之溪流在山与谷之间流淌，正如同一条河；这正宜横亘在我们对往昔与来日的种种梦想之间。"她转向金鬃，对他说出几句话，声音微弱得并非人人都能听见：
"谷民啊，我在此向你道晚安；我还有一句话给你：夜里无论发生何事，都不要在意，只管尽力安睡，因任何事都不会伤你。明日你醒来之时，若我们仍在此处，那很好；若我们不在了，你不必久等，吃些你将在桌上找到的饭菜，便动身回家去吧。然而你大可盼望，在你死之前，还会再见到我们。"

说完她向他伸出手，他接过来吻了一下；她便走向厅下首的阁楼寝间。她走之后，他再次觉得她必是神祇一族。她一离开，他只觉这厅堂变得昏暗、狭小、烟雾缭绕；夜在他觉来格外漫长，而天明之至又甚可疑。

## XLV Of Face-of-God’s Onslaught / 四十五 论面神之猛攻

===Original===
Now the banners of the Wolf flapped and rippled over the heads of the Woodlanders and the Men of the Wolf; and the men shot all they might, nor took heed now to cover themselves against the shafts of the Dusky Men. As for these, for all they were so many, their arrow-shot was no great matter, for they were in very evil order, as has been said; and moreover, their rage was so great to come to handy strokes with these foemen, that some of them flung away their bows to brandish the axe or the sword. Nevertheless were some among the kindred hurt or slain by their arrows.

Now stood Face-of-god with the foremost; and from where he stood he could see somewhat of the battle of the Dalesmen, and he wotted that it was thriving; therefore he looked before him and close around him, and noted what was toward there. The space betwixt the houses and the break of the bent was crowded with the fury of the Dusky Men tossing their weapons aloft, crying to each other and at the kindred, and here and there loosing a bowstring on them; but whatever was their rage they might not come a many together past a line within ten fathom of the bent’s end; for three hundred of the best of bowmen were shooting at them so ceaselessly that no Dusky man was safe of any bare place of his body, and they fell over one another in that penfold of slaughter, and for all their madness did but little.

Yet was the heart of the War-leader troubled; for he wotted that it might not last forever, and there seemed no end to the throng of murder-carles; and the time would come when the arrow-shot would be spent, and they must needs come to handy strokes, and that with so many.

===Chinese===
且说狼族之旌旗，于林中之民与狼之民头顶之上猎猎翻卷；众人竭力放箭，此时已不复顾掩蔽自身、以避黝暗人之矢。至于黝暗人，人数虽众，其箭却不足为患，盖因其阵大乱，一如前述；况且他们急于近身搏杀，怒不可遏，有些人索性抛下弓，去挥舞斧头或刀剑。纵然如此，族中仍有些人被其箭所伤、或被射杀。

面神立于最前列；从他所立之处，可隐约窥见谷民那一边的战况，他知其战况顺遂；于是他环顾身前与近旁，留意彼处情势。屋舍与山坡尽头之间那片空地，挤满了狂暴的黝暗人，他们高擎兵刃，彼此呼喝、向族众叫骂，间或朝他们放出一弦之箭；然其狂怒无论几何，终不能成群结队越过距山坡尽头十寻之内的一条界线；盖因三百名最精良之弓手正向他们不停放箭，黝暗人身上但凡有一寸皮肉暴露，便无安全可言；他们在这屠戮之圈栏中相互压叠、东倒西歪，任凭如何癫狂，亦无所成。

然战首之心，实为忧虑；盖知此景必不能持久，而那帮嗜杀之徒又似源源不绝、不见尽头；终有一刻箭矢耗尽，彼等必须近身搏杀，且是以寡敌众。

===Original===
Now a voice spake to him as he gazed with knitted brows and careful heart on that turmoil of battle:

“What now hast thou done with the Sun-beam, and where is her brother? Is the Chief of the Wolf skulking when our work is so heavy? And thou meseemeth art over-late on the field: the mowing of this meadow is no sluggard’s work.”

He turned and beheld Bow-may, and gazed on her face for a moment, and saw her eyes how they glittered, and how the pommels of her cheeks were burning red and her lips dry and grey; but before he answered he looked all round about to see what was to note; and he touched Bow-may on the shoulder and pointed to down below where a man of the Felons had just come out of the court of one of the houses: a man taller than most, very gaily arrayed, with gilded scales all over him, so that, with his dark face and blue eyes, he looked like some strange dragon. Bow-may spake not, but stamped her foot with anger. Yet if her heart were hot, her hand was steady; for she notched a shaft, and just as the Dusky Chief raised his axe and brandished it aloft, she loosed, and the shaft flew and smote the felon in the armpit and the default of the armour, and he fell to earth. But even as she loosed, Face-of-god cried out in a loud voice:

“O lads of battle! shoot close and all together. Tarry not, tarry not! for we need a little time ere sword meets sword, and the others of the kindreds are at work!”

===Chinese===
正他双眉紧锁、忧心忡忡，凝视那一片战阵纷乱之际，忽有一声音对他道：

"你把日光弄到哪儿去了，她兄长又在哪里？我等战事如此吃紧，狼族之酋长莫非在藏拙躲懒？我看你上阵也太迟了些：这片草场，可不是懒汉割得的。"

他转身，见是弓娥，端详其面容片刻，但见其双目炯炯生光，两颊颧骨赤红如火，唇干而发灰；然他未即作答，先环顾四周，看有何可记之事；他触了触弓娥的肩，指向下方——只见恶徒中有一人正从一座屋舍的院落里走出来：此人高出侪辈，装束极是华丽，通体覆着鎏金鳞甲，配上其黝黑之面庞与碧蓝之双目，望去犹如一条奇异之蛟龙。弓娥不语，只气得跺脚。然她心虽火急，手却稳如磐石；她搭上一箭，正当那黝暗酋长高举战斧、欲作挥舞之时，她一松弦，箭矢飞去，正中那恶徒腋下甲胄缺豁之处，那人应声倒地。然就在她放箭之际，面神亦高声呼喝：

"众位战郎！箭要密、要齐发。莫停，莫停！我们只需再撑片刻，便到剑刃相交之时，其余各族的人马也已动手了！"

===Original===
But Bow-may turned round to him and said: “Wilt thou not answer me? Where is thy kindness gone?”

Even as she was speaking she had notched and loosed another shaft, speaking as folk do who turn from busy work at loom or bench.

Then said Face-of-god: “Shoot on, sister Bow-may! The Sun-beam is gone with her brother, and he is with the Men of the Face.”

He broke off here, for a man fell beside him hurt in the neck, and Face-of-god took his bow from his hands and shot a shaft, while one of the women who had been hurt also tended the newly-wounded man. Then Face-of-god went on speaking:

===Chinese===
弓娥却回过头来道："你不答我么？你那点情谊都到哪里去了？"

她一边说话，一边已搭好一箭、又放出一箭，那神态就像人从织机或工案上忙活里转过身来说话一般。

面神这才道："只管射罢，弓娥妹妹！日光已随她兄长去了，他和面神之族在一起。"

他说到这里一顿，因身旁有一人颈中挂彩倒下，面神便从他手中取过弓，发了一箭，另有一名同样负伤的妇人则去照看那新伤者。随后面神接着道：

===Original===
“She was unwilling to go, but Folk-might and I constrained her; for we knew that this is the most perilous place of the battle﻿—hah! see those three felons, Bow-may! they are aiming hither.”

And again he loosed and Bow-may also, but a shaft rattled on his helm withal and another smote a Woodlander beside him, and pierced through the calf of his leg, as he turned and stooped to take fresh arrows from a sheaf that lay there; but the carle took it by the notch and the point, and brake it and drew it out, and then stood up and went on shooting. And Face-of-god spake again:

“Folk-might skulketh not; nor the Men of the Vine, and the Sickle, and the Face, nor the Shepherd-Folk: soon shall they be making our work easy to us, if we can hold our own till then. They are on the other roads that lead into the square. Now suffer me, and shoot on!”

===Chinese===
"她本不愿去，是民强与我强把她劝走的；因为我们知道，此处乃是整场战事最凶险之地——咦！弓娥你看，那三个恶徒！他们正朝这边瞄准呢。"

他又放一箭，弓娥亦然，但一箭当啷击中其头盔，另一箭则射中他身旁一名林中之民——那人正转身俯身，要去取搁在地上的一捆新箭，箭便贯穿其小腿肚；然那汉子一把捏住箭尾与箭镞，将箭折断拔出，随即站起身来继续放箭。面神又道：

"民强并未藏拙；葡萄之族、镰刀之族、面神之族的人，以及牧羊之民，亦皆不然：只要我等能撑到那时，他们很快便会替我们把这一桩难活变得轻松。他们都在另外那几条通往广场的路上。且容我片刻，你只管射罢！"

===Original===
Therewith he looked round about him, and he saw on the left hand that all was quiet; and before him was the confused throng of the Dusky Men trampling their own dead and wounded, and not able as yet to cross that death-line of the arrow so near to them. But on his right hand he saw how they of the kindreds held them firm on the way. Then for a moment of time he considered and thought, till him-seemed he could see the whole battle yet to be foughten; and his face flushed, and he said sharply: “Bow-may, abide here and shoot, and show the others where to shoot, while the arrows hold out; but we will go further for a while, and ye shall follow when we have made the rent great enough.”

She turned to him and said: “Why art thou not more joyous? thou art like an host without music or banners.”

“Nay,” said he, “heed not me, but my bidding!”

===Chinese===
说罢他四面环顾，见左手一侧一切平静；身前则是乱作一团的黝暗人群，践踏着自家的死伤之躯，尚不能越过近在咫尺的那条箭雨死线。而右手一侧，他看见族众所把守的那条路上阵脚稳固。于是他凝神片刻，细作筹谋，直如能将尚未打响的整场战事尽收眼底；他面上一红，厉声道："弓娥，你留在此处放箭，并指给旁人该射向何处，只要箭未用尽便不停手；我等要往前去一阵，待我们把缺口撕得够大，你们再跟上来。"

她转身对他道："你为何这般不快活？你活像一支没有乐声、没有旗帜的人马。"

"不然，"他道，"别管我，听我号令便是！"

===Original===
She said hastily: “I think I shall die here; since for all we have shot we minish them nowise. Now kiss me this once amidst the battle, and say farewell.”

He said: “Nay, nay; it shall not go thus. Abide a little while, and thou shalt see all this tangle open, as the sun cleaveth the clouds on the autumn morning. Yet lo thou! since thou wilt have it so.”

And he bent forward and kissed her face, and now the tears ran over it, and she said smiling somewhat: “Now is this more than I looked for, whatso may betide.”

But while she was yet speaking he cried in a great voice:

===Chinese===
她急道："我想我必死于此处了；因我们射了这许久，他们毫不见减少。且在这战阵之中吻我这一回，作个别罢。"

他道："不，不；事不至如此。且再忍片刻，你便可见这一团乱麻豁然洞开，一如秋日清晨，太阳劈开云层。然既然你执意如此——看罢！"

他便俯身吻了她的脸，此时泪水正流过那张脸，她微微笑道："如今这一下，倒出乎我所望了，任它后事如何。"

然她话犹未了，他已高声呼喝：

===Original===
“Ye who have spent your shot, or have nigh spent it, to axe and sword, and follow me to clear the ground ’twixt the bent and the halls. Let each help each, but throng not each other. Shoot wisely, ye bowmen, and keep our backs clear of the foe. On, on! for the Burg and the Face, for the Burg and the Face!”

Therewith he leapt down the steep of the hill, bounding like the hart, with Dale-warden naked in his hand; and they that followed were two score and ten; and the arrows of their bowmen rained over their heads on the Dusky Men, as they smote down the first of the foemen, and the others shrieked and shrank from them, or turned on them smiting wildly and desperately.

But Face-of-god swept round the great sword and plunged into that sea of turmoil and noise and evil sights and savours, and even therewith he heard clearly a voice that said: “Gold-ring, I am hurt; take my bow a while!” and knew it for Bow-may’s; but it came to his ears like the song of a bird without meaning; for it was as if his life were changed at once; and in a minute or two he had cut thrice with the edge and thrust twice with the point, eager, but clear-eyed and deft; and he saw as in a picture the foe before him, and the grey roofs of Silverstead, and through the gap in them the tops of the blue ridges far aloof. And now had three fallen before him, and they feared him, and turned on him, and smote so many together that their strokes crossed each other, and one warded him from the other; and he laughed aloud and shielded himself, and drave the point of Dale-warden amidst the tangle of weapons through the open mouth of a captain of the Felons, and slashed a cheek with a backstroke, and swept round the edge to his right hand and smote off a blue-eyed snub-nosed head; and therewith a poleaxe smote him on the left side of his helm, so that he tottered; but he swung himself round, and stood stark and upright, and gave a short hack with the edge, keeping Dale-warden well in hand, and a gold-clad felon, a champion of them, and their tallest on the ground, fell aback, his throat gaping more than the mouth of him.

===Chinese===
"箭已用尽或所剩无几的，持斧提刀，随我冲下去，把山坡与厅堂之间的地面扫荡干净！彼此相援，但莫相互拥挤。弓手们放箭要有章法，看好我等的后背，莫让敌人近身。冲，冲！为堡镇与面神，为堡镇与面神！"

说罢他便纵身跃下山坡，如雄鹿般腾越，手中谷卫出鞘寒光凛凛；随他冲下者，共五十人；其弓手之箭如雨倾泻，越过他们头顶，直落黝暗人头上；他们一举劈倒最前之敌，余者尖叫着退缩，或狂乱绝望地转身反扑。

面神将那柄大剑横扫一圈，纵身投入那一片喧嚣、恶象、恶声、恶味交煎的人海之中；就在此时，他清清楚楚听得一声音道："金环，我挂彩了，替我执弓片刻！"他辨出那是弓娥的声音；然那声音入耳，却如鸟啼一般空无意义；盖因他这一刻仿佛整个人脱胎换骨；一瞬之间，他便以刃三劈、以尖两刺，激昂而不失清明，身手矫捷；眼前之敌、银镇的灰色屋顶、以及自屋顶缺口处望见的远处青蓝山脊之巅，皆如画图般映现于目前。转瞬之间，已有三人倒于其前；敌人惧他，群起围攻，然挥击者太多，兵刃彼此交错，反互为遮挡；他大笑一声，举盾一格，将谷卫之尖锋自那一片兵刃丛中、直送入一名恶徒头目张开之口，又以回手剑划开一面颊，再横转剑锋向右一扫，斩下一颗蓝眼塌鼻的首级；便在此时，一柄长斧劈中他头盔左侧，他身形一晃；然他猛地一旋身，稳稳挺立如初，握紧谷卫，反手以刃短促一斫，一名身披金甲的恶徒——彼辈中之悍将、亦是此地最高大者——仰面便倒，其喉所绽之口，比他本来的嘴还大。

===Original===
Then Face-of-god shouted and waved Dale-warden aloft to the Banner of the Wolf that floated behind and above him, and he cried out: “As I have promised so have I done!” And he looked about, and beheld how valiantly his fellows had been doing; for before him now was a space of earth with no man standing on his feet thereon, like the swathe of the mowers of June; and beyond that was the crowd of the Dusky Men wavering like the tall grass abiding the scythe.

But a minute, and they fell to casting at Face-of-god and his fellows spears and knives and shields and whatsoever would fly; and a spear smote him on the breast, but entered not; and a bossed shield fell over his face withal, and a plummet of sling-lead smote his helm, and he fell to earth; but leapt up again straightway, and heard as he arose a great shout close to him, and a shrill cry, and lo! at his left side Bow-may, her sword in her hand, and the hand red with blood from a shaft-graze on her wrist, and a white cloth stained with blood about her neck; and on his right side Wood-wise bearing the banner and crying the Wolf-whoop; for the whole company was come down from the slope and stood around him.

Then for a little while was there such a stilling of the tumult about him there, that he heard great and glad cries from the Road of the South of “The Burg and the Steer! The Dale and the Bridge! The Dale and the Bull!” And thereafter a terrible great shrieking cry, and a huge voice that cried: “Death, death, death to the Dusky Men!” And thereafter again fierce cries and great tumult of the battle.

===Chinese===
面神一声大喝，将谷卫向身后上方那面飘扬的狼族旗帜挥舞高举，高呼道："我所许之诺，今已践之！"他四下一看，只见同伴们战绩何等彪炳；盖因他面前此刻已是一整片地上空无一人伫立，犹如六月刈草人割后之草痕；再过去，便是那群黝暗人，进退踯躅，如高草之待刈。

不过一刻，敌人便朝面神及其同伙投掷起枪、刀、盾，以及一切可飞掷之物；一杆枪刺中其胸，却未刺入；一面凸心盾随之扣落其面，一枚弹弓铅丸又击中其头盔，他应声倒地；然他一跃复起，起身之际，听得近旁一声大喊、一声锐啸；看哪！其左手边是弓娥，手持利剑，手腕为箭矢擦伤，鲜血淋漓，颈间围着一块染血的白布；右手边则是林智擎着旗帜，口中高呼狼嚎；原来全队人马都已自山坡下来，立在他周围。

其后片刻之间，他周遭那一片喧嚣竟平息下来，使他得以听见南路方向传来高亢欢腾的呼喊："堡镇与壮牛！堡谷与桥！堡谷与公牛！"紧接着是一声可怖的尖嘶，与一个宏亮的嗓音高喊："死，死，黝暗人皆死！"其后又是激烈的呐喊与一片大战的喧嚣。

===Original===
Then Face-of-god shook Dale-warden in the air, and strode forward fiercely, but not speedily, and the whole company went foot for foot along with him; and as he went, would he or would he not, song came into his mouth, a song of the meadows of the Dale, even such as this:

===Chinese===
面神将谷卫向空中一振，大步向前，气势汹汹却不疾不徐，全队人马亦与他齐步并肩而行；他一边走，一首歌不论其愿与不愿，已涌上喉间，一首关于谷中草甸的歌，其辞如是：

===Original===
> The wheat is done blooming and rust’s on the sickle,
 And green are the meadows grown after the scythe.
 Come, hands for the dance! For the toil hath been mickle,
 And ’twixt haysel and harvest ’tis time to be blithe.
> And what shall the tale be now dancing is over,
 And kind on the meadow sits maiden by man,
 And the old man bethinks him of days of the lover,
 And the warrior remembers the field that he wan?
> Shall we tell of the dear days wherein we are dwelling,
 The best days of our Mother, the cherishing Dale,
 When all round about us the summer is telling,
 To ears that may hearken, the heart of the tale?
> Shall we sing of these hands and these lips that caress us,
 And the limbs that sun-dappled lie light here beside,
 When still in the morning they rise but to bless us,
 And oft in the midnight our footsteps abide?
> O nay, but to tell of the fathers were better,
 And of how we were fashioned from out of the earth;
 Of how the once lowly spurned strong at the fetter;
 Of the days of the deeds and beginning of mirth.
> And then when the feast-tide is done in the morning,
 Shall we whet the grey sickle that bideth the wheat,
 Till wan grow the edges, and gleam forth a warning
 Of the field and the fallow where edges shall meet.
> And when cometh the harvest, and hook upon shoulder
 We enter the red wheat from out of the road,
 We shall sing, as we wend, of the bold and the bolder,
 And the Burg of their building, the beauteous abode.
> As smiteth the sickle amid the sun’s burning
 We shall sing how the sun saw the token unfurled,
 When forth fared the Folk, with no thought of returning,
 In the days when the Banner went wide in the world.

===Chinese===
> 麦既扬花，镰上已生锈，
 新刈之草场，碧色转深。
 来罢，携手起舞！劳作何其繁重，
 介于割草与秋获之间，正当快意舒心。
> 舞蹈既罢，将述何事？
 草甸之上，少女伴少年而坐；
 老翁回首，少年相恋之时，
 武士追忆，昔日奏凯之野？
> 当述吾辈居此之良辰？
 吾母——抚育吾辈之谷——之盛世？
 夏日四围，皆向吾辈低诉，
 凡有耳能听者，皆悉此中之情？
> 当歌此双手、此亲抚我之唇？
 当歌卧于身旁、日光斑驳之肢体？
 彼等晨起，唯为祝佑吾辈，
 夜半亦常相随吾人之足迹？
> 不，不！宜述先祖之事，
 宜述吾辈如何自地中塑成；
 昔日卑微之人，奋力踹断枷锁；
 宜述丰功之日、欢乐之初生。
> 及至清晨，宴饮既毕，
 吾辈当磨那待麦之青镰，
 直至刃口苍淡，闪现警兆——
 警兆那刀锋将相交之田与茬。
> 待到秋收，镰钩上肩，
 吾辈自路畔步入红麦之中，
 一路所歌，皆勇者与更勇者之事，
 并吾辈所筑之堡——那华美之居。
> 一如镰挥于烈日之下，
 吾辈当歌彼日旌旗初展——
 吾民出征，更无返顾之念，
 彼时旗帜行遍天下四方。

===Original===
Many saw that he was singing, but heard not the words of his mouth, for great was the noise and clamour. But he heard Bow-may, how she laughed by his side, and cried out:
“Gold-mane, dear-heart, now art thou merry indeed; and glad am I, though they told me that I am hurt.—Ah! now beware, beware!”

===Chinese===
许多人见他唱歌，却听不清他口中之辞，盖因周遭喧嚣震耳。然他却听得见弓娥在他身畔大笑，高声呼道：
"金鬃，心肝，你如今是真快活了；我也欢喜，虽说他们告诉我我已挂彩。——哎呀！当心，当心！"

===Original===
For indeed the Dusky Men, seeing the wall of steel rolling down on them, and cooped up by the houses, so that they scarce knew how to flee, turned in the face of death, the foremost of them, and rushed furiously on the array of the Woodlanders, and all those behind pressed on them like the big wave of the ebbing sea when the gust of the wind driveth it landward.

The Woodlanders met them, shouting out: “The Greenwood and the Wolf, the Greenwood and the Wolf!” But not a few of them fell there, though they gave not back a foot; for so fierce now were the Dusky Men, that hewing and thrusting at them availed nought, unless they were slain outright or stunned; and even if they fell they rolled themselves up against their tall foemen, heeding not death or wounds if they might but slay or wound. There then fell War-grove and ten others of the Woodlanders, and four men of the Wolf, but none before he had slain his foeman; and as each man fell or was hurt grievously, another took his place.

Now a felon leapt up and caught Gold-ring by the neck and drew him down, while another strove to smite his head off; but the stout carle drave a wood-knife into the side of the first felon, and drew it out speedily and smote the other, the smiter, in the face with the same knife, and therewith they all three rolled together on the earth amongst the feet of men. Even so did another felon by Bow-may, and dragged her down to the ground, and smote her with a long knife as she tumbled down; and this was a feat of theirs, for they were long-armed like apes.

===Chinese===
盖因黝暗人见那钢铁之墙朝他们碾压而来，又被屋舍困住，几乎无路可逃，其最前之人遂在死地之前转身，狂怒地朝林中之民的阵列扑来，其后所有之人则如退潮时大风卷起、扑向岸上的大浪一般，层层压将上来。

林中之民迎了上去，高呼："青林与狼！青林与狼！"然其阵虽寸步不退，阵亡者却不在少数；盖因黝暗人此时凶悍已极，砍也砍不动、刺也刺不透，除非将其立时斩杀或打得昏死；即便倒地，他们还要滚身扑向那些高大之敌，只要能杀一人、伤一人，死伤皆所不惜。是役，战林与林中之民十人、狼之民四人皆于此阵亡，然无一不是先已斩杀其敌而后倒下；每有一人倒下或身负重伤，便立有另一人补其位。

忽有一恶徒跃起，一把扼住金环之颈、将他拽倒，另一人则挥刃欲斩其首；然那壮健的汉子将一柄猎刀捅入头一个恶徒之胁，迅速拔出，又以同一刀劈中那挥刀者——即第二人——之面，于是三人一齐滚作一团，倒在众人脚底之间。另有一恶徒亦对弓娥施此故技，将她拽倒在地，趁她跌倒之际以一柄长刀刺之；此乃彼辈所长之技，因其臂长如猿故也。

===Original===
But as to this felon, Dale-warden’s edge split his skull, and Face-of-god gathered his might together and bestrode Bow-may, till he had hewed a space round about him with great two-handed strokes; and yet the blade brake not. Then he caught up Bow-may from the earth, and the felon’s knife had not pierced her hauberk, but she was astonied, and might not stand upon her feet; and Face-of-god turned aside a little with her, and half bore her, half thrust her through the throng to the rearward of his folk, and left her there with two carlines of the Wolf who followed the host for leechcraft’s sake, and then turned back shouting: “For the Face, for the Face!” and there followed him back to the battle, a band of those who were fresh as yet, and their blades unbloodied, the young men of the Woodlands.

===Chinese===
至于这一恶徒，谷卫之锋已将其头颅劈作两半；面神攒足气力，跨立于弓娥之上，以大开大合的双手猛斫，在身周硬生生斫出一方空地；而剑刃竟不断折。他便将弓娥自地上抱起，那恶徒之刀并未刺透其锁子甲，然她已惊骇昏沉，双足不能自立；面神略略带她偏开几步，半搀半推穿过人群，将她送至本阵之后，托付于两名狼族老妇——此二妇随军专为施治医术——随即转身高呼："为面神！为面神！"又随他杀回战阵的，是一队尚未疲倦、刀上犹未见血的人马——林中之民中的少年郎。

===Original===
The wearier fighters made way for them as they came on shouting, and Face-of-god was ahead of them all, and leapt at the foemen as a man unwearied and striking his first stroke, so wondrous hale he was; and they drave a wedge amidst of the Dusky Men, and then turned about and stood back to back hewing at all that drifted on them. But as Face-of-god cleared a space about him, lo! almost within reach of his sword-point up rose a grim shape from the earth, tall, grey-haired, and bloody-faced, who uttered the Wolf-whoop from amidst the terror of his visage, and turned and swung round his head an axe of the Dusky Men, and fell to smiting them with their own weapon. The Dusky Men shrieked in answer to his whoop, and all shrunk from him and Face-of-god; but a cry of joy went up from the kindred, for they knew Gold-ring, whom they had deemed had been slain. So they all pressed on together, smiting down the foe before them, and the Dusky Men, some turned their backs and drave those behind them, till they too turned and were strained through the passages and courts of the houses, and some were overthrown and trodden down as they strove to hold face to the Woodlanders, and some were hewn down where they stood; but the whole throng of those that were on their feet drifted toward the Marketplace, the Woodlanders following them ever with point and edge, till betwixt the bent and the houses no foeman stood up against them.

===Chinese===
疲乏的战卒让出一条路来，让这些呐喊而至的生力军通过；面神冲在最前，向敌人扑去，浑如一个毫不疲倦、正发第一击之人，其气力之盛，实属罕见；他们如一柄楔子直插入黝暗人之中，旋即回身，背靠背斫杀一切涌向他们之敌。正当面神在身周清出一方空地之际，看哪！几近其剑锋所及之处，一个狰狞的身形自地上立起——高大、苍发、满面血污——自其可怖的面容之中迸出一声狼嚎，随即转身，将一柄黝暗人之斧抡过头顶，以其人之兵刃反斫其人。黝暗人以尖啸回应其嚎，尽皆畏缩，不敢近他与面神；然族众之中却迸出一阵欢呼——盖因他们认出了金环，本已以为他阵亡。于是众人一齐压上，将身前之敌斫倒；黝暗人中，有的转身便逃，反撞上身后之人，逼得后者亦转，于是被挤压穿过屋舍之间的夹道与院落；有的为维持面向林中之民，被掀翻踏倒；有的则当场被斫倒；然凡双足尚立之人，整群皆向市集方向漂去，林中之民以枪尖刀锋一路追杀，直至山坡与屋舍之间再无一敌挺立相抗。

===Original===
Then they stood together, and raised the whoop of victory, and blew their horns long and loud in token of their joy, and the Woodland men lifted up their voices and sang:

===Chinese===
众人遂并肩而立，扬起胜利之嚎，将号角吹得又长又响，以示其喜；林中之民遂纵声而歌：

===Original===
> Now far, far aloof
 Standeth lintel and roof,
 The dwelling of days
 Of the Woodland ways:
 Now nought wendeth there
 Save the wolf and the bear,
 And the fox of the waste
 Faring soft without haste.
 No carle the axe whetteth on oak-laden hill;
 No shaft the hart letteth to wend at his will;
 None heedeth the thunderclap over the glade,
 And the windstorm thereunder makes no man afraid.
 Is it thus then that endeth man’s days on Mid-earth,
 For no man there wendeth in sorrow or mirth?
> Nay, look down on the road
 From the ancient abode!
 Betwixt acre and field
 Shineth helm, shineth shield.
 And high over the heath
 Fares the bane in his sheath;
 For the wise men and bold
 Go their ways o’er the wold.
 Now the Warrior hath given them heart and fair day,
 Unbidden, undriven, they fare to the fray.
 By the rock and the river the banners they bear,
 And their battle-staves quiver ’neath halbert and spear;
 On the hill’s brow they gather, and hang o’er the Dale
 As the clouds of the Father hang, laden with bale.
> Down shineth the sun
 On the war-deed half done;
 All the foredoomed to die,
 In the pale dust they lie.
 There they leapt, there they fell,
 And their tale shall we tell;
 But we, e’en in the gate
 Of the war-garth we wait,
 Till the drift of war-weather shall whistle us on,
 And we tread all together the way to be won,
 To the dear land, the dwelling for whose sake we came
 To do deeds for the telling of song-becrowned fame.
 Settle helm on the head then! Heave sword for the Dale!
 Nor be mocked of the dead men for deedless and pale.

===Chinese===
> 遥遥，遥遥相隔，
 门楣与屋顶——
 那昔日岁月之居、
 林中岁月之地：
 今无一物过彼，
 唯狼与熊而已，
 并有荒原之狐，
 徐徐信步而行。
 橡实满山之岗，无人磨斧；
 雄鹿任己意而行，无矢追逼；
 雷劈空旷之野，无人理会，
 其下之风雹，不令任何人惊惧。
 人之岁月于中土之上，遂如此终了？
 彼处更无一人行走，无论悲喜？
> 不然！自那古居
 俯看那条道路！
 耕地与田亩之间，
 盔光闪，盾光明。
 荒原之上，高扬而过，
 煞神藏于鞘中；
 因智勇之人，
 正越原野而行。
 武神已赐彼等勇气与吉日，
 不召自来，不驱而往，奔赴战阵。
 岩石之畔、河流之滨，彼等高举旌旗，
 战棍在戟与矛之下颤动；
 彼等聚于山颜，悬于谷上，
 一如天父之乌云，满载灾殃。
> 日头照耀其下，
 照此半成之战功；
 凡注定当死之人，
 皆卧于苍白尘中。
 彼等跃于斯，仆于斯，
 彼等之事，吾辈当述之；
 而吾辈，正立于
 战庭之门前以待——
 待战阵风云呼啸催吾向前，
 吾辈齐踏那条待取之路，
 奔向那亲爱的土地——吾辈为此而来之居所——
 以行那将传诸加冕之歌的功业。
 且正盔于首！为谷举剑！
 休为已死之人所笑，谓吾辈苍白无功。

## XXXVII Of the Folk-Mote of the Dalesmen, the Shepherd-Folk, and the Woodland Carles: The Banner of the Wolf Displayed / 三十七 谷民、牧羊之民与林中汉子之民众大会：狼之旌旗展扬

===Original===
Now came the day of the Great Folk-mote, and there was much thronging from everywhere to the Motestead, but most from Burgstead itself, whereas few of the Dale-dwellers who had been at the Fair had gone back home. Albeit some of the Shepherds and of the Dalesmen of the westernmost Dale had brought light tents, and tilted themselves in in the night before the Mote down in the meadows below the Motestead. From early morning there had been a stream of folk on the Portway setting westward; and many came thus early that they might hold converse with friends and well-wishers; and some that they might disport them in the woods. Men went in no ordered bands, as the Burgstead men at least had done on the day of the Weapon-show, save that a few of them who were arrayed the bravest gathered about the banners, and went with them to the Motestead; for all the banners must needs be there.

The Folk-mote was to be hallowed-in three hours before noon, as all men knew; therefore an hour before that time were all men of the Dale and the Shepherds assembled that might be looked for, save the Alderman and the chieftains with the banner of the Burg, and these were not like to come many minutes before the Hallowing. Folk were gathered on the Field in such wise, that the men-at-arms made a great ring round about the Doom-ring, (albeit there were many old men there, girt with swords that they should never heave up again in battle), so that without that ring there was nought save women and children. But when all the other Houses were assembled, men looked around, and beheld the place of the Woodlanders that it was empty; and they marvelled that they were thus belated. For now all was ready, and a watcher had gone up to the Tower on the height, and had with him the great Horn of Warning, which could be heard past the Motestead and a great way down the Dale: and if he saw foes coming from the East he should blow one blast; if from the South, two; if from the West, three; if from the North, four.

===Chinese===
盛大之民众大会（the Great Folk-mote）之期已至，自各处往议事坪（the Motestead）赴会者熙熙攘攘，而以堡镇（Burgstead）本处为最多——盖因赴过集市之谷民中，归家者寥寥。纵然如此，一些牧羊之民与堡谷最西端之谷民，仍带了轻便帐篷，于大会前夜在议事坪下方之草甸中安营过夜。自清晨起，港路（the Portway）之上便有一道人流迤逦西行；许多人来得这样早，乃为与亲友故交、善意的相熟之人相会寒暄；有些则是为在林中游赏取乐。众人此番并不结成整队而行——至少堡镇之民在兵器大阅（the Weapon-show）那日是结过队的——只是其中少数装束最华丽之士聚于诸旗之下，随之同赴议事坪；盖因所有旌旗务必齐聚于此。

民众大会须于午前三小时行圣仪开典，此乃人人皆知之事；故开典前一小时，凡所当来之谷民与牧羊之民皆已到齐，唯长老（the Alderman）与众首领举堡镇之旌旗（the banner of the Burg）者不在其列——而此辈不到圣仪（the Hallowing）行将开始前数刻，断不轻至。众人聚于议事场（the Field）上，其列阵如此：持兵之士于判决环（the Doom-ring）四周围成一大圈（虽说其中多有老者，腰间佩剑，然此辈永不再于战阵之上举剑相迎了），是以此圈之外别无他人，唯有妇孺。然当其余诸氏族皆已到齐，众人四顾，只见林中之民（the Woodlanders）那一席空空如也；众人皆奇其何以如此迟来。盖此时一切已备，已有瞭望之人登上高处之望楼（the Tower），随身带着那支大警角（the Horn of Warning），角声可越过议事坪、传至谷中极远之处：若见东面有敌来，吹一声；南面来，吹两声；西面来，吹三声；北面来，吹四声。

===Original===
So half an hour from the appointed time of Hallowing rose the rumour that the Alderman was on the road, and presently they of the women who were on the outside of the throng, by drawing nigh to the edge of the sheer rock, could behold the Banner of the Burg on the Portway, and soon after could see the wain, done about with green boughs, wherein sat the chieftains in their glittering war-gear. Speedily they spread the tidings, and a confused shout went up into the air; and in a little while the wain stayed on Wildlake’s Way at the bottom of the steep slope that went up to the Motestead, and the banner of the Burg came on proudly up the hill. Soon all men beheld it, and saw that the tall Hall-face bore it in front of his brother Face-of-god, who came on gleaming in war-gear better than most men had seen; which was indeed of his father’s fashioning, and his father’s gift to him that morning.

After Face-of-god came the Alderman, and with him Folk-might leading the Sun-beam by the hand, and then Stone-face and the Elder of the Dale-wardens; and then the six Burg-wardens: as to the other Dale-wardens, they were in their places on the Field.

===Chinese===
于是距圣仪所定之时仅余半小时，忽有消息传来说长老已在路上；不一会儿，人群外围的妇人中有几个凑近绝壁之缘，便能望见港路上堡镇之旌旗，旋即又看见那辆缀满青枝之车——车中坐着众首领，个个披挂闪亮之甲胄。她们飞速传开此讯，于是一片纷乱之欢呼腾空而起；不多时，那车便停于野湖径（Wildlake's Way）上、通往议事坪之陡坡脚下，堡镇之旌旗乃昂然上得山来。众人旋即尽皆望见，只见高大之厅面（Hall-face）举旗走在其兄面神（Face-of-god）之前，面神所披甲胄光华烁烁，胜过众人所曾见过；那一身甲胄实乃其父手制，是其父当晨所赠之礼。

面神之后是长老，与他同行者有民强（Folk-might），民强牵着日光（the Sun-beam）之手，其后是石面（Stone-face）与谷卫之长（the Elder of the Dale-wardens）；再其后是六位堡卫（the Burg-wardens）：至于其余的谷卫（the Dale-wardens），则已各就各位立于议事场之上。

===Original===
So now those who had been standing up turned their faces toward the Altar of the Gods, and those who had been sitting down sprang to their feet, and the confused rumour of the throng rose into a clear shout as the chieftains went to their places, and sat them down on the turf-seats amidst the Doom-ring facing the Speech-hill and the Altar of the Gods. Amidmost sat the Alderman, on his right hand Face-of-god, and out from him Hall-face, and then Stone-face and three of the Wardens; but on his left hand sat first the two Guests, then the Elder of the Dale-wardens, and then the other three Burg-wardens; as for the Banner of the Burg, its staff was stuck into the earth behind them, and the Banner raised itself in the morning wind and flapped and rippled over their heads.

There then they sat, and folk abided, and it still lacked some minutes of the due time, as the Alderman wotted by the shadow of the great standing-stone betwixt him and the Altar. Therewithal came the sound of a great horn from out of the wood on the north side, and men knew it for the horn of the Woodland Carles, and were glad; for they could not think why they should be belated; and now men stood up a-tiptoe and on other’s shoulders to look over the heads of the women and children to behold their coming; but their empty place was at the southwest corner of the ring of men.

===Chinese===
于是方才站立之人皆转身面朝诸神之祭坛（the Altar of the Gods），方才坐着之人则一跃而起，人群那纷乱之喧响化作清亮之一片欢呼——正当众首领各归其位，于判决环内之草皮座上落座，面朝议事土台（the Speech-hill）与诸神之祭坛。长老居中而坐，其右手为面神，向外依次为厅面、石面，以及三位守事（the Wardens）；其左手则先坐两位贵客（the two Guests），继之以谷卫之长，再而后是其余三位堡卫；至于堡镇之旌旗，旗杆插于他们身后土中，旌旗在晨风里高高扬起，于众人头顶猎猎飘展。

众首领便如此落座，众人静候，此时距所定之时尚差片刻——长老凭他与祭坛之间那块巨立石之影便知其数。正此之际，北面林中传来一声大角之响，众人一听便识得是林中汉子（the Woodland Carles）之号角，皆大欢喜；盖因他们正想不通彼等何以迟来；此时众人踮足耸肩，越过妇孺之头探望，欲观其来临；而林中汉子所空之位，原在壮士大圈之西南角。

===Original===
So presently men beheld them marching toward their place, cleaving the throng of the women and children, a great company; for besides that they had with them two score more of men under weapons than on the day of the Weapon-show, all their little ones and women and outworn elders were with them, some on foot, some riding on oxen and asses. In their forefront went the two signs of the Battle-shaft and the War-spear. But moreover, in front of all was borne a great staff with the cloth of a banner wrapped round about it, and tied up with a hempen yarn that it might not be seen.

Stark and mighty men they looked; tall and lean, broad-shouldered, dark-faced. As they came amongst the throng the voice of their horn died out, and for a few moments they fared on with no sound save the tramp of their feet; then all at once the man who bare the hidden banner lifted up one hand, and straightway they fell to singing, and with that song they came to their place. And this is some of what they sang:

===Chinese===
不一会儿，众人便见他们朝自己那一席行来，劈开妇孺之人群，浩浩荡荡一大群；盖因他们不仅比兵器大阅那日多带了四十名持兵之士，所有老幼妇孺、年迈力衰之长辈也都随行而来，有的步行，有的骑牛骑驴。其最前列走着战矛（the Battle-shaft）与战枪（the War-spear）两面旗号。更有甚者，最最前头还抬着一根大旗杆，旗布缠绕其上，以麻绳扎紧，不让人看见。

他们看上去皆是壮健魁伟之汉子；身瘦而长，肩阔而面黝。待他们走入人群之中，号角之声渐息，片刻之间，他们只以跫跫足音前行，别无他响；忽然间，那擎着裹藏旌旗之人举起一只手，众人随即齐声高歌，便在这歌声之中来到了自己那一席。以下便是他们所唱之一部分：

===Original===
> O white, white Sun, what things of wonder

Hast thou beheld from thy wall of the sky!

All the Roofs of the Rich and the grief thereunder,

As the fear of the Earl-folk flitteth by!

> Thou hast seen the Flame steal forth from the Forest

To slay the slumber of the lands,

As the Dusky Lord whom thou abhorrest

Clomb up to thy Burg unbuilt with hands.

> Thou lookest down from thy door the golden,

Nor batest thy wide-shining mirth,

As the ramparts fall, and the rooftrees olden

Lie smouldering low on the burning earth.

> When flitteth the half-dark night of summer

From the face of the murder great and grim,

’Tis thou thyself and no newcomer

Shines golden-bright on the deed undim.

> Art thou our friend, O Day-dawn’s Lover?

Full oft thine hand hath sent aslant

Bright beams athwart the Wood-bear’s cover,

Where the feeble folk and the nameless haunt.

> Thou hast seen us quail, thou hast seen us cower,

Thou hast seen us crouch in the Green Abode,

While for us wert thou slaying slow hour by hour,

And smoothing down the war-rough road.

> Yea, the rocks of the Waste were thy Dawns upheaving,

To let the days of the years go through;

And thy Noons the tangled brake were cleaving

The slow-foot seasons’ deed to do.

> Then gaze adown on this gift of our giving,

For the **Wolf** comes wending frith and ford,

And the Folk fares forth from the dead to the living,

For the love of the Lief by the light of the Sword.

===Chinese===
> 皎皎白日，几多惊心骇目之事，

尔曾自天穹之城墙上俯览！

富者万顶华盖与其下之悲辛，

当贵人之所惧飘忽掠过其间！

> 尔曾见烈焰自林中悄然潜出，

去屠戮诸地之沉梦，

如尔所深恶之黝暗之主，

攀上尔那天成之山堡。

> 尔自尔那黄金之门俯瞰，

广照之欢不曾稍减，

当城垣倾颓、古老之屋脊

低低横陈于燃烧之地上闷燃。

> 当夏日半明之夜自那

巨大狰狞之凶杀面前掠过，

正是尔自身，并非新来之人，

金光熠熠照在那未黯之血事上。

> 尔可是我们的朋友，曙光之爱侣？

尔之手屡屡斜斜送出

明亮辉芒，穿射林熊之薮，

那怯弱之民与无名之辈藏身之处。

> 尔曾见我们畏缩，尔曾见我们蜷伏，

尔曾见我们屈身于青庐之中，

正当尔为我们一刻一刻缓慢杀敌，

抹平那战争碾出之崎岖之路。

> 诚然，荒原之岩石乃尔之黎明所举，

好让岁月之日子穿行而过；

而尔之正午劈开纠结之荆丛，

去行那缓步季节所当行之事。

> 那么，俯首垂视这我们献上之礼吧，

因为**狼**正穿林渡水迤逦而来，

族人自死者之中迈向生者，

为所爱之挚爱，凭剑光之引。

===Original===
Then ceased the song, and the whole band of the Woodlanders came pouring tumultuously into the space allotted them, like the waters pouring over a river-dam, their white swords waving aloft in the morning sunlight; and wild and strange cries rose up from amidst them, with sobbing and weeping of joy. But soon their troubled front sank back into ordered ranks, their bright blades stood upright in their hands before them, and folk looked on their company, and deemed it the very Terror of battle and Render of the ranks of war. Right well were they armed; for though many of their weapons were ancient and somewhat worn, yet were they the work of good smiths of old days; and moreover, if any of them lacked good war-gear of his own, that had the Alderman and his sons made good to them.

But before the hedge of steel stood the two tall men who held in their hands the war-tokens of the Battle-shaft and the War-spear, and betwixt them stood one who was indeed the tallest man of the whole assembly, who held the great staff of the hidden banner. And now he reached up his hand, and plucked at the yarn that bound it, which of set purpose was but feeble, and tore it off, and then shook the staff aloft with both hands, and shouted, and lo! the Banner of the Wolf with the Sun-burst behind him, glittering-bright, new-woven by the women of the kindred, ran out in the fresh wind, and flapped and rippled before His warriors there assembled.

===Chinese===
歌声既歇，林中之民整队如水泻过河堰一般，喧腾涌入了分给他们的一方之地，他们雪白的刀剑在晨光中高高挥舞；其中腾起粗犷奇异之呼号，伴着喜极而泣之抽噎。然而不久，他们那骚动的前列便退回复归整秩，明晃晃的刀刃直立手中、列于身前；众人望着他们这一队，只觉直是战阵上之凶神、冲锋破军之锐。他们装备甚是精良；虽说许多兵器已年代久远、略有磨损，然皆出自昔日良匠之手；况且他们当中但凡自有好甲胄不足者，长老与诸子皆已为之补齐。

然而在这刀丛之前，立着两个高大之汉子，手擎战矛、战枪两面战旗；他们之间则站着一人，此人实乃整个集会中最高大者，擎着那裹藏旌旗之大旗杆。但见他伸手扯住那绑扎之麻绳——那绳本是故意系得极不结实——一把扯断，然后双手将旗杆高高扬起，大喝一声；看哪！狼之旌旗（the Banner of the Wolf）赫然展开——苍狼之后衬着旭日（the Sun-burst），光华烁烁，乃族中妇人新近所织——在清风中舒展开来，于彼处所聚之狼之武士前猎猎飘扬。

===Original===
Then from all over the Motestead arose an exceeding great shout, and all men waved aloft their weapons; but the men of Shadowy Vale who were standing amidst the men of the Face knew not how to demean themselves, and some of them ran forth into the Field and leapt for joy, tossing their swords into the air, and catching them by the hilts as they fell: and amidst it all the Woodlanders now stood silent, unmoving, as men abiding the word of onset.

As for that brother and sister: the Sun-beam flushed red all over her face, and pressed her hands to her bosom, and then the passion of tears overmastered her, and her breast heaved, and the tears gushed out of her eyes, and her body was shaken with weeping. But Folk-might sat still, looking straight before him, his eyes glittering, his teeth set, his right hand clutching hard at the hilts of his sword, which lay naked across his knees. And the Bride, who stood clad in her begemmed and glittering war-array in the forefront of the Men of the Steer, nigh unto the seats of the chieftains, beheld Folk-might, and her face flushed and brightened, and still she looked upon him. The Alderman’s face was as of one pleased and proud; yet was its joy shadowed as it were by a cloud of compassion. Face-of-god sat like the very image of the War-god, and stirred not, nor looked toward the Sun-beam; for still the thought of the after-grief of battle, and the death of friends and folk that loved him, lay heavy on his heart, for all that it beat wildly at the shouting of the men.

===Chinese===
于是自整个议事坪升起一片极盛大之欢呼，众人皆将兵器高高挥舞；然而立于面神之族（the men of the Face）之间的幽谷（Shadowy Vale）之民却不知如何自处，其中有人奔入场中，喜极而跃，将刀剑掷向空中，待其落下时又握住剑柄接住：而在这一片喧腾之中，林中之民此刻却静立不动，如待冲锋号令之兵。

至于那一对兄妹：日光满脸涨得通红，双手紧按胸口，继而一股热泪之情汹涌难抑，胸脯起伏，泪水夺眶而出，浑身因哭泣而颤抖。民强却端坐不动，直视前方，双目闪闪，紧咬牙关，右手紧紧攥住横陈膝上那柄出鞘之剑的剑柄。新娘（the Bride）则立于牛部之民（the Men of the Steer）前列，身着缀珠闪亮之战袍，离众首领之座不远；她凝视着民强，面色转红、神采焕发，定定地望着他。长老之面容，如一个既喜且骄之人；然其喜色之上，似为一片悲悯之云所笼。面神则如战神（the War-god）之塑像一般端坐，一动不动，亦不望向日光；因为战后的哀伤、那爱他的亲友族人之死，这些念头仍沉重地压在他心头——纵然众人的呐喊使他心跳如狂。

## XXV Of the Gate-Thing at Burgstead / 二十五 论堡镇之门会

===Original===
But now must he hasten, for the Gate-thing was to be holden two hours before noon; so he betook him speedily to the Hall, and took his shield and did on a goodly helm and girt his sword to his side, for men must needs go to all folk-motes with their weapons and clad in war-gear. Thus he went forth to the Gate with many others, and there already were many folk assembled in the space aforesaid betwixt the Gate of the Burg and the sheer rocks on the face of which were the steps that led up to the ancient Tower on the height. The Alderman was sitting on the great stone by the Gate-side which was his appointed place, and beside him on the stone bench were the six Wardens of the Burg; but of the six Wardens of the Dale there were but three, for the others had not yet heard tell of the battle or had got the summons to the Thing, since they had been about their business down the Dale.

Face-of-god took his place silently amongst the neighbours, but men made way for him, so that he must needs stand in front, facing his father and the Wardens; and there went up a murmur of expectation round about him, both because the word had gone about that he had a tale of new tidings to tell, and also because men deemed him their best and handiest man, though he was yet so young.

===Chinese===
然此刻他须得赶紧，因为门会（Gate-thing）定在午前两个时辰召开；于是他疾步回到大厅，取了盾牌，戴上一顶精良的头盔，将剑佩于腰间——凡赴民众大会（folk-mote），人人皆须携带兵器、披挂战甲，此乃定规。他便随众人一同出门往堡门而去；那前述之地——堡镇之门（the Gate of the Burg）与陡立绝壁之间的一段空地，绝壁表面凿有石阶，通向高处那座古望楼——此时已聚了不少人。长老（the Alderman）坐在门旁一块大石之上，那是他惯常的座位；他身旁的石凳上坐着六位堡镇守事（the Wardens of the Burg）；至于谷中六位守事，只到了三位，其余几位尚在下游谷中操持各自事务，要么未闻战事之报，要么尚未接到议事之召。

面神默然立于邻里之间，众人却纷纷为他让路，使他不得不站到前头，正对着父亲与众守事；他四周登时响起一片期待的低语声——一则因为风声早已传开，说他有一桩新消息要讲；二则因为众人虽知他年纪尚轻，却已视他为全族最出色、最能干的好汉。

===Original===
Now the Alderman looked around and beheld a great throng gathered together, and he looked on the shadow of the Gate which the southering sun was casting on the hard white ground of the Thingstead, and he saw that it had just taken in the standing-stone which was in the midst of the place. On the face of the said stone was carven the image of a fighting man with shield on arm and axe in hand; for it had been set there in old time in memory of the man who had bidden the Folk build the Gate and its wall, and had showed them how to fashion it: for he was a deft house-smith as well as a great warrior; and his name was Iron-hand. So when the Alderman saw that this stone was wholly within the shadow of the Gate he knew that it was the due time for the hallowing-in of the Thing. So he bade one of the wardens who sat beside him and had a great slug-horn slung about him, to rise and set the horn to his mouth.

So that man arose and blew three great blasts that went bellowing about the towers and down the street, and beat back again from the face of the sheer rocks and up them and over into the wildwood; and the sound of it went on the light west-wind along the lips of the Dale toward the mountain wastes. And many a goodman, when he heard the voice of the horn in the bright spring morning, left spade or axe or plough-stilts, or the foddering of the ewes and their younglings, and turned back home to fetch his sword and helm and hasten to the Thing, though he knew not why it was summoned: and women wending over the meadows, who had not yet heard of the battle in the wood, hearkened and stood still on the green grass or amidst the ripples of the ford, and the threat of coming trouble smote heavy on their hearts, for they knew that great tidings must be towards if a Thing must needs be summoned so close to the Great Folk-mote.

===Chinese===
此时长老环顾四周，见一大群人已然聚拢；他又看了看堡门的阴影——那南天的日头将堡门之影投在议事场（Thingstead）坚硬白净的地面上——只见那阴影恰好罩住了场地中央那块立石（standing-stone）。此石正面刻着一名武士的造像：臂上挽盾、手中持斧；此石乃是古时为纪念一人而立——正是他吩咐族人修筑堡门及其城墙，并教众人如何营造：他既是一位伟大的武士，也是一名精巧的营造匠师，其名唤铁手（Iron-hand）。长老见这块石头已整个落入堡门阴影之中，便知圣化开场（hallowing-in）的正当时辰已到。于是他吩咐身旁一位身挂大号角（slug-horn）的守事起身，将号角凑到嘴边。

那人起身，吹了三声长号，号声轰鸣，回荡于诸座望楼之间，沿街而下，又自陡崖壁上反弹回来，攀上崖顶、越过野林（the Wildwood）而去；那声音乘着微弱的西风，沿山谷两唇朝山中荒原一路飘去。许多当家做主的汉子，听见这晴朗春晨传来的号声，撇下了铁锹、斧头或犁柄，或撇下正给母羊及羊羔喂料的活计，转身回家取了剑与头盔，便赶往议事会——虽不知为何而召；还有些正走过草甸的女子，她们尚未听闻林中那一战，听了号声便停下脚步，立在青草之上或涉滩的涟漪之中，一种大难将至的阴影沉沉压上她们的心头——因为她们知道，若非情势重大、必有大消息将至，绝不至于在大民众大会（the Great Folk-mote）召开在即之时，还非要另起一场议事会不可。

===Original===
But now the Alderman stood up and spake amidst the silence that followed the last echoes of the horn:

“Now is hallowed in this Gate-thing of the Burgstead Men and the Men of the Dale, wherein they shall take counsel concerning matters late befallen, that press hard upon them. Let no man break the peace of the Holy Thing, lest he become a man accursed in holy places from the plain up to the mountain, and from the mountain down to the plain; a man not to be cherished of any man of good will, not be holpen with victuals or edge-tool or draught-beast; a man to be sheltered under no rooftree, and warmed at no hearth of man: so help us the Warrior and the God of the Earth, and Him of the Face, and all the Fathers!”

===Chinese===
此时号角余音方歇，一片寂静之中，长老起身说道：

"堡镇之民与谷中之民（Men of the Dale）此番门会，如今宣告圣开；众人将在此就近日发生、紧迫逼人之事共议对策。任何人不得破坏此神圣议事会（the Holy Thing）之安宁，违者必于一切圣地之中沦为见弃之人——自平原以至高山，自高山以至平原；此人不得受任何善人所顾惜，不得受饮食、刀兵、耕畜之助；天下无一檐之下可容其栖身，无一户之炉火可使其取暖：愿武神（the Warrior）、地神（the God of the Earth）、面之神（Him of the Face）及列祖列宗助我等！"

===Original===
When he had spoken men clashed their weapons in token of assent; and he sat down again, and there was silence for a space. But presently came thrusting forward a goodman of the Dale, who seemed as if he had come hurriedly to the Thing; for his face was running down with sweat, his wide-rimmed iron cap sat awry over his brow, and he was girt with a rusty sword without a scabbard, and the girdle was ill-braced up about his loins. So he said:

“I am Red-coat of Waterless of the Lower Dale. Early this morning as I was going afield I met on the way a man akin to me, Fox of Upton to wit, and he told me that men were being summoned to a Gate-thing. So I turned back home, and caught up any weapon that came handy, and here I am, Alderman, asking thee of the tidings which hath driven thee to call this Thing so hard on the Great Folk-mote, for I know them nothing so.”

===Chinese===
他话音落下，众人以兵器相击，表示赞同；长老重新坐下，静默了一会儿。不多时，一名谷中之民挤上前来看，似乎是匆匆赶来议事场的；只见他满脸汗水淋漓，宽檐铁盔歪戴在额上，腰间胡乱系着一柄无鞘的锈剑，腰带也松松垮垮地勒在胯骨上。他说道：

"我是下谷无水地（Waterless）的红衣（Red-coat）。今早我正要下地，路上遇见一个与我同宗的亲戚，便是上屯（Upton）之狐狸（Fox）——他对我说，众人正被召集开一场门会。我于是折回家中，随手抄起一件兵器便赶来了。长老啊，我来问你：是怎样的消息，逼得你赶在大民众大会跟前召开这场议事会？这些消息我竟一无所知。"

===Original===
Then stood up Iron-face the Alderman and said: “This is well asked, and soon shall ye be as wise as I am on this matter. Know ye, O men of Burgstead and the Dale, that we had not called this Gate-thing so hard on the Great Folk-mote had not great need been to look into troublous matters. Long have ye dwelt in peace, and it is years on years now since any foeman hath fallen on the Dale: but, as ye will bear in mind, last autumn were there ransackings in the Dale and amidst of the Shepherds after the manner of deeds of war; and it troubleth us that none can say who wrought these ill deeds. Next, but a little while agone, was Wood-grey, a valiant goodman of the Woodlanders, slain close to his own door by evil men. These men we took at first for mere gangrel felons and outcasts from their own folk: though there were some who spoke against that from the beginning.

“But thirdly are new tidings again: for three days ago, while some of the folk were hunting peaceably in the Wildwood and thinking no evil, they were fallen upon of set purpose by a host of men-at-arms, and nought would serve but mere battle for dear life, so that many of our neighbours were hurt, and three slain outright; and now mark this, that those who there fell upon our folk were clad and armed even as the two felons that slew Wood-grey, and moreover were like them in aspect of body. Now stand forth Hall-face my son, and answer to my questions in a loud voice, so that all may hear thee.”

===Chinese===
于是长老铁面（Iron-face）起身说道："这一问问得好；很快你们便要和我一样明白此事的来龙去脉了。堡镇与谷中的乡亲们，你们须知：若非为了稽查棘手之事、迫不得已，我们绝不会赶在大民众大会跟前召开这场门会。你们长久安居无事，自外敌入侵谷中以来，已不知过了多少岁月：然而你们定还记得，去秋堡谷与牧羊之民（the Shepherds）地面皆遭劫掠，所作所为一如战时行径；可恼的是，无人能说出这些恶事究为何人所为。其次，就在不久之前，林中汉子（the Woodlanders）里一名英勇的家主林灰（Wood-grey），竟在自家门前数步之处为恶人所杀。起初我们以为这些凶手不过是些流浪恶徒，是被本族逐出之人；虽说从一开始也有些人对此不以为然。

"然而第三桩，又是新的消息：三日之前，有几位族人正在野林（the Wildwood）中安然围猎，并无歹意，却遭一伙武装之众蓄意袭击，除了舍命死战之外别无他法，结果许多邻里受伤，三人当场阵亡；你们且记着这一节——在那处袭击族人的家伙，其装束兵器与杀害林灰的两名恶徒如出一辙，而且体貌也和他们相似。我的儿子厅面，你站出来，大声回答我的问话，好叫众人都听得见。"

===Original===
So Hall-face stood forth, clad in gleaming war-gear, with an axe over his shoulder, and seemed a doughty warrior. And Iron-face said to him:

“Tell me, son, those whom ye met in the wood, and of whom ye brought home two captives, how much like were they to the murder-carles at Wood-grey’s?”

Said Hall-face: “As like as peas out of the same cod, and to our eyes all those whom we saw in the wood might have been sons of one father and one mother, so much alike were they.”

“Yea,” said the Alderman; “now tell me how many by thy deeming fell upon you in the wood?”

Said Hall-face: “We deemed that if they were any less than threescore, they were little less.”

“Great was the odds,” said the Alderman. “Or how many were ye?”

“One score and seven,” said Hall-face.

Said the Alderman: “And yet ye escaped with life all save those three?”

Hall-face said: “I deem that scarce one should have come back alive, had it not been that as we fought came a noise like the howling of wolves, and thereat the foemen turned and fled, and there followed on the fleers tall men clad in sheep-brown raiment, who smote them down as they fled.”

“Here then is the story, neighbours,” said the Alderman, “and ye may see thereby that if those slayers of Wood-grey were outcast, their band is a great one; but it seemeth rather that they were men of a folk whose craft it is to rob with the armed hand, and to slay the robbed; and that they are now gathering on our borders for war. Yet, moreover, they have foemen in the woods who should be fellows-in-arms of us. How sayest thou, Stone-face? Thou art old, and hast seen many wars in the Dale, and knowest the Wildwood to its innermost.”

===Chinese===
于是厅面（Hall-face）应声而出，一身战甲锃亮，肩上扛着一柄斧头，看上去好一条英勇的汉子。铁面对他说道：

"儿子，告诉我，你们在林中所遇、并擒回两个活口的那伙人，与在林灰家行凶的恶徒有多相像？"

厅面答道："就如同同一只豆荚里剥出来的豌豆一般相像；在我们眼中，林中所见那伙人，简直像是一个爹一个娘生出来的，彼此像得厉害。"

长老道："好。那么我再问你：据你估量，林中袭击你们的有多少人？"

厅面道："我们估摸着，纵然不到六十，也相差无几。"

长老道："敌众我寡，悬殊甚大。你们又有多少人？"

厅面道："一十七人。"

长老道："然而除却阵亡那三人之外，你们竟全都逃得了性命？"

厅面道："我想，若不是正当酣战之际传来一阵如狼嚎般的声响，怕是一个人也休想活着回来——那声响一起，敌人便转身逃窜；紧追在逃敌身后的，是几个身穿羊褐衣裳的高大汉子，他们追着逃敌一路砍杀，将他们砍倒在地。"

"诸位邻里，事情便是如此，"长老道，"由此可知，若是杀害林灰的凶手乃是被逐之徒，那么他们这一伙人数可不少；但看情形，他们更像是一个以持械劫掠为业、劫后害命的族类，如今正在我边境之上聚众图谋战事。再者，他们在林中尚有仇敌，那些人本该是我等的并肩战友。石面（Stone-face），你怎么看？你年事已高，谷中所历战事甚多，野林（the Wildwood）深处你也尽知根底。"

===Original===
“Alderman,” said Stone-face, “and ye neighbours of the Dale, maybe these foes whom ye have met are not of the race of man, but are trolls and wood-wights. Now if they be trolls it is ill, for then is the world growing worser, and the wood shall be right perilous for those who needs must fare therein. Yet if they be men it is a worse matter; for the trolls would not come out of the waste into the sunlight of the Dale. But these foes, if they be men, are lusting after our fair Dale to eat it up, and it is most like that they are gathering a huge host to fall upon us at home. Such things I have heard of when I was young, and the aspect of the evil men who overran the kindreds of old time, according to all tales and lays that I have heard, is even such as the aspect of those whom we have seen of late. As to those wolves who saved the neighbours and chased their foemen, there is one here who belike knoweth more of all this than we do, and that, O Alderman, is thy son whom I have fostered, Face-of-god to wit. Bid him answer to thy questioning, and tell us what he hath seen and heard of late; then shall we verily know the whole story as far as it can be known.”

===Chinese===
石面道："长老，还有你们诸位谷中邻里：也许你们所遇的这些敌人，并非人类，而是山精巨怪（trolls）与林妖（wood-wights）。他们若是山精巨怪，那便不妙——因为这便意味着这世道愈来愈坏，那片林子对凡是不得不打那里经过的人都将凶险万分。然而他们若是人，事情就更糟；因为山精巨怪原不会走出荒原、闯入谷中这片阳光之地。但这些敌人若是人，便是觊觎我们这条美好的山谷、要将其吞噬干净，十之八九正在聚结一支大军，要打到我们家里来。我年少之时，便曾听闻此类事；据我所听过的所有传说与歌谣，古时那些倾覆各族宗族的恶人，其形貌正与我们近来所见之人一般无二。至于那群救下邻里、追杀敌人的'狼'，此地有一人，想必比我们谁都更知情——长老，那人便是你由我抚养长大的儿子，面神（Face-of-god）。你且叫他答你所问，把他近日的所见所闻讲与我们听；如此我们方能尽可知之限度，确知事情的全部本末。"

===Original===
Then men pressed round, and were eager to hear what Face-of-god would be saying. But or ever the Alderman could begin to question him, the throng was cloven by newcomers, and these were the men who had been sent to bring home the corpses of the Dusky Men: so they had cast loaded hooks into the Weltering Water, and had dragged up him whom Face-of-god had shoved into the eddy, and who had sunk like a stone just where he fell, and now they were bringing him on a bier along with him who had been slain a-land. They were set down in the place before the Alderman, and men who had not seen them before looked eagerly on them that they might behold the aspect of their foemen; and nought lovely were they to look on; for the drowned man was already bleached and swollen with the water, and the other, his face was all wryed and twisted with that spear-thrust in the mouth.

Then the Alderman said: “I would question my son Face-of-god. Let him stand forth!”

And therewith he smiled merrily in his son’s face, for he was standing right in front of him; and he said:

“Ask of me, Alderman, and I will answer.”

“Kinsman,” said Iron-face, “look at these two dead men, and tell me, if thou hast seen any such besides those two murder-carles who were slain at Carlstead; or if thou knowest aught of their folk?”

Said Face-of-god: “Yesterday I saw six others like to these both in array and of body, and three of them I slew, for we were in battle with them early in the morning.”

There was a murmur of joy at this word, since all men took these felons for deadly foemen; but Iron-face said: “What meanest thou by ‘we’?”

“I and the men who had guested me overnight,” said Face-of-god, “and they slew the other three; or rather a woman of them slew the felons.”

“Valiant she was; all good go with her hand!” said the Alderman. “But what be these people, and where do they dwell?”

===Chinese===
众人纷纷围拢上来，急欲听面神要说些什么。然而长老尚未及开口相问，人群便被新到之人从中劈开——来者正是受命去运回黝暗人（the Dusky Men）尸首的那几个汉子：他们将带坠的铁钩抛入翻滚河（the Weltering Water）之中，把被面神推入漩涡、就地如石般沉下去的那一个钩了上来，此时正用担架将他连同岸上被杀的另一个一同抬来。两具尸首被安放在长老面前那块空地上；未曾见过他们的众人争相围观，要看一看敌人的模样；那模样实在无可称善：那溺死之人已被水泡得浑身浮肿、面色惨白，另一个的脸则被嘴中那一矛戳得扭曲歪斜，不成样子。

长老说道："我要问一问我的儿子面神。让他站出来！"

说着，他冲面前的儿子愉快地笑了一笑——原来面神正站在他正前方；面神说道：

"长老但问，我自当如实作答。"

铁面道："我儿，你且看看这两具尸首，告诉我——除却那两个在汉子镇（Carlstead）被杀的凶徒之外，你可曾见过此类人物？或者你可知道他们的族人是什么来历？"

面神道："昨日我另见过六个与他们装束、体貌都相同之人，其中三个为我所杀——因为清晨时分我们与他们打了一场。"

此言一出，人群中发出一阵喜悦之声，因为众人都把这些恶徒当作死敌；铁面却问："你所说的'我们'，是指哪些人？"

面神道："我，还有昨夜款留我过夜的那几位——另外那三个恶徒是他们杀的；或者不如说，是他们中的一名女子将那几个恶徒杀了的。"

长老道："好一位壮烈的女子！愿她那双手万事顺遂！可这些人究竟是什么人，又住在哪里？"

===Original===
Said Face-of-god: “As to what they are, they are of the kindred of the Gods and the Fathers, valiant men, and guest-cherishing: rich have they been, and now are poor: and their poverty cometh of these same felons, who mastered them by numbers not to be withstood. As to where they dwell: when I say the name of their dwelling-place men mock at me, as if I named some valley in the moon: yet came I to Burgdale thence in one day across the mountain-necks led by sure guides, and I tell thee that the name of their abode is Shadowy Vale.”

“Yea,” said Iron-face, “knoweth any man here of Shadowy Vale, or where it is?”

None answered for a while; but there was an old man who was sitting on the shafts of a wain on the outskirts of the throng, and when he heard this word he asked his neighbour what the Alderman was saying, and he told him. Then said that elder:

“Give me place; for I have a word to say hereon.” Therewith he arose, and made his way to the front of the ring of men, and said: “Alderman, thou knowest me?”

“Yea,” said Iron-face, “thou art called the Fiddle, because of thy sweet speech and thy minstrelsy; whereof I mind me well in the time when I was young and thou no longer young.”

===Chinese===
面神道："要说他们是什么人——他们乃是与众神、与列祖同宗的一族，皆为英勇之士，好客敬客：他们原本殷富，如今却贫困潦倒；其贫困之由，正出自这同一伙恶徒——那伙人凭着无可抵挡的人多势众，将他们征服。至于他们住在哪里：我说出他们所居之地的名字时，众人总要嗤笑于我，仿佛我说的是月亮上某条山谷似的；然而我确是被人引着、由可靠的向导带路，越过一道道山颈，一日之间便从彼处来到堡谷（Burgdale）的。我可以告诉你，他们所居之地，名唤幽谷（Shadowy Vale）。"

铁面道："哦——在座可有人知道幽谷、知道它在何处？"

一时无人应答；唯有众人外围，有一老者正坐在一辆大车的车辕上，他听见这话，便问邻座长老方才说了什么，邻座照实相告。那老者便说道：

"给我让个位子；对此我有一言要讲。"说着他便站起身来，挤到人群圈子前头，说道："长老，你认得我吧？"

铁面道："认得，你被唤作提琴（the Fiddle），因你言辞温婉、又善于奏乐之故；这我还记得分明——那时我还年轻，你却已不年轻了。"

===Original===
“So it is,” said the Fiddle. “Now hearken! When I was very young I heard of a vale lying far away across the mountain-necks; a vale where the sun shone never in winter and scantily in summer; for my sworn foster-brother, Fight-fain, a bold man and a great hunter, had happened upon it; and on a day in full midsummer he brought me thither; and even now I see the Vale before me as in a picture; a marvellous place, well grassed, treeless, narrow, betwixt great cliff-walls of black stone, with a green river running through it towards a yawning gap and a huge force. Amidst that Vale was a doom-ring of black stones, and nigh thereto a feast-hall well builded of the like stones, over whose door was carven the image of a wolf with red gaping jaws, and within it (for we entered into it) were stone benches on the dais. Thence we came away, and thither again we went in late autumn, and so dusk and cold it was at that season, that we knew not what to call it save the valley of deep shade. But its real name we never knew; for there was no man there to give us a name or tell us any tale thereof; but all was waste there; the wimbrel laughed across its water, the raven croaked from its crags, the eagle screamed over it, and the voices of its waters never ceased; and thus we left it. So the seasons passed, and we went thither no more: for Fight-fain died, and without him wandering over the waste was irksome to me; so never have I seen that valley again, or heard men tell thereof.

“Now, neighbours, have I told you of a valley which seemeth to be Shadowy Vale; and this is true and no made-up story.”

===Chinese===
提琴道："正是如此。你们且听着！我很小的时候，便听说过有一处山谷，远在重重山颈之外；那山谷冬天不见日光，夏天也光照稀少——因为我那立过誓的义兄弟战欢（Fight-fain），一个胆大包天、极其出色的猎人，曾偶然撞见此地；仲夏某日，他将我带到那里；时至今日，那条山谷仍如一幅画般展现在我眼前：那是一处奇境，牧草丰美、不生树木、地势狭长，夹在两道黑色巨石的崖壁之间，一条碧绿的河穿谷而过，朝一道豁开的山口与一挂巨大的瀑布（force）奔去。谷中正央有一圈以黑石砌成的判决环（the doom-ring），环旁有一座以同样的黑石筑成的宴厅，相当齐整；厅门之上刻着一头张开血红大口的狼像，厅内（我们曾走进去看过）高台之上设有石凳。我们离开那里，暮秋时节又再去了一趟——那时节谷中阴暗寒冷之极，我们除了把它叫做'深荫之谷'，再想不出别的名目。可它的真正名字，我们始终不得而知；因为那里杳无人迹，无人告诉我们它的名字，也无人讲它的故事；那里一切都是荒的；鹬鸟的笑声掠过水面上空，渡鸦在崖石间聒噪，苍鹰在头顶长啸，水流的声音无时或歇；我们便是如此离开那里的。岁月流转，我们再未去过：因为战欢死了，没有他相伴，独自跋涉荒原于我太觉劳顿——于是我从此再没见过那条山谷，也未曾听人谈起过它。

"诸位邻里，我方才所讲这条山谷，想必便是幽谷了；句句实情，绝非编造。"

===Original===
The Alderman nodded kindly to him, and then said to Face-of-god: “Kinsman, is this word according with what thou knowest of Shadowy Vale?”

“Yea, on all points,” said Face-of-god; “he hath put before me a picture of the valley. And whereas he saith, that in his youth it was waste, this also goeth with my knowledge thereof. For once was it peopled, and then was waste, and now again is it peopled.”

“Tell us then more of the folk thereof,” said the Alderman; “are they many?”

“Nay,” said Face-of-god, “they are not. How might they be many, dwelling in that narrow Vale amid the wastes? But they are valiant, both men and women, and strong and well-liking. Once they dwelt in a fair dale called Silverdale, the name whereof will be to you as a name in a lay; and there were they wealthy and happy. Then fell upon them this murderous Folk, whom they call the Dusky Men; and they fought and were overcome, and many of them were slain, and many enthralled, and the remnant of them escaped through the passes of the mountains and came back to dwell in Shadowy Vale, where their forefathers had dwelt long and long ago; and this overthrow befell them ten years agone. But now their old foemen have broken out from Silverdale and have taken to scouring the wood seeking prey; so they fall upon these Dusky Men as occasion serves, and slay them without pity, as if they were adders or evil dragons; and indeed they be worse. And these valiant men know for certain that their foemen are now of mind to fall upon this Dale and destroy it, as they have done with others nigher to them. And they will slay our men, and lie with our women against their will, and enthrall our children, and torment all those that lie under their hands till life shall be worse than death to them. Therefore, O Alderman and Wardens, and ye neighbours all, it behoveth you to take counsel what we shall do, and that speedily.”

===Chinese===
长老对他和蔼地点了点头，转而向面神说道："我儿，他这话与你所知的幽谷，可相符否？"

面神道："相符，处处相符；他给我画出了一幅幽谷之图。至于他说自己年少时那里原是一片荒芜，这一点也与我所知相合。因为那里曾有人烟，其后荒芜，如今又再有人烟。"

长老道："那便再多讲讲那里的族人吧；他们人多吗？"

面神道："不多。住在那样一条夹于荒原之间的狭谷里，又怎会多呢？可他们不论男女，都英勇强壮、品貌端正。他们从前住在一处名叫银谷（Silverdale）的佳美山谷里——这名字在你们听来，将如歌谣中一个名字一般；他们在那里曾富足安乐。后来这一族嗜杀之民——他们唤作黝暗人——猝然降临；他们迎战了，却被击败，许多人为人所杀，许多人为人所奴，余下的人翻越山间诸隘口逃脱，回到幽谷居住下来——他们的远祖很久很久以前便曾居住于此；这一场倾覆，是在十年之前。如今他们昔日的大仇人自银谷破巢而出，四出林中搜寻猎物；他们便伺机袭杀这些黝暗人，毫不留情，如同屠戮蝮蛇、恶龙一般；其实这些人比蝮蛇恶龙更坏。这些壮士确知无疑：他们的大仇人如今正打定主意要来侵犯这条山谷、将其夷为平地，一如他们已在邻近各处所为。他们要杀尽我们的男丁，强污我们的妻女，奴役我们的孩童，折磨一切落入他们手中之人，直叫人觉得生不如死。因此，长老与众守事啊，还有诸位邻里，你们当赶紧计议我们日后所应为。"

===Original===
There was again a murmur, as of men nothing daunted, but intent on taking some way through the coming trouble. But no man said aught till the Alderman spake:

“When didst thou first happen upon this Earl-folk, son?”

“Late last autumn,” said Face-of-god.

Said Iron-face: “Then mightest thou have told us of this tale before.”

“Yea,” said his son, “but I knew it not, or but little of it, till two days agone. In the autumn I wandered in the woodland, and on the fell I happened on a few of this folk dwelling in a booth by the pinewood; and they were kind and guest-fain with me, and gave me meat and drink and lodging, and bade me come to Shadowy Vale in the spring, when I should know more of them. And that was I fain of; for they are wise and goodly men. But I deemed no more of those that I saw there save as men who had been outlawed by their own folk for deeds that were unlawful belike, but not shameful, and were biding their time of return, and were living as they might meanwhile. But of the whole Folk and their foemen knew I no more than ye did, till two days agone, when I met them again in Shadowy Vale. Also I think before long ye shall see their chieftain in Burgstead, for he hath a word for us. Lastly, my mind it is that those brown-clad men who helped Hall-face and his company in the wood were nought but men of this Earl-kin seeking their foemen; for indeed they told me that they had come upon a battle in the woodland wherein they had slain their foemen. Now have I told you all that ye need to know concerning these matters.”

===Chinese===
人群中又起了一阵低语，像是众人并不畏惧，只一心要在将至的祸事中找出一条出路。却无人开口，直到长老说道：

"儿子，你是何时初次撞见这壮士之族（Earl-folk）的？"

面神道："去年深秋。"

铁面道："那么你本可以早些把此事告诉我们。"

他儿子道："不错；可直到两天以前，这些事我还一无所知，或只略知一二。去年秋天我在林间游荡，在荒岭上一座松林边的棚屋里，偶然撞见这一族中的几个人；他们待我甚厚、热情留客，给我饮食与住处，邀我春日去幽谷一聚，到时我便可对他们知道更多。那正合我意；因为他们都是些明智而美好的人。但我当时对所见之人别无他想，只把他们当作因某些事被本族逐出之人——那些事或许不合法，却并非可耻——他们正等待时机重返家园，暂且随遇而安地过活。至于全族之事与其仇敌，我知道的并不比你们多，直到两天前我在幽谷与他们再度相遇。此外我想，不久你们便能在堡镇见到他们的首领，因为他有一言要带给我们。最后，依我之见，林中相助厅面及其同伙的那些羊褐衣人，无非就是这壮士之族（Earl-kin）中寻觅仇敌之人；因为他们确曾告诉我，他们在林中撞见一场战斗，并在战阵中斩杀了他们的仇敌。关于这些事，该让你们知道的，我都已讲完了。"

===Original===
Again was there silence as Iron-face sat pondering a question for his son; then a goodman of the Upper Dale, Gritgarth to wit, spake and said:

“Gold-mane mine, tell us how many is this folk; I mean their fighting-men?”

“Well asked, neighbour,” said Iron-face.

Said Face-of-god: “Their fighting-men of full age may be five score; but besides that there shall be some two or three score of women that will fight, whoever says them nay; and many of these are little worse in the field than men; or no worse, for they shoot well in the bow. Moreover, there will be a full score of swains not yet twenty winters old whom ye may not hinder to fight if anything is a-doing.”

“This is no great host,” said the Alderman; “yet if they deem there is little to lose by fighting, and nought to gain by sitting still, they may go far in winning their desire; and that more especially if they may draw into their quarrel some other valiant Folk more in number than they be. I marvel not, though, they were kind to thee, son Gold-mane, if they knew who thou wert.”

“They knew it,” said Face-of-god.

===Chinese===
铁面坐着，暗暗盘算一个要问儿子的问题，众人又静下来；随后上谷一位家主——便是人称砾庭（Gritgarth）的那位——开口说道：

"我的金鬃啊，你且说说这一族人有多少；我是说他们能上阵的壮丁。"

铁面道："邻居问得好。"

面神道："他们成年的壮丁，约莫一百之数；除此之外，还有大约四十至六十名女子愿意参战——任谁也拦不住；其中许多人在战场上比起男子毫不逊色，甚至不遑多让，因为她们弓箭射得极准。此外，还有足足二十名未满二十岁的少年，一旦有事，谁也拦不住他们上阵。"

长老道："这算不得一支大军；然而他们若是觉得战则损失无几、坐守则一无所获，便能在实现所愿之上走得甚远；尤其若是他们能将另一族人数更多、同样英勇之民拉入其事之中。不过，金鬃吾儿，他们既知你是何人，待你这么好，我并不奇怪。"

面神道："他们知道。"

===Original===
“Neighbours,” said the Alderman, “have ye any rede hereon, and aught to say to back your rede?”

Then spake the Fiddle: “As ye know and may see, I am now very old, and, as the word goes, unmeet for battle: yet might I get me to the field, either on mine own legs or on the legs of some four-foot beast, I would strike, if it were but one stroke, on these pests of the earth. And, Alderman, meseemeth we shall do amiss if we bid not the Earl-folk of Shadowy Vale to be our fellows in arms in this adventure. For look you, how few soever they be, they will be sure to know the ways of our foemen, and the mountain passes, and the surest and nighest roads across the necks and the mires of the waste; and though they be not a host, yet shall they be worth a host to us?”

When men heard his words they shouted for joy of them; for hatred of the Dusky Men who should so mar their happy life in the Dale was growing up in them, and the more that hatred waxed, the more waxed their love of those valiant ones.

===Chinese===
长老道："诸位邻里，于此事你们可有良策？可有陈词以佐你们之策？"

于是提琴说道："诸位所共见、所共知，我如今已十分老迈，俗话说的，不堪一战了：然而只要我能到得阵前——或是凭自家双腿，或是借某头四脚牲口的腿——我也要对这些世间大害挥上一击，哪怕只砍得一下也好。长老啊，依我之见，我们若不邀请幽谷这壮士之族与我们结盟并肩，共赴此役，那便是我们的失策。因为你想，他们无论多么人少，必定熟知我们敌人的路数、山间的诸隘口，以及越过荒原诸山颈与沼地最稳最近的道路；他们虽算不得一支大军，于我们却抵得上一支大军，是不是？"

众人闻言，欢呼称善；因为对那要将他们山谷中的安乐生活毁于一旦的黝暗人，众人心中正生出仇恨，而这仇恨愈盛，对那些壮士的爱戴也随之愈深。

===Original===
Now Red-coat of Waterless spake again: he was a big man, both tall and broad, ruddy-faced and red-haired, some forty winters old. He said:

“Life hath been well with us of the Lower Dale, and we deem that we have much to lose in losing it. Yet ill would the bargain be to buy life with thralldom: we have been over-merry hitherto for that. Therefore I say, to battle! And as to these men, these well-wishers of Face-of-god, if they also are minded for battle with our foes, we were fools indeed if we did not join them to our company, were they but one score instead of six.”

Men shouted again, and they said that Red-coat had spoken well. Then one after other the goodmen of the Dale came and gave their word for fellowship in arms with the Men of Shadowy Vale, if there were such as Face-of-god had said, which they doubted not; and amongst them that spake were Fox of Nethertown, and War-well, and Gritgarth, and Bearswain, and Warcliff, and Hart of Highcliff, and Worm of Willowholm, and Bullsbane, and Highneb of the Marsh: all these were stout men-at-arms and men of good counsel.

===Chinese===
此时无水地之红衣又开口了：他身材魁梧，高大宽阔，脸膛红润、一头红发，约莫四十岁上下。他说道：

"我们下谷这一带日子一向过得不错，丢了这样的日子，我们损失可不小。然而用奴役来换活命，这笔买卖可太亏了：我们从前日子过得太舒坦，可受不了那个。因此我说——开战吧！至于这些人，这些与面神交好之人，他们若是也有意与我们同仇敌忾，那我们若不把他们拉入伙，便是天大的蠢事——哪怕他们只有二十人，而非一百二十人。"

众人再次欢呼，都说红衣说得好。于是谷中各位家主一个接一个上前，许下与幽谷之民并肩结盟的誓言——只消幽谷果有面神所言之人，而他们对此毫不怀疑；其中表态的，有下屯（Nethertown）之狐狸（Fox）、战泉（War-well）、砾庭（Gritgarth）、熊僮（Bearswain）、战崖（Warcliff）、高崖（Highcliff）之鹿（Hart）、柳洼（Willowholm）之蛟（Worm）、牛祸（Bullsbane）、沼地（the Marsh）之高喙（Highneb）：这些人个个都是剽悍的战兵，也是有识之士。

===Original===
Last of all the Alderman spake and said:

“As to the war, that must we needs meet if all be sooth that we have heard, and I doubt it not.
