“Now therefore let us look to it like wise men while time yet serves. Ye shall know that the muster of the Dalesmen will bring under shield eight long hundreds of men well-armed, and of the Shepherd-Folk four hundreds, and of the Woodlanders two hundreds; and this is a goodly host if it be well ordered and wisely led. Now am I your Alderman and your Doomster, and I can heave up a sword as well as another maybe, nor do I think that I shall blench in the battle; yet I misdoubt me that I am no leader or orderer of men-of-war: therefore ye will do wisely to choose a wiser man-at-arms than I be for your War-leader; and if at the Great Folk-mote, when all the Houses and Kindreds are gathered, men yea-say your choosing, then let him abide; but if they naysay it, let him give place to another. For time presses. Will ye so choose?”

“Yea, yea!” cried all men.

“Good is that, neighbours,” said the Alderman. “Whom will ye have for War-leader? Consider well.”

Short was their rede, for every man opened his mouth and cried out “Face-of-god!” Then said the Alderman:

“The man is young and untried; yet though he is so near akin to me, I will say that ye will do wisely to take him; for he is both deft of his hands and brisk; and moreover, of this matter he knoweth more than all we together. Now therefore I declare him your War-leader till the time of the Great Folk-mote.”

===Chinese===
最后，长老开口说道：

"至于这一战——倘若我们所闻句句属实，这一战我们非打不可；我对此并不怀疑。

"既然如此，时机尚容得我们，我们便当如明智之人那样早作筹画。你们须知：谷民（the Dalesmen）征召起来，可领出兵甲齐备之壮丁八个长百（long hundreds），牧羊之民（the Shepherd-Folk）出四百，林中汉子（the Woodlanders）出两百——这可算得一支堂堂之师，只要调度得宜、统率有方。我如今是你们的长老、你们的裁断者（Doomster）；我也能和别人一样举剑挥砍，临阵之时我也自问不会退缩；但我自忖并非统兵列阵之才：因此你们若另举一位比我更通兵事的壮士作你们的战首（War-leader），乃是明智之举；待到大民众大会之上，各族各宗齐聚之时，众人若肯应承你们此番推举，便让他留任；若众人不允，便让他让位于另一个人。因为时日迫促。你们可愿这般推举？"

"愿意，愿意！"众人齐声呼道。

"好极了，邻里们，"长老道，"你们要推何人作战首？还须细细斟酌。"

他们的计议短得很，因为人人张开嘴，同声高呼"面神！"长老于是说道：

"此人年轻、未经考验；然而他虽与我如此亲近，我仍要说，你们选他乃是明智之举；因为他既手巧、又麻利；再者，此事之中，他所知道的胜过我们所有人加在一起。故此我现在宣布：在大民众大会召开之前，他是你们的战首。"

===Original===
Then all men shouted with great glee and clashed their weapons; but some few put their heads together and spake apart a little while, and then one of them, Red-coat of Waterless to wit, came forward and said: “Alderman, some of us deem it good that Stone-face, the old man wise in war and in the ways of the Wood, should be named as a counsellor to the War-leader; and Hall-face, a very brisk and strong young man, to be his right hand and sword-bearer.”

“Good is that,” said Iron-face. “Neighbours, will ye have it so?” This also they yeasaid without delay, and the Alderman declared Stone-face and Hall-face the helpers of Face-of-god in this business. Then he said:

“If any hath aught to say concerning what is best to be done at once, it were good that he said it now before all and not to murmur and grudge hereafter.”

None spake save the Fiddle, who said: “Alderman and War-leader, one thing would I say: that if these foemen are anywise akin to those overrunners of the Folks of whom the tales went in my youth (for I also as well as Stone-face mind me well of those tales concerning them), it shall not avail us to sit still and await their onset. For then may they not be withstood, when they have gathered head and burst out and over the folk that have been happy, even as the waters that overtop a dyke and cover with their muddy ruin the deep green grass and the flower-buds of spring. Therefore my rede is, as soon as may be to go seek these folk in the woodland and wheresoever else they may be wandering. What sayest thou, Face-of-god?”

“My rede is as thine,” said he; “and to begin with, I do now call upon ten tens of good men to meet me in arms at the beginning of Wildlake’s Way tomorrow morning at daybreak; and I bid my brother Hall-face to summon such as are most meet thereto. For this I deem good, that we scour the wood daily at present till we hear fresh tidings from them of Shadowy Vale, who are nigher than we to the foemen. Now, neighbours, are ye ready to meet me?”

Then all shouted, “Yea, we will go, we will go!”

===Chinese===
众人皆大欢喜，高声欢呼，兵器相击；但有少数几人交头接耳、在一旁私议了片刻，随后其中一人——便是无水地之红衣——上前说道："长老，我们几人以为：宜推举深谙战事与林中路数的老人石面，出任战首的参谋；再由极为利落强壮的年轻人厅面，作他的右臂与执剑官。"

铁面道："很好。邻里们，你们意下如何？"众人也立即应承，长老便宣布石面与厅面为面神在此事中之辅佐。随后他说道：

"若有人对眼下立刻该做什么有话要说，最好现在当众说出来，免得日后窃窃私语、心怀怨怼。"

除提琴外无人开口。提琴说道："长老与战首先听我一言：假如这些敌人与我年少时传说中倾覆各族的那伙人有所瓜葛（因为我也和石面一样，清楚地记得那些关于他们的传说），那么坐守待敌便毫无益处。因为一旦他们聚成势头，冲将出来、淹没那些一向安乐的族人，那时便无可抵挡了——正如洪水漫过堤坝，以其浑浊的毁坏，将深绿的青草与春天的花蕾尽数淹没。因此我的主意是：尽早进入林中，四处搜寻这帮家伙，无论他们在何处游荡。面神，你以为如何？"

面神道："我的主意和你一样；首先，我现在就号召一百名好汉，明晨天亮之时，全副武装到野湖径（Wildlake's Way）起点与我相会；我并委托我兄弟厅面，去召集其中最为合用之人。因为依我之见，目前我们每日都应扫荡林子，直至再得幽谷方面的消息——他们离敌人比我们更近。诸位邻里，你们可愿来赴约？"

众人齐声呼道："愿意，我们去，我们去！"

===Original===
Said the Alderman: “Now have we made provision for the war in that which is nearest to our hands. Yet have we to deal with the matter of the fellowship with the Folk whom Face-of-god hath seen. This is a matter for thee, son, at least till the Great Folk-mote is holden. Tell me then, shall we send a messenger to Shadowy Vale to speak with this folk, or shall we abide the chieftain’s coming?”

“By my rede,” said Face-of-god, “we shall abide his coming: for first, though I might well make my way thither, I doubt if I could give any the bearings, so that he could come there without me; and belike I am needed at home, since I am become War-leader. Moreover, when your messenger cometh to Shadowy Vale, he may well chance to find neither the chieftain there, nor the best of his men; for whiles are they here, and whiles there, as they wend following after the Dusky Men.”

“It is well, son,” said the Alderman, “let it be as thou sayest: soothly this matter must needs be brought before the Great Folk-mote. Now will I ask if any other hath any word to say, or any rede to give before this Gate-thing sundereth?”

But no man came forward, and all men seemed well content and of good heart; and it was now well past noontide.

===Chinese===
长老道："眼下手边最近的战事之备，我们已然安排妥当。然而与面神所见之族结盟一事，尚待料理。吾儿，此事至少在大民众大会召开之前，由你来主理。那么你且说，我们是该遣一名使者前往幽谷与此族接洽，还是在此等候他们的首领前来？"

面神道："依我之见，我们当等候他前来：一则，虽说我大可亲自领人前往那里，但我不信我能给旁人说清路径、叫他离了我便能寻到；二则，我既已成战首，家中多半也离不开我。再者，贵使到了幽谷，也很可能既见不着首领，也见不着他们最精锐的部下；因为他们追踪黝暗人，行踪无定，时在此处，时在彼处。"

长老道："甚好，吾儿，便依你所言：此事日后确须拿到大民众大会之上再议。现在我再问一句：这场门会散会之前，可还有旁人有话要说、有策可献？"

却无一人上前；众人皆面露满意之色、心怀壮志；此时已过了正午许久。

## XXXVIII Of the Great Folk-Mote: Atonements Given, and Men Made Sackless / 三十八 大民众大会：偿金既献，众人皆得清白

===Original===
Amidst the clamour uprose the Alderman; for it was clear to all men that the Folk-mote should be holden at once, and the matters of the War, and the Fellowship, and the choosing of the War-leader, speedily dealt with. So the Alderman fell to hallowing in the Folk-mote: he went up to the Altar of the Gods, and took the Gold-ring off it, and did it on his arm; then he drew his sword and waved it toward the four airts, and spake; and the noise and shouting fell, and there was silence but for him:

"Herewith I hallow in this Folk-mote of the Men of the Dale and the Sheepcotes and the Woodland, in the name of the Warrior and the Earth-god and the Fathers of the kindreds. Now let not the peace of the Mote be broken. Let not man rise against man, or bear blade or hand, or stick or stone against any. If any man break the Peace of the Holy Mote, let him be a man accursed, a wild-beast in the Holy Places; an outcast from home and hearth, from bed and board, from mead and acre; not to be holpen with bread, nor flesh, nor wine; nor flax, nor wool, nor any cloth; nor with sword, nor shield, nor axe, nor ploughshare; nor with horse, nor ox, nor ass; with no saddle-beast nor draught-beast; nor with wain, nor boat, nor way-leading; nor with fire nor water; nor with any world's wealth. Thus let him who hath cast out man be cast out by man. Now is hallowed-in the Folk-mote of the Men of the Dale and the Sheepcotes and the Woodlands."

===Chinese===
喧嚣之中，长老起立；盖众人皆明白，民众大会须当即召开，战事、结盟、战首之选诸项，皆须从速议决。于是长老着手为此民众大会行圣化之礼：他登上诸神祭坛，取下其上之金环，戴于臂上；继而拔剑，朝四方挥舞，开口陈词；喧呼呐喊之声乃息，全场唯余其一人之声：

"借此，我以武神（the Warrior）、地神（the Earth-god）及诸宗族先祖之名，圣化此堡谷、羊栏、林莽之民的民众大会。自今以后，大会之和平不可破坏。人不可起而攻人，不可持刃、动手，亦不可以棍棒、石块加于任何人。若有人破坏此神圣大会之和平，他便当受诅咒，于圣地之中视若野兽；逐出于家宅与炉火之外，床笫与餐桌之外，草地与田亩之外；不得以面包、肉食、酒醴助之；不得以麻、以毛、以任何布帛助之；不得以剑、以盾、以斧、以犁刃助之；不得以马、以牛、以驴助之；不得以任何坐骑、任何挽兽助之；不得以车、以舟、以指路助之；不得以火、以水助之；不得以世间任何财货助之。凡驱逐人者，亦当为人所驱逐。如今，堡谷、羊栏、林莽之民的民众大会，圣化已成。"

===Original===
Therewith he waved his sword again toward the four airts, and went and sat down in his place. But presently he arose again, and said:

"Now if man hath aught to say against man, and claimeth boot of any, or would lay guilt on any man's head, let him come forth and declare it; and the judges shall be named, and the case shall be tried this afternoon or tomorrow. Yet first I shall tell you that I, the Alderman of the Dalesmen, doomed one Iron-face of the House of the Face to pay a double fine, for that he drew a sword at the Gate-thing of Burgstead with the intent to break the peace thereof. Thou, Green-sleeve, bring forth the peace-breaker's fine, that Iron-face may lay the same on the Altar."

===Chinese===
说罢，他又朝四方挥剑，归座于己位。然而不多时他又起立，说道：

"如今，人与人之间若有何话要说，若向某人索取赔偿，或欲将罪责加于某人头上，便请他上前当众声明；届时将推举判官，此案于今日午后或明日审理。然有一事先须告知诸位：我，谷民之长老，曾判面神之宅的铁面（Iron-face）缴纳双倍罚金，缘由是他在堡镇城门议事会（the Gate-thing of Burgstead）之上拔剑，意图破坏其和平。绿袖（Green-sleeve），你将那破坏和平者所应缴之罚金取来，好让铁面将其献于祭坛之上。"

===Original===
Then came forth a man from the men of the Face bearing a bag, and he brought it to Iron-face, who went up to the Altar and poured forth weighed gold from the bag thereon, and said:

"Warden of the Dale, come thou and weigh it!"

"Nay," quoth the Warden, "it needeth not, no man here doubteth thee, Alderman Iron-face."

===Chinese===
于是面族（the Face）之中走出一人，手捧一囊，送至铁面跟前；铁面登上祭坛，自囊中倾出已称好的金子于其上，说道：

"堡谷的守事，你来称一称！"

"不必，"那守事答道，"无须如此，在座并无一人疑你，长老铁面。"

===Original===
A murmur of yea-say went up, and none had a word to say against the Alderman, but they praised him rather: also men were eager to hear of the war, and the fellowship, and to be done with these petty matters. Then the Alderman rose again and said:

"Hath any man a grief against any other of the Kindreds of the Dale, or the Sheepcotes, or the Woodlands?"

None answered or stirred; so after he had waited a while, he said:

"Is there any who hath any guilt to lay against a Stranger, an Outlander, being such a man as he deems we can come at?"

===Chinese===
一片附和之声四起，无人对长老有一言非议，反倒纷纷称许：众人也急于听闻战事、结盟之事，只想早日了结这些琐碎纠葛。于是长老再次起立，说道：

"堡谷诸宗族、牧羊之民、林中之民之中，可有人对他人心怀怨隙？"

无人应声，亦无人动；他等候片刻，又道：

"可有人要将罪责加之于某个外乡人、异乡客身上——只要是诸位以为我等所能找得到之人？"

===Original===
Thereat was a stir amongst the Men of the Fleece of the Shepherds, and their ranks opened, and there came forth an ill-favoured lean old man, long-nebbed, blear-eyed, and bent, girt with a rusty old sword, but not otherwise armed. And all men knew Penny-thumb, who had been ransacked last autumn. As he came forth, it seemed as if his neighbours had been trying to hold him back; but a stout, broad-shouldered man, black-haired and red-bearded, made way for the old man, and led him out of the throng, and stood by him; and this man was well armed at all points, and looked a doughty carle. He stood side by side with Penny-thumb, right in front of the men of his house, and looked about him at first somewhat uneasily, as though he were ashamed of his fellow; but though many smiled, none laughed aloud; and they forbore, partly because they knew the man to be a good man, partly because of the solemn tide of the Folk-mote, and partly in sooth because they wished all this to be over, and were as men who had no time for empty mirth.

===Chinese===
此言一出，牧羊之民中"羊皮族"（the Fleece）的队伍里一阵骚动，人列分作两开，走出一人：是个面目可憎、瘦骨嶙峋的老者，长鼻、浊眼、背弓，腰间悬一口生锈的旧剑，除此之外并无武装。众人都认得他——此人便是去秋曾遭洗劫的铜板拇（Penny-thumb）。他走出来时，似乎邻人们本欲将他拦住；却有一个壮硕、肩宽背阔、黑发红须的汉子，为这老者让开路，引他出了人群，立在旁侧；此人全副武装，一望便是个剽悍的好汉。他与铜板拇并肩而立，正对着自家氏族之人，起初四下张望，神色有几分不自在，仿佛以这同伴为耻；众人之中虽多有含笑者，却并无一人出声大笑；他们之所以隐忍不发，一来因知这汉子本是个好人，二来因民众大会之时庄严肃穆，三来其实也因众人但愿这些琐事早些了结，正如那无暇空作欢笑之人。

===Original===
Then said the Alderman: "What wouldest thou, Penny-thumb, and thou, Bristler, son of Brightling?"

Then Penny-thumb began to speak in a high squeaky voice: "Alderman, and Lord of the Folk!" But therewithal Bristle, pulled him back, and said:

"I am the man who hath taken this quarrel upon me, and have sworn upon the Holy Boar to carry this feud through; and we deem, Alderman, that if they who slew Rusty and ransacked Penny-thumb be not known now, yet they soon may be."

===Chinese===
于是长老道："铜板拇，你所求为何？还有你，鬃子（Bristler），亮林（Brightling）之子，你所求又为何？"

铜板拇便以又高又尖的嗓音开口道："长老，万民之主啊——"话未说完，鬃子已将他一把拉住，说道：

"我才是承下这桩争执之人，我已对圣猪（the Holy Boar）起誓，定要将此仇追究到底；长老，我们以为，杀害锈子（Rusty）、洗劫铜板拇之人，纵然眼下尚未查明，不久也必可水落石出。"

===Original===
As he spake, came forth those three men of the Shepherds and the two Dalesmen who had sworn with him on the Holy Boar. Then up stood Folk-might, and came forth into the field, and said:

===Chinese===
他说话之间，曾随他一同在圣猪前起誓的那三位牧羊之民与两位谷民，也都走了出来。这时民强（Folk-might）起立，步入场中，说道：

===Original===
"Bristler, son of Brightling, and ye other good men and true, it is but sooth that the ransackers and the slayer may soon be known; and here I declare them unto you: I it was and none other who slew Rusty; and I was the leader of those who ransacked Penny-thumb, and cowed Harts-bane of Greentofts. As for the slaying of Rusty, I slew him because he chased me, and would not forbear, so that I must either slay or be slain, as hath befallen me erewhile, and will befall again, methinks. As for the ransacking of Penny-thumb, I needed the goods that I took, and he needed them not, since he neither used them, nor gave them away, and, they being gone, he hath lived no worser than aforetime. Now I say, that if ye will take the outlawry off me, which, as I hear, ye laid upon me, not knowing me, then will I handsel self-doom to thee, Bristler, if thou wilt bear thy grief to purse, and I will pay thee what thou wilt out of hand; or if perchance thou wilt call me to Holm, thither will I go, if thou and I come unslain out of this war. As to the ransacking and cowing of Harts-bane, I say that I am sackless therein, because the man is but a ruffler and a man of violence, and hath cowed many men of the Dale; and if he gainsay me, then do I call him to the Holm after this war is over; either him or any man who will take his place before my sword."

===Chinese===
"鬃子，亮林之子，以及诸位义士良民：那洗劫之徒与杀人凶手不久便可查明——此言不虚；我此刻便向你们和盘托出：杀锈子的人是我，并非我之外的任何人；率众洗劫铜板拇、威吓绿草丘（Greentofts）的鹿厄（Harts-bane）的，也是我。至于杀锈子一事，我之所以杀他，是因为他一路追逼于我、不肯罢休，致使我不杀他便必为他所杀——此等情形，我先前已曾遇上，想来日后还会再遇上。至于洗劫铜板拇一事，我所取之物乃我所需，他却不所需，因他既不用，也不施与，那些东西既已不存，他的日子也过得不比从前差。如今我说：你们若肯撤销对我的放逐之判——据我所闻，你们在不知我身份之时曾下此判——那么，鬃子，你若肯将此怨了之于钱财，我便授你以自定裁决之权（self-doom），你要多少，我当场偿付；倘若你要约我霍尔姆（Holm，决斗之岛）一决，只要你我皆能自此战中全身而归，我必赴约。至于洗劫、威吓鹿厄一事，我声明我于此无罪，因那人本是个横行生事之徒、暴戾之辈，曾威吓过谷中多人；他若不服，那么待此战事一了，我也约他霍尔姆决斗——无论他本人，还是任何敢代他立于我剑前之人。"

===Original===
Then he held his peace, and man spake to man, and a murmur arose, as they said for the more part that it was a fair and manly offer. But Bristler called his fellows and Penny-thumb to him, and they spake together; and sometimes Penny-thumb's shrill squeak was heard above the deep-voiced talk of the others; for he was a man that harboured malice. But at last Bristler spake out and said:

"Tall man, we know that thou art a chieftain and of good will to the men of the Dale and their friends, and that want drave thee to the ransacking, and need to the manslaying, and neither the living nor the dead to whom thou art guilty are to be called good men; therefore will I bring the matter to purse, if thou wilt handsel me self-doom."

"Yea, even so let it be," quoth Folk-might; and stepped forward and took Bristler by the hand, and handselled him self-doom. Then said Bristler:

===Chinese===
他说完便默然不语；人与人之间交头接耳，一阵低语四起，多数人都道这是一番公道磊落的提议。鬃子却将自己的同伴与铜板拇召到身边，几人聚议；众人低沉的语声之中，时时冒出铜板拇那尖利的尖叫——他原是个心怀宿怨、耿耿于怀之人。末了鬃子扬声说道：

"高汉子，我们知道你是一位首领，对谷民及其友盟心怀善意；也知道是窘迫驱你去洗劫、是不得已逼你去杀人；况且你所亏欠的，无论活人还是死者，都算不得什么好人；因此，你若肯授我自定裁决之权，我便将此事了之于钱财。"

"好，便如此定下。"民强道。他上前一步，握住鬃子的手，授他以自定裁决之权。鬃子于是说道：

===Original===
"Though Rusty was no good man, and though he followed thee to slay thee, yet was he in his right therein, since he was following up his goodman's gear; therefore shalt thou pay a full blood-wite for him, that is to say, the worth of three hundreds in weed-stuff in whatso goods thou wilt. As for the ransacking of Penny-thumb, he shall deem himself well paid if thou give him our hundreds in weed-stuff for that which thou didst borrow of him."

===Chinese===
"锈子虽不是什么好人，他追你欲杀你，却也实在理之当然——因他不过是在追讨自家东家的财物；所以，你必须为他缴一份足额的血金（blood-wite），亦即值三长百布帛之物，任凭你以何种货物偿付。至于洗劫铜板拇一事，你所'借'去不还的那些东西，你若还他两长百布帛之物，他便该自认偿付丰厚了。"

===Original===
Then Penny-thumb set up his squeak again, but no man hearkened to him, and each man said to his neighbour that it was well doomed of Bristler, and neither too much nor too little. But Folk-might bade Wood-wont to bring thither to him that which he had borne to the Mote; and he brought forth a big sack, and Folk-might emptied it on the earth, and lo! the silver rings of the slain felons, and they lay in a heap on the green field, and they were the best of silver. Then the Elder of the Dale-wardens weighed out from the heap the blood-wite for Rusty, according to the due measure of the hundred in weed-stuff, and delivered it unto Bristler. And Folk-might said:

"Draw nigh now, Penny-thumb, and take what thou wilt of this gear, which I need not, and grudge not at me henceforward."

But Penny-thumb was afraid, and abode where he was; and Bristler laughed, and said: "Take it, goodman, take it; spare not other men's goods as thou dost thine own."

And Folk-might stood by, smiling faintly: so Penny-thumb plucked up a heart, and drew nigh trembling, and took what he durst from that heap; and all that stood by said that he had gotten a full double of what had been awarded to him. But as for him, he went his ways straight from the Motestead, and made no stay till he had gotten him home, and laid the silver up in a strong coffer; and thereafter he bewailed him sorely that he had not taken the double of that which he took, since none would have said him nay.

===Chinese===
铜板拇又叫嚷起来，却无人理睬他；人人皆与邻座称道鬃子裁得公允，不多不少，恰到好处。民强却命林习（Wood-wont）将他带来大会之物取至此处；林习取出一只大口袋，民强将其倾倒于地——看哪！皆是那些被杀恶徒身上的银环，堆作一堆，落在青草地上，乃是成色最上等的纯银。堡谷众守事之长便自那堆中，按每一长百布帛应折银两的恰当成数，称出锈子的血金，交付鬃子。民强说道：

"铜板拇，你如今上前来吧，这堆东西我并不需要，你要什么便拿什么，往后可莫再怨我。"

铜板拇却害怕起来，立在原地不敢上前；鬃子大笑，说道："拿吧，老人家，拿吧；莫像吝惜自家东西那样，吝惜别人的东西呀。"

民强立在一旁，微微含笑：铜板拇这才壮起胆来，哆嗦着上前，从那堆中尽拣自己敢拿之物；旁观之人都说，他所取之物，已是所判给他之数的整整两倍。至于他自己，却径自从议事坪（the Motestead）离了场，一路不作停留，直奔到家，将银子锁进一口坚固的柜子里；此后他又痛悔不已——悔不曾将所拿之数再翻上一番，因为反正无人会拦他。

===Original===
When he was gone, the Alderman arose and said:

"Now, since the fines have been paid duly and freely, according to the dooming of Bristler, take we off the outlawry from Folk-might and his fellows, and account them to be sackless before us."

Then he called for other cases; but no man had aught more to bring forward against any man, either of the kindreds or the Strangers.

===Chinese===
他既去，长老起立说道：

"如今，罚金既已依照鬃子之裁决，如数而情愿地缴清，我们便撤销对民强及其同伴的放逐之判，在我等面前视其为清白无罪之人。"

随后他又询问可有其他案子；然而无论诸宗族之人，还是外乡客人，再无人对任何人提出任何控告。

## XXXIX Of the Great Folk-Mote: Men Take Rede of the War-Faring, the Fellowship, and the War-Leader. Folk-Might Telleth Whence His People Came. The Folk-Mote Sundered / 三十九 论大民众大会：众议远征、同盟与战首之人。民强述其族之所从来。民众大会解散

===Original===
Now a great silence fell upon the throng, and they stood as men abiding some new matter. Unto them arose the Alderman, and said:
"Men of the Dale, and ye Shepherds and Woodlanders; it is well known to you that we have foemen in the wood and beyond it; and now have we gotten sure tidings, that they will not abide at home or in the wood, but are minded to fall upon us at home. Now therefore I will not ask you whether ye will have peace or war; for with these foemen ye may have peace no otherwise save by war. But if ye think with me, three things have ye to determine: first, whether ye will abide your foes in your own houses, or will go meet them at theirs; next, whether ye will take to you as fellows in arms a valiant folk of the children of the Gods, who are foemen to our foemen; and lastly, what man ye will have to be your War-leader. Now, I bid all those here assembled, to speak hereof, any man of them that will, either what they may have conceived in their own minds, or what their kindred may have put into their mouths to speak."

===Chinese===
此时众人之中忽然一片大寂静，众皆肃立，如同等待新事一般。于是长老（the Alderman）起身，对他们说道：

「谷中之民，尔等牧羊之民与林中汉子（Woodlanders）啊：尔等皆知，林中及林外皆有敌寇；今我等已得确讯，彼等不再安居于家、盘桓于林，而欲兴兵犯我乡土。故而我今日不再问尔等欲和欲战；因为对此等敌寇，除一战之外，别无他途可得和平。然而尔等若与我所见相同，则有三种事须要决断：其一，是据守自家以待敌至，抑或径往敌巢迎击；其二，是否接纳一支神之子女（children of the Gods）的勇武之族为同袍并肩——他们乃我敌之敌；其三，欲推何人为我等之战首（War-leader）。我今请在此集会之人，凡愿发言者，皆可就此陈词——或述一己之所筹谋，或传本族之所嘱托。」

===Original===
Therewith he sat down, and in a little while came forth old Hall-ward of the House of the Steer, and stood before the Alderman, and said: "O Alderman, all we say: Since war is awake we will not tarry, but will go meet our foes while it is yet time. The valiant men of whom thou tellest shall be our fellows, were there but three of them. We know no better War-leader than Face-of-god of the House of the Face. Let him lead us."

Therewith he went his ways; and next came forth War-well, and said: "The House of the Bridge would have Face-of-god for War-leader, these tall men for fellows, and the shortest way to meet the foe." And he went back to his place.

Next came Fox of Upton, and said: "Time presses, or much might be spoken. Thus saith the House of the Bull: Let us go meet the foe, and take these valiant strangers for way-leaders, and Face-of-god for War-leader." And he also went back again.

Then came forth two men together, an old man and a young, and the old man spake as soon as he stood still: "The Men of the Vine bid me say their will: They will not stay at home to have their houses burned over their heads, themselves slain on their own hearths, and their wives haled off to thralldom. They will take any man for their fellow in arms who will smite stark strokes on their side. They know Face-of-god, and were liefer of him for War-leader than any other, and they will follow him wheresoever he leadeth. Thus my kindred biddeth me say, and I hight Fork-beard of Lea. If I live through this war, I shall have lived through five."

Therewith he went back to his place; but the young man lifted up his voice and said: "To all this I say yea, and so am I bidden by the kindred of the Sickle. I am Red-beard of the Knolls, the son of my father." And he went to his place again.

Then came forth Stone-face, and said: "The House of the Face saith: Lead us through the wood, O Face-of-god, thou War-leader, and ye warriors of the Wolf. I am Stone-face, as men know, and this word hath been given to me by the kindred." And he took his place again.

Then came forth together the three chiefs of the Shepherds, to wit Hound-under-Greenbury, Strongitharm, and the Hyllier; and Strongitharm spake for all three, and said:
"The Men of Greenbury, and they of the Fleece and the Thorn, are of one accord, and bid us say that they are well pleased to have Face-of-god for War-leader; and that they will follow him and the warriors of the Wolf to live or die with them; and that they are ready to go meet the foe at once, and will not skulk behind the walls of Greenbury."

Therewith the three went back again to their places.

===Chinese===
长老言罢坐下。不多时，犍牛族（the House of the Steer）年高的厅卫（Hall-ward）走上前来，立于长老跟前，说道：「长老啊，我等异口同声：战端既启，我等决不迁延，当乘时未晚，径迎我等之敌。尔所言那勇武之人，当为我等之同袍，纵彼等只有三人。战首之人，我等不知更有谁胜过面族之面神（Face-of-god of the House of the Face）。便请他率我等前行罢。」

言罢自去。其次武泉（War-well）上前，说道：「桥族（the House of the Bridge）愿推面神为战首，愿以这些高大之人为同袍，愿取最近之路以迎敌。」说罢归位。

其次上屯之狐（Fox of Upton）上前，说道：「时日紧迫，不然尽有多话可讲。公牛族（the House of the Bull）之意如此：当径迎敌寇，当以这些勇武的外来人为引路之导，当推面神为战首。」说罢亦归位。

继而两人一同上前，一老一少。那老者立定便开口：「葡藤族（the Men of the Vine）命我转陈其意：彼等决不坐守家中，任屋宇焚于头顶、己身毙于灶前、妻女被掳为奴（thralldom）。凡能在彼等身侧痛下重手、击敌寇之人，彼等皆愿与之结为同袍。彼等素识面神，与其以他人为战首，宁取面神；无论他引往何处，彼等皆愿相从。此乃我宗族命我转陈之言，我名河滩之叉须（Fork-beard of Lea）。若我能活过此战，便是活过五战之人了。」

言罢归位；那年轻人却扬声道：「此言我尽附议，镰族（the Sickle）之意亦正如此。我乃丘岗之红须（Red-beard of the Knolls），家父之子。」说罢亦归位。

继而石面（Stone-face）上前，说道：「面族（the House of the Face）之意如此：面神啊，尔乃战首；尔等狼族（the Wolf）之武士啊，请引我等穿过林莽。我乃石面，人所共知；此言乃宗族所授。」说罢归位。

继而牧羊之民的三位首领一同上前，即绿堡下之猎犬（Hound-under-Greenbury）、强臂（Strongitharm）与希利尔（the Hyllier）；强臂代三人发言，说道：

「绿堡（Greenbury）之民，羊毛与荆棘两族（the Fleece and the Thorn）之民，俱同心同德，命我等转陈：得面神为战首，甚慰其心；彼等愿追随他、追随狼族武士，与之同生共死；彼等即刻便欲迎敌，决不躲于绿堡墙后。」

三人说罢，俱各归位。

===Original===
Then came forth that tall man that bare the Banner of the Wolf, when he had given the staff into the hands of him who stood next. He came and stood over against the seat of the chieftains; and for a while he could say no word, but stood struggling with the strong passion of his joy; but at last he lifted his hands aloft, and cried out in a loud voice:
"O war, war! O death! O wounding and grief! O loss of friends and kindred! let all this be rather than the drawing back of meeting hands and the sundering of yearning hearts!" and he went back hastily to his place. But from the ranks of the Woodlanders ran forth a young man, and cried out:
"As is the word of Red-wolf, so is my word, Bears-bane of Carlstead; and this is the word which our little Folk hath put into our mouths; and O! that our hands may show the meaning of our mouths; for nought else can."

Then indeed went up a great shout, though many forebore to cry out; for now were they too much moved for words or sounds. And in special was Face-of-god moved; and he scarce knew which way to look, lest he should break out into sobs and weeping; for of late he had been much among the Woodlanders, and loved them much.

Then all the noise and clamour fell, and it was to men as if they who had come thither a folk, had now become an host of war.

===Chinese===
继而那高大之人——方才擎狼之旗者——将旗杆交于身旁之人，走上前来。他来至首领座席对面而立；半晌不能出一言，只立在原地与心中汹涌之喜悦搏斗；终于他双手高举，放声呼道：

「战啊，战！死啊！创伤与悲恸！亲友宗族之丧亡！让这一切都来罢，胜过相握之手收回、相慕之心离散！」说罢急急归位。然自林中汉子队中跑出一个年轻人，高声呼道：

「红狼（Red-wolf）之言，亦我之言——我是汉子镇（Carlstead）之熊厄（Bears-bane）；此言亦我等这一小族托付于我等口中之言；啊！愿我等之手能明我等口中之意；因为除手而外，别无可明。」

一时群声大作，纵有许多人不发一语——因彼等此时感动已极，言语声响皆不能出。面神之感尤深；他几不知当视向何处，唯恐一时失声啜泣落泪；因为近来他常与林中汉子相伴，深爱其人。

继而诸声喧嚷俱息；在众人感觉之中，方才以一族之身前来之人，如今已化作一支征战之师。

===Original===
But once again the Alderman rose up and spake:
"Now have ye yeasaid three things: That we take Face-of-god of the House of the Face for our War-leader; that we fare under weapons at once against them who would murder us; and that we take the valiant Folk of the Wolf for our fellows in arms."

Therewith he stayed his speech, and this time the shout arose clear and most mighty, with the tossing up of swords and the clashing of weapons on shields.

Then he said: "Now, if any man will speak, here is the War-leader, and here is the chief of our new friends, to answer to whatso any of the kindred would have answered."

Thereon came forth the Fiddle from amongst the Men of the Sickle, and drew somewhat nigh to the Alderman, and said:
"Alderman, we would ask of the War-leader if he hath devised the manner of our assembling, and the way of our war-faring, and the day of our hosting. More than this I will not ask of him, because we wot that in so great an assembly it may be that the foe may have some spy of whom we wot not; and though this be not likely, yet some folk may babble; therefore it is best for the wise to be wise everywhere and always. Therefore my rede it is, that no man ask any more concerning this, but let it lie with the War-leader to bring us face to face with the foe as speedily as he may."

All men said that this was well counselled. But Face-of-god arose and said: "Ye Men of the Dale, ye Shepherds and Woodlanders, meseemeth the Fiddle hath spoken wisely. Now therefore I answer him and say, that I have so ordered everything since the Gate-thing was holden at Burgstead, that we may come face to face with the foemen by the shortest of roads. Every man shall be duly summoned to the Hosting, and if any man fail, let it be accounted a shame to him forever."

A great shout followed on his words, and he sat down again. But Fox of Upton came forth and said:
"O Alderman, we have yeasaid the fellowship of the valiant men who have come to us from out of the waste; but this we have done, not because we have known them, otherwise than by what our kinsman Face-of-god hath told us concerning them, but because we have seen clearly that they will be of much avail to us in our warfare. Now, therefore, if the tall chieftain who sitteth beside thee were to do us to wit what he is, and whence he and his are come, it were well, and fain were we thereof; but if he listeth not to tell us, that also shall be well."

===Chinese===
然则长老再次起身，说道：

「尔等如今已附议三事：推面族之面神为我等战首；即刻披甲兴兵，以讨彼欲谋杀我等之人；接纳勇武的狼之民（the Folk of the Wolf）为我等并肩之同袍。」

言罢稍歇；此番呼声清亮而极壮伟，伴随着无数刀剑上挥、兵器击盾之声。

他又道：「如今若还有人欲言，这里便是战首，这里便是新友之酋，可答尔等宗族中任何人欲问之事。」

于是提琴手（the Fiddle）自镰族（the Men of the Sickle）中走出，稍近长老，说道：

「长老，我等欲问战首：他可已筹定我等集结之法、远征之路、起兵之日？此外我不愿再多问，因为我等知道，如此盛大之集会中，敌寇或有可能安插我等所不知之间谍；纵此可能性不大，或有人信口多言；故智者无论何时何地皆当持其为智。故我之议如下：再莫有人就此多问，任此事由战首决断，唯求他尽快引我等直至敌寇之前。」

众人皆称此言善哉。然则面神起身说道：「谷中之民，尔等牧羊之民、林中汉子啊，提琴手所言甚智。我今答他：自堡镇（Burgstead）门议（Gate-thing）开过以来，我已将诸事调度妥当，使我等可以最短之路径直至敌寇之前。每一名应征之人皆当依时受召点阅，若有人失期不至，当视为其人永世之辱。」

言罢又起一阵欢呼，他坐下。然上屯之狐上前说道：

「长老啊，我等已附议，愿与那自荒原外来归的勇武之人结为同盟；然我等此举，非因认识他们——除我等宗族面神所述之外，别无所知——只因我等明见：此番征战之中，彼等必大有助于我。如今若那位坐在尔旁的高大首领肯令我等知悉：他是何人，他与他族之所从来，那便甚善，我等亦欣然愿闻；若他不愿相告，那也无妨。」

===Original===
Then arose Folk-might in his place; but or ever he could open his mouth to speak, the tall Red-wolf strode forward bearing with him the Banner of the Wolf and the Sun-burst, and came and stood beside him; and the wind ran through the folds of the banner, and rippled it out above the heads of those twain. Then Folk-might spake and said:

> "O Men of the Dale and the Sheepcotes, I will do as ye bid me do;
 

 And fain were ye of the story if every deal ye knew.
 

 But long, long were its telling, were I to tell it all:
 

 Let it bide till the Cup of Deliverance ye drink from hall to hall.
> "Like you we be of the kindreds, of the Sons of the Gods we come,
 

 Midst the Mid-earth's mighty Woodland of old we had our home;
 

 But of older time we abided 'neath the mountains of the Earth,
 

 O'er which the Sun ariseth to waken woe and mirth.
> Great were we then and many; but the long days wore us thin,
 

 And war, wherein the winner hath weary work to win.
 

 And the woodland wall behind us e'en like ourselves was worn,
 

 And the tramp of the hosts of the foemen adown its glades was borne
 

 On the wind that bent our wheat-fields. So in the morn we rose,
 

 And left behind the stubble and the autumn-fruited close,
 

 And went our ways to the westward, nor turned aback to see
 

 The glare of our burning houses rise over brake and tree.
 

 But the foe was fierce and speedy, nor long they tarried there,
 

 And through the woods of battle our laden wains must fare;
 

 And the Sons of the Wolf were minished, and the maids of the Wolf waxed few,
 

 As amidst the victory-singing we fared the wildwood through.
> "So saith the ancient story, that west and west we went,
 

 And many a day of battle we had in brake, on bent;
 

 Whilst here a while we tarried, and there we hastened on,
 

 And still the battle-harvest from many a folk we won.
> "Of the tale of the days who wotteth? Of the years what man can tell,
 

 While the Sons of the Wolf were wandering, and knew not where to dwell?
 

 But at last we clomb the mountains, and mickle was our toil,
 

 As high the spear-wood clambered of the drivers of the spoil;
 

 And tangled were the passes and the beacons flared behind,
 

 And the horns of gathering onset came up upon the wind.
 

 So saith the ancient story, that we stood in a mountain-cleft,
 

 Where the ways and the valleys sundered to the right hand and the left.
 

 There in the place of sundering all woeful was the rede;
 

 We knew no land before us, and behind was heavy need.
 

 As the sword cleaves through the byrny, so there the mountain flank
 

 Cleft through the God-kin's people; and ne'er again we drank
 

 The wine of war together, or feasted side by side
 

 In the Feast-hall of the Warrior on the fruit of the battle-tide.
 

 For there we turned and sundered; unto the North we went
 

 And up along the waters, and the clattering stony bent;
 

 And unto the South and the Sheepcotes down went our sister's sons;
 

 And O for the years passed over since we saw those valiant ones!"

===Chinese===
于是民强（Folk-might）在原位起身；然而他尚未启唇，那高大的红狼便已大步上前，手执狼与旭日之旗（the Banner of the Wolf and the Sun-burst），来立在他身旁；风穿旗褶而过，将其吹展于两人头顶之上，猎猎作响。民强遂开口说道：

> 「山谷与羊栏之民啊，尔等所命，我必遵行；
 

 尔等欣然愿闻此段故事，若每一细节皆能知晓；
 

 然我若尽述无遗，则其辞甚长、甚长：
 

 且留待尔等自一厅至一厅饮解脱之杯（the Cup of Deliverance）之时再讲。
> 「如尔等一样，我等亦出于宗族；我等乃神之子（the Sons of the Gods），出自彼系，
 

 古昔我等之家园，在中土（Mid-earth）莽莽大林之间；
 

 然更古之时，我等曾栖于大地之山下，
 

 日头自此山升起，唤醒悲愁，亦唤醒欢愉。
> 我等昔日族大且盛；然漫长之岁月将我等磨薄，
 

 且战争之中，纵是胜者欲胜，亦须历尽辛劳。
 

 我等身后之林墙，亦如我等自身，日见消损，
 

 敌寇大军之脚步，沿林间通道而下，
 

 借吹弯我等麦田之风传来。于是我等于清晨起身，
 

 撇下身后残茬与秋实累累之围田，
 

 一路向西而行，并不回头去看
 

 我等燃烧屋宅之火光，自灌木与树梢之间升起。
 

 然敌寇凶猛迅捷，在彼处也未久留，
 

 我等满载之辎车，只得穿过鏖战之林；
 

 狼之子（the Sons of the Wolf）日渐减少，狼族之女亦日渐稀少，
 

 我等一路高唱凯歌，穿过那一片野林。
> 「古老传说如此说道：我等向西、向西而行，
 

 在灌木丛中、在山脊之上，度过许多鏖战之日；
 

 在此处稍歇片刻，在彼处又急忙前行，
 

 我等自一族又一族之中，仍屡获鏖战之收成。
> 「那些岁月之故事，有谁能尽知？那些年数，有谁能道尽，
 

 当狼之子仍在流浪、不知何处可栖身之时？
 

 然最终我等攀越群山，其劳苦甚巨，
 

 那驱掠之军的长枪之林，正高高攀起；
 

 山路崎岖纠缠，身后烽火熊熊燃起，
 

 集结进攻之号角，乘风而向我等来。
 

 古老传说如此说道：我等立于一处山隙之中，
 

 其处道路与山谷向左右两方分去。
 

 在那分道之处，所议之谋极为悲苦；
 

 前路我等无地可识，后顾则是迫在眉睫之危。
 

 如剑之劈开锁子甲，那山之侧翼
 

 将神族之民（the God-kin's people）一分为二；此后我等再未
 

 共饮鏖战之酒，再未并肩而坐，
 

 于武神之宴厅（the Feast-hall of the Warrior）享鏖战之果。
 

 因为在那里我等转身分离；一路向北而去，
 

 沿溪而行，沿那碎石嶙峋之山脊而上；
 

 而我等姊妹之子，则南下奔向羊栏之民；
 

 啊，自那日我等不见那些勇士以来，多少岁月已逝！」

===Original===
He ceased, and laid his right hand on the banner-staff a little below the left hand of Red-wolf; and men were so keen to hear each word that he spake, that there was no cry nor sound of voices when he had done, only the sound of the rippling banner of the Wolf over the heads of those twain. The Sun-beam bowed her head now, and wept silently. But the Bride, she had drawn her sword, and held it upright in her hand before her, and the sun smote fire from out of it.
Then it was but a little while before Red-wolf lifted up his voice, and sang:

> "Hearken a wonder, O Folk of the Field,
 

 How they that did sunder stand shield beside shield!
> Lo! the old wont and manner by fearless folk made,
 

 On the Bole of the Banner the brothers' hands laid.
> Lo! here the token of what hath betid!
 

 Grown whole is the broken, found that which was hid.
> Now one way we follow whate'er shall befall;
 

 As seeketh the swallow his yesteryear's hall.
> Seldom folk fewer to fightstead hath fared;
 

 Ne'er have men truer the battle-reed bared.
> Grey locks now I carry, and old am I grown,
 

 Nor looked I to tarry to meet with mine own.
> For we who remember the deeds of old days
 

 Were nought but the ember of battle ablaze.
> For what man might aid us? what deed and what day
 

 Should come where Weird laid us aloof from the way?
> What man save that other of Twain rent apart,
 

 Our war-friend, our Brother, the piece of our heart.
> Then hearken the wonder how shield beside shield
 

 The twain that did sunder wend down to the Field!"

===Chinese===
他言罢，将右手按于旗杆之上、略低于红狼左手所按之处；众人急于听他所说的每一字，故他言毕之时，并无呼号喧哗之声，唯闻那二人头顶之上狼之旗猎猎飘展之声。此时日光（Sun-beam）已垂首，暗自泣下。然则新娘（the Bride）已拔剑出鞘，于身前握之直立，日光击于其上，自剑上迸出火花。

过了不多时，红狼便放声而歌：

> 「田野之民啊，请听一桩奇事，
 

 那曾经离散之人，如今盾牌并肩而立！
> 看哪！此乃无畏之民所立之旧俗旧仪，
 

 兄弟之手，共按于旗杆（the Bole of the Banner）之上。
> 看哪！此乃已发生之事之征记！
 

 破者已合，隐者已现。
> 如今我等同行一路，无论何事临头，
 

 一如燕子寻去年之旧巢。
> 奔赴战阵之人，鲜有比吾辈更少；
 

 然出阵之兵，未有比吾辈更真。
> 如今我已白发盈头，年已老迈，
 

 本不望有生之年，尚能与同族相逢。
> 因为我等这些追忆昔日功业之人，
 

 不过是鏖战余烬中尚存之一缕残焰。
> 盖有何人能助我等？有何作为、何日之时，
 

 能至命运（Weird）将我等抛离正途之处？
> 除却另一人之外，又有何人——那从两分之人中被割开的一位，
 

 我等之战友、我等之兄弟，我等心头之一片。
> 故请听此桩奇事，那曾经离散之两方，
 

 如今如何盾牌并肩，齐向战阵而往！」

===Original===
Now when he had made an end, men could no longer forebear the shout; and it went up into the heavens, and was borne by the west-wind down the Dale to the ears of the stay-at-home women and men unmeet to go abroad, and it quickened their blood and the spirits within them as they heard it, and they smiled and were fain; for they knew that their kinsfolk were glad.
But when there was quiet on the Mote-field again, Folk-might spake again and said;

> "It is sooth that my Brother sayeth, and that now again we wend,
 

 All the Sons of the Wolf together, till the trouble hath an end.
 

 But as for that tale of the Ancients, it saith that we who went
 

 To the northward, climbed and stumbled o'er many a stony bent,
 

 Till we happed on that isle of the wasteland, and the grass of Shadowy Vale,
 

 Where we dwelt till we throve a little, and felt our might avail.
> "Then we fared abroad from the shadow and the little-lighted hold,
 

 And the increase fell to the valiant, and the spoil to the battle-bold,
 

 And never a man gainsaid us with the weapons in our hands;
 

 And in Silverdale the happy we gat us life and lands.
> "So wore the years o'er-wealthy; and meseemeth that ye know
 

 How we sowed and reaped destruction, and the Day of the overthrow:
 

 How we leaned on the staff we had broken, and put our lives in the hand
 

 Of those whom we had vanquished and the feeble of the land;
 

 And these were the stone of stumbling, and the burden not to be borne,
 

 When the battle-blast fell on us and our day was overworn.
 

 Thus then did our wealth bewray us, and left us wise and sad;
 

 And to you, bold men, it falleth once more to make us glad,
 

 If so your hearts are bidding, and ye deem the deed of worth.
 

 Such were we; what we shall be, 'tis yours to say henceforth."

===Chinese===
他唱罢之时，众人再也按捺不住，呼声冲天；其声入云霄，由西风沿堡谷而下，传入家居之妇人及不配出门远行之男子耳中；他们闻之，血脉与精神皆为之振奋，含笑欣然；因为他们知道他们的族人正满怀喜悦。

待议事原（the Mote-field）上重归寂静，民强又开口说道：

> 「我兄弟所言诚然不虚，如今我等又再启程，
 

 狼之子全体一同，直至这场纷扰告终。
 

 然则那段古老传说又言：我等这些北去之人，
 

 攀缘跌撞，越过无数碎石山脊，
 

 直到寻见那片荒原中之岛屿、幽谷（Shadowy Vale）之青草，
 

 在彼处栖身，直至稍稍兴盛，自知力量可用。
> 「于是我等走出幽影与那少光之堡寨，
 

 勇敢者得其增益，鏖战者得其卤获，
 

 手中既握兵刃，再无人与我等相争；
 

 在安乐的银谷（Silverdale），我等获得了生计与田地。
> 「富足之年便如此流去；尔等想必已知，
 

 我等如何播种并收割了毁灭，及那覆亡之日：
 

 我等如何倚靠那根已折断之杖，将我等性命
 

 交付于那些我等曾击败之人、与地上之怯弱之手；
 

 彼等成了我等之绊脚石，成了不可承之重担，
 

 当鏖战之灾袭我等之日，我等气数已尽。
 

 如是，我等之财富出卖了我等，留我等于明智而悲痛之中；
 

 而今又落于尔等壮士之手，再令我等欢欣，
 

 若尔等之心如此相招，且视此举为有为之事。
 

 我等昔日如此；至于今后将何如，则全凭尔等定夺。」

===Original===
He said furthermore: "How great we have been I have told you already; and ye shall see for yourselves how little we be now. Is it enough, and will ye have us for friends and brothers? How say ye?"
They answered with shout upon shout, so that all the place and the wildwood round about was full of the voice of their crying; but when the clamour fell, then spake the Alderman and said:
"Friend, and chieftain of the Wolf, thou mayst hear by this shouting of the people that we have no mind to naysay our yea-say. And know that it is not our use and manner to seek the strong for friends, and to thrust aside the weak; but rather to choose for our friends them who are of like mind to us, men in whom we put our trust. From henceforth then there is brotherhood between us; we are yours, and ye are ours; and let this endure forever!"
Then were all men full of joy; and now at last the battle seemed at hand, and the peace beyond the battle.
Then men brought the hallowed beasts all garlanded with flowers into the Doom-ring, and there were they slain and offered up unto the Gods, to wit the Warrior, the Earth-god, and the Fathers; and thereafter was solemn feast holden on the Field of the folk-mote, and all men were fain and merry. Nevertheless, not all men abode there the feast through; for or ever the afternoon was well worn, were many men wending along the Portway eastward toward the Upper Dale, each man in his war-gear and with a scrip hung about him; and these were they who were bound for the trysting-place and the journey over the waste.
So the Folk-mote was sundered; and men went to their houses, and there abode in peace the time of their summoning; since they wotted well that the Hosting was afoot.
But as for the Woodlanders, who were at the Motestead with all their folk, women, children, and old men, they went not back again to Carlstead; but prayed the neighbours of the Middle Dale to suffer them to abide there awhile, which they yeasaid with a good will. So the Woodlanders tilted themselves in, the more part of them, down in the meadows below the Motestead, along either side of Wildlake's Way; but their ancient folk, and some of the women and children, the neighbours would have into their houses, and the rest they furnished with victual and all that they needed without price, looking upon them as their very guests. For indeed they deemed that they could see that these men would never return to Carlstead, but would abide with the Men of the Wolf in Silverdale, once it were won. And this they deemed but meet and right, yet were they sorry thereof; for the Woodlanders were well beloved of all the Dalesmen; and now that they had gotten to know that they were come of so noble a kindred, they were better beloved yet, and more looked upon.

===Chinese===
他复又言道：「我等昔日之盛，我曾已告尔等；尔等亦将亲眼见我等今日之微。这便够了么？尔等可愿收我等为友、为兄弟？尔等以为如何？」

众人连声欢呼相答，那地与四围之野林，尽满其呼号之声；然喧嚷既息，长老开口说道：

「朋友啊，狼之酋长啊，尔等可从众人之呼号听得，我等绝无翻悔应允之意。须知我等之俗，不在于趋附强者以为友、弃弱者于不顾；而在于择与我等同心者为友，择我等所信之人。自今以后，我等之间便是兄弟之谊；我等为尔等之所有，尔等为我等之所有；愿此谊永世长存！」

一时众人尽皆满心欢喜；如今战事似已迫在眉睫，而战事之后之太平，亦已隐然可见。

继而众人将缀满花环之圣兽牵入判决环（the Doom-ring）之中，在那里将它们宰杀，献于诸神——即武神（the Warrior）、地神（the Earth-god），及列祖；其后便于民众大会之原（the Field of the folk-mote）设庄严之宴，众人皆悦而欢。然并非人人都守至宴罢；因为在午后未深之时，便已有许多人沿港路（the Portway）东行，直向上谷（the Upper Dale）而去，各各身披战甲，腰悬干粮袋；这些便是奔赴约地、欲横渡荒原之人。

民众大会（the Folk-mote）便如此散会；众人各归其家，平静等待征召之时；因为他们深知集结（the Hosting）已在酝酿。

至于那些林中汉子——他们举族齐至议事坪（the Motestead），妇人、孩童、老人俱在其中——并不返回汉子镇；他们恳请中谷（the Middle Dale）之邻人容他们暂住些时，邻人欣然应允。于是林中汉子大半在议事坪下方之草甸上、沿野湖径（Wildlake's Way）两侧安营扎寨；然其族中老者，以及部分妇孺，邻人将其接入家中；余者则邻人供以粮食及一切所需，不取分文，视如真客。因为他们其实看得出来：这些人将永不返回汉子镇，一旦银谷被攻下，便要与狼之民同住于彼。此事他们认为理所应当，却也为之惋惜；因为林中汉子为一切谷民所深爱；如今众人既知他们乃出于如此高贵之宗族，便更爱之、更敬之。

## XL Of the Hosting in Shadowy Vale / 论幽谷之聚兵

===Original===
It was on the evening of the fourth day after the Folk-mote that there came through the Waste to the rocky edge of Shadowy Vale a band of some fifteen score of men-at-arms, and with them a multitude of women and children and old men, some afoot, some riding on asses and bullocks; and with them were sumpter asses and neat laden with household goods, and a few goats and kine. And this was the whole folk of the Woodlanders come to the Hosting in Shadowy Vale and the Home of the Children of the Wolf. Their leaders of the way were Wood-father and Wood-wont and two other carles of Shadowy Vale; and Red-wolf the tall, and Bears-bane and War-grove were the captains and chieftains of their company.

Thus then they entered into the narrow pass aforesaid, which was the ingate to the Vale from the Waste, and little by little its dimness swallowed up their long line. As they went by the place where the lowering of the rock-wall gave a glimpse of the valley, they looked down into it as Face-of-god had done, but much change was there in little time. There was the black wall of crags on the other side stretching down to the ghyll of the great Force; there ran the deep green waters of the Shivering Flood; but the grass which Face-of-god had seen naked of everything but a few kine, thereon now the tents of men stood thick. Their hearts swelled within them as they beheld it, but they forebore the shout and the cry till they should be well within the Vale, and so went down silently into the darkness. But as their eyes caught that dim image of the Wolf on the wall of the pass, man pointed it out to man, and not a few turned and kissed it hurriedly; and to them it seemed that many a kiss had been laid on that dear token since the days of old, and that the hard stone had been worn away by the fervent lips of men, and that the air of the mirk place yet quivered with the vows sworn over the sword-blade.

===Chinese===
民众大会过后第四日傍晚，有一队约三百之数——十五个廿——的甲士穿过大荒原，来到幽谷那石崖的边沿；与他们同行的，还有大批妇人、孩童与老叟，或徒步，或骑驴骑犍牛；随行的又有驮驴和驮牛（neat），满载家什器物，还有几只山羊、几头奶牛。这便是林中汉子（the Woodlanders）全族之人，前来赴幽谷之聚兵（the Hosting），前来投狼之子民（the Children of the Wolf）的家园。其引路之人，乃是林父（Wood-father）、林习（Wood-wont）以及幽谷的另外两条汉子；而高大的红狼（Red-wolf the tall）、熊厄（Bears-bane）与战林（War-grove），则是这支人马的首领与头目。

于是他们便进了前述那道狭隘的隘口——那是由大荒原入谷的必经之门——长长的人列一点一点地被那昏暗吞没。当他们经过那处岩壁低陷、可以窥见谷底之地时，便如面神（Face-of-god）当日那样向下望去，然而短短时日之间，景物已大不相同。对面那道黑色的峭壁悬崖，依旧直延至大瀑布（the great Force）之涧；战栗川（the Shivering Flood）那墨绿的深水依旧奔流；只是面神当日所见那片空空荡荡、唯余数牛散落其上的草地，如今已密密立满了人的营帐。他们望见此景，胸中豪情激荡，却强自忍住，不到全然入谷便不呐喊出声，于是默然下入那黑暗之中。然而当他们的目光捕捉到隘壁之上那模糊的狼之造像时，这人便指给那人看，更有不少人转过身去匆匆地吻它；在他们想来，自古至今，不知多少亲吻已落在那可敬的记号之上，那坚硬的石头已被人们炽热的嘴唇磨蚀，那幽暗之处的空气，犹自为昔日于剑刃之上所发之誓愿而震颤。

===Original===
But down through the dark they went, and so came on to the stony scree at the end of the pass and into the Vale; and the whole Folk save the three chieftains flowed over it and stood about it down on the level grass of the Vale. But those three stood yet on the top of the scree, bearing the war-signs of the Shaft and the Spear, and betwixt them the banner of the Wolf and the Sun-burst newly displayed to the winds of Shadowy Vale.

Up and down the Vale they looked, and saw before the tents of men the old familiar banners of Burgdale rising and falling in the evening wind. But amidst of the Doom-ring was pitched a great banner, whereon was done the image of the Wolf with red gaping jaws on a field of green; and about him stood other banners, to wit, The Silver Arm on a red field, the Red Hand on a white field, and on green fields both, the Golden Bushel and the Ragged Sword.

All about the plain shone glittering war-gear of men as they moved hither and thither, and a stream of folk began at once to draw toward the scree to look on those newcomers; and amidst the helmed Burgdalers and the white-coated Shepherds went the tall men of the Wolf, bareheaded and unarmed save for their swords, mingled with the fair strong women of the kindred, treading barefoot the soft grass of their own Vale.

Presently there was a great throng gathered round about the Woodlanders, and each man as he joined it waved hand or weapon toward them, and the joy of their welcome sent a confused clamour through the air. Then forth from the throng stepped Folk-might, unarmed save his sword, and behind him was Face-of-god, in his war-gear save his helm, hand in hand with the Sun-beam, who was clad in her goodly flowered green kirtle, her feet naked like her sisters of the kindred.

===Chinese===
他们在黑暗中一路下行，于是来到隘口尽头那片碎石乱滩，进入谷中；除三位头人之外，全族之人皆漫过那片乱滩，停立于谷中平地的芳草之上。唯有那三人仍立在碎石滩之顶，擎着矛旗与枪旗（the Shaft and the Spear）两面战旗，二人之间，则新展着狼与旭日（the Sun-burst）的大旗，在幽谷的风中猎猎招展。

他们上下望遍这条山谷，看见众人的营帐之前，堡谷（Burgdale）那些旧日熟悉的大旗在晚风之中起起落落。然而在判决环（the Doom-ring）正中，竖着一面大旗，旗上绿底之中绘着一只张着血红之口的老狼；它四周还立着别的大旗，即红底之上的银臂（the Silver Arm），白底之上的赤手（the Red Hand），以及同为绿底的金斗（the Golden Bushel）与残锋剑（the Ragged Sword）。

原野之上，处处闪闪发光，皆是兵甲之士往来穿梭之身影；当即有一股人流朝那碎石滩涌来，要看看这些新到之人；在戴盔的堡谷人与白衣的牧羊人之间，走着那些高大的狼之子民，他们不戴帽、不持兵，唯携腰间之剑，与本族那美丽健壮的女子相杂其间，赤足踏着自己谷中柔软的芳草。

顷刻之间，林中汉子周围已聚起一大群人，每一个新加入的人都朝他们挥着手或兵器，欢迎之喜化作一片嘈杂的喧腾，直冲夜空。随后民强（Folk-might）自人群中步出，除腰间之剑外不披甲胄；他身后跟着面神，除未戴盔外一身甲胄俱全，手挽着日光（the Sun-beam）——日光身上穿着她那件华美的绣花绿袍，如她族中诸姐妹一般赤着双足。

===Original===
Then Folk-might cried aloud: “A full and free greeting to our brothers! Well be ye, O Sons of our Ancient Fathers! And today are ye the dearer to us because we see that ye have brought us a gift, to wit, your wives and children, and your grandsires unmeet for war. By this token we see how great is your trust in us, and that it is your meaning never to sunder from us again. O well be ye; well be ye!”

Then spake Red-wolf, and said: “Ye Sons of the Wolf, who parted from us of old time in that cleft of the mountains, it is our very selves that we give unto you; and these are a part of ourselves; how then should we leave them behind us? Bear witness, O men of Burgdale and the Sheepcotes, that we have become one Folk with the men of Shadowy Vale, never to be sundered again!”

Then all that multitude shouted with a loud voice; and when the shout had died away, Folk-might spake again:

===Chinese===
于是民强大声喊道："我们向众位兄弟致以全心全意的欢迎！愿众位安好，啊，远古先祖之子（Sons of our Ancient Fathers）！今日你们于我们格外亲近，因为我们看见你们带来了一份馈赠，那便是你们的妻儿子女，以及不堪上阵的高年祖辈。我们由这一番心意，便知你们对我们是何等信赖，又知你们的心意，是再不与我们分离了。啊，愿你们安好；愿你们安好！"

红狼遂开口说道："狼之子民啊，昔日你们在那道山峡之中与我们分袂，如今我们奉上给你们的，正是我们自身；这些人便是我们自身的一部分，我们岂能将他们撇在身后？堡谷与羊栏（the Sheepcotes）之人啊，请你们作证：我们已与幽谷之人合为一族，永不再分！"

那一片人海便齐声高呼；待呼喊之声平息，民强又说道：

===Original===
“O Warriors of the Sundering, here shall your wives and children abide, while we go a little journey to rejoice our hearts with the hard handplay, and take to us that which we have missed: and tomorrow morn is appointed for this same journey, unless ye be over foot-weary with the ways of the Waste.”

Red-wolf smiled as he answered: “This ye say in jest, brother; for ye may see that our day’s journey hath not been overmuch for our old men; how then should it weary those who may yet bear sword? We are ready for the road and eager for the handplay.”

“This is well,” said Folk-might, “and what was to be looked for. Therefore, brother, do ye and your counsel-mates come straightway to the Hall of the Wolf; wherein, after ye have eaten and drunken, shall we take counsel with our brethren of Burgdale and the Sheepcotes, so that all may be ordered for battle!”

Said Red-wolf: “Good is that, if we must needs abide till tomorrow; for verily we came not hither to eat and drink and rest our bodies; but it must be as ye will have it.”

===Chinese===
"离散之勇士（Warriors of the Sundering）啊，你们的妻儿就留在此处，我们要去走一小段路，以那场硬碰硬的白刃厮杀（handplay）快意心头，取回我们所久缺之物：而这趟出征，已定在明早启程，除非你们被大荒原的路途磨得脚力不支。"

红狼微笑着答道："兄弟，这话你是说笑的；你们看得见，我们今日这一程路，连我们这些老汉也算不得太苦，何况那些尚能执剑之人？我们已备好上路，正盼着那场白刃厮杀呢。"

民强道："这便好，这也是意料中事。所以，兄弟，你与你的议事同伴们即刻随我到狼之厅（the Hall of the Wolf）去；在那里，你们吃饱饮足之后，我们便与堡谷和羊栏的众兄弟一同商议，好把出战之事一一安排妥当！"

红狼道："这话甚好，倘若非得等到明日不可的话；因为说实在的，我们可不是为着吃喝、为着歇息身子才到此地来的；不过，就照你们的安排罢了。"

===Original===
Then the Sun-beam left the hand of Face-of-god and came forward, and held out both her palms to the Woodland-folk, and spake in a voice that was heard afar, though it were a woman’s, so clear and sweet it was; and she said:

“O Warriors of the Sundering, ye who be not needed in the Hall, and ye our sisters with your little ones and your fathers, come now to us and down to the tents which we have arrayed for you, and there think for a little that we are all at our very home that we long for and have yet to win, and be ye merry with us and make us merry.”

Therewith she stepped forward daintily and entered into their throng, and took an old man of the Woodlanders by the hand, and kissed his cheek and led him away, and the coming rest seemed sweet to him. And then came other women of the Vale, kind and fair and smiling, and led away, some an old mother of the Woodlanders, some a young wife, some a pair of lads; and not a few forsooth kissed and embraced the stark warriors, and went away with them toward the tents, which stood along the side of the Shivering Flood where it was at its quietest; for there was the grass the softest and most abundant. There on the green grass were tables arrayed, and lamps were hung above them on spears, to be litten when the daylight should fail. And the best of the victual which the Vale could give was spread on the boards, along with wine and dainties, bought in Silverdale, or on the edges of the Westland with sword-strokes and arrow-flight.

===Chinese===
于是日光松开面神的手，走上前来，向林中之民摊开双掌，开口说话；她虽是女子，声音却清越甜美，传至远处亦清晰可闻；她说道：

"离散之勇士啊，你们这些不必入厅议事的人，还有你们这些姐妹，带着你们的小孩和父辈，现在就随我们来，下到我们为你们备好的营帐里去；在那里，你们且把这一刻当作我们日思夜想、尚待夺回的家园，与我们一起欢喜，也叫我们欢喜。"

她说完便轻盈地上前，走入他们的人群之中，牵起林中汉子中一位老人的手，吻了他的脸颊，将他领走；那老人觉得即将到来的歇息，甜美无比。随后谷中其他女子也来了，温柔、美丽、面带笑意，她们领走的，有的是林中汉子的一位老母，有的是一位年轻妻子，有的是一对少年；不消说，也有不少女子与那些壮健的武士亲吻拥抱，一同朝营帐而去；那些营帐就扎在战栗川水流最缓之处的沿岸，因为那里的草地最软、最丰。青草之上已摆开了桌案，长枪挑着灯笼挂在案上，只等天色一暗便点燃。谷中所能拿出的最好的饮食都已摆在案上，还有美酒与珍馐——这些有的是在银谷（Silverdale）买下的，有的则是以刀剑和箭矢，在西土（the Westland）的边沿换来的。

===Original===
There then they feasted and were merry; and the Sun-beam and Bow-may and the other women of the Vale served them at table, and were very blithe with them, caressing them with soft words, and with clipping and kissing, as folk who were grown exceeding dear to them; so that that eve of battle was softer and sweeter to them than any hour of their life. With these feasters were God-swain and Spear-fist of the delivered thralls of Silverdale as glad as glad might be; but Wolf-stone their eldest was gone with Dallach to the Council in the Hall.

The men of Burgdale and the Shepherds feasted otherwhere in all content, nor lacked folk of the Vale to serve them. Amongst the men of the Face were the ten delivered thralls who had heart to meet their masters in arms: seven of them were of Rosedale and three of Silverdale.

The Bride was with her kindred of the Steer, with whom were many men of Shadowy Vale, and she served her friends and fellows clad in her war-gear, save helm and hauberk, bearing herself as one who is serving dear guests. And men equalled her for her beauty to the Gods of the High Place and the Choosers of the Slain; and they who had not beheld her before marvelled at her, and her loveliness held all men’s hearts in a net of desire, so that they forebore their meat to gaze upon her; and if perchance her hand touched some young man, or her cheek or sweet-breathed mouth came nigh to his face, he became bewildered and wist not where he was, nor what to do. Yet was she as lowly and simple of speech and demeanour as if she were a gooseherd of fourteen winters.

===Chinese===
于是他们便在那里设宴畅饮、欢喜快乐；日光、弓娥（Bow-may）和谷中其他女子在席间侍奉他们，与众人一同欢悦，以温柔的话语抚慰他们，又拥抱他们、亲吻他们，仿佛这些人已是她们心头至亲至爱之人；于是那战前之夜，对他们而言，竟比平生任何时刻都更温柔、更甜美。在这些赴宴之人当中，还有神仆（God-swain）和枪拳（Spear-fist）——他们都是从银谷救回的奴隶（thrall）——也都乐得不能再乐；只是他们中最年长的狼石（Wolf-stone），已随达拉赫（Dallach）赴厅中议事去了。

堡谷的人和牧羊人在别处也是心满意足地设宴，谷中也不缺侍奉他们的人。在面族（the Face）之人当中，有十个被救回来的奴隶，他们有心与昔日的主人在阵前交锋：其中七个出自玫瑰谷（Rosedale），三个出自银谷。

新娘（the Bride）在她犍牛族（the Steer）的亲族之中——其中也有许多幽谷之人——她身上穿着甲胄，只除开盔与锁子甲，招待她的朋友和同伴，举止一如侍奉贵客之人。众人将她之美貌，比作高地之神（the Gods of the High Place）与择亡之女（the Choosers of the Slain）；素未见过她的人无不惊叹，她的丽色将所有男人的心都网在一张欲念之网里，以致他们放着肉食不吃，只顾凝望她；倘若她的手偶然触到某个少年，或是她的脸颊、她那吐气如兰的嘴凑近他的脸，那少年便神魂颠倒，不知身在何处、所当何为。然而她言谈举止却谦和质朴得很，仿佛只是个十四岁的牧鹅少女。

===Original===
In the Hall was a goodly company, and all the leaders of the Folk were therein, and Folk-might and the War-leader sitting in the midst of those stone seats on the days. There then they agreed on the whole ordering of the battle and the wending of the host, as shall be told later on; and this matter was long a-doing, and when it was done, men went to their places to sleep, for the night was well worn.

But when men had departed and all was still, Folk-might, light-clad and without a weapon, left the Hall and walked briskly toward the nether end of the Vale. He passed by all the tents, the last whereof were of the House of the Steer, and came to a place where was a great rock rising straight up from the plain like sheaves of black staves standing close together; and it was called Staff-stone, and tales of the elves had been told concerning it, so that Stone-face had beheld it gladly the day before.

The moon was just shining into Shadowy Vale, and the grass was bright wheresoever the shadows of the high cliffs were not, and the face of Staff-stone shone bright grey as Folk-might came within sight of it, and he beheld someone sitting at the base of the rock, and as he drew nigher he saw that it was a woman, and knew her for the Bride; for he had prayed her to abide him there that night, because it was nigh to the tents of the House of the Steer; and his heart was glad as he drew nigh to her.

She sat quietly on a fragment of the black rock, clad as she had been all day, in her glittering kirtle, but without hauberk or helm, a wreath of windflowers about her head, her feet crossed over each other, her hands laid palm uppermost in her lap. She moved not as he drew nigh, but said in a gentle voice when he was close to her:

===Chinese===
厅中此时人才济济，一族的首领都在其中，民强和战首（the War-leader）坐在那些古老的石座之中。众人便在那里议定整场战役的部署和全军进发的路线，其详情后文再表；这桩事议了许久，议毕之后，众人各归其处就寝，因为夜已深了。

等人散去、一切归于寂静之时，民强只着单衣、不携一兵一刃，走出厅堂，快步朝谷地下端走去。他走过一座座营帐，最后一座是犍牛族之宅（the House of the Steer）的帐子，随后来到一处地方：那里有一块巨岩自平地拔起，直直矗立，仿佛一捆紧紧扎在一起的黑色杖棒；此石名唤杖石（Staff-stone），关于它素来有精灵的传说流传，所以石面（Stone-face）前一日见了它，也极是欣喜。

此时月光初照入幽谷，凡高处崖影未遮之处，草地皆一片明亮；民强远远望见杖石之面闪着明亮的灰光，又见有人坐在巨岩之下；待走近了，才看清是个女子，认出她便是新娘——原来他曾求她当夜在那里等他，因为那地方离犍牛族之宅的营帐甚近；他朝她走去，心头欢喜。

她静静地坐在一块黑岩的碎石上，衣着一如整日所穿，那身闪闪发亮的短袍，只是不披锁子甲、不戴盔；头上戴着一圈银莲花（windflowers）编成的花环，双足交叠，双手掌心向上放在膝上。他走近时她一动不动，待他到得近前，才柔声说道：

===Original===
“Chief of the Wolf, great warrior, thou wouldest speak with me; and good it is that friends should talk together on the eve of battle, when they may never meet alive again.”

He said: “My talk shall not be long; for thou and I both must sleep tonight, since there is work to hand tomorrow. Now since, as thou sayest, O fairest of women, we may never meet again alive, I ask thee now at this hour, when we both live and are near to one another, to suffer me to speak to thee of my love of thee and desire for thee. Surely thou, who art the sweetest of all things the Gods and the kindreds have made, wilt not gainsay me this?”

She said very sweetly, yet smiling: “Brother of my father’s sons, how can I gainsay thee thy speech? Nay, hast thou not said it? What more canst thou add to it that will have fresh meaning to mine ears?”

He said: “Thou sayest sooth: might I then but kiss thine hand?”

She said, no longer smiling: “Yea surely, even so may all men do who can be called my friends﻿—and thou art much my friend.”

He took her hand and kissed it, and held it thereafter; nor did she draw it away. The moon shone brightly on them; but by its light he could not see if she reddened, but he deemed that her face was troubled. Then he said: “It were better for me if I might kiss thy face, and take thee in mine arms.”

===Chinese===
"狼之首领，伟大的勇士，你有话要与我说；在战前之夜，在朋友或许此生再不能活着相见之时，朋友之间能聚谈一番，是件好事。"

他说道："我的话不会长；因为你我今夜都须安睡，明日还有事要做。既然，正如你所说，啊，最美的女子，我们也许再不能活着相见，那么我便趁此你我俱活、彼此相近之时，求你容我对你说一说我对你之爱、对你的渴慕。你乃是众神与众族所造万物之中最甜美者，想必不会拒绝我这番请求吧？"

她甜甜地、却含笑说道："我骨肉之亲的兄弟啊，我怎能拒绝你这番话？不，你这岂不是已经说出口了么？你还能再添上什么，叫我耳中听来有新的意思呢？"

他说："你说的是实话：那么，我可否一吻你的手？"

她不再含笑，说道："是，自然可以，凡称得上我朋友的人，皆可如此——而你，是我极亲近的朋友。"

他握住她的手吻了它，此后仍握着不放；她亦不曾抽回。明月照在他们身上；然而借着那月光，他看不出她是否红了脸，却觉得她面容似有不安。于是他说："若我能吻你的脸、将你拥入怀中，于我便是更好。"

===Original===
Then said she: “This only shall a man do with me when I long to do the like with him. And since thou art so much my friend, I will tell thee that as for this longing, I have it not. Bethink thee what a little while it is since the lack of another man’s love grieved me sorely.”

“The time is short,” said Folk-might, “if we tell up the hours thereof; but in that short space have a many things betid.”

She said: “Dost thou know, canst thou guess, how sorely ashamed I went amongst my people? I durst look no man in the face for the aching of mine heart, which methought all might see through my face.”

“I knew it well,” he said; “yet of me wert thou not ashamed but a little while ago, when thou didst tell me of thy grief.”

She said: “True it is; and thou wert kind to me. Thou didst become a dear friend to me, methought.”

“And wilt thou hurt a dear friend?” said he.

“O no,” she said, “if I might do otherwise. Yet how if I might not choose? Shall there be no forgiveness for me then?”

He answered nothing; and still he held her hand that strove not to be gone from his, and she cast down her eyes. Then he spake in a while:

===Chinese===
她说道："唯独当我亦愿与那人如此时，那人才可对我如此。既然你是我如此亲近的朋友，我便告诉你：至于这一份心意，我并无之。你且想想，不久之前，因另一个人之爱的缺失，我是何等痛切地悲伤过。"

民强道："若把时辰一一数算，这时间确实不长；然而就在这短短一段里，已有许多事发生。"

她说道："你可知，你能猜到么，我是怀着何等的羞愧走入我的族人之中？我心痛如绞，自觉所有人都能从我脸上看穿我的心，竟不敢正眼去看任何一个人。"

他说："我深知此事；然而不久之前，你向我倾诉你的悲伤之时，你对我却不以为耻。"

她说："此言不差；你待我很厚道。我觉得，你已成为我一位至交了。"

他说："那么你忍心伤害一位至交么？"

她说："啊，不，若我能不作此事。然而倘若我无从选择呢？到那时，难道就没有原谅我了么？"

他不答；却仍握着她的手，那只手并不挣扎着要离他的手而去；她垂下眼。过了一会，他说道：

===Original===
“My friend, I have been thinking of thee and of me; and now hearken: if thou wilt declare that thou feelest no sweetness embracing thine heart when I say that I desire thee sorely, as now I say it; or when I kiss thine hand, as now I kiss it; or when I pray thee to suffer me to cast mine arms about thee and kiss thy face, as now I pray it: if thou wilt say this, then will I take thee by the hand straightway, and lead thee to the tents of the House of the Steer, and say farewell to thee till the battle is over. Canst thou say this out of the truth of thine heart?”

She said: “What then if I cannot say this word? What then?”

But he answered nothing; and she sat still a little while, and then arose and stood before him, looking him in the eyes, and said:

“I cannot say it.”

Then he caught her in his arms and strained her to him, and then kissed her lips and her face again and again, and she strove not with him. But at last she said:

“Yet after all this shalt thou lead me back to my folk straightway; and when the battle is done, if both we are living, then shall we speak more thereof.”

So he took her hand and led her on toward the tents of the Steer, and for a while he spake nought; for he doubted himself, what he should say; but at last he spake:

===Chinese===
"我的朋友，我方才一直在想你、想我；如今你且听着：倘若你肯说出——当我说我极是渴慕你，如我现在所说；当我吻你的手，如我现在所吻；当我求你容我将双臂拥住你、吻你的脸，如我现在所求——当我说这些之时，你心中拥抱的，全无一丝甜蜜：倘若你肯如此说，我便立刻携你之手，领你回到犍牛族之宅的营帐，向你说一声珍重，待战事完结。你能从你心底的真实之中，说出这话么？"

她说："那么，倘若我说不出这话呢？那又如何？"

他又不答；她静静坐了一会儿，随即起身立在他面前，直视他的双眼，说道：

"我说不出。"

于是他将她拥入怀中，紧紧抱住，接着一遍又一遍地吻她的唇、她的脸，她也不与他挣扎。终于她说道：

"然而这一切之后，你仍须立刻领我回到我的族人那里；待战事完结，你我若都还活着，那时我们再细论此事。"

于是他牵着她的手，朝犍牛族之宅的营帐走去，有一程他不发一言；因为他对自己也拿不准，该说什么；终于他说道：

===Original===
“Now is this better for me than if it had not been, whether I live or whether I die. Yet thou hast not said that thou lovest me and desirest me.”

“Wilt thou compel me?” she said. “Tonight I may not say it. Who shall say what words my lips shall fashion when we stand together victorious in Silverdale; then indeed may the time seem long from now.”

He said: “Yea, true is that; yet once again I say that so measured long and long is the time since first I saw thee in Burgdale before thou knewest me. Yet now I will not bicker with thee, for be sure that I am glad at heart. And lo you! our feet have brought us to the tents of thy people. All good go with thee!”

“And with thee, sweet friend,” she said. Then she lingered a little, turning her head toward the tents, and then turned her face toward him and laid her hand on his neck, and drew his head adown to her and kissed his cheek, and therewith swiftly and lightly departed from him.

Now the night wore and the morning came; and Face-of-god was abroad very early in the morning, as his custom was; and he washed the night from off him in the Carles’ Bath of the Shivering Flood, and then went round through the encampment of the host, and saw none stirring save here and there the last watchmen of the night. He spake with one or two of these, and then went up to the head of the Vale, where was the pass that led to Silverdale; and there he saw the watch, and spake with them, and they told him that none had as yet come forth from the pass, and he bade them to blow the horn of warning to rouse up the Host as soon as the messengers came thence. For forerunners had been sent up the pass, and had been set to hold watch at divers places therein to pass on the word from place to place.

===Chinese===
"如今于我而言，这已胜过此事不曾发生，无论我是死是活。然而你尚未说过你爱我、你渴慕我。"

她说："你要逼迫我么？今夜我不能说这话。待我们一同凯旋立于银谷之时，我的双唇将说出什么话，谁能预料呢？从现在到那时，时日确然可能显得漫长。"

他说："是啊，此言不差；然而我再说一遍，自那回你在堡谷初见我、尚不识我之时起，那段日子，我数来数去，竟觉其长而又长。不过如今我不与你拌嘴了，因为你尽可相信，我心中是欢喜的。你看！我们的脚已经把你族人的营帐带到了。愿一切美好与你同在！"

她说："也与你同在，亲爱的朋友。"她便在原地流连片刻，把头转向营帐，随即又转过脸来向他，伸手搭上他的脖颈，将他的头引向自己，吻了他的脸颊，随即轻盈迅捷地离他而去。

长夜渐尽，清晨来临；面神清早便出门了，这是他的习惯；他在战栗川的汉子浴（the Carles' Bath）里洗去一身夜色，随后走遍全军营盘，见无人在外走动，唯偶尔遇见几个夜里最后一班的守卒。他与其中一两个攀谈了几句，便上到谷地上端，那里是通往银谷的隘口；他见了守卒，与之交谈，守卒告诉他，隘口中尚无人出来，他便吩咐他们：一旦哨报自隘口而来，便立刻吹响警号，唤醒全军。因为此前已有前哨被派上隘口，分驻其中数处，好将消息一处一处接力传下。

===Original===
Thence went Face-of-god back toward the Hall; but when he was yet some way from it, he saw a slender glittering warrior come forth from the door thereof, who stood for a moment looking round about, and then came lightly and swiftly toward him; and lo! it was the Sun-beam, with a long hauberk over her kirtle falling below her knees, a helm on her head and plated shoes on her feet. She came up to him, and laid her hand to his cheek and the golden locks of his head (for he was bareheaded), and said to him, smiling:

“Gold-mane! thou badest me bear arms, and Folk-might also constrained me thereto. Lo thou!”

Said Face-of-god: “Folk-might is wise then, even as I am; and forsooth as thou art. For bethink thee if the bow drawn at a venture should speed the eyeless shaft against thy breast, and send me forth a wanderer from my Folk! For how could I bear the sight of the fair Dale, and no hope to see thee again therein?”

She said: “The heart is light within me today. Deemest thou that this is strange? Or dost thou call to mind that which thou spakest the other day, that it was of no avail to stand in the Doom-ring of the Folk and bear witness against ourselves? This will I not. This is no light-mindedness that thou beholdest in me, but the valiancy that the Fathers have set in mine heart. Deem not, O Gold-mane, fear not, that we shall die before they dight the bride-bed for us.”

===Chinese===
面神自那里折回，朝厅堂走去；离厅尚有一程之时，却见一个身形纤秀、闪闪发光的武士自厅门走出，立在门口四下一望，随即轻盈迅捷地朝他奔来；原来不是别人，正是日光！她短袍之外罩着一件长及膝下的锁子甲，头戴盔，足穿鳞甲鞋。她走到他跟前，伸手抚了抚他的脸颊、抚了抚他头上那金色的鬈发（因他未戴帽），含笑对他说道：

"金鬃（Gold-mane）！你曾命我执兵，民强也力劝我如此。你看！"

面神道："那么民强是聪明的，一如我一样；说实在的，也一如你一样。因为你且想想，倘若那张随缘开射的弓，将一支瞎目之箭（eyeless shaft）射向你的胸膛，使我从此成了流浪于本族之外的人，那可如何是好！这条美丽的山谷，倘若再无望于其中见到你，我怎能忍心再看它呢？"

她说："今日我心头轻松。你以为这奇怪么？你可记得前几日你所说的话——在族人的判决环之中站出来、对我们自己作证，是徒劳无益的？我不愿如此。你在我身上所见到的，并非心思轻浮，而是先祖们置于我心中的勇毅。金鬃啊，不要以为、也不要怕，我们会在他们为我们铺设新婚之榻以前便死去。"

===Original===
He would have kissed her mouth, but she put him away with her hand, and doffed her helm and laid it on the grass, and said:

“This is not the last time that thou shalt kiss me, Gold-mane, my dear; and yet I long for it as if it were, so high as the Fathers have raised me up this morn above fear and sadness.”

He said nought, but drew her to him, and wonder so moved him, that he looked long and closely at her face before he kissed her; and forsooth he could find no blemish in it: it was as if it were but new come from the smithy of the Gods, and exceeding longing took hold of him. But even as their lips met, from the head of the Vale came the voice of the great horn; and it was answered straightway by the watchers all down the tents; and presently arose the shouts of men and the clash of weapons as folk armed themselves, and laughter therewith, for most men were battle-merry, and the cries of women shrilly-clear as they hastened about, busy over the morning meal before the departure of the Host. But Face-of-god said softly, still caressing the Sun-beam, and she him:

“Thus then we depart from this Valley of the Shadows, but as thou saidst when first we met therein, there shall be no sundering of thee and me, but thou shalt go down with me to the battle.”

And he led her by the hand into the Hall of the Wolf, and there they ate a morsel, and thereafter Face-of-god tarried not, but busied himself along with Folk-might and the other chieftains in arraying the Host for departure.

===Chinese===
他原要吻她的嘴，她却抬手将他轻轻推开，摘下头盔放在草地上，说道：

"金鬃，我的爱人，这并非你最后一次吻我；然而我盼望这一吻，却仿佛它就是最后一回一般，因为先祖们今晨已把我高高举到恐惧与悲伤之上。"

他未言语，只将她拉向自己；他惊奇得不能自已，竟细细端详她的脸许久，才去吻它；说实在的，他在那脸上找不出一丝瑕疵：那张脸仿佛才从众神的锻炉之中新铸出炉；一股极深的渴望攫住了他。然而正当他们两唇相接之时，谷地尽头传来了那柄大号角之声；下游各帐的守卒立刻应之以号；须臾之间，人们的呼喝声、兵器的碰撞声四起——众人正在披甲执兵，其间夹着笑声，因为大多数人都因将战而心喜；又有妇人尖锐清亮的喊声，她们在军队开拔之前忙着预备早膳，往来奔走。然而面神一面仍抚慰着日光，日光也抚慰着他，一面轻声说道：

"那么我们便离开这阴影之谷吧，然而正如我们初见之时你所说过的，你与我再不相离，你要与我一同下到战场上去。"

他牵着她的手走进狼之厅，二人在那里吃了一口东西；随后面神便不再耽搁，与民强及其他首领一同忙碌起来，整顿全军，准备开拔。

## LII Of the New Beginning of Good Days in Silverdale / 五十二 银谷佳日之新始

===Original===
On the third day there was high-tide and great joy amongst all men from end to end of the Dale; and the delivered thralls were feasted and made much of by the kindreds, so that they scarce knew how to believe their own five senses that told them the good tidings.

For none strove to grieve them and torment them; what they would, that did they, and they had all things plenteously; since for all was there enough and to spare of goods stored up for the Dusky Men, as corn and wine and oil and spices, and raiment and silver. Horses were there also, and neat and sheep and swine in abundance. Withal there was the good and dear land; the waxing corn on the acres; the blossoming vines on the hillside; and about the orchards and alongside the ways, the plum-trees and cherry-trees and pear-trees that had cast their blossom and were overhung with little young fruit; and the fair apple-trees a-blossoming, and the chestnuts spreading their boughs from their twisted trunks over the green grass. And there was the goodly pasture for the horses and the neat, and the thymy hill-grass for the sheep; and beyond it all, the thicket of the great wood, with its unfailing store of goodly timber of ash and oak and holly and yoke-elm. There need no man lack unless man compelled him, and all was rich enough and wide enough for the waxing of a very great folk.

===Chinese===
到了第三日，谷中自这头到那头，人人皆大庆，欢声载道；被解救的奴虏（thralls）受诸氏族设宴款待、倍加优礼，几乎不敢相信自家五官所传来的喜讯。

因再无人存心折磨他们、苦待他们；他们随心所欲，一无所缺，万物丰足；盖因当初为黝暗人（the Dusky Men）所蓄之物——麦、酒、油、香料，以及衣帛与银——堆积如山，人人皆取用不尽。马匹、牛、羊、猪，亦所在多有。此外还有那肥美可爱之地土；田亩间日渐长成的麦子；山坡上正盛放的葡萄藤；果园四周及道路两旁，李树、樱桃树、梨树花已落尽，低垂着累累嫩果；佳美的苹果树正当花期，栗树自其虬曲之干上舒展枝柯，荫覆青草。又有肥美之牧地以养马与牛，长满麝香草的山坡之草以饲羊；这一切之外，便是那片大林的密灌丛，其中梣、柞、冬青、枷榆（yoke-elm）之良材，取之不竭。此间无人会感匮乏，除非有人强逼于他；此间一切既丰饶且广袤，足以成就一个极盛之族的繁衍壮大。

===Original===
Now, therefore, men betook them to what was their own before the coming of the Dusky Men; and though at first many of the delivered thrall-folk feasted somewhat above measure, and though there were some of them who were not very brisk at working on the earth for their livelihood; yet were the most part of them quick of wit and deft of hand, and they mostly fell to presently at their cunning, both of husbandry and handicraft. Moreover, they had great love of the kindreds, and especially of the Woodlanders, and strove to do all things that might pleasure them. And as for those who were dull and listless because of their many torments of the last ten years, they would at least fetch and carry willingly for them of the kindreds; and these last grudged them not meat and raiment and houseroom, even if they wrought but little for it, because they called to mind the evil days of their thralldom, and bethought them how few are men’s days upon the earth.

Thus all things throve in Silverdale, and the days wore on toward the summer, and the Yuletide rest beyond it, and the years beyond and far beyond the winning of Silverdale.

===Chinese===
于是众人各归本业，重操黝暗人来犯之前的旧业；起初虽有许多被解救的奴虏饮宴稍过度量，虽则其中有些人于耕作谋生并不甚勤勉；然他们大多心思灵巧、双手娴熟，不久便各自归了本行，无论农耕、百工，皆上手极快。再者，他们深为敬爱诸氏族，尤其敬爱林中汉子（the Woodlanders），凡能使他们欢心之事，无不竭力为之。至于那些因过去十年所受百般折磨而变得迟钝萎靡之人，至少也甘心为诸氏族之人奔走执役；而诸氏族也不吝给他们饭食、衣物、住所，哪怕他们干活甚少，因为诸氏族念及他们昔日为奴的苦日子，又想到人活于世，岁月本自无多。

于是银谷（Silverdale）万物兴旺；日子一天天推向盛夏，推向盛夏之后岁末冬至节（Yuletide）的休歇，推向夺取银谷之后的一年又一年，乃至久远的将来。

## XLIV Of the Onslaught of the Men of the Steer, the Bridge, and the Bull / 四十四 犍牛族、桥族与公牛族人之猛攻

===Original===
Wild was the turmoil and confusion in the Marketstead; for the more part of the men therein knew not what had befallen about the altar, though some clomb up to the top of that stack of faggots built for the burning of the thralls, and when they saw what was toward fell to yelling and cursing; and their fellows on the plain Place could not hear their story for the clamour, and they also fell to howling as if a wood full of wild dogs was there.

And still the shafts rained down on that throng from the Bent of the Bowmen, for another two score men of the Woodlanders had crept down the hill to them, and shafts failed them not. But the Dusky Men about the altar, for all their terror, or even maybe because of it, now began to turn upon the scarce-seen foemen, and to press up wildly toward the hillside, though as it were without any order or aim. Every man of them had his weapons, and those no mere gilded toys, but their very tools of battle; and some, but no great number, had their bows with them and a few shafts; and these began to shoot at whatsoever they could see on the hillside, but at first so wildly and hurriedly that they did no harm.

===Chinese===
集市坪（the Marketstead）中一片纷乱骚动，野蛮而无序；因为其中大半之人并不知祭坛周围发生了何事，纵有几人攀上了那为焚杀奴隶而堆起的柴堆之巅，望见情势如何，便破口叫骂起来；然而平地上的同伴为喧嚷所蔽，听不清他们所说，于是也跟着嚎叫起来，仿佛那里有一整林子的野狗。

弓手坡（the Bent of the Bowmen）上射下的箭矢仍如雨般倾落在这群人丛之上，因林中汉子又有四十余人悄悄下山与他们汇合，箭矢丝毫不曾短缺。然而祭坛周围的黝暗人（the Dusky Men），尽管惊恐万分——或者正因这惊恐之故——此刻竟开始转身扑向那些几乎看不清的敌人，疯狂地朝山坡上压去，却毫无秩序，也毫无目标。他们人人手中都有兵器，且绝非镀金的玩艺儿，而是他们真正的战阵利器；其中有些人——为数不多——随身带着弓和几支箭；这些人开始朝山坡上他们所能瞥见的一切射去，但起初射得又急又乱，全无所中。

===Original===
It must be said of them that at first only those about the altar fell on toward the hill; for those about the road that led southward knew not what had betided nor whither to turn. So that at this beginning of the battle, of all the thousands in the great Place it was but a few hundreds that set on the Bent of the Bowmen, and at these the bowmen of the kindreds shot so close and so wholly together that they fell one over another in the narrow ways between the houses whereby they must needs go to gather on the plain ground betwixt the backs of the houses and the break of the hillside. But little by little the archers of the Dusky Men gathered behind the corpses of the slain, and fell to shooting at what they could see of the men of the kindreds, which at that while was not much, for as bold as they were, they fought like wary hunters of the Wood and the Waste.

===Chinese===
须得说明的是：起初唯有祭坛周围那些人朝山坡上扑来；至于通往南方那条大路附近的人，还不知出了何事，也不知该转向何方。因此在这场战斗之初，偌大广场中成千上万的人，攻向弓手坡的不过数百；诸族的弓手朝他们射得又密又齐，他们便在房屋之间那些狭窄的通道里——他们必经此路方能集结于屋背与山坡断崖之间那片平地——纷纷滚落，一个压着一个。但黝暗人的弓手渐渐聚集到死者尸骸之后，朝他们所能瞥见的诸族之人放箭；然而此刻他们所能见的并不多，因为诸族之人虽然英勇，却如林间与荒原上谨慎的猎人那般作战。

===Original===
But now at last throughout all that throng of Felons in the Marketplace the tale began to spread of foemen come into the Dale and shooting from the Bents, and all they turned their faces to the hill, and the whole set of the throng was thitherward; though they fared but slowly, so evil was the order of them, each man hindering his neighbour as he went. And not only did the Dusky Men come flockmeal toward the Bent of the Bowmen, but also they jostled along toward the road that led southward. That beheld Wood-wise from the Bent, and he was minded to get him and his aback, now that they had made so great a slaughter of the foemen; and two or three of his fellows had been hurt by arrows, and Bow-may, she would have been slain thrice over but for the hammer-work of the Alderman. And no marvel was that; for now she stood on a little mound not half covered by a thin thorn-bush, and notched and loosed at whatever was most notable, as though she were shooting at the mark on a summer evening in Shadowy Vale. But as Wood-wise was at point to give the word to depart, from behind them rang out the merry sound of the Burgdale horns, and he turned to look at the woodside, and lo! thereunder was the hill bright and dark with men-at-arms, and over them floated the Banners of the Wolf, and the Banners of the Steer, the Bridge, and the Bull. Then gave forth the bowmen of the kindreds their first shout, and they made no stay in their shooting; but shot the eagerer, for they deemed that help would come without their turning about to draw it to them: and even so it was. For straightway down the bent came striding Face-of-god betwixt the two Banners of the Wolf, and beside him were Red-wolf the tall and War-grove, and therewithal Wood-wont and Wood-wicked, and many other men of the Wolf; for now that the men of the kindreds had been brought face to face with the foe, and there was less need of them for way-leaders, the more part of them were liefer to fight under their own banner along with the Woodlanders; so that the company of those who went under the Wolves was more than three long hundreds and a half; and the bowmen on the edge of the bent shouted again and merrily, when they felt that their brothers were amongst them, and presently was the arrow-storm at its fiercest, and the twanging of bowstrings and the whistle of the shafts was as the wind among the clefts of the mountains; for all the newcomers were bowmen of the best.

===Chinese===
但此刻，集市坪中那群恶徒（the Felons）之间，终于开始传开一股消息：有敌人进了山谷，正自坡上放箭；于是所有人都把脸转向山坡，整个人潮都朝那边涌去；然而他们行进甚慢，因为队列混乱至极，人人都在路上碍着自己邻人。黝暗人不仅蜂拥朝弓手坡而去，也挤向通往南方的大路。林智从坡上望见此景，既已大杀敌人，便想带着自己的人退回后方；他的同伴中已有两三人中箭负伤，而弓娥，若非长老挥舞铁锤护持，她早已死过三回了。这也不足为奇：此刻她立在一个小土丘上，身后一丛稀疏荆棘连一半身子都遮不住，她搭箭、放弦，专朝最显眼的目标射去，仿佛仍是仲夏之夜在幽谷（Shadowy Vale）中对着靶子习射一般。正当林智将要下令撤退之际，他们身后忽然响起堡谷号角欢快的声响；他转身朝林坡望去，看哪！山坡之下，甲兵之众明暗交织；其上方飘扬着狼之诸旗（the Banners of the Wolf），以及犍牛族、桥族与公牛族之旗。诸族弓手随即发出第一声呐喊，毫不稍停；反而射得更急，因为他们知道援兵自会而来，不必他们回头去招引：事实也正是如此。只见面神夹在两面狼旗之间，大步从坡上走下；他身旁是高个红狼（Red-wolf）与战林（War-grove），又有林习与林狡（Wood-wicked），并狼族其余许多壮士；因为如今诸族之人既已与敌人正面相对，对引路之人的需求大减，他们大半情愿在自家旗下与林中汉子并肩作战；如此一来，随狼旗下出征的那一队人便超过了三个半长百（long hundreds）；坡沿上的弓手感到自家兄弟已在其间，再次欢然呐喊；顷刻之间箭雨最为猛烈，弓弦之鸣与箭矢之啸，如风穿群山之罅；因为新到之人，无一不是上等弓手。

===Original===
But the kindreds of the Steer, the Bridge, and the Bull, they hung yet a while longer on the hills’ brow, their banners floating over them and their horns blowing; and the Dusky Felons in the Marketplace beheld them, and fear and rage at once filled their hearts, and a fierce and dreadful yell brake out from them, and joyously did the Men of Burgdale answer them, and song arose amongst them even such as this:

Therewith they ceased a moment, and then gave a great and hearty shout all together, and all their horns blew, and they moved on down the hill as one man, slowly and with no jostling, the spearmen first, and then they of the axe and the sword; and on their flanks the deft archers loosed on the stumbling jostling throng of the Dusky Men, who for their part came on drifting and surging up the road to the hill.

===Chinese===
然而犍牛族、桥族与公牛族这些支族，仍在山脊之上流连片刻，诸旗在他们头顶飘扬，号角齐鸣；集市坪中那些黝暗恶徒望着他们，心中一时既惧且怒，发出一声凶厉可怖的嚎叫；堡谷之人则欣然回以呐喊，歌声自他们之中而起，其辞大略如此：

随即他们静了片刻，接着齐声发出一声响亮雄壮的呐喊，所有号角齐鸣；他们如同一人般朝山下推进，从容而不拥挤，长枪手居前，斧兵与剑手继之；两翼灵巧的弓手朝跌跌撞撞、挤成一团的黝暗人放箭，而黝暗人那边，则沿着通向山坡的大路潮涌而来。

===Original===
But when those big spearmen of the Dale had gone a little way the horns’ voice died out, and their great-staved spears rose up from their shoulders into the air, and stood so a moment, and then slowly fell forward, as the oars of the longship fall into the rowlocks, and then over the shoulders of the foremost men showed the steel of the five ranks behind them, and their own spears cast long bars of shadow on the whiteness of the sunny road. No sound came from them now save the rattle of their armour and the tramp of their steady feet; but from the Dusky Men rose up hideous confused yelling, and those that could free themselves from the tangle of the throng rushed desperately against the on-rolling hedge of steel, and the whole throng shoved on behind them. Then met steel and men; here and there an ash-stave broke; here and there a Dusky Felon rolled himself unhurt under the ash-staves, and hewed the knees of the Dalesmen, and a tall man came tottering down; but what men or wood-wights could endure the push of spears of those mighty husbandmen? The Dusky Ones shrunk back yelling, or turned their backs and rushed at their own folk with such fierce agony that they entered into the throng, till the terror of the spear reached to the midmost of it and swayed them back on the hindermost; for neither was there outgate for the felons on the flanks of the spearmen, since there the feathered death beset them, and the bowmen (and the Bride amongst the foremost) shot wholly together, and no shaft flew idly.
