But the wise leaders of the Dalesmen would not that they should thrust in too far amongst the howling throng of the Dusky Men, lest they should be hemmed in by them; for they were but a handful in regard to them: so there they stayed, barring the way to the Dusky Men, and the bowmen still loosed from the flanks of them, or aimed deftly from betwixt the ranks of the spearmen.

===Chinese===
但当谷中那些魁梧的长枪手行出不远，号角之声渐渐息了；他们那粗杆长枪从肩头竖起直指苍穹，如此静立片刻，随即缓缓向前倾倒——如同长船之桨落入桨叉一般——继而在前列诸人肩后，露出其后五排人马的钢铁锋刃，他们自家的枪影在阳光洁白的大路上投下长长的横条阴影。此刻他们再无声息，唯有甲胄的铿锵与沉稳整齐的脚步声；而黝暗人那边则爆发出可怖而混乱的嚎叫，那些能从人丛纠缠中挣脱出来的，拼死朝那滚滚压来的钢铁藩篱冲去，整个人潮在他们身后推挤。于是钢铁与人相遇；处处有梣木枪杆折断；处处有黝暗恶徒毫发无伤地从枪丛之下滚过，斫砍谷民之膝，魁梧大汉便摇摇晃晃倒下；然而无论何人——无论人或林中之灵——怎能受得住那些壮健农人长枪之推刺？黝暗人嚎叫着退缩，或转过身朝自己人冲去，其状之苦痛狂乱，竟直冲入人群之中，直至长枪之惧深入其腹心，将他们朝最后方的人推挤而去；因为恶徒们在长枪手两翼也无出路，那里飞羽之死围困着他们，弓手们（新娘亦在其最前列）齐射而出，无一箭落空。然而谷民中那些明智的首领不愿他们过于深入黝暗人那嚎叫的人丛，恐怕反被其包围；因为与对方相比，他们不过是寥寥之众：于是他们便止步于此，挡住黝暗人的去路，弓手仍从两翼放箭，或从长枪手阵列之间精准瞄准。

===Original===
And now was there a space of ten strides or more betwixt the Dalesmen and their foes, over which the spears hung terribly, nor durst the Dusky Men adventure there; and thereon was nought but men dead or sorely hurt. Then suddenly a horn rang thrice shrilly over all the noise and clamour of the throng, and the ranks of the spearmen opened, and forth into that space strode two score of the swordsmen and axe-wielders of the Dale, their weapons raised in their hands, and he who led them was Iron-hand of the House of the Bull: tall he was, wide-shouldered, exceeding strong, but beardless and fair-faced. He bore aloft a two-edged sword, broad-bladed, exceeding heavy, so that few men could wield it in battle, but not right long; it was an ancient weapon, and his father before him had called it the Barley-scythe. With him were some of the best of the kindreds, as Wolf of Whitegarth, Long-hand of Oakholt, Hart of Highcliff, and War-well the captain of the Bridge. These made no tarrying on that space of the dead, but cried aloud their cries: “For the Burg and the Steer! for the Dale and the Bridge! for the Dale and the Bull!” and so fell at once on the Felons; who fled not, nor had room to flee; and also they feared not the edge-weapons so sorely as they feared those huge spears. So they turned fiercely on the swordsmen, and chiefly on Iron-hand, as he entered in amongst them the first of all, hewing to the right hand and the left, and many a man fell before the Barley-scythe; for they were but little before him. Yet as one fell another took his place, and hewed at him with the steel axe and the crooked sword; and with many strokes they clave his shield and brake his helm and rent his byrny, while he heeded little save smiting with the Barley-scythe, and the blood ran from his arm and his shoulder and his thigh.

===Chinese===
此刻谷民与敌人之间已隔出十步开阔之地，长枪可怖地悬在其上，黝暗人再不敢贸然踏入；那地面上唯余死者与重伤之人。忽然一声号角凌越所有人丛的喧嚣，连鸣三声，长枪手阵列洞开，四十名谷中的剑手与斧手大步踏入那片空地，手中高举兵刃；率众者乃是公牛族之铁手（Iron-hand）：他身量高大、肩宽背阔、力大无穷，却无须髯，面容清俊。他高擎一柄双刃阔剑，剑身极重，寻常人于战阵中少有能挥舞者，却不甚长；此乃一柄古兵，其父在世时便称之为麦镰（the Barley-scythe）。与他同行的，皆是诸族中最精锐的壮士，如白院之狼（Wolf of Whitegarth）、橡林之长手（Long-hand of Oakholt）、高崖之鹿（Hart of Highcliff），以及桥族之长战井（War-well）。这些人并不在那片死地之上稍作逗留，只高呼战号："为堡镇与犍牛族！为堡谷与桥族！为堡谷与公牛族！"便径直扑向那些恶徒；恶徒们不曾逃，也无路可逃；况且他们也并不像怕那些巨枪那样畏惧刀斧之属。于是他们凶猛地转身迎战那些剑手，尤其围攻铁手——他第一个杀入敌丛之中，左右挥砍，麦镰之下倒下了一人又一人；因为他们与他不过咫尺之近。然而一人倒下，另一人便补上其位，以钢斧和弯剑斫他；一击又一击，他们劈碎了他的盾、砸裂了他的盔、撕开了他的锁子甲，而他几乎全然不顾，只顾挥舞麦镰砍杀，鲜血从他的手臂、肩头和大腿汩汩流下。

===Original===
But War-well had entered in among the foe on his left hand, and unshielded hove up a great broad-bladed axe, that clave the iron helms of the Dusky Men, and rent their horn-scaled byrnies. He was not very tall, but his shoulders were huge and his arms long, and nought could abide his stroke. He cleared a ring round Iron-hand, whose eyes were growing dim as the blood flowed from him, and hewed three strokes before him; then turned and drew the champion out of the throng, and gave him into the arms of his fellows to stanch the blood that drained away the might of his limbs; and then with a great wordless roar leaped back again on the Dusky Men as the lion leapeth on the herd of swine; and they shrank away before him; and all the swordsmen shouted, “For the Bridge, for the Bridge!” and pressed on the harder, smiting down all before them. On his left hand now was Hart of Highcliff wielding a good sword hight Chip-driver, wherewith he had slain and hurt a many, fighting wisely with sword and shield, and driving the point home through the joints of the armour. But even therewith, as he drave a great stroke at a lord of the Dusky Ones, a cast-spear came flying and smote him on the breast, so that he staggered, and the stroke fell flatlings on the shield-boss of his foe, and Chip-driver brake atwain nigh the hilts; but Hart closed with him, and smote him on the face with the pommel, and tore his axe from his hand and clave his skull therewith, and slew him with his own weapon, and fought on valiantly beside War-well.

===Chinese===
而战井已杀入他左手边的敌丛之中，他不用盾牌，单手挥起一柄阔刃大斧，劈开黝暗人的铁盔，撕裂他们那角鳞编缀的锁子甲。他个子并不甚高，但肩膀宽阔异常、双臂修长，无人能挡他一击。他在铁手周围清出一圈空地——铁手双眼已渐模糊，鲜血正从他身上汩汩流下——向前连砍三斧；随即转身，将这位勇士从敌丛中拖出，交到同伴臂间，好止住那正抽走他肢体气力的鲜血；接着他发出一声无言的大吼，如雄狮扑入猪群般再度扑向黝暗人；他们在他面前纷纷退却；所有剑手齐声高呼："为桥族！为桥族！"更加奋勇地压上，将眼前一切砍倒。此刻在他左手边，是高崖之鹿，手中挥着一柄名为碎木（Chip-driver）的好剑；他持此剑已杀戮伤损甚众，以剑盾明智应战，专将剑尖刺入甲胄的接缝之处。然而就在此时，当他朝一位黝暗人首领挥出一记重击之际，一支飞掷之枪破空而来，正中他胸口，令他一个趔趄；那重重一击便平拍在敌人的盾首之上，碎木在近柄处断为两截；然而高崖之鹿与他贴身缠斗，以剑柄首猛击其面，夺下他手中的斧，反手劈开他的头颅，以他自家的兵刃取他性命，随即继续在战井身旁英勇奋战。

===Original===
Now War-well had fought so fiercely that he had rent his own hauberk with the might of his strokes, and as he raised his arm to smite a huge stroke, a deft man of the Felons thrust the spike of his war-axe up under his arm; and when War-well felt the smart of the steel, he turned on that man, and, letting his axe fall down to his wrist and hang there by its loop, he caught the foeman up by the neck and the breech, and drave him against the other Dusky Ones before him, so that their weapons pierced and rent their own friend and fellow. Then he put forth the might of his arms and the pith of his body, and hove up that felon and cast him on to the heads of his fellow murder-carles, so that he rent them and was rent by them. Then War-well fell on again with the axe, and all the champions of the Dale shouted and fell on with him, and the foe shrank away; and the Dalesmen cleared a space five fathoms’ length before them, and the spearmen drew onward and stood on the space whereon the first onslaught had been.

===Chinese===
战井战得如此凶猛，竟以挥斧之力撕开了自家的锁子甲；当他扬臂欲挥一记重斧之时，恶徒中一名灵巧之人将战斧之刺顶入了他的腋下；战井感到那钢铁刺痛，便转身扑向那人，任大斧滑到手腕处、由绳套挂住，他一手揪住那敌人的脖颈，一手揪住其臀腿，将他朝前面其余黝暗人撞去，使他们的兵刃刺穿、撕裂了自家的同伴与兄弟。随即他使尽双臂之力与腰身之气，将那恶徒高高举起，朝他那群凶徒（murder-carles）同伴的头顶掷去，令他既撕裂别人、也被人撕裂。战井随即又挥斧扑上，谷中所有壮士齐声呐喊，随之俱进，敌人纷纷退却；谷民在他们前方清出一片五噚（fathom）见长的空地，长枪手向前推进，驻足于第一次猛攻曾发生的那片地面之上。

===Original===
Then drew those hewers of the Dale together, and forth from the company came the man that bare the Banner of the Bridget and the champions gathered round him, and they ordered their ranks and strode with the Banner before them three times to and fro across the road athwart the front of the spearmen, and then with a great shout drew back within the spear-hedge. Albeit five of the champions of the Dale had been slain outright there, and the more part of them hurt more or less.

But when all were well within the ranks, once again blew the horn, and all the spears sank to the rest, and the kindreds drave the spear-furrow, and a space was swept clear before them, and the cries and yells of the Dusky Men were so fierce and wild that the rough voices of the Dalesmen were drowned amidst them.

===Chinese===
谷中那些刀斧手随即聚拢；举桥族之旗（the Banner of the Bridge）的那人从队列中步出，壮士们聚集到他周围；他们整顿队形，举旗行于前，在长枪手阵前那条大路上来回横走了三趟，随即在一片大喝声中退回枪篱之内。然而谷中的壮士已有五人当场阵亡于此，其余大半也都或多或少了负了伤。

待得众人尽数退回阵列之中，号角再度吹响，所有长枪一齐沉下成待发之势，诸族以枪阵如犁推进，前方又扫出一片空地；黝暗人的呐喊与嚎叫凶厉狂乱至极，竟将谷民粗犷的嗓音尽数淹没其中。

===Original===
Forth then came every bowman of the kindred that was there and loosed on the Dusky Men; and they forsooth had some bowmen amongst them, but cooped up and jostled as they were they shot but wildly; whereas each shaft of the Dale went home truly.

But amongst the bowmen forth came the Bride in her glittering war-gear, and stepped lightly to the front of the spearmen. Her own yew bow had been smitten by a shaft and broken in her hand: so she had caught up a short horn bow and a quiver from one of the slain of the Dusky Men; and now she knelt on one knee under the shadow of the spears nigh to her grandsire Hall-ward, and with a pale face and knitted brow notched and loosed, and notched and loosed on the throng of foemen, as if she were some daintily fashioned engine of war.

===Chinese===
于是族中所有在场的弓手一齐上前，朝黝暗人放箭；对方其实也有几个弓手，但困在人丛之中、互相推挤，射得毫无准头；而谷民这边，每一箭都精准中的。

而在众弓手之中，新娘也步出阵列，她身披闪亮的战甲，轻快地走到长枪手之前。她原本那张紫杉弓被一支箭射中，在她手中折断：于是她从一个黝暗人死者身上抄起一张短角弓和一壶箭；此刻她单膝跪在长枪的阴影之下，挨着她的祖父厅卫（Hall-ward），面色苍白、眉头紧锁，搭箭、放弦，再搭箭、放弦，朝敌丛射去——仿佛她是一具精心打造的战争器械。

===Original===
So fared the battle on the road that went from the south into the Marketstead. Valiantly had the kindred fought there, and no man of them had blenched, and much had they won; but the way was perilous before them, for the foe was many and many.

===Chinese===
从南方通往集市坪的那条大路上的战事，便是如此。诸族在此战得英勇，无一人退缩，斩获甚丰；然而前路仍险，因为敌人众多，数不胜数。

## XXXI Of the Weapon-Show of the Men of Burgdale and Their Neighbours / 三十一 论堡谷之民及其邻人之武器大阅

===Original===
Now on the day appointed for the Weapon-show came the Folk flockmeal to the great and wide meadow that was cleft by Wildlake as it ran to join the Weltering Water. Early in the morning, even before sunrise, had the wains full of women and children begun to come thither. Also there came little horses and asses from the Shepherd country with one or two or three damsels or children sitting on each, and by wain-side or by beast strode the men of the house, merry and fair in their war-gear. The Woodlanders, moreover, man and woman, elder and swain and young damsel, streamed out of the wood from Carlstead, eager to make the day begin before the sunrise, and end before his setting.

Then all men fell to pitching of tents and tilting over of wains; for the April sun was hot in the Dale, and when he arose the meads were gay with more than the spring flowers; for the tents and the tilts were stained and broidered with many colours, and there was none who had not furbished up his war-gear so that all shone and glittered. And many wore gay surcoats over their armour, and the women were clad in all their bravery, and the Houses mostly of a suit; for one bore blue and another corn-colour, and another green, and another brazil, and so forth, and all gleaming and glowing with broidery of gold and bright hues. But the women of the Shepherds were all clad in white, embroidered with green boughs and red blossoms, and the Woodland women wore dark red kirtles. Moreover, the women had set garlands of flowers on their heads and the helms of the men, and for the most part they were slim of body and tall and light-limbed, and as dainty to look upon as the willow-boughs that waved on the brook-side.

===Chinese===
到了预定的武器大阅（Weapon-show）之日，众民如潮涌至那片广袤草甸——那草甸为野湖溪（Wildlake）所截分，溪水由此处汇入翻滚河（the Weltering Water）。清晨时分，日头尚未升起，载满妇孺的大车便已开始络绎而来。又有牧羊之乡的小马与驴子，每头牲口上坐着两三个少女或孩童，车旁或牲口边，便是家中的汉子们，披挂齐整、神采飞扬地大步而行。至于林中之民，男女老少、长者少年与年轻少女，从汉子镇（Carlstead）鱼贯而出林，唯愿这一日能在日出之前起始、日落之前结束。

于是众人纷纷动手搭帐篷、支起车篷；盖因谷中四月，日头已烈；待日头升起，草甸上比春花更绚烂的，是那染绣斑斓的帐篷与车篷：人人皆将自己甲胄兵刃打磨一新，处处闪亮夺目。许多人甲外更罩鲜艳罩袍（surcoat），妇人们皆盛装而出，各氏族多为一色装束：有蓝色，有谷穗色，有绿色，有苏木红，不一而足；金线与诸般鲜色绣出之花纹熠熠生辉。然牧羊人之妇皆衣白，绣以青枝红花；林中妇人身着暗红短袍（kirtle）。妇人们更将花环戴在头上、戴在男子的盔上；她们大多身段纤细、体态高挑、四肢轻盈，望之婀娜可爱，恰如溪边摇曳之柳枝。

===Original===
Thither had the goodmen who were guesting the Runaways brought their guests, even now much bettered by their new soft days; and much the poor folk marvelled at all this joyance, and they scarce knew where they were; but to some it brought back to their minds days of joyance before the thralldom and all that they had lost, so that their hearts were heavy a while, till they saw the warriors of the kindreds streaming into the mead and bethought them why they carried steel.

Now by then the sun was fully up there was a great throng on the Portway, and this was the folk of the Burg on their way to the Weapon-mead. The men-at-arms were in the midst of the throng, and at the head of them was the War-leader, with the banner of the Face before him, wherein was done the image of the God with the ray-ringed head. But at the rearward of the warriors went the Alderman and the Burg-wardens, before whom was borne the banner of the Burg pictured with the Gate and its Towers; but in the midst betwixt those two was the banner of the Steer, a white beast on a green field.

So when the Dale-wardens who were down in the meadow heard the music and beheld who were coming, they bade the companies of the Dale and the Shepherds and the Woodlanders who were down there to pitch their banners in a half circle about the ingle of the meadow which was made by the streams of Wildlake and the Weltering Water, and gather to them to be ordered there under their leaders of scores and half-hundreds and hundreds; and even so they did. But the banners of the Dale without the Burg were the Bridge, and the Bull, and the Vine, and the Sickle. And the Shepherds had three banners, to wit Greenbury, and the Fleece, and the Thorn.

===Chinese===
那收留逃奴（the Runaways）的主人们，也将客人们带到了此处——这些客人如今已在新得的安乐日子里好转了许多；这班可怜人见了这番盛况，大为惊叹，几乎不知身在何处；而其中有人，则被勾起了奴役之前那些欢乐日子的回忆，想起所失的一切，心头一时沉重，直至看见各族武士鱼贯进入草甸，才想起他们为何身披铁甲。

待到日头完全升起，港路（the Portway）之上已是人潮涌动——那是堡（the Burg）中之民，正前往阅兵草甸。甲士们走在人群当中，为首的便是战首（the War-leader），他前面是面族（the Face）的旗帜，旗上绘着那头部光芒环绕的神像。武士队伍的殿后，则是长老（the Alderman）与众堡卫（the Burg-wardens），他们前面打着堡旗，旗上绘着堡门与诸塔楼；而介于前后两面旗之间的，是犍牛族（the Steer）的旗号——绿底上一头白色牲口。

草甸上的谷卫（the Dale-wardens）听见乐声、看见来者是谁，便下令谷中各队、牧羊之民、林中之民在野湖溪与翻滚河相汇所成的草甸角落处，列成半圆阵、竖起各自的旗帜，并在廿长（leaders of scores）、半百长（half-hundred-leaders）、百长（hundred-leaders）之下整队听令；众人依令而行。堡谷在堡以外的旗号，是桥族（the Bridge）、公牛族（the Bull）、葡藤族（the Vine）、镰族（the Sickle）。牧羊之民则有旗三面，即绿堡（Greenbury）、羊绒旗（the Fleece）、荆棘旗（the Thorn）。

===Original===
As for the Woodlanders, they said that they were abiding their great banner, but it should come in good time; "and meantime," said they, "here are the war-tokens that we shall fight under; for they are good enough banners for us poor men, the remnant of the valiant of time past." Therewith they showed two great spears, and athwart the one was tied an arrow, its point dipped in blood, its feathers singed with fire; and they said, "This is the banner of the War-shaft."

On the other spear there was nought; but the head thereof was great and long, and they had so burnished the steel that the sun smote out a ray of light from it, so that it might be seen from afar. And they said: "This is the Banner of the Spear! Down yonder where the ravens are gathering ye shall see a banner flying over us. There shall fall many a mother's son."

Smiled the Dale-wardens, and said that these were good banners to fight under; and those that stood nearby shouted for the valiancy of the Woodland Carles.

Now the Dale-wardens went to the entrance from the Portway to the meadow, and there met the Men of the Burg, and two of them went one on either side of the War-leader to show him to his seat, and the others abode till the Alderman and Burg-wardens came up, and then joined themselves to them, and the horns blew up both in the meadow and on the road, and the newcomers went their ways to their appointed places amidst the shouts of the Dalesmen; and the women and children and old men from the Burg followed after, till all the mead was covered with bright raiment and glittering gear, save within the ring of men at the further end.

===Chinese===
至于林中之民，他们说在等他们的大旗，那旗自会按时而来；"与此同时，"他们道，"这便是我们要在其下作战的战记；对我们这些可怜人——往昔壮士之余裔——来说，这已是够好的旗帜了。"说着便亮出两杆长枪：其中一杆横绑着一支箭，箭头蘸过血，箭羽为火所燎焦；他们道："这便是战箭旗（the War-shaft）。"

另一杆枪上空无一物；但枪头硕大修长，他们将钢头磨得锃亮，日头一照便射出一道光来，远远即可望见。他们道："这便是长枪之旗（the Spear）！下面那群乌鸦聚集之处，你们将要看见一面旗子飘在我们头顶。那里将有许多母亲之子倒下。"

谷卫们微微一笑，说这都是作战的好旗帜；旁边的人则大声喝彩，称赞林中汉子（the Woodland Carles）的勇武。

谷卫们便走到港路通往草甸的入口处，迎上堡中之众；其中二人一左一右伴着战首，将他引至座位；其余人则等候长老与众堡卫上前，然后与他们相合。号角齐鸣，草甸与路上俱起乐声；新来者在谷民欢呼之声中走向各自指定之处；堡中妇孺老者随后鱼贯而入，直至整片草甸为鲜衣亮甲所覆，唯有最里端那圈武士围着之处除外。

===Original===
So came the War-leader to his seat of green turf raised in the ingle aforesaid; and he stood beside it till the Alderman and Wardens had taken their places on a seat behind him raised higher than his; below him on the step of his seat sat the Scrivener with his pen and ink-horn and scroll of parchment, and men had brought him a smooth shield whereon to write.

On the left side of Face-of-god stood the men of the Face all glittering in their arms, and amongst them were Wolf-stone and his two fellows, but Dallach was not yet whole of his hurts. On his right were the folk of the House of the Steer: the leader of that House was an old white-bearded man, grandfather of the Bride, for her father was dead; and who but the Bride herself stood beside him in her glorious war-gear, looking as if she were new come from the City of the Gods, thought most men; but those who beheld her closely deemed that she looked heavy-eyed and haggard, as if she were aweary. Nevertheless, wheresoever she passed, and whosoever looked on her (and all men looked on her), there arose a murmur of praise and love; and the women, and especially the young ones, said how fair her deed was, and how meet she was for it; and some of them were for doing on war-gear and faring to battle with the carles; and of these some were sober and solemn, as was well seen afterwards, and some spake lightly: some also fell to boasting of how they could run and climb and swim and shoot in the bow, and fell to baring of their arms to show how strong they were: and indeed they were no weaklings, though their arms were fair.

There then stood the ring of men, each company under its banner; and beyond them stood the women and children and men unmeet for battle; and beyond them again the tilted wains and the tents.

===Chinese===
战首便来到那设于前述角落处的草皮座位前；他立于座旁，等候长老与众卫事在身后一座比他更高的座位上落座；他下方那级台阶上，坐着书吏（the Scrivener），手执笔、墨角、羊皮卷，旁人已为他备好一面光滑盾牌，用以书写。

面神左侧站着面族之众，甲胄鲜明、光彩夺目；其中便有狼石（Wolf-stone）及其两名同伴，只是达拉赫（Dallach）的伤尚未痊愈。其右侧是犍牛族之众：此族之首是一位白须老者，乃新娘之外祖，盖因其父已逝；而立在他身边的，不是别人，正是新娘自己，身着华美军装；多数人皆以为她望之恍若方自诸神之城（the City of the Gods）而来；然细看她的人则觉她眼睑沉重、面色憔悴，似是十分倦怠。纵然如此，凡她所过之处、凡目视她之人——而人人皆注视她——必兴起一阵赞美怜爱的低语；妇人们，尤其是年轻妇人，都说她此举何其壮美，又何其相称；其中有些便要披甲上阵，与汉子们同赴战场；这些人里有些庄重肃穆——其后事果然证实了——也有些不过信口一说；还有些便开始夸耀自己能跑、能爬、能泅水、能射箭，又捋起衣袖露出胳膊，以示自己气力如何了得：她们的胳膊虽白皙，倒也确实并非弱质。

武士之圈便如此立定，每一队各立于其旗下；他们之外，是不堪上阵之妇孺男子；再外一层，则是支篷之车与帐篷。

===Original===
Now Face-of-god sat him down on the turf-seat with his bright helm on his head and his naked sword across his knees, while the horns blew up loudly, and when they had done, the elder of the Dale-wardens cried out for silence. Then again arose Face-of-god and said:

"Men of the Dale, and ye friends of the Shepherds, and ye, O valiant Woodlanders; we are not assembled here to take counsel, for in three days' time shall the Great Folk-mote be holden, whereat shall be counsel enough. But since I have been appointed your Chief and War-leader, till such time as the Folk-mote shall either yea-say or naysay my leadership, I have sent for you that we may look each other in the face and number our host and behold our weapons, and see if we be meet for battle and for the dealing with a great host of foemen. For now no longer can it be said that we are going to war, but rather that war is on our borders, and we are blended with it; as many have learned to their cost; for some have been slain and some sorely hurt. Therefore I bid you now, all ye that are weaponed, wend past us that the tale of you may be taken. But first let every hundred-leader and half-hundred-leader and score-leader make sure that he hath his tale aright, and give his word to the captain of his banner that he in turn may give it out to the Scrivener with his name and the House and Company that he leadeth."

So he spake and sat him adown; and the horns blew again in token that the companies should go past; and the first that came was Hall-ward of the House of the Steer, and the first of those that went after him was the Bride, going as if she were his son.

So he cried out his name, and the name of his House, and said, "An hundred and a half," and passed forth, his men following him in most goodly array. Each man was girt with a good sword and bore a long heavy spear over his shoulder, save a score who bare bows; and no man lacked a helm, a shield, and a coat of fence.

===Chinese===
于是面神便在草皮座上坐下，头戴明盔，膝上横放出鞘之剑；号角高鸣，吹罢，谷卫中之长者高声喝令肃静。面神复又起身，说道：

"谷中之民啊，牧羊之民的友人们啊，勇武的林中之民啊：我们今日并非聚于此处议事，因三日之后便要召开大民众大会（the Great Folk-mote），届时自有议不完的事。然我既已被任为你们的首领、你们的战首，直至民众大会对我这统帅之位或可或否为止，我便传你们前来，好叫我们彼此相看一面、清点兵马、检视兵刃，看看我们可堪一战、可堪抵御敌军大队。如今已不能再说我方才欲启战端，应当说是战火已临我境、我等已与之交缠；许多人已付出代价方才明白此理：有的已被杀，有的身负重伤。故此我今命你们：凡持兵刃者，皆从我面前鱼贯而过，好叫人清点你们之数。但先须令各位百长、半百长、廿长核清自己之数，禀报旗尉；旗尉再转报书吏，附上自己之名，以及所领之氏族与队号。"

他说罢坐下；号角再起，示意各队依次通过；最先过来的，是犍牛族的厅卫（Hall-ward）；而紧随他之后的第一人，便是新娘，行走之间仿若便是他的儿子。

他高声报出自己之名、本族之名，道："一百五十。"便阔步而过，所部以极整齐之队列相随。每人都腰佩好剑，肩扛沉重长枪，唯其中二十人持弓；人人皆备盔、盾、与护身铠甲（coat of fence），无一或缺。

===Original===
Then came a goodly man of thirty winters, and stayed before the Scrivener and cried out:

"Write down the House of the Bridge of the Upper Dale at one hundred, and War-well their leader."

And he strode on, and his men followed clad and weaponed like those of the Steer, save that some had axes hanging to their girdles instead of swords; and most bore casting-spears instead of the long spears, and half a score were bowmen.

Then came Fox of Upton leading the men of the Bull of Mid-dale, an hundred and a half lacking two; very great and tall were his men, and they also bore long spears, and one score and two were bowmen.

Then Fork-beard of Lea, a man well on in years, led on the men of the Vine, an hundred and a half and five men thereto; two score of them bare bow in hand and were girt with sword; the rest bore their swords naked in their right hands, and their shields (which were but small bucklers) hanging at their backs, and in the left hand each bore two casting-spears. With these went two doughty women-at-arms among the bowmen, tall and well-knit, already growing brown with the spring sun, for their work lay among the stocks of the vines on the southward-looking bents.

Next came a tall young man, yellow-haired, with a thin red beard, and gave himself out for Red-beard of the Knolls; he bore his father's name, as the custom of their house was, but the old man, who had long been head man of the House of the Sickle, was late dead in his bed, and the young man had not seen twenty winters. He bade the Scrivener write the tale of the Men of the Sickle at an hundred and a half, and his folk fared past the War-leader joyously, being one half of them bowmen; and fell shooters they were; the other half were girt with swords, and bore withal long ashen staves armed with great blades curved inwards, which weapon they called heft-sax.

===Chinese===
接着来了一位三十岁之英俊汉子，止步于书吏之前，高声喊道：

"记下：上谷桥族（the Bridge of the Upper Dale），一百人，其首领为战井（War-well）。"

他便大步前行，所部紧随，装束兵刃与犍牛族相仿，只是有些人腰间挂的是斧而非剑；多数人持投枪，而非长枪；其中十人为弓手。

其后是上镇之狐（Fox of Upton），率中谷公牛族之众而来，数为一百五十缺二；其部下身躯极高大，亦持长枪，其中二十二人为弓手。

其后是草地之叉须（Fork-beard of Lea），一位上了年岁之人，率葡藤族之众而来，数为一百五十五人；其中四十人持弓、佩剑；余人右手持出鞘之剑，盾（不过是小圆盾）悬于背，左手各持两杆投枪。随此队者，有两位勇健女甲士，杂于弓手之间，身形高挑、筋骨结实，因春日做活肤色已晒成褐——她们的活计本就在南向坡上葡萄藤架之间。

其后是一位高挑少年，黄发，疏而红的胡须，自报名为丘陵之红须（Red-beard of the Knolls）；他袭的是父亲之名——这是他家的规矩——但那位久为镰族之长的老者，近日方才病殁于床榻，这少年尚不满二十之数。他令书吏记下：镰族之众，一百五十；其部属欣然自战首面前而过，其中半数为弓手，且皆是善射之人；另一半腰佩剑，又持长大白蜡杆，杆头装有内向弯曲之大刃——此种兵刃他们唤作柄刀（heft-sax）。

===Original===
All these bands, as the name and the tale of them was declared were greeted with loud shouts from their fellows and the bystanders; but now arose a greater shout still, as Stone-face, clad in goodly glittering array, came forth and said:

"I am Stone-face of the House of the Face, and I bring with me two hundreds of men with their best war-gear and weapons: write it down, Scrivener!"

And he strode on like a young man after those who had gone past, and after him came the tall Hall-face and his men, a gallant sight to see: two score bowmen girt with swords, and the others with naked swords waving aloft, and each bearing two casting-spears in his left hand.

Then came a man of middle age, broad-shouldered, yellow-haired, blue-eyed, of wide and ruddy countenance, and after him a goodly company; and again great was the shout that went up to the heavens; for he said:

"Scrivener, write down that Hound-under-Greenbury, from amongst the dwellers in the hills where the sheep feed, leadeth the men who go under the banner of Greenbury, to the tale of an hundred and four score."

Therewith he passed on, and his men followed, stout, stark, and merry-faced, girt with swords, and bearing over their shoulders long-staved axes, and spears not so long as those which the Dalesmen bore; and they had but a half score of arrow-shot with them.

===Chinese===
这些队伍报名报数之时，同伴与旁观者皆以高声喝彩相迎；然此刻升起更大一阵欢呼，因石面（Stone-face）身着辉煌灿烂之军装而出，说道：

"我是面族之石面，随我而来者，是两百名携其最佳军装兵刃之士：记下，书吏！"

他如少年般大步追随前人而去；其后便是高大的厅面（Hall-face）及其部下，好不威风：四十名弓手皆佩剑，余人挥舞出鞘之剑高举过顶，左手各持两杆投枪。

接着是一位中年汉子，肩宽、黄发、蓝眼、面庞阔而红润，身后随着一队精壮；又是一阵直冲云霄的欢呼；只听他说道：

"书吏，记下：绿堡之下猎犬（Hound-under-Greenbury），出自羊群所牧之山岭居人之中，率绿堡旗下来之众，数为一百八十。"

说罢而过，其部下相随，个个粗壮、结实、面带欢容，腰佩剑，肩扛长柄斧，又持枪，但枪不如谷民所用之枪那样长；他们随身的箭手不过五人而已。

===Original===
Next came a young man, blue-eyed also, with hair the colour of flax on the distaff, broad-faced and short-nosed, low of stature, but very strong-built, who cried out in a loud, cheerful voice:

"I am Strongitharm of the Shepherds, and these valiant men are of the Fleece and the Thorn blended together, for so they would have it; and their tale is one hundred and two score and ten."

Then the men of those kindreds went past merry and shouting, and they were clad and weaponed like to them of Greenbury, but had with them a score of bowmen. And all these Shepherd-folk wore over their hauberks white woollen surcoats broidered with green and red.

Now again uprose the cry, and there stood before the War-leader a very tall man of fifty winters, dark-faced and grey-eyed, and he spake slowly and somewhat softly, and said:

"War-leader, this is Red-wolf of the Woodlanders leading the men who go under the sign of the War-shaft, to the number of an hundred and two."

Then he passed on, and his men after him, tall, lean, and silent amidst the shouting. All these men bare bows, for they were keen hunters; each had at his girdle a little axe and a wood-knife, and some had long swords withal. They wore, everyone of the carles, short green surcoats over their coats of fence; but amongst them were three women who bore like weapons to the men, but were clad in red kirtles under their hauberks, which were of good ring-mail gleaming over them from throat to knee.

===Chinese===
其后是一位少年，亦是蓝眼，发色如纺竿上之亚麻，面庞宽阔、鼻短，身量不高却极结实，以洪亮欢快之声高喊道：

"我是牧羊之民之强臂（Strongitharm），这些壮士乃羊绒旗与荆棘旗两队合而为一，因他们自愿如此；其数为一百五十人。"

于是这些氏族之人欢呼欣然而过，装束兵刃与绿堡之人相仿，但带有二十名弓手。所有这些牧羊之民，皆在锁子甲（hauberk）外罩白毛料罩袍，上绣绿与红。

呼声再起，战首面前站着一位五十岁极高之人，面庞黝黑、灰眼，说话缓慢而略带柔和，说道：

"战首，此乃林中之民之红狼（Red-wolf），率战箭旗下之众而来，数为一百零二人。"

他便前行，其部下随之，在欢呼之中个个高挑、清瘦、默然无声。这些人皆持弓，盖因他们是好猎手；每人腰间挂着小斧与一把林刀，有些人还带有长剑。这些汉子每人都于护甲之外着短绿罩袍；但其中有三位女子，所持兵刃与男子相同，铠甲之内着红短袍，其铠乃精良环甲（ring-mail），自颈至膝闪闪覆于身上。

===Original===
Last came another tall man, but young, of twenty-five winters, and spake:

"Scrivener, I am Bears-bane of the Woodlanders, and these that come after me wend under the sign of the Spear, and they are of the tale of one hundred and seven."

And he passed by at once, and his men followed him, clad and weaponed no otherwise than they of the War-shaft, and with them were two women.

Now went all those companies back to their banners, and stood there; and there arose among the bystanders much talk concerning the Weapon-show, and who were the best arrayed of the Houses. And of the old men, some spake of past weapon-shows which they had seen in their youth, and they set them beside this one, and praised and blamed. So it went on a little while till the horns blew again, and once more there was silence. Then arose Face-of-god and said:

===Chinese===
最后是一位高挑汉子，却年轻，年方二十五，说道：

"书吏，我是林中之民之熊厄（Bears-bane），随我而来者，行走于长枪之旗下，其数一百零七。"

他便径自而过，部下相随，装束兵刃与战箭旗下之人无异，其中亦有两位女子。

于是诸队皆归本旗下，立定其间；旁观者之间遂起诸多议论，谈此次武器大阅，谈哪一族军装最为齐整。老者们之中，有人谈起少年时所见过往之武器大阅，将其与今日者并列相较，或赞或弹。如此过了一阵，号角再起，又复肃静。面神复又起身，说道：

===Original===
"Men of Burgdale, and ye Shepherd-folk, and ye of the Woodland, now shall ye wot how many weaponed men we may bring together for this war. Scrivener, arise and give forth the tale of the companies, as they have been told unto you."

Then the Scrivener stood up on the turf-bench beside Face-of-god, and spake in a loud voice, reading from his scroll:

"Of the Men of Burgdale there have passed by me nine hundreds and six; of the Shepherds three hundreds and eight and ten; and of the Woodlanders two hundreds and nine; so that all told our men are fourteen hundreds and thirty and three."

Now in those days men reckoned by long hundreds, so that the whole tale of the host was one thousand, five hundred, and four score and one, telling the tale in short hundreds.

===Chinese===
"堡谷之民啊，牧羊之民啊，林中之民啊：如今你们将知，此战我们能召集多少持兵之士。书吏，起来，照各队报于你之数，宣告总账。"

于是书吏起身，立于面神身旁之草皮阶上，朗声读其卷上所记：

"堡谷之民，过我前者，九百零六人；牧羊之民，三百一十八人；林中之民，二百零九人；合计共一千四百三十三人。"

彼时之人以长百（long hundreds）计之，故全军总数折为短百计之，实为一千五百八十一人。

===Original===
When the tale had been given forth and heard, men shouted again, and they rejoiced that they were so many. For it exceeded the reckoning which the Alderman had given out at the Gate-thing. But Face-of-god said:

"Neighbours, we have held our Weapon-show; but now hold you ready, each man, for the Hosting toward very battle; for belike within seven days shall the leaders of hundreds and twenties summon you to be ready in arms to take whatso fortune may befall. Now is sundered the Weapon-show. Be ye as merry today as your hearts bid you to be."

Therewith he came down from his seat with the Alderman and the Wardens, and they mingled with the good folk of the Dale and the Shepherds and the Woodlanders, and merry was their converse there. It yet lacked an hour of noon; so presently they fell to and feasted in the green meadow, drinking from wain to wain and from tent to tent; and thereafter they played and sported in the meads, shooting at the butts and wrestling, and trying other masteries. Then they fell to dancing one and all, and so at last to supper on the green grass in great merriment. Nor might you have known from the demeanour of any that any threat of evil overhung the Dale. Nay, so glad were they, and so friendly, that you might rather have deemed that this was the land whereof tales tell, wherein people die not, but live forever, without growing any older than when they first come thither, unless they be born into the land itself, and then they grow into fair manhood, and so abide. In sooth, both the land and the folk were fair enough to be that land and the folk thereof.

But a little after sunset they sundered, and some fared home; but many of them abode in the tents and tilted wains, because the morrow was the first day of the Spring Market: and already were some of the Westland chapmen come; yea, two of them were with the bystanders in the meadow; and more were looked for ere the night was far spent.

===Chinese===
报数既出，众皆闻之，欢声复起；人皆喜己方之众如此之多，盖此数已超过长老于门会（the Gate-thing）所宣布之估算。然面神道：

"邻里们，武器大阅已毕；但你们每个人要为真正的临阵集结（the Hosting）做好准备；因为不出七日，百长与廿长便会传令你们整装待发，以迎任何不测之命运。武器大阅到此解散。今日你们要心中如何欢喜，便如何欢喜地去吧。"

说罢，他与长老、众卫事一同下座，与谷中良民、牧羊之民、林中之民相混杂；其间言谈甚欢。其时距正午尚有一时；不多时众人便动手在那青草甸上设席痛饮，自一车至一车、自一帐至一帐地互相劝酒；其后在草甸上游玩戏耍，或射靶、或角力，比试诸般本领。然后众人一同跳起舞来，最后又在青草之上大设晚宴，尽欢而罢。从任何人之神色上，你都不会看出此谷有何祸患临头。不，他们如此欢悦、如此友善，你倒宁可相信这便是传说中所说之地：其民不死，长生不老，永保初到时之年貌；除非本生于此地，则长成壮美之人而永驻。说实在的，此地与此地之民，也确实够美，足以充当那地与那民。

然日落未久，众人便散；有的归家，但许多人留在帐篷与支篷车中，因次日乃是春市（the Spring Market）之首日：西土（the Westland）客商已有几人先到；其中两人便在草甸旁观者之中；夜未深时，尚有更多客商可期而至。

## LIII Of the Word Which Hall-Ward of the Steer Had for Folk-Might / 五十三 牛族厅卫向民强所进之言

===Original===
But of the time then passing, it is to be said that the whole host abode in Silverdale in great mirth and good liking, till they should hear tidings of Dallach and his company, who had followed hotfoot on the fleers of the Dusky Men. And on the tenth day after the battle, Iron-face and his two sons and Stone-face were sitting about sunset under a great oak-tree by that stream-side which ran through the Motestead; there also was Folk-might, somewhat distraught because of his love for the Bride, who was now mending of her hurts. As they sat there in all content they saw folk coming toward them, three in number, and as they drew nigher they saw that it was old Hall-ward of the Steer, and the Sun-beam and Bow-may following him hand in hand.

When they came to the brook Bow-may ran up to the elder to help him over the stepping-stones; which she did as one who loved him, as the old man was stark enough to have waded the water waist-deep. She was no longer in her war-gear, but was clad after her wont of Shadowy Vale, in nought but a white woollen kirtle. So she stood in the stream beside the stones, and let the swift water ripple up over her ankles, while the elder leaned on her shoulder and looked down upon her kindly. The Sun-beam followed after them, stepping daintily from stone to stone, so that she was a fair sight to see; her face was smiling and happy, and as she stepped forth on to the green grass the colour flushed up in it, but she cast her eyes adown as one somewhat shamefaced.

===Chinese===
至于当时这段时日，须得交代一句：全军驻于银谷之中，极为欢畅满足，只待达拉赫及其部众的消息——他们一路火速穷追黝暗人的溃逃者而去。战后第十日，约莫日落时分，铁面与二子及石面坐于议事坪旁那条溪畔的一棵大橡树之下；民强亦在彼处，因心系正在养伤渐愈的新娘，神思略有不属。众人正安坐闲适之际，见有人向他们走来，共三名；及至行近，认出是牛族（the Steer）的老厅卫，日光与弓娥手牵着手随在其后。

三人行至溪畔，弓娥抢步上前搀扶老者踏石而过；她此举全然出于爱敬——其实以老翁之硬朗，本可涉水没腰而渡。她已不披战甲，而是按幽谷的旧惯，只着一袭白羊毛裙衫。她便立于溪中踏石之旁，任湍急的水流漫过脚踝，老者则倚在她肩头，慈祥地俯视着她。日光随在他们身后，自一块踏石轻盈地挪向另一块，其姿之美，令人赏心悦目；她面带微笑、满心欢喜，待双足踏上青草之时，脸上泛起红晕，却如含羞一般垂下双目。

===Original===
So the chieftains rose up before the leader of the Steer, and Folk-might went up to him, and greeted him, and took his hand and kissed him on the cheek. And Hall-ward said:

“Hail to the chiefs of the kindred, and my earthly friends!”

Then Folk-might bade him sit down by him, and all the men sat down again; but the Sun-beam leaned her back against a sapling ash hard by, her feet set close together; and Bow-may went to and fro in short turns, keeping well within earshot.

Then said Hall-ward: “Folk-might, I have prayed thy kinswoman Bow-may to lead me to thee, that I might speak with thee; and it is good that I find my kinsmen of the Face in thy company; for I would say a word to thee that concerns them somewhat.”

===Chinese===
众首领遂在牛族首领面前起身相迎，民强走上前去致意，握其手而吻其颊。厅卫说道：

「宗族的诸位首领，我在世间的挚友们，万安！」

于是民强请他在身旁落座，众人皆重新坐下；日光却倚在近旁一株幼龄白蜡树上，双足并拢；弓娥则在近处来回踱着短步，始终不走出听得见话声的范围。

厅卫乃道：「民强，我请了你同宗的弓娥引我来见你，好与你一谈；能在此遇见面族的诸位亲族，甚好；因我有一句话要对你说，与他们也有些干系。」

===Original===
Said Folk-might: “Guest, and warrior of the Steer, thy words are ever good; and if this time thou comest to ask aught of me, then shall they be better than good.”

Said Hall-ward: “Tell me, Folk-might, hast thou seen my daughter the Bride today?”

“Yea,” said Folk-might, reddening.

“What didst thou deem of her state?” said Hall-ward.

Said Folk-might: “Thou knowest thyself that the fever hath left her, and that she is mending.”

===Chinese===
民强道：「客人，牛族的武士，你的话向来是好的；若此番你是来有所求于我，那么你的话便好上加好了。」

厅卫道：「民强，告诉我，你今日可曾见我女儿新娘？」

「见过了。」民强说道，脸上一红。

厅卫道：「你觉得她情形如何？」

民强道：「你自己也知道，热已退了，她正在好转。」

===Original===
Hall-ward said: “In a few days belike we shall be wending home to Burgdale: when deemest thou that the Bride may travel, if it were but on a litter?”

Folk-might was silent, and Hall-ward smiled on him and said:

“Wouldst thou have her tarry, O chief of the Wolf?”

===Chinese===
厅卫道：「过不了几日，我们大概便要启程回堡谷去了：依你之见，新娘何时才能上路，即便是用担架抬着走？」

民强默然不语，厅卫对他微微一笑，说道：

「狼族的首领啊，你莫非要她留下？」

===Original===
“So it is,” said Folk-might, “that it might be labour lost for her to journey to Burgdale at present.”

“Thinkest thou?” said Hall-ward; “hast thou a mind then that if she goeth she shall speedily come back hither?”

“It has been in my mind,” said Folk-might, “that I should wed her. Wilt thou gainsay it? I pray thee, Iron-face my friend, and ye Stone-face and Hall-face, and thou, Face-of-god, my brother, to lay thy words to mine in this matter.”

===Chinese===
民强道：「正是如此——此刻要她前往堡谷，恐怕是白费功夫。」

厅卫道：「你是这般想的么？那么你的意思莫非是——她若去了，便会很快回到此处？」

民强道：「我心下早有此意——我要娶她为妻。你可反对？我也恳请你，我的朋友铁面，还有你们，石面、厅面，以及我的兄弟面神，在这件事上替我帮衬一句话。」

===Original===
Then said Hall-ward stroking his beard: “There will be a seat missing in the Hall of the Steer, and a sore lack in the heart of many a man in Burgdale if the Bride come back to us no more. We looked not to lose the maiden by her wedding; for it is no long way betwixt the House of the Steer and the House of the Face. But now, when I arise in the morning and miss her, I shall take my staff and walk down the street of Burgstead; for I shall say, The Maiden hath gone to see Iron-face my friend; she is well in the House of the Face. And then shall I remember how that the wood and the wastes lie between us. How sayest thou, Alderman?”

===Chinese===
厅卫捋着胡须说道：「新娘若不再回来，牛族厅堂里便要空出一个座位，堡谷许多人心中也要深以为缺。我们本不曾料到因她出嫁而失了这女子；因牛族之宅与面神之宅之间原非路途遥远。可如今，我早晨起来想她不见，便会拄着手杖沿堡镇的街道走去；因为我心中会想：这女郎是去看望我的朋友铁面了；她在面神之宅中安好。可随即便会想起，那漫漫林莽与荒原隔在你我之间。长老，你以为如何？」

===Original===
“A sore lack it will be,” said Iron-face; “but all good go with her! Though whiles shall I go hatless down Burgstead street, and say, Now will I go fetch my daughter the Bride from the House of the Steer; while many a day’s journey shall lie betwixt us.”

Said Hall-ward: “I will not beat about the bush, Folk-might; what gift wilt thou give us for the maiden?”

Said Folk-might: “Whatever is mine shall be thine; and whatsoever of the Dale the kindred and the poor folk begrudge thee not, that shalt thou have; and deemest thou that they will begrudge thee aught? Is it enough?”

===Chinese===
铁面道：「确实是深以为缺；可一切福祉都随她去吧！虽说我日后也会不戴帽子便走下堡镇的街道，口中念着：我如今要去牛族之宅接我女儿新娘回来了——殊不知你我之间已隔着多少日的路程。」

厅卫道：「民强，我不兜圈子了：你愿拿什么礼物来换这女子？」

民强道：「凡我所有，皆归于你；凡堡谷之中宗族与贫苦之人不吝于给你的，你皆可取；你以为他们会吝惜什么么？这够不够？」

===Original===
Hall-ward said: “I wot not, chieftain; see thou to it! Bow-may, my friend, bring hither that which I would have from Silverdale for the House of the Steer in payment for our maiden.”

Then Bow-may came forward speedily, and went up to the Sun-beam, and led her by the hand in front of Folk-might and Hall-ward and the other chieftains. Then Folk-might started, and leapt up from the ground; for, sooth to say, he had been thinking so wholly of the Bride, that his sister was not in his mind, and he had had no deeming of whither Hall-ward was coming, though the others guessed well enough, and now smiled on him merrily, when they saw how wild Folk-might stared. As for the Sun-beam, she stood there blushing like a rose in June, but looking her brother straight in the face, as Hall-ward said:

“Folk-might, chief of the Wolf, since thou wouldst take our maiden the Bride away from us, I ask thee to make good her place with this maiden; so that the House of the Steer may not lack, when they who are wont to wed therein come to us and pray us for a bedfellow for the best of their kindred.”

===Chinese===
厅卫道：「我不晓得，首领；你自己瞧着办吧！我的朋友弓娥，去把我要从银谷带走、用以偿付我们这女子的东西，带到此处来。」

弓娥随即快步上前，走到日光身旁，牵起她的手，将她领到民强、厅卫及诸位首领面前。民强一惊，从地上跃起；说实话，他方才满心想的都是新娘，全然未将其妹放在心上，全不曾料到厅卫意欲何为——旁人却早已猜到了，此刻见他瞠目结舌的模样，皆开怀欢笑。至于日光，立在那里，脸红得如同六月的玫瑰，却直直望着哥哥的脸；只听厅卫说道：

「民强，狼族的首领，你既要将我们的新娘带走，我便要你以此女子来填补她的位子；好叫牛族之宅不至于有所短缺——日后族中惯来通婚之人前来恳求我们、为他们最出色的子弟求一位良配时，不至于落空。」

===Original===
Then became Folk-might smiling and merry like unto the others, and he said: “Chief of the Steer, this gift is thine, together with aught else which thou mayst desire of us.”

Then he kissed the Sun-beam, and said: “Sister, we looked for this to befall in some fashion. Yet we deemed that he that should lead thee away might abide with us for a moon or two. But now let all this be, since if thou art not to bear children to the kindreds of Silverdale, yet shalt thou bear them to their friends and fellows. And now choose what gift thou wilt have of us to keep us in thy memory.”

She said: “The memory of my people shall not fade from me; yet indeed I ask thee for a gift, to wit, Bow-may, and the two sons of Wood-father that are left since Wood-wicked was slain; and belike the elder and his wife will be fain to go with their sons, and ye will not hinder them.”

===Chinese===
民强随即也如旁人一般含笑开怀，说道：「牛族首领，此女是你的了，此外凡你愿向我们索取的，一并随你。」

他随即吻了日光，说道：「妹妹，我们早料到此事终会以某种方式发生。只是原以为那个带你走的人会在我们这里住上一两个月。罢了，不提这些——你虽不再为银谷的宗族生儿育女，却仍要为他们的朋友和同伴传宗接代。如今你且挑一件愿意从我们这里带走的礼物，好时时记着我们。」

她道：「我族之人，我永不会忘；然而我确实要向你讨一件礼物，那就是弓娥，以及自林邪（Wood-wicked）被杀之后林父所余的两个儿子；多半林父老两口也乐意随儿子同去，你们不会拦阻他们吧？」

===Original===
“Even so shall it be done,” said Folk-might, and he was silent a while, pondering; and then he said:

“Lo you, friends! doth it not seem strange to you that peace sundereth as well as war? Indeed I deem it grievous that ye shall have to miss your well-beloved kinswoman. And for me, I am now grown so used to this woman my sister, though at whiles she hath been masterful with me, that I shall often turn about and think to speak to her, when there lie long days of wood and waste betwixt her voice and mine.”

The Sun-beam laughed in his face, though the tears stood in her eyes, as she said: “Keep up thine heart, brother; for at least the way is shorter betwixt Burgdale and Silverdale than betwixt life and death; and the road we shall learn belike.”

===Chinese===
「就照你说的办。」民强道。他默然思忖了一阵，又说道：

「诸位朋友，你们瞧！和平竟也同战争一样能将人分开，这岂不奇怪么？你们将不得不思念你们深爱的同宗女子，我确实为此痛心。至于我，我如今已这般习惯了我这个妹妹——虽说她有时对我颇为霸道——日后我常常会转过身来想要同她说话，殊不知那漫漫林莽与荒原，已隔在她我的声音之间。」

日光当面笑了起来，虽则眼中噙着泪，说道：「哥哥，打起精神来；至少堡谷与银谷之间的路途，比生与死之间的路途要短些；这条路，我们总归会摸熟的。」

===Original===
Said Hall-face: “So it is that my brother is no ill woodman, as ye learned last autumn.”

Iron-face smiled, but somewhat sadly; for he beheld Face-of-god, who had no eyes for anyone save the Sun-beam; and no marvel was that, for never had she looked fairer. And forsooth the War-leader was not utterly well-pleased; for he was deeming that there would be delaying of his wedding, now that the Sun-beam was to become a maid of the Steer; and in his mind he half deemed that it would be better if he were to take her by the hand and lead her home through the wildwood, he and she alone; and she looked on him shyly, as though she had a deeming of his thought. Albeit he knew it might not be, that he, the chosen War-leader, should trouble the peace of the kindred; for he wotted that all this was done for peace’ sake.

So Hall-ward stood forth and took the Sun-beam’s right hand in his, and said:

“Now do I take this maiden, Sun-beam of the kindred of the Wolf, and lead her into the House of the Steer, to be in all ways one of the maidens of our House, and to wed in the blood wherein we have been wont to wed. Neither from henceforth let anyone say that this woman is not of the blood of the Steer; for we have given her our blood, and she is of us duly and truly.”

===Chinese===
厅面道：「我那位兄弟倒并非不通林路之人——这一点诸位去年秋天是领教过的。」

铁面微微一笑，却略带伤色；因他瞧着面神——面神此刻眼中再无旁人，唯有日光；这也不足为奇，因她从未如此美丽。说实话，这位战首心中并非全然畅快；因他想，日光既要去牛族做一介女郎，自己的婚事只怕又要延宕了；他心中暗自半想，若是他牵起她的手、带她穿过野林回家去，只有他与她二人，那该多好；而她羞怯地望着他，似乎猜到了他的心思。然而他深知这不可能——他身为众人推举的战首，岂能为了一己之私扰乱宗族的和局；因他明白这一切皆是为和平而为之。

于是厅卫走上前来，握住日光的右手，说道：

「我今日收下这女子——狼族宗族的日光——带她进入牛族之宅，从此在各方面做我族中一名女郎，并在我等惯于通婚的血胤之中婚配。自今以后，谁也不得说此女不是牛族的血脉；因我们已将我们的血脉给了她，她千真万确是我们中人。」

===Original===
Thereafter they talked together merrily for a little, and then turned toward the houses, for the sun was now down; and as they went Iron-face spake to his son, and said:

“Gold-mane, wilt thou verily keep thine oath to wed the fairest woman in the world? By how much is this one fairer than my dear daughter who shall no more dwell in mine house?”

Said Face-of-god: “Yea, father, I shall keep mine oath; for the Gods, who know much, know that when I swore last Yule I was thinking of the fair woman going yonder beside Hall-ward, and of none other.”

===Chinese===
此后众人又欢谈了一阵，便转身向那些屋宇走去，此时日已落山；行走之间，铁面对其子说道：

「金鬃，你当真要守住你的誓言、娶那世上最美的女子么？这一位比我那再不得住在自家的爱女，又美上多少呢？」

面神道：「是的，父亲，我定要守住我的誓言；因无所不知的众神晓得，去年冬至节我起誓之时，心中所想正是那个此刻走在那边厅卫身旁的美丽女子，再无别人。」

===Original===
“Ah, son!” said Iron-face, “why didst thou beguile us? Hadst thou but told us the truth then!”

Said Face-of-god smiling, “Yea, Alderman, and how thou wouldest have raged against me then, when thou hast scarce forgiven me now! In sooth, father, I feared to tell you all: I was young; I was one against the world. Yea, yea; and even that was sweet to me, so sorely as I loved her﻿—Hast thou forgotten, father?”

Iron-face smiled, and answered not; and so came they to the house wherein they were guested.

===Chinese===
「唉，儿啊！」铁面道，「你当初为何要瞒我们？你那时若说了实话该多好！」

面神微笑道：「是啊，长老，你那时若知道，该会怎样对我大发雷霆啊——你如今尚且勉强才肯原谅我呢！说实话，父亲，那时我不敢把一切都告诉你们：我年轻；我孤身一人对抗整个世界。是啊，是啊；可即便是那份孤苦，于我亦是甜的，只因我爱她爱得那般深——父亲，你莫非忘了？」

铁面微微一笑，不再作答；众人便这样走到了他们作客的那座屋中。

## XII Stone-Face Telleth Concerning the Wood-Wights / 十二 石面述林精之事

===Original===
Early on the morrow Gold-mane arose and clad himself and went out-a-doors and over the trodden snow on to the bridge over the Weltering Water, and there betook himself into one of the coins of safety built over the upstream piles; there he leaned against the wall and turned his face to the Thorp, and fell to pondering on his case. And first he thought about his oath, and how that he had sworn to wed the Mountain Woman, although his kindred and her kindred should gainsay him, yea and herself also. Great seemed that oath to him, yet at that moment he wished he had made it greater, and made all the kindred, yea and the Bride herself, sure of the meaning of the words of it: and he deemed himself a dastard that he had not done so. Then he looked round him and beheld the winter, and he fell into mere longing that the spring were come and the token from the Mountain. Things seemed too hard for him to deal with, and he between a mighty folk and two wayward women; and he went nigh to wish that he had taken his father’s offer and gone down to the Cities; and even had he met his bane: well were that! And, as young folk will, he set to work making a picture of his deeds there, had he been there. He showed himself the stricken fight in the plain, and the press, and the struggle, and the breaking of the serried band, and himself amidst the ring of foemen doing most valiantly, and falling there at last, his shield o’er-heavy with the weight of foemen’s spears for a man to uphold it. Then the victory of his folk and the lamentation and praise over the slain man of the Mountain Dales, and the burial of the valiant warrior, the praising weeping folk meeting him at the City-gate, laid stark and cold in his arms on the gold-hung garlanded bier.

===Chinese===
次日清晨，金鬃（Gold-mane）起身披衣，出门踏过踩实之积雪，行至翻滚河（the Weltering Water）之桥上，闪入一处建于上游桥桩上方之避险龛中；他倚墙而立，面朝屯子，开始思忖自身之事。他先想到自己所立之誓——他曾立誓要娶那山女（the Mountain Woman），纵然自己亲族与她的亲族都来反对，甚至她自己亦反对。此誓在他看来已是极其重大，然此刻他却恨未能立得更加重大，恨未能使所有亲族、乃至新娘（the Bride）本人，都确确明了其中之言意：他深以自己未曾如此为怯懦。继而环顾四周，凝望这隆冬之景，他不由得一味盼望春日早至、山中之信物早至。诸事于他似乎太难应对——他夹在一个强盛之族与两个任性之女之间；他几乎要后悔未曾依父亲之议下山去诸城（the Cities）；纵然在彼处遭了死劫：那也很好！于是，如少年人常做的那样，他开始描绘起自己倘若真去了彼处、当有的种种功业。他眼前浮起平原之上那一场血战，那混战、那厮搏、那密集阵线之崩溃，而他自己置身于仇敌之围中奋战至极，终竟力竭倒地，盾上所中敌矛之重，已非人力所能支。继而，族人凯旋，对那位来自山地诸谷（the Mountain Dales）的阵亡者哀悼颂扬，那英勇武士之葬礼，哭泣颂赞之众人迎至城门（the City-gate）之前——他僵冷地躺于自己臂中，卧于悬金缀花环之灵柩之上。

===Original===
There ended his dream, and he laughed aloud and said: “I am a fool! All this were good and sweet if I should see it myself; and forsooth that is how I am thinking of it, as if I still alive should see myself dead and famous!”

Then he turned a little and looked at the houses of the Thorp lying dark about the snowy ways under the starlit heavens of the winter morning: dark they were indeed and grey, save where here and there the half-burned Yule-fire reddened the windows of a hall, or where, as in one place, the candle of some early waker shone white in a chamber window. There was scarce a man astir, he deemed, and no sound reached him save the crowing of the cocks muffled by their houses, and a faint sound of beasts in the byres.

===Chinese===
幻梦至此而止，他朗声大笑，说道：“我真是个痴人！这一切，若我能亲眼目睹，自然又美又甜；殊不知我心里正是这般在想——仿佛我自己尚活着，却要来看自己死后成名的那般光景！”

他随即略略转身，望向屯中屋舍：在冬日清晨那满天星斗之下，屋舍黑黝黝地散落于雪径之旁。其色诚然乌暗灰沉，唯此处彼处，半烬的岁末冬至节（Yuletide）炉火将某座厅堂之窗映得微红；又或如某处那般，某个早醒之人所燃之烛，在卧室窗内泛出一点白光。他心想，此时怕是少有人起；耳中所闻，唯有被鸡舍所蒙闷的鸡啼，以及厩中牲畜微微之声。

===Original===
Thus he stood a while, his thoughts wandering now, till presently he heard footsteps coming his way down the street and turned toward them, and lo it was the old man Stone-face. He had seen Gold-mane go out, and had risen and followed him that he might talk with him apart. Gold-mane greeted him kindly, though, sooth to say, he was but half content to see him; since he doubted, what was verily the case, that his foster-father would give him many words, counselling him to refrain from going to the wood, and this was loathsome to him; but he spake and said:

“Meseems, father, that the eastern sky is brightening toward dawn.”

“Yea,” quoth Stone-face.

“It will be light in an hour,” said Face-of-god.

“Even so,” said Stone-face.

“And a fair day for the morrow of Yule,” said the swain.

“Yea,” said Stone-face, “and what wilt thou do with the fair day? Wilt thou to the wood?”

“Maybe, father,” said Gold-mane; “Hall-face and some of the swains are talking of elks up the fells which may be trapped in the drifts, and if they go a-hunting them, I may go in their company.”

===Chinese===
他这般立了一会儿，心思已渐渐游离，忽听得一阵脚步声沿街而来，他转身相迎，来者竟是老者石面（Stone-face）。石面见金鬃出门，便也起身随后，欲与他说几句私语。金鬃亲切地与他见礼，然实话实说，见他来心中并不甚痛快；因为他猜疑——而且所猜亦确——义父必会絮絮叨叨，劝他切勿入林，此话于他甚是逆耳；然他仍开口道：

“父亲，我看东边天色，似已向晓。”

“正是。”石面道。

“再过一个时辰便要天亮了。”面神（Face-of-god）道。

“诚然如此。”石面道。

“冬至次日，当是个好天。”那少年道。

“是啊，”石面道，“这么好的天，你有何打算？可要入林去？”

“或许罢，父亲，”金鬃道，“厅面（Hall-face）和几个少年正说山上雪堆里困住了几头麋鹿，倘若他们入山猎鹿，我或可与之同行。”

===Original===
“Ah, son,” quoth Stone-face, “thou wilt look to see other kind of beasts than elks. Things may ye fall in with there who may not be impounded in the snow like to elks, but can go light-foot on the top of the soft drift from one place to another.”

Said Gold-mane: “Father, fear me not; I shall either refrain me from the wood, or if I go, I shall go to hunt the wood-deer with other hunters. But since thou hast come to me, tell me more about the wood, for thy tales thereof are fair.”

===Chinese===
“唉，儿啊，”石面道，“你将看到的，怕不只是麋鹿之类的兽。林中或有那种生灵，并不像麋鹿一般被困雪中，却能以轻足踏在软雪堆之巅，自一处飘忽至另一处。”

金鬃道：“父亲，勿为我忧；我要么自禁不入林，要么即便入林，也只与其他猎户一同猎那林鹿。但你既已来此，便再多与我讲讲那林中之事罢，你那些故事着实动人。”

===Original===
“Yea,” said Stone-face, “fair tales of foul things, as oft it befalleth in the world. Hearken now! if thou deemest that what thou seekest shall come readier to thine hand because of the winter and the snow, thou errest. For the wights that waylay the bodies and souls of the mighty in the wildwood heed such matters nothing; yea and at Yuletide are they most abroad, and most armed for the fray. Even such an one have I seen time agone, when the snow was deep and the wind was rough; and it was in the likeness of a woman clad in such raiment as the Bride bore last night, and she trod the snow light-foot in thin raiment where it would scarce bear the skids of a deft snow-runner. Even so she stood before me; the icy wind blew her raiment round about her, and drifted the hair from her garlanded head toward me, and she as fair and fresh as in the midsummer days. Up the fell she fared, sweetest of all things to look on, and beckoned on me to follow; on me, the Warrior, the Stout-heart; and I followed, and between us grief was born; but I it was that fostered that child and not she. Always when she would be, was she merry and lovely; and even so is she now, for she is of those that be long-lived. And I wot that thou hast seen even such an one!”

“Tell me more of thy tales, foster-father,” said Gold-mane, “and fear not for me!”

===Chinese===
“是啊，”石面道，“美哉斯言，所述却乃是恶物——世间之事，往往如此。你且听好！你若以为因时值隆冬、大雪封山，你所求之物便会更易到手，那你便错了。盖因那些在莽林之中、专伺天下豪杰之身与魂的精怪，并不把这些放在心上；不仅如此，每逢岁末冬至节，它们反而最为出没，最为严阵以待。昔年大雪方深、寒风正烈之时，我亦曾亲眼见过这样一个：她作女子之形，衣裳恰如新娘昨夜所穿；她衣衫单薄，却以轻足踏雪，行于连善行雪之能人的雪板都几乎承不住的软雪之上。她便那样立于我前；寒风将她衣袂吹得团团旋转，自她戴花环的首上，将发丝朝着我的方向飘送；她容颜之美、气色之鲜，恰如仲夏之日。她向山上行去，乃天地之间至美之物，招手令我相随；令的乃是我——武士、壮心；我便随了，于是乎悲伤在我们之间诞生；然而抚育此子的，乃是我，并不是她。她想欢愉之时，无不娇美可爱；时至今日依然如此，盖因其乃长生之属。我知你所见者，亦是这般一个！”

“义父，再讲几个你的故事罢，”金鬃道，“不必为我担忧！”

===Original===
“Ah, son,” he said, “mayst thou have no such tales to tell to those that shall be young when thou art old. Yet hearken! We sat in the hall together and there was no third; and methought that the birds sang and the flowers bloomed, and sweet was their savour, though it was midwinter. A rose-wreath was on her head; grapes were on the board, and fair unwrinkled summer apples on the day that we feasted together. When was the feast? sayst thou. Long ago. What was the hall, thou sayest, wherein ye feasted? I know not if it were on the earth or under it, or if we rode the clouds that even. But on the morrow what was there but the stark wood and the drift of the snow, and the iron wind howling through the branches, and a lonely man, a wanderer rising from the ground. A wanderer through the wood and up the fell, and up the high mountain, and up and up to the edges of the ice-river and the green caves of the ice-hills. A wanderer in spring, in summer, autumn and winter, with an empty heart and a burning never-satisfied desire; who hath seen in the uncouth places many an evil unmanly shape, many a foul hag and changing ugly semblance; who hath suffered hunger and thirst and wounding and fever, and hath seen many things, but hath never again seen that fair woman, or that lovely feast-hall.

“All praise and honour to the House of the Face, and the bounteous valiant men thereof! and the like praise and honour to the fair women whom they wed of the valiant and goodly House of the Steer!”

===Chinese===
“唉，儿啊，”他说，“愿到你年迈之时，对那些那时正当年轻之人，你并无此类故事可讲。然你且听好！我们曾同坐于一座厅堂之内，并无第三人；我恍惚闻得鸟啼鸣、花盛开，其味馨香，虽其时乃是仲冬。她首戴玫瑰花环，案上陈着葡萄，还有光洁无皱的夏日苹果——那是我们一同设宴之日。你问那是何时？我说：很久以前。你又问，那设宴之厅堂是何处？我不知其究竟在地上、还是在地下，抑或我们那夜是骑在云上。然到了次日，眼前还剩下什么呢？不过荒寒之林、堆积之雪、铁一般的寒风穿啸于枝柯之间，以及一个孤独之人，一个自地上爬起来的流浪者。这流浪者穿过林莽、攀上那荒山、再攀上那高山，再往上、再往上，直攀到冰河之涯、冰山的翠洞之前。这流浪者，春也如是，夏也如是，秋也如是，冬也如是，怀着一颗空空之心，一团永难餍足的欲火；他在幽僻不毛之地，曾见无数邪恶非人之形、无数丑陋妖妪与变幻之恶相；他曾历饥渴、创伤、寒热，曾见过诸多事物，却再未曾见过那美貌之女，亦未曾再见那可爱之宴厅。

“愿一切赞颂与荣耀归于面神之宅（the House of the Face），归于其中慷慨英勇的男儿！亦愿同样的赞颂与荣耀归于他们所婚娶的、那英勇美好的牡牛之族（the House of the Steer）中的美貌女子！”

===Original===
“Even so say I,” quoth Gold-mane calmly; “but now wend we aback to the House, for it is morning indeed, and folk will be stirring there.”

So they turned from the bridge together; and Stone-face was kind and fatherly, and was telling his foster-son many wise things concerning the life of a chieftain, and the giving-out of dooms and the gathering for battle; to all which talk Face-of-god seemed to hearken gladly, but indeed hearkened not at all; for verily his eyes were beholding that snowy waste, and the fair woman upon it; even such an one as Stone-face had told of.

===Chinese===
“我亦如是说，”金鬃从容道，“但我们这便回宅中去罢，毕竟天已大亮，宅里的人都要起身了。”

二人便一同离了桥；石面慈和关切，犹如慈父，一路上对义子讲了许多智者之言，论及首领之生涯、判决之颁下、征伐之点兵；对这一切话语，面神似乎欣然倾听，实则一句也未入耳；因为他的双目所凝望的，实是那一片雪荒之野，以及立于其上的那美貌之女——恰如石面所讲述的那一种。

## XXIII Talk in the Hall of the House of the Face / 廿三 面神之宅厅中之言

===Original===
In sooth they were come to the very Gate of Burgstead, and the great gates were shut, and only a wicket was open, and a half score of stout men in all their war-gear were holding ward thereby. They gave place to Hall-face and his company, albeit some of the warders followed them through the wicket that they might hear the story told.

The street was full of folk, both men and women, talking together eagerly concerning all these tidings, and when they saw the men of the Hue-and-cry they came thronging about them, so that they might scarce get to the door of the House of the Face because of the press; so Hall-face (who was a very tall man) cried out:

===Chinese===
诚然，他们已径直来到堡镇城门之前。大门紧闭，唯余一道边门洞开，十名全副戎装的壮汉在彼处把守。守卫们让路给厅面及其一行，虽有数名守卫亦随其穿过边门，欲听事情原委。

街上人头攒动，男女皆有，正热烈议论此番种种消息。众人一见追缉队中人，便蜂拥围拢上来，挤挤挨挨，几乎到不了面神之宅门前；于是厅面（其人甚是高大）高声喊道：

===Original===
“Good people, all is well! the runaways are slain, and Face-of-god is come back with us; give place a little, that we may come into our house.”

Then the throng set up a shout, and made way a little, so that Hall-face and Gold-mane and the others could get to the door. And they entered into the Hall, and saw much folk therein; and men were sitting at table, for supper was not yet over. But when they saw the newcomers they mostly rose up from the board and stood silent to hear the tale, for they had been talking many together each to each, so that the Hall was full of confused noise.

===Chinese===
“各位乡亲，一切无恙！逃犯已诛，面神亦随我们同归；且让一让，好教我们进自家门去。”

众人闻言齐声欢呼，让开些许，于是厅面、金鬃及其余众人方能挤到门前。他们步入大厅，见其中人众甚多；众人正坐于桌旁，因晚饭尚未用毕。然一见这些新来之人，大多离席起身，默然而立，欲听事情原委——盖因方才他们三五成群、彼此议论，厅中一片嘈杂喧哗。

===Original===
So Hall-face again cried out: “Men in this hall, good is the tidings. The runaways are slain; and it was Face-of-god who slew them as he came back safe from the waste.”

Then they shouted for joy, and the brethren and Stone-face with them (for he had entered with them from the street) went up on to the dais, while the others of the Hue-and-cry gat them seats where they might at the endlong tables.

===Chinese===
于是厅面又高声道：“厅中诸位，喜讯到了。逃犯已诛；乃是面神自荒野安然归来途中亲手诛之。”

众人闻之欢声雷动。兄弟二人与石面（他亦随众人自街上入内）一同登上高座，追缉队其余之人则在长桌旁各自觅座坐下。

===Original===
But when Face-of-god came up on to the dais, there sat Iron-face looking down on the thronged Hall with a ruddy cheerful countenance, and beside him sat the Bride; for he had caused her to be brought thither when he had heard of the tidings of battle. She was daintily clad in a flame-coloured kirtle embroidered with gold about the bosom and sleeves, and there was a fillet of golden roses on her ruddy hair. Her eyes shone bright and eager, and the pommels of her cheeks were flushed and red contrary to their wont. Needs must Gold-mane sit by her, and when he came close to her he knew not what to do, but he put forth his hand to her, yet with a troubled countenance; for he feared her grief mingled with her beauty: as for her, she wavered in her mind whether she should forbear to touch him or not; but she saw that men about were looking at them, and especially was Iron-face looking on her: therefore she stood up and took Gold-mane’s hand and kissed his face as she had been wont to do, and by then was her face as white as paper; and her anguish pierced his heart, so that he well-nigh groaned for grief of her. But Iron-face looked on her and said kindly:

===Chinese===
及至面神登上高座，只见铁面端坐其上，面色红润欢悦，俯瞰满厅拥挤之人；新娘就坐在他身旁——原来他闻听战讯之后，便已着人将她请至此处。她身着火红罗裙，胸前袖口皆以金线绣纹，一头红发之上戴一道金玫瑰花环。她双目明亮而热切，双颊圆处泛起红晕，反乎素日常态。金鬃不得不坐在她身旁，及至挨近，竟不知如何是好，仍向她伸出手去，面色却颇为不安；盖因他惧怕她那与美貌交织的悲苦：至于她，心里犹豫不定，不知该不该伸手碰他；然她见周围之人都看着他们，尤其铁面正注目于她：于是她站起身来，握住金鬃之手，吻了他的脸——一如往日惯常所为；到此时她的脸已白如素纸；她那痛苦直刺他心，使他几乎要为她痛楚出声。铁面看着她，和颜悦色地说道：

===Original===
“Kinswoman, thou art pale; thou hast feared for thy mate amidst all these tidings of war, and still fearest for him. But pluck up a heart; for the man is a deft warrior for all his fair face, which thou lovest as a woman should, and his hands may yet save his head. And if he be slain, yet are there other men of the kindred, and the earth will not be a desert to thee even then.”

She looked at Iron-face, and the colour was come back to her face somewhat, and she said:
“It is true; I have feared for him; for he goeth into perilous places. But for thee, thou art kind, and I thank thee for it.”

And therewith she kissed Iron-face and sat down in her place, and strove to overmaster her grief, that her face might not be changed by it; for now were thoughts of battle, and valiant hopes arising in men’s hearts; and it seemed to her too grievous if she should mar that feast on the eve of battle.

===Chinese===
“孩子，你面色苍白；在这战讯纷传之中，你为你的良人忧惧，至今仍为他担忧。但且振作精神；这男子虽生得一副俊俏面孔——那面孔你爱之，正合女子本分——却是一员善战之将，他那双手或还能保住项上人头。纵然他阵亡了，宗族之中尚有其他男儿，即使到那时，这世间于你也不至成为一片荒漠。”

她望着铁面，脸上略恢复了几分血色，说道：
“是真的；我一直为他忧惧；因为他总是深入险地。至于你，你这般慈爱，我深为感激。”

说罢，她吻了铁面，坐回自己位上，竭力压制悲伤，不教它形之于色；因为此时众人心中正涌起征战之念与豪壮之志；她觉得，若因自己败坏了这战前之夜的宴饮，未免太过不该。

===Original===
But Iron-face kissed and embraced his son and said: “Art thou late come from the waste? Hast thou seen new things? We look to have a notable tale from thee; though here also have been tidings, and it is not unlike that we shall presently have new work on our hands.”

“Father,” quoth Face-of-god, “I deem that when thou hast heard my tale thou wilt think no less of it than that there are valiant folk to be holpen, poor folk to be delivered, and evil folk to be swept from off the face of the earth.”

“It is well, son,” said Iron-face. “I see that thy tale is long; let it alone for tonight. Tomorrow shall we hold a Gate-thing, and then shall we hear all that thou hast to tell. Now eat thy meat and drink a bowl of wine, and comfort thy troth-plight maiden.”

===Chinese===
铁面遂吻抱其子，说道：“你从荒野迟归？可曾见了什么新异之事？我们正指望听你讲一段了不得的故事；不过此地也有了消息，只怕我们眼下就要有新的差事上手了。”

“父亲，”面神道，“我料想，待你听完我的故事，便知其要紧不亚于此：有豪勇之民当助，有困苦之民当救，有邪恶之民当从这世间扫除净尽。”

“很好，儿啊，”铁面道，“我看你这故事短不了；今夜且先搁下。明日我们召开城门议事（Gate-thing），到时再细听你所要讲的一切。现在且吃你的饭，喝一碗酒，宽慰宽慰你那订了亲的未婚妻吧。”

===Original===
So Gold-mane sat down by the Bride, and ate and drank as he needs must; but he was ill at ease and he durst not speak to her. For, on the one hand, he thought concerning his love for the Sun-beam, and how sweet and good a thing it was that she should take him by the hand and lead him into noble deeds and great fame, caressing him so softly and sweetly the while; and, on the other hand, there sat the Bride beside him, sorrowful and angry, begrudging all that sweetness of love, as though it were something foul and unseemly; and heavy on him lay the weight of that grudge, for he was a man of a friendly heart.

===Chinese===
于是金鬃在新娘身旁坐下，不得不勉强吃喝；然而他心神不宁，竟不敢与她说话。因为，一方面，他心里想着自己对日光的爱慕，想着那是何等甜美而美好的事——她要执他之手，引他走向壮烈功业与盛大荣名，一面又那般温柔甘美地抚慰他；而另一方面，新娘就坐在他身旁，悲苦而恼怒，仿佛那一切爱的甘美都是某种污秽不堪之事，满怀嫉恨；那份怨恨沉沉地压在他心头，因为他本是个心地友善之人。

===Original===
Stone-face sat outward from him on the other side of the Bride; and he leaned across her towards Gold-mane and said:
“Fair shall be thy tale tomorrow, if thou tellest us all thine adventure. Or wilt thou tell us less than all?”
Said Face-of-god: “In good time shalt thou know it all, foster-father; but it is not unlike that by the time that thou hast heard it, there shall be so many other things to tell of, that my tale shall seem of little account to thee—even as the saw saith that one nail driveth out the other.”
“Yea,” said Stone-face, “but one tale belike shall be knit up with the others, as it fareth with the figures that come one after other on the weaver’s cloth; though one maketh not the other, yet one cometh of the other.”
Said Face-of-god: “Wise art thou now, foster-father, but thou shalt be wiser yet in this matter by then a month hath worn: and tomorrow shalt thou know enough to set thine hands a-work.”

===Chinese===
石面坐在他外侧、新娘的另一边；他隔着新娘倾身向金鬃，说道：
“明日你的故事定然精彩，若你把全部经历都讲与我们听的话。还是说，你打算有所保留、不全讲出来？”
面神道：“义父，到时你自然会全都知道；但只怕待你听完之后，又会有许多别的事可讲，以致我的故事在你看来无足轻重——正所谓一钉挤出一钉。”
“不错，”石面道，“但一个故事多半与其余的交织相扣，恰如织工布上一幅接一幅现出的花样——虽则这一幅并不造就那一幅，然这一幅却由那一幅而生。”
面神道：“义父，你如今已甚明智，但待过完一个月，你在此事上将更见明智：到明日，你所知便足以使你着手行事了。”

===Original===
So the talk fell between them; and the night wore, and the men of Burgdale feasted in their ancient hall with merry hearts, little weighed down by thought of the battle that might be and the trouble to come; for they were valorous and kindly folk.

===Chinese===
话头便就此落下；夜渐深，堡谷之民在他们古老的厅堂中设宴痛饮，心怀欢快，对于将来或有之战事及将至之忧患，几不以为意；因为他们本是一族勇武宽厚之人。

## LVI Talk Upon the Wildwood Way / 五十六 野林途中之谈

===Original===
On the morrow morning when they were on their way again Face-of-god left his own folk to go with the House of the Steer a while; and amongst them he fell in with the Sun-beam going along with Bow-may. So they greeted him kindly, and Face-of-god fell into talk with the Sun-beam as they went side by side through a great oak-wood, where for a space was plain greensward bare of all underwood.

===Chinese===
次日清晨，众人重新上路，面神暂别自家族人，去陪壮牛之族（the House of the Steer）走一段路；其间正遇见日光与弓女（Bow-may）结伴同行。二人殷勤见礼，面神便与日光并肩而行，一路攀谈。其时他们正穿过一片广阔的橡林，林间有一段平铺的绿草地，寸木不生。

===Original===
So in their talk he said to her: “What deemest thou, my speech-friend, concerning our coming back to guest in Silverdale one day?”

“The way is long,” she said.

“That may hinder us but not stay us,” said Face-of-god.

“That is sooth,” said the Sun-beam.

Said Face-of-god: “What things shall stay us? Or deemest thou that we shall never see Silverdale again?”

She smiled: “Even so I think thou deemest, Gold-mane. But many things shall hinder us besides the long road.”

Said he: “Yea, and what things?”

===Chinese===
谈话之间，他对她说道："我的言谈之友，关于我们日后重来银谷作客一事，你怎么看？"

她道："路途遥远啊。"

面神道："那或可阻我们一时，却挡不住我们。"

日光道："诚然如是。"

面神道："那又有什么能挡得住我们？莫非你以为我们再也见不到银谷了？"

她微微一笑："金鬃，我想你心中也作如是想。只是除却漫长的路途之外，还有许多事会阻我们一时。"

他道："是啊，还有什么事？"

===Original===
“Thinkest thou,” said the Sun-beam, “that the winning of Silverstead is the last battle which thou shalt see?”

“Nay,” said he, “nay.”

“Shall thy Dale—our Dale—be free from all trouble within itself henceforward? Is there a wall built round it to keep out forever storm, pestilence, and famine, and the waywardness of its own folk?”

“So it is as thou sayest,” quoth Face-of-god, “and to meet such troubles and overcome them, or to die in strife with them, this is a great part of a man’s life.”

“Yea,” she said, “and hast thou forgotten that thou art now a great chieftain, and that the folk shall look to thee to use thee many days in the year?”

He laughed and said: “So it is. How many days have gone by since I wandered in the wood last autumn, that the world should have changed so much!”

“Many deeds shall now be in thy days,” she said, “and each deed as the corn of wheat from which cometh many corns; and a man’s days on the earth are not over many.”

“Then farewell, Silverdale!” said he, waving his hand toward the north. “War and trouble may bring me back to thee, but it maybe nought else shall. Farewell!”

===Chinese===
日光道："你以为攻下银镇（Silverstead），便是你此生所见的最后一战么？"

他道："非也，非也。"

"你那个谷——我们那个谷——从此便能在内里一切太平了么？莫非有一道墙将它团团围住，能永远挡住风雨、瘟疫、饥荒，以及它自家子民的乖张妄作？"

面神道："你说的正是。迎击此等祸患而加以克服，又或与之搏斗而死——这便是人一生的一大部分。"

她道："是啊，再者，你可曾忘了你如今已是一员大首领，一年之中许多日子族人都须仰你出来任事？"

他笑道："正是如此。自去秋我在林中流浪至今，才过了多少日子，天下竟已变了这么多！"

她道："你今后的日子里要做的事正多，每一件事都如同麦粒，能结出许多子粒来；而人在世上的日子，本就无多。"

他向北挥了挥手，道："那么，银谷，别了！战祸与患难或许还能将我带回你这里，但此外或许再没别的事能够了。别了！"

===Original===
She looked on him fondly but unsmiling, as he went beside her strong and warrior-like. Three paces from him went Bow-may, barefoot, in her white kirtle, but bearing her bow in her hand; a leash of arrows was in her girdle, her quiver hung at her back, and she was girt with a sword. On the other side went Wood-wont and Wood-wise, lightly clad but weaponed. Wood-mother was riding in an ox-wain just behind them, and Wood-father went beside her bearing an axe. Scattered all about them were the men of the Steer, gaily clad, bearing weapons, so that the oak-wood was bright with them, and the glades merry with their talk and singing and laughter, and before them down the glades went the banner of the Steer, and the White Beast led them the nearest way to Burgdale.

===Chinese===
她含情脉脉地看着他，却不带笑意；他在她身侧大步而行，雄健矫捷，俨然一员武将。距他三步之遥走着弓女，赤着双足，一袭白色长裙，手中却提着弓；腰带上挂着一组箭，背后悬着箭囊，腰间又佩着一口剑。另一边走着林习（Wood-wont）与林智（Wood-wise），衣着轻简，却也带着兵器。林母（Wood-mother）乘坐于紧随其后的一辆牛车之上，林父（Wood-father）手执一斧，走在她身侧。壮牛之族的汉子三三两两散在他们四周，衣饰鲜丽，个个携着兵器；那片橡林因他们而光华焕发，林间空地因他们的谈话、歌唱与欢笑而喧阗热闹；在他们之前，沿着林间空地一路向前的，是壮牛之族的大旗；那白兽（the White Beast）则引他们抄最近的路，往堡谷而去。

## XXXIII The Alderman Gives Gifts to Them of Shadowy Vale / 三十三 长老赐礼于幽谷之人

===Original===
In the Hall of the Face Folk-might sat on the dais at the right hand of the Alderman, and the Sun-beam on his left hand. But Iron-face also had beheld the Bride how her face changed, and he knew the cause, and was grieved and angry and ashamed thereof: also he bethought him how this stranger was sitting in the very place where the Bride used to sit, and of all the love, as of a very daughter, that he had had for her; howbeit he constrained himself to talk courteously and kindly both to Folk-might and the Sun-beam, as behoved the Chief of the House and the Alderman of the Dale. Moreover, he was not a little moved by the goodliness and wisdom of the Sun-beam and the manliness of Folk-might, who was the most chieftain-like of men.

But while they sat there Face-of-god went from man to man of the Guests, and made much of each, but especially of Wood-father and his sons and Bow-may, and they loved him, and praised him, and deemed him the best of hall-mates. Nor might the Sun-beam altogether refrain her from looking lovingly on him, and it could be seen of her that she deemed he was doing well, and like a wise leader and chieftain.

===Chinese===
在面神之厅堂之上，民强坐于高台，居于长老右手，日光则在其左手。然铁面也已察觉新娘面色之变，知其缘故，为此既痛且怒、又复生惭：他又想到这个异乡女子所坐之处，正是新娘往日所坐之地，又想到自己素日待新娘之情，宛若亲生女儿一般；纵然如此，他仍强自克制，对民强与日光皆以礼相待、和颜悦色，这正是身为此宅之长、堡谷长老所当为。再者，日光之端庄明智、民强之丈夫气概（民强乃须眉之中最有大将之风者），亦令他颇为动容。

然当他们坐于此时，面神却自一位客走到另一位客前，一一殷勤款待，尤以林父及其诸子、弓娘为甚；他们皆爱重他、称誉他，视之为厅上之最佳良伴。日光亦不能自已，每每含情凝望于他；众人可见她心中之意：深以他所为为是，视之如明智之领袖、运筹之首领。

===Original===
So wore away awhile, and men were fulfilled of meat and drink; so then the Alderman arose and spake, and said:

"Is it not so, Guests, that ye would now gladly behold our market, and the goodly wares which the chapmen have brought us from the Cities?"

Then most men cried out: "Yea, yea!" and Iron-face said:

"Then shall ye go, nor be holden by me from your pleasure. And ye kinsmen who are the most guest-fain and the wisest, go ye with our friends, and make all things easy and happy for them. But first of all, Guests, I were well pleased if ye would take some small matters out of our abundance; for it were well that ye see them ere ye stand before the chapmen's booths, lest ye chaffer with them for what ye have already."

===Chinese===
如此消磨了一阵，众人都已酒足饭饱；于是长老起身发话道：

「列位贵客，尔等此时想必乐意去看看我们的集市，看看那些行商从诸城邑贩来的佳美货物，是不是？」

众人大叫：「是，是！」铁面便道：

「那么尔等便去吧，我绝不阻拦尔等之乐。尔等宗亲之中最乐于待客、又最明智的，便随我们这些朋友同去，为他们把一切安排得便易妥帖。但首要之事，列位贵客：尔等若肯从我等充盈之物中取些微薄之礼，我便甚为欢喜；因为尔等在行商摊前站定之前先看一看，倒也是好——免得尔等与他们讨价还价，买的却是自家已经有的东西。」

===Original===
They all praised his bounty and thanked him for his goodwill: so he arose to go to his treasury, and bade certain of his folk go along with him to bear in the gifts. But ere he had taken three steps down the hall, Face-of-god prevented him and said:

"Kinsman, if thou hast anywhere a hauberk somewhat better than folk are wont to bear, such as thine own hand fashioneth, and a sword of the like stuff, I would have thee give them, the sword to my brother-in-arms Wood-wise here, and the war-coat to my sister Bow-may, who shooteth so well in the bow that none may shoot closer, and very few as close; and her shaft it was that delivered me when my skull was amongst the axes of the Dusky Men: else had I not been here."

===Chinese===
众人皆称颂他的慷慨，谢他的好意：于是他起身欲往库房去，并吩咐几个从人同去搬取礼物。然他尚未行出三步，面神便赶前一步拦住他道：

「族兄，你若何处有一件比寻常人所穿稍胜之锁子甲——便是你亲手所制那种——再加一柄同样质料之剑，便请你赐下：剑给我这位同袍兄弟林智，战袍则给我妹妹弓娘。她弓射得极准，无人能比她射得更密，能与之并驾者亦寥寥无几；当日我的头颅夹在黝暗人斧刃之间，正是她那一箭救了我的命：若非如此，我今日也不在此了。」

===Original===
Thereat Bow-may reddened and looked down, like a scholar who hath been overpraised for his learning and diligence; but the Alderman smiled on her and said:

"I thank thee, son, that thou hast let me know what these our two friends may be fain of: and as for this damsel-at-arms, it is a little thing that thou askest for her, and we might have found her something more worthy of her goodliness; yet forsooth, since we are all bound for the place where shafts and staves shall be good cheap, a greater treasure might be of less avail to her."

===Chinese===
弓娘闻言双颊泛红，垂下目光，恰似一个学童因勤学而被过度夸奖那般；长老却向她微笑道：

「儿啊，多谢你让我知道这两位朋友所好。至于这位女战士，你所求之物于她不过是小事一桩；我们本可寻一件更配她之佳美的礼物相赠；然说实话，既然大家都要去那箭矢棍杖充盈易得之地，给她一件更大的宝贝，反倒未必有这般合用。」

===Original===
Thereat men laughed, and the Alderman went down the Hall with those bearers of gifts, and was away for a space while they drank and made merry: but presently back they came from the treasury bearing loads of goodly things which were laid on one of the endlong boards. Then began the gift-giving: and first he gave unto Folk-might six golden cups marvellously fashioned, the work of four generations of wrights in the Dale, and he himself had wrought the last two thereof. To Sun-beam he gave a girdle of gold, fashioned with great mastery, whereon were images of the Gods and the Fathers, and warriors, and beasts of the field and fowls of the air; and as he girt it about her loins, he said in a soft voice so that few heard:

"Sun-beam, thou fair woman, time has been when thou wert to us as the edge of the poisonous sword or the midnight torch of the murderer; but now I know not how it will be, or if the grief which thou hast given me will ever wear out or not. And now that I have beheld thee, I have little to do to blame my son; for indeed when I look on thee I cannot deem that there is any evil in thee. Yea, however it may be, take thou this gift as the reward of thine exceeding beauty."

===Chinese===
众人闻言大笑。长老便带着那些捧礼之人下堂而去，离开了一阵，众人则继续饮酒作乐：不多时他们便自库房回来，捧着一件件佳美之物，都摆在一张长案之上。于是赐礼开始：他先赐给民强六只金杯，制作奇巧，乃堡谷四代匠人之作，末后两只乃是他亲手所制。又赐给日光一条金腰带，工艺精湛绝伦，带上錾刻诸神与先祖、武士之像，以及田野之走兽、空中之飞禽；他将此带系于她腰间之时，低声说了几句，旁人少有听见：

「日光，你这美貌女子，曾有一时你于我们而言，正如毒剑之锋刃、凶人半夜所举之火把；但如今我却不知将来如何，不知你所给我的伤痛是否会随岁月磨灭。如今我既已见你，也就难怪我儿如此了——因为我看着你时，实在不能相信你身上有半分邪恶。无论如何，请收下此礼，权当对你这绝世容光的一份酬答。」

===Original===
She looked on him with kind eyes, and said meekly:

"Indeed, if I have hurt thee unwittingly, I grieve to have hurt so good a man. Hereafter belike we may talk more of this, but now I will but say, that whereas at first I needed but to win thy son's goodwill, so that our Folk might come to life and thriving again, now it is come to this, that he holdeth my heart in his hand and may do what he will with it; therefore I pray thee withhold not thy love either from him or from me."

He looked on her wondering, and said: "Thou art such an one as might make the old man young, and the boy grow into manhood suddenly; and thy voice is as sweet as the voice of the songbirds singing in the dawn of early summer soundeth to him who hath been sick unto death, but who hath escaped it and is mending. And yet I fear thee."

===Chinese===
她以温柔之目视之，柔声答道：

「诚然，若我无心之下伤了你，我为伤了你这样的好人而心痛。此事日后我们或许还会再谈，但眼下我只想说：起初我所需者，不过是赢取你儿子的好感，使我们一族得以重获生机、重得兴旺；如今事已至此——他已将我的心握在掌中，可以任意处之；故此我求你，莫要收回你对他的爱，也莫要收回对我的爱。」

他惊奇地望着她，说道：「你这般人物，足以使老人返老还童，使孩童转眼间长成丈夫；你的声音，在死里逃生、日渐痊愈之人听来，宛似初夏黎明时分歌鸟啼啭一般甜美。然而我仍怕你。」

===Original===
Therewith he kissed her hand and turned unto the others, and he gave unto Bow-may a hauberk of ring-mail of his own fashioning, a sure defence and a wonderful work, and the collar thereof was done with gold and gems.

But he said to her: "Fair damsel-at-arms, faithful is thy face, and the fashion of thee is goodly: now art thou become one of the best of our friends, and this is little enough to give thee; yet would we fain ward thy body against the foeman; so grieve us not by gainsaying us."

And Bow-may was exceeding glad, and scarce knew how to cease handling that marvel of ring-mail.

===Chinese===
说罢他吻了她的手，便转向他人。他将一件亲手所制之环锁锁子甲赐予弓娘——此甲既为可靠之护身，又是一件妙绝之工艺品，其领圈以黄金宝石镶饰。

他又对她说道：「美丽的女战士，你的面容忠诚可信，你的仪态端庄佳美：如今你已成了我们最好的朋友之一，这点东西送你实在微薄；但我们诚心要为你的身躯挡住敌人之刀兵；所以请勿推辞，免得使我们伤心。」

弓娘喜不自胜，爱不释手，几乎不知如何停下抚弄那件环锁宝甲。

===Original===
Then to Wood-wise Iron-face gave a most goodly sword, the blade all marked with dark lines like the stream of an eddying river, the hilts of steel and gold marvellously wrought; and all the work of a smith who had dwelt in the house of his father's father, and was a great warrior.

Unto Wood-father he gave a very goodly helm parcel-gilded; and to his sons and the other folk fair gifts of weapons and jewels and girdles and cups and other good things; so that their hearts were full of joy, and they all praised his open hand.

Then some of the best and merriest of the kinsmen of the Face, and Face-of-god with them, brought the Guests out into the street and among the booths. There Face-of-god beheld the Bride again; and she was standing by the booth of a chapman and dealing with him for a piece of goodly silken cloth to be a gown for one of her guests, and she was talking and smiling as she chaffered with him, as her wont was; for she was ever very friendly of demeanour with all men. But he noted that she was yet exceeding pale, and he was right sorry thereof, for he loved her friendly; yet now had he no shame for all that had befallen, when he bethought him of the Sun-beam and the love she had for him. And also he had a deeming that the Bride would better of her grief.

===Chinese===
随后铁面赐给林智一柄极美之剑，剑身满布暗纹，似漩涡激流之水脉，剑柄以钢与金合制，工艺奇巧；此剑乃出其祖父之宅中一位匠人之手，那人本是一位伟大的武士。

又赐给林父一顶极其华美之半鎏金盔；赐给他的诸子及其他人以诸多佳礼——兵器、珠宝、腰带、杯盏及其他珍物；众人心满意足、欢喜满怀，皆称颂他的慷慨。

于是面神一族中几位最贤良、最开朗的宗亲，连同面神本人，引领众客出门来到街上、走入摊位之间。在那里，面神又见到了新娘；她正立在一个行商摊前，与那人议价，要买一匹佳美丝绸，为的是给她的某位客人做一件长袍；她一边议价一边谈笑，一如其素习；因为她素来待一切人都和蔼可亲。但他留意到她依旧面色惨白，他为此十分难过，因为他素以友爱之情待她；然而此刻，当他想到日光、想到日光对他之情，他对所发生之事已无羞愧之感。他也隐隐觉得，新娘这份忧伤终会渐渐好转。

## LIX The Behest of Face-of-God to the Bride Accomplished: A Motestead Appointed for the Three Folks, to Wit, the Men of Burgdale, the Shepherds, and the Children of the Wolf / 五十九 面神对新娘之托得偿：为三族之民——即堡谷之人、牧羊之民与狼之子民——约定一处议事坪

===Original===
Three years and two months thereafter, three hours after noon in the days of early autumn, came a wain tilted over with precious webs of cloth, and drawn by eight white oxen, into the Marketplace of Silverstead: two score and ten of spearmen of the tallest, clad in goodly war-gear, went beside it, and much people of Silverdale thronged about them. The wain stayed at the foot of the stair that led up to the door of the Mote-house, and there lighted down therefrom a woman goodly of fashion, with wide grey eyes, and face and hands brown with the sun’s burning. She had a helm on her head and a sword girt to her side, and in her arms she bore a yearling child.

And there was come Bow-may with the second man-child born to Face-of-god.

She stayed not amidst the wondering folk, but hastened up the stair, which she had once seen running with the blood of men: the door was open, and she went in and walked straightway, with the babe in her arms, up the great Hall to the dais.

===Chinese===
此后三年又两个月，初秋时节，午后三时，有一辆覆着珍贵锦绣的辎车，由八头白牛牵引，驶入银镇的集市（Marketplace）；车旁行着五十名身材最高大的枪兵，皆披精良战甲，银谷之人蜂拥围随。辎车停在通往议事堂之门的阶梯脚下，车上下来一位仪态端庄的女子，一双灰色的大眼睛，脸和双手都被烈日晒成棕色。她头戴盔，腰间佩剑，怀中抱着一个约莫一岁的孩童。

来者正是弓娥，带着面神所生的第二个男孩。

她不在惊异的众人中停留，径自快步登上阶梯——这阶梯她曾见其上流淌过人血：门是敞开的，她便走入其中，怀抱着婴孩，径直穿过大堂，走向高台。

===Original===
There were men on the dais: amidmost sat Folk-might, little changed since the last day she had seen him, yet fairer, she deemed, than of old time; and her heart went forth to meet the Chieftain of her Folk, and the glad tears started in her eyes and ran down her cheeks as she drew near to him.

By his side sat the Bride, and her also Bow-may deemed to have waxed goodlier. Both she and Folk-might knew Bow-may ere she had gone half the length of the hall; and the Bride rose up in her place and cried out Bow-may’s name joyously.

With these were sitting the elders of the Wolf and the Woodlanders, the more part of whom Bow-may knew well.

On the dais also stood aside a score of men weaponed, and looking as if they were awaiting the word which should send them forth on some errand.

===Chinese===
高台之上坐着数人：正中坐着的是民强，自她上次见他以来几乎未变，然而她觉得他比从前更加俊伟；她的心飞向前去迎接她族人的首领，欣喜的泪水涌上眼眶，当她走近他时，泪珠顺着脸颊滚落下来。

他身旁坐着新娘，弓娥也觉得新娘比从前更加丰丽了。她和民强在弓娥尚未走到大厅一半之处便已认出她来；新娘从座上起身，欢悦地高呼弓娥的名字。

与他们同坐的还有狼族与林中汉子的长老们，其中大半弓娥都熟识。

高台一侧还站着二十名执兵器的男子，看神情仿佛正等待一声号令，便要出发去办某件差事。

===Original===
Now stood up Folk-might and said: “Fair greeting and love to my friend and the daughter of my Folk! How farest thou, Bow-may, best of all friendly women? How fareth my sister, and Face-of-god my brother? and how is it with our friends and helpers in the goodly Dale?”

Said Bow-may: “It is well both with all those and with me; and my heart laughs to see thee, Folk-might, and to look on the elders of the valiant, and our lovely sister the Bride. But I have a message for thee from Face-of-god: wilt thou that I deliver it here?”
