“Yea surely,” said Folk-might, and came forth and took her hand, and kissed her cheeks and her mouth. The Bride also came forth and cast her arms about her, and kissed her; and they led her between them to a seat on the dais beside Folk-might.

But all men looked on the child in her arms and wondered what it was. But Bow-may took the babe, which was both fair and great, and set it on the knees of the Bride, and said:

===Chinese===
于是民强起身说道："向我友善的朋友、我族之女，致以美好的问候与爱意！弓娥啊，所有友善女子之中最善者，你可安好？我的妹妹、面神我的兄弟可安好？我们在那佳美山谷中的朋友与帮手们又如何？"

弓娥说："他们众人和我都好；我的心因见到你、民强，见到这些勇者的长老，以及我们可爱的妹妹新娘而欢笑。但我从面神那里带了一句话给你：你要不要我在此处传达？"

"自然要的，"民强说着走上前来，握住她的手，吻了她的双颊和嘴唇。新娘也走上前来，张开双臂抱住她，吻了她；她二人在两旁引着她，走到高台上民强身旁的一个座位。

众人都望着她怀中的孩子，不知是怎么回事。弓娥却抱起那婴孩——那孩子既俊美又壮健——将他放在新娘的膝上，说道：

===Original===
“Thus saith Face-of-god: ‘Friend and kinswoman, well-beloved playmate, the gift which thou badest of me in sorrow do thou now take in joy, and do all the good thou wouldest to the son of thy friend. The ring which I gave thee once in the garden of the Face, give thou to Bow-may, my trusty and well-beloved, in token of the fulfilment of my behest.’ ”

Then the Bride kissed Bow-may again, and fell to fondling of the child, which was loth to leave Bow-may.

But she spake again: “To thee also, Folk-might, I have a message from Face-of-god, who saith: ‘Mighty warrior, friend and fellow, all things thrive with us, and we are happy. Yet is there a hollow place in our hearts which grieveth us, and only thou and thine may amend it. Though whiles we hear tell of thee, yet we see thee not, and fain were we, might we see thee, and wot if the said tales be true. Wilt thou help us somewhat herein, or wilt thou leave us all the labour? For sure we be that thou wilt not say that thou rememberest us no more, and that thy love for us is departed.’ This is his message, Folk-might, and he would have an answer from thee.”

===Chinese===
"面神这样说：『朋友兼亲人，深受爱重的玩伴，你从前在悲伤中所求于我的礼物，如今便在欢乐中收下吧；对你朋友之子，尽你所能施以一切美意。我从前在面神之宅的花园中给你的那枚戒指，请你交给我那忠实而深爱的弓娥，作为我履行所托的信物。』"

于是新娘又吻了弓娥，便开始抚弄那孩子——那孩子还舍不得离开弓娥。

她又说道："民强，面神也有一句话给你，他说：『英勇的武士，朋友和同袍，我们这里百事兴旺，我们很快乐。然而我们心中有一处空缺令我们伤感，唯有你和你的族人才能弥补。虽然我们时或听人谈起你，却见不到你；我们多盼能见你一面，好知道那些传闻是否属实。你愿否在此事上略略助我们一臂之力，还是要把所有操劳都留给我们？因为我们确信，你绝不会说你已不再记挂我们，你对我们的情谊已经消逝。』民强，这就是他的话，他要你给一个答复。"

===Original===
Then laughed Folk-might and said: “Sister Bow-may, seest thou these weaponed men hereby?”

“Yea,” she said.

Said he: “These men bear a message with them to Face-of-god my brother. Crow the Shaft-speeder, stand forth and tell thy friend Bow-may the message I have set in thy mouth, every word of it.”

Then Crow stood forth and greeted Bow-may friendly, and said: “Friend Bow-may, this is the message of our Alderman: ‘Friend and helper, in the Dale which thou hast given to us do all things thrive; neither are we grown old in three years’ wearing, nor are our memories worsened. We long sore to see you and give you guesting in Silverdale, and one day that shall befall. Meanwhile, know this: that we of the Wolf and the Woodland, mindful of the earth that bore us, and the pit whence we were digged, have a mind to go see Shadowy Vale once in every three years, and there to hold high-tide in the ancient Hall of the Wolf, and sit in the Doom-ring of our Fathers. But since ye have joined yourselves to us in battle, and have given us this Dale, our health and wealth, without price and without reward, we deem you our very brethren, and small shall be our hall-glee, and barren shall our Doom-ring seem to us, unless ye sit there beside us. Come then, that we may rejoice each other by the sight of face and sound of voice; that we may speak together of matters that concern our welfare; so that we three Kindreds may become one Folk. And if this seem good to you, know that we shall be in Shadowy Vale in a half-month’s wearing. Grieve us not by forbearing to come.’ Lo, Bow-may, this is the message, and I have learned it well, for well it pleaseth me to bear it.”

Then said Folk-might: “What say’st thou to the message, Bow-may?”

===Chinese===
民强听了大笑，说道："弓娥妹妹，你可见到旁边这些执兵器的人？"

"见到了，"她说。

他说："这些人带给面神我兄弟一句话。疾箭者克劳（Crow the Shaft-speeder），站出来，把我教给你口传的话——一字不漏地——告诉你朋友弓娥。"

于是克劳站上前去，友善地向弓娥致意，说道："弓娥朋友，这是我们长老的话：『朋友和帮手啊，在你们赠予我们的这条山谷之中，百事兴旺；三年的光阴并未使我们衰老，我们的记忆也未尝减退。我们极其渴望见到你们，在银谷款待你们——这一日终将到来。与此同时，请知悉：我们狼族与林中之民，上念生养我等之土地、掘出我等之土坑，有意每过三年重返幽谷一行，在古老的狼族厅堂中举行盛会，坐进我们先祖的判决环之中。然而，既然你们在战场上与我们并肩，又无偿无酬地将这条山谷——我们的性命与财富——赐予我们，我们便视你们为真正的兄弟；你们若不与我们同坐其处，我们厅堂中的欢乐便微不足道，我们的判决环在我们看来也将空虚无趣。那么来吧，好让我们以睹面容、以闻声音而彼此欢悦；好让我们共议关乎福祉之事；使我们三族能合为一族。若此事在你们看来可行，须知我们将于半月之后身在幽谷。切勿令我们伤心而不来。』弓娥，这就是口信，我已背得烂熟，因为传这口信令我十分欢喜。"

于是民强说："弓娥，你觉得这口信如何？"

===Original===
“It is good in all ways,” said she, “but is it timely? May our folk have the message and get to Shadowy Vale, so as to meet you there?”

“Yea surely,” said Folk-might, “for our kinsmen here shall take the road through Shadowy Vale, and in four days’ time they shall be in Burgdale, and as thou wottest, it is scant a two days’ journey thence to Shadowy Vale.”

Therewith he turned to those men again, and said: “Kinsman Crow, depart now, and use all diligence with thy message.”

So the messengers began to stir; but Bow-may cried out: “Ho! Folk-might, my friend, I perceive thou art little changed from the man I knew in Shadowy Vale, who would have his dinner before the fowl were plucked. For shall I not go back with these thy messengers, so that I also may get all ready to wend to the Mote-house of Shadowy Vale?”

===Chinese===
"各方面都好，"她说，"但时间上来得及么？我们的人能否得到这口信、赶到幽谷，以便与你们在那里相会？"

"自然来得及，"民强说，"因为我们这些族人将取道幽谷而行，四日之后便可抵达堡谷，而你也知道，从堡谷到幽谷不过区区两日路程。"

说罢他又转向那些人，说道："族人克劳，现在出发吧，尽心尽力去传达你的口信。"

信使们便起身要行；弓娥却叫道："嘿！民强，我的朋友，我看你跟我在幽谷时所认识的那个人没什么两样——那时家禽还没拔毛，他便要吃晚饭了。因为我难道不该随你这些信使回去，好让我也把一切准备妥当、动身前往幽谷的议事堂么？"

===Original===
But the Bride looked kindly on her, and laughed and said: “Sister Bow-may, his meaning is that thou shouldest abide here in Silverdale till we depart for the Folk-thing, and then go thither with us; and this I also pray thee to do, that thou mayst rejoice the hearts of thine old friends; and also that thou mayst teach me all that I should know concerning this fair child of my brother and my sister.”

And she looked on her so kindly as she caressed the babe, that Bow-may’s heart melted, and she cried out:

“Would that I might never depart from the house wherein thou dwellest, O Bride of my Kinsman! And this that thou biddest me is easy and pleasant for me to do. But afterwards I must get me back to Burgdale; for I seem to have left much there that calleth for me.”

===Chinese===
新娘却和善地望着她，笑道："弓娥妹妹，他的意思是：你应当在银谷住下，等到我们启程前往民众大会（the Folk-thing）之时再与我们同去；我也求你这样做，好让你旧日朋友的心欢喜；也让你可以教导我一切我应当知道的、关于我兄弟和我妹妹这可爱孩子的事。"

她一边抚弄着婴孩，一边如此和善地望着她，弓娥的心都融化了，叫道：

"但愿我永远不必离开你所居住的这所宅子，我族人的新娘啊！你所吩咐我的事，我做来既轻松又愉快。但之后我必须回到堡谷去；因为我似乎在那里留下了许多牵挂我的东西。"

===Original===
“Yea,” said Folk-might, “and art thou wedded, Bow-may? Shalt thou never bend the yew in battle again?”

Said Bow-may soberly: “Who knoweth, chieftain? Yea, I am wedded now these two years; and nought I looked for less when I followed those twain through the wildwood to Burgdale.”

She sighed therewith, and said: “In all the Dale there is no better man of his hands than my man, nor any goodlier to look on, and he is even that Hart of Highcliff whom thou knowest well, O Bride!”

Said the Bride: “Thou sayest sooth, there is no better man in the Dale.”

Said Bow-may: “Sun-beam bade me wed him when he pressed hard upon me.” She stayed awhile, and then said: “Face-of-god also deemed I should not naysay the man; and now my son by him is of like age to this little one.”

===Chinese===
"哦，"民强说，"那么你可成了婚，弓娥？你难道再也不在战阵之上弯动紫杉之弓了么？"

弓娥郑重地说："首领，谁能知道呢？是的，我成婚已两年了；当初我追随他二人穿过野林前往堡谷之时，对此也并不感到意外。"

她说着叹了口气，说道："整条山谷之中，论手艺没有比我丈夫更好的男子，论相貌也没有比他更俊伟的；他便是那高崖之鹿（the Hart of Highcliff），新娘，你是熟知他的！"

新娘说："你说的是实情，这山谷中确实没有比他更好的男子了。"

弓娥说："他苦苦求我之时，是日光劝我嫁给他的。"她停了一阵，又说："面神也觉得我不该拒绝他；如今我跟他生的儿子，年纪与这小家伙相仿。"

===Original===
“Good is thy story,” said Folk-might; “or deemest thou, Bow-may, that such strong and goodly women as thou, and women so kind and friendly, should forbear the wedding and the bringing forth of children? Yea, and we who may even yet have to gather to another field before we die, and fight for life and the goods of life.”

“Thou sayest well,” she said; “all that hath befallen me is good since the day whereon I loosed shaft from the break of the bent over yonder.”

Therewith she fell a-musing, and made as though she were hearkening to the soft voice of the Bride caressing the new-come baby; but in sooth neither heard nor saw what was going on about her, for her thoughts were in bygone days. Howbeit presently she came to herself again, and fell to asking many questions concerning Silverdale and the kindred, and those who had once been thralls of the Dusky Men; and they answered all duly, and told her the whole story of the Dale since the Day of the Victory.

===Chinese===
"你的故事很好，"民强说，"——弓娥，难道你以为像你这般强壮美丽、这般和善亲切的女子，竟不该婚配、不该生儿育女么？况且我们这些人，到死之前或许还要在另一个战场上集结，为性命与性命所资而战呢。"

"你说得对，"她说，"自从那日我在那边草坡之巅射出一箭以来，凡临到我身上的一切都是好的。"

说罢她便陷入沉思，装作在倾听新娘抚弄新来婴孩时的轻柔声音；实则周围发生的一切她既没听见也没看见，因为她的心思都飞到了往昔岁月之中。不过不久她又回过神来，开始询问许多关于银谷和族人、以及那些从前为黝暗人所奴之人的事；众人一一作答，把自胜利之日（the Day of the Victory）以来山谷中的全部故事都讲给她听。

===Original===
So Bow-may and the carles who had come with her abode for that half-month in Silverdale, guested in all love by the folk thereof, both the kindreds and the poor folk. And Bow-may deemed that the Bride loved Face-of-god’s child little less than her own, whereof she had two, a man and a woman; and thereat was she full of joy, since she knew that Face-of-god and the Sun-beam would be fain thereof.

Thereafter, when the time was come, fared Folk-might and the Bride, and many of the elders and warriors of the Wolf and the Woodland, to Shadowy Vale; and Dallach and the best of Rosedale went with them, being so bidden; and Bow-may and her following, according to the word of the Bride. And in Shadowy Vale they met Face-of-god and Alderman Iron-face, and the chiefs of Burgdale and the Shepherds, and many others; and great joy there was at the meeting. And the Sun-beam remembered the word which she spoke to Face-of-god when first he came to Shadowy Vale, that she would be wishful to see again the dwelling wherein she had passed through so much joy and sorrow of her younger days. But if anyone were fain of this meeting, the Alderman was glad above all, when he took the Bride once more in his arms, and caressed her whom he had deemed should be a very daughter of his House.

===Chinese===
于是弓娥和随她同来的汉子们在银谷住了那半个月，受到当地诸族之人与贫苦之民满心热爱的款待。弓娥觉得新娘对面神的孩子爱护得几乎不亚于己出——她自己有两个孩子，一男一女；她对此满心欢喜，因为她知道面神和日光得知此事必定高兴。

此后，时日一到，民强和新娘，以及狼族与林中的许多长者和武士，便动身前往幽谷；达拉赫和玫瑰谷的佼佼者也受邀随行；弓娥及其随从则按新娘的话同去。在幽谷，他们与面神、长老铁面、堡谷和牧羊之民的首领们以及其他许多人相会；相聚之时，欢喜无限。日光记起她初见面神来到幽谷时对他说过的话——她曾盼望能再看一眼那座居所，她在其中度过了少年时代那么多的悲欢。然而这次相聚若说有谁最为欣喜，那便是长老：当他再次将新娘拥入怀中，抚爱这位他曾以为必当成为他宅中真正女儿的人——他比谁都高兴。

===Original===
Now telleth the tale of all these kindreds, to wit, the Men of Burgdale and the Sheepcotes; and the Children of the Wolf, and the Woodlanders, and the Men of Rosedale, that they were friends henceforth, and became as one Folk, for better or worse, in peace and in war, in waning and waxing; and that whatsoever befell them, they ever held Shadowy Vale a holy place, and for long and long after they met there in mid-autumn, and held converse and counsel together.

No more as now telleth the tale of these Kindreds and Folks, but maketh an ending.

===Chinese===
如今故事讲到所有这些族类——即堡谷之人与牧羊之民、狼之子民、林中汉子，以及玫瑰谷之人——他们从此结为友朋，合为一体，无论顺逆、无论和战、无论盛衰，皆如一族；无论遭遇何事，他们始终奉幽谷为圣地，此后很久很久，每逢仲秋便在那里相聚，共话共商。

关于这些族类与子民，故事此刻不再多讲，就此作结。

## XVI The Bride Speaketh with Face-of-God / 十六 新娘与面神相语

===Original===
February had died into March, and March was now twelve days old, on a fair and sunny day an hour before noon; and Face-of-god was in a meadow a scant mile down the Dale from Burgstead. He had been driving a bull into a goodman’s byre nearby, and had had to spend toil and patience both in getting him out of the fields and into the byre; for the beast was hot with the spring days and the new grass. So now he was resting himself in happy mood in an exceeding pleasant place, a little meadow to wit, on one side whereof was a great orchard or grove of sweet chestnuts, which went right up to the feet of the Southern Cliffs: across the meadow ran a clear brook towards the Weltering Water, free from big stones, in some places dammed up for the flooding of the deep pasture-meadow, and with the grass growing on its lips down to the very water. There was a low bank just outside the chestnut trees, as if someone had raised a dyke about them when they were young, which had been trodden low and spreading through the lapse of years by the faring of many men and beasts. The primroses bloomed thick upon it now, and here and there along it was a low blackthorn bush in full blossom; from the mid-meadow and right down to the lip of the brook was the grass well nigh hidden by the blossoms of the meadow-saffron, with daffodils sprinkled about amongst them, and in the trees and bushes the birds, and chiefly the blackbirds, were singing their loudest.

There sat Face-of-god on the bank resting after his toil, and happy was his mood; since in two days’ wearing he should be pacing the Maiden Ward awaiting the token that was to lead him to Shadowy Vale; so he sat calling to mind the Friend as he had last seen her, and striving as it were to set her image standing on the flowery grass before him, till all the beauty of the meadow seemed bare and empty to him without her. Then it fell into his mind that this had been a beloved trysting-place betwixt him and the Bride, and that often when they were little would they come to gather chestnuts in the grove, and thereafter sit and prattle on the old dyke; or in spring when the season was warm would they go barefoot into the brook, seeking its treasures of troutlets and flowers and clean-washed agate pebbles. Yea, and time not long ago had they met here to talk as lovers, and sat on that very bank in all the kindness of good days without a blemish, and both he and she had loved the place well for its wealth of blossoms and deep grass and goodly trees and clear running stream.

As he thought of all this, and how often there he had praised to himself her beauty, which he scarce dared praise to her, he frowned and slowly rose to his feet, and turned toward the chestnut-grove, as though he would go thence that way; but or ever he stepped down from the dyke he turned about again, and even therewith, like the very image and ghost of his thought, lo! the Bride herself coming up from out the brook and wending toward him, her wet naked feet gleaming in the sun as they trod down the tender meadow-saffron and brushed past the tufts of daffodils. He stood staring at her discomforted, for on that day he had much to think of that seemed happy to him, and he deemed that she would now question him, and his mind pondered divers ways of answering her, and none seemed good to him. She drew near and let her skirts fall over her feet, and came to him, her gown hem dragging over the flowers: then she stood straight up before him and greeted him, but reached not forth her hand to him nor touched him. Her face was paler that its wont, and her voice trembled as she spake to him and said:

===Chinese===
二月已没入三月，三月又过了十二日；是日晴好明媚，正午前一小时。面神身在堡镇下游不足一里处的一片草地上。他方才正将一头公牛赶入近旁一户人家的牛栏，既费了力气，又耗了耐性，才把那畜生从田间弄进栏里——盖因春日初临、新草初生，那畜生燥热难当。如今他心情甚是畅快，在一处极其宜人之地歇息；那是一片小草地，一侧乃是大片的果园，或可谓甜栗之林，一直延展到南崖脚下：一道清溪横穿草地，流向翻滚河（the Weltering Water），水中无大石，有几处筑了坝，用以漫灌那片低深的牧草草地，溪岸上的青草直长到水边。栗林外缘有一道低堤，仿佛有人在这些树幼时曾为它们筑过一道土围，历经岁月、人畜往来践踏，如今已低矮平缓、四下铺展。此时堤上报春花密密盛开，沿堤各处还可见矮矮的黑刺李，花团锦簇；自草地中央直到溪岸，青草几乎被秋水仙之花尽数遮没，其间又散落点缀着黄水仙；树丛灌木之中，众鸟齐啼，尤以乌鸫为最，歌声最为嘹亮。

面神就坐在堤上，劳顿之后小歇，心绪甚欢；盖因再过两日，他便要踱步于少女之守望（Maiden Ward），等候那将引他往幽谷（Shadowy Vale）而去的信物。于是他坐着，将那位朋友（the Friend）自上次相见后的模样细细唤回心头，竭力要使她的身形立在他面前那繁花之草上；如此一来，没有她，这草地的诸般美景于他便似空荡寂寥。继而又想起，此处原是他与新娘昔日两情相悦的幽会之地；幼时二人常来林中拾栗，事后便坐在那条旧堤上絮絮叨叨；或逢春日和暖，便赤足踏入溪中，去寻溪中的宝贝——小鳟鱼、花朵、以及被水洗得干干净净的玛瑙卵石。是啊，便是不久之前，他们还曾在此相会、如恋人般对谈，就坐在那道堤上，彼时日子美好无瑕，他和她都深爱此地——爱其繁花如锦、深草如毯、佳木葱茏、清流潺潺。

他正想着这一切，又想起自己曾在此多少回暗自赞叹她的美貌——那美貌他几乎不敢当面称扬——想到此处，他皱起眉，缓缓起身，转身朝栗林那边走去，似欲由那一路离去；然而还不等他迈下堤来，却又回过身去；恰在此时，宛如他心思的真身与幻影一般——你看！新娘本人正自溪中上来，朝他走来，赤足湿漉漉的，踏倒娇嫩的秋水仙、拂过一簇簇黄水仙，在日头下闪闪发亮。他怔怔地盯着她，心头大窘；盖因那日他有许多念想，桩桩似都令他欢喜，他只怕她此刻要盘问，心中暗暗盘算了种种答法，却没一条合他的意。她走到近前，任裙裾垂落盖住双足，朝他走来，衣摆拖过满地繁花；随即在他面前笔直站定，向他见礼，却并未向他伸手，也不曾触碰他。她的面色比平日苍白，开口对他说话时声音发颤：

===Original===
“Face-of-god, I would ask thee a gift.”

“All gifts,” he said, “that thou mayest ask, and I may give, lie open to thee.”

She said: “If I be alive when the time comes this gift thou mayst well give me.”

“Sweet kinswoman,” said he, “tell me what it is that thou wouldest have of me.” And he was ill-at-ease as he waited for her answer.

She said: “Ah, kinsman, kinsman! Woe on the day that maketh kinship accursed to me because thou desirest it!”

===Chinese===
"面神，我要向你求一件礼物。"

"凡你所能求、我所能给的礼物，"他说，"尽都摆在你面前。"

她说："若到时候我尚在人世，这件礼物你原是可以给我的。"

"好表妹，"他说，"告诉我，你要我给你什么。"他等着她的回答，心中好不自在。

她说："唉，表哥，表哥！可恨这日子，你贪恋着这层亲缘，这亲缘于我却成了咒诅！"

===Original===
He held his peace and was exceeding sorry; and she said:

“This is the gift that I ask of thee, that in the days to come when thou art wedded, thou wilt give me the second man-child whom thou begettest.”

He said: “This shalt thou have, and would that I might give thee much more. Would that we were little children together other again, as when we played here in other days.”

===Chinese===
他默然不语，心中极为难过；她说：

"我所求你的礼物便是：将来你成婚之后，把你所生的第二个男孩给我。"

他说："这个你必能得到，恨不得我能给你的还多得多。但愿我们还能再做回从前那样的小儿女，就像往日我们在这里玩耍之时。"

===Original===
She said: “I would have a token of thee that thou shalt show to the God, and swear on it to give me the gift. For the times change.”

“What token wilt thou have?” said he.

She said: “When next thou farest to the Wood, thou shalt bring me back, it maybe a flower from the bank ye sit upon, or a splinter from the dais of the hall wherein ye feast, or maybe a ring or some matter that the strangers are wont to wear. That shall be the token.”

She spoke slowly, hanging her head adown, but she lifted it presently and looked into his face and said:

===Chinese===
她说："我要你给我一件信物，你好拿到地神（the God）面前，对着它起誓，许我这礼物。因为时日会变。"

"你要什么样的信物？"他说。

她说："下次你去林中之时，须给我带一样东西回来——许是你们所坐堤岸上的一朵花，许是你们设宴厅中高台上的一枚木屑，又或者是一只戒指，或那些陌生人惯常佩戴的什么物事。那便是信物了。"

她说话时低垂着头，语调缓慢；但随即抬起头来，直视他的脸，说道：

===Original===
“Woe’s me, woe’s me, Gold-mane! How evil is this day, when bewailing me I may not bewail thee also! For I know that thine heart is glad. All through the winter have I kept this hidden in my heart, and durst not speak to thee. But now the spring-tide hath driven me to it. Let summer come, and who shall say?”

Great was his grief, and his shame kept him silent, and he had no word to say; and again she said:

“Tell me, Gold-mane, when goest thou thither?”

He said: “I know not surely, may happen in two days, may happen in ten. Why askest thou?”

“O friend!” she said, “is it a new thing that I should ask thee whither thou goest and whence thou comest, and the times of thy coming and going. Farewell today! Forget not the token. Woe’s me, that I may not kiss thy fair face!”

===Chinese===
"苦啊我，苦啊我，金鬃（Gold-mane）！今日何其可恨——我哀叹自己，却不能连你一同哀叹！因为我知道你的心是欢喜的。整个冬天，我都把这事藏在心头，不敢对你说。可如今春潮涌动，逼得我不得不说。待到夏天来了，又有谁说得准呢？"

他心中悲痛之极，羞愧使他无言以对，一句话也说不出；她又说道：

"告诉我，金鬃，你何时去那里？"

他说："我也说不准，也许两日之后，也许十日之后。你为何问起？"

"噢，朋友！"她说，"我问你去哪里、从哪里来，问你往来的时候，这难道是头一遭么？今日就此别过！那信物，你别忘了。苦啊我，竟不能亲一亲你这张俊脸！"

===Original===
She spread her arms abroad and lifted up her face as one who waileth, but no sound came from her lips; then she turned about and went away as she had come.

But as for him he stood there after she was gone in all confusion, as if he were undone: for he felt his manhood lessened that he should thus and so sorely have hurt a friend, and in a manner against his will. And yet he was somewhat wroth with her, that she had come upon him so suddenly, and spoken to him with such mastery, and in so few words, and he with none to make answer to her, and that she had so marred his pleasure and his hope of that fair day. Then he sat him down again on the flowery bank, and little by little his heart softened, and he once more called to mind many a time when they had been there before, and the plays and the games they had had together there when they were little. And he bethought him of the days that were long to him then, and now seemed short to him, and as if they were all grown together into one story, and that a sweet one. Then his breast heaved with a sob, and the tears rose to his eyes and burned and stung him, and he fell a-weeping for that sweet tale, and wept as he had wept once before on that old dyke when there had been some child’s quarrel between them, and she had gone away and left him.

Then after a while he ceased his weeping, and looked about him lest anyone might be coming, and then he arose and went to and fro in the chestnut-grove for a good while, and afterwards went his ways from that meadow, saying to himself: “Yet remaineth to me the morrow of tomorrow, and that is the first of the days of the watching for the token.”

But all that day he was slow to meet the eyes of men; and in the hall that eve he was silent and moody; for from time to time it came over him that some of his manhood had departed from him.

===Chinese===
她张开双臂，仰起脸，如同哀号之人；然而唇间却不曾透出半点声息；随即她转过身，如她来时一般离去。

至于他呢，她走后，他仍怔怔地站在原地，神魂无主，仿佛整个人都散了：盖因他觉得自己作为男子汉的气性减损了——他竟这般深地伤了一位朋友，而此事又多半与他的本意相违。然而他又有些恼她，恼她这般突兀地扑到他跟前，又用这般凌厉的态度、这般寥寥几句话对他说话，叫他竟无从置答；恼她就这样毁了他那日的欢喜与盼望。于是他又在繁花之堤上坐下，心肠渐渐软了下来，又想起从前他们多少次在此地相会，想起他们小时候在这里一同玩过的把戏与游戏。他想起那些当时觉得漫长的日子，如今却觉得短暂，仿佛全合在一处，成了一个故事，一个甜蜜的故事。他胸膛因抽噎而起伏，眼泪涌上眼眶，灼热地刺痛着他；他为那甜蜜的故事哭了起来，哭得正如从前在这条旧堤上哭过一回——那回他们之间生了孩子气的口角，她便走掉，丢下了他。

过了一会儿，他止住哭泣，四下里望了望，生怕有人走来；然后起身，在栗林中来回踱了许久，之后便离开了那片草地，自言自语道："还有明日的明日留给我，那才是守望信物的头一日。"

那一整天，他都羞于与人的目光相对；是夜在厅中，他沉默寡言、郁郁寡欢；因为他不时觉得，自己男子汉的气性已有一份离他而去。

## XXXIV The Chieftains Take Counsel in the Hall of the Face / 三十四 首领们于面神之宅议事

===Original===
Then turned Face-of-god back into the Hall, and saw where Iron-face sat at the dais, and with him Folk-might and Stone-face and the Elder of the Dale-wardens, and Sun-beam withal; so he went soberly up to the board, and sat himself down thereat beside Stone-face, over against Folk-might and his father, beside whom sat the Sun-beam; and Folk-might looked on him gravely, as a man powerful and trustworthy, yet was his look somewhat sour.

Then the Alderman said: “My son, I said not to thee come back presently, because I wotted that thou wouldst surely do so, knowing that we have much to speak of. For, whatever these thy friends may have done, or whatsoever thou hast done with them to grieve us, all that must be set aside at this present time, since the matter in hand is to save the Dale and its folk. What sayest thou hereon? Since, young as thou mayst be, thou art our War-leader, and doubtless shalt so be after the Folk-mote hath been holden.”

===Chinese===
面神（Face-of-god）转身回到厅堂之内，看见铁面（Iron-face）坐在高台之上，与他同坐的有民强（Folk-might）、石面（Stone-face）、谷卫之长（the Elder of the Dale-wardens），还有日光（Sun-beam）也在其侧；他便稳步走上桌前，在石面旁边坐下，与民强和他的父亲相对，日光照旧坐在铁面身旁；民强神情凝重地注视着他，一副强干可信之人的模样，然而目光之中带几分酸涩。

于是长老（the Alderman）开口道："我的儿，我未曾叫你即刻回来，因为我知道你定然会回来——明摆着我们有许多话要商量。因为，无论你这些朋友做了什么，无论你与他们一同做了什么令我们伤心之事，眼下都得暂且搁置不提，因为当务之急乃是保全此谷与谷中之民。你于此有何话说？因为，你纵然年轻，却已是我们的战首（War-leader），待到民众大会（the Folk-mote）开过之后，无疑仍将由你担任。"

===Original===
Face-of-god answered not hastily: indeed, as he sat thinking for a minute or two, the fair spring day seemed to darken about them or to glare into the light of flames amidst the night-tide; and the joyous clamour without doors seemed to grow hoarse and fearful as the sound of wailing and shrieking. But he spake firmly and simply in a clear voice, and said:

“There can be no two words concerning what we have to aim at; these Dusky Men we must slay every one, though we be fewer than they be.”

Folk-might smiled and nodded his head; but the others sat staring down the hall or into the hangings.

Then spake Folk-might: “Thou wert a boy methought when I cast my spear at thee last autumn, Face-of-god, but now hast thou grown into a man. Now tell me, what deemest thou we must do to slay them all?”

Said Face-of-god: “Once again it is clear that we must fall upon them at home in Rosedale and Silverdale.”

Again Folk-might nodded: but Iron-face said:

“Needeth this? May we not ward the Dale and send many bands into the wood to fall upon them when we meet them? Yea, and so doing these our guests have already slain many, as this valiant man hath told me e’en now. Will ye not slay so many at last, that they shall learn to fear us, and abide at home and leave us at peace?”

===Chinese===
面神并不急着作答：他坐着寻思了一两分钟，那明媚的春日在他们周围仿佛骤然阴沉下来，又仿佛在半夜之时化作熊熊火光；门外的欢声喧闹也仿佛变得嘶哑可怖，如哀号尖叫之声一般。然而他坚定、质朴地以清朗之声开口说道：

"我们所求之事，没有半点含糊的余地：这些黝暗人（the Dusky Men），我们非得斩尽杀绝不可，哪怕我们人数少于他们。"

民强微微一笑，点了点头；其余众人却坐着直直地望向厅堂深处，或凝视着壁帷。

于是民强说道："面神，去年秋天我朝你掷出长枪之时，还当你是个孩子，如今你已长成一个男子汉了。那么你告诉我，你以为要怎样才能将他们斩尽杀绝？"

面神道："还是那句话，明摆着我们非得直捣他们在玫瑰谷（Rosedale）和银谷（Silverdale）的巢穴不可。"

民强又点了点头；铁面却说：

"非如此不可么？难道我们不能守卫此谷，遣数队人马入林，相遇之时加以袭击么？而且这样做，我们这些客人已经杀了他们不少，正如这位壮士方才告诉我的。你们到头来岂不会杀得他们够多，叫他们学会怕我们，乖乖守在老家，与我们相安无事？"

===Original===
But Face-of-god said: “Meseemeth, father, that this is not thy rede, and that thou sayest this but to try me: and perchance ye have been talking about me when I was without in the street e’en now. Even if it might be that we should thus cow these felons into abiding at home and tormenting their own thralls at their ease, yet how then are our friends of the Wolf holpen to their own again? And I shall tell thee that I have promised to this man and this woman that I will give them no less than a man’s help in this matter. Moreover, I have spoken in every house of the Dale, and to the Shepherds and the Woodlanders, and there is no man amongst them but will follow me in the quarrel. Furthermore, they have heard of the thralldom that is done on men no great way from their own houses; yea, they have seen it; and they remember the old saw, ‘Grief in thy neighbour’s hall is grief in thy garth,’ and sure it is, father, that whether thou or I gainsay them, go they will to deliver the thralls of the Dusky Men, and will leave us alone in the Dale.”

“This is no less than sooth,” said the Dale-warden, “never have men gone forth more joyously to a merrymaking than all men of us shall wend to this war.”

“But,” said Face-of-god, “of one thing ye may be sure, that these men will not abide our pleasure till we cut them all off in scattered bands, nor will they sit deedless at home. Nor indeed may they; for we have heard from their thralls that they look to have fresh tribes of them come to hand to eat their meat and waste their servants, and these and they must find new abodes and new thralls; and they are now warned by the overthrows and slayings that they have had at our hands that we are astir, and they will not delay long, but will fall upon us with all their host; it might even be today or tomorrow.”

===Chinese===
面神道："父亲，依我看来，这并非您的本意，您这样说不过是试探我罢了：也许方才我在外面街上之时，你们正在议论我呢。就算我们当真能把这些恶徒（the Felons）吓得龟缩在家、安安逸逸地折磨自家的奴隶（thralls），可我们狼族（the Wolf）的朋友又怎能借此收复故土呢？而且我要告诉您，我已向这一男一女许下诺言：此事上给他们的帮助，决不少于一个男子汉所能给的。况且，我已经在谷中每一户人家都说过了，对牧羊之民（the Shepherds）和林中汉子（the Woodlanders）也都说过，他们之中没有一人不肯追随我投入这一场纷争。再者，他们已听说就在离自家不远之处，有人把人当作奴隶役使；不但是听说，简直亲眼见过；他们还记得那句老话：'邻家厅堂之祸，便是自家院中之祸。'父亲，这是千真万确的——无论您或我怎样反对，他们都要去解救黝暗人手下的奴隶，把我们独留在谷中。"

谷卫（the Dale-warden）道："此言丝毫不差。世人赴宴游赏，都未曾有过这般欢欣的，而我们众人前去打这一仗，也必这样欢欣前往。"

面神道："然而有一件事你们尽可放心：这些人决不会安安分分地等我们把他们一支支零敲碎打地全歼掉，也不会坐在家里无所作为。其实他们也不能；因为我们从他们的奴隶口中听说，他们正盼望本族的新部落前来，分食他们的口粮、糟蹋他们的奴仆，这些新旧之人必须另觅新的住所和新的奴隶；而且他们既已在我们手下连吃败仗、死伤累累，晓得我们已经行动起来，必不会久久拖延，而要倾全军来攻；说不定就在今日或明日。"

===Original===
Said Folk-might: “In all this thou sayest sooth, brother of the Dale; and to cut this matter short, I will tell you all, that yesterday we had with us a runaway from Silverdale (it is overlong to tell how we fell in with her; for it was a woman). But she told us that this very moon is a new tribe come into the Dale, six long hundreds in number, and twice as many more are looked for in two eights of days, and that ere this moon hath waned, that is, in twenty-four days, they will wend their ways straight for Burgdale, for they know the ways thereto. So I say that Face-of-god is right in all wise. But tell me, brother, hast thou thought of how we shall come upon these men?”

“How many men wilt thou lead into battle?” said Face-of-god.

Folk-might reddened, and said: “A few, a few; maybe two-hundreds all told.”

“Yea,” said Face-of-god, “but some special gain wilt thou be to us.”

“So I deem at least,” said Folk-might.

Said Face-of-god: “Good is that. Now have we held our Weapon-show in the Dale, and we find that we together with you be sixteen long hundreds of men; and the tale of the foemen that be now in Silverdale, newcomers and all, shall be three thousands or thereabout, and in Rosedale hard on a thousand.”

===Chinese===
民强道："堡谷（the Dale）的兄弟，你所说的句句是实；长话短说，我告诉你们大家：昨日我们这里来了一个从银谷逃出的人（如何邂逅说来话长；因为是个女子）。可她告诉我们，本月之内便有一支新部落进入银谷，人数计六长百（long hundreds）之多，再过十六日，还有两倍于此之数可期；待本月之晦，也就是二十四日之内，他们便要径直开赴堡谷，因为他们认得通往那里的路。所以我只能说，面神所言桩桩都对。可是告诉我，兄弟，你可曾想过我们当如何袭击这些人？"

面神道："你能带多少人参战？"

民强红了脸，说道："不多，不多；算尽了大约两百人。"

面神道："不错，但你于我们必有一桩特别的用处。"

民强道："至少我是这样以为的。"

面神道："那便好。如今我们已在谷中举行过武器大阅（Weapon-show），算来我们连同你们合计，共有十六长百之众；而银谷中眼下之敌，连新来者在内，约有三千之数，玫瑰谷中也将近一千。"

===Original===
“Scarce so many,” said Folk-might; “some of the felons have died; we told over our silver arm-rings yesterday, and the tale was three hundred and eighty and six. Besides, they were never so many as thou deemest.”

“Well,” said Face-of-god, “yet at least they shall outnumber us sorely. We may scarce leave the Dale unguarded when our host is gone; therefore I deem that we shall have but one thousand of men for our onslaught on Silverdale.”

“How come ye to that?” said Stone-face.

===Chinese===
民强道："没那么多；那些恶徒已死了不少；我们昨日清点了银臂环，数目是三百八十六枚。况且他们向来没有你所估的那么多。"

面神道："也罢，但至少他们的人数要远远超过我们。大军既出，谷中不可不设防；因此我以为，进击银谷之兵，至多不过一千。"

石面道："这怎么算出来的？"

===Original===
Said Face-of-god: “Abide a while, fosterer! Though the odds between us be great, it is not to be hidden that I wot how ye of the Wolf know of privy passes into Silverdale; yea, into the heart thereof; and this is the special gain ye have to give us. Therefore we, the thousand men, falling on the foe unawares, shall make a great slaughter of them; and if the murder be but grim enough, those thralls of theirs shall fear us and not them, as already they hate them and not us, so that we may look to them for rooting out these sorry weeds after the overthrow. And what with one thing, what with another, we may cherish a good hope of clearing Silverdale at one stroke with the said thousand men.

“There remaineth Rosedale, which will be easier to deal with, because the Dusky Men therein are fewer and the thralls as many: that also would I fall on at the same time as we fall on Silverdale with the men that are left over from the Silverdale onslaught. Wherefore my rede is, that we gather all those unmeet for battle in the field into this Burg, with ten tens of men to strengthen them; which shall be enough for them, along with the old men, and lads, and sturdy women, to defend themselves till help comes, if aught of evil befall, or to flee into the mountains, or at the worst to die valiantly. Then let the other five hundreds fare up to Rosedale, and fall on the Dusky Men therein about the same time, but not before our onslaught on Silverdale: thus shall hand help foot, so that stumbling be not falling; and we may well hope that our rede shall thrive.”

===Chinese===
面神道："且慢，养父（fosterer）！你我之间虽然众寡悬殊，但有一桩瞒不住的事：我知道你们狼族晓得潜入银谷的秘径，而且能直抵其腹心；这便是你们能给的特别用处。所以我们这一千人出其不意地扑向敌人，必能大肆屠戮；只要这一场杀戮够狠，那些奴隶便要怕我们、不怕他们——他们如今恨的本来就不是我们，而是那些恶徒——这样一来，败局既定之后，我们还可以指望他们去把这群恶草连根拔尽。这样那样加在一处，我们大可以怀抱一线希望：单凭这一千人之众，一鼓作气扫清银谷。

"剩下的便是玫瑰谷，处置起来倒要容易些：因为谷中的黝暗人较少，而奴隶之数与之相当。我也愿以进攻银谷之后剩下来的人马，在进击银谷的同一时间，扑向玫瑰谷。因此我的主意是：将所有不堪上阵野战之人悉数迁入此堡，另留百人加以护卫；有这一百人，加上老人、少年和健壮的妇人，足可自卫以待援军——万一有祸事临头；或退入山中；至不济，也能壮烈而死。然后让另外五百人开赴玫瑰谷，约在我们进击银谷的同一时间，却不略早于我们银谷之战，扑向那里的黝暗人：这样手足以相扶，跌一跤不至摔倒；我们的方略可望大获成功。"

===Original===
Then was he silent, and the Sun-beam looked upon him with gleaming eyes and parted lips, waiting eagerly to hear what Folk-might would say. He held his peace a while, drumming on the board with his fingers, and none else spake a word. At last he said:

“War-leader of Burgdale, all that thou hast spoken likes me well, and even so must it be done, saving that parting of our host and sending one part to fall upon Rosedale. I say, nay; let us put all our might into that one stroke on Silverdale, and then we are undone indeed if we fail; but so shall we be if we fail anywise; but if we win Silverdale, then shall Rosedale lie open before us.”

“My brother,” said Face-of-god, “thou art a tried warrior, and I but a lad: but dost thou not see this, that whatever we do, we shall not at one onslaught slay all the Dusky Men of Silverdale, and those that flee before us shall betake them to Rosedale, and tell all the tale, and what shall hinder them then from falling on Burgdale (since they are no great way from it) after they have murdered what they will of the unhappy people under their hands?”

Said Folk-might: “I say not but that there is a risk thereof, but in war we must needs run such risks, and all should be risked rather than that our blow on Silverdale be light. For we be the fewer; and if the foemen have time to call that to mind, then are we all lost.”

Said Stone-face: “Meseemeth, War-leader, that there is nought much to dread in leaving Rosedale to itself for a while; for not only may we follow hard on the fleers if they flee to Rosedale, and be there no long time after them, before they have time to stir their host; but also after the overthrow we shall be free to send men back to Burgdale by way of Shadowy Vale. I deem that herein Folk-might hath the right of it.”

“Even so say I,” said the Alderman; “besides, we might theft leave more folk behind us for the warding of the Dale. So, son, the risk whereof thou speakest groweth the lesser the longer it is looked on.”

Then spake the Dale-warden: “Yet saving your wisdom, Alderman, the risk is there yet. For if these felons come into the Dale at all, even if the folk left behind hold the Burg and keep themselves unmurdered, yet may they not hinder the foe from spoiling our homesteads; so that our folk coming back in triumph shall find ruin at home, and spend weary days in hunting their foemen, who shall, many of them, escape into the Wildwood.”

“Yea,” said the Sun-beam, “sooth is that; and Face-of-god is wise to think of it and of other matters. Yet one thing we must bear in mind, that all may not go smoothly in our day’s work in Silverdale; so we must have force there to fall back on, in case we miss our stroke at first. Therefore, I say, send we no man to Rosedale, and leave we no able man-at-arms behind in the Burg, so that we have with us every blade that may be gathered.”

Iron-face smiled and said: “Thou art wise, damsel; and I marvel that so fair-fashioned a thing as thou can think so hardly of the meeting of the fallow blades. But hearken! will not the Dusky Men hear that we have stripped the Dale of fighting-men, and may they not then give our host the go-by and send folk to ruin us?”

===Chinese===
他说完便不再言语。日光双目熠熠、微启朱唇，凝视着他，急切地盼望听民强怎样回答。民强沉默了一会儿，用手指敲着桌面，旁人也都一言不发。终于他开口道：

"堡谷的战首，你方才所说的一字一句我都赞同，事情也理当如此办理；唯独分兵一部去攻玫瑰谷那一条，我不能依。我说不可；让我们把全部力量都集中在进攻银谷那一击上，那么若失败我们固然全盘皆输——可无论如何我们败了便是全盘皆输；但只要我们拿下银谷，玫瑰谷自然便敞开在我们面前了。"

面神道："兄弟，你是久经战阵之人，我不过是个后生：可你难道看不见这一层——无论我们怎样做，单凭一击都不可能将银谷的黝暗人尽数诛灭，那些在我们面前逃脱的，必将逃往玫瑰谷，把原委和盘托出，那时他们在杀了手下那些可怜人中所要杀的之后，谁能阻挡他们转而进犯堡谷呢（既然他们离此不远）？"

民强道："我不是说没有这个风险，但打仗就不能不冒这种风险，宁可尽付一掷，也不能叫我们攻银谷那一击落得轻飘。因为我们人少；倘若敌人有闲暇想起这一层，那我们便全都完了。"

石面道："依我看来，战首，暂且将玫瑰谷搁置不理，并无多少可怕之处；因为那些人若逃往玫瑰谷，我们大可紧紧追赶，到得也不比他们迟多久——赶在他们调动兵马之前；而且败局既定之后，我们尽可由幽谷（Shadowy Vale）这条路派兵回堡谷。我以为此事上民强所言有理。"

长老道："我亦如此说；况且，我们事后还可留下更多人马守卫山谷。所以，儿啊，你所言的风险，越琢磨便越小。"

谷卫道："长老，恕我直言，纵然您智虑过人，风险仍在。因为那些恶徒一旦进入谷中，纵然留下的人守住此堡、保住性命，却也无法阻挡敌人劫掠我们的家宅；于是我们凯旋之师归来，看见的便是满目疮痍，还要花上许多劳顿的日子去搜剿敌人，而其中不少人必将逃入野林（the Wildwood）。"

日光道："此言不虚；面神虑及此节及其他种种，很是明达。然而有一件事我们须铭记在心：我们在银谷那一日之事未必尽皆顺遂；所以我们手边必须留有可作退步的兵力，以防头一击失手。因此我说，我们一兵一卒也不派往玫瑰谷，堡中也莫留一个能战之兵，好叫我们身边聚集起所有能召集的刀剑。"

铁面微笑道："姑娘，你真聪明；我奇怪像你这般标致的人儿，竟对刀剑相交之事这般不喜。且听我说！黝暗人若听说我们抽空了谷中的战兵，难道不会绕开我们的大军，派人前来糟蹋我们么？"

===Original===
There was silence while Face-of-god looked down on the board; but presently he lifted up his face and said:

“Folk-might was right when he said that all must be risked. Let us leave Rosedale till we have overcome them of Silverdale. Moreover, my father, thou must not deem of these felons as if they were of like wits to us, to forecast the deeds to come, and weigh the chances nicely, and unravel tangled clues. Rather they move like to the stares in autumn, or the winter wild-geese, and will all be thrust forward by some sting that entereth into their imaginations. Therefore, if they have appointed one moon to wear before they fall upon us, they will not stir till then, and we have time enough to do what must be done. Wherefore am I now of one mind with the rest of you. Now meseemeth it were well that these things which we have spoken here, and shall speak, should not be noised abroad openly; nay, at the Folk-mote it would be well that nought be said about the day or the way of our onslaught on Silverdale, lest the foe take warning and be on their guard. Though, sooth to say, did I deem that if they had word of our intent they of Rosedale would join themselves to them of Silverdale, and that we should thus have all our foes in one net, then were I fain if the word would reach them. For my soul loathes the hunting that shall befall up and down the wood for the slaying of a man here, and two or three there, and the wearing of the days in wandering up and down with weapons in the hand, and the spinning out of hatred and delaying of peace.”

===Chinese===
厅中一时沉寂，面神低头望着桌面；但不久他抬起头来，说道：

"民强说得对，必须尽付一掷。我们先拿下银谷，再理会玫瑰谷。再者，我的父亲，你们切莫把这些恶徒看得与我们一般有智谋，能预断将来之事、细细权衡得失、理清纷乱之丝。他们的行止，倒像秋日的椋鸟、冬日的野雁，受着某种钻进他们心头的刺所驱使，一齐蜂拥向前。所以，他们若定下一个月份之期才来进攻，到那时才会动身，我们便有充裕的时间办该办之事。因此，我如今与诸位所见相同。我以为我们在此处所谈之事、将谈之事，不宜在外面张扬出去；不，在民众大会上，对进攻银谷的日期和路径，最好只字不提，免得敌人闻风戒备。不过说句实话，倘若我以为只要玫瑰谷之敌得知我们的图谋，便会与银谷之敌合兵一处、让我们将所有敌人一网打尽，那我倒巴不得这消息传到他们耳中。因为我心底里厌恶那种在林中四处搜剿的打法——此处杀一人，彼处杀两三人——又厌恶手执兵刃在山林间终日跋涉、把仇恨拖延日久、迟迟不能太平。"

===Original===
Then Iron-face reached his hand across the board and took his son’s hand, and said:

“Hail to thee, son, for thy word! Herein thou speakest as if from my very soul, and fain am I of such a War-leader.”

And desire drew the eyes of the Sun-beam to Face-of-god, and she beheld him proudly. But he said:

“All hath been spoken that the others of us may speak; and now it falleth to the part of Folk-might to order our goings for the tryst for the onslaught, and the trysting-place shall be in Shadowy Vale. How sayest thou, Chief of the Wolf?”

Said Folk-might: “I have little to say; and it is for the War-leader to see to this closely and piecemeal. I deem, as we all deem, that there should be no delay; yet were it best to wend not all together to Shadowy Vale, but in divers bands, as soon as ye may after the Folk-mote, by the sure and nigh ways that we shall show you. And when we are gathered there, short is the rede, for all is ready there to wend by the passes which we know throughly, and whereby it is but two days’ journey to the head of Silverdale, nigh to the caves of the silver, where the felons dwell the thickest.”

He set his teeth, and his colour came and went: for as constantly as the onslaught had been in his mind, yet whenever he spake of the great day of battle, hope and joy and anger wrought a tumult in his soul; and now that it was so nigh withal, he could not refrain his joy.

But he spake again: “Now therefore, War-leader, it is for thee to order the goings of thy folk. But I will tell thee that they shall not need to take aught with them save their weapons and victual for the way, that is, for thirty hours; because all is ready for them in Shadowy Vale, though it be but a poor place as to victual. Canst thou tell us, therefore, what thou wilt do?”

===Chinese===
铁面伸手越过桌面，握住他儿子的手，说道：

"儿啊，你这番话真该喝彩！你这几句话简直像是从我心底里说出来的，有这样的战首，我心里好生欢喜。"

日光的眼波含情，禁不住望向面神，骄傲地打量着他。他却说：

"我们几人该说的话都已说完；如今轮到民强来安排我们进兵约会之事了，约会之地定在幽谷。狼族之长，你以为如何？"

民强道："我无可多说；此事须由战首亲自逐一仔细督办。我正如大家一样以为：事不宜迟；然而最好莫要一齐开往幽谷，而要分作数队，在民众大会之后尽早启程，走我们将指给你们的那几条稳妥近便之路。待到我们在那里聚齐，方略十分简短：一切都已备妥，只等沿我们烂熟于胸的几处隘口进兵，由那些隘口走到银谷之头，不过两日路程，那里靠近银矿之洞，正是恶徒聚居最密之处。"

他咬紧牙关，脸上血色忽红忽白：因为这场进攻虽然时刻萦绕在他心头，可每当他谈起那大战之日，希望、欢喜与愤怒便在他灵魂中掀起一阵翻腾；如今这事又近在眼前，他按捺不住心头的欢喜。

他又说道："所以如今，战首，安排你本族人马的行止，全在于你。但我告诉你，他们除了兵器和路上的口粮——也就是三十个钟头的口粮——之外，什么都不必带；因为幽谷之中一切都已为他们备齐，虽然那地方粮食不算丰足。那么，你能告诉我们你打算怎样办么？"

===Original===
Face-of-god had knit his brows and become gloomy of countenance; but now his face cleared, and he set his hand to his pouch, and drew forth a written parchment, and said:

“This is the order whereof I have bethought me. Before the Folk-mote I and the Wardens shall speak to the leaders of hundreds, who be mostly here at the Fair, and give them the day and the hour whereon they shall, each hundred, take their weapons and wend to Shadowy Vale, and also the place where they shall meet the men of yours who shall lead them across the Waste. These hundred-leaders shall then go straightway and give the word to the captains of scores, and the captains of scores to the captains of tens; and if, as is scarce doubtful, the Folk-mote yea-says the onslaught and the fellowship with you of the Wolf, then shall those leaders of tens bring their men to the trysting-place, and so go their ways to Shadowy Vale. Now here I have the roll of our Weapon-show, and I will look to it that none shall be passed over; and if ye ask me in what order they had best get on the way, my rede is that a two hundred should depart on the very evening of the day of the Folk-mote, and these to be of our folk of the Upper Dale; and on the morning of the morrow of the Folk-mote another two hundreds from the Dale; and in the evening of the same day the folk of the Shepherds, three hundreds or more, and that will be easy to them; again on the next day two more bands of the Lower Dale, one in the morning, one in the evening. Lastly, in the earliest dawn of the third day from the Folk-mote shall the Woodlanders wend their ways. But one hundred of men let us leave behind for the warding of the Burg, even as we agreed before. As for the place of tryst for the faring over the Waste, let it be the end of the knolls just by the jaws of the pass yonder, where the Weltering Water comes into the Dale from the East. How say ye?”

===Chinese===
面神一直皱着眉头，面色阴沉；这时他脸上云开雾散，伸手入囊，抽出一张写着字的羊皮纸来，说道：

"这便是我想出的部署。在民众大会之前，我与守事们（the Wardens）要先对百长（leaders of hundreds）们传话——他们大多已在此市集（the Fair）上——把每个百人队各自启程、带上兵器、开赴幽谷的日期和时辰告知他们，并告知他们与你方接引之人相遇的地点，由那些人领他们过大荒原（the Waste）。这些百长随后便径直去通知廿长（captains of scores），廿长再通知十长（captains of tens）；如果——这一点几乎无可疑——民众大会通过进攻之举及与你们狼族结盟之事，那么那些十长便率领本队人马前往约会之地，由此上路去幽谷。如今我这儿有我们武器大阅的名册，我会逐一核对，不使一人遗漏；你们若问我他们以何顺序启程最为相宜，我的主意是：在民众大会正日的傍晚，便有两百人启程，这两百人出自我们上谷（the Upper Dale）之人；在民众大会之次日清晨，再有两百人自谷中出发；同日傍晚，牧羊之民出发，三百人乃至更多，这事于他们甚是便当；再下一日，下谷（the Lower Dale）又分两队启程，一队在清晨，一队在傍晚。最后，在民众大会之后第三日最早的黎明时分，林中汉子启程。但我们要留下百人守堡，正如我们先前所议。至于过大荒原的约会之地，就定在那边隘口之口、丘陵尽处，翻滚河自东流入谷的地方。你们以为如何？"

===Original===
They all said, and Folk-might especially, that it was right well devised, and that thus it should be done.

Then turned Face-of-god to the Dale-warden, and said:

“It were good, brother, that we saw the other wardens as soon as may be, to do them to wit of this order, and what they have to do.”

Therewith he arose and took the Elder of the Dale-wardens away with him, and the twain set about their business straightway. Neither did the others abide long in the Hall, but went out into the Burg to see the chapmen and their wares. There the Alderman bought what he needed of iron and steel and other matters; and Folk-might cheapened him a dagger curiously wrought, and a web of gold and silk for the Sun-beam, for which wares he paid in silver arm-rings, new-wrought and of strange fashion.

But amidst of the chaffer was now a great ring of men; and in the midst of the ring stood Redesman, fiddle and bow in hand, and with him were four damsels wondrously arrayed; for the first was clad in a smock so craftily wrought with threads of green and many colours, that it seemed like a piece of the green field beset with primroses and cowslips and harebells and windflowers, rather than a garment woven and sewn; and in her hand she bore a naked sword, with golden hilts and gleaming blade. But the second bore on her roses done in like manner, both blossoms and green leaves, wherewith her body was covered decently, which else had been naked. The third was clad as though she were wading the wheat-field to the waist, and above was wrapped in the leaves and bunches of the wine-tree. And the fourth was clad in a scarlet gown flecked with white wool to set forth the winter’s snow, and broidered over with the burning brands of the Holy Hearth; and she bore on her head a garland of mistletoe. And these four damsels were clearly seen to image the four seasons of the year—Spring, Summer, Autumn, and Winter. But amidst them stood a fountain or conduit of gilded work cunningly wrought, and full of the best wine of the Dale, and gilded cups and beakers hung about it.

===Chinese===
众人都说——民强尤其如此——此计安排得十分妥当，便当照此办理。

面神转向谷卫，说道：

"兄弟，我们最好尽快见一见其余各位谷卫，把这部署告诉他们，让他们知道自己该做什么。"

说罢他站起身来，带着谷卫之长一同离席而去，两人立刻着手办理此事。其余众人也未在厅中久留，纷纷出到堡中去看那些客商与他们的货物。长老在那里买下他所需要的铁、钢及其他物品；民强为日光讨价还价，买下一柄花纹精巧的匕首、一匹金银丝线的锦缎，这些货物他都付以新打的花样奇特的银臂环。

正在这买卖喧阗之际，众人围成了一个大圈；圈中站着雷德斯曼（Redesman），手持提琴与琴弓，与他同在一起的还有四位装束奇异的少女：第一个少女身上穿着一件以绿色及诸色丝线精巧织成的衫子，看似一片绿草地，上缀樱草、莲香花、风铃草与银莲花，倒不像是一件缝制出来的衣裳；她手中擎着一口出鞘之剑，剑柄镏金，剑刃生辉。第二个少女身上以同样手法缀满玫瑰——花朵与绿叶俱全——恰将其身躯遮掩得合乎体统，否则便要赤身露体了。第三个少女装束得仿佛正没入麦田及腰，腰以上则披裹着葡萄藤的叶与串。第四个少女则穿一件缀以白羊毛的猩红长袍，以喻冬日之雪，袍上又绣着圣灶（the Holy Hearth）熊熊燃烧的薪柴；她头上戴着一顶槲寄生编的花冠。这四位少女显然象征着一年四时——春、夏、秋、冬。她们中间立着一座精工镏金的喷泉，注满了谷中最好的美酒，四下悬着镏金的杯盏。

===Original===
So now Redesman fell to caressing his fiddle with the bow till it began to make sweet music, and therewith the hearts of all danced with it; and presently words come into his mouth, and he fell to singing; and the damsels answered him:

> Earth-wielders, that fashion the Dale-dwellers’ treasure,
> Soft are ye by seeming, yet hardy of heart!
> No warrior amongst us withstandeth your pleasure;
> No man from his meadow may thrust you apart.
>
> Fresh and fair are your bodies, but far beyond telling
> Are the years of your lives, and the craft ye have stored.
> Come give us a word, then, concerning our dwelling,
> And the days to befall us, the fruit of the sword.

===Chinese===
当下雷德斯曼便以琴弓抚琴，直拉得琴上发出悠扬乐音，众人的心都随之翩跃；不久歌词自他口中涌出，他便唱了起来；众少女齐声相和：

> 主掌大地之神，化育谷中之珍，
> 尔貌虽柔婉，尔心实刚强！
> 我辈甲士，无由逆尔之意；
> 草野之人，无能逐尔离场。
>
> 尔形鲜妍，然尔寿数、
> 尔所积之巧智，非言可尽。
> 且赐一言，论此居止，
> 论将临之日——刀剑之果。

===Original===
Therewith the throng opened, and a young man stepped lightly into the ring, clad in very fair armour, with a gilded helm on his head; and he took the sword from the hand of the Maiden of Spring, and waved it in the air till the westering sun flashed back from it. Then each of the four damsels went up to the swain and kissed his mouth; and Redesman drew the bow across the strings, and the four damsels sang together, standing round about the young warrior:

> It was but a while since for earth’s sake we trembled,
> Lest the increase our life-days had won for the Dale,
> All the wealth that the moons and the years had assembled,
> Should be but a mock for the days of your bale.
>
> But now we behold the sun smite on the token
> In the hand of the Champion, the heart of a man;
> We look down the long years and see them unbroken;
> Forth fareth the Folk by the ways it began.
>
> So bid ye these chapmen in autumn returning,
> To bring iron for ploughshares and steel for the scythe,
> And the oversea oil that hath felt the sun’s burning,
> And fair webs for your women soft-spoken and blithe;
>
> And pledge ye your word in the market to meet them,
> As many a man and as many a maid,
> As eager as ever, as guest-fain to greet them,
> And bide till the booth from the wagon is made.
>
> Come, guests of our lovers! for we, the year-wielders,
> Bid each man and all to come hither and take
> A cup from our hands midst the peace of our shielders,
> And drink to the days of the Dale that we make.

===Chinese===
话音方落，人群让开一条路，一个年轻男子轻盈地步入圈中，身披精良甲胄，头戴鎏金之盔；他从春之少女（the Maiden of Spring）手中取过那口剑，向空中挥舞，直挥到西斜的日头自剑身返照出光芒。然后四位少女一一走向那青年，吻了他的嘴；雷德斯曼运弓过弦，四位少女环绕着那年轻武士齐声唱道：

> 不久之前，我等尚为大地之故战栗，
> 恐我等有生之年为谷中赢得之丰饶、
> 众月众岁所积聚之赀财，
> 将沦为尔等祸日之笑柄。
>
> 然今我等见日光照临那徽记——
> 徽记在壮士之手，壮士有男儿之心；
> 我等纵目遥年，见其绵绵不绝；
> 族人循其初行之道，奋然而前。
>
> 故尔等当嘱这些客商秋日重来，
> 携来制犁之铁、制镰之钢，
> 与那越海之油——曾受烈日之炙——
> 并为尔等柔声欢颜之妇人，携来美锦；
>
> 且在市中许下重约，必与之再会，
> 男男女女，熙熙而来，
> 依旧殷勤，依旧热中迎客，
> 直候到车上之棚搭就。
>
> 来吧，敬我者之客！因我等——执掌岁时者——
> 邀每位、邀众人，咸来此处，
> 于我等护卫之太平中，从我等手中
> 接过一盏，为我等所造之谷中岁月而饮。

===Original===
Then went the damsels to that wine-fountain, and drew thence cups of the best and brightest wine of the Dale, and went round about the ring, and gave drink to whomsoever would, both of the chapmen and the others; while the weaponed youth stood in the midst bearing aloft his sword and shield like an image in a holy place, and Redesman’s bow still went up and down the strings, and drew forth a sweet and merry tune.

Great game it was now to see the stark Burgdale carles dragging the Men of the Plain, little loth, up to the front of the ring, that they might stretch out their hands for a cup, and how many a one, as he took it, took as much as he might of the damsel’s hand withal. As for the damsels, they played the Holy Play very daintily, neither reddening nor laughing, but faring so solemnly, and withal so sweetly and bright-faced, that it might well have been deemed that they were in very sooth Maidens of the God of Earth sent from the ever-enduring Hall to cheer the hearts of men.

So simply and blithely did the Men of Burgdale disport them after the manner of their fathers, trusting in their valour and beholding the good days to be.

===Chinese===
于是众少女走向那座酒泉，从其中舀出谷中最好最澄澈的美酒，绕行一圈，凡愿饮者皆赐一杯——无论客商还是本地之人；那披甲青年立于中央，高举剑与盾，俨然如圣地之中的一尊造像；雷德斯曼的琴弓仍在弦上起伏，奏出一支甜美欢快的曲调。

只见那些壮健的堡谷汉子拖着那些平原人（Men of the Plain）——他们倒也半推半就——拉到圈前，好让他们伸手接一杯；许多人接过杯之时，恨不得连那少女的手也一并多握一会儿。至于众少女，她们把这出圣剧（the Holy Play）演得极为端庄，既不脸红，也不发笑，举止如此庄重，却又如此甜美、容光焕发，让人简直要以为她们当真是地神（the God of Earth）座下、从那永恒之殿（the ever-enduring Hall）遣来抚慰人心的神女。

堡谷之民便这般质朴欢畅地效法祖辈之行乐，自负其勇，瞻望来日之美。

===Original===
So wore the evening, and when night was come, men feasted throughout the Burg from house to house, and every hall was full. But the Guests from Shadowy Vale feasted in the Hall of the Face in all glee and goodwill; and with them were the chief of the chapmen and two others; but the rest of them had been laid hold of by goodmen of the Burg, and dragged into their feast-halls, for they were fain of those guests and their tales. One of the chapmen in the House of the Face knew Folk-might, and hailed him by the name he had borne in the Cities, Regulus to wit; indeed, the chief chapman knew him, and even somewhat over-well, for he had been held to ransom by Folk-might in those past days, and even yet feared him, because he, the chapman, had played somewhat of a dastard’s part to him. But the other was an openhearted and merry fellow, and no weakling; and Folk-might was fain of his talk concerning times bygone, and the fields they had foughten in, and other adventures that had befallen them, both good and evil.

===Chinese===
暮色渐深，及至夜来，堡中家家户户皆设宴庆贺，座无虚席。而从幽谷来的客人们在面神之宅的厅堂里欢宴，情谊殷殷，和乐融融；与他们同席的有客商首领及另外两人；其余的客人早被堡中的好客主人拉去自家宴厅，因为那些主人都爱这些客人、爱听他们讲故事。面神之宅里有一位客商认得民强，以他当年在平原诸城（the Cities）所用之名"雷古拉斯（Regulus）"相呼；其实那位客商首领也认得他，而且认得太熟了——因为从前他曾被民强掳去勒索赎金，至今仍怕他，缘由是那客商当年曾对民强干过一件颇为怯懦的事。另一位却是个心胸豁达、性情开朗之人，也并非等闲之辈；民强很爱听他谈往事、谈从前他们厮杀过的战场，以及他们所经历的种种或吉或凶的奇遇。

===Original===
As for Face-of-god, he went about the Hall soberly, and spake no more than behoved him, so as not to seem a mar-feast; for the image of the slaughter to be yet abode with him, and his heart foreboded the after-grief of the battle. He had no speech with the Sun-beam till men were sundering after the feast, and then he came close to her amidst of the turmoil, and said:

“Time presses on me these days; but if thou wouldest speak with me tomorrow as I would with thee, then mightest thou go on the Bridge of the Burg about sunrise, and I will be there, and we two only.”

Her face, which had been somewhat sad that evening (for she had been watching his), brightened at that word, and she took his hand as folk came thronging round about them, and said:

“Yea, friend, I shall be there, and fain of thee.” And therewithal they sundered for that night.

And all men went to sleep throughout the Burg: howbeit they set a watch at the Burg-Gate; and Hall-face, when he was coming back from the woodland ward about sunset, fell in with Red-coat of Waterless and four score men on the Portway coming to meet him and take his place. All which was clean contrary to the wont of the Burgdalers, who at most whiles held no watch and ward, not even in Fair-time.

===Chinese===
至于面神，他在厅中持重周旋，言语不过分寸所必需，免得扫人之兴；因为那场尚未到来的屠杀之象仍盘踞在他心头，他的心预感到战后将随之而来的哀痛。直到宴罢众人将散之时，他才与日光说上话——他在纷扰之中凑近她身边，说道：

"这几日我俗务缠身；但你若愿意明日与我相语——如我之愿与你相语一般——你可在日出时分到堡桥（the Bridge of the Burg）上去，我会到那里，只我们两人。"

她那晚上本来神色有些黯然（因为她一直在留神看他的脸色），听了这话顿生光采，在众人涌上来围住他们之时，她握住他的手，说道：

"好，朋友，我会去的，与你相见我心甚喜。"于是当夜二人就此作别。

于是堡中人人安寝：不过他们在堡门（the Burg-Gate）设了岗哨；厅面（Hall-face）日落时分从林地哨岗回来时，在港路（the Portway）上遇见了无水地（Waterless）的红衣（Red-coat），带着八十人来接替他的防务。这一切全然不合堡谷人的旧习——他们平日里多半不设岗不放哨，连市集之时也不例外。

## LI The Dead Borne to Bale: The Mote-House Re-Hallowed / 五十一 亡者舁至柴堆：议事厅重行圣化

===Original===
On the morrow they bore to bale their slain men, and there withal what was left of the bodies of the four chieftains of the Great Undoing. They brought them into a most fair meadow to the west of Silverstead, where they had piled up a very great bale for the burning. In that meadow was the Doom-ring and Thingstead of the Folk of the Wolf, and they had hallowed it when they had first conquered Silverdale, and it was deemed far holier than the Mote-house aforesaid, wherein the men of the kindred might hold no due court; but rather it was a Feast-hall, and a house where men had converse together, and wherein precious things and tokens of the Fathers were stored up.

===Chinese===
次日，他们将其阵亡之人舁至柴堆，并将大覆灭（the Great Undoing）中四位酋长遗体所余之残骸，一并付诸焚化。他们将遗体舁至银镇（Silverstead）以西一片极美之草甸，在那里早已垛起一座极大之柴堆，以供焚化。此草甸之中有狼族（the Folk of the Wolf）之判决环（the Doom-ring）与议事场（Thingstead），乃他们初征服银谷（Silverdale）之时即已祝圣之地；世人视此地为远较前述议事厅（the Mote-house）更为神圣——盖宗族之人于彼厅之中不得举行正式之裁断；彼处实乃一宴厅（Feast-hall），为众人相聚交谈之所，亦为珍藏贵重之物及列祖遗物之处。

===Original===
The Thingstead in the meadow was flowery and well-grassed, and a little stream winding about thereby nearly cast a ring around it; and beyond the stream was a full fair grove of oak-trees, very tall and ancient. There then they burned the dead of the Host, wrapped about in exceeding fair raiment. And when the ashes were gathered, the men of Burgdale and the Shepherds left those of their folk for the kindred to bury there in Silverdale; for they said that they had a right to claim such guesting for them that had helped to win back the Dale.

===Chinese===
草甸之中这一方议事场，繁花铺地、青草丰美，一道细溪蜿蜒其间，几乎绕成一环；溪流彼岸有一片极美之柞树林，极其高大古老。他们便在那里焚化大军之阵亡者，遗骸皆裹以极其华美之衣裳。待骨灰收聚既毕，堡谷（Burgdale）之人与牧羊之民（the Shepherds）将其本族阵亡者留下，托宗族在银谷就地安葬；因为他们说，那些助其夺回此谷之人，有权求得这般客葬之礼。

===Original===
But when the Burning was done and the bale quenched, and the ashes gathered and buried (and that was on the morrow), then men bore forth the Banners of the Jaws of the Wolf, and the Red Hand, and the Silver Arm, and the Golden Bushel, and the Ragged Sword, and the Wolf of the Woodland; and with great joy and triumph they brought them into the Mote-house and hung them up over the dais; and they kindled fire on the Holy Hearth by holding up a disk of bright glass to the sun; and then they sang before the banners. And this is somewhat of the song that they sang before them:

> Why are ye wending? O whence and whither?
 
 What shineth over the fallow swords?
 
 What is the joy that ye bear in hither?
 
 What is the tale of your blended words?
> No whither we wend, but here have we stayed us,
 
 Here by the ancient Holy Hearth;
 
 Long have the moons and the years delayed us,
 
 But here are we come from the heart of the dearth.
> We are the men of joy belated;
 
 We are the wanderers over the waste;
 
 We are but they that sat and waited,
 
 Watching the empty winds make haste.
> Long, long we sat and knew no others,
 
 Save alien folk and the foes of the road;
 
 Till late and at last we met our brothers,
 
 And needs must we to the old abode.
> For once on a day they prayed for guesting;
 
 And how were we then their bede to do?
 
 Wild was the waste for the people’s resting,
 
 And deep the wealth of the Dale we knew.
> Here were the boards that we must spread them
 
 Down in the fruitful Dale and dear;
 
 Here were the halls where we would bed them:
 
 And how should we tarry otherwhere?
> Over the waste we came together:
 
 There was the tangle athwart the way;
 
 There was the windstorm and the weather;
 
 The red rain darkened down the day.
> But that day of the days what grief should let us,
 
 When we saw through the clouds the dale-glad sun?
 
 We tore at the tangle that beset us,
 
 And stood at peace when the day was done.
> Hall of the Happy, take our greeting!
 
 Bid thou the Fathers come and see
 
 The Folk-signs on thy walls a-meeting,
 
 And deem today what men we be.
> Look on the Holy Hearth new-litten,
 
 How the sparks fly twinkling up aloof!
 
 How the wavering smoke by the sunlight smitten,
 
 Curls up around the beam-rich roof!
> For here once more is the Wolf abiding,
 
 Nor ever more from the Dale shall wend,
 
 And never again his head be hiding,
 
 Till all days be dark and the world have end.

===Chinese===
焚化既毕、柴堆熄灭，骨灰收聚安葬（此乃又次日之事），众人乃请出诸旗：狼之颚（the Jaws of the Wolf）、红手（the Red Hand）、银臂（the Silver Arm）、金斛（the Golden Bushel）、破锋剑（the Ragged Sword）、林中之狼（the Wolf of the Woodland）；他们满怀极大之喜悦与凯旋，将诸旗舁入议事厅，悬于高堂之上；又举一块明亮之玻璃圆盘对准太阳，于圣灶（the Holy Hearth）之上借日光以点燃火种；随后便在诸旗之前高歌。下面便是他们在诸旗之前所唱之歌的一部分：

> 尔等去向何方？自何处来，向何处去？
 
 闲置之剑上，有何光华闪烁？
 
 尔等怀中，携来何种欢欣？
 
 尔等交错之言，述何故事？
> 吾等不向他适，已驻足于此，
 
 此地，古老圣灶之旁；
 
 月月年年，久羁吾等之步履，
 
 然吾等今已自荒歉之渊而来归。
> 吾等乃迟来之喜乐之民；
 
 吾等乃荒原之上之漂泊者；
 
 吾等不过是枯坐等待之人，
 
 目送空寂之长风匆匆而过。
> 久矣、久矣，吾等枯坐，不识他人，
 
 唯见异族之民与道路之寇仇；
 
 直至迟迟、终见吾等之兄弟，
 
 吾等遂不得不归于旧日之居。
> 因一日，他们乞求留宿款待；
 
 吾等当时如何能不应其所请？
 
 荒原之于斯民歇息，实属过于荒凉，
 
 而此谷之富庶，吾等又深谙于心。
> 此处便是吾等须为他们铺设宴席之地，
 
 在下方丰饶可爱之谷中；
 
 此处便是吾等愿为他们安置卧处之厅：
 
 吾等又怎会在他处逗留？
> 吾等一同越过荒原而来：
 
 路上有荆棘丛莽横阻；
 
 又有狂风骤雨、风霜雪雹；
 
 血红的雨使白昼为之黯淡。
> 然在那诸日之一日，有何忧患能阻吾等，
 
 当吾等透过云隙，见到令此谷欢欣之日轮？
 
 吾等撕裂围困吾等之荆棘丛莽，
 
 至日暮之时，安然伫立。
> 幸福者之厅啊，请受吾等之礼敬！
 
 请你召列祖列宗前来观看
 
 厅墙之上氏族之徽会聚一堂，
 
 且看今日吾等为何等之人。
> 且看那新燃之圣灶，
 
 火星闪烁，飞升得何其高远！
 
 那摇曳之烟为日光所映照，
 
 袅袅盘绕于密梁之屋顶！
> 因狼族再度安居于此，
 
 永不再从此谷远去，
 
 再不至垂首藏头，
 
 直至诸日皆暗、天地终穷。

## XXVI The Ending of the Gate-Thing / 二十六 门会之终

===Original===
But just as the Alderman was on the point of rising to declare the breaking-up of the Thing, there came a stir in the throng and it opened, and a warrior came forth into the innermost of the ring of men, arrayed in goodly glittering War-gear; clad in such wise that a tunicle of precious gold-wrought web covered the hauberk all but the sleeves thereof, and the hem of it beset with blue mountain-stones smote against the ankles and well-nigh touched the feet, shod with sandals gold-embroidered and gemmed. This warrior bore a goodly gilded helm on the head, and held in hand a spear with gold-garlanded shaft, and was girt with a sword whose hilts and scabbard both were adorned with gold and gems: beardless, smooth-cheeked, exceeding fair of face was the warrior, but pale and somewhat haggard-eyed: and those who were nearby beheld and wondered; for they saw that there was come the Bride arrayed for war and battle, as if she were a messenger from the House of the Gods, and the Burg that endureth forever.

===Chinese===
然正当长老欲起身宣告议事会散会之际，人群中忽起一阵骚动，人墙随之分开；只见一名武士步入人群最内圈，一身华美耀目之战甲：外罩一件以金线织就的珍贵锦袍，将锁子甲遮得严严实实，唯余两袖外露；锦袍下摆缀满蓝色山间宝石，拂及足踝，几乎垂落至足——双足趿着金绣嵌宝之凉履。此武士头戴镀金之华美头盔，手执一杆金花缠柄之长矛，腰间佩着一口剑，剑柄剑鞘皆以黄金宝石为饰：其人无须、面颊光洁、容貌极美，却面色苍白、双目略显憔悴：近处之人见了皆诧异不已；因为他们看出，来的正是新娘——她披挂上阵，一身战时装束，仿佛是从众神之殿、那永存不灭之堡中派来的使者。

===Original===
Then she fell to speech in a voice which at first was somewhat hoarse and broken, but cleared as she went on, and she said:

“There sittest thou, O Alderman of Burgdale! Is Face-of-god thy son anywhere nigh, so that he can hear me?”

===Chinese===
随后她开口说话；起初声音有些嘶哑断续，说着说着便渐渐清朗，她说道：

"堡谷的长老啊，你坐在那里！你的儿子面神可在近处，能不能听得见我说话？"

===Original===
But Iron-face wondered at her word, and said: “He is beside thee, as he should be.” For indeed Face-of-god was touching her, shoulder to shoulder. But she looked not to the right hand nor the left, but said:

“Hearken, Iron-face! Chief of the House of the Face, Alderman of the Dale, and ye also, neighbours and goodmen of the Dale: I am a woman called the Bride, of the House of the Steer, and ye have heard that I have plighted my troth to Face-of-god to wed with him, to love him, and lie in his bed. But it is not so: we are not troth-plight; nor will I wed with him, nor any other, but will wend with you to the war, and play my part therein according to what might is in me; nor will I be worser than the wives of Shadowy Vale.”

===Chinese===
铁面听了她这话甚是诧异，说道："他就在你身边，理当如此。"原来面神果真紧挨着她，肩并着肩。可她既不左顾、也不右盼，只是说道：

"铁面听好！面神之宅之长、本谷之长老，还有你们——谷中的诸位邻里、当家汉子们：我是一名女子，人称新娘，出于犍牛族；你们风闻我已将终身许给面神，要与他成婚、爱他、与他同床共枕。然而并非如此：我们并未互许婚约；我也不愿嫁他，更不愿嫁与任何他人——我只愿随你们一同出征，凭我胸中所有之力，在战阵中尽我一份职责；我绝不愿落于幽谷诸妇之后。"

===Original===
Face-of-god heard her words with no change of countenance; but Iron-face reddened over all his face, and stared at her, and knit his brows and said:

“Maiden, what are these words? What have we done to thee? Have I not been to thee as a father, and loved thee dearly? Is not my son goodly and manly and deft in arms? Hath it not ever been the wont of the House of the Face to wed in the House of the Steer? and in these two Houses there hath never yet been a goodlier man and a lovelier maiden than are ye two. What have we done then?”

“Ye have done nought against me,” she said, “and all that thou sayest is sooth; yet will I not wed with Face-of-god.”

===Chinese===
面神听了她这番话，面不改色；铁面却涨红了整张脸，直瞪着她，皱起眉头，说道：

"姑娘，这是说的什么话？我们做了什么对不起你的事？我待你岂不像父亲一般，疼爱你疼得不够么？我的儿子难道不英俊、不刚毅、不通武艺么？面神之宅与犍牛族通婚，难道不是历来就有的规矩么？这两族之中，还从未有过比你二人更出色的男子、更可爱的少女呢。那么我们到底做了什么？"

"你们并未做过什么对不起我的事，"她说道，"你方才所说的句句属实；然而我仍不嫁给面神。"

===Original===
Yet fiercer waxed the face of the Alderman, and he said in a loud voice:

“But how if I tell thee that I will speak with thy kindred of the Steer, and thou shalt do after my bidding whether thou wilt or whether thou wilt not?”

“And how will ye compel me thereto?” she said. “Are there thralls in the Dale? Or will ye make me an outlaw? Who shall heed it? Or I shall betake me to Shadowy Vale and become one of their warrior-maidens.”

===Chinese===
长老的面色却愈发严厉，他扬起声音说道：

"倘若我告诉你，我要去同你犍牛族的亲族们说一声，那么无论你愿意不愿意，都须照我的吩咐去做——你又待如何？"

"你们又要怎样强迫我呢？"她说道，"谷中难道有锁人的奴隶么？还是你们要宣布我为逐徒？谁又会理睬？大不了我投奔幽谷去，做她们那号女战士便是。"

===Original===
Now was the Alderman’s face changing from red to white, and belike he forgat the Thing, and what he was doing there, and he cried out:

“This is an evil day, and who shall help me? Thou, Face-of-god, what hast thou to say? Wilt thou let this woman go without a word? What hath bewitched thee?”

But never a word spake his son, but stood looking straight forward, cold and calm by seeming. Then turned Iron-face again to the Bride, and said in a softer voice:

“Tell me, maiden, whom I erst called daughter, what hath befallen, that thou wilt leave my son; thou who wert once so kind and loving to him; whose hand was always seeking his, whose eyes were ever following his; who wouldst go where he bade, and come when he called. What hath betid that ye have cast him out, and flee from our House?”

===Chinese===
此刻长老的面色由红转白，多半是把这场议事会、把自己身在何处都忘到脑后了，他叫喊道：

"这是什么倒霉的日子啊，谁来帮帮我？面神你啊，你可有话说？你就让这女子一言不发地走掉么？你是中了什么邪？"

可他的儿子半个字也不吐，只是直直地望向前方，神态冷淡平静。铁面便又转向新娘，放缓了声音说道：

"姑娘啊，我曾唤作女儿的姑娘，到底出了什么事，你竟要离开我的儿子？你从前对他是何等温存多情——你的手总要去寻他的手，你的眼总在追随着他；他让你去哪儿你便去哪儿，他一唤你你便应声而到。究竟发生了什么，竟使你们将他抛开、从我们家中逃离？"

===Original===
She flushed red beneath her helm and said:

“There is war in the land, and I have seen it coming, and that things shall change around us. I have looked about me and seen men happy and women content, and children weary for mere mirth and joy. And I have thought, in a day, or two days or three, all this shall be changed, and the women shall be, some anxious and wearied with waiting, some casting all hope away; and the men, some shall come back to the garth no more, and some shall come back maimed and useless, and there shall be loss of friends and fellows, and mirth departed, and dull days and empty hours, and the children wandering about marvelling at the sorrow of the house. All this I saw before me, and grief and pain and wounding and death; and I said: Shall I be any better than the worst of the folk that loveth me? Nay, this shall never be; and since I have learned to be deft with mine hands in all the play of war, and that I am as strong as many a man, and as hardy-hearted as any, I will give myself to the Warrior and the God of the Face; and the battlefield shall be my home, and the after-grief of the fight my banquet and holiday, that I may bear the burden of my people, in the battle and out of it; and know every sorrow that the Dale hath; and cast aside as a grievous and ugly thing the bed of the warrior that the maiden desires, and the toying of lips and hands and soft words of desire, and all the joy that dwelleth in the Castle of Love and the Garden thereof; while the world outside is sick and sorry, and the fields lie waste and the harvest burneth. Even so have I sworn, even so will I do.”

===Chinese===
她在头盔下红着脸说道：

"这土地上要有战事了，我已看见它逼近，看见我们周遭的一切都将改变。我环顾四周，看见男人们欢欢喜喜、女人们心满意足，孩子们则一心只盼着点欢笑嬉闹。我又想：再过一日、两日、三日，这一切都要变样——女人们，有的要忧心如焚、为等候熬尽了气力，有的要把一切指望都抛个干净；男人们呢，有的再也回不到这庭院里来，有的虽回来了，却折手断脚、成了废人；失去的，是朋友、是伙伴；远去的，是欢笑；接踵而来的，是灰闷的日子、空荡荡的时辰；孩子们在屋里院外游荡着，睁大眼睛奇怪这家中为何如此愁惨。这一切都浮现在我眼前，还有哀伤、疼痛、创伤与死亡；我对自己说：难道我该比爱我那族中最不济的人还要不如么？不，绝不可如此；既然我已学会一双巧手娴于战阵的种种功夫，既然我的气力不亚于许多男子、胆气不输于任何人，我便要将自己献与武神与面之神；战场便是我的家，战后之哀痛便是我的宴席、我的节庆——好叫我能为我族人担起重任，在战阵之内如此，在战阵之外亦然；好叫我能尽知这条山谷所承受的每一种苦；好叫我能把少女心心念念的那张武士之榻，把唇齿、手指间的狎昵、那些甜软的爱欲之辞，把爱情之堡与其花园中所寄寓的一切欢愉，都当作可厌丑陋之物抛在一旁——而此时外面的世界正病苦不堪、田地荒废、庄稼焚毁。我已如此立誓，便当如此去做。"

===Original===
Her eyes glittered and her cheek was flushed, and her voice was clear and ringing now; and when she ended there arose a murmur of praise from the men round about her. But Iron-face said coldly:

“These are great words; but I know not what they mean. If thou wilt to the field and fight among the carles (and that I would not naysay, for it hath oft been done and praised aforetime), why shouldest thou not go side by side with Face-of-god and as his plighted maiden?”

The light which the sweetness of speech had brought into her face had died out of it now, and she looked weary and hapless as she answered him slowly:

“I will not wed with Face-of-god, but will fare afield as a virgin of war, as I have sworn to the Warrior.”

===Chinese===
她双目炯炯、双颊飞红，嗓音此时也清越如铃；她话音刚落，周围众人便响起一阵称许的低语。铁面却冷冷地说道：

"这话气魄不小；可我听不懂是什么意思。你若是要上阵、与那些汉子们一同厮杀（这事我倒不拦你，从前也常有此事，为人称道），那你为何不能与面神并肩同行、作为他许下婚约的未婚妻去呢？"

那因言辞动人而浮上她面庞的光彩，此刻已经消逝；她面露疲色、神色无助，缓缓答道：

"我不嫁面神，我只作为立誓于武神的战阵处女，出征沙场。"

===Original===
Then waxed Iron-face exceeding wroth, and he rose up before all men and cried loudly and fiercely:

“There is some lie abroad, that windeth about us as the gossamers in the lanes of an autumn morning.”

And therewith he strode up to Face-of-god as though he had nought to do with the Thing; and he stood before him and cried out at him while all men wondered:

“Thou! what hast thou done to turn this maiden’s heart to stone? Who is it that is devising guile with thee to throw aside this worthy wedding in a worthy House, with whom our sons are ever wont to wed? Speak, tell the tale!”

===Chinese===
铁面闻言勃然大怒，当着众人之面站起身来，厉声高叫：

"此地必有什么谎言四下流传，如秋朝巷陌间的游丝一般缠绕着我们。"

说着他便大步走到面神跟前，仿佛早已把议事会的事丢开不管；他立在儿子面前，冲他大吼——众人尽皆惊愕：

"你！你做了什么，竟把这姑娘的心肠化作石头？是谁在和你一同设下诡计，要丢开这一门体面人家里的体面亲事——我们的儿郎历来都是与这族人通婚的！说，把事情讲出来！"

===Original===
But Face-of-god held his peace and stood calm and proud before all men.

Then the blood mounted to Iron-face’s head, and he forgat folk and kindred and the war to come, and he cried so that all the place rang with the words of his anger:

“Thou dastard! I see thee now; it is thou that hast done this, and not the maiden; and now thou hast made her bear a double burden, and set her on to speak for thee, whilst thou standest by saying nought, and wilt take no scruple’s weight of her shame upon thee!”

===Chinese===
面神却默然无语，当着众人从容矜持地立着。

铁面此时气血上涌、直冲脑门，把宗族亲党、把将至的战事一概丢在脑后，厉声大吼，整个议事场都回荡着他怒气冲冲的字句：

"你这个懦夫！我如今看清你了；做下这事的不是姑娘，正是你！如今你又逼她背上一副双重的重担，煽她出来替你说话，自己却站在一旁一声不吭，连她羞辱的一丝一毫也不肯替她担受！"

===Original===
But his son spake never a word, and Iron-face cried: “Out on thee! I know thee now, and why thou wouldest not to the Westland last winter. I am no fool; I know thee. Where hast thou hidden the stranger woman?”

Therewith he drew forth his sword and hove it aloft as if to hew down Face-of-god, who spake not nor flinched nor raised a hand from his side. But the Bride threw herself in front of Gold-mane, while there arose an angry cry of “The Peace of the Holy Thing! Peace-breaking, peace-breaking!” and some cried, “For the War-leader, the War-leader!” and as men could for the press they drew forth their swords, and there was tumult and noise all over the Thingstead.

===Chinese===
他的儿子仍一言不发，铁面叫道："不要脸的东西！我如今识得你了，也识得你去冬为何不肯往西土去。我不是傻子；我看穿你了。你把那个外乡女人藏在哪里了？"

说罢他拔剑出鞘，高高举过头顶，似要一剑劈下面神来；面神却既不说话、也不躲闪、更不动垂于身侧之手。新娘却一个箭步扑到金鬃身前护住他——这时人丛中响起一片怒喝："神圣议事会之安宁！破坏安宁！破坏安宁！"又有人喊："护战首！护战首！"众人挤作一团，能抽出剑的都抽了出来，整个议事场一片纷乱喧嚣。

===Original===
But Stone-face caught hold of the Alderman’s right arm and dragged down the sword, and the big carle, Red-coat of Waterless, came up behind him and cast his arms about his middle and drew him back; and presently he looked around him, and slowly sheathed his sword, and went back to his place and sat him down; and in a little while the noise abated and swords were sheathed, and men waxed quiet again, and the Alderman arose and said in a loud voice, but in the wonted way of the head man of the Thing:

“Here hath been trouble in the Holy Thing; a violent man hath troubled it, and drawn sword on a neighbour; will the neighbours give the dooming hereof into the hands of the Alderman?”

===Chinese===
石面抢上前一把抓住长老的右臂，将他持剑的手按了下去；那魁梧的汉子、无水地之红衣，又从背后上前来，双臂抱住他的腰，将他往后拽；过了一会儿，他环顾四周，缓缓收剑入鞘，回到自己位子上坐下；不多时，喧嚣渐息，宝剑尽皆归鞘，众人也复归安静。长老这才起身，以议事主持人惯有的口吻朗朗说道：

"神圣议事会中刚才起了风波；一个暴性之人搅扰了它，并拔剑指向邻里；诸位邻里可愿将此事的裁断之权交与长老？"

===Original===
Now all knew Iron-face, and they cried out, “That will we.” So he spake again:

“I doom the troubler of the Peace of the Holy Thing to pay a fine, to wit double the blood-wite that would be duly paid for a full-grown freeman of the kindreds.”

Then the cry went up and men yeasaid his doom, and all said that it was well and fairly doomed; and Iron-face sat still.

===Chinese===
众人皆认得铁面，便齐声呼道："我们愿意。"他便又说道：

"我判此搅扰神圣议事会安宁之人缴纳罚金——具体而言，是族中成年自由民正规血金的双倍。"

一阵呼喝响起，众人应承他的判决，都说此判判得公允得当；铁面依旧坐着不语。

===Original===
But Stone-face stood forth and said:

“Here have been wild words in the air; and dreams have taken shape and come amongst us, and have bewitched us, so that friends and kin have wrangled. And meseemeth that this is through the wizardry of these felons, who, even dead as they are, have cast spells over us. Good it were to cast them into the Death Tarn, and then to get to our work; for there is much to do.”

===Chinese===
这时石面站出来，说道：

"方才空中有许多狂言妄语；梦境也竟成了形，闯入我们中间，对我们施了迷魂法，使得朋友亲党竟相争吵。依我之见，这都是那几个恶徒的妖术作祟——他们虽已死了，仍在对我等施咒。不如把这几个恶徒扔进死潭（the Death Tarn）里去，然后我们也好着手办正事；因为要做的事还多得很。"

===Original===
All men yeasaid that; and Fork-beard of Lea went with those who had borne the corpses thither to cast them into the black pool.

===Chinese===
众人皆称是；草地之叉须（Fork-beard of Lea）便与先前抬尸首来的那几个人一同去，将尸首抛入那黑潭之中。

===Original===
But the Fiddle spake and said:

“Stone-face sayeth sooth. O Alderman, thou art no young man, yet am I old enough to be thy father; so will I give thee a rede, and say this: Face-of-god thy son is no liar or dastard or beguiler, but he is a young man and exceeding goodly of fashion, well-spoken and kind; so that few women may look on him and hear him without desiring his kindness and love, and to such men as this many things happen. Moreover, he hath now become our captain, and is a deft warrior with his hands, and as I deem, a sober and careful leader of men; therefore we need him and his courage and his skill of leading. So rage not against him as if he had done an ill deed not to be forgiven﻿—whatever he hath done, whereof we know not﻿—for life is long before him, and most like we shall still have to thank him for many good deeds towards us. As for the maiden, she is both lovely and wise. She hath a sorrow at her heart, and we deem that we know what it is. Yet hath she not lied when she said that she would bear the burden of the griefs of the people. Even so shall she do; and whether she will, or whether she will not, that shall heal her own griefs. For tomorrow is a new day. Therefore, if thou do after my rede, thou wilt not meddle betwixt these twain, but wilt remember all that we have to do, and that war is coming upon us. And when that is over, we shall turn round and behold each other, and see that we are not wholly what we were before; and then shall that which were hard to forgive, be forgotten, and that which is remembered be easy to forgive.”

===Chinese===
提琴却开口说道：

"石面所言极是。长老啊，你已不再年轻；可我年纪更大，足够做你的父亲了；所以我来给你出一个主意，道这么一句话：你的儿子面神，绝非说谎之人、懦怯之徒、行骗之辈；他是个年轻人，仪表极为出众，谈吐可亲、心地温厚——因此世间少有女子见了他的容貌、听了他说话，而不盼他垂怜相待的；这样的男子，总会有些事落在他身上。况且他如今已成了我们的首领，双手娴于战阵，依我看，统兵之才也是稳健细密的；因此我们少不得他，少不得他的勇气与他的将略。故而莫要拿他像犯了不可饶恕之罪那样对他发作——无论他到底做下了什么，我们所不知的事情——他前头的日子还长着呢，多半我们往后还要为他日后的诸多功劳而谢他。至于那位姑娘，她又美又慧。她心中有一桩愁苦，我们自以为知道那是什么。然而她说自己要为族人的哀愁挑起担子时，并未说谎；她确会如此去做；而且由不得她愿与不愿，这事反倒能医治她自家的心病。因为明日又是崭新的一天。所以你若依我的主意，便莫要去干预这二人之间的事，只要记着我们手头要做的事还很多、战事已经压到我们头上便是。等那战事一了，我们回过身来彼此打量，便会发觉彼此都已不再是原先那副模样了；那时，原本难以宽恕之事，将随之淡忘；而仍记在心上的，也将易于宽恕了。"

===Original===
So he spake; and Iron-face sat still and put his left hand to his beard as one who pondereth; but the Bride looked in the face of the old man the Fiddle, and then she turned and looked at Gold-mane, and her face softened, and she stood before the Alderman, and bent down before him and held out both her hands to him the palms upward. Then she said: “Thou hast been wroth with me, and I marvel not; for thy hope, and the hope which we all had, hath deceived thee. But kind indeed hast thou been to me ere now: therefore I pray thee take it not amiss if I call to thy mind the oath which thou swearedst on the Holy Boar last Yule, that thou wouldst not gainsay the prayer of any man if thou couldest perform it; therefore I bid thee naysay not mine: and that is, that thou wilt ask me no more about this matter, but wilt suffer me to fare afield like any swain of the Dale, and to deal so with my folk that they shall not hinder me. Also I pray thee that thou wilt put no shame upon Face-of-god my playmate and my kinsman, nor show thine anger to him openly, even if for a little while thy love for him be abated. No more than this will I ask of thee.”

===Chinese===
提琴说完；铁面依旧坐着，左手抚着胡须，似在沉思；新娘则望着提琴老人那张脸，又回过头去看了一眼金鬃，神色为之柔和；她走到长老面前，向他屈身行礼，双手手心向上向他伸出。然后说道："你方才为我动了怒，我也不觉奇怪；因为你那份指望——也是我们大家共同的指望——把你骗了。但你从前待我确实是好的：所以我求你不要见怪，容我把你去岁岁末冬至节对着圣猪所发的那一誓提醒你一句——你曾立誓，但凡能做到，决不驳回任何人的请求；故此我也求你不要驳回我这一求：只求你不再向我追问此事，容我如同谷中任何一个少年郎那样出征沙场，并容我把家中之事料理得让他们不来阻我。再求你一件事：不要使我的玩伴、我的亲人面神蒙羞，也不要把你的怒气公开向他发作——哪怕你对他的慈爱暂时减了一些，也请如此。我所求于你的，仅此而已。"

===Original===
All men who heard her were moved to the heart by her kindness and the sweetness of her voice, which was like to the robin singing suddenly on a frosty morning of early winter. But as for Gold-mane, his heart was smitten sorely by it, and her sorrow and her friendliness grieved him out of measure.

===Chinese===
凡听见她这番话的人，都被她的温厚、被她那甜美的嗓音所打动——那嗓音，一如早冬霜晨里知更雀猝然唱出的歌。至于金鬃，却被这话刺得心头作痛；她的哀伤、她的亲切，令他悲伤难抑。

===Original===
But Iron-face answered after a little while, speaking slowly and hoarsely, and with the shame yet clinging to him of a man who has been wroth and has speedily let his wrath run off him. So he said:

“It is well, my daughter. I have no will to forswear myself; nor hast thou asked me a thing which is over-hard. Yet indeed I would that today were yesterday, or that many days were worn away.”

===Chinese===
过了一会儿，铁面才回答；他说话又慢又哑，身上还黏着一种方才动了怒、又急急把怒气卸下之人所有的羞惭。他说道：

"就这样吧，我的女儿。我不愿自食其誓；你所求我的，也不算过分。然而我诚愿今日仍是昨日，或者许多日子早已悄然流去。"

===Original===
Then he stood up and cried in a loud voice over the throng:

“Let none forget the muster; but hold him ready against the time that the Warden shall come to him. Let all men obey the War-leader, Face-of-god, without question or delay. As to the fine of the peace-breaker, it shall be laid on the altar of the God at the Great Folk-mote. Herewith is the Thing broken up.”

Then all men shouted and clashed their weapons, and so sundered, and went about their business.

===Chinese===
随后他站起身来，朝着众人高声呼道：

"谁都别忘了点兵之期；各自整装待命，等候守事上门来传。所有人均须听从战首面神之命，不得迟疑、不得延误。至于那破会之人的罚金，将奉于大民众大会上神之祭坛之上。议事会就此散了。"

众人便齐声欢呼，兵器相击，随即便各自散去，料理自家的事务。

===Original===
And the talk of men it was that the breaking of the troth-plight between those twain was ill; for they loved Face-of-god, and as for the Bride they deemed her the Dearest of the kindreds and the Jewel of the Folk, and as if she were the fairest and the kindest of all the Gods. Neither did the wrath of Iron-face mislike any; but they said he had done well and manly both to be wroth and to let his wrath run off him. As to the war which was to come, they kept a good heart about it, and deemed it as a game to be played, wherein they might show themselves deft and valiant, and so get back to their merry life again.

So wore the day through afternoon to even and night.

===Chinese===
众人私下议论，都说这一对新人解除婚约之事，实在可惋；因为他们都喜爱面神；至于新娘，他们视她为诸族之挚爱、众民之珠玉，仿佛她是众神之中最美最慈的一位。铁面的那场怒火，也没有人觉得不妥；众人说他做得得体而有丈夫气——既动了怒，又能把怒气卸下，皆恰到好处。至于将至的那场战事，他们倒满怀信心，把它当作一场要打的游戏，以为自己可以借机一显身手、逞一逞英武，然后便可以回到从前那欢快的日子里去。

这一日便如此从午后走到傍晚，又入于夜。

## XIX The Fair Woman Telleth Face-of-God of Her Kindred / 十九 美妇人向面神讲述其亲族

===Original===
When he came back to the dais he saw that there was meat upon the board, and the Friend said to him:
"Now art thou Gold-mane indeed: but come now, sit by me and eat, though the Wood-woman giveth thee but a sorry banquet, O guest; but from the Dale it is, and we be too far now from the dwellings of men to have delicate meat on the board, though tonight when they come back thy cheer shall be better. Yet even then thou shalt have no such dainties as Stone-face hath imagined for thee at the hands of the Wood-wight."

She laughed therewith, and he no less; and in sooth the meat was but simple, of curds and new cheese, meat of the herdsmen. But Face-of-god said gaily: "Sweet it shall be to me; good is all that the Friend giveth."

===Chinese===
他回到高台之旁时，见案上已摆了饭菜，那朋友便对他说道：
"你如今果然是金鬃（Gold-mane）了：且来，坐在我身旁吃些东西罢，客官啊，林中妇（the Wood-woman）款待你的，不过是一顿寒酸的筵席；但这都是谷中带来的，我们如今离人烟已太远，案上摆不出精致之物，虽说今晚他们回来时，你的伙食便会好些。可即便到那时，你也尝不到石面（Stone-face）所设想的、那林中精怪（the Wood-wight）供奉你的佳馔。"

她说着笑了起来，他也跟着笑了；说实在的，那饭菜确实简单，不过是凝乳和新做的奶酪，乃牧人之食。面神（Face-of-god）却欢快地说："在我吃来都是甘美的；朋友所赐之物，样样都是好的。"

===Original===
Then she raised her hand and made the sign of the Hammer over the board, and looked up at him and said:
"Hath the Earth-god changed my face, Gold-mane, to what I verily am?"

He held his face close to hers and looked into it, and him-seemed it was as pure as the waters of a mountain lake, and as fine and well-wrought every deal of it as when his father had wrought in his stithy many days and fashioned a small piece of great mastery. He was ashamed to kiss her again, but he said to himself, "This is the fairest woman of the world, whom I have sworn to wed this year." Then he spake aloud and said:
"I see the face of the Friend, and it will not change to me."

Again she reddened a little, and the happy look in her face seemed to grow yet sweeter, and he was bewildered with longing and delight.
