But she stood up and went to an ambrye in the wall and brought forth a horn shod and lipped with silver of ancient fashion, and she poured wine into it and held it forth and said:
"O guest from the Dale, I pledge thee! and when thou hast drunk to me in turn we will talk of weighty matters. For indeed I bear hopes in my hands too heavy for the daughters of men to bear; and thou art a chieftain's son, and mayst well help me to bear them; so let us talk simply and without guile, as folk that trust one another."

So she drank and held out the horn to him, and he took the horn and her hand both, and he kissed her hand and said:
"Here in this Hall I drink to the Sons of the Wolf, whosoever they be." Therewith he drank and he said: "Simply and guilelessly indeed will I talk with thee; for I am weary of lies, and for thy sake have I told a many."

"Thou shalt tell no more," she said; "and as for the health thou hast drunk, it is good, and shall profit thee. Now sit we here in these ancient seats and let us talk."

===Chinese===
随后她举起手，在案上画了个锤符（the sign of the Hammer），抬头看着他，说道：
"地神（the Earth-god）可曾把我的容颜，金鬃，变回我真正的模样？"

他把脸凑近她的脸，凝视着她。在他看来，那容颜澄澈如高山湖中之水，每一处都精妙绝伦、巧夺天工，一如其父在铁砧前连日锤打、所制成的那一件巧夺天工的小器物。他不好意思再吻她，心中却暗道："这便是世间最美的女子，我今年已立誓要娶她为妻。"于是他出声说道：
"我所见的，是朋友的面容，它在我眼中不会改变。"

她又微微红了脸，脸上那欢悦的神情似乎愈发甜美，他被渴望与欢喜弄得心神恍惚。

她却站起身来，走到墙边一个小橱前，取出一只古制的角杯，杯底杯口都镶着银子；她斟上酒，递了过来，说道：
"谷中来的客人啊，我敬你一杯！等你回敬我之后，我们便谈些紧要之事。因为我手中所托的期望，实在重得不是凡间女子所能承受；而你是首领之子，尽可帮我一同承担。我们便如彼此信托之人一般，坦诚无欺地谈一谈罢。"

于是她饮了一口，将角杯递给他；他接杯之时，连她的手也一并握住，吻了吻她的手，说道：
"在这厅堂之中，我敬狼之子（the Sons of the Wolf）一杯，不论他们究竟是谁。"说罢一饮而尽，又道："我定会坦诚无欺地与你交谈；因为我已厌倦了谎言，为了你，我不知说过多少谎。"

"你再也用不着说谎了，"她说，"至于你方才所祝的康健，那是好的，必有益于你。我们且在这古座上坐下，说说话罢。"

===Original===
So they sat them down while the sun was westering in the March afternoon, and she said:
"Tell me first what tidings have been in the Dale."

So he told her of the ransackings and of the murder at Carlstead.

She said: "These tidings have we heard before, and some deal of them we know better than ye do, or can; for we were the ransackers of Penny-thumb and Harts-bane. Thereof will I say more presently. What other tidings hast thou to tell of? What oaths were sworn upon the Boar last Yule?"

So he told her of the oath of Bristler the son of Brightling. She smiled and said: "He shall keep his oath, and yet redden no blade."

Then he told of his father's oath, and she said:
"It is good; but even so would he do and no oath sworn. All men may trust Iron-face. And thou, my friend, what oath didst thou swear?"

His face grew somewhat troubled as he said: "I swore to wed the fairest woman in the world, though the Dalesmen gainsaid me, and they beyond the Dale."

"Yea," she said, "and there is no need to ask thee whom thou didst mean by thy 'fairest woman,' for I have seen that thou deemest me fair enough. My friend, maybe thy kindred will be against it, and the kindred of the Bride; and it might be that my kindred would have gainsaid it if things were not as they are. But though all men gainsay it, yet will not I. It is meet and right that we twain wed."

===Chinese===
三月午后，日头偏西，两人就此坐下，她说道：
"先告诉我，谷中可有什么消息。"

他便把那些劫掠之事，以及在汉子镇（Carlstead）那桩凶杀，一一对她说了。

她说："这些消息我们早已听说了，其中有些，我们比你们更清楚，你们是没法比我们更明白的；因为洗劫铜板拇指（Penny-thumb）和害鹿（Harts-bane）的，正是我们。此事我稍后再细讲。你还有什么别的消息要讲？去年岁末冬至节（Yuletide），在圣猪（the Boar）前起过什么誓？"

他便把布莱特林之子布里斯勒（Bristler the son of Brightling）所立之誓，告诉了她。她微微一笑，说道："他必会履行誓言，却又不必使刀剑见血。"

接着他讲了父亲的誓言，她说：
"这誓起得好；可即便不起誓，他也会这般做的。铁面（Iron-face）这人，人人都信得过。那么你呢，我的朋友，你起了什么誓？"

他面色微现不安，说道："我立誓要娶世间最美的女子为妻，哪怕谷民（the Dalesmen）反对，谷外之人也反对。"

"是了，"她说，"你那句'最美的女子'指的是谁，我也不必再问你，因为我已瞧出，你觉得我生得够美了。我的朋友，这事也许你的亲族会反对，新娘（the Bride）的亲族也会反对；若非事已至此，连我的亲族也许都会反对。可即便人人都反对，我也不反对。你我二人成婚，本是合宜正当之事。"

===Original===
She spake very soberly and quietly, but when she had spoken there was nothing in his heart but joy and gladness: yet shame of her loveliness refrained him, and he cast down his eyes before hers. Then she said in a kind voice:
"I know thee, how glad thou art of this word of mine, because thou lookest on me with eyes of love, and thinkest of me as better than I am; though I am no ill woman and no beguiler. But this is not all that I have to say to thee, though it be much; for there are more folk in the world than thou and I only. But I told thee this first, that thou mightest trust me in all things. So, my friend, if thou canst, refrain thy joy and thy longing a little, and hearken to what concerneth thee and me, and thy people and mine."

"Fair woman and sweet friend," he said, "thou knowest of a gladness which is hard to bear if one must lay it aside for a while; and of a longing which is hard to refrain if it mingle with another longing—knowest thou not?"

"Yea," she said, "I know it."

"Yet," said Face-of-god, "I will forbear as thou biddest me. Tell me, then, what were the felons who were slain at Carlstead? Knowest thou of them?"

"Over well," she said, "they are our foes this many a year; and since we met last autumn they have become foes of you Dalesmen also. Soon shall ye have tidings of them; and it was against them that I bade thee arm yesterday."

Said Face-of-god: "Is it against them that thou wouldst have us do battle along with thy folk?"

"So it is," she said; "no other foemen have we. And now, Gold-mane, thou art become a friend of the Wolf, and shalt before long be of affinity with our House; that other day thou didst ask me to tell thee of me and mine, and now will I do according to thine asking. Short shall my tale be; because maybe thou shalt hear it told again, and in goodly wise, before thine whole folk.

===Chinese===
她说这话时，语调极为郑重沉静，可她说完之后，他心中便只剩下欢喜快乐：然而她那容颜之美令他生怯，不敢与之对视，遂在她面前垂下目光。接着她温声说道：
"我知道，我这句话叫你心里多么欢喜，因为你用爱慕的眼光看我，把我看得比实际的我要好；虽说我并非坏女人，也不是骗人的人。但这并非我要对你说的全部，虽说这已不少；因为世上除了你我二人，还有别的人。我之所以先把这事告诉你，是为了让你在万事上都能信我。所以，我的朋友，你若能，且稍稍按捺住你的欢喜和渴望，听一听那些关乎你我、关乎你族人我族人之事。"

"美丽的女子、甜蜜的朋友，"他说，"你知道有一种欢喜，若要人暂且搁置片刻，是何等难忍；又有一种渴望，若与另一种渴望相交织，便难以抑制——你不是知道的么？"

"是，"她说，"我知道。"

"然而，"面神说，"我愿如你所嘱，暂且按捺。那么告诉我，在汉子镇被杀的那些恶徒，究竟是什么人？你可知道？"

"太清楚了，"她说，"他们多年来便是我们的仇敌；自去年秋天我们相遇以来，他们如今也成了你们谷民的仇敌。不久你们便会听到他们的消息；昨日我叫你备甲执兵，正是为了防他们。"

面神问："你要我们与你的族人并肩对敌的，便是他们？"

"正是，"她说，"我们没有别的仇敌。如今，金鬃，你已成了狼族（the Wolf）之友，不久还要与我家结亲；前些日你曾求我把我和我族人的来历讲给你听，如今我便依你所愿讲来。我这故事不会长；因为你也许很快就要在全族之人面前，再听人堂堂正正地讲一遍。

===Original===
"As thou wottest we be now outlaws and Wolves' Heads; and whiles we lift the gear of men, but ever if we may of ill men and not of good; there is no worthy goodman of the Dale from whom we would take one hoof, or a skin of wine, or a cake of wax.

"Wherefore are we outlaws? Because we have been driven from our own, and we bore away our lives and our weapons, and little else; and for our lands, thou seest this Vale in the howling wilderness and how narrow and poor it is, though it hath been the nurse of warriors in time past.

"Hearken! Time long ago came the kindred of the Wolf to these Mountains of the World; and they were in a pass in the stony maze and the utter wilderness of the Mountains, and the foe was behind them in numbers not to be borne up against. And so it befell that the pass forked, and there were two ways before our Folk; and one part of them would take the way to the north and the other the way to the south; and they could not agree which way the whole Folk should take. So they sundered into two companies, and one took one way and one another. Now as to those who fared by the southern road, we knew not what befell them, nor for long and long had we any tale of them.

"But we who took the northern road, we happened on this Vale amidst the wilderness, and we were weary of fleeing from the overmastering foe; and the dale seemed enough, and a refuge, and a place to dwell in, and no man was there before us, and few were like to find it, and we were but a few. So we dwelt here in this Vale for as wild as it is, the place where the sun shineth never in the winter, and scant is the summer sunshine therein. Here we raised a Doom-ring and builded us a Hall, wherein thou now sittest beside me, O friend, and we dwelt here many seasons.

===Chinese===
"你也晓得，我们如今是亡命之徒、狼头之徒（Wolves' Heads）；我们有时也劫取他人的财物，但总是尽量劫恶人，不劫善人；谷中但凡正经的当家人，我们不会从他那里拿走一只蹄子、一皮囊酒，或一块蜡饼。

"我们为何沦为亡命之徒？因为我们被人从自己的家园里赶了出来，逃出来时只带走了性命和兵器，旁的几乎一无所有；至于土地么，你瞧这幽谷（Shadowy Vale）位于虎啸狼嚎的荒野之中，何其狭小、何其贫瘠，虽说从前它也曾是孕育勇士的摇篮。

"听着！很久很久以前，狼族来到这世界之山（Mountains of the World）之中；他们正走在一条山道上，那道处于乱石迷宫般的高山、彻底的荒野之中，而追兵在身后，人数之多，根本无法抵挡。也是命中注定，那山道分了岔，全族面前便有了两条路；一部分人要走北边那条，另一部分人要走南边那条；一时定不下全族究竟该走哪条。于是分作两支，各走各路。至于走南边那条路的人，我们不知他们遭遇了什么，漫长岁月里，也再无他们的半点音讯。

"可我们这一支走了北路的，在这荒野之中撞见了这条山谷；我们早已厌倦了被那势不可挡的仇敌追杀；这谷地看着倒也凑合，是个避难之所，可作安身之地；谷中先前并无他人，能找到这里的人也不多，而我们本就人数寥寥。于是我们便在这野性的山谷里安了家——这地方冬日里终年不见日光，夏日阳光也稀薄得很。我们在这里立起一座判决环（the Doom-ring），建起一座厅堂——朋友，你如今便坐在这厅堂里我的身旁——我们在此住了许多个寒暑。

===Original===
"We had a few sheep in the wilderness, and a few neat fed down the grass of the Vale; and we found gems and copper in the rocks about us wherewith at whiles to chaffer with the aliens, and fish we drew from our river the Shivering Flood. Also it is not to be hidden that in those days we did not spare to lift the goods of men; yea, whiles would our warriors fare down unto the edges of the Plain and lie in wait there till the time served, and then drive the spoil from under the very walls of the Cities. Our men were not little-hearted, nor did our women lament the death of warriors overmuch, for they were there to bear more warriors to the Folk.

"But the seasons passed, and the Folk multiplied in Shadowy Vale, and livelihood seemed like to fail them, and needs must they seek wider lands. So by ways which thou wilt one day wot of, we came into a valley that lieth northwest of Shadowy Vale: a land like thine of Burgdale, or better; wide it was, plenteous of grass and trees, well watered, full of all things that man can desire.

"Were there men before us in this Dale? sayest thou. Yea, but not very many, and they feeble in battle, weak of heart, though strong of body. These, when they saw the Sons of the Wolf with weapons in their hands, felt themselves puny before us, and their hearts failed them; and they came to us with gifts, and offered to share the Dale between them and us, for they said there was enough for both folks. So we took their offer and became their friends; and some of our Houses wedded wives of the strangers, and gave them their women to wife. Therein they did amiss; for the blended Folk as the generations passed became softer than our blood, and many were untrusty and greedy and tyrannous, and the days of the whoredom fell upon us, and when we deemed ourselves the mightiest then were we the nearest to our fall. But the House whereof I am would never wed with these Westlanders, and other Houses there were who had affinity with us who chiefly wedded with us of the Wolf, and their fathers had come with ours into that fruitful Dale; and these were called the Red Hand, and the Silver Arm, and the Golden Bushel, and the Ragged Sword. Thou hast heard those names once before, friend?"

"Yea," he said, and as he spoke the picture of that other day came back to him, and he called to mind all that he had said, and his happiness of that hour seemed the more and the sweeter for that memory.

===Chinese===
"我们在荒野里有几只羊，谷中几头牛（neat）啃着青草；在周围岩石里我们又寻见宝石和铜，偶尔拿来与异族（the aliens）做交易；又从我们的河——战栗川（the Shivering Flood）——里捕鱼。也不必讳言，那阵子我们劫掠他人财物，从不手软；是的，我们的勇士有时会下到大平原（the Plain）边上，埋伏起来，等到时机成熟，便从那诸城（the Cities）的城墙之下，把掳获之物赶将回来。我们的男儿并不胆怯，我们的女子对勇士之死也不大哀恸过甚，因为她们还须为族人生养更多的勇士。

"然而寒来暑往，族人在幽谷中生齿日繁，生计却眼看要养不活他们了，他们不得不去寻更宽广的土地。于是经由一些你总有一天会知晓的路，我们来到了幽谷西北方的一条山谷：那地方和你们的堡谷（Burgdale）相仿，或者更好；地方宽广，草木丰美，水源充足，凡人所欲之物一应俱全。

"你要问：这谷中在我们之前可有人住？有的，但不多；他们战场上羸弱，心地也怯懦，身躯倒还壮实。这些人一见狼之子们手执兵刃，便自觉在我们面前渺小，心都凉了；于是带着礼物来见我们，提议与我们对分这条山谷，他们说谷中之地足敷两族共用。我们便接受了他们的提议，与之交好；我们有些宗族娶了这些外人的女儿为妻，也把自己的女子嫁给他们。在这事上他们做得不对；因为两族混血的后代，一代代传下来，性情比我们的血脉软弱了许多，其中许多人奸诈、贪婪、暴虐，淫乱之风也随之而来；正当我们自以为最强盛之时，其实离覆亡最近。可我所出的这一宗族，从不与这些西土之人（Westlanders）通婚；另有几个与我们关系亲近的宗族，也主要与我们狼族相互婚配，他们的先人当年是随我们的先人一同进入那条丰饶的山谷的；这些宗族名唤：赤手（the Red Hand）、银臂（the Silver Arm）、金斗（the Golden Bushel）、残锋剑（the Ragged Sword）。朋友，这些名字你从前听过一次吧？"

"是的，"他说；说话之间，那一日的情景又浮上心头，他记起了自己当时说过的一切；因着那段回忆，此时此刻的喜悦愈发深切、愈发甜美。

===Original===
She went on: "Fair and goodly is that Dale as mine own eyes have seen, and plentiful of all things, and up in its mountains to the east are caves and pits whence silver is digged abundantly; therefore is the Dale called Silverdale. Hast thou heard thereof, my friend?"

"Nay," said Face-of-god, "though I have marvelled whence ye gat such foison of silver."

He looked on her and marvelled, for now she seemed as if it were another woman: her eyes were gleaming bright, her lips were parted; there was a bright red flush on the pommels of her two cheeks as she spake again and said:
"Happy lived the Folk in Silverdale for many and many winters and summers: the seasons were good and no lack was there: little sickness there was and less war, and all seemed better than well. It is strange that ye Dalesmen have not heard of Silverdale."

"Nay," said he, "but I have not; of Rosedale have I heard, as a land very far away: but no further do we know of toward that airt. Lieth Silverdale anywhere nigh to Rosedale?"

She said: "It is the next dale to it, yet is it a far journey betwixt the two, for the ice-sea pusheth a horn in betwixt them; and even below the ice the mountain-neck is passable to none save a bold crag-climber, and to him only bearing his life in his hands. But, my friend, I am but lingering over my tale, because it grieveth me sore to have to tell it. Hearken then! In the days when I had seen but ten summers, and my brother was a very young man, but exceeding strong, and as beautiful as thou art now, war fell on us without rumour or warning; for there swarmed into Silverdale, though not by the ways whereby we had entered it, a host of aliens, short of stature, crooked of limb, foul of aspect, but fierce warriors and armed full well: they were men having no country to go back to, though they had no women or children with them, as we had when we were young in these lands, but used all women whom they took as their beastly lust bade them, making them their thralls if they slew them not. Soon we found that these foemen asked no more of us than all we had, and therewithal our lives to be cast away or used for their service as beasts of burden or pleasure. There then we gathered our fighting-men and withstood them; and if we had been all of the kindreds of the Wolf and the fruit of the wives of warriors, we should have driven back these felons and saved the Dale, though it maybe more than half ruined: but the most part of us were of that mingled blood, or of the generations of the Dalesmen whom we had conquered long ago, and stout as they were of body their hearts failed them, and they gave themselves up to the aliens to be as their oxen and asses.

===Chinese===
她接着说："那山谷之美、之壮丽，是我亲眼所见，物产丰饶，一应俱全；东边高山之中，有洞穴矿坑，白银取之不竭；因此这谷名为银谷（Silverdale）。我的朋友，你可曾听说过？"

"没有，"面神说，"不过我倒一直纳闷，你们这么多白银是从哪里来的。"

他看着她，心中称奇，因为她此刻仿佛换了一个女子：双目炯炯有神，双唇微启；两颊的颧骨上泛起一片鲜红的血色，她又开口道：
"许多个寒冬酷暑之间，银谷之民生活得十分幸福：时令丰顺，无所匮乏；少有疾病，更少兵戈；一切看上去好得不能再好了。你们谷民竟没听过银谷之名，实在奇怪。"

"没，"他说，"我确实没听过；玫瑰谷（Rosedale）我倒听过，说是一个极远的地方；再往那个方向有什么，我们就一无所知了。银谷可在玫瑰谷附近么？"

她说："它与玫瑰谷是紧邻，可两谷之间路途遥远，因为一条冰川海的尖角插入了两者之间；即便是冰舌之下那道山颈，除了胆大包天的攀崖好手——而且还得把性命捏在手里的那种——谁也过不去。可是，我的朋友，我不过是在故事前头徘徊流连，因为接下来要讲的，叫我心痛万分。那么听着！在我才见过十个夏天的那些日子，我的哥哥已是个年轻汉子，极其强壮，相貌之美正如你如今这般；战事却毫无风声、毫无征兆地降临到我们头上：因为有一支异族大军蜂拥闯入银谷——虽不是我们当年进谷的那些路——那是一群异族人，身材矮短，四肢畸形，面目丑陋，却是凶猛的战士，甲兵齐整：这些人是没有故国可归的，虽说他们随军并未携带妻儿——不像我们初到这些地方时那样——但凡所掠之女，他们都任凭兽欲驱使，恣意蹂躏，若不杀掉，便收为奴婢。不久我们便发现，这些敌人向我们索求的，无非是我们所有的一切；除此之外，还要我们的性命——或被随手弃如敝屣，或被当作驮畜、玩物而供其驱使。于是我们召集战士，奋起抵抗；当年我们若全是狼族诸宗的血统、全是勇士之妻所出，我们本可击退这班恶徒，保住此谷，纵然谷地可能已毁去大半：可我们之中，大多数是那混血的后代，或是我们多年前所征服的谷民的后裔；他们身躯虽壮，心却先怯了，竟向异族投降，甘心作他们的牛马。

===Original===
"Why make a long tale of it? We who were left, and could brook death but not thraldom, fought it out together, women as well as men, till the sweetness of life and a happy chance for escape bid us flee, vanquished but free men. For at the end of three days' fight we had been driven up to the easternmost end of the Dale, and up anigh to the jaws of the pass whereby the Folk had first come into Silverdale, and we had those with us who knew every cranny of that way, while to strangers who knew it not it was utterly impassable; night was coming on also, and even those murder-carles were weary with slaying; and, moreover, on this last day, when they saw that they had won all, they were fighting to keep, and not to slay, and a few stubborn carles and queens, of what use would they be, or where was the gain of risking life to win them?

"So they forbore us, and night came on moonless and dark; and it was the early spring season, when the days are not yet long, and so by night and cloud we fled away, and back again to Shadowy Vale.

"Forsooth, we were but a few; for when we were gotten into this Vale, this strip of grass and water in the wilderness, and had told up our company, we were but two hundred and thirty and five of men and women and children. For there were an hundred and thirty and three grown men of all ages, and of women grown seventy and five, and one score and seven children, whereof I was one; for, as thou mayst deem, it was easier for grown men with weapons in their hands to escape from that slaughter than for women and children.

"There sat we in yonder Doom-ring and took counsel, and to some it seemed good that we should all dwell together in Shadowy Vale, and beset the skirts of the foemen till the days should better; but others deemed that there was little avail therein; and there was a mighty man of the kindred, Stone-wolf by name, a man of middle-age, and he said, that late in life had he tasted of war, and though the banquet was made bitter with defeat, yet did the meat seem wholesome to him. 'Come down with me to the Cities of the Plain,' said he, 'all you who are stout warriors; and leave we here the old men and the swains and the women and children. Hateful are the folk there, and full of malice, but soft withal and dastardly. Let us go down thither and make ourselves strong amongst them, and sell our valour for their wealth till we come to rule them, and they make us their kings, and we establish the Folk of the Wolf amongst the aliens; then will we come back hither and bring away that which we have left.'

===Chinese===
"何必把故事拖长呢？我们剩下这些人，宁死不愿为奴，男女一同死战到底；直到求生之甘与一个侥幸的脱身之机，催促我们出走——虽是败军，却是自由之人。因为三日鏖战下来，我们已被逼到山谷最东头，一直被赶到当年族人初次进入银谷所经那道山隘的口子上；我们身边有熟知道路每一处缝隙的人，而对不知路径的生人来说，那条道根本无从通行；加之夜幕将垂，连那班杀人如麻的恶汉也杀得手软了；再者，这最后一日，他们见胜局已定，便为生擒而战，不为杀戮而战——几个顽强的男女汉子，于他们又有何用？冒死夺之，又有何益？

"于是他们暂且放过了我们，那一夜无月无光，漆黑一片；其时正是早春，白昼尚未变长；我们便趁着夜色云翳逃了出来，又回到了幽谷。

"说实话，我们人数不多；因为待我们逃入此谷——这片荒野中的草与水之地——清点人数，男女老幼合计不过二百三十五人。其中各年龄的成年男子，共一百三十三人；成年女子七十五人；孩子一十七人，我便是其中之一；因为，你想必明白，手执兵刃的成年男子，要逃出那场屠杀，比女子和孩子容易得多。

"我们便坐在那边那座判决环里议事；有人主张全族同住幽谷，伺机骚扰敌族边鄙，以待时局好转；也有人认为此举用处不大。族中有一位壮士，名唤石狼（Stone-wolf），是个中年汉子，他说：他到岁数不小了才尝到战争的滋味，虽说这场筵席因败绩而发苦，但那肉吃来倒觉得受用。'你们这些壮士，随我下到大平原诸城（the Cities of the Plain）去吧，'他说，'老人、少年、女子、孩童，且留在这里。那边的人可恨，心地狠毒，却也软弱、怯懦。我们下到他们中间去，壮大自己的势力，把我们的勇武卖作他们的财富，直到我们统治他们，他们奉我们为王，把狼族（the Folk of the Wolf）在异族之中扎下根来；然后我们再回到这里，把留下的人接走。'

===Original===
"So he spake, and the more part of the warriors yea said his rede, and they went with him to the Westland, and amongst these was my brother Folk-might (for that is his name in the kindred). And I sorrowed at his departure, for he had borne me thither out of the flames and the clash of swords and the press of battle, and to me had he ever been kind and loving, albeit he hath had the Words of hard and froward used on him full oft.

"So in this Vale abode we that were left, and the seasons passed; some of the elders died, and some of the children also; but more children were born, for amongst us were men and women to whom it was lawful to wed with each other. Even with this scanty remnant was left some of the life of the kindred of old days; and after we had been here but a little while, the young men, yea and the old also, and even some of the women, would steal through passes that we, and we only, knew of, and would fall upon the Aliens in Silverdale as occasion served, and lift their goods both live and dead; and this became both a craft and a pastime amongst us. Nor may I hide that we sometimes went lifting otherwhere; for in the summer and autumn we would fare west a little and abide in the woods the season through, and hunt the deer thereof, and whiles would we drive the spoil from the scattered folk not far from your Shepherd-Folk; but with the Shepherds themselves and with you Dalesmen we meddled not.

"Now that little wood-lawn with the toft of an ancient dwelling in it, wherein, saith Bow-may, thou didst once rest, was one of our summer abodes; and later on we built the hall under the pinewood that thou knowest.

"Thus then grew up our young men; and our maids were little softer; e'en such as Bow-may is (and kind is she withal), and it seemed in very sooth as if the Spirit of the Wolf was with us, and the roughness of the Waste made us fierce; and law we had not and heeded not, though love was amongst us."

===Chinese===
"他这番话一出，大半勇士都赞成他的主意，便随他去了西土（the Westland），我哥哥民强（Folk-might——这是他在族中的名字）也在其中。他这一走，我心里十分难过，因为当年是他把我从烈火、刀兵相交、战阵的挤压之中抱了出来，带到这里的；他对我向来慈爱有加，虽说他性子刚烈执拗，旁人对他说的话也不在少数。

"于是我们剩下的人便在这幽谷住了下来，寒来暑往；老人死了几个，孩子也死了几个；但更多的孩子出生了，因为我们之中还有可相互婚配的男女。这残存的一小撮人里，尚留着几分旧日族人的元气；在此住下不久，年轻汉子——连老汉、乃至一些女子——都会悄悄穿过那些只有我们才知晓的山隘，寻机袭击银谷中的异族（the Aliens），掠取他们的财物，不论活物死物；这事在我们中间既成了一门手艺，也成了一种消遣。我也不必隐瞒，有时我们也到别处去劫掠；因为夏秋之际，我们会往西走一段，整个季节都住在树林里，在林中猎鹿；有时也从那些零散的人家——离你们牧羊之民（the Shepherd-Folk）不远的人家——那里赶些掳获之物回来；但与牧羊之民本身，与你们谷民，我们从不相扰。

"那片小林间草地，里面有一座古屋的屋基，据弓娥（Bow-may）说你曾在那里歇过脚，那便是我们的夏日居所之一；后来我们又在你知道的那片松林下，建起了那座厅堂。

"我们这里的年轻汉子便这么长大；我们的少女也不见得多娇柔；便如弓媚那般（为人心地倒也和善）；真的，仿佛狼之灵（the Spirit of the Wolf）就在我们中间，荒野的粗砺使我们性情凶悍；我们没有律法，也不在意律法，只是彼此之间，相爱相亲。"

===Original===
She stopped awhile and fell a-musing, and her face softened, and she turned to him with that sweet happy look upon it and said:
"Desolate and dreary is the Dale, thou deemest, friend; and yet for me I love it and its dark-green water, and it is to me as if the Fathers of the kindred visit it and hold converse with us; and there I grew up when I was little, before I knew what a woman was, and strange communings had I with the wilderness. Friend, when we are wedded, and thou art a great chieftain, as thou wilt be, I shall ask of thee the boon to suffer me to abide here at whiles that I may remember the days when I was little and the love of the kindred waxed in me."

"This is but a little thing to ask," said Face-of-god; "I would thou hadst asked me more."

"Fear not," she said, "I shall ask thee for much and many things; and some of them belike thou shalt deny me."

He shook his head; but she smiled in his face and said:
"Yea, so it is, friend; but hearken. The seasons passed, and six years wore, and I was grown a tall slim maiden, fleet of foot and able to endure toil enough, though I never bore weapons, nor have done. So on a fair even of midsummer when we were together, the most of us, round about this Hall and the Doom-ring, we saw a tall man in bright war-gear come forth into the Dale by the path that thou camest, and then another and another till there were two score and seven men-at-arms standing on the grass below the scree yonder; by that time had we gotten some weapons in our hands, and we stood together to meet the newcomers, but they drew no sword and notched no shaft, but came towards us laughing and joyous, and lo! it was my brother Folk-might and his men, those that were left of them, come back to us from the Westland.

===Chinese===
她停了一会儿，陷入沉思，面容也柔和下来；转过脸来，带着那甜美的欢颜，对他说道：
"朋友，你心里想必觉得，这条山谷荒凉冷寂；可在我而言，我爱这山谷，爱它墨绿色的河水；在我看来，仿佛族中的先祖常来此探访，与我们交谈；我便是在那里长大的——在我还小、还不知女子之身意味着什么的年岁——我与这片荒野有过奇异的交感。朋友，待我们成亲之后，你成了一位大首领——你必会成为那样的人——我会向你求一个恩典：许我偶尔来这里住一住，好让我记起年幼之时，记起族人之爱在我心里日渐生长的那些日子。"

"这不过是件小事，"面神说，"我倒宁愿你向我要得更多些。"

"别担心，"她说，"我会向你要许多、许多东西；其中有些，你也许会拒绝我。"

他摇摇头；她却笑着看他的脸，说道：
"是了，朋友，便是如此；但听我说。寒暑易逝，六年过去，我已长成一个高挑纤细的少女，步履轻捷，足以胜任劳苦，虽说我从不佩戴兵器，至今依然如此。于是在一个美好的仲夏（midsummer）傍晚，我们大半的人都聚在这厅堂和判决环四周，我们看见一个高大汉子，身披鲜明甲胄，顺着你来时所走的那条路走入山谷；接着又是一个、又是一个，直到那边山碎石坡之下的草地上，立着四十七名战士；那时我们手里已经抄起了几件兵器，便站在一起，迎上前去；他们却既不拔剑，也不搭箭，只笑着、欢欢喜喜地朝我们走来——你瞧！竟是我哥哥民强和他的人马——他们所剩的那些人——从西土回来了。

===Original===
"Glad indeed was I to behold him; and for him when he had taken me in his arms and looked up and down the Dale, he cried out: 'In many fair places and many rich dwellings have I been; but this is the hour that I have looked for.'

"Now when we asked him concerning Stone-wolf and the others who were missing (for ten tens of stalwarth men had fared to the Westland), he swept out his hand toward the west and said with a solemn face: 'There they lie, and grass groweth over their bones, and we who have come aback, and ye who have abided, these are now the children of the Wolf: there are no more now on the earth.'

"Let be! It was a fair even and high was the feast in the Hall that night, and sweet was the converse with our folk come back. A glad man was my brother Folk-might when he heard that for years past we had been lifting the gear of men, and chiefly of the Aliens in Silverdale: and he himself was become learned in war and a deft leader of men.

"So the days passed and the seasons, and we lived on as we might; but with Folk-might's return there began to grow up in all our hearts what had long been flourishing in mine, and that was the hope of one day winning back our own again, and dying amidst the dear groves of Silverdale. Within these years we had increased somewhat in number; for if we had lost those warriors in the Westland, and some old men who had died in the Dale, yet our children had grown up (I have now seen twenty and one summers) and more were growing up. Moreover, after the first year, from the time when we began to fall upon the Dusky Men of Silverdale, from time to time they who went on such adventures set free such thralls of our blood as they could fall in with and whom they could trust in, and they dwelt (and yet dwell) with us in the Dale: first and last we have taken in three score and twelve of such men, and a score of women-thralls withal.

===Chinese===
"我见到他，自然欢喜万分；他呢，一把将我抱住，上下打量这条山谷，大声喊道：'我到过许多好地方，住过许多华美的宅院；可这一刻，才是我日思夜想的时刻。'

"待我们问起石狼和其他那些下落不明的人（当初去西土的，足有一百条壮汉），他向西方一挥手，面色凝重地说：'他们就长眠在那里，青草已盖没了他们的白骨；我们这些回来的，和你们这些留下的，如今便是狼之裔（the children of the Wolf）了：这世上再没有别的了。'

"罢了！那是个美好的傍晚，那一夜厅堂里的盛宴极为隆重，与归来的族人促膝交谈，其乐融融。我哥哥民强听说我们这些年一直在劫人财物——主要是银谷中异族的财物——心里很高兴；而他本人也已成了精通战阵之人，善能用兵。

"日子一天天、一季季过去，我们尽力过活；可民强归来之后，众人心里便开始萌生一种念头，那念头在我心里早已郁郁葱葱——那便是有朝一日夺回我们自己的家业，在银谷那可爱的林丛之中死去。这些年来，我们的人数略有增长；因为虽说我们在西土损失了那些战士，谷中也死了些老人，但我们的孩子已长大成人（我如今已见过二十一个夏天），还有更多的正在长大。再者，自我们开始袭击银谷的黝暗人（the Dusky Men）那一年的次年算起，出外行劫的人，凡能遇上我族血统、又信得过的奴婢，便把他们解救出来，他们便（至今仍）与我们同住在谷中：前前后后，我们一共收留了七十二名男子，还有二十名女奴。

===Original===
"Now during these seasons, and not very long ago, after I was a woman grown, the thought came to me, and to Folk-might also, that there were kindreds of the people dwelling anear us whom we might so deal with that they should become our friends and brothers in arms, and that through them we might win back Silverdale.

"Of Rosedale we wotted already that the Folk were nought of our blood, feeble in the field, cowed by the Dusky Men, and at last made thralls to them; so nought was to do there. But Folk-might went to and fro to gather tidings: at whiles I with him, at whiles one or more of Wood-father's children, who with their father and mother and Bow-may have abided in the Vale ever since the Great Undoing.

"Soon he fell in with thy Folk, and first of all with the Woodlanders, and that was a joy to him; for wot ye what? He got to know that these men were the children of those of our Folk who had sundered from us in the mountain passes time long and long ago; and he loved them, for he saw that they were hardy and trusty, and warriors at heart.

"Then he went amongst the Shepherd-Folk, and he deemed them good men easily stirred, and deemed that they might soon be won to friendship; and he knew that they were mostly come from the Houses of the Woodlanders, so that they also were of the kindred.

"And last he came into Burgdale, and found there a merry and happy Folk, little wont to war, but stouthearted, and nowise puny either of body or soul; he went there often and learned much about them, and deemed that they would not be hard to win to fellowship. And he found that the House of the Face was the chiefest house there; and that the Alderman and his sons were well beloved of all the folk, and that they were the men to be won first, since through them should all others be won. I also went to Burgstead with him twice, as I told thee erst; and I saw thee, and I deemed that thou wouldest lightly become our friend; and it came into my mind that I myself might wed thee, and that the House of the Face thereby might have affinity thenceforth with the Children of the Wolf."

===Chinese===
"这些年里——也不算太久之前，在我长大成人之后——我心里、民强心里，都生出一个念头：住在我们周围的，有一些别族人，我们若与之打交道，他们或许能成为我们的朋友、我们的战友；借着他们，我们也许能夺回银谷。

"至于玫瑰谷，我们早已知道那里的人并非我们的血脉，战阵之上软弱无力，被黝暗人吓破了胆，最终成了他们的奴婢；所以那里没什么可图。民强却四处奔走，打探消息：有时我陪着他，有时是林父（Wood-father）的一个或几个孩子同去；他们与父母，还有弓媚，自大倾覆（the Great Undoing）以来，一直住在谷中。

"不久他就遇上了你们的人，最先碰到的是林中汉子（the Woodlanders），这让他十分欢喜；你道为何？他得知，这些人正是很久很久以前、在山隘之中与我们分道扬镳的那部分族人的后裔；他爱这些人，因为他看得出他们健壮可靠，骨子里便是战士。

"其后他又到牧羊之民中间走动，觉得他们是好人，性情易于激发，不久便能与之结交为友；他也知道，他们大多出自林中汉子诸族，因此也是同宗。

"最后他来到堡谷，见那里有一族人，欢乐、快活，不甚习战，却心志壮健，无论身心都不孱弱；他常去那里，对他们了解不少，觉得要与之结盟，并不难。他又发现，面神之宅（the House of the Face）是那里的首户；长老（the Alderman）及其诸子深为众人所爱，是最该先结交的人，因为通过他们，旁人都能争取过来。我也随他去过堡镇（Burgstead）两次，从前告诉过你的；我见到了你，觉得你很容易便会成为我们的朋友；我心里便动了念头：我或可嫁与你为妻，面神之宅由此便可与狼之裔（the Children of the Wolf）结为姻亲。"

===Original===
He said: "Why didst thou deem thus of me, O friend?"

She laughed and said: "Dost thou long to hear me say the words when thou knowest my thought well? So be it. I saw thee both young and fair; and I knew thee to be the son of a noble, worthy, guileless man and of a beauteous woman of great wits and good rede. And I found thee to be kind and openhanded and simple like thy father, and like thy mother wiser than thou thyself knew of thyself; and that thou wert desirous of deeds and fain of women."

She was silent for a while, and he also: then he said: "Didst thou draw me to the woods and to thee?"

She reddened and said: "I am no spell-wife: but true it is that Wood-mother made a waxen image of thee, and thrust through the heart thereof the pin of my girdle-buckle, and stroked it every morning with an oak-bough over which she had sung spells. But dost thou not remember, Gold-mane, how that one day last Hay-month, as ye were resting in the meadows in the cool of the evening, there came to you a minstrel that played to you on the fiddle, and therewith sang a song that melted all your hearts, and that this song told of the Wildwood, and what was therein of desire and peril and beguiling and death, and love unto Death itself? Dost thou remember, friend?"

"Yea," he said, "and how when the minstrel was done Stone-face fell to telling us more tales yet of the woodland, and the minstrel sang again and yet again, till his tales had entered into my very heart."

"Yea," she said, "and that minstrel was Wood-wont; and I sent him to sing to thee and thine, deeming that if thou didst hearken, thou would'st seek the woodland and happen upon us."

He laughed and said: "Thou didst not doubt but that if we met, thou mightest do with me as thou wouldest?"

"So it is," she said, "that I doubted it little."

===Chinese===
他说："朋友，你为何这样看我？"

她笑道："你明明知道我的心意，却还要听我亲口说出来？也罢。我见你又年轻又俊美；我又知道你父亲是个高贵、正直、毫无欺诈的男子，你母亲是个绝色的女子，既有大智慧，又能出好主意。我又看出你心地仁善、慷慨大方、心思单纯，像你父亲；又像你母亲，比你自己所知的还要聪慧；而且你既渴望建功立业，又钟情于女子。"

她沉默了一会，他也沉默；然后他说："是你把我引到林中、引到你身边的么？"

她红了脸，说道："我并非巫婆：不过，林母（Wood-mother）确曾照你的模样做了一具蜡像，把我腰带扣上的针，刺进了蜡像的心口，每天早晨用一枝橡树枝拂拭它，那橡枝她已对着念过咒。可是，金鬃，你难道不记得：去年干草月（Hay-month），有一天傍晚凉爽之时，你们在草甸上歇息，来了一个弹唱的乐人，给你们拉起琴来，边拉边唱，唱得你们人人都心里酸软；那支歌唱的是野林之事，唱的是林中的渴望与凶险、欺瞒与死亡，以及那直抵死亡本身的爱？朋友，你可记得？"

"记得，"他说，"我还记得那乐人一曲终了，石面便接着给我们讲了好些林中的故事，那乐人又一曲接一曲地唱，直唱到那些故事钻进了我的心底。"

"是了，"她说，"那个乐人便是林习（Wood-wont）；是我派他去为你和你的人唱歌的，我心想，你若听进去了，便会寻到林子里来，便能撞见我们。"

他笑了，说道："你毫不怀疑：只要我们相见，你便能随你的意摆布我？"

"是这样，"她说，"我几乎没有怀疑过。"

===Original===
"Therein wert thou wise," said Face-of-god; "but now that we are talking without guile to each other, mightest thou tell me wherefore it was that Folk-might made that onslaught upon me? For certain it is that he was minded to slay me."

She said: "It was sooth what I told thee, that whiles he groweth so battle-eager that whatso edge-tool he beareth must needs come out of the scabbard; but there was more in it than that, which I could not tell thee erst. Two days before thy coming he had been down to Burgstead in the guise of an old carle such as thou sawest him with me in the marketplace. There was he guested in your Hall, and once more saw thee and the Bride together; and he saw the eyes of love wherewith she looked on thee (for so much he told me), and deemed that thou didst take her love but lightly. And he himself looked on her with such love (and this he told me not) that he deemed nought good enough for her, and would have had thee give thyself up wholly to her; for my brother is a generous man, my friend. So when I told him on the morn of that day whereon we met that we looked to see thee that eve (for indeed I am somewhat foreseeing), he said: 'Look thou, Sun-beam, if he cometh, it is not unlike that I shall drive a spear through him.' 'Wherefore?' said I; 'can he serve our turn when he is dead?' Said he: 'I care little. Mine own turn will I serve. Thou sayest Wherefore? I tell thee this stripling beguileth to her torment the fairest woman that is in the world—such an one as is meet to be the mother of chieftains, and to stand by warriors in their day of peril. I have seen her; and thus have I seen her.' Then said I: 'Greatly forsooth shalt thou pleasure her by slaying him!' And he answered: 'I shall pleasure myself. And one day she shall thank me, when she taketh my hand in hers and we go together to the Bride-bed.' Therewith came over me a clear foresight of the hours to come, and I said to him: 'Yea, Folk-might, cast the spear and draw the sword; but him thou shalt not slay: and thou shalt one day see him standing with us before the shafts of the Dusky Men.' So I spake; but he looked fiercely at me, and departed and shunned me all that day, and by good hap I was hard at hand when thou drewest nigh our abode. Nay, Gold-mane, what would'st thou with thy sword? Why art thou so red and wrathful? Would'st thou fight with my brother because he loveth thy friend, thine old playmate, thy kinswoman, and thinketh pity of her sorrow?"

He said, with knit brow and gleaming eyes: "Would the man take her away from me perforce?"

"My friend," she said, "thou art not yet so wise as not to be a fool at whiles. Is it not so that she herself hath taken herself from thee, since she hath come to know that thou hast given thyself to another? Hath she noted nought of thee this winter and spring? Is she well pleased with the ways of thee?"

He said: "Thou hast spoken simply with me, and I will do no less with thee. It was but four days agone that she did me to wit that she knew of me how I sought my love on the Mountain; and she put me to sore shame, and afterwards I wept for her sorrow."

===Chinese===
"这一点上你倒聪明，"面神说，"不过，如今我们彼此坦诚相告，你可否告诉我，民强为何要对我下那番毒手？因为毫无疑问，他是动了杀心的。"

她说："我从前告诉你的，是真的：有时他战意一起，所佩的任何利刃都非得出鞘不可；但此事除此之外还有别的内情，我先前没法告诉你。你来之前两日，他乔装成一个老汉——就是你跟我在集市上见到的那个老汉模样——下到堡镇去了。他在你们厅里被款待留宿，又一次看见你和新娘在一起；他看见她望向你时那含情脉脉的目光（这些是他告诉我的），便觉得你把她的情意看得太轻。而他自己也用那样的爱慕看她（这一点他没告诉我），以致觉得世上没有配得上她的东西，巴不得你把自己整个献给她；因为我的朋友，我哥哥是个慷慨的人。所以，我们相见那一日早晨，我告诉他当晚可望见到你（因为我确有几分先见之明），他便说：'你听好，日光（Sun-beam），他若来了，我说不定一枪把他扎个对穿。'我说：'为什么？他死了还能为我们所用么？'他说：'我才不管那么多。我只为我自己。你问为什么？我告诉你，这小子哄骗世间最美的女子，害她受煎熬——这样一个女子，本该做首领之母，在勇士临危之日伴其左右。我见过她；我便是这样看见她的。'我便说：'你杀了他，可真让她高兴啊！'他答道：'我让自己高兴。有朝一日她要谢我——那时她握住我的手，与我一同走向新婚之榻。'就在这时，未来的时刻清清楚楚地在我眼前显现，我便对他说：'是了，民强，你掷枪拔剑都行，但你不能杀他：有朝一日，你会看见他与我们并肩，一同面对黝暗人的箭雨。'我这样说了；他却凶狠地瞪了我一眼，转身走了，那一整天都躲着我；还算侥幸，你走近我们住处时，我正好就在近旁。哎，金鬃，你拔剑做什么？你怎么脸涨得通红、这般恼怒？你要跟我哥哥动手，就因为他爱你的朋友、你幼时的玩伴、你的同族姐妹，怜惜她的哀伤？"

他皱着眉、目光灼灼地说："那人要硬把她从我手里抢走么？"

"我的朋友，"她说，"你还没聪明到不会偶尔犯傻的地步。难道不是她自己离开了你么——自从她知道你已把自己交给另一个女子？这一个冬天、一个春天，她难道没看出你什么？她对你的种种作为，可曾满意？"

他说："你既坦诚待我，我也坦诚待你。不过四天之前，她让我知道，她已晓得我上山去寻我所爱；她叫我羞愧难当，过后我又为她的哀伤而落泪。"

===Original===
Therewith he told her all that the Bride had said to him, as he well might, for he had forgotten no word of it.

Then said the Friend: "She shall have the token that she craveth, and it is I that shall give it to her."

Therewith she took from her finger a ring wherein was set a very fair changeful mountain-stone, and gave it to him, and said:
"Thou shalt give her this and tell her whence thou hadst it; and tell her that I bid her remember that Tomorrow is a new day."

===Chinese===
于是他把新娘对他说的那番话，原原本本告诉了她——他原也做得到，因为那些话他一字未忘。

那朋友便说："她所要的信物，她必会得到；而给她信物的人，便是我。"

说着，她从指上取下一枚戒指，戒面上镶着一颗极美的、变幻着光彩的山中宝石，交给他，说道：
"你把这个给她，告诉她你是从哪里得来的；再告诉她，我叫她记住：明日又是新的一天。"

## XLII The Host Cometh to the Edges of Silverdale / 四十二 大军抵达银谷之缘

===Original===
So wore the night, and when the dawn was come were the two captains afoot, and they went from band to band to see that all was ready, and all men were astir betimes, and by the time that the sun smote the eastern side of Shield-broad ruddy, they had broken their fast and were dight for departure. Then the horns blew up beside the banners, and rejoiced the hearts of men. But by the command of the captains this was the last time that they should sound till they blew for onset in Silverdale, because now would they be drawing nigher and nigher to the foemen, and they wotted not but that wandering bands of them might be hard on the lips of the pass, and might hear the horns’ voice, and turn to see what was toward.

===Chinese===
夜就这样渐渐过去。黎明一到，两位首领便已起身，自一队队人马之间穿行巡视，查看一切是否齐备；众人也都早早起身忙碌。待到朝阳将盾阔（Shield-broad）东坡照得一片通红之时，他们已用罢朝食，整装待发。于是号角在旌旗之畔嘹然响起，振奋了众人之心。然首领们有令：此乃最后一次鸣角，非至银谷吹响进攻之号，不得再作；因为如今他们离敌人将愈逼愈近，谁知那些四散游荡的敌队会不会正紧挨隘口之唇，闻得角声，便掉头来窥探动静。

===Original===
Forth then went the banners of the Wolf, and the men of the vanward fell to threading the rock-maze toward the north, and in two hours’ time were clear of the Dale under Shield-broad. All went in the same order as yesterday; but on this day the Sun-beam would bear her hauberk, and had a sword girt to her side, and her heart was high and her speech merry.

When they left the Dale under Shield-broad the way was easy and wide for a good way, the river flowing betwixt low banks, and the pass being more like a string of little valleys than a mere gap, as it had been on the other side of the Dale. But when one third of the day was past, the way began to narrow on them again, and to rise up little by little; and at last the rock-walls drew close to the river, and when men looked toward the north they saw no way, and nought but a wall. For the gap of the Shivering Flood turned now to the east, and the Flood came down from the east in many falls, as it were over a fearful stair, through a gap where there was no path between the cliffs and the water, nought but the boiling flood and its turmoil; so that they who knew not the road wondered what they should do.

===Chinese===
于是狼之旌旗向前开拔，前队之人开始鱼贯穿过那片乱石迷阵向北进发，两个时辰之后，便已出了盾阔之下的山谷。一切行进次序皆照昨日之旧；只是这一日日光（the Sun-beam）非要亲身披挂锁子甲不可，腰间又悬了一柄剑，她意气高昂，谈笑风生。

离了盾阔之下那座山谷之后，好长一段路都宽阔平易：河水在低矮的两岸之间流淌，这处隘道与其说是一道山豁，倒不如说像一串小山谷连缀而成，与山谷那一边的形势截然不同。然一日已过三分之一之时，道路又渐渐向他们逼窄起来，且一寸一寸往上攀升；末了石壁直逼到河岸，人朝北一望，再无路可寻，唯见一堵石墙。盖因战栗川（the Shivering Flood）的豁口至此折向东去，川水自东方层层跌落，仿佛沿一道可畏的阶梯倾泻而下，那道豁口之中，绝壁与水之间并无路径，唯有翻滚沸腾的洪流与其轰鸣；故不知此路之人，都不免犯愁，不知如何是好。

===Original===
But Folk-might led the banners to where a great buttress of the cliffs thrust itself into the way, coming well-nigh down to the water, just at the corner where the river turned eastward, and they got them about it as they might, and on the other side thereof lo! another gap exceeding strait, scarce twenty foot over, wall-sided, rugged beyond measure, going up steeply from the great valley: a little water ran through it, mostly filling up the floor of it from side to side; but it was but shallow. This was now the battle-road of the Host, and the vanward entered it at once, turning their backs upon the Shivering Flood.

Full toilsome and dreary was that strait way; often great stones hung above their heads, bridging the gap and hiding the sky from them; nor was there any path for them save the stream itself; so that whiles were they wading its waters to the knee or higher, and whiles were they striding from stone to stone amidst the rattle of the waters, and whiles were they stepping warily along the ledges of rock above the deeper pools, and in all wise labouring in overcoming the rugged road amidst the twilight of the gap.

===Chinese===
然而民强将旌旗引至一处：那里一道巨大的崖壁支脉突入路中，几乎直抵水边，正当河道折向东去之拐角处；众人尽力从它旁边绕过，待到了它的另一面——看哪！又是一道极为狭窄的豁口，宽不过二十尺，两壁如墙，崎岖难行之极，自那大山谷中陡然上升：一道细流从中穿过，几乎将豁底的地面从这边到那边漫满；所幸水并不深。这便是大军此刻的征战之路了，前队当即踏入其中，将战栗川抛在身后。

这条狭窄之路既劳苦，又凄凉：时常有巨石悬在头顶之上，如桥一般横跨豁口，将天光遮蔽；他们又别无路可走，唯有那溪流本身而已；故而他们时而涉水及膝、乃至更深，时而在哗然水声之中从一石跨到另一石，时而小心翼翼地沿着深潭上方石壁的岩边踩踏而行，千方百计地在这豁口半明半暗的光影里，征服这条崎岖之路。

===Original===
Thus they toiled till the afternoon was well worn, and so at last they came to where the rock-wall was somewhat broken down on the north side, and great rocks had fallen across the gap, and dammed up the waters, which fell scantily over the dam from stone to stone into a pool at the bottom of it. Up this breach, then, below the force they scrambled and struggled, for rough indeed was the road for them; and so came they up out of the gap on to the open hillside, a great shoulder of the heath sloping down from the north, and littered over with big stones, borne thither belike by some ice-river of the earlier days; and one great rock was in special as great as the hall of a wealthy goodman, and shapen like to a hall with hipped gables, which same the men of the Wolf called House-stone.

There then the noise and clatter of the vanward rose up on the face of the heath, and men were exceeding joyous that they had come so far without mishap. Therewith came weaponed men out from under House-stone, and they came toward the men of the vanward, and they were a half-score of the forerunners of the Wolf; therefore Folk-might and Face-of-god fell at once into speech with them, and had their tidings; and when they had heard them, they saw nought to hinder the host from going on their road to Silverdale forthright; and there were still three hours of daylight before them. So the vanward of the host tarried not, and the captains left word with the men from under House-stone that the rest of the Host should fare on after them speedily, and that they should give this word to each company, as men came up from out the gap. Then they fared speedily up the hillside, and in an hour’s wearing had come to the crest thereof, and to where the ground fell steadily toward the north, and hereabout the scattered stones ceased, and on the other side of the crest the heath began to be soft and boggy, and at last so soft, that if they had not been wisely led, they had been bemired oftentimes. At last they came to where the flows that trickled through the mires drew together into a stream, so that men could see it running; and thereon some of the Woodlanders cried out joyously that the waters were running north; and then all knew that they were drawing nigh to Silverdale.

===Chinese===
他们这般劳顿，直至午后已深，终于来到一处：北面的石壁稍有坍塌，巨石横亘豁口之上，将水拦住，水从坝上自一石至一石稀稀落下，坠入坝底的一处深潭。于是他们就在这瀑布之下，自那豁口攀爬挣扎而上，因那条路实在崎岖难行；就这样，他们从豁口爬了上来，到了开阔的山坡之上——那是一片自北面斜斜而下的大荒原山肩，遍地散布着巨石，大概是远古某条冰河搬运到此的；其中有一块巨石格外惹眼，竟有殷实富户整座厅堂那么大，形状也像一座带斜脊山墙的厅堂，狼之民将这块石头唤作屋石（House-stone）。

于是在那荒原坡面之上，前队的喧腾嘈杂之声扬起，众人因一路无灾无难地行到此地，都喜不自胜。正这时，有持械之人从屋石之下走出来，朝前队之人迎上前来——他们正是狼族十名打前站的先遣；于是民强与面神当即上前与他们交谈，听取他们的消息；听罢，二人觉出并无什么能阻挡大军径直向银谷进发；而此刻距天黑尚有三个时辰的天光。于是前队并不耽搁，首领们给屋石下之人留下话：大军其余各队须立即跟上，每有一队自豁口出来，便将此话传与那一队。然后他们便快步上了山坡，行了一个时辰光景，已到山脊之上，到了地势稳稳向北倾斜之处；这一带散乱的石头已尽，过了山脊另一面，荒原开始变得松软泥泞，末了竟软到这般地步：若非有人明智引路，他们早就要屡屡陷进泥潭之中了。终于他们来到一处，那从各处泥沼中渗出的涓流在此汇成一道溪水，可以看见水在流淌了；当下林中之民里有几人欢然高呼：水是向北流的！于是众人都知道，他们已经逼近银谷了。

===Original===
No man they met on the road, nor did they of Shadowy Vale look to meet any; because the Dusky Men were not great hunters for the more part, except it were of men, and especially of women; and, moreover, these hill-slopes of the mountain-necks led no-whither and were utterly waste and dreary, and there was nought to be seen there but snipes and bitterns and whimbrel and plover, and here and there a hill-fox, or the great erne hanging over the heath on his way to the mountain.

===Chinese===
一路上他们未遇见一人，幽谷之人也不指望遇见什么人；因为黝暗人多半并非好猎手——除非所猎的是人，尤其是女人；况且这些山颈上的山坡哪儿也不通，乃是彻底荒凉凄寂之地，所能见到的不过是鹬鸟、苇鳽、杓鹬、鸻鸟之属，间或一只山狐，或是一只硕大的海雕，正掠过荒原，飞往山中去。

===Original===
When sunset came, they were getting clear of the miry ground, and the stream which they had come across amidst of the mires had got clearer and greater, and rattled down between wide stony sides over the heath; and here and there it deepened as it cleft its way through little knolls that rose out of the face of the mountain-neck. As the Host climbed one of these and was come to its topmost (it was low enough not to turn the stream), Face-of-god looked and beheld dark-blue mountains rising up far off before him, and higher than these, but away to the east, the snowy peaks of the World-mountains. Then he called to mind what he had seen from the Burg of the Runaways, and he took Folk-might by the arm, and pointed toward those far-off mountains.

“Yea,” said Folk-might, “so it is, War-leader. Silverdale lieth between us and yonder blue ridges, and it is far nigher to us than to them.”

But the Sun-beam came close to those twain, and took Face-of-god by the hand and said: “O Gold-mane, dost thou see?” and he turned about and beheld her, and saw how her cheeks flamed and her eyes glittered, and he said in a low voice: “Tomorrow for mirth or silence, for life or death.”

But the whole vanward as they came up stayed to behold the sight of the mountains on the other side of Silverdale, and the banners of the Folk hung over their heads, moving but little in the soft air of the evening: so went they on their ways.

===Chinese===
日落时分，他们正将那片泥泞之地抛在身后；他们在泥沼中央所遇的那道溪水，此时已变得更清、更大，在荒原上宽阔的石质两岸之间哗然奔泻；它一路劈开山颈坡面上隆起的一座座小阜，时而在此处冲出深槽。大军攀上其中一座小阜、来到它顶上时（此阜矮小，并未使溪水改道），面神举目望去，只见远方前方，深蓝色的群山拔地而起，比这些更远处、却偏在东边的，是世界之山的雪峰。他想起在逃奴堡（the Burg of the Runaways）之上所见之景，便拉住民强的手臂，朝那些远山指去。

"是啊，"民强说，"正是如此，战首。银谷就在我们与那蓝色山脊之间，它离我们可比离那些山脊近多了。"

然而日光走到那二人近前，拉住面神的手，说："啊，金鬃，你看见了么？"他转过身来望着她，见她双颊绯红如火，双目闪闪生辉，便低声道："明日，非欢即寂，非生即死。"

可是整个前队上来之时，都驻足观赏银谷那一边群山的景象，族人的旌旗就悬在他们头顶上方，在傍晚柔和的空气里微微飘动、几乎不动：他们便这样继续上路。

===Original===
The sun sank, and dusk came on them as they followed down the stream, and night came, and was clear and starlit, though the moon was not yet risen. Now was the ground firm and the grass sweet and flowery, and wind-worn bushes were scattered round about them, as they began to go down into the ghyll that cleft the wall of Silverdale, and the night-wind blew in their faces from the very Dale and place of the Battle to be. The path down was steep at first, but the ghyll was wide, and the sides of it no longer straight walls, as in the gaps of their earlier journey, but broken, sloping back, and (as they might see on the morrow) partly of big stones and shaly grit, partly grown over with bushes and rough grass, with here and there a little stream trickling down their sides. As they went, the ghyll widened out, till at last they were in a valley going down to the plain, in places steep, in places flat and smooth, the stream ever rattling down the midst of it, and they on the west side thereof. The vale was well grassed, and oak-trees and ash and holly and hazel grew here and there about it; and at last the Host had before it a wood which filled the vale from side to side, not much tangled with undergrowth, and quite clear of it nigh to the stream-side. Thereinto the vanward entered, but went no long way ere the leaders called a halt and bade pitch the banners, for that there should they abide the daylight. Thus it had been determined at the Council of the Hall of the Wolf; for Folk-might had said: “With an Host as great as ours, and mostly of men come into a land of which they know nought at all, an onslaught by night is perilous: yea, and our foes should be overmuch scattered, and we should have to wander about seeking them. Let us rather abide in the wood of Wood-dale till the morning, and then display our banners on the hillside above Silverdale, so that they may gather together to fall upon us: in no case shall they keep us out of the Dale.”

===Chinese===
太阳落下，他们沿溪下行，暮色渐渐袭来；夜降临了，天宇澄澈，星光满天，虽然月亮尚未升起。此时地面已坚实，芳草甘美，遍生野花，四下散布着为风所摧的灌木丛——他们开始步入那道劈开银谷石墙的深壑了；夜风从那正要交战的谷地、从那将来的战场之地，迎面吹来。下行之路起初颇陡，但深壑宽阔，壑的两壁不再是先前一路那些豁口中的笔直石墙，而是破碎的、向后倾斜的（他们翌日便可看清）：一部分是巨石与页状砂砾，一部分为灌木和粗草所覆，间或一道细流沿壁淌下。他们一路前行，深壑愈展愈宽，终于他们已身处一条下通平原的山谷之中——谷地或陡或缓、或崎岖或平坦，那条溪水始终在谷中央哗然奔泻，而他们走在溪的西岸。谷中芳草丰美，柞、梣、冬青、榛树处处散生；末了，大军面前出现了一片树林，将山谷从这边到那边满满占满，林下灌丛并不甚纠缠，近溪一带更是全无杂木。前队便踏入林中，没走多远，几位首领便下令暂停，吩咐立起旌旗——就在此处等候天明。此乃狼之厅议事之时早已定下的；因为民强曾说过："以我们这样一支大军，又多是初入一无所知之地的人，夜间突袭实为凶险：况且我们的敌人未免过于分散，我们还得四处游荡去寻觅他们。不如在林谷的树林中歇到天明，然后在银谷上方的山坡上展开旌旗，好让他们聚拢来攻我们：无论如何，他们休想挡住我们进谷。"

===Original===
There then they stayed, and as each company came up to the wood, they were marshalled into their due places, so that they might set the battle in array on the edge of Silverdale.

===Chinese===
于是他们便在此驻扎下来；每有一队人马来到林中，便被引至各自应分的位置，以便在银谷之缘列阵布战。

## XLI The Host Departeth from Shadowy Vale: The First Day’s Journey / 四十一 大军离幽谷：第一日之程

===Original===
It was about three hours before noon that the Host began to enter into the pass out of Shadowy Vale by the riverside; and the women and children, and men unfightworthy, stood on the higher ground at the foot of the cliffs to see the Host wend on the way. Of these a many were of the Woodlanders, who were now one folk with them of Shadowy Vale. And all these had chosen to abide tidings in the Vale, deeming that there was little danger therein, since that last slaughter which Folk-might had made of the Dusky Men; albeit Face-of-god had offered to send them all to Burgstead with two score and ten men-at-arms to guard them by the way and to eke out the warders of the Burg.

===Chinese===
约莫距正午尚差三个时辰之时，大军开始循河岸边进入出幽谷的隘道；妇女孩童以及不能上阵的男子，都站在崖脚的高处，目送大军启程上路。这些人当中有许多是林中汉子——他们如今已与幽谷之人合为一族。他们都选择留在谷中等候消息，认为自从民强上次对黝暗人那场屠杀之后，此地已无甚危险；虽然面神曾提议将他们悉数送往堡镇，并派五十名兵士沿途护送，兼以充实山堡（burg）的守卫。

===Original===
Now the fighting-men of Shadowy Vale were two long hundreds lacking five; of whom two score and ten were women, and three score and ten lads under twenty winters; but the women, though you might scarce see fairer of face and body, were doughty in arms, all good shooters in the bow; and the swains were eager and light-foot, cragsmen of the best, wont to scaling the cliffs of the Vale in search of the nests of gerfalcons and suchlike fowl, and swimming the strong streams of the Shivering Flood; tough bodies and wiry, stronger than most grown men, and as fearless as the best.

===Chinese===
幽谷的战丁共有两个长百（long hundreds）少五人；其中五十人为女子，七十人为不满二十个冬天的少年；那些女子虽则容貌身段之秀美世间罕有其匹，却个个勇武善战，精于弓射；少年们则意气昂扬，脚步轻捷，是最出色的攀崖好手，惯于攀爬谷中悬崖寻觅矛隼（gerfalcon）之类猛禽的巢穴，又能泅渡战栗川的湍流；他们筋骨坚韧瘦劲，胜过多数成年壮汉，胆气之大，不逊于最勇之人。

===Original===
The order of the Departure of the Host was this:

The Woodlanders went first into the pass, and with them were two score of the ripe Warriors of the Wolf. Then came of the kindreds of Burgdale, the Men of the Steer, the Bridge, and the Bull; then the Men of the Vine and the Sickle; then the Shepherd-folk; and lastly, the Men of the Face led by Stone-face and Hall-face. With these went another two score of the dwellers in Shadowy Vale, and the rest were scattered up and down the bands of the Host to guide them into the best paths and to make the way easier to them. Face-of-god was sundered from his kindred, and went along with Folk-might in the forefront of the Host, while his father the Alderman went as a simple man-at-arms with his House in the rearward. The Sun-beam followed her brother and Face-of-god amidst the Warriors of the Wolf, and with her were Bow-may clad in the Alderman’s gift, and Wood-father and his children. Bow-may had caused her to doff her hauberk for that day, whereon they looked to fall in with no foeman. As for the Bride, she went with her kindred in all her war-gear; and the morning sun shone in the gems of her apparel, and her jewelled feet fell like flowers upon the deep grass of the upper Vale, and shone strange and bright amongst the black stones of the pass. She bore a quiver at her back and a shining yew bow in her hand, and went amongst the bowmen, for she was a very deft archer.

===Chinese===
大军启程的次序如下：

林中汉子先入隘道，与他们同行的有四十名狼族中精壮老练的武士。接着是堡谷诸族之人：犍牛族、桥族、公牛族之人；再后是葡藤族与镰族之人；再后是牧羊之民；最后是由石面与厅面率领的面族之人。与他们同行的又有四十名幽谷居民，其余的则分散在大军各队之中，引他们走最佳的路径，为他们开路。面神离开了本族，与民强同在大军最前列；他的父亲长老则作为一名寻常兵士，随本族之人殿后。日光随其兄长与面神行于狼族武士之间；与她同行的有身着长老所赠锁子甲的弓娥，还有林父及其子女。弓娥劝她那一日卸下锁子甲，因为当日他们并不指望会遇上敌人。至于新娘，她全身披挂战具，随本族而行；晨光照在她衣饰的宝石之上，她那缀满珠宝的双足踏在幽谷上段的深草之上，宛若花朵坠落，又在隘道那些黑色乱石之间闪耀出奇异的明辉。她背上一壶箭矢，手执一张闪闪发亮的紫杉弓，行于弓手之间——因为她是一名极精于射术的射手。

===Original===
So fared they into the pass, leaving peace behind them, with all their banners displayed, and the banner of the Red-mouthed Wolf went with the Wolf and the Sun-burst in the forefront of their battle next after the two captains.

===Chinese===
他们便这样开入隘道，将安宁留在身后，所有旌旗尽数展开；赤口狼之旗（the Red-mouthed Wolf）、狼旗与旭日旗（the Sun-burst）一同行于阵列最前，紧随两位首领之后。

===Original===
As for their road, the grassy space between the rock-wall and the water was wide and smooth at first, and the cliffs rose up like bundles of spear-shafts high and clear from the green grass with no confused litter of fallen stones; so that the men strode on briskly, their hearts high-raised and full of hope. And as they went, the sweetness of song stirred in their souls, and at last Bow-may fell to singing in a loud clear voice, and her cousin Wood-wise answered her, and all the warriors of the Wolf who were in their band fell into the song at the ending, and the sound of their melody went down the water and reached the ears of those that were entering the pass, and of those who were abiding till the way should be clear of them: and this is some of what they sang:

===Chinese===
至于他们所行之路，石壁与河水之间那片青草平地起初宽阔平整，两岸悬崖如一捆捆矛杆，自碧草之上高高耸起，轮廓分明，并无崩石杂乱的堆砌；于是众人步履轻捷，意气高昂，满怀希望。行进之间，歌之甜美在他们心头涌动，终于弓娥放声高歌起来，她的从兄林智应声相和，他们那一队中所有的狼族武士到末尾都齐声加入；他们的歌声顺流而下，传入正在进入隘道之人的耳中，也传入那些候到道路通空之人的耳中：以下便是他们所唱的一部分——

===Original===
Therewith they shook their naked swords in the air, and fared on eagerly, and as swiftly as the pass would have them fare. But so it was, that when the rearward of the Host was entering the first of the pass, and was going on the wide smooth sward, the vanward was gotten to where there was but a narrow space clear betwixt water and cliff; for otherwhere was a litter of great rocks and small, hard to be threaded even by those who knew the passes well; so that men had to tread along the very verge of the Shivering Flood, and wary must they be, for the water ran swift and deep betwixt banks of sheer rock half a fathom below their very foot-soles, which had but bare space to go on the narrow a way. So it held on for a while, and then got safer, and there was more space for going betwixt cliff and flood; albeit it was toilsome enough, since for some way yet there was a drift of stones to cumber their feet, some big and some little, and some very big. After a while the way grew better, though here and there, where the cliffs lowered, were wide screes of loose stones that they must needs climb up and down. Thereafter for a space was there an end of the stony cumber, but the way betwixt the river and the cliffs narrowed again, and the black crags grew higher, and at last so exceeding high, and the way so narrow, that the sky overhead was to them as though they were at the bottom of a well, and men deemed that thence they could see the stars at noontide. For some time withal had the way been mounting up and up, though the cliffs grew higher over it; till at last they were but going on a narrow shelf, the Shivering Flood swirling and rattling far below them betwixt sheer rock-walls grown exceeding high; and above them the cliffs going up towards the heavens as black as a moonless starless night of winter. And as the flood thundered below, so above them roared the ceaseless thunder of the wind of the pass, that blew exceeding fierce down that strait place; so that the skirts of their garments were wrapped about their knees by it, and their feet were well-nigh stayed at whiles as they breasted the push thereof.

===Chinese===
于是他们将出鞘的裸剑挥向空中，急切前行，速度之快，只凭隘道能容他们走多快。然而情形却是：当大军后队正进入隘道头一段、走在那片宽阔平整的草地上时，前队却已到了水与崖之间仅剩一条窄道可通的地方；因为别处尽是大石小石乱堆一气，即便熟识隘道之人也难以从中穿过；故众人不得不沿着战栗川的极边缘行走，且须格外当心——河水在陡峭的石岸之间又深又急地奔流，就在他们脚底下半寻之处，而脚下那条窄道几乎无立锥之地可容落脚。这般情形持续了一阵，随后安全了些，崖与水之间有了更多通路；虽然仍颇为劳顿，因为再往前一段路上，仍有碎石碍足，有大有小，有些极大。过了一阵，路好走起来，虽然崖壁低垂之处，时有宽阔的松散碎石坡，他们不得不爬上爬下。此后一段路上碎石之患暂歇，但河与崖之间的路又窄了起来，黑色峭壁愈长愈高，末了竟高到那般地步、路窄到那般地步，头顶的天对他们而言恍如身处井底，众人觉得由此处正午也能望见星辰。同时路早已一路攀升上去，虽然崖壁在头顶愈发高耸；末了他们不过是在一道窄窄的石架上行走，战栗川在远远的下方、在极高耸的笔直石壁之间翻滚哗然；头顶的崖壁则直插云霄，黑得如同隆冬无月无星之夜。川水在下方轰鸣，头顶则响着隘道之风不息的轰隆之声——那风顺着这条窄道猛灌而下，极其凌厉；风将他们的衣摆裹缠在膝上，他们逆风顶住其推力而行之时，脚下不时几乎被阻住。

===Original===
But as they mounted higher and higher yet, the noise of the waters swelled into a huge roar that drowned the bellowing of the prisoned wind, and down the pass came drifting a fine rain that fell not from the sky, for between the clouds of that drift could folk see the heavens bright and blue above them. This rain was but the spray of the great force up to whose steps they were climbing.

===Chinese===
然而他们愈攀愈高，水声愈涨愈大，终化作一片巨吼，将那被困之风的呼啸也尽数淹没；隘道之中飘来一阵细雨——这雨并非自天而降，因为透过那团飞雾之间的空隙，人们还能望见头顶之上天宇晴朗湛蓝。这雨不过是那道大瀑布溅起的水雾，他们正攀登向它的脚下。

===Original===
Now the way got rougher as they mounted; but this toil was caused by their gain; for the rock-wall, which thrust out a buttress there as if it would have gone to the very edge of the gap wherethrough the flood ran, and so have cut the way off utterly, was here somewhat broken down, and its stones scattered down the steep bent, so that there was a passage, though a toilsome one.

===Chinese===
他们愈往上攀，路愈崎岖；但这番劳苦正是他们升高所致；盖因此处石壁伸出一道支脉，仿佛要一直延到那洪水奔流之豁口的边缘，将通路彻底截断，然而在此处它已稍有坍塌，碎石散落于陡坡之上，于是尚有一条通路——虽然行之甚苦。

===Original===
Thus then through the wind-borne drift of the great force, through which men could see the white waters tossing down below, amidst the clattering thunder of the Shivering Flood and the rumble of the wind of the gap, that tore through their garments and hair as if it would rend all to rags and bear it away, the banners of the Wolf won their way to the crest of the midmost height of the pass, and the long line of the Host came clambering after them; and each band of warriors as it reached the top cast an unheard shout from amidst the tangled fury of wind and waters.

===Chinese===
于是，穿过那道大瀑布随风飘扬的水雾——透过水雾人们可以望见下方白色水浪翻腾——在战栗川哗然轰鸣之声与隘道之风的轰隆怒号之中（那风撕扯他们的衣裳头发，仿佛要将一切扯成碎布条卷走），狼族的旌旗终于夺路而抵隘道正中最高处的山顶；大军长长的队列在他们身后攀爬而上；每一队武士攀到顶上之时，都从那风与水交织的怒涛之中迸发出一声无人能闻的呐喊。

===Original===
A little further on and all that turmoil was behind them; the sun, now grown low, smote the wavering column of spray from the force at their backs, till the rainbows lay bright across it; and the sunshine lay wide over a little valley that sloped somewhat steeply to the west right up from the edge of the river; and beyond these western slopes could men see a low peak spreading down on all sides to the plain, till it was like to a bossed shield, and the name of it was Shield-broad. Dark grey was the valley everywhere, save that by the side of the water was a space of bright greensward hedged about toward the mountain by a wall of rocks tossed up into wild shapes of spires and jagged points. The river itself was spread out wide and shallow, and went rattling about great grey rocks scattered here and there amidst it, till it gathered itself together to tumble headlong over three slant steps into the mighty gap below.

===Chinese===
再往前走不多远，那一切喧嚣便都落到了他们身后；此时已低的太阳斜照在身后瀑布扬起的那柱摇曳水雾之上，于是道道彩虹明媚地横跨其上；阳光铺满一条小山谷——那山谷自河边起，向西颇陡地倾斜而上；在这些西坡之外，人们可以望见一座低峰向四面八方铺展至平原，末了形如一面中央带圆凸之盾，它的名字叫做盾阔（Shield-broad）。满谷皆呈深灰之色，唯有水边有一片明媚的青草地，朝山那一边为一道岩壁所围，那岩壁之石被抛成尖塔与锯齿参差的种种奇形。河水本身则又宽又浅地铺展开来，在散布其间的大块灰色岩石之间哗然奔流，直至汇拢起来，从三级倾斜的石阶上奋身翻落下去，坠入下方那巨大的豁口。

===Original===
From the height in the pass those grey slopes seemed easy to traverse; but the warriors of the Wolf knew that it was far otherwise, for they were but the molten rock-sea that in time long past had flowed forth from Shield-broad and filled up the whole valley endlong and overthwart, cooling as it flowed, and the tumbled hedge of rock round about the green plain by the river was where the said rock-sea had been stayed by meeting with soft ground, and had heaped itself up round about the greensward. And that great rock-flood as it cooled split in divers fashions; and the rain and weather had been busy on it for ages, so that it was worn into a maze of narrow paths, most of which, after a little, brought the wayfarer to a dead stop, or else led him back again to the place whence he had started; so that only those who knew the passes throughly could thread that maze without immeasurable labour.

===Chinese===
从隘道的高处望去，那些灰色山坡似乎不难跨越；但狼族武士深知远非如此——它们不过是远古之时自盾阔涌出的一片熔岩之海，曾纵横灌满整条山谷，一边流淌一边冷却；河边青草地四周那道乱石堆叠的岩壁，便是这片熔岩之海为软土所阻、在草地四周堆拥而成之处。那股巨大的岩浆之流在冷却之时以种种方式裂开；千万年来雨水与风霜不断侵蚀它，将其消磨成一座由窄径组成的迷宫，而这些窄径大多走不多远便将行人引到尽头，要么便将他引回出发点；故唯有彻底熟识路径之人，方能不费极大气力穿行那座迷宫。

===Original===
Now when the men of the Host looked from the high place whereon they stood toward the green plain by the river, they saw on the top of that rock-wall a red pennon waving on a spear, and beside it three or four weaponed men gleaming bright in the evening sun; and they waved their swords to the Host, and made lightning of the sunbeams, and the men of the Host waved swords to them in turn. For these were the outguards of the Host; and the place whereon they were was at whiles dwelt in by those who would drive the spoil in Silverdale, and midmost of the greensward was a booth builded of rough stones and turf, a refuge for a score of men in rough weather.

===Chinese===
当大军之人从所立的高处朝河边青草地望去时，只见那道岩壁顶上，一面红色三角旗在一杆长矛上飘扬，旁边有三四名持械之人，在夕阳下甲兵闪亮；他们朝大军挥剑，将阳光舞成一道道闪电，大军之人也挥剑还礼。原来这些正是大军的远哨；他们所在的这处地方，往日偶尔被那些要去银谷劫掠之人借宿；青草地正中有一座以粗石草皮搭就的棚屋，是恶劣天气时可容二十人栖身的避难之所。

===Original===
So the men of the vanward gat them down the hill, and made the best of their way toward the grassy plain through that rocky maze which had once been as a lake of molten glass; and as short as the way looked from above, it was two hours or ever they came out of it on to the smooth turf, and it was moonlight and night ere the House of the Face had gotten on to the greensward.

===Chinese===
于是前队之人下了山，竭力穿过那片昔日曾宛如一湖熔融玻璃的乱石迷宫，朝青草地赶去；从上面望去那段路虽显得很短，他们却走了两个时辰才从其中出来踏上平整的草地；待到面神之宅之人踏上那片青草地时，已是月华皎洁的夜里了。

===Original===
There then the Host abode for that night, and after they had eaten lay down on the green grass and slept as they might. Bow-may would have brought the Sun-beam into the booth with some others of the women, but she would not enter it, because she deemed that otherwise the Bride would abide without; and the Bride, when she came up, along with the House of the Steer, beheld the Sun-beam, that Wood-father’s children had made a lair for her without like a hare’s form; and forsooth many a time had she lain under the naked heaven in Shadowy Vale and the waste about it, even as the Bride had in the meadows of Burgdale. So when the Bride was bidden thereto, she went meekly into the booth, and lay there with others of the damsels-at-arms.

===Chinese===
大军便在那里歇宿过夜；众人吃完之后，便躺在青草之上，尽量入睡。弓娥本想把日光同另外几名女子一起带进棚屋里，她却不肯进去，因为她想，否则新娘也要在外过夜了；而新娘随犍牛族一行人赶上来时，看见日光——林父的子女们已在棚外为她铺了一个卧处，形如野兔的伏窝；诚然她在幽谷及其周围的荒野之中，已有过许多次露宿苍天之下的经历，正如新娘在堡谷的草甸之上也曾多次露宿一般。于是新娘受邀之后，便温顺地走进棚屋，与另外几名武装少女一同躺下歇息。

## XLVII The Kindreds Win the Mote-House / 四十七 诸宗族攻克议事堂

===Original===
The din and tumult still came from the north side of the Marketplace, so that all the air was full of noise; and Face-of-god deemed that the thralls had gotten weapons into their hands and were slaying their masters.

===Chinese===
集市坪北面仍旧传来喧闹鼎沸之声，满空为之震动；面神心想必是那些奴隶已夺得兵刃在手，正在诛杀其主。

===Original===
Now he lifted up his face, and put his hand on Folk-might’s shoulder, and said in a loud voice:

“Kinsmen, it were well if our brother were to bid the banners into the Mote-house of the Wolf, and let all the Host set itself in array before the said house, and abide till the chasers of the foe come to us thither; for I perceive that they are now become many, and are more than those of our kindred.”

Then Folk-might looked at him with kind eyes, and said:

“Thou sayest well, brother; even so let it be!”

And he lifted up his sword, and Face-of-god cried out in a loud voice: “Forward, banners! blow up horns! fare we forth with victory!”

===Chinese===
他于是扬起脸来，一手按在民强肩上，朗声说道：

"诸位宗亲，若由我们这位兄弟传令诸旗进狼之议事堂，令全军于该堂前列阵待命，等候追击来敌之我众到此会合，便甚妥当；因我见那些追兵如今已成大群，反比我等此处宗族之人更多。"

民强遂以亲切之目视之，说道：

"兄弟说得是；便如此办吧！"

他举起剑来，面神朗声高呼："旗帜前行！号角齐鸣！我军奏凯而进！"

===Original===
So the Host drew its ranks together in good order, and they all set forward, and old Stone-face took the Sun-beam by the hand and led on behind Folk-might and the War-leader. But when they came to the Hall, then saw they how the steps that led up to the door were high and double, going up from each side without any railing or fool-guard; and crowding the stairs and the platform thereof was a band of the Dusky Men, as many as could stand thereon, who shot arrows at the host of the kindreds, howling like dogs, and chattering like apes; and arrows and spears came from the windows of the Hall; yea, and on the very roof a score of these felons were riding the ridge and mocking like the trolls of old days.

===Chinese===
于是大军整队成列，井然向前开拔；老石面携日光之手，随在民强与战首之后同行。既至厅前，只见通向大门之台阶高峻而分作两股，自两侧各自拾级而上，并无栏干或防跌之护；阶梯与其上平台尽被一伙黝暗人挤满，能立几人便立几人，向宗族大军放箭，嗥如犬吠、噪如猿啼；箭与矛自厅堂窗中飞出；乃至屋脊之上，亦有二十名恶徒跨坐其上，如古时所传山魈恶鬼一般戏谑嘲笑。

===Original===
Now when they saw this they stayed a while, and men shielded them against the shafts; but the leaders drew together in front of the Host, and Folk-might fell to speech; and his face was very pale and stern; for now he had had time to think of the case of the Bride, and fierce wrath, and grief unholpen filled his soul. So he said:

“Brothers, this is my business to deal with; for I see before me the stair that leadeth to the Mote-house of my people, and now would I sit there whereas my fathers sat, when peace was on the Dale, as once more it shall be tomorrow. Therefore up this stair will I go, and none shall hinder me; and let no man of the host follow me till I have entered into the Hall, unless perchance I fall dead by the way; but stand ye still and look on.”

===Chinese===
众既见此，停步不前，举起盾牌遮挡箭矢；众首领聚于大军之前，民强开言；其面极为苍白严厉；盖此时他已得暇思及新娘之遭际，一腔怒火与无助之悲充满其心。遂说道：

"兄弟们，此事当由我来料理；我眼前所见，正是通向我族议事堂之阶，而今我欲坐于我父祖所坐之处——彼时谷中尚是太平，一如明日必将再归太平。故此我必登此阶，无人可挡；在我未入厅堂之前，军中任何人不得随我同上，除非我中途倒毙；尔等且伫立旁观。"

===Original===
“Nay,” said Face-of-god, “this is partly the business of the War-leader. There are two stairs. Be content to take the southern one, and I will take the northern. We shall meet on the plain stone at the top.”

But Hall-face said: “War-leader, may I speak?”

“Speak, brother,” said Face-of-god.

Said Hall-face: “I have done but little today, War-leader. I would stand by thee on the northern stair; so shall Folk-might be content, if he doeth two men’s work who are not little-hearted.”

Said Face-of-god: “The doom of the War-leader is that Folk-might shall fall on by the southern stair to slake his grief and increase his glory, and Face-of-god and Hall-face by the northern. Haste to the work, O brothers!”

===Chinese===
"不然，"面神道，"此亦是战首之分内事。台阶有两道。你且取南面一道，我取北面一道。我们当在阶顶那方平石之上相会。"

厅面却说："战首，我可否进一言？"

面神道："兄弟，但说无妨。"

厅面道："战首，我今日所建功业甚少。我愿随你立于北阶之上；如此则民强亦可遂其愿——他一人当两员不怯之将的活计。"

面神道："战首裁定如下：民强自南阶冲杀，以舒其悲而增其荣；面神与厅面自北阶冲杀。兄弟们，速速动手！"

===Original===
And he and Hall-face went to their places, while all looked on. But the Sun-beam, with her hand still in Stone-face’s, she turned white to the lips, and stared with wild eyes before her, not knowing where she was; for she had deemed that the battle was over, and Face-of-god saved from it.

===Chinese===
他与厅面遂各归其位，众人尽皆注视。而日光——一手仍握在石面手中——嘴唇都白了，双目发直、茫然前视，不知身在何处；盖她原以为战事已了、面神已安然而归。

===Original===
But Folk-might tossed up his head and laughed, and cried out, “At last, at last!” And his sword was in his hand, the Sleep-thorn to wit, a blade of ancient fame; so now he let it fall and hang to his wrist by the leash, while he clapped his hands together and uttered the Wolf-whoop mightily, and all the men of the Wolf that were in the host, and the Woodlanders withal, uttered it with him. Then he put his shield over his head and stood before the first of the steps, and the Dusky Men laughed to see one man come against them, though there was death in their hearts. But he laughed back at them in triumph, and set his foot on the step, and let Sleep-thorn’s point go into the throat of a Dusky lord, and thrust amongst them, hewing right and left, and tumbling men over the edge of the stair, which was to them as the narrow path along the cliff-side that hangeth over the unfathomed sea. They hewed and thrust at him in turn; but so close were they packed that their weapons crossed about him, and one shielded him from the other, and they swayed staggering on that fearful verge, while the Sleep-thorn crept here and there amongst them, lulling their hot fury. For, as desperate as they were, and fighting for death and not for life, they had a horror of him and of the sea of hatred below them, and feared where to set their feet, and he feared nought at all, but from feet to sword-point was but an engine of slaughter, while the heart within him throbbed with fury long held back as he thought upon the Bride and her wounding, and all the wrongs of his people since their Great Undoing.

===Chinese===
民强却仰头大笑，高呼道："终有此时，终有此时！"他手中之剑——即睡刺（Sleep-thorn），一柄古来驰名之刃——此刻被他一松，凭系于腕间的剑绳垂下；他一面鼓掌，一面厉声发出狼吼（the Wolf-whoop），军中一切狼族之人、并林中之民，皆随之同吼。继而他将盾顶在头上，立于第一级阶前，众黝暗人见一人独来攻，皆大笑，虽然其心已存必死之志。他却以凯旋之笑回敬，一脚踏上石阶，让睡刺之尖刺入一名黝暗贵人之咽喉，闯入人群，左右劈砍，将人纷纷自阶沿翻落下去——那阶沿于他们，不啻悬于无底海上的崖畔狭径。他们回身劈砍刺击；但他们挤得太密，兵刃在他四周相互交错，一人反替他挡了另一人之击，在那可怖的阶沿上摇晃踉跄；而睡刺则在人群中四处游走，将其狂暴一一催入长眠。盖他们虽已绝望、虽为求死而战非为求生而战，却对这个人、对脚下那片仇恨之海心存恐惧，不知何处下脚；而他毫无所惧，自足至剑尖无非一具杀戮之器，其心搏动不已，满腔积压已久之怒火——一念及新娘与其所受之伤、一念及自大倾覆以来其族所受之种种冤屈。

===Original===
So he smote and thrust, till him-seemed the throng of foes thinned before him: with his sword-pommel he smote a lord of the Dusky Ones in the face, so that he fell over the edge amongst the spears of the kindred; then he thrust the point of Sleep-thorn towards the Hall-door through the breast of another, and then it seemed to him that he had but one before him; so he hove up the edges to cleave him down, but ere the stroke fell, close to his ears exceeding loud rang out the cry, “For the Burg and the Face! for the Face, for the Face!” and he drew aback a little, and his eyes cleared, and lo! it was Hall-face the tall, his long sword all reddened with battle; and beside him stood Face-of-god, silent and panting, his face pale with the fierce anger of the fight, and the weariness which was now at last gaining upon him. There stood those three with no other living man upon the plain of the stairs.

===Chinese===
他一路劈砍刺杀，直杀到眼前敌锋渐稀：以剑首击中一名黝暗贵人之面，那人翻落阶沿，坠入宗族众矛之中；继而又将睡刺之尖透过另一人胸膛，直指向厅门；此时他只觉眼前仅剩一人；遂高举双刃欲将其劈倒，然那一击尚未落下，耳畔忽闻大声疾呼："为堡与面！为面、为面！"他略退半步，双目一清，看哪！却是高大的厅面，长剑之上尽染战血；其旁立着面神，默然喘息，面色苍白——一则因战斗之烈怒，二则因终于袭来之疲倦。三人立于那片阶顶平地之上，再无第四个活人。

===Original===
Then Face-of-god turned shouting to the Folk, and cried:

“Forth now with the banners! For now is the Wolf come home. On into the Hall, O Kindred of the Gods!”

Then poured the Folk up over the stairs and into the Hall of the Wolf, the banners flapping over their heads; and first went the War-leader and Folk-might and Hall-face, and then the three delivered thralls, Wolf-stone, God-swain, and Spear-fist, and Dallach with them, though both he and Wolf-stone had been hurt in the battle; and then came blended together the Men of the Face along with them of the Wolf who had entered the Marketstead with them, and with these were Stone-face and Wood-wont and Bow-may, leading the Sun-beam betwixt them; and now was she come to herself again, though her face was yet pale, and her eyes gleamed as she stepped across the threshold of the Hall.

===Chinese===
面神遂转向众人高呼，喊道：

"旗帜前行！狼已归家。诸神之宗族啊，杀入厅堂去！"

众人遂如潮水般涌上台阶、涌入狼之厅堂，旗帜在众人头顶猎猎飘扬；当先者是战首与民强、厅面；其次是三名得释之奴——狼石（Wolf-stone）、神仆（God-swain）、矛拳（Spear-fist）——达拉赫也与之同在，虽他与狼石俱已在战中受伤；继之是面族之人与初入集市坪时同来的狼族人混作一处，其中尚有石面、林习、弓娥，三人搀扶着日光走在中间；此时她已神魂初定，面色犹白，双目却在迈过厅堂门槛之时闪闪生光。

===Original===
But when a many were gotten in, and the first-comers had had time to handle their weapons and look about them, a cry of the utmost wrath broke from Folk-might and those others who remembered the Hall from of old. For wretched and befouled was that well-builded house: the hangings rent away; the goodly painted walls daubed and smeared with wicked tokens of the Alien murderers: the floor, once bright with polished stones of the mountain, and strewn with sweet-smelling flowers, was now as foul as the den of the man-devouring troll of the heaths. From the fair-carven roof of oak and chestnut-beams hung ugly knots of rags and shapeless images of the sorcery of the Dusky Men. And furthermore, and above all, from the last tie-beam of the roof over the dais dangled four shapes of men-at-arms, whom the older men of the Wolf knew at once for the embalmed bodies of their four great chieftains, who had been slain on the day of the Great Undoing; and they cried out with horror and rage as they saw them hanging there in their weapons as they had lived.

===Chinese===
及至大批人众涌入，先入者得暇整理兵刃、环顾四周，民强与那些还记得此厅旧貌之人，尽皆发出一腔震天之怒。盖那座营建精良之屋，已被糟蹋得不堪入目：帷幕尽被撕裂；彩绘之美墙为外族凶手种种邪恶魔记涂抹污损：其地本以磨光山石铺就、香花满布，如今却秽如荒原食人山魈之巢。橡与栗木所雕之美栋之下，悬着一团团丑陋之破布结、一尊尊黝暗人巫术所制之无形怪像。更有甚者、最为可怖者——高台之上屋顶最后一道横梁之上，悬着四具甲士之躯；狼族老者一眼便认出，那是他们四大首领经防腐处理的尸身——皆是当年大倾覆之日被杀之人；众人见他们身着生前甲胄兵刃、如生时一般悬在那里，皆以惊骇与愤怒相呼。

===Original===
There was the Hostage of the Earth, his shield painted with the green world circled with the worm of the sea. There was the older Folk-might, the uncle of the living man, bearing a shield with an oak and a lion done thereon. There was Wealth-eker, on whose shield was done a golden sheaf of wheat. There was he who bore a name great from of old, Folk-wolf to wit, bearing on his shield the axe of the hewer. There they hung, dusty, befouled, with sightless eyes and grinning mouths, in the dimmed sunlight of the Hall, before the eyes of that victorious Host, stricken silent at the sight of them.

===Chinese===
其一为地之质（the Hostage of the Earth），其盾上绘着绿色的大地，外绕以海中之巨蟒。其二为老民强，即今在世民强之叔，盾上绘着一株橡树与一头雄狮。其三为富积（Wealth-eker），其盾上绘着一束金色的麦穗。其四乃自古声名赫赫之人，名唤族狼（Folk-wolf），盾上绘着樵夫之斧。四人悬于该处，尘封垢污，目盲口龇，在厅堂昏暗的日光里，悬于那支见之默然无声的得胜大军眼前。

===Original===
Underneath them on the dais stood the last remnant of the battle of the Dusky Men; and they, as men mad with coming death, shook their weapons, and with shrieking laughter mocked at the overcomers, and pointed to the long-dead chiefs, and called on them in the tongue of the kindreds to come down and lead their dear kinsmen to the high-seat; and then they cried out to the living warriors of the Wolf, and bade them better their deed of slaying, and set to work to make alive again, and cause their kinsmen to live merry on the earth.

With that last mock they handled their weapons and rushed howling on the warriors to meet their death; nor was it long denied them; for the sword of the Wolf, the axe of the Woodland, and the spear of the Dale soon made an end of the dreadful lives of these destroyers of the Folks.

===Chinese===
其下高台之上，立着黝暗人战阵中所余的最后一批；他们如将死而发狂之人，挥舞兵刃，以尖笑嘲弄战胜之人，指着那些死去已久的首领，用宗族之语唤他们下来、引导亲爱的族亲登上高座；继而又向活着的狼族武士大喊，叫他们胜过杀人之举，动手使死人复生，让其族亲在世间重新欢乐度日。

说完这最后一番嘲讽，他们握紧兵刃，嗥叫着扑向众武士，前去受死；其死也不久即如愿以偿：盖狼之剑、林之斧、谷之矛，顷刻之间便了结了这些屠族者可怖的一生。

## XXVIII The Men of Burgdale Meet the Runaways / 二十八 堡谷之人遇见逃亡者

===Original===
Now ere the night was far spent, Dallach arose and said:
“Kind folk, ye will presently be sleeping; but I bid you keep a good watch, and if ye will be ruled by me, ye will kindle no fire on the morrow, for the smoke riseth thick in the morning air, and is as a beacon. As for me, I shall leave you here to rest, and I myself will fare on mine errand.”

They bade him sleep and rest him after so many toils and hardships, saying that they were not tied to an hour to be back in Burgdale; but he said: “Nay, the moon is high, and it is as good as daylight to me, who could find my way even by starlight; and your tarrying here is nowise safe. Moreover, if I could find those folk and bring them part of the way by night and cloud it were well; for if we were taken again, burning quick would be the best death by which we should die. As for me, now am I strong with meat and drink and hope; and when I come to Burgdale there will be time enough for resting and slumber.”

===Chinese===
话说夜尚未深，达拉赫（Dallach）起身说道：
"诸位好心人，你们马上就要安歇了；但我劝你们务要好好守望，若肯听我一言，明日切莫生火——晨间烟雾腾起，浓重直上，便如一座烽燧。至于我，我要把你们留在此处歇息，我自己则去办我的事。"

众人劝他历经这许多劳苦艰辛，理当睡一觉歇一歇，说他们回堡谷（Burgdale）并不拘定甚么时辰；他却道："不然，月已高悬，于我如同白昼，便凭星光我也能寻得路；你们在此逗留，实在不稳当。况且，我若能趁着夜色云影寻见那些人，领他们走上一程，岂不是好？因为我们若是再被拿住，活活烧死怕已是最好的死法了。至于我，如今吃饱喝足、心怀盼望，气力正壮；待我到了堡谷，歇息睡觉的时辰多的是。"

===Original===
Said Face-of-god: “Shall I not wend with thee to see these people and the lairs wherein they hide?”

The man smiled: “Nay, earl,” said he, “that shall not be. For wot ye what? If they were to see me in company of a man-at-arms they would deem that I was bringing the foe upon them, and would flee, or mayhappen would fall upon us. For as for me, when I saw thee, thou wert close anigh me, so I knew thee to be no Dusky Man; but they would see the glitter of thine arms from afar, and to them all weaponed men are foemen. Thou, lord, knowest not the heart of a thrall, nor the fear and doubt that is in it. Nay, I myself must cast off these clothes that ye have given me, and fare naked, lest they mistrust me. Only I will take a spear in my hand, and sling a knife round my neck, if ye will give them to me; for if the worst happen, I will not be taken alive.”

Therewith he cast off his raiment, and they gave him the weapons and wished him good speed, and he went his way twixt moonlight and shadow; but the Burgdalers went to sleep when they had set a watch.

===Chinese===
面神道："我不同你一道去看看那些人，看看他们藏身的窝巢么？"

那人微微一笑，道："不，首领（earl），"他说，"这却使不得。你可知缘故？他们若是见我与一个顶盔贯甲之人同行，必当我是引来敌寇，或逃、或竟来攻杀我们。至于我，初见你时你离我甚近，故而我知你不是黝暗人（Dusky Man）；可他们老远便会望见你兵刃上的闪光，在他们的眼里，凡是持兵刃之人皆为仇敌。大人，你不晓得一个奴隶的心，不晓得那里头装的恐惧与疑虑。不，连我自己也须脱去你们给我的这些衣裳，赤身而去，免得他们疑心于我。只消你们肯给我一杆矛握在手中，再把一柄刀悬在颈间，我便知足；万一事急，我决不甘心被活捉。"

说罢他便脱去衣裳，众人给了他那几件兵刃，祝他一路顺风；他便在月光与阴影之间上路去了。堡谷之人则派定了守望，也各自睡下。

===Original===
Early in the morning they awoke, and the sun was shining and the thrushes singing in the thorn-brake, and all seemed fair and peaceful, and a little haze still hung about the face of the burg over the river. So they went down to the water and washed the night from off them; and thence the most part of them went back to their lair among the thorn-bushes: but four of them went up the dale into the oak-wood to shoot a buck, and five more they sent out to watch their skirts around them; and Face-of-god with old Stone-face went over a ford of the stream, and came on to the lower slope of the burg, and so went up it to the top. Thence they looked about to see if aught were stirring, but they saw little save the waste and the wood, which on the northeast was thick of big trees stretching out a long way. Their own lair was clear to see over its bank and the bushes thereof, and that misliked Face-of-god, lest any foe should climb the burg that day. The morning was clear, and Face-of-god looking north-and-by-west deemed he saw smoke rising into the air over the tree-covered ridges that hid the further distance toward that airt, though further east uphove the black shoulders of the Great that Waste and the snowy peaks behind them. The said smoke was not such as cometh from one great fire, but was like a thin veil staining the pale blue sky, as when men are burning ling on the heath-side and it is seen aloof.

===Chinese===
