清晨他们醒来，日头正明，荆棘丛中鸫鸟啼鸣，万物都显得明媚安宁，河对面那座山堡（burg）的面上犹自挂着一层薄雾。他们便下到水边，洗去一夜的尘劳；随后大多数人回到荆棘丛中的窝巢里去；其中四人沿谷而上，进入橡林去射一头雄鹿，又派出五人到四周外围去放哨守望；面神则与老石面（Stone-face）涉过溪流的一道浅滩，来到山堡下方较缓的坡脚，由此攀上了山顶。二人站在高处四下眺望，看可有甚么动静，却几乎一无所见，但见一片荒原、一片林木，东北方一带大树浓密，迤逦延伸出去好远。他们自己的藏身之处隔着土坎和一丛丛灌木也看得清清楚楚，面神心下不乐，只怕当日会有敌寇爬上山堡来。那早天气清朗，面神朝北偏西的方向望去，只见遮断那一带远处、覆满林木的山脊之上，似有一缕烟升入空中；再往东一些，大荒原（the Great Waste）的黑色山肩便高高拱起，其后还有一座座积雪的峰峦。那烟并非一处大火所起，倒像一层薄纱，染污了淡蓝的天色，正如人在石楠坡上焚烧石楠花、远远望去的样子。

===Original===
He showed that smoke to Stone-face, who smiled and said:
“Now will they be lighting the cooking fires in Rosedale: would I were there with a few hundreds of axes and staves at my back!”

“Yea,” said Face-of-god, smiling in his face, “but where I pray thee are these elves and wood-wights, that we meet them not? Grim things there are in the woods, and things fair enough also: but meseemeth that the trolls and the elves of thy young years have been frighted away.”

Said Stone-face: “Maybe, foster-son; that hath been seen ere now, that when one race of man overrunneth the land inhabited by another, the wights and elves that love the vanquished are seen no more, or get them away far off into the outermost wilds, where few men ever come.”

“Yea,” said Face-of-god, “that may well be. But deemest thou by that token that we shall be vanquished?”

“As for us, I know not,” said Stone-face; “but thy friends of Shadowy Vale have been vanquished. Moreover, concerning these felons whom now we are hunting, are we all so sure that they be men? Certain it is, that when I go into battle with them, I shall smite with no more pity than my sword, as if I were smiting things that may not feel the woes of man.”

===Chinese===
他将那烟指给石面看，石面微微一笑，道：
"这会儿他们该在玫瑰谷（Rosedale）生火做饭了：恨不得我身后能带上几百柄斧头、几百根棍棒，与他们同去！"

"是啊，"面神朝他脸上含笑说道，"可是我且问你，你说的那些精灵林怪都在哪里呢，怎么一个也碰不上？林子里固然有狰狞之物，也不乏秀美之属：只是我看，你年少时那些山魈精灵，怕早被吓跑了。"

石面道："也许罢，义子（foster-son）；这种事从前也是有的：当一族之人征服另一族所居之地时，那些亲近败族的灵怪精灵便从此不见，或远远遁入人迹罕至的极荒之野去了。"

面神道："是了，这倒也说得通。不过照这个征候看来，你以为我们也要被人征服么？"

"至于我们，我不知晓，"石面道，"但你在幽谷（Shadowy Vale）的那些朋友，确是被征服过了。再者说，如今我们所追讨的这伙恶徒，我们岂能那么确信他们也是人？有一件事是确定的——待我上阵与他们交锋之时，我的剑落下绝不留情，便仿佛砍的是那些不能感知人之苦难的物件一般。"

===Original===
Said Face-of-god: “Yea, even so shall it be with me. But what thinkest thou of these runaways? Shall we have tidings of them, or shall Dallach bring the foe upon us? It was for the sake of that question that I have clomb the burg: and that we might watch the land about us.”

“Nay,” said Stone-face, “I have seen many men, and I deem of Dallach that he is a true man. I deem we shall soon have tidings of his fellows; and they may have seen the elves and wood-wights: I would fain ask them thereof, and am eager to see them.”

Said Face-of-god: “And I somewhat dread to see them, and their rags and their misery and the weals of their stripes. It irked me to see Dallach when he first fell to his meat last night, how he ate like a dog for fear and famine. How shall it be, moreover, when we have them in the Dale, and they fall to the deed of kind there, as they needs must. Will they not bear us evil and thrall-like men?”

“Maybe,” said Stone-face, “and maybe not; for they have been thralls but for a little while: and I deem that in no long time shall ye see them much bettered by plenteous meat and rest. And after all is said, this Dallach bore him like a valiant man; also it was valiant of him to flee; and of the others may ye say the like. But look you! there are men going down yonder towards our lair: belike those shall be our guests, and there be no Dusky Men amongst them. Come, let us home!”

===Chinese===
面神道："是了，我也是这般。只是你对这些逃亡者怎么看？我们能不能得到他们的消息，还是达拉赫反而会把敌寇引来？正是为了这一点，我才爬上这山堡：好把四周的土地看个分明。"

石面道："不然。我见过的人多了，我看达拉赫是个实诚人。我想我们很快便会有他那些同伴的消息；他们说不定见过那些精灵林怪：我正想拿这话问问他们，巴不得早些见到他们呢。"

面神道："我却有些怕见他们，怕见他们的破衣烂衫、他们的凄惨模样和他们身上一道道鞭痕。昨夜达拉赫头一回扑在食物上的时候，我看他心有余悸、饿得慌了，吃得像条狗似的，我心里就不好受。再者，待我们把人带到谷里，他们必然要在那儿成其男女之事——这事终究免不了——到那时又当如何？他们岂不会变成一帮粗鄙的、奴才似的坏人？"

石面道："或许如此，或许不然；因为他们做奴为时不久：我想用不了多久，丰足的饮食和休养便会使他们大见起色。说到底，这个达拉赫举止像个勇士；他那回出逃，也是一桩勇举；其余的人，你大可作如是观。你看！那边有人正朝我们的窝巢下去：多半就是我们那些客人了，里头没有黝暗人。走，我们回去罢！"

===Original===
So Face-of-god looked and beheld from the height of the burg shapes of men grey and colourless creeping toward the lair from sunshine to shadow, like wild creatures shy and fearful of the hunter, or so he deemed of them.

So he turned away, angry and sad of heart, and the twain went down the burg and across the water to their camp, having seen little to tell of from the height.

===Chinese===
于是面神举目望去，从山堡高处看见几个灰扑扑、没有血色的人影，正从阳光里潜行入阴影，朝那窝巢而去，像那惧怕猎人、怯生生的野兽——至少他心里这般想。

他便转过身去，又怒又悲，二人下了山堡，涉水回到营地；在高处其实没看到甚么值得说的。

===Original===
When they came to their campment there were their folk standing in a ring round about Dallach and the other runaways. They made way for the War-leader and Stone-face, who came amongst them and beheld the Runaways, that they were many more than they looked to see; for they were of carles one score and three, and of women eighteen, all told save Dallach. When they saw those twain come through the ring of men and perceived that they were chieftains, some of them fell down on their knees before them and held out their joined hands to them, and kissed the Burgdalers’ feet and the hems of their garments, while the tears streamed out of their eyes: some stood moving little and staring before them stupidly: and some kept glancing from face to face of the well-liking happy Burgdale carles, though for a while even their faces were sad and downcast at the sight of the poor men: some also kept murmuring one or two words in their country tongue, and Dallach told Face-of-god that these were crying out for victual.

===Chinese===
待他们回到营地，只见自己的人已围成一圈，将达拉赫和其余逃亡者围在当中。众人让开一条路给战首（War-leader）和石面，二人走进圈内，打量那些逃亡者——人数之多，远出他们所料：男子二十三名，女子十八名，除达拉赫在外，合计如此。那些人见这二人穿过人环进来，又认出他们是首领，便有人跪倒在他们面前，将合拢的双手伸向他们，亲吻堡谷人的脚和衣襟，泪水夺眶而出；有人站着几乎不动，呆呆地望着他们；也有人的目光不停地在那些体面快活的堡谷汉子脸上一张张扫过，虽说开头连那些汉子的脸，见到这般可怜人时也是悲戚低沉的；还有人不断用本乡话喃喃念着一两个字，达拉赫告诉面神，这些人是喊着要吃的。

===Original===
It must be said of these poor folk that they were of divers conditions, and chiefly of three: and first there were seven of Rosedale and five of Silverdale late come to the wood (of these Silverdalers Dallach had told but of two, for the other three were but just come). Of these twelve were seven women, and all, save two of the women, were clad in one scanty kirtle or shirt only; for such was the wont of the Dusky Men with their thralls. They had brought away weapons, and had amongst them six axes and a spear, and a sword, and five knives, and one man had a shield.

===Chinese===
说起这些可怜人，须得交代一句：他们出身各异，大致可分三类：第一类是七个玫瑰谷人和五个银谷（Silverdale）人，新近逃入林中（这五个银谷人里，达拉赫先前只提过两个，因为其余三个才到不久）。这十二人里有七个是女子，除两名女子外，都只穿着一件窄小的短袍或衫子；因为黝暗人对待奴隶的惯例便是如此。他们逃出时带了几件兵器，共有六柄斧、一杆矛、一口剑、五柄刀，还有一人带了一面盾。

===Original===
Yet though these were clad and armed, yet in some wise were they the worst of all; they were so timorous and cringing, and most of them heavy-eyed and sullen and down-looking. Many of them had been grievously mishandled: one man had had his left hand smitten off; another was docked of three of his toes, and the gristle of his nose slit up; one was halt, and four had been ear-cropped, nor did any lack weals of whipping. Of the Silverdale newcomers the three men were the worst of all the Runaways, with wild wandering eyes, but sullen also, and cringing if any drew nigh, and would not look anyone in the face, save presently Face-of-god, on whom they were soon fond to fawn, as a dog on his master. But the women who were with them, and who were well-nigh as timorous as the men, were those two gaily-dad ones, and they were soft-handed and white-skinned, save for the last days of weather in the wood; for they had been bed-thralls of the Dusky Men.

===Chinese===
然而这一类人虽有衣裳、有兵器，在某种意义上却是所有人里最糟的；他们胆小畏缩，多半眼神发木，闷闷不乐，垂头丧气。他们中许多人受过残酷的虐害：一人左手被砍掉；一人被削去三根脚趾，鼻软骨也被划开；一人瘸腿；四人被割过耳朵；至于鞭痕，更是人人都有。银谷新来的那三人，是所有逃亡者里最不堪的，眼神狂乱游移，却又阴沉，有人走近便瑟缩，不肯正眼看任何人，唯有不久之后对面神例外——很快他们便像狗对主人一般缠着他献媚。至于与他们同来的女子，虽说几乎和男子一样胆小，却是那两个衣着鲜丽的人，她们手细皮白——除了这几天在林中风吹日晒的缘故；因为她们本是黝暗人的床奴。

===Original===
Such were the newcomers to the wood. But others had been, like Dallach, months therein; it may be said that there were eighteen of these, carles and queens together. Little raiment they had amongst them, and some were all but stark naked, so that on these might well be seen as on Dallach the marks of old stripes, and of these also were there men who had been shorn of some member or other, and they were all burnt and blackened by the weather of the woodland; yet for all their nakedness, they bore themselves bolder and more manlike than the later comers, nor did they altogether lack weapons taken from their foemen, and most of them had some edge-tool or another. Of these folk were four from Silverdale, though Dallach knew it not.

===Chinese===
新入林的人便是这般模样。还有一些人，则与达拉赫一样，在林中已住了数月；这些人可以说有十八名，男女合计。他们衣衫极少，有的几乎赤身露体，于是和达拉赫一样，旧鞭痕在他们身上清晰可见；其中也有人被割去这样那样的肢体，一个个都被林地里的风雨晒得焦黑；然而尽管如此赤裸，他们的举止却比后来者更为胆壮、更有男子气概，手里也不全然没有从敌人手中夺来的兵器，多数人都有一两件带刃的家伙。这些人里有四个银谷人，只是达拉赫并不知晓。

===Original===
Besides these were a half score and one who had been years in the wood instead of months; weather-beaten indeed were these, shaggy and rough-skinned like wild men of kind. Some of them had made themselves skin breeches or clouts, some went stark naked; of weapons of the Dale had they few, but they bore bows of hazel or wych-elm strung with deer-gut, and shafts headed with flint stones; staves also of the same fashion, and great clubs of oak or holly: some of them also had made them targets of skin and willow-twigs, for these were the warriors of the Runaways: they had a few steel knives amongst them, but had mostly learned the craft of using sharp flints for knives: but four of these were women.

Three of these men were of the kindreds of the Wolf from Silverdale, and had been in the wood for hard upon ten years, and wild as they were, and without hope of meeting their fellows again, they went proudly and boldly amongst the others, overtopping them by the head and more. For the greater part of these men were somewhat short of stature, though by nature strong and stout of body.

===Chinese===
除此之外，还有十一个人在林中已住了好几年，而非区区数月；他们确实饱受风霜，毛发蓬乱、皮肤粗砺，天性一如野人。有人给自己做了皮裤或遮羞布，有人则赤身露体；谷里所产的兵器他们几乎没有，却带着榛木或山榆木做的弓，以鹿筋为弦，箭头是燧石磨成；又有同样制式的木棒，以及橡木、冬青的大棍：有些人还用兽皮和柳枝给自己做了盾——这些人便是逃亡者中的战士：他们中间共有几柄铁刀，但大多已学会用利燧石当刀使的功夫：他们之中有四个是女子。

这些人里有三个男子，出身银谷的狼之氏族（the kindreds of the Wolf），在林中已住了将近十年；他们尽管粗野，也不存再会族人之望，走在众人当中却昂首阔步、气概不凡，比众人高出一头还多。因为这些人大多身材偏矮，虽说天生筋骨强健壮实。

===Original===
It must be told that though Dallach had thus gotten all these many Runaways together, yet had they not been dwelling together as one folk; for they durst not, lest the Dusky Men should hear thereof and fall upon them, but they had kept themselves as best they could in caves and in brakes three together or two, or even faring alone as Dallach did: only as he was a strong and stouthearted man, he went to and fro and wandered about more than the others, so that he foregathered with most of them and knew them. He said also that he doubted not but that there were more Runaways in the wood, but these were all he could come at. Divers who had fled had died from time to time, and some had been caught and cruelly slain by their masters. They were none of them old; the oldest, said Dallach, scant of forty winters, though many from their aspect might have been old enough.

===Chinese===
还有一节须得交代：达拉赫虽把这许多逃亡者都聚到一处，他们原先却并非如一族人那样住在一起；他们不敢，怕黝暗人听闻了来攻，只得以洞穴、以荆棘丛为藏身之处，三人或两人一组，乃至像达拉赫那样独行：只因他是个身强胆壮的汉子，比旁人更敢四下走动游荡，这才与大多数人都照过面、彼此相识。他又说，他确信林中还有别的逃亡者，只是他能寻见的就这些了。逃出来的人陆续有死的，也有被主人抓回去残酷处死的。他们当中没有一个老者；据达拉赫说，最年长的也不过勉强四十个冬天，虽然单看模样，许多人显得老得多。

===Original===
So Face-of-god looked and beheld all these poor people; and said to himself, that he might well have dreaded that sight. For here was he brought face to face with the Sorrow of the Earth, whereof he had known nought heretofore, save it might be as a tale in a minstrel’s song. And when he thought of the minutes that had made the hours, and the hours that had made the days that these men had passed through, his heart failed him, and he was dumb and might not speak, though he perceived that the men of Burgdale looked for speech from him; but he waved his hand to his folk, and they understood him, for they had heard Dallach say that some of them were crying for victual. So they set to work and dighted for them such meat as they had, and they set them down on the grass and made themselves their carvers and serving-men, and bade them eat what they would of such as there was. Yet, indeed, it grieved the Burgdalers again to note how these folk were driven to eat; for they themselves, though they were merry folk, were exceeding courteous at table, and of great observance of manners: whereas these poor Runaways ate, some of them like hungry dogs, and some hiding their meat as if they feared it should be taken from them, and some cowering over it like falcons, and scarce any with a manlike pleasure in their meal. And, their eating over, the more part of them sat dull and mopish, and as if all things were forgotten for the time present.

===Chinese===
面神望着这一切，打量尽这些可怜人；暗自说道：他先前会惧怕见这番光景，原是难怪的。因为此刻他直面了这世间的苦难（the Sorrow of the Earth）——这苦难他从前一无所知，至多不过在吟游诗人的歌里当作一个故事听过。当他想到这些人所度过的一分一分积成一时、一时一时积成一日的那许多日子，他便心灰气馁，哑口无言，虽然他看出堡谷之人正等着他开口；他只朝自己人摆了摆手，众人便明白了他的意思，因为他们已听达拉赫说过，有些人正喊着要吃的。于是他们动手，把手上所有的肉食替他们整治好，请他们在草地上坐下，自己作了切肉的人、伺候的人，叫他们随便吃，有甚么吃甚么。然而堡谷人再度看在眼里，又是心酸：因为他们自己虽是乐天的人，在饭桌上却极其有礼，处处讲究规矩：而这些可怜的逃亡者吃东西的样子，有的像饿狗，有的把肉食藏起来，仿佛怕被人夺了去，有的像只鹰隼似地蹲伏在食物上，几乎没一个人吃东西带着点像人一样的乐趣。吃罢，他们大半都木然坐着、呆呆发愣，仿佛眼下一切都已被遗忘。

===Original===
Albeit presently Dallach bestirred him and said to Face-of-god: “Lord of the Earl-folk, if I might give thee rede, it were best to turn your faces to Burgdale without more tarrying. For we are over-nigh to Rosedale, being but thus many in company. But when we come to our next resting-place, then shall bring thee to speech with the last-comers from Silverdale; for there they talk with the tongue of the kindreds; but we of Rosedale for the more part talk otherwise; though in my house it came down from father to son.”

“Yea,” said Face-of-god, gazing still on that unhappy folk, as they sat or lay upon the grass at rest for a little while: but him-seemed as he gazed that some memories of past time stirred in some of them; for some, they hung their heads and the tears stole out of their eyes and rolled down their cheeks. But those older Runaways of Silverdale were not crouched down like most of the others, but strode up and down like beasts in a den; yet were the tears on the face of one of these. Then Face-of-god constrained himself, and spake to the folk, and said: “We are now over-nigh to our foes of Rosedale to lie here any longer, being too few to fall upon them. We will come hither again with a host when we have duly questioned these men who have sought refuge with us: and let us call yonder height the Burg of the Runaways, and it shall be a landmark for us when we are on the road to Rosedale.”

===Chinese===
不多时，达拉赫又活动起来，对面神道："贵胄之民（Earl-folk）的首领，若容我进一言，最好不要再耽搁，立即掉头回堡谷去。因为我们离玫瑰谷太近，而人数又只有这些。待我们到了下一处歇脚之地，我便领您与银谷最后逃出的那些人对上话；因为在那边，人们说的还是各氏族的语言；我们玫瑰谷人大多说的是另一种话；只是在我家中，那族语是父传子、世代传下来的。"

"好，"面神应道，眼睛仍望着那些不幸的人，看他们或坐或躺在草地上略作喘息：但他凝望之际，觉得他们有些人似乎被往事的记忆触动了；有些人低垂着头，泪水悄悄涌出眼眶，顺着脸颊滚落。银谷那些较早逃出的逃亡者，并不像大多数旁人那样蜷蹲着，却像笼中困兽一般大步走来走去；然而其中一个脸上也挂着泪。于是面神强自振作，对众人说道："我们此刻离玫瑰谷的仇敌太近，不能再在此停留了，我们人数太少，不足进攻他们。待我们把前来投奔的这些人好好问过一番，再来时便要带一支大军前来：我们就把那边那座高地叫作逃奴堡（the Burg of the Runaways）罢，日后我们往玫瑰谷进军的路上，它可作一个路标。"

===Original===
Then the Burgdalers bade the Runaways courteously and kindly to arise and take the road with them; and by that time were their men all come in; and four of them had venison with them, which was needful, if they were to eat that night or the morrow, as the guests had eaten them to the bone.

So they tarried no more, but set out on the homeward way; and Face-of-god bade Dallach walk beside him, and asked him such concerning Rosedale and its Dusky Men. Dallach told him that these were not so many as they were masterful, not being above eight hundreds of men, all fighting-men. As to women, they had none of their own race, but lay with the Daleswomen at their will, and begat children of them; and all or most of the said children favoured the race of their begetters. Of the men-children they reared most, but the women-children they slew at once; for they valued not women of their own blood: but besides the women of the Dale, they would go at whiles in bands to the edges of the Plain and beguile wayfarers, and bring back with them thence women to be their bed-thralls; albeit some of these were bought with a price from the Westland men.

As to the number of the folk of Rosedale, its own folk, he said they would number some five thousand souls, one with another; of whom some thousand might be fit to bear arms if they had the heart thereto, as they had none. Yet being closely questioned, he deemed that they might fall on their masters from behind, if battle were joined.

===Chinese===
于是堡谷人客客气气、和颜悦色地请逃亡者们起身，随他们上路；其时他们的人已全部归来；其中四人带回了鹿肉——这是必需的，如果他们今夜或明日还想吃东西的话，因为客人们已把他们先前的存粮啃到了骨头。

于是他们不再耽搁，动身踏上归途；面神叫达拉赫走在他身旁，向他打听玫瑰谷及其黝暗人的种种情形。达拉赫告诉他，黝暗人之所以难对付，不在于人多，而在于横行霸道；他们总共不过八百来人，全是能战之兵。至于女子，他们本族并没有，只是随意霸占谷民（the Daleswomen）的女子，与之生养后代；这些孩子全部或大多数都随其生父之族。男孩他们大多养大，女婴则一落地便杀掉；因为他们并不看重自己血统的女子：但除了谷地的女子之外，他们还时常成群结伙到平原（the Plain）的边缘去诱骗过路的行人，把女子掳回去做床奴；其中也有一些，是用价钱从西地人（Westland men）手里买来的。

至于玫瑰谷本族的人丁，他说男女老少算在一起，约有五千之众；其中约一千人若胆子够大，是可以拿起兵器的，可惜他们全无此胆。然而细细追问之下，他认为一旦两军交锋，他们也许可以从背后袭击其主人。

===Original===
He said that the folk of Rosedale had been a goodly folk before they were enthralled, and peaceable with one another, but that now it was a sport of the Dusky Men to set a match between their thralls to fight it out with sword and buckler or otherwise; and the vanquished man, if he were not sore hurt, they would scourge, or shear some member from him, or even slay him outright, if the match between the owners were so made. And many other sad and grievous tales he told to Face-of-god, more than need be told again; so that the War-leader went along sorry and angry, with his teeth set, and his hand on the sword-hilt.

Thus they went till night fell on them, and they could scarce see the signs they had made on their outward journey. Then they made stay in a little valley, having set a watch duly; and since they were by this time far from Rosedale, and were a great company as regarded scattered bands of the foe, they lighted their fires and cooked their venison, and made good cheer to the Runaways, and so went to sleep in the wildwood.

When morning was come they gat them at once to the road; and if the Burgdalers were eager to be out of the wood, their eagerness was as nought to the eagerness of the Runaways, most of whom could not be easy now, and deemed every minute lost unless they were wending on to the Dale; so that this day they were willing to get over the more ground, whereas they had not set out on their road till afternoon yesterday.

===Chinese===
他说，玫瑰谷人在被奴役之前，原是一个体面的种族，彼此相安无事，可如今黝暗人却拿一种把戏取乐：让两个奴隶配成一对，用剑和圆盾或别的法子拼个你死我活；战败的那个若伤得不重，他们便鞭打他，或削去他身上某件肢体，甚至当场处死——只要两个主人之间事先如此约定。他还讲了许多别的悲惨酷毒之事，多到不必一一复述；这位战首一路走去，又悲又怒，咬紧牙关，一只手按在剑柄上。

他们如此赶路，直到夜色降临，几乎看不见来时路上所留的记号。他们便在一条小山谷里歇下，照例派了守望；此时他们离玫瑰谷已远，比起敌寇零星的小股人马，他们人数众多，于是点起火堆，煮了鹿肉，好好款待了那些逃亡者，便在野林中睡下。

到了早晨，他们立即上路；堡谷人急于出林，可他们的急切与逃亡者相比，简直算不得甚么——逃亡者中大多数人此刻已坐立不安，以为每一刻不在赶往山谷的路上便是虚掷；所以这一日他们情愿多赶些路，毕竟昨日是过了正午才动身上路的。

===Original===
Howsoever, they rested at noontide, and Face-of-god bade Dallach bring him to speech with others of the Runaways, and first that he might talk with those three men of the kindreds who had fled from Silverdale in early days. So Dallach brought them to him; but he found that though they spake the tongue, they were so few-spoken from wildness and loneliness, at least at first, that nought could come from them that was not dragged from them.

These men said that they had been in the wood more than nine years, so that they knew but little of the conditions of the Dale in that present day. However, as to what Dallach had said concerning the Dusky Men, they strengthened his words; and they said that the Dusky Men took no delight save in beholding torments and misery, and that they doubted if they were men or trolls. They said that since they had dwelt in the wood they had slain not a few of the foemen, waylaying them as occasion served, but that in this warfare they had lost two of their fellows. When Face-of-god asked them of their deeming of the numbers of the Dusky Men, they said that before those bands had broken into Rosedale, they counted them, as far as they could call to mind, at about three thousand men, all warriors; and that somewhat less than one thousand had gone up into Rosedale, and some had died, and many had been cast away in the wildwood, their fellows knew not how. Yet had not their numbers in Silverdale diminished; because two years after they (the speakers) had fled, came three more Dusky Companies or Tribes into Silverdale, and each of these tribes was of three long hundreds; and with their coming had the cruelty and misery much increased in the Dale, so that the thralls began to die fast; and that drave the Dusky Men beyond the borders of Silverdale, so that they fell upon Rosedale. When asked how many of the kindreds might yet be abiding in Silverdale, their faces clouded, and they seemed exceeding wroth, and answered, that they would willingly hope that most of those that had not been slain at the time of the overthrow were now dead, yet indeed they feared there were yet some alive, and mayhappen not a few women.

===Chinese===
不过，他们在正午歇了一歇，面神叫达拉赫领他与其余逃亡者对对话，首先要与那三个早年从银谷逃出的氏族之人谈谈。达拉赫便把他们领了来；可是面神发觉，他们虽说会讲族里的语言，却因野居独处、性子粗野，至少一开始寡言得很，不从他们身上硬拽，便套不出半句话来。

这几个人说，他们在林中已住了九年有余，所以对眼下银谷里的情形所知甚少。不过，关于达拉赫论及黝暗人的那番话，他们倒是为其作了印证；他们说黝暗人除了观看酷刑与苦难之外别无乐趣可言，他们自己都拿不准这些究竟是人是魑魅。他们说，自从住进林中以来，他们已瞅机会伏杀了为数不少的敌人，但在这种战斗中，他们也折了两个同伴。面神问他们对黝暗人的数目作何估量，他们说，在那几伙人冲入玫瑰谷之前，凭他们所能记得的，约有三千之众，全是战士；其中不到一千人进入了玫瑰谷，有些死了，许多则在野林中折损，同伴也不知是怎么折损的。然而他们在银谷的人数并未减少；因为在他们（说话的这几人）逃出之后两年，又有三个黝暗人的部族或氏族开进了银谷，每个氏族约有三个长百（long hundreds，每百作一百二十计）；他们一来，谷中的酷虐与苦难便大大加重，奴隶开始大批死亡；这就逼着黝暗人越出银谷的边界，去攻袭玫瑰谷。当被问到银谷里可能还剩下多少同族时，他们脸色阴沉下来，似极为愤怒，答道：他们情愿相信，亡国之时未被杀的人大多如今已经死了，可实际上他们害怕还有一些人活着，也许还有不少女子。

===Original===
By then must they get on foot again, and so the talk fell between them; but when they made stay for the night, after they had done their meat, Face-of-god prayed Dallach bring to him some of the latest-come folk from Silverdale, and he brought to him the man and the woman who had been in the Dale within that moon. As to the man, if those of the Earl-folk had been few-spoken from fierceness and wildness, he was no less so from mere dullness and weariness of misery; but the woman’s tongue went glibly enough, and it seemed to pleasure her to talk about her past miseries. As aforesaid, she was better clad than most of those of Rosedale, and indeed might be called gaily clad, and where her raiment was befouled or rent, it was from the roughness of the wood and its weather, and not from the thralldom. She was a young and fair woman, black-haired and grey-eyed. She had washed herself that day in a woodland stream which they had crossed on the road, and had arrayed her garments as trimly as she might, and had plucked some fumitory, wherewith she had made a garland for her head. She sat down on the grass in front of Face-of-god, while the man her mate stood leaning against a tree and looked on her greedily. The Burgdale carles drew near to her to hearken her story, and looked kindly on the twain. She smiled on them, but especially on Face-of-god, and said:

===Chinese===
这时他们又得起身上路，谈话就此中断；待到晚间歇下、吃完饭食之后，面神请达拉赫把银谷最晚逃出的几个人领几个来，达拉赫便把那个男子和那个女子领到他跟前——这两人是一个月之内才离开银谷的。至于那个男子，如果说贵胄之民那几个人是因为粗野孤傲而寡言，他则是纯粹因为苦难造成的麻木和厌倦而同样寡言；那女子的舌头却利落得很，谈起自己过往的苦楚，倒似颇为自得。如前所述，她的衣着比大多数玫瑰谷人都好，简直可称鲜丽，衣裳上凡是有污损之处，都是林中的粗砺和风雨所致，并非为奴的痕迹。她是个年轻貌美的女子，黑发灰眼。那天她已在路上所过的一条林间溪水里洗过身，又把衣裳尽可能穿戴整齐，还采了些延胡索，编成一只花环戴在头上。她在面神面前的草地上坐下，她那个汉子却倚着一棵树站着，贪婪地盯着她看。堡谷的汉子们凑近前来听她讲述，和颜悦色地看着这两人。她朝众人笑了笑，却格外朝着面神，说道：

===Original===
“Thou hast sent for me, lord, and I wot well thou wouldst hear my tale shortly, for it would be long to tell if I were to tell it fully, and bring into it all that I have endured, which has been bitter enough, for all that ye see me smooth of skin and well-liking of body. I have been the bed-thrall of one of the chieftains of the Dusky Men, at whose house many of their great men would assemble, so that ye may ask me whatso ye will; as I have heard much talk and may call it to mind. Now if ye ask me whether I have fled because of the shame that I, a free woman come of free folk, should be a mere thrall in the bed of the foes of my kin, and with no price paid for me, I must needs say it is not so; since over long have we of the Dale been thralls to be ashamed of such a matter. And again, if ye deem that I have fled because I have been burdened with grievous toil and been driven thereto by the whip, ye may look on my hands and my body and ye will see that I have toiled little therewith: nor again did I flee because I could not endure a few stripes now and again; for such usage do thralls look for, even when they are delicately kept for the sake of the fairness of their bodies, and this they may well endure; yea also, and the mere fear of death by torment now and again. But before me lay death both assured and horrible; so I took mine own counsel, and told none for fear of bewrayal, save him who guarded me; and that was this man; who fled not from fear, but from love of me, and to him I have given all that I might give. So we got out of the house and down the Dale by night and cloud, and hid for one whole day in the Dale itself, where I trembled and feared, so that I deemed I should die of fear; but this man was well pleased with my company, and with the lack of toil and beating even for the day. And in the night again we fled and reached the wildwood before dawn, and well-nigh fell into the hands of those who were hunting us, and had outgone us the day before, as we lay hid. Well, what is to say? They saw us not, else had we not been here, but scattered piecemeal over the land. This carle knew the passes of the wood, because he had followed his master therein, who was a great hunter in the wastes, contrary to the wont of these men, and he had lain a night on the burg yonder; therefore he brought me thither, because he knew that thereabout was plenty of prey easy to take, and he had a bow with him; and there we fell in with others of our folk who had fled before, and with Dallach; who e’en now told us what was hard to believe, that there was a fair young man like one of the Gods leading a band of goodly warriors, and seeking for us to bring us into a peaceful and happy land; and this man would not have gone with him because he feared that he might fall into thralldom of other folk, who would take me away from him; but for me, I said I would go in any case, for I was weary of the wood and its roughness and toil, and that if I had a new master he would scarcely be worse than my old one was at his best, and him I could endure. So I went, and glad and glad I am, whatever ye will do with me. And now will I answer whatso ye may ask of me.”

===Chinese===
"大人，您差人唤我前来，我深知您想略略听一听我的故事；若要原原本本细讲，把我所受的一切苦都讲进来，那可就长了——我所受的苦已经够苦的了，虽说您看我皮肤光洁、身段齐整。我原是黝暗人一名首领的床奴，他的住处是他们许多大人物聚会议事之所，所以你们要问甚么尽可问我；我在那里听了许多议论，都还记在心里。如今你们若问我：我出逃，是不是因为耻于身为自由人的后代、本是个自由女子，竟在仇敌的床上做个没有身价的小奴——我不得不说，并非如此；我们谷地之人做奴为时已久，这种事早已不以为耻了。再者，你们若以为我是被重活压垮、被鞭子赶着才逃的，你们只消看看我的手和身子，便知我没怎么干过粗活：我又不是受不住隔三差五的几下鞭子才逃的；因为这种待遇，奴隶们是料得到的，即便因为生得貌美被娇养着，也免不了，这些他们也忍得过去；就连时不时死于酷刑的那种恐惧，他们也忍得过去。可摆在我面前的，是一种铁定无疑、又惨不可言的死；于是我自拿主意，为防走漏风声，除了看守我的那个人，我一个也没告诉；那个人便是这一位；他不是因为惧怕才逃的，而是因为爱我，我已把我能给的一切都给了他。于是我们乘着黑夜出得宅去，趁着夜色与云影下了山谷，在谷里整整躲了一天；那一天我浑身战栗、心惊胆战，直以为自己要被活活吓死；这个汉子却因有我作伴、因那一日免了劳役与鞭打而满心欢喜。到了夜里我们又逃，天亮前赶到了野林，险些落进追捕我们的人手里——那些人前一天我们藏身时还走到了我们前头。唉，还说甚么呢？他们没看见我们，不然我们也不会到这里来了，早被零碎抛尸于野了。这个汉子熟悉林中的路径，因为他从前跟着主人进过林——他主人是个在荒地里打猎的好手，与这些人的惯例正相反，还在那边那座山堡上歇过一夜；所以他把我带到那里，因为他知道那一带猎物多、容易下手，而他身上还有一张弓；在那儿我们遇上了另一些先前逃出来的族人，也遇上了达拉赫；他当时对我们说了一件叫人难以置信的事：说有个俊美的年轻人，像天神一般，领着一队雄壮的战士，正寻我们、要把我们带到一个太平快乐的国度去；这一位汉子本不愿随他走，因为怕自己再落到别人为奴、人家又把我从他手里夺走；至于我，我说无论如何我都要去，因为我已厌倦了这林子、厌倦了它的粗砺和劳苦，而且就算我换个新主人，也断不会比我那旧主人最好之时更坏，他那种程度的，我忍得过去。于是我来了，我来了真叫千欢万喜，随你们将我怎样发落。如今，凡你们要问的，我都答。"

===Original===
She laid her limbs together daintily and looked fondly on Face-of-god, and the carle scowled at her somewhat at first, but presently, as he watched her, his face smoothed itself out of its wrinkles.

But Face-of-god pondered a little while, and then asked the woman if she had heard any words to remember of late days concerning the affairs of the Dusky Men and their intent; and he said:
“I pray thee, sister, be truthful in thine answer, for somewhat lieth on it.”

She said: “How could I speak aught but the sooth to thee, O lovely lord? The last word spoken hereof I mind me well: for my master had been mishandling me, and I was sullen to him after the smart, and he mocked and jeered me, and said: Ye women deem we cannot do without you, but ye are fools, and know nothing; we are going to conquer a new land where the women are plenty, and far fairer than ye be; and we shall leave you to fare afield like the other thralls, or work in the digging of silver; and belike ye wot what that meaneth. Also he said that they would leave us to the new tribe of their folk, far wilder than they, whom they looked for in the Dale in about a moon’s wearing; so that they needs must seek to other lands. Also this same talk would we hear whenever it pleased any of them to mock us their bed-thralls. Now, my sweet lord, this is nought but the very sooth.”

Again spake Face-of-god after a while:
“Tell me, sister, hast thou heard of any of the Dusky Men being slain in the wood?”

===Chinese===
她娇娇巧巧地把四肢并拢，含情脉脉地望着面神，那汉子起先还朝她皱着眉头沉脸，可不一会儿，盯着她看着，那脸上的皱纹便自己舒展开了。

面神沉吟片刻，便问那女子近日可曾听到甚么关于黝暗人及其图谋、值得记住的话语；他说："好妹妹，我求你据实而答，因为这件事关系不小。"

她道："俊美的主人，我对您怎敢不说真话？这事最后说的一番话，我记得清清楚楚：那一回我主人折腾了我，我疼过之后没给他好脸色，他便讥讽嘲弄我，说道：你们这些女人以为我们离了你们不行，可你们是蠢货，甚么也不懂；我们要去征服一片新地方，那里的女子多得是，比你们好看得多；我们就要把你们像别的奴隶一样赶到地里去干活，或是去挖银子；那是个甚么滋味，想必你们也明白。他又说，他们要把我们丢给他们一族新来的部众——那部众比他们还要凶蛮得多，他们估计过一个月光景便要进入谷地；所以他们不得不另寻他处。再者，这种话，凡是他们哪一个想起来要嘲弄我们这些床奴，我们都会听见。如今，我那甜蜜的主人，我说的句句是实。"

过了一会儿，面神又说道："好妹妹，你告诉我，你可曾听说有黝暗人在林中被杀的事么？"

===Original===
“Yea,” she said, and turned pale therewith and caught her breath as one choking; but said in a little while:
“This alone was it hard for me to tell thee amongst all the I griefs I have borne, whereof I might have told thee many tales, and will do one day if thou wilt suffer it; but fear makes this hard for me. For in very sooth this was the cause of my fleeing, that my master was brought in slain by an arrow in the wood; and he was to be borne to bale and burned in three days’ wearing; and we three bed-thralls of his, and three of the best of the men-thralls, were to be burned quick on his balefire after sore torments; therefore I fled, and hid a knife in my bosom, that I might not be taken alive; but sweet was life to me, and belike I should not have smitten myself.”

And she wept sore for pity of herself before them all. But Face-of-god said:
“Knowest thou, sister, by whom the man was slain?”

“Nay,” she said, still sobbing; “but I heard nought thereof, nor had I noted it in my terror. The death of others, who were slain before him, and the loss of many, we knew not how, made them more bitterly cruel with us.”

And again was she weeping; but Face-of-god said kindly to her: “Weep no more, sister, for now shall all thy troubles be over; I feel in my heart that we shall overcome these felons, and make an end of them, and there then is Burgdale for thee in its length and breadth, or thine own Dale to dwell in freely.”

“Nay,” she said, “never will I go back thither!” and she turned round to him and kissed his feet, and then arose and turned a little toward her mate; and the carle caught her by the hand and led her away, and seemed glad so to do.

===Chinese===
"有的，"她说，当即脸色发白，倒抽一口气，像噎住了一般；过了一会儿才道：在我所受的这一切苦楚当中，唯独这一桩我难于向您启齿——这些苦楚我本可以给您讲许多故事，他日您若容许，我一定会讲；只是恐惧使我难以开口。因为实实在在，我出逃的缘由便是：我主人被人用箭射死在林中，被抬了回来；三日后他便要被送上柴堆焚化；我们三个床奴，连同三个最好的男奴，都要先受尽酷刑、再活活烧死在他的火葬堆上；所以我才逃了，又在怀里藏了一柄刀，免得被活捉；可是性命于我毕竟甘甜，多半我也不会真的对自己动手。

她当着众人的面，为自己痛哭失声。面神却道："好妹妹，你可知那人是谁所杀？"

"不知道，"她仍在抽噎，"这事我一个字也没听见，以我当时那般惊恐，也留意不到。只是别人——在他之前被杀的那些人——的死，还有许多人莫名其妙地失踪，使他们对我们更加狠毒残忍。"

她又哭了起来；面神和颜悦色地对她说："好妹妹，莫再哭了，如今你这一切苦都要到头了；我心里觉得，我们必能胜过这些恶徒，将他们尽数除灭；那时，整个堡谷随你长住宽住，你自己的山谷也随你自在安居。"

她道："不，我再也不回那里去了！"她转过身来亲吻他的脚，然后起身，稍稍转向她的汉子；那汉子一把抓住她的手，把她领走了，似乎很高兴能这样。

===Original===
So once again they fell asleep in the woods, and again the next morning fared on their way early that they might come into Burgdale before nightfall. When they stayed a while at noontide and ate, Face-of-god again had talk with the Runaways, and this time with those of Rosedale, and he heard much the same story from them that he had heard before, told in divers ways, till his heart was sick with the hearing of it.

On this last day Face-of-god led his men well athwart the wood, so that he hit Wildlake’s Way without coming to Carlstead; and he came down into the Dale some four hours after noon on a bright day of latter March. At the ingate to the Dale he found watches set, the men whereof told him that the tidings were not right great. Hall-face’s company had fallen in with a band of the Felons three score in number in the oak-wood nigh to Boars-bait, and had slain some and chased the rest, since they found it hard to follow them home as they ran for the tangled thicket: of the Burgdalers had two been slain and five hurt in this battle.

As for Red-coat’s company, they had fallen in with no foemen.

===Chinese===
于是他们又在林中睡下，次日一早又上路，好赶在天黑前进入堡谷。正午歇脚吃饭之时，面神又与逃亡者们交谈，这一回是和那些玫瑰谷人谈；从他们口里，他听到的故事与先前所闻大同小异，只是说法各有不同，听得他心里作呕。

最后这一日，面神领着众人斜穿过林子，恰到好处，未到汉子镇（Carlstead）便接上了野湖径（Wildlake's Way）；他在三月末一个晴朗的日子里、约莫午后四个钟头走下山谷。在山谷入口处，他遇见设下的哨兵，哨兵告诉他并无甚么大消息。厅面（Hall-face）那一队人马在野猪饵（Boars-bait）附近的橡林里，与一伙六十人的恶徒（the Felons）相遇，杀了一些，又把其余的赶跑了——因为那些人逃进纠缠的密丛里，实在难以一路追到老巢：这一仗堡谷人折了两人、伤了五人。

至于红衣（Red-coat）那一队，并未遇上任何敌寇。

## XXXII The Men of Shadowy Vale Come to the Spring Market at Burgstead / 三十二 幽谷之人来堡镇赶春市

===Original===
On the morrow betimes in the morning the Westland chapmen, who were now all come, went out from the House of the Face, where they were ever wont to be lodged, and set up their booths adown the street betwixt gate and bridge. Gay was the show; for the booths were tilted over with painted cloths, and the merchants themselves were clad in long gowns of fine cloth; scarlet, and blue, and white, and green, and black, with broidered welts of gold and silver; and their knaves were gaily attired in short coats of divers hues, with silver rings about their arms, and short swords girt to their sides. People began to gather about these chapmen at once when they fell to opening their bales and their packs, and unloading their wains. There had they iron, both in pigs and forged scrap and nails; steel they had, and silver, both in ingots and vessel; pearls from over sea; cinnabar and other colours for staining, such as were not in the mountains: madder from the marshes, and purple of the sea, and scarlet grain from the holm-oaks by its edge, and woad from the deep clayey fields of the plain; silken thread also from the outer ocean, and rare webs of silk, and jars of olive oil, and fine pottery, and scented woods, and sugar of the cane. But gold they had none with them, for that they took there; and for weapons, save a few silver-gilt toys, they had no market.

===Chinese===
翌日清晨，西土（the Westland）的客商们——此时已悉数到齐——自面神之宅（the House of the Face）而出，他们向来都在此处下榻；于是在城门与桥之间的街两旁支起摊棚。那场面甚是鲜丽：摊棚上张着彩绘布幔，商人们身着细布长袍，有猩红、蓝、白、绿、黑诸色，上以金银线绣边为饰；他们的仆役也打扮得光鲜，衣五色短衫，臂上戴银环，腰间悬短剑。客商们一开箱解囊、卸下车上的货物，众人便围拢过来。他们带来的货物中，有铁——既有铁锭，也有锻过的废铁与铁钉；有钢，有银——银锭与银器皆有；有海外来的珍珠；有朱砂及山中所无的各色染料：沼地所产的茜草、海中所制的紫、海滨橡树所产的猩红胭脂虫、平原深黏土田里所产的靛蓝；又有外洋来的丝线、罕见的丝绸织物、一坛坛橄榄油、精致的陶器、香料木、甘蔗所制的糖。唯独黄金他们未曾携来——因为黄金正是在此地收取的；至于兵器，除少量鎏金的玩物小件外，他们并不发卖。

===Original===
So presently they fell to chaffer; for the carles brought them little bags of the river-borne gold, so that the weights and scales were at work; others had with them scrolls and tallies to tell the number of the beasts which they had to sell, and the chapmen gave them wares therefor without beholding the beasts; for they wotted that the Dalesmen lied not in chaffer. While the day was yet young withal came the Dalesmen from the mid and nether Dale with their wares and set up their booths; and they had with them flasks and kegs of the wine which they had to sell; and bales of the good winter-woven cloth, some grey, some dyed, and pieces of fine linen; and blades of swords, and knives, and axes of such fashion as the Westland men used; and golden cups and chains, and fair rings set with mountain-blue stones, and copper bowls, and vessels gilt and parcel-gilt, and mountain-blue for staining. There were men of the Shepherds also with such fleeces as they could spare from the daily chaffer with the neighbours. And of the Woodlanders were four carles and a woman with peltries and dressed deer-skins, and a few pieces of well-carven woodwork for bedsteads and chairs and suchlike.

===Chinese===
于是众人不久便做起交易：汉子们拿来一小袋一小袋河中淘得的砂金，天平砝码随之忙碌起来；也有人带着卷册与符木（tallies），记下要出售的牲畜数目，客商们据此付给货物，并不去看牲口；因为他们知道谷民（the Dalesmen）在做买卖时从不说谎。日头尚早，谷中及下游的谷民也带着货物赶来，支起摊棚：他们带来了一瓶瓶、一桶桶要出售的酒；一捆捆冬日织成的好布，有素灰的，有染色的；还有上等的亚麻布匹；有剑刃、刀具、斧头，样式正如西土人所惯用；又有金杯金链，镶嵌山中蓝宝石的精美戒指，铜碗，以及鎏金或半鎏金的器皿，还有作染料用的山蓝。牧羊之民（the Shepherd-Folk）中也有人带来羊毛——那是从平日与邻人交易之余省下来的。林中汉子（the Woodland-Carles）也来了四个汉子、一个妇人，带着皮货、鞣制好的鹿皮，还有几件雕工精良的木器，是做床架、椅子之类的用物。

===Original===
Soon was the Burg thronged with folk in all its open places, and all were eager and merry, and it could not have been told from their demeanour and countenance that the shadow of a grievous trouble hung over them. True it was that every man of the Dale and the neighbours was girt with his sword, or bore spear or axe or other weapon in his hand, and that most had their bucklers at their backs and their helms on their heads; but this was ever their custom at all meetings of men, not because they dreaded war or were fain of strife, but in token that they were free men, from whom none should take the weapons without battle.

Such were the folk of the land: as for the chapmen, they were well-spoken and courteous, and blithe with the folk, as they well might be, for they had good pennyworths of them; yet they dealt with them without using measureless lying, as behoved folk dealing with simple and proud people; and many was the tale they told of the tidings of the Cities and the Plain.

There amongst the throng was the Bride in her maiden's attire, but girt with the sword, going from booth to booth with her guests of the Runaways, and doing those poor people what pleasure she might, and giving them gifts from the goods there, such as they set their hearts on. And the more part of the Runaways were about among the people of the Fair; but Dallach, being still weak, sat on a bench by the door of the House of the Face looking on well-pleased at all the stir of folk.

===Chinese===
不多时，堡镇（Burgstead）各处空地都挤满了人，个个兴高采烈、欢天喜地；单看他们的神色举止，决看不出有一重忧患的阴影笼罩在众人头上。诚然，谷中及四邻的男子个个腰悬刀剑，或手执长枪、斧头等兵器，大多数人背上还负着小圆盾，头上戴着盔；但这原是他们凡有人聚之处一向的规矩，并非因为畏惧战事、好兴干戈，而是以此为记：他们乃是自由之人，除非兵戎相见，谁也不能夺去他们的兵器。

当地之民便是如此；至于那些客商，谈吐文雅、举止有礼，与众人相处甚欢——这也难怪，他们从这些人身上做足了便宜买卖；然而他们与众人交易时，并不用漫天谎话，正如与淳朴而高傲之民打交道时所应当的那般；他们又讲了许多平原诸城（the Cities of the Plain）与平原（the Plain）上的见闻故事。

新娘（the Bride）也在人群之中，穿的是闺中少女的衣裳，腰间却佩着剑；她带着她那些逃奴（the Runaways）客人，从一个摊子走到另一个摊子，尽其所能讨这些可怜人的欢心，从摊上货物中挑出他们心仪之物赠给他们。那些逃奴大半都在集市的人群中走动；唯有达拉赫（Dallach）身子尚弱，坐在面神之宅门前一条长凳上，满心欢喜地看着人来人往的热闹。

===Original===
Hall-face was gone on the woodland ward; while Face-of-god went among the folk in his most glorious attire; but he soon betook him to the place of meeting without the Gate, where Stone-face and some of the elders were sitting along with the Alderman, beside whom sat the head man of the merchants, clad in a gown of fine scarlet embroidered with the best work of the Dale, with a golden chaplet on his head, and a good sword, golden-hilted, by his side, all which the Alderman had given to it him that morning. These chiefs were talking together concerning the tidings of the Plain, and many a tale the guest told to the Dalesmen, some true, some false. For there had been battles down there, and the fall of kings, and destruction of people, as oft befalleth in the guileful Cities. He told them also, in answer to their story of the Dusky Men, of how men even suchlike, but riding on horses, or drawn in wains, an host not to be numbered, had erewhile overthrown the hosts of the Cities of the Plain, and had wrought evils scarce to be told of; and how they had piled up the skulls of slaughtered folk into great hills beside the city-gates, so that the sun might no longer shine into the streets; and how because of the death and the rapine, grass had grown in the kings' chambers, and the wolves had chased deer in the Temples of the Gods.

===Chinese===
厅面（Hall-face）已去巡林之役了；面神则盛装走入人群之中；但他不久便转到城门外那处聚议之所去了，石面（Stone-face）与几位老人正与长老（the Alderman）同坐一处，长老身旁坐着众商之首，身着一件细绒猩红长袍，绣的是堡谷（Burgdale）最精的工，头戴金编花冠，腰悬一口鎏金剑柄的好剑——这一切都是长老那天早晨赠给他的。这几位首脑人物正谈论着平原上的消息，那客人向谷民讲了许多故事，有真有假。原来南方彼处曾有战役，有国王倾覆，有百姓遭殃——这在奸险的诸城之中乃是常事。他又应他们所讲的黝暗人（the Dusky Men）之事说道：有一族与此相类之人，骑马或乘辇车而来，其数不可胜计，不久之前倾覆了平原诸城的大军，所造之恶几乎难以尽述；他们把所杀之人的头颅堆在城门两旁，垒成一座座大丘，使日头再也照不进街巷之中；又因杀戮与劫掠，国王的宫室里长出了野草，神庙之中，狼群追逐着野鹿。

===Original===
"But," quoth he, "I know you, bold tillers of the soil, valiant scourers of the Wildwood, that the worst that can befall you will be to die under shield, and that ye shall suffer no torment of the thrall. May the undying Gods bless the threshold of this Gate, and oft may I come hither to taste of your kindness! May your race, the uncorrupt, increase and multiply, till your valiant men and clean maidens make the bitter sweet and purify the earth!"

===Chinese===
"然而，"他道，"我知道你们这些勇敢的耕夫、纵横野林（the Wildwood）的壮士，你们所能遭逢的最坏下场，也不过是执盾战死沙场，断不会受那为奴的苦楚。愿那不死的众神赐福这座城门的门槛！愿我常常能来此，领受你们的厚谊！愿你们这未曾腐化的种族繁衍兴旺，直到你们的壮士与贞洁的少女，将苦涩化为甘甜，涤净这大地！"

===Original===
He spake smooth-tongued and smiling, handling the while the folds of his fine scarlet gown, and belike he meant a full half of what he said; for he was a man very eloquent of speech, and had spoken with kings, uncowed and pleased with his speaking; and for that cause and his riches had he been made chief of the chapmen. As he spake the heart of Face-of-god swelled within him, and his cheek flushed; but Iron-face sat up straight and proud, and a light smile played about his face, as he said gravely:

"Friend of the Westland, I thank thee for the blessing and the kind word. Such as we are, we are; nor do I deem that the very Gods shall change us. And if they will be our friends, it is well; for we desire nought of them save their friendship; and if they will be our foes, that also shall we bear; nor will we curse them for doing that which their lives bid them to do. What sayest thou, Face-of-god, my son?"

"Yea, father," said Face-of-god, "I say that the very Gods, though they slay me, cannot unmake my life that has been. If they do deeds, yet shall we also do."

The Outlander smiled as they spake, and bowed his head to Iron-face and Face-of-god, and wondered at their pride of heart, marvelling what they would say to the great men of the Cities if they should meet them.

===Chinese===
他说得辞令圆融、面带微笑，一面抚弄着那件猩红细绒长袍的褶裥；他这番话，怕是有大半是真心。原是个极善言辞之人，曾与国王对语而不卑不亢、颇自得意；正因如此，加上他的财力，才被推为众客商之首。他说话之际，面神心潮激荡，双颊泛红；铁面（Iron-face）却挺身端坐，傲然不羁，嘴角浮起一丝淡笑，郑重说道：

"西土的朋友，多谢你的祝福与善言。我们是什么样的人，便是什么样的人；我并不以为众神便能改变我们。他们若肯与我们为友，那是好事；因为我们除他们的情谊外，别无所求；他们若要与我为敌，我们也承受得起；他们不过是各为其生而行事，我们决不因此而咒骂他们。面神，我的儿，你以为如何？"

面神道："父亲，我以为，便是众神亲自将我杀了，也不能抹除我已经走过的一生。他们行事，我们也行事。"

那外乡人（the Outlander）听他们说话，含笑点头，向铁面与面神拱手，心中暗暗惊异他们的心高气傲，不禁揣想：倘若他们遇见诸城中的大人物，又会说出怎样的话来。

===Original===
But as they sat a-talking, there came two men running to them from the Portway, their weapons all clattering upon them, and they heard withal the sound of a horn winded not far off very loud and clear; and the Chapman's cheek paled: for in sooth he doubted that war was at hand, after all he had heard of the Dalesmen's dealings with the Dusky Men. And all battle was loathsome to him, nor for all the gain of his chaffer had he come into the Dale, had he known that war was looked for.

But the chiefs of the Dalesmen stirred not, nor changed countenance; and some of the goodmen who were in the street nigh the Gate came forth to see what was toward; for they also had heard the voice of the horn.

Then one of those messengers came up breathless, and stood before the chiefs, and said:

"New tidings, Alderman; here be weaponed strangers come into the Dale."

===Chinese===
正谈间，自港路（the Portway）那头跑来两个汉子，身上兵器叮当作响，又听得近处号角之声嘹亮清越；那客商面色登时发白：他素来听闻谷民与黝暗人之间的事，此刻当真怕是战事临头了。他生平最厌恶兵戈，倘若早知道此地料将有战，莫说图这买卖上的赚头，他断不会踏入此谷。

然而谷民的首脑们纹丝不动，面不改色；街市近城门处有几个户主走出来看是怎么一回事，因为他们也听见了号角之声。

随即一个信使气喘吁吁奔近前来，立在那几位首脑面前，说道：

"长老，有新消息；有带兵器的陌生人入了山谷。"

===Original===
The Alderman smiled on him and said: "Yea, son, and are they a great host of men?"

"Nay," said the man, "not above a score as I deem, and there is a woman with them."

"Then shall we abide them here," said the Alderman, "and thou mightest have saved thy breath, and suffered them to bring tidings of themselves; since they may scarce bring us war. For no man desireth certain and present death; and that is all that such a band may win at our hands in battle today; and all who come in peace are welcome to us. What like are they to behold?"

Said the man: "They are tall men gloriously attired, so that they seem like kinsmen of the Gods; and they bear flowering boughs in their hands."

The Alderman laughed, and said: "If they be Gods they are welcome indeed; and they shall grow the wiser for their coming; for they shall learn how guest-fain the Burgdale men may be. But if, as I deem, they be like unto us, and but the children of the Gods, then are they as welcome, and it may be more so, and our greeting to them shall be as their greeting to us would be."

===Chinese===
长老对他笑了笑，说道："好啦，孩子，他们是一支大军么？"

那汉子道："不然，依我看不过二十来人，其中还有一个女子。"

长老道："那我们就在此迎候他们罢，你这口气原可省下，由他们自己来报信；这般人数，总不至于带来战祸。须知无人自寻必死之途——这样一支小队今日与我们在战场上相见，所能赢的，不过是一场眼前必死之战罢了；凡是怀善意而来的，我们都欢迎。他们相貌如何？"

那汉子道："都是些高大汉子，装束华美，看去宛如众神的亲族；他们手中都擎着花枝。"

长老大笑，说道："若是神祇，那真是再欢迎不过；他们此来定要长些见识，因为他们将见识到堡谷之民是如何好客。然而若如我所料，他们与我们相类，不过是众神的子孙，那也一样欢迎，说不定更加欢迎；我们待他们的礼数，当与他们待我们的一样。"

===Original===
Even as he spake the horn was winded nearer yet, and more loudly, and folk came pouring out of the Gate to learn the tidings. Presently the strangers came from off the Portway into the space before the Gate; and their leader was a tall and goodly man of some thirty winters, in glorious array, helm on head and sword by side, his surcoat green and flowery like the spring meads. In his right hand he held a branch of the blossomed blackthorn (for some was yet in blossom), and his left had hold of the hand of an exceeding fair woman who went beside him: behind him was a score of weaponed men in goodly attire, some bearing bows, some long spears, but each bearing a flowering bough in hand.

The tall man stopped in the midst of the space, and the Alderman and they with him stirred not; though, as for Face-of-god, it was to him as if summer had come suddenly into the midst of winter, and for the very sweetness of delight his face grew pale.

===Chinese===
他话音未落，号角之声又起，更近更响，众人纷纷自城门涌出探听消息。不多时，那些陌生人从港路转入了城门前的空地；为首一人是个三十来岁的魁梧好汉，装束华美，头戴盔，腰悬剑，罩袍碧绿，上绣繁花，宛如春日之草甸。他右手擎着一枝开花的黑刺李（其时尚有花未谢），左手携着一位极美貌的女子之手，那女子行在他身侧：他身后随着二十名带甲之士，装束鲜明，有的持弓，有的执长枪，但每个人手中都擎着一枝花枝。

那高大汉子在空地中央停下，长老及左右之人纹丝不动；至于面神，只觉如严冬之中忽然到了盛夏，那份欢喜之甘美，竟教他面色发白了。

===Original===
Then the newcomer drew nigh to the Alderman and said:

"Hail to the Gate and the men of the Gate! Hail to the kindred of the children of the Gods!"

But the Alderman stood up and spake: "And hail to thee, tall man! Fair greeting to thee and thy company! Wilt thou name thyself with thine own name, or shall I call thee nought save Guest? Welcome art thou, by whatsoever name thou wilt be called. Here may'st thou and thy folk abide as long as ye will."

===Chinese===
那新来之人走上前至长老跟前，说道：

"城门及守门之人万福！众神之子的亲族万福！"

长老起身答道："高大的壮士，你也万福！你与你的同伴们受我敬礼！你是要自报姓名呢，还是要我只称你为客？你愿人如何称呼你，都一律欢迎。你与你的人尽可在此久住，随你们心意。"

===Original===
Said the newcomer: "Thanks have thou for thy greeting and for thy bidding! And that bidding shall we take, whatsoever may come of it; for we are minded to abide with thee for a while. But know thou, O Alderman of the Dalesmen, that I am not sackless toward thee and thine. My name is Folk-might of the Children of the Wolf, and this woman is the Sun-beam, my sister, and these behind me are of my kindred, and are well beloved and trusty. We are no evil men or wrongdoers; yet have we been driven into sore straits, wherein men must needs at whiles do deeds that make their friends few and their foes many. So it may be that I am thy foeman. Yet, if thou doubtest of me that I shall be a baneful guest, thou shalt have our weapons of us, and then mayest thou do thy will upon us without dread; and here first of all is my sword!"

===Chinese===
那新来之人道："多谢你的礼遇与相邀！这相邀我们领下了，无论后果如何；因为我们正有意在你这里盘桓一时。然而，谷民的长老啊，你要知道，我对你与你族中人并非无罪在身。我的名字叫民强（Folk-might），出自狼之子民（the Children of the Wolf）；这女子是日光（the Sun-beam），我的妹妹；我身后这些人都是我的族人，都是我深爱而信赖之人。我们并非恶徒，亦非为非作歹之辈；然而我们被人逼入绝境，人在那种境地之中，有时不得不行些令朋友稀少、仇人增多的举动。所以我或许正是你的仇敌。然而，你若疑心我是个招祸之客，尽管取去我们的兵器，然后便可毫无顾忌地随意处置我们；这便是我的剑，先交与你！"

===Original===
Therewith he cast down the flowering branch he was bearing, and pulled his sword from out his sheath, and took it by the point, and held out the hilt to Iron-face.

But the Alderman smiled kindly on him and said:

"The blade is a good one, and I say it who know the craft of sword-forging; but I need it not, for thou seest I have a sword by my side. Keep your weapons, one and all; for ye have come amongst many and those no weaklings: and if so be that thy guilt against us is so great that we must needs fall on you, ye will need all your war-gear. But hereof is no need to speak till the time of the Folk-mote, which will be holden in three days' wearing; so let us forbear this matter till then; for I deem we shall have enough to say of other matters. Now, Folk-might, sit down beside me, and thou also, Sun-beam, fairest of women."

===Chinese===
说着，他将所擎的花枝掷下，拔剑出鞘，握住剑尖，将剑柄递向铁面。

长老却和颜悦色对他一笑，说道：

"这是一口好剑，我这懂锻剑手艺的人说这话是不假的；然而我并不需它，你瞧，我自己腰下也佩着剑。你们的兵器，一个个都留着罢；因为你们是来到众多之人中间，而且都不是软弱之辈：倘若你对我所负之罪果真重到我们非动手不可的地步，你们也用得着全副披挂。但此事不必现在谈论，等到三日之后的民众大会（the Folk-mote）之时再说；这事便搁到那时再议罢，我料我们还有许多别的话要说。民强，如今且坐在我身旁；日光，你这最美的女子，也请坐下。"

===Original===
Therewith he looked into her face and reddened, and said:

"Yet belike thou hast a word of greeting for my son, Face-of-god, unless it be so that ye have not seen him before?"

Then Face-of-god came forward, and took Folk-might by the hand and kissed him; and he stood before the Sun-beam and took her hand, and the world waxed a wonder to him as he kissed her cheeks; and in no wise did she change countenance, save that her eyes softened, and she gazed at him full kindly from the happiness of her soul.

Then Face-of-god said: "Welcome, Guests, who erewhile guested me so well: now beginneth the day of your well-doing to the men of Burgdale; therefore will we do to you as well as we may."

===Chinese===
说着他凝视她的脸，面上一红，说道：

"然而，你对我儿面神，怕是有一句问候的话罢——除非你们从前并未见过？"

于是面神上前，执民强之手与他亲吻为礼；又立在日光面前，执起她的手，亲吻她的双颊——这一刻，整个天地在他眼中都化作了奇境；她却面不改色，只眼中柔了几分，自心底的欢悦里，极尽温柔地凝望着他。

面神于是说道："欢迎你们，往日盛情款待过我的客人：你们对堡谷之民行善的日子，今日方才起头；因此我们也要尽我们所能善待你们。"

===Original===
Then Folk-might and the Sun-beam sat them down with the chieftains, one on either side of the Alderman, but Face-of-god passed forth to the others, and greeted them one by one: of them was Wood-father and his three sons, and Bow-may; and they rejoiced exceedingly to see him, and Bow-may said:

"Now it gladdens my heart to look upon thee alive and thriving, and to remember that day last winter when I met thee on the snow, and turned thee back from the perilous path to thy pleasure, which the Dusky Men were besetting, of whom thou knewest nought. Yea, it was merry that tide; but this is better. Nay, friend," she said, "it availeth thee nought to strive to look out of the back of thine head: let it be enough to thee that she is there. Thou art now become a great chieftain, and she is no less; and this is a meeting of chieftains, and the folk are looking on and expecting demeanour of them as of the Gods; and she is not to be dealt with as if she were the daughter of some little goodman with whom one hath made tryst in the meadows. There! hearken to me for a while; at least till I tell thee that thou seemest to me to hold thine head higher than when last I saw thee; though that is no long time either. Hast thou been in battle again since that day?"

===Chinese===
于是民强与日光与众首领同坐，分坐长老左右；面神则走到其他人那里，与他们一一见礼：其中有林父（Wood-father）与他的三个儿子，还有弓娥（Bow-may）；众人见了他都喜出望外，弓娥说道：

"见你安然无恙、神采飞扬，我心下甚喜；又想起去年冬天那日，我在雪地里遇见你，将你从那条险途上劝回你那条寻欢之路——那时黝暗人正埋伏其上，你却一无所知。哈，那时节也颇有意思；然而今日更好。哎，朋友，"她道，"你纵然拼命想从后脑勺上张望，也是枉然；你只须知她在那里便够了。你如今成了一位大首领，她也毫不逊色；这是一场首领与会之礼，众人都望着，盼你们举止如众神一般；她可不是那草野小户人家、在草甸上与人私订终身的女儿，可以由人随便相待。好啦！且听我说一会儿话；至少听我把话说完：我看你如今昂首挺胸，比上次见你时气宇更轩昂了——虽说那也并没过多久。自那日以后，你可又上过战场么？"

===Original===
"Nay," he said, "I have stricken no stroke since I slew two felons within the same hour that we parted. And thou, sister, what hast thou done?"

She said: "The grey goose hath been on the wing thrice since that, bearing on it the bane of evil things."

===Chinese===
他道："不曾。自我们分手那一时辰之内我杀了两个恶徒（the Felons）之后，再未动过一剑一拳。你呢，姐姐，你又做过什么？"

她道："自那以后，灰雁羽箭已三度离弦翱翔，箭上所负，尽是诛灭恶物的煞气。"

===Original===
Then said Wood-wise: "Kinswoman, tell him of that battle, since thou art deft with thy tongue."

She said: "Weary on battles! it is nought save this: twelve days agone needs must every fighting-man of the Wolf, carle or of queen, wend away from Shadowy Vale, while those unmeet for battle we hid away in the caves at the nether end of the Dale: but Sun-beam would not endure that night, and fared with us, though she handled no weapon. All this we had to do because we had learned that a great company of the Dusky Men were over-nigh to our Dale, and needs must we fall upon them, lest they should learn too much, and spread the story. Well, so wise was Folk-might that we came on them unawares by night and cloud at the edge of the Pinewood, and but one of our men was slain, and of them not one escaped; and when the fight was over we counted four score and ten of their arm-rings."

He said: "Did that or aught else come of our meeting with them that morning?"

"Nay," she said, "nought came of it: those we slew were but a straying band. Nay, the four score and ten slain in the Pinewood belike knew not of Shadowy Vale, and had no intent for it: they were but scouring the wood seeking their warriors that had gone out from Silverdale and came not aback."

===Chinese===
林智（Wood-wise）道："族姐，你既善辞令，便把那场战事讲给他听罢。"

她道："厌倦啊，这些打仗！不过是这样：十二日之前，狼族凡是能战之人，无论男女，都得离开幽谷（Shadowy Vale）；不能上阵的，我们藏到山谷尽头处的山洞里去：然而日光那一夜不肯独留，随我们同去，只是不持兵器。我们之所以不得不如此，是因为得知一大队黝暗人离我们山谷过近，我们非得突袭他们不可，免得他们窥探得太多、把风声传扬出去。嗯，民强调度有方，我们趁夜黑云密之际，在松林（the Pinewood）边缘攻其不备；我方仅折了一人，他们却无一脱逃；战罢点数，共得臂环九十枚。"

他道："那日早晨我们与他们相遇之后，可有什么后续，或别的事情发生？"

她道："不曾，并无后续：我们所杀的，不过是一队迷了路的人。那松林中所杀的九十人，怕是根本不知有幽谷这地方，也无意前来：他们不过是在林中搜巡，找那些自银谷（Silverdale）派出而一去不归的战士罢了。"

===Original===
"Thou art wise in war, Bow-may," said Face-of-god, and he smiled withal.

Bow-may reddened and said: "Friend Gold-mane, dost thou perchance deem that there is aught ill in my warring? And the Sun-beam, she naysayeth the bearing of weapons; though I deem that she hath little fear of them when they come her way."

Said Face-of-god: "Nay, I deem no ill of it, but much good. For I suppose that thou hast learned overmuch of the wont of the Dusky Men, and hast seen their thralls?"

She knitted her brows, and all the merriment went out of her face at that word, and she answered: "Yea, thou hast it; for I have both seen their thralls and been in the Dale of thralldom; and how then can I do less than I do? But for thee, I perceive that thou hast been nigh unto our foes and hast fallen in with their thralls; and that is well; for whatso tales we had told thee thereof it is like thou wouldst not have trowed in, as now thou must do, since thou thyself hast seen these poor folk. But now I will tell thee, Gold-mane, that my soul is sick of these comings and goings for the slaughter of a few wretches; and I long for the Great Day of Battle, when it will be seen whether we shall live or die; and though I laugh and jest, yet doth the wearing of the days wear me."

===Chinese===
"弓娥，你深谙战阵之道。"面神说着，微微一笑。

弓娥脸一红，道："金鬃（Gold-mane）朋友，莫非你觉得我这份厮杀有什么不好？日光她是反对执持兵器的；然而兵器临到她跟前时，我看她也不怎么惧怕。"

面神道："不，我不以为不好，反以为大有好处。我猜你对黝暗人的行径知道得太多，又见过他们的奴隶（thralls）罢？"

她皱起眉头，满脸的欢快一时尽去，答道："正是，你说对了；我既见过他们的奴隶，也到过那奴役之谷；我怎能不如此行事？至于你，我瞧出来你也曾接近我们的仇敌，遇见过他们所奴役的人；那是好事；因为不论我们如何向你说这些事，你怕是都不肯轻信，如今却不得不信了，因为你自己亲眼见过那些可怜之人。然而金鬃，如今我要告诉你，这般来来去去、不过杀掉几个可怜虫的日子，我已厌倦透顶；我渴望那大战之日（the Great Day of Battle）——到了那日，便能见分晓，我们是生是死；我虽笑谑如常，然而光阴一日日的磨折，也真磨折着我。"

===Original===
He looked kindly on her and said: "I am War-leader of this Folk, and trust me that the waiting-tide shall not be long; wherefore now, sister, be merry today, for that is but meet and right; and cast aside thy care, for presently shalt thou behold many new friends. But now meseemeth overlong have ye been standing before our Gate, and it is time that ye should see the inside of our Burg and the inside of our House."

===Chinese===
他温和地看着她，说道："我是此族之战首（War-leader），信我罢，等候之时不会太长；所以姐姐，今日只管欢饮，这才是应当的；把心事放下罢，因为不久你便要见到许多新朋友。然而我看，你们在我们城门前立得也太久了，是时候看看我们堡内、看看我们宅中的光景了。"

===Original===
Indeed by this time so many men had come out of the street that the place before the Gate was all thronged, and from where he stood Face-of-god could scarce see his father, or Folk-might and the Sun-beam and the chieftains.

So he took Wood-father by the hand, and close behind him came Wood-wise and Bow-may, and he cried out for way that he might speak with the Alderman, and men gave way to them, and he led those newcomers close up to the gate-seats of the Elders, and as he clove the press smiling and bright-eyed and happy, all gazed on him; but the Sun-beam, who was sitting between Iron-face and the Westland Chapman, and who heretofore had been agaze with eyes beholding little, past whose ears the words went unheard, and whose mind wandered into thoughts of things unfashioned yet, when she beheld him close to her again, then, taken unawares, her eyes caressed him, and she turned as red as a rose, as she felt all the sweetness of desire go forth from her to meet him. So that, he perceiving it, his voice was the clearer and sweeter for the inward joy he felt, as he said:

"Alderman, meseemeth it is now time that we bring our Guests into the House of our Fathers; for since they are in warlike array, and we are no longer living in peace, and I am now War-leader of the Dale, I deem it but meet that I should have the guesting of them. Moreover, when we are come into our House, I will bid thee look into thy treasury, that thou may'st find therein somewhat which it may pleasure us to give to our Guests."

===Chinese===
此时自街上涌出的人已如此之多，城门前空地被挤得水泄不通；面神立在原处，几乎望不见他的父亲，也望不见民强、日光与众首领。

于是他执林父之手，林智与弓娥紧随其后；他高声呼喝开路，要与长老说话，众人让出一条路来；他引着那些新来之人直走到长老们的城门座前，他含笑、目光炯炯、满怀喜悦地分开人群之际，众人都目不转睛望着他；然而日光——她本是坐在铁面与那西土客商之间的——在此之前一直目不转睛却视而不见，旁人言语入耳也充耳不闻，心思飘忽到尚未成形之事上；待她忽然又见他近在眼前，猝不及防之间，她的眼睛便不由自主地爱抚起他来，她面红得像一朵玫瑰——因为她感到心中那股渴慕的甘甜尽数涌出，迎着他而去。他既觉察此情，因心中之喜，声音愈发清朗甘甜，说道：

"长老，我看如今是时候把我们这些客人请进父祖之宅了；他们既已披甲而来，我们又已非太平之日，而我如今是此谷之战首，我以为这迎客之礼自当由我来操持。再者，等进了宅中，我要请你打开库房看看，从中寻出一些我们乐意赠给这些客人的好物。"

===Original===
Said Iron-face: "Thou sayest well, son, and since the day is now worn past noon, and these folk are but just come from the Waste, therefore such as we have of meat and drink abideth them. And surely there is within our house a coffer which belongeth to thee and me; and forsooth I know not why we keep the treasures hoarded therein, save that it be for this cause: that if we were to give to our friends that which we ourselves use and love, which would be of all things pleasant to us, if we gave them such goods, they would be worn and worsened by our use of them. For this reason, therefore, do we keep fair things which we use not, so that we may give them to our friends.

"Now, Guests, both of the Waste and the Westland, since here is no Gate-thing or meeting of the Dale-wardens, and we sit here but for our pleasure, let us go take our pleasure within doors for a while, if it seem good to you."

===Chinese===
铁面道："儿啊，你说得是；此时日已过午，这些人又刚从大荒原（the Great Waste）赶来，我们所有的一切饮食正可款待他们。况且我们宅中确有一只柜子，是属于你我的；老实说，我也不知为何要将那些珍宝积藏其中——除非是为着这个缘故：倘若我们把自家所用所爱之物赠给朋友——把那些我们用着最觉称心之物赠出去——那些东西被我们用得久了，必已磨损朽坏。正因如此，我们才另留着那些未曾动用的精美之物，好赠给朋友。

"众位客人，来自荒原的与来自西土的，此处既无城门议事（Gate-thing），又非众守事（the Dale-wardens）集会，我们坐在这里不过是为了消遣，那么便请随我们入内消遣一时，如何？"

===Original===
Therewith he arose, and the folk made way for him and his Guests; and Folk-might went on the right hand of Iron-face, and beside him went the Chapman, who looked on him with a half-smile, as though he knew somewhat of him. But on the other side of Iron-face went the Sun-beam, whose hand he held, and after these came Face-of-god, leading in the rest of the Newcomers, who yet held the flowery branches in their hands.

===Chinese===
说罢他起身，众人为他与宾客们让路；民强行在铁面右手，与他并肩的是那客商，脸上带着似笑非笑的神情瞧着他，仿佛知道他一些底细。铁面左手则是日光，携着她的手；后面随着的是面神，引着其余新来之人——这些人手中仍擎着花枝。

===Original===
Now so much had Face-of-god told the Dalesmen, that they deemed they all knew these men for their battle-fellows of whom they had heard tell; and this the more as the men were so goodly and manly of aspect, especially Folk-might, so that they seemed as if they were nigh akin to the Gods. As for the Sun-beam, they knew not how to praise her beauty enough, but they said that they had never known before how fair the Gods might be. So they raised a great shout of welcome as the men came through the Gate into the Burg, and all men turned their backs on the booths, so eager were they to behold closely these new friends.

===Chinese===
原来面神早已向谷民说过许多，以致他们都认得这些人是他们听人讲过的那些战友；况且这些人相貌如此英伟雄壮，民强尤其如此，看上去简直与众神相去不远。至于日光，他们不知如何赞美她的美貌才好，只说从前竟不知众神能有这般姣好。于是当这些人穿过城门入堡之时，众人齐声高呼欢迎，人人都背对着摊棚——因为他们都急于一睹这些新朋友的真容。

===Original===
But as the Guests went from the Gate to the House of the Face, going very slowly because of the press, there in the front of the throng stood the Bride with the women of the Runaways, whom she had caused to be clad very fairly; and she was fain to do them a pleasure by bringing them to sight of these newcomers, of whom she had not heard who they were, though she had heard the cry that strangers were at hand. So there she stood smiling a little with the pleasure of showing a fair sight to the poor people, as folk do with children. But when she saw those twain going on each side of the Alderman she knew them at once; and when the Sun-beam, who was on his left side, passed so close to her that she could see the very smoothness and dainty fashion of her skin, then was she astonied, and the world seemed strange to her, and till they were gone by, and for a while afterwards, she knew not where she was nor what she did, though it seemed to her as if she still saw the face of that fair woman as in a picture.

===Chinese===
宾客们自城门往面神之宅而行，因人太挤，走得很慢；其时人群最前面立着新娘，带着她那些逃奴中的女眷——新娘已给她们换上了很体面的衣裳；她有心让这些可怜人一睹这些新来者的风采，讨她们一个欢喜——新娘尚不知这些是谁，虽已听见呼声说有陌生人到来。她立在那里，微微含笑，因能将这桩美事指给那些可怜人看而心生欢喜，正如大人哄孩童一般。然而当她看见那两人分行于长老两侧，她立刻认出了他们；当日光——她行在长老左手——挨得那样近擦身而过，近到她能看清日光肌肤之细润娇嫩，她一时惊呆了，天地仿佛都陌生起来；待他们走过，又过一会儿，她都不知身在何处、所做何事，只觉那美貌女子的容颜仍如画中一般浮在眼前。

===Original===
But the Sun-beam had noted her at first, even amongst the fair women of Burgstead, and she so steady and bright beside the wandering timorous eyes and lowering faces of the thralls. But suddenly, as eye met eye, she saw her face change; she saw her cheek whiten, her eyes stare, and her lips quiver, and she knew at once who it was; for she had not seen her before as Folk-might had. Then the Sun-beam cast her eyes adown, lest her compassion might show in her face, and be a fresh grief to her that had lost the wedding and the love; and so she passed on.

===Chinese===
然而日光一眼便注意到她——即便在堡镇那些美貌女子之间——她那样沉稳明净，与奴隶们游移畏怯的眼神、阴沉抑郁的面容截然不同。可是忽然之间，四目相交之际，她见新娘脸色骤变；见她双颊失色、双目圆睁、嘴唇颤动，立刻便认出她是谁——此前她并不像民强那样见过她。于是日光垂下眼帘，唯恐脸上露出怜悯，反成这位已失去婚礼与所爱之人的新痛；她便这样走了过去。

===Original===
As for Folk-might, he had seen her at once amongst all that folk as he came into the street, and in sooth he was looking for her; and when he saw her face change, as the sight of the Sun-beam smote upon her heart, his own face burned with shame and anger, and he looked back at her as he went toward the House. But she saw him not, nor noted him; and none deemed it strange that he looked long on the Bride, the treasure of Burgstead. But for some while Folk-might was few-spoken and sharp-spoken amongst the chieftains; for he was slow to master his longing and his wrath.

===Chinese===
至于民强，他一走入街市便在众人之中一眼看见了她——他原本便在找她；当他看见日光的出现如何击中新娘的心、令她脸色骤变，他自己的脸也因羞愧与愤怒而灼热起来，一面朝宅子走去，一面回头望她。可她并未看见他，也未曾留意他；众人也不以为怪——谁不多看几眼新娘这堡镇的珍宝呢？然而有一阵子，民强在众首领之间寡言少语、语带锋芒；因为他那渴望与怒火，一时不易按捺。

===Original===
So when all the Guests had entered the door of the House of the Face, the Alderman turned back, and, standing on the threshold of his House, spake unto the throng:

"Men of the Dale, and ye Outlanders who may be here, know that this is a happy day; for hither have come to us Guests, men of the kindred of the Gods, and they are even those of whom Face-of-god my son hath told you. And they are friends of our friends and foes of our foes. These men are now in my House, as is but right; but when they come forth I look to you to cherish them in the best way ye know, and make much of them, as of those who may help us and who may by us be holpen."

Therewith he went in again and into the Hall, and bade show the Newcomers to the dais; and wine of the best, and meat such as was to hand, was set before them. He bade men also get ready high feast as great as might be against the evening; and they did his bidding straightway.

===Chinese===
待众宾客都进了面神之宅的门，长老转过身来，立在自家宅第门槛之上，对众人说道：

"谷中之民，以及在座的外乡人，要知道今日是个吉日；因为有宾客来到我们这里，是众神亲族之裔，正是我儿面神向你们讲过的那些人。他们是我们朋友的朋友，是我们仇敌的仇敌。这些人如今在我宅中，这本是应当的；待他们出来时，我望你们以你们所知最好的礼数厚待他们，敬重他们，视他们为能助我们、也能为我们所助之人。"

说罢他又转身入内，进了厅堂，命人引新来之人到高台之上就座；送上最好的酒，及现成可得的肉食。他又吩咐众人尽力备下一席盛筵，以备傍晚之用；众人即刻依命去办。

## XVII The Token Cometh from the Mountain / 十七 信物自山中来

===Original===
The next day wore away tidingless; and the day after Face-of-god arose betimes; for it was the first day of his watch, and he was at the Maiden Ward before the time appointed on a very fair and bright morning, and he went to and fro on that place, and had no tidings. So he came away somewhat cast down, and said within himself: "Is it but a lie and a mocking when all is said?"

On the morrow he went thither again, and the morn was wild and stormy with drift of rain, and low clouds hurrying over the earth, though for the sunrise they lifted a little in the east, and the sun came up over the passes, amidst the red and angry rack of clouds. This morn also gave him no tidings of the token, and he was wroth and perturbed in spirit: but towards evening he said:

"It is well: ten days she gave me, so that she might be able to send without fail on one of them; she will not fail me."

===Chinese===
次日无消息度过；又过一日，面神一早便起，因这一日是他当值守望之首日，他在一个十分晴朗明媚的清晨，早于约定之时便到了少女岗（the Maiden Ward），在那处来来回回地走，却一无消息。于是他颇为沮丧地离去，心中暗自道："难道说到底，那不过是一句谎言、一场戏弄么？"

次日他又去那里，清晨狂风骤雨，雨沫飘飞，低云在地面之上匆匆掠过；虽然日出之时，云在东方稍稍掀起一角，太阳自诸隘口之间升起，穿过那殷红怒号的乱云。这一早同样没给他带来信物的消息，他心中恼怒烦躁：但近暮之时他道：

"也好：她给了我十日之期，以便她必能于其中一日遣人送来；她不会误我的。"

===Original===
So again on the morrow he was there betimes, and the morn was windy as on the day before, but the clouds higher and of better promise for the day. Face-of-god walked to and fro on the Maiden Ward, and as he turned toward Burgstead for the tenth time, he heard, as he deemed, a bowstring twang afar off, and even therewith came a shaft flying heavily like a winged bird, which smote a great standing stone on the other side of the way, where of old some chieftain had been buried, and fell to earth at its foot. He went up to it and handled it, and saw that there was a piece of thin parchment wrapped about it, which indeed he was eager to unwrap at once, but forebore; because he was on the highway, and people were already astir, and even then passed by him a goodman of the Dale with a man of his going afield together, and they gave him the sele of the day. So he went along the highway a little till he came to a place where was a footbridge over into the meadow. He crossed thereby and went swiftly till he reached a rising ground grown over with hazel-trees; there he sat down among the rabbit-holes, the primrose and wild-garlic blooming about him, and three blackbirds answering one another from the edges of the coppice. Straightway when he had looked and seen none coming he broke the threads that were wound about the scroll and the arrow, and unrolled the parchment; and there was writing thereon in black ink of small letters, but very fair, and this is what he read therein:

===Chinese===
于是次日他又早早到了那里，清晨风大，与昨日一般，但云层更高，预示此日天气较好。面神在少女岗上来回踱步，当他第十次转身朝堡镇方向望去时，他仿佛听见远处弓弦一响，紧接着一支箭沉重地飞来，犹如一只生翼之鸟，射中路对面一方大立石——那是古时某位酋长的埋骨之所——然后坠落于石脚下。他走上前去，拿起那支箭把弄，见箭上缠着一片薄羊皮纸，他确然急欲即刻展开，却强自忍住；因为他正站在大路之上，人已起来走动，正其时有一位谷中的良人带着他的一名雇工一同下地经过，与他互道了日安。于是他沿大路稍走一段，到了一处有便桥通入草地的地方。他从那里过桥，快步前行，直至抵达一处生满榛树的高地；他在兔穴之间坐下，四周报春花与野蒜盛开，三只乌鸫在矮林边缘彼此应答。他四下一望，见无人来，便立即扯断缠在卷轴与箭上的细线，将羊皮纸展开；其上以黑墨写着细字，却甚工美，他所读到的，是这样的：

===Original===
> Come thou to the Mountain Hall by the path which thou knowest of, on the morrow of the day whereon thou readest this. Rise betimes and come armed, for there are other men than we in the wood; to whom thy death should be a gain. When thou art come to the Hall, thou shalt find no man therein; but a great hound only, tied to a bench nigh the dais. Call him by his name, Sure-foot to wit, and give him to eat from the meat upon the board, and give him water to drink. If the day is then far spent, as it is like to be, abide thou with the hound in the hall through the night, and eat of what thou shalt find there; but see that the hound fares not abroad till the morrow’s morn: then lead him out and bring him to the northeast corner of the Hall, and he shall lift the slot for thee that leadeth to the Shadowy Yale. Follow him and all good go with thee.

===Chinese===
> 汝读此书之次日，可循汝所知之路，至山厅（the Mountain Hall）。须早起携兵以行，盖林中除吾辈外尚有他人；汝之死，于彼等乃是一桩利得。汝至厅后，必不见一人其中；唯有一条大猎犬，拴于高台近旁一条凳上。以名字唤它，名曰稳足（Sure-foot），以案上之肉喂它食，给它水饮。若此时日已将暮——多半如此——汝当与那犬在厅中过夜，就所发现之物充饥；但务必使那犬次日清晨之前不出厅外：届时将它牵出，领至厅之东北角，它便会为汝嗅出通往幽谷（the Shadowy Vale）的踪迹。循之前行，万事大吉。

===Original===
Now when he had read this, earth seemed fair indeed about him, and he scarce knew whither to turn or what to do to make the most of his joy. He presently went back to Burgstead and into the House of the Face, where all men were astir now, and the day was clearing. He hid the shaft under his kirtle, for he would not that any should see it; so he went to his shut-bed and laid it up in his chest, wherein he kept his chiefest treasures; but the writing on the scroll he set in his bosom and so hid it. He went joyfully and proudly, as one who knoweth more tidings and better than those around him. But Stone-face beheld him, and said “Foster-son, thou art happy. Is it that the spring-tide is in thy blood, and maketh thee blithe with all things, or hast thou some new tidings? Nay, I would not have an answer out of thee; but here is good rede: when next thou goest into the wood, it were nought so ill for thee to have a valiant old carle by thy side; one that loveth thee, and would die for thee if need were; one who might watch when thou wert seeking. Or else beware! for there are evil things abroad in the Wood, and moreover the brethren of those two felons who were slain at Carlstead.”

Then Gold-mane constrained himself to answer the old carle softly; and he thanked him kindly for his offer, and said that so it should be before long. So the talk between them fell, and Stone-face went away somewhat well-pleased.

And now was Face-of-god become wary; and he would not draw men’s eyes and speech on him; so he went afield with Hall-face to deal with the lambs and the ewes, and did like other men. No less wary was he in the hall that even, and neither spake much nor little; and when his father spake to him concerning the Bride, and made game of him as a somewhat sluggish groom, he did not change countenance, but answered lightly what came to hand.

===Chinese===
他读过此信，只觉四周大地诚然秀美，竟不知该转向何处、该做何事以尽其欢。他随即折返堡镇，进入面神之宅，其时宅中人皆已起身，天色也渐渐放晴。他将箭藏于外袍之下，因他不愿被人瞧见；于是他走到自己的封闭木榻卧间，将箭收入他贮藏最珍贵之物的箱箧之中；至于卷轴上的字条，则贴身藏在怀中。他欢欣而骄傲地走着，仿佛一个比周遭之人知晓更多更好消息的人。但石面看着他，说道："义子，你心里欢喜。可是春潮涌入你的血液，使你对万物都感到欢悦，还是你得了什么新消息？罢了，我不求你回答；但我有一句良言：下次你入林之时，有一位勇悍的老汉陪在你身边，于你不算坏事；一个爱你之人，事急之际愿为你舍命；一个能在你四下寻觅时为你守望之人。不然就多加小心！因为林中正有邪祟横行，何况还有那两个在汉子镇被杀之凶徒的同伙。"

于是金鬃强自按捺，柔声答那老汉；他诚恳谢过他的好意，说不久之后必当如此。两人之间的话便落下了，石面颇为满意地离去。

从此面神变得十分谨慎；他不愿惹人注目、引人议论；于是他与厅面一同下地去料理小羊和母羊，与众人一样做事。当晚在厅中他也同样谨慎，不多话也不少话；当他的父亲同他谈起新娘之事，并取笑他是个颇为怠惰的新郎时，他面不改色，随口信手作答。

===Original===
On the morrow ere the earliest dawn he was afoot, and he clad himself and did on his hauberk, his father’s work, which was fine-wrought and a stout defence, and reached down to his knees; and over that he did on a goodly green kirtle well embroidered: he girt his war-sword to his side, and it was the work of his father’s father, and a very good sword: its name was Dale-warden. He did a good helm on his head, and slung a targe at his back, and took two spears in his hand, short but strong-shafted and well-steeled. Thus arrayed he left Burgstead before the dawn, and came to Wildlake’s Way and betook him to the Woodland. He made no stop or stay on the path, but ate his meat standing by an oak-tree close by the half-blind track. When he came to the little wood-lawn, where was the toft of the ancient house, he looked all round about him, for he deemed that a likely place for those ugly wood-wights to set on him; but nought befell him, though he stooped and drank of the woodland rill warily enough. So he passed on; and there were other places also where he fared warily, because they seemed like to hold lurking felons; though forsooth the whole wood might well serve their turn. But no evil befell him, and at last, when it yet lacked an hour to sunset, he came to the wood-lawn where Wild-wearer had made his onset that other eve.

He went straight up to the house, his heart beating, and he scarce believing but that he should find the Friend abiding him there: but when he pushed the door it gave way before him at once, and he entered and found no man therein, and the walls stripped bare and no shield or weapon hanging on the panels. But the hound he saw tied to a bench nigh the dais, and the bristles on the beast’s neck arose, and he snarled on Face-of-god, and strained on his leathern leash. Then Face-of-god went up to him and called him by his name, Sure-foot, and gave him his hand to lick, and he brought him water, and fed him with flesh from the meat on the board; so the beast became friendly and wagged his tail and whined and slobbered his hand.

===Chinese===
次日最早的天光未露之前，他便已起身，穿戴齐整，披上锁子甲——那是他父亲的手艺，打造精良、坚固护身，下垂及膝；锁子甲之外，又套上一件绣工精美的好看绿外袍：他将战剑佩于腰间，那剑乃是他祖父之作，是一柄极好的剑：其名曰谷卫（Dale-warden）。他头上戴好一顶好盔，背后斜挎一面圆盾，手中提两杆短矛，矛虽短，杆却粗壮，矛头淬钢精良。他如此装束停当，在黎明之前离了堡镇，到了野湖径，便进入林莽。他在路上一刻不停，只在一棵橡树旁站着吃了干粮，那树紧邻那条半隐半现的小径。当他来到那片林中小草地——古屋基址所在之处——他四面张望，因他觉得那是那些丑陋林妖埋伏袭击他的好去处；然而并无异事，他虽俯身小心翼翼地在林间小溪喝了水，却安然无恙。他继续前行；还有几处地方他也走得小心翼翼，因那些地方似有伏匪藏匿之状；不过说实话，整座林子处处都可作为伏匪之所。但他一路并未遇险，终于，距日落尚差一个时辰之际，他来到了那片林中小草地——上一回那个傍晚野披（Wild-wearer）就是在此发起袭击的。

他直走到屋前，心怦怦直跳，几乎相信自己会在那里看到那位朋友等着他：然而当他推门时，门应手而开，他走进去，发觉其中空无一人，墙壁已光秃秃地剥落，墙板上既无盾牌也无兵器悬挂。但他看见一条猎犬拴在高台近旁一条凳上，那畜生颈毛倒竖，冲着面神龇牙低吼，挣扯着皮索。于是面神走上前去，唤它的名字——稳足——伸手让它舔舐，又给它端水来，用案上之肉喂它；那畜生便友善起来，摇尾呜咽，涎水沾满他一手。

===Original===
Then he went all about the house, and saw and heard no living thing therein save the mice in the panels and Sure-foot. So he came back to the dais, and sat him down at the board and ate his fill, and thought concerning his case. And it came into his mind that the Woman of the Mountain had some deed for him to do which would try his manliness and exalt his fame; and his heart rose high and he was glad, and he saw himself sitting beside her on the dais of a very fair hall beloved and honoured of all the folk, and none had aught to say against him or owed him any grudge. Thus he pleased himself in thinking of the good days to come, sitting there till the hall grew dusk and dark and the night-wind moaned about it.

Then after a while he arose and raked together the brands on the hearth, and made light in the hall and looked to the door. And he found there were bolts and bars thereto, so he shot the bolts and drew the bars into their places and made all as sure as might be. Then he brought Sure-foot down from the dais, and tied him up so that he might lie down athwart the door, and then lay down his hauberk with his naked sword ready to his hand, and slept long while.

When he awoke it was darker than when he had lain him for the moon had set; yet he deemed that the day was at point of breaking. So he fetched water and washed the night off him, and saw a little glimmer of the dawn. Then he ate somewhat of the meat on the board, and did on his helm and his other gear, and unbarred the door, and led Sure-foot without, and brought him to the northeast corner of the house, and in a little while he lifted the slot and they departed, the man and the hound, just as broke dawn from over the mountains.

===Chinese===
然后他满屋走了一圈，里面除了墙板间的老鼠与稳足之外，再不见、也再听不见任何活物。于是他回到高台前，在案前坐下，饱餐一顿，心中思量自己的处境。他忽然想到：那山中女子（the Woman of the Mountain）必是有一桩事要他去做，一桩足以试炼他男子气概、抬高他名望的事；他心潮澎湃，喜不自胜，恍惚间看见自己与那女子并肩坐在一座极其华美厅堂的高台之上，受全体族民的爱戴与敬重，无人对他有半句闲话、无人对他怀有半分怨恨。他便这样坐在那里，沉醉于对未来好日子的遐想，一直坐到厅中暮色四合、黑暗笼罩，夜风在屋外呜咽。

过了一会儿，他起身将炉中的柴火拨拢，使厅中重新亮起来，又去查看大门。他见门上有插销和门闩，便将插销推上、门闩归位，把一切弄得尽可能牢固。然后他将稳足从高台前牵下来，把它拴好，让它横卧在门前；他自己则解下锁子甲，将出鞘之剑置于手边，沉沉睡去，睡了许久。

他醒来时，比他躺下时更黑，因为月亮已经落下；但他觉得天将破晓。于是他取水洗去一夜的倦气，看见一线微熹的晨光。然后他吃了些案上的肉，戴好头盔和其余装备，拔开大门的门闩，将稳足牵到屋外，领到屋的东北角；不多时那犬便嗅到了踪迹，他们一人一犬就此启程，正是群山那边天光初破之时。

===Original===
Sure-foot led right into the heart of the pinewood, and it was dark enough therein, with nought but a feeble glimmer for some while, and long was the way therethrough; but in two hours’ space was there something of a break, and they came to the shore of a dark deep tarn on whose windless and green waters the daylight shone fully. The hound skirted the water, and led on unchecked till the trees began to grow smaller and the air colder for all that the sun was higher; for they had been going up and up all the way.

So at last after a six hours’ journey they came clean out of the pinewood, and before them lay the black wilderness of the bare mountains, and beyond them, looking quite near now, the great ice-peaks, the wall of the world. It was but an hour short of noon by this time, and the high sun shone down on a barren boggy moss which lay betwixt them and the rocky waste. Sure-foot made no stay, but threaded the ways that went betwixt the quagmires, and in another hour led Face-of-god into a winding valley blinded by great rocks, and everywhere stony and rough, with a trickle of water running amidst of it. The hound fared on up the dale to where the water was bridged by a great fallen stone, and so over it and up a steep bent on the further side, on to a marvellously rough mountain-neck, whiles mere black sand cumbered with scattered rocks and stones, whiles beset with mires grown over with the cottony mire-grass; here and there a little scanty grass growing; otherwhere nought but dwarf willow ever dying ever growing, mingled with moss or red-blossomed sengreen; and all blending together into mere desolation.

Few living things they saw there; up on the neck a few sheep were grazing the scanty grass, but there was none to tend them; yet Face-of-god deemed the sight of them good, for there must be men anigh who owned them. For the rest, the whimbrel laughed across the mires; high up in heaven a great eagle was hanging; once and again a grey fox leapt up before them, and the heath-fowl whirred up from under Face-of-god’s feet. A raven who was sitting croaking on a rock in that first dale stirred uneasily on his perch as he saw them, and when they were passed flapped his wings and flew after them croaking still.

===Chinese===
