稳足径直领他深入松林之心，林中极为幽暗，好一阵子只有一线微弱的光，穿林之路也极长；但约两个时辰之后，林子略有断缺，他们便到了一个幽深水潭的岸边，潭水无风、绿沉沉的，日光已能全然照在其上。那犬沿着潭边走，毫不迟疑地继续前行，直到树木开始变得矮小、空气变得寒冷——尽管太阳已经升得更高了；因为他们一路上都是不断地向上、再向上。

终于，走了足足六个时辰之后，他们完全走出了松林，眼前是一片光秃秃群山的黑色荒原，再过去——如今看上去近在咫尺——便是巨大的冰峰，那世界尽头的屏障。此时距正午只差一个时辰，高悬的太阳照在他们与那岩石荒原之间的一片泥泞沼泽之上。稳足毫不歇脚，在泥沼之间的条条路径中穿行；又过一个时辰，它将面神引入一道蜿蜒的峡谷，谷中为大石所遮蔽，处处乱石嶙峋、崎岖难行，中间有一线细流涓涓淌过。那犬沿谷而上，走到水流被一块巨石横搭成桥之处，越过此石，登上对岸一道陡坡，登上一道奇峻之极的山鞍——此处时而不过是黑沙上壅塞着散乱的岩石石头，时而则为滋生棉絮般沼草的泥潭所围；处处生着一点稀疏的青草；他处则唯有矮柳，死了又生、生了又死，与苔藓或开着红花的长生草交缠一处；一切都汇成一片荒凉。

那里的活物不多；山鞍之上，有几只羊在啃那稀疏的青草，却无人看管；但面神觉得看见它们是件好事，因为附近必有人家拥有它们。除此之外，鹬鸟在泥潭之间啼笑；高天之上悬着一只大鹫；一只灰狐在他们面前一再跃起，松鸡从面神脚下扑棱棱飞起。先前那道峡谷里有一只渡鸦蹲在岩上呱呱直叫，见他们走来，在栖处不安地挪动；待他们过去之后，便扑棱翅膀，一路呱呱叫着追随他们飞来。

===Original===
Now they fared over that neck somewhat east, making but slow way because the ground was so broken and rocky; and in another hour’s space Sure-foot led downhill due east to where the stony neck sank into another desolate miry heath still falling toward the east, but whose further side was walled by a rampart of crags cleft at their tops into marvellous-shapes, coal-black, ungrassed and unmossed. Thitherward the hound led straight, and Gold-mane followed wondering: as he drew near them he saw that they were not very high, the tallest peak scant fifty feet from the face of the heath.

They made their way through the scattered rocks at the foot of these crags, till, just where the rock-wall seemed the closest, the way through the stones turned into a path going through it skew-wise; and it was now so clear a path that belike it had been bettered by men’s hands. Down thereby Face-of-god followed the hound, deeming that he was come to the gates of the Shadowy Vale, and the path went down steeply and swiftly. But when he had gone down a while, the rocks on his right hand sank lower for a space, so that he could look over and see what lay beneath.

There lay below him a long narrow vale quite plain at the bottom, walled on the further side as on the hither by sheer rocks of black stone. The plain was grown over with grass, but he could see no tree therein: a deep river, dark and green, ran through the vale, sometimes through its midmost, sometimes lapping the further rock-wall: and he thought indeed that on many a day in the year the sun would never shine on that valley.

===Chinese===
他们过那山鞍时略向东行，因地面如此崎岖破碎，行进极慢；又过一个时辰，稳足径直向东下坡，走到那石山鞍沉入另一片荒凉泥沼之处，那泥沼仍向东倾斜，但其尽头被一道峭壁横垣，峭壁之顶劈成种种奇形怪状，黑如煤炭，无草无苔。那犬径直朝那峭壁奔去，金鬃满怀好奇地紧随其后：走近了才看出那峭壁并不甚高，最高之峰距荒原之面也不到五十英尺。

他们在这些峭壁脚下穿行于散乱之石间，直到那石墙看起来最逼窄之处，石间之路转为一条斜穿而过的路径；如今这条路已是十分清晰，多半曾经过人手修整。面神沿着它随那犬下行，心想自己已来到幽谷的门户口，那路陡然急转直下。但他下了一阵之后，右手边的岩壁暂时低伏下去，他便可以从上面俯瞰，看清下面有什么。

他脚下一片狭长的谷地尽在眼底，谷底颇平，两边皆以黑色石头之绝壁为垣。平地之上青草丛生，却看不见一棵树：一道深河，又暗又绿，穿谷而过，时而流经谷之正中，时而贴着对面的石墙：他心中暗想，一年之中多半有许多日子，太阳绝不会照到那谷中。

===Original===
Thus much he saw, and then the rocks rose again and shut it from his sight; and at last they drew so close together over head that he was in a way going through a cave with little daylight coming from above, and in the end he was in a cave indeed and mere darkness: but with the last feeble glimmer of light he thought he saw carved on a smooth space of the living rock at his left hand the image of a wolf.

This cave lasted but a little way, and soon the hound and the man were going once more between sheer black rocks, and the path grew steeper yet and was cut into steps. At last there was a sharp turn, and they stood on the top of a long stony scree, down which Sure-foot bounded eagerly, giving tongue as he went; but Face-of-god stood still and looked, for now the whole Dale lay open before him.

That river ran from north to south, and at the south end the cliffs drew so close to it that looking thence no outgate could be seen; but at the north end there was as it were a dreary street of rocks, the river flowing amidmost and leaving little foothold on either side, somewhat as it was with the pass leading from the mountains into Burgdale.

Amidmost of the Dale a little toward the north end he saw a doom-ring of black stones, and hard by it an ancient hall builded of the same black stone both wall and roof, and thitherward was Sure-foot now running. Face-of-god looked up and down the Dale and could see no break in the wall of sheer rock: toward the southern end he saw a few booths and cots built roughly of stone and thatched with turf; thereabout he saw a few folk moving about, the most of whom seemed to be women and children; there were some sheep and lambs near these cots, and a herd of fifty or so of somewhat goodly mountain-kine were feeding higher up the valley. He could look down into the river from where he stood, and he saw that it ran between rocky banks going straight down from the face of the meadow, which was rather high above the water, so that it seemed little likely that the water should rise over its banks, either in summer or winter; and in summer was it like to be highest, because the vale was so near to the high mountains and their snows.

===Chinese===
他只见到了这些，然后那岩壁重又拔起，将谷地遮去不见；最后岩壁在头顶上方合得如此之近，使他仿佛走在一条洞穴之路上，头顶只有少许天光透下；末了他竟真个走入了一个洞穴，四下里一片漆黑：但在最后一线微弱的光里，他觉得他看见左手边一块平整的生石之上，刻着一头狼的像。

这洞穴并不长，不多时犬与人便又走在黑色绝壁之间，路更陡了，且被凿成一级一级的阶蹬。终于是一个急转，他们立于一道长长的乱石碎石坡之顶上，稳足急切地一路吠叫着蹦跳而下；面神却驻足而望，因为此刻整个谷地尽铺展于他眼前。

那河自北向南流，至南端处，两岸绝壁逼临河身，自那里望去，看不到任何出路；但在北端，却仿佛一条阴森的岩石长街，河居其中，两岸所留可立之处甚少，情形与自山中通往堡谷的那条隘路颇为相似。

谷地正中、稍偏北端之处，他看见一圈黑色石头所成的判决环（doom-ring），紧挨着它是一座古厅，墙与顶皆以同样的黑石筑成，稳足此刻正向那里奔去。面神上下打量那谷地，只见绝壁之墙了无缺豁：靠近南端之处，他看见几座粗糙的石筑棚屋草舍，顶上铺着草皮；那附近他看见几个人影在走动，其中大多数似乎是妇女和孩童；这些草舍旁边有些绵羊与羔羊，谷地更高之处有一群约莫五十头的颇为壮美的山牛在吃草。他可以从自己所站之处俯视河中，看见河水流于石岸之间，河岸自草地之面直坠而下，那草地高出水面颇为可观，所以无论冬夏，河水似乎都不至于漫上两岸；而且夏天的河水倒像是最高的时候，因为这谷地离高山及其积雪太近。

## XXIX They Bring the Runaways to Burgstead / 二十九 携逃奴归堡镇

===Original===
So now being out of the wood, they went peaceably and safely along the Portway, the Runaways mingling with the Dalesmen. Strange showed amidst the health and wealth of the Dale the rags and misery and nakedness of the thralls, like a dream amidst the trim gaiety of spring; and whomsoever they met, or came up with on the road, whatso his business might be, could not refrain himself from following them, but mingled with the men-at-arms, and asked them of the tidings; and when they heard who these poor people were, even delivered thralls of the Foemen, they were glad at heart and cried out for joy; and many of the women, nay, of the men also, when they first came across that misery from out the heart of their own pleasant life, wept for pity and love of the poor folk, now at last set free, and blessed the swords that should do the like by the whole people.

===Chinese===
且说众人既已出了林子，便沿港路（the Portway）平平安安地前行，逃奴（the Runaways）杂在谷民（the Dalesmen）之中。在这山谷的富足康宁之中，那些奴隶的褴褛、凄惨与赤裸，显得格格不入，仿佛春日齐整欢快的景象之中一场荒唐的梦；路上凡是遇见他们的、或是被他们赶上的，不论有何等要事，都忍不住跟随而来，杂入甲士之中，打听消息；待听说了这些可怜人究竟是谁——竟是从敌寇手中解救出来的奴隶——众人皆满心欢喜，欢呼雀跃；其中许多女子，甚至男子亦然，初见这等凄惨景象从自己优游安乐的生活之中闯入眼帘，都因怜悯、因爱护这些如今终于得脱苦海的可怜人而落泪，并祝福那些即将为全族如法炮制的刀剑。

===Original===
They went slowly as men began to gather about them; yea, some of the good folk that lived hard by must needs fare home to their houses to fetch cakes and wine for the guests; and they made them sit down and rest on the green grass by the side of the Portway, and eat and drink to cheer their hearts; others, women and young swains, while they rested went down into the meadows and plucked of the spring flowers, and twined them hastily with deft and well-wont fingers into chaplets and garlands for their heads and bodies. Thus indeed they covered their nakedness, till the lowering faces and weather-beaten skins of those hardly-entreated thralls looked grimly out from amidst the knots of cowslip and oxlip, and the branches of the milk-white blackthorn bloom, and the long trumpets of the daffodils, of the hue that wrappeth round the quill which the webster takes in hand when she would pleasure her soul with the sight of the yellow growing upon the dark green web.

===Chinese===
众人走得很慢，因为已有越来越多的人聚拢到他们周围；是啊，住在近处的良善之人，竟非要赶回家中去为宾客取来糕饼与酒；他们让逃奴在港路旁的青草地上坐下歇息，吃些东西、喝些酒以宽慰心怀；另一些人——女子和少年——乘他们歇息之时下到草甸之中，采了春日之花，以灵巧熟练的指尖匆匆编成花冠与花环，戴在他们头上、挂在他们身上。如此一来，倒将他们的赤裸遮掩起来，只是那些备受折磨的奴隶们那阴沉的脸膛与饱经风霜的皮肤，从一簇簇的莲香花与樱草花之中，从一支支乳白如雪的黑刺李（blackthorn）花枝之间，从一只只长长的喇叭状水仙花——那颜色恰如织女为悦己心、欲观黄色如何在深绿织物上渐渐晕染而执于手中之线管所缠之色——之间，冷峻地探将出来。

===Original===
So they went on again as the evening was waning, and when they were gotten within a furlong of the Gate, lo! there was come the minstrelsy, the pipe and the tabor, the fiddle and the harp, and the folk that had learned to sing the sweetest, both men and women, and Redesman at the head of them all.

Then fell the throng into an ordered company; first went the music, and then a score of Face-of-god’s warriors with drawn swords and uplifted spears; and then the flower-bedecked misery of the Runaways, men and women going together, gaunt, befouled, and hollow-eyed, with here and there a flushed cheek or gleaming eye, or tear-bedewed face, as the joy and triumph of the eve pierced through their wonted weariness of grief; then the rest of the warriors, and lastly the mingled crowd of Dalesfolk, tall men and fair women gaily arrayed, clean-faced, clear-skinned, and sleek-haired, with glancing eyes and ruddy lips.

===Chinese===
暮色渐深之时，众人又上路了；待走到距堡门（the Gate）不足一浪（furlong）之处，瞧啊！乐人已迎了上来，有吹笛的、击鼓的、拉琴的、弹竖琴的，还有那些学过最动听曲调的歌者，男女皆有，雷德斯曼（Redesman）走在最前头。

于是众人排成了一支井然有序的队伍：音乐居前，其后是面神部下二十名甲士，刀出鞘、枪高举；再后是满身花饰、形容凄惨的逃奴，男女相携而行，形销骨立、污垢满身、眼窝深陷，却也时而可见绯红的脸颊、闪光的眼目，或是泪湿的面庞——那是今夕的欢乐与凯旋穿透了他们素日因悲苦而生的疲乏；其后是余下的甲士，最后是杂沓的谷民人群，男子高大、女子美丽，装束鲜丽，面容洁净、肌肤明润、头发光亮，目光炯炯、双唇红艳。

===Original===
And now Redesman turned about to the music and drew his bow across his fiddle, and the other bows ran out in concert, and the harps followed the story of them, and he lifted up his voice and sang the words of an old song, and all the singers joined him and blended their voices with his. And these are some of the words which they sang:

> Lo! here is Spring, and all we are living,
 

 We that were wan with Winter’s fear;
 

 Reach out your hands to her hands that are giving,
 

 Lest ye lose her love and the light of the year.
> Many a morn did we wake to sorrow,
 

 When low on the land the cloud-wrath lay;
 

 Many an eve we feared tomorrow,
 

 The unbegun unfinished day.
> Ah we﻿—we hoped not, and thou wert tardy;
 

 Nought wert thou helping; nought we prayed.
 

 Where was the eager heart, the hardy?
 

 Where was the sweet-voiced unafraid?
> But now thou lovest, now thou leadest,
 

 Where is gone the grief of our minds?
 

 What was the word of the tale, that thou heedest
 

 E’en as the breath of the bygone winds?
> Green and green is thy garment growing
 

 Over thy blossoming limbs beneath;
 

 Up o’er our feet rise the blades of thy sowing,
 

 Pierced are our hearts with thine odorous breath.
> But where art thou wending, thou newcomer?
 

 Hurrying on to the Courts of the Sun?
 

 Where art thou now in the House of the Summer?
 

 Told are thy days and thy deed is done.
> Spring has been here for us that are living
 

 After the days of Winter’s fear;
 

 Here in our hands is the wealth of her giving,
 

 The Love of the Earth, and the Light of the Year.

===Chinese===
此时雷德斯曼转身面向乐班，将琴弓在小提琴上一拉，其余琴弓齐声应和，竖琴也随之应和他们的曲调；他扬起嗓音，唱起一首古歌的词句，所有歌者都加入进来，将声音融于他一处。他们所唱的，有几句是这样的：

> 看哪！春已至此，我等尽皆生还，
 

 我等曾因冬之恐惧而面色苍白；
 

 伸出你们的手，去接她那赐予之手，
 

 免得失了她的爱，失了这一年的光彩。
> 多少个清晨，我们醒来唯余悲苦，
 

 那时云怒低低压在大地之上；
 

 多少个黄昏，我们惧怕明日，
 

 那尚未开始、未竟之日子。
> 唉，我们——我们不存指望，而你也姗姗来迟；
 

 你不曾相助；我们也不曾祈求。
 

 那热切之心、那刚毅之人，今在何处？
 

 那嗓音甜美、无所畏惧之人，今在何方？
> 然如今你既爱了，如今你既引领，
 

 我们心头之悲苦，又往何处去了？
 

 那故事里说的是何言辞，你竟留意，
 

 一如那已逝之风的一息？
> 青而又青，你的衣裳渐渐滋长，
 

 覆在你那花团锦簇的肢体之上；
 

 你所播之青苗，自我等足畔升起，
 

 我们的心，被你那芬芳之气所刺透。
> 然你这新来者，要往何处去？
 

 匆匆奔赴太阳之宫庭？
 

 你此刻在夏日之居何处？
 

 你的时日已数尽，你的功业已成。
> 春已为我等生还之人降临，
 

 在那些冬之恐惧的日子之后；
 

 她所赐的丰饶，尽在我们手中，
 

 那大地之爱，那岁华之光。

===Original===
Thus came they to the Gate, and lo! the Bride thereby, leaning against a buttress, gazing with no dull eyes at the coming throng. She was now clad in her woman’s attire again, to wit a light flame-coloured gown over a green kirtle; but she yet bore a gilded helm on her head and a sword girt to her side in token of her oath to the God. She had been in Hall-face’s company in that last battle, and had done a man’s service there, fighting very valiantly, but had not been hurt, and had come back to Burgstead when the shift of men was.

Now she drew herself up and stood a little way before the Gate and looked forth on the throng, and when her eyes beheld the Runaways amidst of the weaponed carles of Burgdale, her face flushed, and her eyes filled with tears as she stood, partly wondering, partly deeming what they were. She waited till Stone-face came by her, and then she took the old man by the sleeve, and drew him apart a little and said to him: “What meaneth this show, my friend? Who hath clad these folk thus strangely; and who be these three naked tall ones, so fierce-looking, but somewhat noble of aspect?”

===Chinese===
众人就这样来到堡门之前，瞧啊！新娘（the Bride）正倚在一根扶壁旁，以并不迟钝的目光，注视着涌来的众人。她此刻又换回了女子装束，即一件浅色火焰色外袍，内衬绿色短袍；但她头上仍戴着一顶镀金盔，腰间仍佩着一口剑，以为她对神所立之誓的标记。在那最后一场战事中，她曾随厅面（Hall-face）一同出征，并在阵前立下男子般的功勋，奋勇厮杀，却未曾负伤，待到换防之时便回了堡镇。

此时她挺身站定，在堡门前不远之处，望着那群人；待她目光看见那些逃奴杂在堡谷（Burgdale）的持械汉子之间，她脸上泛起红晕，眼中盈满泪水，站在那里，一半是惊奇，一半是在揣测这些人是谁。她等到石面（Stone-face）走到跟前，便扯住老人的衣袖，将他稍稍拉到一旁，对他说道："朋友，这等排场是何意？是谁给这些人穿戴上如此古怪的装扮？那三个赤身露体、身材高大、面相凶悍却又略带贵气的人，又是谁？"

===Original===
For indeed those three men of the kindreds, when they had gotten into the Dale, and had rested them, and drunk a cup of wine, and when they had seen the chaplets and wreaths of the spring-flowers wherewith they were bedecked, and had smelt the sweet savour of them, fell to walking proudly, heeding not their nakedness; for no rag had they upon them save breech-clouts of deerskin: they had changed weapons with the Burgdale carles; and one had gotten a great axe, which he bore over his shoulder, and the shaft thereof was all done about with copper; and another had shouldered a long heavy thrusting-spear, and the third, an exceeding tall man, bore a long broad-bladed war-sword. Thus they went, brown of skin beneath their flower-garlands, their long hair bleached by the sun falling about their shoulders; high they strode amongst the shuffling carles and tripping women of the later-come thralls. But when they heard the music, and saw that they were coming to the Gate in triumph, strange thoughts of old memories swelled up in their hearts, and they refrained them not from weeping, for they felt that the joy of life had come back to them.

Nor must it be deemed that these were the only ones amongst the Runaways whose hearts were cheered and softened: already were many of them coming back to life, as they felt their worn bodies caressed by the clear soft air of Burgdale, and the sweetness of the flowers that hung about them, and saw all round about the kind and happy faces of their well-willers.

So Stone-face looked on the Bride as she stood with face yet tear-bedewed, awaiting his answer, and said:

===Chinese===
原来那三个宗族出身之人，待进了山谷、歇息片刻、饮过一杯酒，又看见戴在自己身上的春花所编的花冠与花环，闻到那芬芳之气，便昂首阔步起来，全不以赤身为意；原来他们身上除了一方鹿皮的裈裤之外，再无寸缕：他们已与堡谷的汉子交换了兵器；一个得了一柄大斧，扛在肩上，斧柄全以铜缠裹；一个扛了一杆又长又重的刺枪；第三个——一个极其高大之人——则持一口长而宽刃的战剑。他们就这样走着，在花环之下露出棕色的皮肤，那被日光晒淡的长发披散在肩头；他们在那些后来才沦为奴隶的、步履蹒跚的汉子与踉跄的女子之间，高视阔步。然而待他们听见音乐，又看见自己正凯旋地向堡门行来，心中便涌起一种种古老记忆的奇异思绪，他们也不再抑制眼泪，因为他们感到生命之乐又回到了身上。

也不可认为，逃奴之中唯这几人的心肠得到了宽慰与软化：他们之中已有许多人正在重获新生，因为他们感到自己那疲惫的身躯正为堡谷清朗柔和的空气所抚慰，为挂在身上的花朵之甜香所抚慰，又看见周围尽是一张张和善快乐的、好心人的面孔。

于是石面望着新娘——她还泪痕满面地站在那里等他回答——说道：

===Original===
“Daughter, thou sayest who clad these folk thus? It was misery that hath so dight them; and they are the images of what we shall be if we love foul life better than fair death, and so fall into the hands of the Felons, who were the masters of these men. As for the tall naked men, they are of our own blood, and kinsmen to Face-of-god’s new friends; and they are of the best of the vanquished: it was in early days that they fled from thralldom; as we may have to do. Now, daughter, I bid thee be as joyous as thou art valiant, and then shall all be well.”

Therewith she smiled on him, and he departed, and she stood a little while, as the throng moved on and was swallowed by the Gate, and looked after them; and for all her pity for the other folk, she thought chiefly of those fearless tall men who were of the blood of those with whom it was lawful to wed.

There she stood as the wind dried the tears upon her cheeks, thinking of the sorrow which these folk had endured, and their stripes and mocking, their squalor and famine; and she wondered and looked on her own fair and shapely hands with the precious finger-rings thereon, and on the dainty cloth and trim broidery of her sleeve; and she touched her smooth cheek with the back of her hand, and smiled, and felt the spring sweet in her mouth, and its savour goodly in her nostrils; and therewith she called to mind the aspect of her lovely body, as whiles she had seen it imaged, all its full measure, in the clear pool at midsummer, or piecemeal, in the shining steel of the Westland mirror. She thought also with what joy she drew the breath of life, yea, even amidst of grief, and of how sweet and pure and well-nurtured she was, and how well beloved of many friends and the whole folk, and she set all this beside those woeful bodies and lowering faces, and felt shame of her sorrow of heart, and the pain it had brought to her; and ever amidst shame and pity of all that misery rose up before her the images of those tall fierce men, and it seemed to her as if she had seen something like to them in some dream or imagination of her mind.

===Chinese===
"女儿啊，你问是谁给这些人穿上这等装束？正是苦难把他们打扮成这样；他们的模样，正是我们若贪恋苟活、轻弃美死，从而落入恶徒（the Felons）——即这些人昔日之主——之手后的写照。至于那三个赤身的高大汉子，他们与我们同宗同血，是面神新交的朋友的族人；他们是被征服者中最优秀的一批：早在昔日，他们便已逃离了奴役；正如我们将来或许也要这样做。如今，女儿啊，我劝你既勇毅，便也欢欣起来吧，如此则一切皆安。"

她闻言对他一笑，他便离去了；她又站了一会儿，看那人群向前涌去，被堡门吞没，目送他们远去；她虽怜悯其余众人，心头所想的，却尽是那几个无所畏惧的高大汉子——他们正是与族人合法通婚的那一血脉之人。

她就那样站着，任风干去颊上的泪，想着这些人所承受的苦难，他们的鞭笞与戏弄、他们的肮脏与饥荒；她惊讶地望着自己那双美丽匀称、戴着贵重指环的手，望着袖上精致的衣料与齐整的绣工；她以手背轻触自己光滑的脸颊，微笑了，觉得春之味在口中是甜的，其香在鼻中是美好的；于是她又想起自己可爱身躯的模样——她有时曾在仲夏时节清澈的水潭中，照见自己全身的倒影，或在那西土（the Westland）镜子的闪耀钢面上，照见自己一肢一节。她又想，自己怀着何等的喜悦吸入生命之气——即便身处悲哀之中亦然——自己是何等甜美、纯净、教养良好，又何等深得众友与全族之爱；她将这一切，与那些愁苦的身躯、阴沉的面孔并列，竟为自己方才心中的悲伤、以及那悲伤所带来的痛楚，感到羞愧；然而在那羞愧与怜悯之中，那些高大凶悍之人的身影，总在她眼前一再浮现，她仿佛曾在某场梦里、或心中的某种想象里，见过与他们相类之人。

===Original===
So came the Burgdalers and their guests into the street of Burgstead amidst music and singing; and the throng was great there. Then Face-of-god bade make a ring about the strangers, and they did so, and he and the Runaways alone were in the midst of it; and he spake in a loud voice and said:

“Men of the Dale and the Burg, these folk whom here ye see in such a sorry plight are they whom our deadly foes have rejoiced to torment; let us therefore rejoice to cherish them. Now let those men come forth who deem that they have enough and more, so that they may each take into their houses some two or three of these friends such as would fain be together. And since I am War-leader, and have the right hereto, I will first choose them whom I will lead into the House of the Face. And lo you! will I have this man (and he laid his hand on Dallach), who is he whom I first came across, and who found us all these others, and next I will have yonder tall carles, the three of them, because I perceive them to be men meet to be with a War-leader, and to follow him in battle.”

===Chinese===
于是堡谷人携他们的宾客，在乐声与歌声之中，走进了堡镇的街衢；那里人山人海。面神便命人在这些异乡人周围围成一圈，众人依言而行，圈中只有他与逃奴；他扬声说道：

"谷中之民、堡中之民，你们在这里所见的这些穷愁潦倒之人，正是我们的死敌以折磨他们为乐的那一班；那么，让我们以抚恤他们为乐吧。如今，凡自以为衣食丰足有余的，都请站出来，好各自领这两三个朋友——那般愿意相聚一处的人——回自己家去。我既是战首（War-leader），便有此权，我要第一个挑选我愿领入面神之宅（the House of the Face）的人。瞧啊！我要这个人——"（他把手按在达拉赫（Dallach）身上）——"他是我最先遇见的那一个，也是他为我们找来了所有其余的人；其次，我要那边那三个高大汉子，因为我看出他们正是宜于随侍战首、在战场之上追随他的人。"

===Original===
Therewith he drew the three Men of the Wolf towards him, but Dallach already was standing beside him. And folk rejoiced in Face-of-god.

But the Bride came forward next, and spake to him meekly and simply:

“War-leader, let me have of the women those who need me most, that I may bring them to the House of the Steer, and try if there be not some good days yet to be found for them, wherein they shall but remember the past grief as an ugly dream.”

===Chinese===
说着，他便将那三个狼之子（the Men of the Wolf）拉到自己身边，而达拉赫早已立在他身旁了。众人皆因面神而欢喜。

其后，新娘走上前来，谦和而率直地对他说道：

"战首，让我领走那些女子中最需要我的人吧，好把她们带到犍牛族之宅（the House of the Steer）去，看看是否还能为她们寻得几个好日子，使她们把过去的悲苦只当作一场丑陋的梦来回忆。"

===Original===
Then Face-of-god looked on her, and him-seemed he had never seen her so fair; and all the shame wherewith he had beheld her of late was gone from him, and his heart ran over with friendly love towards her as she looked into his face with kindly eyes; and he said:

“Kinswoman, take thy choice as thy kindness biddeth, and happy shall they be whom thou choosest.”

She bowed her head soberly, and chose from among the guests four women of the saddest and most grievous, and no man of their kindred spake for going along with them; then she went her ways home, leading one of them by the hand, and strange was it to see those twain going through sun and shade together, that poor wretch along with the goodliest of women.

Then came forward one after other of the worthy goodmen of the Dale, and especially such as were old, and they led away one one man, and another two, and another three, and often would a man crave to go with a woman or a woman with a man, and it was not gainsaid them. So were all the guests apportioned, and ill-content were those goodmen that had to depart without a guest; and one man would say to another: “Such-an-one, be not downcast; this guest shall be between us, if he will, and shall dwell with thee and me month about; but this first month with me, since I was first comer.” And so forth was it said.

===Chinese===
面神看着她，只觉自己从未见过她如此美丽；近来他看她时心中所有的那份羞愧，此刻已荡然无存，当她和善地望着他的脸时，他的心溢满了对她的友爱之情；他说道：

"族姐，随你的善心所愿去挑吧，被你挑中的人，必是有福的。"

她庄重地低下头，从宾客中挑了四个最为愁苦可怜的女子，她们的族中并无男子开口要随同前去；她便领着其中一人之手，径自回家去了；这一对一同穿行于日影与树阴之间，那可怜人与这最美的女子同行，倒是奇异的景象。

其后，谷中那些体面的户主一个接一个走上前来，尤其是那些上了年纪的，他们或领走一人，或两人，或三人；常有男子愿随女子同去，或女子愿随男子同去，也不曾有人驳回。如此一来，所有宾客都被分派尽了，那些不得不空手而归的户主，心中大为不满；一人会对另一人说："某某啊，莫要沮丧；这个客人，若他愿意，便算我们两人共有的，在你我两家一月一轮地住；不过头一个月归我，因为是我先来的。"诸如此类，不一而足。

===Original===
Now to prevent the time to come, it may be said about the Runaways, that when they had been a little while amongst the Burgdalers, well fed and well clad and kindly cherished, it was marvellous how they were bettered in aspect of body, and it began to be seen of them that they were well-favoured people, and divers of the women exceeding goodly, black-haired and grey-eyed, and very clear-skinned and white-skinned; most of them were young, and the oldest had not seen above forty winters. They of Rosedale, and especially such as had first fled away to the wood, were very soon seen to be merry and kindly folk; but they who had been longest in captivity, and notably those from Silverdale who were not of the kindreds, were for a long time sullen and heavy, and it availed little to trust to them for the doing of work; albeit they would follow about their friends of Burgdale with the love of a dog; also they were, divers of them, somewhat thievish, and if they lacked anything would liefer take it by stealth than ask for it; which forsooth the Burgdale men took not amiss, but deemed of it as a jest rather.

===Chinese===
此处且先提一句后话：关于这些逃奴，可以这样说——他们在堡谷人之中住了不多几时，吃得饱、穿得暖、又蒙善意相待，其形容体貌之好转实在令人称奇；众人这才渐渐看出，他们原来都是些容貌端正之人，其中更有几个女子极其标致，黑发灰瞳，肌肤洁净白皙；他们大多年纪尚轻，最年长的也不曾过四十个冬天。那些来自玫瑰谷（Rosedale）的人——尤其是最早逃入林中的那一批——很快便显出是些快活和善的人；然而那些被囚最久的人，尤其是银谷（Silverdale）之中非宗族出身的那些，长久地郁郁沉闷、神思迟钝，要指望他们干活是没有什么用的；虽说他们会如犬之恋主一般，寸步不离地追随他们在堡谷的朋友；他们之中也有好些人略有些手脚不干净，缺了什么，宁可偷偷摸摸地拿，也不肯开口讨要；不过堡谷人倒也不以为忤，反而当作一桩笑谈。

===Original===
Very few of the Runaways had any will to fare back to their old homes, or indeed could be got to go into the wood, or, after a day or two, to say any word of Rosedale or Silverdale. In this and other matters the Burgdalers dealt with them as with children who must have their way; for they deemed that their guests had much time to make up; also they were well content when they saw how goodly they were, for these Dalesmen loved to see men goodly of body and of a cheerful countenance.

As for Dallach and the three Silverdale men of the kindred, they went gladly whereas the Burgdale men would have them; and half a score others took weapons in their hands when the war was foughten: concerning which more hereafter.

===Chinese===
逃奴之中，极少有人愿意回到故土去；事实上，连哄他们进林子都办不到，过了一两日，连玫瑰谷或银谷的字眼都不肯提一个。在这件事及其他诸事上，堡谷人都把他们当作非任性不可的孩子一般看待；因为他们想，这些客人有好长的时日要弥补；再者，他们看到这些客人形容俊美，也很是欢喜，因为谷民向来喜欢看到体格健美、神色开朗之人。

至于达拉赫与那三个银谷宗族出身之人，堡谷人要他们到哪里，他们便欣然到哪里；另有十个人在那场战事打响之时也执起了兵器：这些事下文再说。

===Original===
But on the even whereof the tale now tells, Face-of-god and Stone-face and their company met after nightfall in the Hall of the Face clad in glorious raiment, and therewith were Dallach and the men of Silverdale, washen and docked of their long hair, after the fashion of warriors who bear the helm; and they were clad in gay attire, with battle-swords girt to their sides and gold rings on their arms. Somewhat stern and sad-eyed were those Silverdalers yet, though they looked on those about them kindly and courteously when they met their eyes; and Face-of-god yearned towards them when he called to mind the beauty and wisdom and loving-kindness of the Sun-beam. They were, as aforesaid, strong men and tall, and one of them taller than any amidst that house of tall men. Their names were Wolf-stone, the tallest, and God-swain, and Spear-fist; and God-swain the youngest was of thirty winters, and Wolf-stone of forty. They came into the Hall in such wise, that when they were washed and attired, and all men were assembled in the Hall, and the Alderman and the chieftains sitting on the dais, Face-of-god brought them in from the out-bower, holding Dallach by the right hand and Wolf-stone by the left; and he looked but a stripling beside that huge man.

And when the men in the Hall beheld such goodly warriors, and remembered their grief late past, they all stood up and shouted for joy of them. But Face-of-god passed up the Hall with them, and stood before the dais and said:

“O Alderman of the Dale and Chief of the House of the Face, here I bring to you the foes of our foemen, whom I have met in the Wildwood, and bidden to our House; and meseemeth they will be our friends, and stand beside us in the day of battle. Therefore I say, take these guests and me together, or put us all to the door together; and if thou wilt take them, then show them to such places as thou deemest meet.”

===Chinese===
然而，在这故事所述的那日傍晚，入夜之后，面神与石面及其一行人，皆身着华服，会聚于面神之宅的厅堂之中；与他们同在的，还有达拉赫与那几个银谷人，他们已经沐浴过，又按戴盔武士之俗，剪短了长发；他们穿着鲜丽的衣裳，腰间佩着战剑，臂上戴着金环。那些银谷人仍有些严峻、目光带些忧愁，然而当与旁人对视之时，他们的目光却和蔼有礼；面神一想起日光（Sun-beam）的美丽、智慧与慈爱，便对他们心生怜惜。如前所述，他们都是些强壮高大之人，其中一人比这座满是大汉之宅中任何一人都要高。他们的名字是：最高的那个叫狼石（Wolf-stone），还有神仆（God-swain）、枪拳（Spear-fist）；最年轻的神仆三十个冬天，狼石则四十个冬天。他们是这样进入厅堂的：待他们沐浴穿戴完毕，众人也都聚在厅中，长老与众首领坐于高台之上，面神便从外厢将他们领入——他右手牵着达拉赫，左手牵着狼石；在那大汉身边，他看来不过是个少年。

厅中众人见到如此英武的战士，又想起他们方才所受的苦，全都站起身来，为他们欢呼。面神陪着他们走过厅堂，立于高台之前，说道：

"堡谷的长老啊、面神之宅的首领啊，我在这里给你们带来的是我们敌人的敌人，是我在野林（the Wildwood）中所遇、邀至我家的客人；据我看，他们将成为我们的朋友，在征战之日与我们并肩而立。所以我说，要么连同这些客人一并收下我，要么把我们一同逐出门外；你若肯收留他们，便请给他们安排你认为相称的座位。"

===Original===
Then stood up the Alderman and said:

“Men of Silverdale and Rosedale, I bid you welcome! Be ye our friends, and abide here with us as long as seemeth good to you, and share in all that is ours. Son Face-of-god, show these warriors to seats on the dais beside thee, and cherish them as well as thou knowest how.”

Then Face-of-god brought them up on to the dais and sat down on the right hand of his father, with Dallach on his right hand, and then Wolf-stone out from him; then sat Stone-face, that there might be a man of the Dale to talk with them and serve them; and on his right hand first Spear-fist and then God-swain. And when they were all sat down, and the meat was on the board, Iron-face turned to his son Face-of-god and took his hand, and said in a loud voice, so that many might hear him:

“Son Face-of-god, son Gold-mane, thou bearest with thee both ill luck and good. Erewhile, when thou wanderedst out into the Wildwood, seeking thou knewest not what from out of the Land of Dreams, thou didst but bring aback to us grief and shame; but now that thou hast gone forth with the neighbours seeking thy foemen, thou hast come aback to us with thine hands full of honour and joy for us, and we thank thee for thy gifts, and I call thee a lucky man. Herewith, kinsman, I drink to thee and the lasting of thy luck.”

Therewith he stood up and drank the health of the War-leader and the Guests: and all men were exceeding joyous thereat, when they called to mind his wrath at the Gate-thing, and they shouted for gladness as they drank that health, and the feast became exceeding merry in the House of the Face; and as to the war to come, it seemed to them as if it were over and done in all triumph.

===Chinese===
于是长老（the Alderman）站起身来，说道：

"银谷与玫瑰谷的人们，我欢迎你们！做我们的朋友吧，只要你们觉得如意，便在这里与我们同住，与我们共享我们所有的一切。面神儿啊，引这些武士到高台上你身边的座位去，尽你所知尽力地款待他们吧。"

面神便把他们引上高台，坐在他父亲的右手边，达拉赫坐在他的右手，再过去是狼石；其下坐着石面，以便有一个谷中之人陪他们说话、侍奉他们；石面右手边先坐枪拳，再坐神仆。众人坐定，肉肴已上桌，铁面（Iron-face）转向他的儿子面神，握住他的手，扬声说道，好让许多人都能听见：

"面神儿啊，金鬃（Gold-mane）儿啊，你带来的既有厄运，也有好运。前些时你信步走入野林，从那梦之乡中寻觅连你自己也说不清的东西，给我们带回的不过是悲愁与耻辱；而如今你随邻里一同出去、寻你的仇敌而去，却满载着赐予我们的荣光与欢愉而归，我们为你的馈赠致谢，我说你是个有福气的人。族亲啊，我以此杯祝你，祝你的福气长存不衰。"

说着他便站起身来，为战首与众宾客祝饮：众人想起他在门会（the Gate-thing）上的那场怒火，此刻无不格外欣喜，一边饮那祝酒，一边欢呼雀跃，面神之宅中的盛宴变得极为热闹欢腾；至于那场将来之战，在他们看来，仿佛早已凯旋、尘埃落定一般。

## XIII They Fare to the Hunting of the Elk / 十三 众人出猎麋鹿

===Original===
When they came into the Hall, the hearth-fire had been quickened, and the sleepers on the floor had been woken, and all folk were astir. So the old man sat down by the hearth while Gold-mane busied himself in fetching wood and water, and in sweeping out the Hall, and other such works of the early morning. In a little while Hall-face and the other young men and warriors were afoot duly clad, and the Alderman came from his chamber and greeted all men kindly. Soon meat was set upon the boards, and men broke their fast; and day dawned while they were about it, and ere it was all done the sun rose clear and golden, so that all men knew that the day would be fair, for the frost seemed hard and enduring.

Then the eager young men and the hunters, and those who knew the mountain best drew together about the hearth, and fell to talking of the hunting of the elk; and there were three there who knew both the woods and also the fells right up to the ice-rivers better than any other; and these said that they who were fain of the hunting of the elk would have no likelier time than that day for a year to come. Short was the rede betwixt them, for they said they would go to the work at once and make the most of the short winter daylight. So they went each to his place, and some outside that House to their fathers' houses to fetch each man his gear. Face-of-god for his part went to his shut-bed, and stood by his chest, and opened it, and drew out of it a fine hauberk of ring-mail which his father had made for him: for though Face-of-god was a deft wright, he was not by a long way so deft as his father, who was the deftest of all men of that time and country; so that the alien merchants would give him what he would for his hauberks and helms, whenso he would chaffer with them, which was but seldom. So Face-of-god did on this hauberk over his kirtle, and over it he cast his foul-weather weed, so that none might see it: he girt a strong war-sword to his side, cast his quiver over his shoulder, and took his bow in his hand, although he had little lust to shoot elks that day, even as Stone-face had said; therewithal he took his skids, and went forth of the hall to the gate of the Burg; whereto gathered the whole company of twenty-three, and Gold-mane the twenty-fourth. And each man there had his skids and his bow and quiver, and whatso other weapon, as short-sword, or wood-knife, or axe, seemed good to him.

So they went out-a-gates, and clomb the stairway in the cliff which led to the ancient watchtower: for it was on the lower slopes of the fells which lay near to the Weltering Water that they looked to find the elks, and this was the nighest road thereto. When they had gotten to the top they lost no time, but went their ways nearly due east, making way easily where there were but scattered trees close to the lip of the sheer cliffs.

===Chinese===
待他们进入厅堂，炉火已重新拨旺，席地而卧之人已被唤醒，众人皆已起身忙活。老人便在炉边坐下，金鬃则忙于打柴挑水，清扫厅堂，并做些清晨的杂活。不多时，厅面与那班少年武士都已穿戴齐整、纷纷起身，长老自卧房出来，与众人和颜相见。须臾肉食布满案几，众人便用早膳；用膳之际天色已明，事尚未毕，一轮金灿灿的日头已自天边升起，众人都晓得今日必是晴好之天，盖因那霜看来下得又厚又坚。

于是心急的少年们、猎手们，以及最熟知山势之人，皆围聚炉畔，谈起猎麋之事；其中有三人，无论林莽还是远至冰河之山岳，皆比任何人都熟；此三人道：好猎麋之人，今后一年之内再无更胜今日的时机了。三人计议甚短，只说须即刻动手，好好用上冬日这短短的白昼。于是众人各归其处，有的走出此宅，回父宅去取各自的器械。面神自回其封闭木榻卧间，立于箱箧之侧，开箧，从中取出一件精良的锁子环甲——此甲乃其父为他亲手所制：盖因面神虽是巧匠，比起其父却差得远；其父乃彼时彼地一切匠人中之最巧者，故异乡商人但与他交易甲胄头盔，无不任其开价、予取予求——只是他甚少与他们做这等买卖罢了。于是面神将这锁子甲穿在长袍之外，外头再罩上一件风雪外袍，使人不得而见：腰间佩一口利战剑，肩上挎一壶箭，手中提着弓——虽然他那一日并无心射麋，正如石面所言；他又取了雪板，自厅中出来，往堡门而去；众人共二十三名陆续聚于堡门之处，加上金鬃，恰为第二十四人。人人各携雪板、弓、箭壶，以及各自所好的旁的器械——或短剑，或猎刀，或斧。

于是众人出堡门外，攀上那道通往古望楼的崖阶：盖因他们料想在濒临翻滚河（the Weltering Water）的崇山下部山坡之上，可寻得麋鹿，而这条路是去彼处最近之路。既登其巅，不敢耽搁，便径直东行，于绝壁唇口近旁、林木疏落之处，举步甚易。

===Original===
They went merrily on their skids over the close-lying snow, and were soon up on the great shoulders of the fells that went up from the bank of the Weltering Water: at noon they came into a little dale wherein were a few trees, and there they abided to eat their meat, and were very merry, making for themselves tables and benches of the drifted snow, and piling it up to windward as a defence against the wind, which had now arisen, little but bitter from the southeast; so that some, and they the wisest, began to look for foul weather: wherefore they tarried the shorter while in the said dale or hollow.

But they were scarcely on their way again before the aforesaid southeast wind began to grow bigger, and at last blew a gale, and brought up with it a drift of fine snow, through which they yet made their way, but slowly, till the drift grew so thick that they could not see each other five paces apart.

Then perforce they made stay, and gathered together under a bent which by good luck they happened upon, where they were sheltered from the worst of the drift. There they abode, till in less than an hour's space the drift abated and the wind fell, and in a little while after it was quite clear, with the sun shining brightly and the young waxing moon white and high up in the heavens; and the frost was harder than ever.

===Chinese===
众人踏着雪板，于平铺厚实之雪上欢然前行，不多时便登上自翻滚河岸拔起的那几座大山肩：至正午，进入一座几株树木散生的小山谷，遂在那里停下吃肉食，兴致甚高，以积起来的雪堆作桌、作凳，并在上风处堆起雪墙以挡风——此时风已起，自东南吹来，虽不大却冷冽刺骨；于是其中几位——也是最老成稳重之人——开始担心天要变坏：因此他们在这座小山谷，亦即那处洼地里，并未久留。

然而他们方才上路不多时，前述之东南风便越刮越大，终至狂风大作，又夹着一阵细雪飞旋；众人仍勉力前行，却走得甚慢，到后来飞雪浓密，相隔五步之遥竟彼此不能相辨。

无奈之下众人只得停下，幸而撞见一处背风土坡，便聚于其下，得以避开飞雪最猛之处。他们便在那里暂避，不到一个钟头，飞雪渐止，风亦息；再过一会儿便豁然晴朗，日头明晃晃地照着，初生渐盈之月皓白高悬于天；霜寒反倒比前更重。

===Original===
This seemed good to them; but now that they could see each other's faces they fell to telling over their company, and there was none missing save Face-of-god. They were somewhat dismayed thereat, but knew not what to do, and they deemed he might not be far off, either a little behind or a little ahead; and Hall-face said:

"There is no need to make this to-do about my brother; he can take good care of himself; neither does a warrior of the Face die because of a little cold and frost and snowdrift. Withal Gold-mane is a wilful man, and of late days hath been wilful beyond his wont; let us now find the elks."

So they went on their ways hoping to fall in with him again. No long story need be made of their hunting, for not very far from where they had taken shelter they came upon the elks, many of them, impounded in the drifts, pretty much where the deft hunters looked to find them. There then was battle between the elks and the men, till the beasts were all slain and only one man hurt: then they made them sleighs from wood which they found in the hollows thereby, and they laid the carcasses thereon, and so turned their faces homeward, dragging their prey with them. But they met not Face-of-god either there or on the way home; and Hall-face said: "Maybe Gold-mane will lie on the fell tonight; and I would I were with him; for adventures oft befall such folk when they abide in the wilds."

===Chinese===
众人见此甚喜；但既已能看见彼此面目，便点算起人数来，一数之下，独独少了一个面神。众人颇为忧急，却也不知所措，只道他离此不远，或在前，或在后；厅面便道：

「我兄弟这事，何必大惊小怪；他自己保管没事；面神一族的武士，岂会因区区寒冷霜雪便丧了性命。况且金鬃本是个任性之人，近日里更比往常加倍任性；且由他去，我们去找麋鹿罢。」

于是众人继续前行，盼着再与他相会。这场猎事不必细表：盖因离他们避风之处不远，便撞上一群麋鹿，为数甚多，皆陷于雪堆之中不得脱身，恰在那班巧猎手所料之处。于是人鹿之间展开一场鏖战，直到鹿群尽数被杀，唯独一名猎手受了伤：众人便就附近洼地中寻得木材，造了几副雪橇，将鹿尸一一抬上，遂掉头转向归途，拖曳猎物而回。然而无论在彼处还是在归途之上，他们都未见面神；厅面说道：「金鬃今夜多半要在山上过夜了；但愿我能与他同在；盖因这种人物一旦流落荒野之中，每每遭遇奇遇。」

===Original===
Now it was late at night by then they reached Burgstead, so laden as they were with the dead beasts; but they heeded the night little, for the moon was well-nigh as bright as day for them. But when they came to the gate of the Thorp, there were assembled the goodmen and swains to meet them with torches and wine in their honour. There also was Gold-mane come back before them, yea for these two hours; and he stood clad in his holiday raiment and smiled on them.

Then was there some jeering at him that he was come back empty-handed from the hunting, and that he was not able to abide the wind and the drift; but he laughed thereat, for all this was but game and play, since men knew him for a keen hunter and a stout woodsman; and they had deemed it a heavy loss of him if he had been cast away, as some feared he had been: and his brother Hall-face embraced him and kissed him, and said to him: "Now the next time that thou farest to the wood will I be with thee foot to foot, and never leave thee, and then meseemeth I shall wot of the tale that hath befallen thee, and belike it shall be no sorry one."

Face-of-god laughed and answered but little, and they all betook them to the House of the Face and held high feast therein, for as late as the night was, in honour of this Hunting of the Elk.

===Chinese===
且说众人到达堡镇之时，已是深夜，所携死兽甚是沉重；但他们并不以夜行为意，盖因月色明亮，几乎如同白昼。然而当他们来到屯门之时，堡中的户长与少年们已执火炬、捧美酒齐集相迎。金鬃也先他们而归——已回来足足两个钟头了；只见他身着节庆华服，对他们微笑而立。

于是有人取笑他空手而归、说他经不起风雪、半途而废；他却一笑置之，盖因这一切不过是戏耍玩笑，因众人素知他是个厉害的猎手、硬朗的林中汉子；又素来当他是个宝——倘若他真如某些人所担心的那样葬身雪海，必是莫大损失：他的兄弟厅面则搂住他亲了一口，对他说道：「下次你再去林中，我必与你并肩同行、寸步不离，到那时，你遭逢的故事我自然就知道了，料想必不是一桩乏味之事。」

面神只笑，不多答话，众人便一同回到面神之宅（the House of the Face），于其中大设宴席——虽夜已深——以庆贺此番猎麋之事。

===Original===
No man cared to question Face-of-god closely as to how or where he had strayed from the hunt; for he had told his own tale at once as soon as he came home, to wit, that his right-foot skid-strap had broken, and even while he stopped to mend it came on that drift and weather; and that he could not move from that place without losing his way, and that when it had cleared he knew not whither they had gone because the snow had covered their slot. So he deemed it not unlike that they had gone back, and that he might come up with one or two on the way, and that in any case he wotted well that they could look after themselves; so he turned back, not going very swiftly. All this seemed like enough, and a little matter except to jest about, so no man made any question concerning it: only old Stone-face said to himself:

"Now were I fain to have a true tale out of him, but it is little likely that anything shall come of my much questioning; and it is ill forcing a young man to tell lies."

So he held his peace, and the feast went on merrily and blithely.

===Chinese===
无人有意当面神之面细问他如何走失、于何处走失；盖因他在归家之时已将自己一番话原原本本说过：右脚雪板的束带断了，他停下来修理之时，正赶上那阵飞雪与坏天；他若一离开那处便要迷路，待到天色放晴，他已不知众人去了何方，因雪已盖住了他们的踪迹。于是他料想众人多半已经折返，便掉头回来，路上或许还能追上一两个同伴；况且他深知众人自能照料自己；于是他便回转，行得也不甚急。这番话听起来颇为有理，又是无关紧要的小事一桩，无非拿来打趣罢了，故而无人深究：唯独老石面暗自思忖：

「我倒很想从他口中套出实话，只是再三盘问未必能问出什么来；况且逼一个年轻人撒谎，到底不是好事。」

于是他按捺不发，宴席依旧欢畅热烈地进行下去。

## III They Talk of Divers Matters in the Hall / 三 众人于厅中谈论诸事

===Original===
Now Face-of-god, who is also called Gold-mane, rose up to meet the newcomers, and each of them greeted him kindly, and the Bride kissed him on the cheek, and he her in likewise; and he looked kindly on her, and took her hand, and went on up the hall to the dais, following his father and the old man; as for him, he was of the kindred of the House, and was foster-father of Iron-face and of his sons both; and his name was Stone-face: a stark warrior had he been when he was young, and even now he could do a man's work in the battlefield, and his understanding was as good as that of a man in his prime. So went these and four others up on to the dais and sat down before the thwart-table looking down the hall, for the meat was now on the board; and of the others there were some fifty men and women who were deemed to be of the kindred and sat at the endlong tables.

===Chinese===
面神——亦即人称金鬃者——起身迎接新到的客人，众人皆亲切地与他见礼，新娘在他颊上亲了一下，他也同样回亲；他和善地看着她，牵起她的手，随父亲与那位老人继续向厅堂高台走去。至于那位老人，他是此宅宗族中人，乃是铁面及其诸子的养父；他名叫石面：年轻时是一名猛将，至今在战场上仍能做壮汉之事，其心智见识也不减盛年之人。于是这几位连同另外四人登上高台，在横案前坐定，居高临下望着整座厅堂——此时肉食已陈于案上；此外还有约五十名男女，皆被视为同族之人，坐在两侧的纵长案旁。

===Original===
So then the Alderman stood up and made the sign of the Hammer over the meat, the token of his craft and of his God. Then they fell to with good hearts, for there was enough and to spare of meat and drink. There was bread and flesh (though not Gold-mane's venison), and leeks and roasted chestnuts of the grove, and red-cheeked apples of the garth, and honey enough of that year's gathering, and medlars sharp and mellow: moreover, good wine of the western bents went up and down the hall in great gilded copper bowls and in mazers girt and lipped with gold.

===Chinese===
于是长老起身，在肉食之上画了锤符（the sign of the Hammer）——那是他手艺与所奉之神的标记。众人便兴致勃勃地大吃起来，盖因酒肉丰足，尽够食用。席上有面包、有肉（虽不是金鬃的鹿肉），有韭菜，有林中烤熟的栗子，有园圃里红颊的苹果，有当年采得的丰足蜂蜜，还有酸甜参半的欧楂：更有西面草坡所产的佳酿，盛在镀金的大铜碗与镶金包口的枫木碗中，于厅堂里来回传递不绝。

===Original===
But when they were full of meat, and had drunken somewhat, they fell to speech, and Iron-face spake aloud to his son, who had but been speaking softly to the Bride as one playmate to the other: but the Alderman said: "Scarce are the wood-deer grown, kinsman, when I must needs eat sheep's flesh on a Thursday, though my son has lain abroad in the woods all night to hunt for me."

And therewith he smiled in the young man's face; but Gold-mane reddened and said: "So is it, kinsman, I can hit what I can see; but not what is hidden."

===Chinese===
众人吃饱喝足、略带酒意之后，便攀谈起来。铁面高声对儿子说话——方才那儿子不过是在和新娘低声细语，如同一对玩伴一般；只听这位长老说道：「族亲啊，林中的鹿何时竟这般稀少了，竟教我在星期四非得吃起羊肉来——虽说我的儿子为替我打猎，在林中野外宿了一整夜。」

说着，他朝年轻人的脸露出笑意；金鬃却红了脸，说道：「确是如此，族亲；我射得中我看得见的，却射不中那藏起来的。」

===Original===
Iron-face laughed and said: "Hast thou been to the Woodland-Carles? are their women fairer than our cousins?"

Face-of-god took up the Bride's hand in his and kissed it and laid it to his cheek; and then turned to his father and said: "Nay, father, I saw not the Wood-carles, nor went to their abode; and on no day do I lust after their women. Moreover, I brought home a roebuck of the fattest; but I was over-late for Kettel, and the flesh was ready for the board by then I came."

"Well, son," quoth Iron-face, for he was merry, "a roebuck is but a little deer for such big men as are thou and I. But I rede thee take the Bride along with thee the next time; and she shall seek whilest thou sleepest, and hit when thou missest."

===Chinese===
铁面笑道：「你莫不是去了林中汉子（the Woodland-Carles）那里？他们的女子比咱们的表姐妹更美么？」

面神将新娘的手握在自己掌中，吻了一下，贴在脸颊上；然后转向父亲说道：「不曾，父亲，我没见那些林中汉子，也没去他们的住处；我也从不贪慕他们的女子。况且，我还带了一只最肥的獐子回来；只是回来时已误了下锅的时辰，等我到家，案上肉食早已备妥了。」

「也好，儿子，」铁面说道，他心情甚好，「獐子对于像你我这般壮汉来说，不过是只小小的鹿罢了。不过我劝你下次带着新娘同去；她可以在你睡觉时搜寻猎物，你射不中时她来射。」

===Original===
Then Face-of-god smiled, but he frowned somewhat also, and he said: "Well were that, indeed! But if ye must needs drag a true tale out of me: that roebuck I shot at the very edge of the wood nigh to the Motestead as I was coming home: harts had I seen in the wood and its lawns, and boars, and bucks, and loosed not at them: for indeed when I awoke in the morning in that wood-lawn ye wot of, I wandered up and down with my bow unbent. So it was that I fared as if I were seeking something, I know not what, that should fill up something lacking to me, I know not what. Thus I felt in myself even so long as I was underneath the black boughs, and there was none beside me and before me, and none to turn aback to: but when I came out again into the sunshine, and I saw the fair dale, and the happy abode lying before me, and folk abroad in the meads merry in the eventide; then was I full fain of it, and loathed the wood as an empty thing that had nought to give me; and lo you! all that I had been longing for in the wood, was it not in this House and ready to my hand?—and that is good meseemeth."

===Chinese===
面神笑了笑，却也微微皱了皱眉，说道：「那确实再好不过！但你们若非要逼我说出实话不可：那只獐子，是我在归途中、在议事坪（the Motestead）附近的林子边上射的：我在林中和林间草地上见过雄鹿，见过野猪，见过牡鹿，都没有放箭：因为当日清早，我在你们知道的那片林间草地上醒来时，便拿着未上弦的弓走来走去。那时我走着，仿佛在寻找什么——我不知道是什么——要来填补我心中所缺的什么——我也不知道是什么。我在黑色枝叶之下行走时，心中一直怀着这种感觉：身旁无人，前路无人，也没有人可以回头去看：但当我重新走进阳光之中，看见那美丽的山谷、那快乐的家园就在眼前，草地上的人们在傍晚中快活地走动——那时我满心欢喜，只觉得那片林子空空洞洞，什么也给不了我；你们看！我在林中所渴望的一切，岂不都在这座宅子里、都唾手可得么？——在我看来，那便是好的。」

===Original===
Therewith he drank of the cup which the Bride put into his hand after she had kissed the rim, but when he had set it down again he spake once more:

"And yet now I am sitting honoured and well-beloved in the House of my Fathers, with the holy hearth sparkling and gleaming down there before me; and she that shall bear my children sitting soft and kind by my side, and the bold lads I shall one day lead in battle drinking out of my very cup: now it seems to me that amidst all this, the dark cold wood, wherein abide but the beasts and the Foes of the Gods, is bidding me to it and drawing me thither. Narrow is the Dale and the World is wide; I would it were dawn and daylight, that I might be afoot again."

And he half rose up from his place.

===Chinese===
说着，他接过新娘递来的杯子饮了一口——新娘递杯之前，先在杯沿上亲了一下——但他放下杯子后，又开口说道：

「然而此刻，我坐在列祖列宗之宅中，受人敬重、被人深爱；神圣的灶火在下面熠熠生辉；将来要为我生儿育女的她，温柔和善地坐在我身旁；我将来要在战场上率领的那些勇猛少年，正用我这只杯子饮酒：可是在这一切之中，我却觉得，那片幽暗阴冷的林子——其中不过住着野兽与众神之敌——正在召唤我、吸引我前去。山谷太窄，而天地甚宽；我恨不得此刻便是拂晓天明，好让我重新上路。」

他说着，半欠身子要从座上站起来。

===Original===
But his father bent his brow on him and said: "Kinsman, thou hast a long tongue for a half-trained whelp: nor see I whitherward thy mind is wandering, but if it be on the road of a lad's desire to go further and fare worse. Hearken then, I will offer thee somewhat! Soon shall the West-country merchants be here with their winter truck. How sayest thou? hast thou a mind to fare back with them, and look on the Plain and its Cities, and take and give with the strangers? To whom indeed thou shalt be nothing save a purse with a few lumps of gold in it, or maybe a spear in the stranger's band on the stricken field, or a bow on the wall of an alien city. This is a craft which thou mayst well learn, since thou shalt be a chieftain; a craft good to learn, however grievous it be in the learning. And I myself have been there; for in my youth I desired sore to look on the world beyond the mountains; so I went, and I filled my belly with the fruit of my own desires, and a bitter meat was that; but now that it has passed through me, and I yet alive, belike I am more of a grown man for having endured its grip. Even so may it well be with thee, son; so go if thou wilt; and thou shalt go with my blessing, and with gold and wares and wain and spearmen."

===Chinese===
但他父亲对他沉下脸来，说道：「族亲啊，你不过是只半调教的幼犬，舌头倒长得长了：我也看不出你的心思跑到哪里去了，除非是顺着少年人'走得越远、日子越糟'的那条老路去了。那么听着，我来给你出个主意！西地的商人们很快就要带着他们过冬的货色到了。你觉得如何？你可愿意跟他们回去，去看看那平原（the Plain）和它的诸城，和陌生人做些买卖交涉？在他们眼里，你不过是一只装了几块金子的钱袋，或者是在战场上异邦队列里的一杆长矛，又或者是异邦城墙上一张挂着的弓罢了。这是一门你该学的手艺，因为你将来要做首领；这门手艺虽然学起来辛苦，却值得一学。我自己也去过；年轻时我极其渴望去看看山外的世界；于是我便去了，把自己欲望的果实饱餐了一顿，那是一块苦涩的肉；可如今它既已从我身上过去了，而我尚且活着，也许正因为忍受了它的钳制，我反倒更像一个成年的汉子了。你也未尝不能如此，儿子；所以你若要去，便去罢；你可以带着我的祝福去，带着金子、货物、车马和枪兵一同去。」

===Original===
"Nay," said Face-of-god, "I thank thee, for it is well offered; but I will not go, for I have no lust for the Plain and its Cities; I love the Dale well, and all that is round about it; therein will I live and die."

Therewith he fell a-musing; and the Bride looked at him anxiously, but spake not. Sooth to say her heart was sinking, as though she foreboded some new thing, which should thrust itself into their merry life.

===Chinese===
「不，」面神说，「多谢你，这番好意我心领了；但我不去，因为我并不向往那平原与它的诸城；我爱这条山谷，也爱它周围的一切；我要在此生、在此死。」

说罢他便陷入沉思；新娘不安地望着他，却没有说话。说老实话，她的心正在下沉，仿佛预感到有什么新的事情将要发生，要闯入他们快乐的生活中来。

===Original===
But the old man Stone-face took up the word and said:

"Son Gold-mane, it behoveth me to speak, since belike I know the wildwood better than most, and have done for these threescore and ten years; to my cost. Now I perceive that thou longest for the wood and the innermost of it; and wot ye what? This longing will at whiles entangle the sons of our chieftains, though this Alderman that now is hath been free therefrom, which is well for him. For, time was this longing came over me, and I went whither it led me: overlong it were to tell of all that befell me because of it, and how my heart bled thereby. So sorry were the tidings that came of it, that now meseemeth my heart should be of stone and not my face, had it not been for the love wherewith I have loved the sons of the kindred. Therefore, son, it were not ill if ye went west away with the merchants this winter, and learned the dealings of the cities, and brought us back tales thereof."

===Chinese===
这时老人石面接过话头，说道：

「金鬃吾儿，我不得不开口说几句，因为这片野林（the Wildwood），多半我比旁人都更熟悉——这七十年间深有体会，也付出了代价。如今我看得出，你渴望着那片林子、渴望着林子的最深处；你们知道么？这种渴望有时会缠上首领们的子孙——虽然如今这位长老幸而未曾被它缠上，这于他倒是好事。因为，曾几何时，这渴望也曾袭上我心头，我便随它指引而去：因它而遭遇的种种、我的心又如何因此而流血——都不必细说了，太长了。由此传回的消息是如此凄惨，以至于我如今常想：若非出于我对宗族子孙们的这份爱，我的心倒真该是石头做的，而不只是脸罢了。所以，吾儿，你若趁今年冬天跟那些商人往西去，去学学诸城的经营之道，回来给我们讲讲那里的故事，那也未尝不是好事。」

===Original===
But Gold-mane cried out somewhat angrily, "I tell thee, foster-father, that I have no mind for the cities and their men and their fools and their whores and their runagates. But as for the wood and its wonders, I have done with it, save for hunting there along with others of the Folk. So let thy mind be at ease; and for the rest, I will do what the Alderman commandeth, and whatso my father craveth of me."

===Chinese===
金鬃却有些恼怒地叫道：「养父，我告诉你，我对那些城池毫无兴趣——不稀罕城里的男人、蠢货、娼妓和逃徒。至于那片林子和它的奇景，我已经跟它了结了，往后不过是随族人一同去打打猎罢了。所以你大可安心；至于其余的事，长老吩咐什么我便做什么，父亲要我怎样我便怎样。」

===Original===
"And that is well, son," said Stone-face, "if what ye say come to pass, as sore I misdoubt me it will not. But well it were, well it were! For such things are in the wood, yea and before ye come to its innermost, as may well try the stoutest heart. Therein are Kobbolds, and Wights that love not men, things unto whom the grief of men is as the sound of the fiddle-bow unto us. And there abide the ghosts of those that may not rest; and there wander the dwarfs and the mountain-dwellers, the dealers in marvels, the givers of gifts that destroy Houses; the forgers of the curse that clingeth and the murder that flitteth to and fro. There moreover are the lairs of Wights in the shapes of women, that draw a young man's heart out of his body, and fill up the empty place with desire never to be satisfied, that they may mock him therewith and waste his manhood and destroy him. Nor say I much of the strong-thieves that dwell there, since thou art a valiant sword; or of them who have been made Wolves of the Holy Places; or of the Murder-Carles, the remnants and off-scourings of wicked and wretched Folks—men who think as much of the life of a man as of the life of a fly. Yet happiest is the man whom they shall tear in pieces, than he who shall live burdened by the curse of the Foes of the Gods."

===Chinese===
「那很好，吾儿，」石面说，「倘若你说到做到的话——尽管我深怕你做不到。但那样才好啊，才好啊！因为林中有那样一些东西，是的，在你到达林子的最深处之前就会遇上，足以考验最坚强的心。那里有地精（Kobbolds），有不喜爱人类的妖灵（Wights）——在它们看来，人的悲伤不过如同琴弓拉出的声响之于我们。那里栖息着不得安息的鬼魂；那里游荡着矮人和山民，他们是贩卖奇术之人，是赐予毁灭宗族之礼物的施与者；他们锻造那缠绵不去的诅咒、那飞来飞去的杀戮。此外，那里还有以女子之形出现的妖灵的巢穴，她们能将一个年轻人的心从身体里勾出来，再用永不能满足的欲望填满那空处，好以此来嘲弄他、消损他的丈夫气概、将他毁灭。至于那些盘踞在林中的强人，我不必多说什么——因为你手中有一把利剑；至于那些被变成圣地之狼的人，我也不多说了；至于那些凶徒（Murder-Carles）——那些邪恶悲惨的族群残留下来的渣滓——这些人看一条人命，和看一只苍蝇的命没什么两样。然而被他们撕成碎片的人，还算是最幸运的呢；比起那背负着众神之敌的诅咒、苟活在世的人，要好得多了。」

===Original===
The housemaster looked on his son as the old carle spake, and a cloud gathered on his face a while; and when Stone-face had made an end he spake:

"This is long and evil talk for the end of a merry day, O fosterer! Wilt thou not drink a draught, O Redesman, and then stand up and set thy fiddle-bow a-dancing, and cause it draw some fair words after it? For my cousin's face hath grown sadder than a young maid's should be, and my son's eyes gleam with thoughts that are far away from us and abroad in the wildwood seeking marvels."

===Chinese===
老人说话之时，家主注视着自己的儿子，面上掠过一片阴云，停了一阵；待石面说完，他便开口道：

「在欢宴一日将尽之时说这番又长又凶的话，养父啊！雷德斯曼，你可愿饮上一杯，然后站起来，让你的琴弓跳起舞来，引出一些美好的辞句？因为我这表妹的面容已变得比一个少女该有的还要凄伤了，而我儿子的眼里闪烁着心思——那心思离我们远去，跑到野林里追寻奇迹去了。」

===Original===
Then arose a man of middle-age from the top of the endlong bench on the east side of the hall: a man tall, thin and scant-haired, with a nose like an eagle's neb: he reached out his hand for the bowl, and when they had given to him he handled it, and raised it aloft and cried:

"Here I drink a double health to Face-of-god and the Bride, and the love that lieth between them, and the love betwixt them twain and us."

He drank therewith, and the wine went up and down the hall, and all men drank, both carles and queens, with shouting and great joy. Then Redesman put down the cup (for it had come into his hands again), and reached his hand to the wall behind him, and took down his fiddle hanging there in its case, and drew it out and fell to tuning it, while the hall grew silent to hearken: then he handled the bow and laid it on the strings till they wailed and chuckled sweetly, and when the song was well awake and stirring briskly, then he lifted up his voice and sang:

===Chinese===
这时，一个中年人从厅堂东侧纵长案的尽头站了起来：他身量高而瘦，头发稀疏，生着一只鹰喙般的鼻子：他伸手去接酒碗，接到手中后，高高举起，高声呼道：

「我在此饮一杯双重的祝福——祝面神与新娘，祝他们二人之间的情爱，也祝他们二人与我们众人之间的情爱！」

他饮了一口，酒便在厅堂里来回传递，所有人都饮了，无论男女，在欢呼声中满心喜悦。然后雷德斯曼放下杯子（那杯子又传回了他手中），伸手到身后的墙上，取下挂在套子里的提琴，抽出来便调起弦来，厅堂也随之安静下来聆听：然后他操起琴弓，搭在弦上，直拉得琴弦如泣如诉、又婉转低吟，待到歌声彻底苏醒、欢跃而起之时，他便放开喉咙唱道：

===Original===
Therewith he made an end, and shouts and glad cries arose all about the hall; and an old man arose and cried: "A cup to the memory of the Mighty of the Day of the Warding of the Ways." For you must know this song told of a custom of the Folk, held in memory of a time of bygone battle, wherein they had overthrown a great host of aliens on the Portway betwixt the river and the cliffs, two furlongs from the gate of Burgstead. So now two weeks before Midsummer those maidens who were presently to be wedded went early in the morning to that place clad in very fair raiment, swords girt to their sides and spears in their hands, and abode there on the highway from morn till even as though they were a guard to it. And they made merry there, singing songs and telling tales of times past: and at the sunsetting their grooms came to fetch them away to the Feast of the Eve of the Wedding.

===Chinese===
一曲终了，满堂喝彩欢呼；一位老人站起来高呼：「为大道守卫之日（the Day of the Warding of the Ways）的先烈们，满饮一杯！」须知这首歌唱的是族中一桩旧俗，为纪念昔日一场战役——在那场战役中，他们于港路（the Portway）之上、河流与峭壁之间、距堡镇大门两浪（furlong）之处，大败了一支异邦大军。所以如今每年仲夏（Midsummer）前两周，那些即将出嫁的少女们便在清早来到那个地方，身穿极华美的衣裳，腰间佩剑，手执长矛，从早到晚守在那条路上，仿佛是它的护卫。她们在那里欢度时光，唱歌谣，讲古时候的故事：到日落时分，她们的新郎便来接她们去参加婚礼前夜的宴席。

===Original===
While the song was a-singing Face-of-god took the Bride's hand in his and caressed it, and was soft and blithe with her; and she reddened and trembled for pleasure, and called to mind wedding feasts that had been, and fair brides that she had seen thereat, and she forgot her fears and her heart was at peace again.

And Iron-face looked well-pleased on the two from time to time, and smiled, but forbore words to them.

But up and down the hall men talked with one another about things long ago betid: for their hearts were high and they desired deeds; but in that fair Dale so happy were the years from day to day that there was but little to tell of. So deepened the night and waned, and Gold-mane and the Bride still talked sweetly together, and at whiles kindly to the others; and by seeming he had clean forgotten the wood and its wonders.

Then at last the Alderman called for the cup of good night, and men drank thereof and went their ways to bed.

===Chinese===
歌声唱起之时，面神握住新娘的手，轻轻抚弄，对她温柔体贴；她红了脸，欢喜得颤抖起来，想起从前参加过的婚宴，想起在那些婚宴上见过的美丽新娘，便忘了方才的忧惧，心中重归安宁。

铁面不时满怀欣慰地看着这两人，面带微笑，却不与他们说话。

厅堂上下众人彼此谈论着古时候发生的事：因为人心气高，渴望着壮举；但在那条美丽的山谷中，年年岁岁如此幸福安宁，竟没有多少事情可讲。夜越来越深，金鬃和新娘仍在甜蜜地低语，偶尔也与旁人和善地攀谈几句；看他的样子，似乎已把那片林子和它的奇景忘得一干二净了。

最后，长老终于吩咐斟上晚安酒，众人饮罢，便各自回房安寝去了。

## IX Those Brethren Fare to the Yew-Wood with the Bride / 九 兄弟偕新娘赴紫杉林

===Original===
Next morning Face-of-god dight himself for work, and took his axe; for his brother Hall-face had bidden him go down with him to the Yew-wood and cut timber there, since he of all men knew where to go straight to the sticks that would quarter best for bow-staves; whereas the Alderman had the right of hewing in that wood. So they went forth, those brethren, from the House of the Face, but when they were gotten to the gate, who should be there but the Bride awaiting them, and she with an ass duly saddled for bearing the yew-sticks. Because Hall-face had told her that he and belike Gold-mane were going to hew in the wood, and she thought it good to be of the company, as oft had befallen erst. When they met she greeted Face-of-god and kissed him as her wont was; and he looked upon her and saw how fair she was, and how kind and friendly were her eyes that beheld him, and how her whole face was eager for him as their lips parted. Then his heart failed him, when he knew that he no longer desired her as she did him, and he said within himself:
"Would that she had been of our nighest kindred! Would that I had had a sister and that this were she!"

===Chinese===
次晨，面神（Face-of-god）整束衣装、预备作务，手提一斧；盖其弟厅面（Hall-face）已邀他同下紫杉林中砍伐材木，因众人之中唯他最谙何处可径直寻得最易剖作弓背之材段；而那林中伐木之权，本属长老（the Alderman）所有。于是兄弟二人自面神之宅（the House of the Face）出门而行，然方至城门，却见新娘（the Bride）已在那里相候，并已为一头驴子备好驮鞍，专为装载紫杉材段。盖因厅面对她言及，自己与金鬃（Gold-mane）或将入林伐木，她便觉当与此行同往，一如往昔常有之事。两人相见，新娘依平素之礼迎面神而吻之；面神凝目视她，见她何其姝丽，那双望着他的眼眸何其温存恳切，唇分之际，整张脸庞皆盈满对他的切切之情。他心下便自颓然——盖已知自己已不复如她爱己一般爱她——遂暗自思忖：
"但愿她是我们至亲骨肉！但愿我曾有一妹，而此妹即是她！"

===Original===
So the three went along the highway down the Dale, and Hall-face and the Bride talked merrily together and laughed, for she was happy, since she knew that Gold-mane had been to the wood and was back safe and much as he had been before. So indeed it seemed of him; for though at first he was moody and of few words, yet presently he cursed himself for a mar-sport, and so fell into the talk, and enforced himself to be merry; and soon he was so indeed; for he thought: "She drew me thither: she hath a deed for me to do. I shall do the deed and have my reward. Soon will the spring-tide be here, and I shall be a young man yet when it comes."

So came they to the place where he had met the three maidens yesterday; there they also turned from the highway; and as they went down the bent, Gold-mane could not but turn his eyes on the beauty of the Bride and the lovely ways of her body: but presently he remembered all that had betid, and turned away again as one who is noting what it behoves him not to note. And he said to himself: "Where art thou, Gold-mane? Whose art thou? Yea, even if that had been but a dream that I have dreamed, yet would that this fair woman were my sister!"

===Chinese===
三人便沿大路下行入谷，厅面与新娘一路笑语欢谈；她心下甚乐，因知金鬃曾入林中、今已安然归来，状貌仍与从前无甚异样。他看起来也确是如此；盖虽初时闷闷不乐、寡言少语，然旋即自骂败兴，遂加入谈笑，勉力作欢；不一时，竟也真个欢畅起来；因他心想："是她将我引至彼处：她有一桩功业要我去做。我当为此功业、得其酬报。春汛将至，待它来时，我仍是一少年郎。"

于是他们来到他昨日遇见那三位少女之处；三人亦于此离了大路；下坡之时，金鬃忍不住将目光投向新娘之美貌，及她身姿举止之可爱处：然旋即忆起所发生的一切，便又移开目光，一如那留意了不该留意之物之人。他暗自道："金鬃，你在何处？你又是何人之人？是了，纵然我所历者不过是一场梦，我仍愿这位佳丽是我的姊妹！"

===Original===
So came they to the Yew-wood, and the brethren fell to work, and the Bride with them, for she was deft with the axe and strong withal. But at midday they rested on the green slope without the Yew-wood; and they ate bread and flesh and onions and apples, and drank red wine of the Dale. And while they were resting after their meat, the Bride sang to them, and her song was a lay of time past; and here ye have somewhat of it:

> 'Tis over the hill and over the dale

 Men ride from the city fast and far,

 If they may have a soothfast tale,

 True tidings of the host of war.
> And first they hap on men-at-arms,

 All clad in steel from head to foot:

 Now tell true tale of the new-come harms,

 And the gathered hosts of the mountain-root.
> Fair sirs, from murder-carles we flee,

 Whose fashion is as the mountain-trolls';

 No man can tell how many they be,

 And the voice of their host as the thunder rolls.
> They were weary men at the ending of day,

 But they spurred nor stayed for longer word.

 Now ye, O merchants, whither away?

 What do ye there with the helm and the sword?
> O we must fight for life and gear,

 For our beasts are spent and our wains are stayed,

 And the host of the Mountain-men draws near,

 That maketh all the world afraid.
> They left the chapmen on the hill,

 And through the eve and through the night

 They rode to have true tidings still,

 And were there on the way when the dawn was bright.
> O damsels fair, what do ye then

 To loiter thus upon the way,

 And have no fear of the Mountain-men,

 The host of the carles that strip and slay?
> O riders weary with the road,

 Come eat and drink on the grass hereby!

 And lay you down in a fair abode

 Till the midday sun is broad and high;
> Then unto you shall we come aback,

 And lead you forth to the Mountain-men,

 To note their plenty and their lack,

 And have true tidings there and then.
> 'Tis over the hill and over the dale

 They ride from the mountain fast and far;

 And now have they learned a soothfast tale,

 True tidings of the host of war.
> It was summer-tide and the Month of Hay,

 And men and maids must fare afield;

 But we saw the place were the bow-staves lay,

 And the hall was hung with spear and shield.
> When the moon was high we drank in the hall,

 And they drank to the guests and were kind and blithe,

 And they said: Come back when the chestnuts fall,

 And the wine-carts wend across the hythe.
> Come oft and o'er again, they said;

 Wander your ways; but we abide

 For all the world in the little stead;

 For wise are we, though the world be wide.
> Yea, come in arms if ye will, they said;

 And despite your host shall we abide

 For life or death in the little stead;

 For wise are we, though the world be wide.

===Chinese===
于是他们来到紫杉林，兄弟二人便动手做工，新娘亦与他们同作，盖她用斧精熟、气力又壮。至正午，三人在紫杉林外青草坡上歇息；吃的是面包、肉食、葱头与苹果，饮的是谷中所酿之红酒。饭毕歇息之际，新娘为他们唱歌，所唱乃一曲往古之歌；此处姑录其略：

> 越彼山阿越彼谷，
> 城中飞骑去匆匆；
> 但求一得真消息，
> 知彼大军几许雄。

> 前行先遇甲士群，
> 铁衣自顶覆至踵：
> "为我言说新祸殃，
> 山根之下聚何军？"

> "诸公，吾避凶徒遁，
> 凶徒形若山中怪；
> 人数几多无人知，
> 大军之声如霆雷。"

> 日暮彼辈皆疲倦，
> 然策马行不稍留。
> "商贾诸君向何往？
> 戴盔佩剑欲何求？"

> "吾辈当为命财战，
> 马疲车止不克行；
> 山人之军日渐近，
> 天下闻之皆震惊。"

> 彼辈弃商于山头，
> 穿暮穿夜不息驱；
> 欲得真讯频探侦，
> 破晓之时尚在途。

> "佳人兮，尔何所为，
> 迟迟淹留此路旁？
> 不畏山中豪强辈，
> 劫掠杀人之众狂？"

> "倦旅骑士路途劳，
> 来此草地饮且食！
> 安置尔躯于佳所，
> 待至日午高且极。"

> "届时吾辈自当归，
> 引尔前赴山中军；
> 观其虚实辨其形，
> 真讯即时可得闻。"

> 越彼山阿越彼谷，
> 山中飞骑去匆匆；
> 今已探得真消息，
> 知彼大军几许雄。

> 时维夏月打草天，
> 男女皆当赴田畴；
> 然吾见彼弓材处，
> 厅堂高悬矛与盾。

> 月高之时饮于厅，
> 主客相酬极欢欣；
> 彼乃言：待栗落时，
> 重来此地酒车临。

> 彼等言："频来重至莫辞数，
> 尔自漫游吾自驻；
> 为应天下居此庄——
> 吾曹有智，天下纵广。"

> 彼等复言："执兵而来亦无妨，
> 尔纵大众吾不避；
> 死生于此小庄中——
> 吾曹有智，天下纵广。"

===Original===
So she made an end and looked at the fairness of the dale spreading wide before her, and a robin came nigh from out of a thorn-bush and sung his song also, the sweet herald of coming winter; and the lapwings wheeled about, black and white, above the meadow by the river, sending forth their wheedling pipe as they hung above the soft turf.

She felt the brothers near her, and knew their friendliness from of old, and she was happy; nor had she looked closer at Gold-mane would she have noted any change in him belike; for the meat and the good wine, and the fair sunny time, and the Bride's sweet voice, and the ancient song softened his heart while it fed the desire therein.

So in a while they arose from their rest and did what was left them of their work, and so went back to Burgstead through the fair afternoon; by seeming all three in all content. But yet Gold-mane, as from time to time he looked upon the Bride, kept saying to himself: "O if she had been but my sister! sweet had the kinship been!"

===Chinese===
歌罢，她纵目望去，只见谷之秀美铺展眼前；一只知更鸟自荆棘丛中飞近，也唱起它的歌来——那是将至之冬的甜美信使；田凫黑白相间，在河畔草地上空盘旋，悬于柔软草皮之上，发出婉转诱人的啼声。

她感到兄弟二人就在身畔，深知他们素来的情谊，心下甚乐；纵使她细看金鬃，也未必能察觉他有丝毫异样；盖因肉食与美酒、明媚晴暖之时、新娘甜润的嗓音，以及那支古歌，一面软化了她的心，一面又滋养了他心中的欲念。

歇息片刻，三人起身，把余下的活计做完，便在晴美的午后返回堡镇（Burgstead）；看去三人皆满心怡然。然金鬃每望新娘一眼，便暗自反复道："啊，她若做我的妹妹该多好！那份亲情该是何等甘美！"

## XX Those Two Together Hold the Ring of the Earth-God / 二十 这二人共执地神之环

===Original===
And now they fell silent both of them, and sat hearkening the sounds of the Dale, from the whistle of the plover down by the waterside to the far-off voices of the children and maidens about the kine in the lower meadows. At last Gold-mane took up the word and said:
"Sweet friend, tell me the uttermost of what thou would'st have of me. Is it not that I should stand by thee and thine in the Folk-mote of the Dalesmen, and speak for you when ye pray us for help against your foemen; and then again that I do my best when ye and we are arrayed for battle against the Dusky Men? This is easy to do, and great is the reward thou offerest me."

===Chinese===
如今二人俱寂然无语，坐着倾听谷中诸般声响：自水畔鸻鸟的啼唤，直到下方草甸上孩童与少女在牛群四周远远的话语。末了，金鬃（Gold-mane）开口说道：
"亲爱的朋友，请把你对我的所求，到尽头和盘告诉我。莫不是要我在谷民（the Dalesmen）的民众大会（the Folk-mote）上，与你和你族人并肩而立；在你们恳求我们出兵相助、共御你们仇敌之时，替你们进言；而后再要我在你我这双方列阵迎击黝暗人（the Dusky Men）之时，竭力死战？这事易办，而你所酬谢于我的，却又何其丰厚。"

===Original===
"I look for this service of thee," she said, "and none other."

"And when I go down to the battle," said he, "shalt thou be sorry for our sundering?"

She said: "There shall be no sundering; I shall wend with thee."

Said he: "And if I were slain in the battle, would'st thou lament me?"

"Thou shalt not be slain," she said.

===Chinese===
她道："我所指望于你的，正是这一桩效力，再无别的。"

他道："那么我下阵赴战之时，你会因你我分离而难过么？"

她道："并无分离可言；我当与你同去。"

他道："倘若我战死沙场，你可会为我哀悼？"

她道："你不会死。"

===Original===
Again was there silence betwixt them, till at last he said:
"This then is why thou didst draw me to thee in the Wildwood?"
"Yea," said she.
Again for a while no word was spoken, and Face-of-god looked on her till she cast her eyes down before him.
Then at last he spake, and the colour came and went in his face as he said: "Tell me thy name what it is."
She said: "I am called the Sun-beam."

===Chinese===
二人之间又是一阵沉默，末了他才说道：
"那么，你当初在野林（the Wildwood）里把我引到你身边，便是为了此事？"
"正是。"她道。
又是一时无人言语，面神（Face-of-god）只望着她，直望得她在他面前垂下眼帘。
末了，他终于开口，说话之间脸上血色忽来忽去："请告诉我，你叫什么名字。"
她道："人皆唤我日光（the Sun-beam）。"

===Original===
Then he said, and his voice trembled therewith: "O Sun-beam, I have been seeking pleasant and cunning words, and can find none such. But tell me this if thou wilt: dost thou desire me as I desire thee? or is it that thou wilt suffer me to wed thee and bed thee at last as mere payment for the help that I shall give to thee and thine? Nay, doubt it not that I will take the payment, if this is what thou wilt give me and nought else. Yet tell me."

===Chinese===
于是他说道，声音为之颤抖："日光啊，我一直在寻觅动听而巧妙的话语，却一句也寻不到。然而你若愿意，请告诉我这一桩：你是否如我渴望你这般渴望我？还是说，你不过是容忍我终有一日娶你、与你同床，当作我助你助你族人的酬报罢了？也罢，若这就是你肯给我的、此外别无他物，切勿疑心我会不收这份酬报。可你仍要告诉我。"

===Original===
Her face grew troubled, and she said:
"Gold-mane, maybe that thou hast now asked me one question too many; for this is no fair game to be played between us. For thee, as I deem, there are this day but two people in the world, and that is thou and I, and the earth is for us two alone. But, my friend, though I have seen but twenty and one summers, it is nowise so with me, and to me there are many in the world; and chiefly the Folk of the Wolf, amidst whose very heart I have grown up. Moreover, I can think of her whom I have supplanted, the Bride to wit; and I know her, and how bitter and empty her days shall be for a while, and how vain all our redes for her shall seem to her. Yea, I know her sorrow, and see it and grieve for it: so canst not thou, unless thou verily see her before thee, her face unhappy, and her voice changed and hard. Well, I will tell thee what thou askest. When I drew thee to me on the Mountain I thought but of the friendship and brotherhood to be knitted up between our two Folks, nor did I anywise desire thy love of a young man. But when I saw thee on the heath and in the Hall that day, it pleased me to think that a man so fair and chieftain-like should one day lie by my side; and again when I saw that the love of me had taken hold of thee, I would not have thee grieved because of me, but would have thee happy. And now what shall I say?—I know not; I cannot tell. Yet am I the Friend, as erst I called myself."

"And, Gold-mane, I have seen hitherto but the outward show and image of thee, and though that be goodly, how would it be if thou didst shame me with little-heartedness and evil deeds? Let me see thee in the Folk-mote and the battle, and then may I answer thee."

===Chinese===
她面露为难之色，说道：
"金鬃，你这一问，怕是多问了一桩；因为这并非你我之间可拿来消遣的公平游戏。至于你么，我料想今日这世上在你眼中只有两个人，那便是你与我，这天地只为咱二人而设。然而我的朋友，我虽不过二十一岁，我心中却绝非如此；在我看来这世上的人有许多；首当其冲的便是狼之民（the Folk of the Wolf），我正是生长在他们心腹之中的。再者，我还能念及那位被我夺了位的女子——便是新娘（the Bride）；我认得她，知道她的日子将有一阵是何等苦涩空茫，知道我们为她所筹谋的一切打算，在她看来将何等可笑。是的，我知道她的悲苦，看得见它，也为之心痛：这些你却做不到，除非你当真看见她立在你面前，面带愁容，嗓音都变得生硬冷峻。好吧，你问的我便告诉你。当初我在山上将你引到我身边时，所想的不过是咱两族之间要结下的交情与兄弟之谊，丝毫没有存心要你一个少年男子的爱恋。可是那一日，当我在荒原之上、厅堂之中见到你，我便欣然想到：这样一个俊美而具首领气度的男子，有一日当卧于我身侧；后来我又见爱慕我之情已将你攫住，我便不愿你因我而忧愁，却愿你得欢喜。如今要我怎么说呢？——我不知道；我说不出来。然而我仍是那'朋友'，正如从前我自称的那般。"

"还有，金鬃，至今我所见的，不过是你的外表与形影；这外表固然俊美，可你若以怯懦卑劣之行叫我蒙羞，又将如何？且让我在民众大会和沙场之上看见你，那时我才能答复你。"

===Original===
Then she held her peace, and he answered nothing; and she turned her face from him and said:
"Out on it! have I beguiled myself as well as thee? These are but empty words I have been saying. If thou wilt drag the truth out of me, this is the very truth: that today is happy to me as it is to thee, and that I have longed sore for its coming. O Gold-mane, O speech-friend, if thou wert to pray me or command me that I lie in thine arms tonight, I should know not how to gainsay thee. Yet I beseech thee to forbear, lest thy death and mine come of it. And why should we die, O friend, when we are so young, and the world lies so fair before us, and the happy days are at hand when the Children of the Wolf and the kindreds of the Dale shall deliver the Folk, and all days shall be good and all years?"

===Chinese===
她于是默然，他也无言以对；她转过脸去，说道：
"呸！莫非我把你骗了，连我自己也一并骗了？我方才所说的，不过是些空话。你若要逼出我心底的真话，这便是千真万确的实话：今日于我和于你一般欢喜，我苦苦盼望这一天已有好久了。哦，金鬃，哦，言友（speech-friend）啊，你今夜若是求我、命我卧于你怀中，我竟不知如何推拒。可我恳求你按捺住，免得你我的死都由此而起。我的朋友，我们为何要死呢？你我年纪尚轻，这世界在眼前如此美好，那幸福的日子已近在咫尺——到那日，狼之子民（the Children of the Wolf）与谷中诸族将要拯救我等之民，从此日日皆佳、岁岁皆好。"

===Original===
They had both risen up as she spake, and now he put forth his hands to her and took her in his arms, wondering the while, as he drew her to him, how much slenderer and smaller and weaker she seemed in his embrace than he had thought of her; and when their lips met, he felt that she kissed him as he her. Then he held her by the shoulders at arms' length from him, and beheld her face how her eyes were closed and her lips quivering. But before him, in a moment of time, passed a picture of the life to be in the fair Dale, and all she would give him there, and the days good and lovely from morn to eve and eve to morn; and though in that moment it was hard for him to speak, at last he spoke in a voice hoarse at first, and said:
"Thou sayest sooth, O friend; we will not die, but live; I will not drag our deaths upon us both, nor put a sword in the hands of Folk-might, who loves me not."

===Chinese===
她说这话时，二人俱已起身；此时他向她伸出手去，将她拥入怀中，一面将她揽近，一面暗暗诧异：她在自己臂抱里竟比他平日所想的要纤细得多、娇小得多、柔弱得多；二人的嘴唇相触之时，他觉出她回吻他，正如他吻她一般。随后他握住她的双肩，将她推到一臂之远，端详她的脸——她的眼睛如何紧闭着，嘴唇如何微微颤动。然而就在一瞬间，眼前掠过一幅图景：日后在那佳美的山谷中将要过的日子，她将在那里给予他的一切，以及从早到晚、从晚到早那些美好可爱的时光；此刻虽难以启齿，他末了仍用起初有些沙哑的嗓音说道：
"朋友，你说的是实在话；我们不死，要活；我不会把死亡强拽到你我二人头上，也不会把剑塞到民强（Folk-might）手里——他本就不喜我。"

===Original===
Then he kissed her on the brow and said: "Now shalt thou take me by the hand and lead me forth from the Hall. For the day is waxing old, and here meseemeth in this dim hall there are words crossing in the air about us—words spoken in days long ago, and tales of old time, that keep egging me on to do my will and die, because that is all that the world hath for a valiant man; and to such words I would not hearken, for in this hour I have no will to die, nor can I think of death."

She took his hand and led him forth without more words, and they went hand in hand and paced slowly round the Doom-ring, the light air breathing upon them till their faces were as calm and quiet as their wont was, and hers especially as bright and happy as when he had first seen her that day.

===Chinese===
随后他吻了吻她的额头，说道："现在你当携我之手，领我出这厅堂。因为天色已晏，在这昏暗的厅中，我似乎觉得有言语在我们四周凌空交错——那是很久以前说过的言语，是古时的故事，它们一个劲儿地撺掇我任性而行、赴死方休，仿佛一个勇士在这世间所能得的，也不过是这些罢了；这样的言语我不愿听，因为此时此刻我并无死志，也想不得死。"

她拉起他的手，一言不发地领他出去；二人携手同行，缓步绕着判决环（the Doom-ring）踱着，轻风拂面，直到二人的脸色都如平素一般沉静安宁——尤其是她的脸，又如那一日他初次见她时那般明朗欢欣。

===Original===
The sun was sinking now, and only sent one golden ray into the valley through a cleft in the western rock-wall, but the sky overhead was bright and clear; from the meadows came the sound of the lowing of kine and the voices of children a-sporting, and it seemed to Gold-mane that they were drawing nigher, both the children and the kine, and somewhat he begrudged it that he should not be alone with the Friend.

Now when they had made half the circuit of the Doom-ring, the Sun-beam stopped him, and then led him through the Ring of Stones, and brought him up to the altar which was amidst of it; and the altar was a great black stone hewn smooth and clean, and with the image of the Wolf carven on the front thereof; and on its face lay the gold ring which the priest or captain of the Folk bore on his arm between the God and the people at all folk-motes.

So she said: "This is the altar of the God of Earth, and often hath it been reddened by mighty men; and thereon lieth the Ring of the Sons of the Wolf; and now it were well that we swore troth on that ring before my brother cometh; for now will he soon be here."

===Chinese===
此时日头西沉，只从西面岩壁的一道裂缝里送进一道金光，落入谷中，然而头顶的天宇却澄澈明朗；草甸那边传来牛群的哞声与孩童嬉戏的笑语，金鬃却觉得那孩子与牛群都愈走愈近了，他心里隐隐不愿与这位"朋友"独处的时光就此被打断。

二人绕判决环走过半圈，日光将他止住，随后领他穿过那石环，走到石环中央的祭坛跟前；那祭坛是一块巨大的黑石，斫得光洁，正面雕着一头狼的造像；坛上放着一只金环，那是族中的祭司或首领在一切民众大会上，戴于臂上、以介于神与族人之间之物。

于是她说道："这是地神（the God of the Earth）的祭坛，曾被许多壮士的鲜血染红；其上所陈的，便是狼之子之环（the Ring of the Sons of the Wolf）；如今我们最好在这环上起誓订盟，趁我兄长未到之前——因为他不久就要来了。"

===Original===
Then Gold-mane took the Ring and thrust his right hand through it, and took her right hand in his; so that the Ring lay on both their hands, and therewith he spake aloud:
"I am Face-of-god of the House of the Face, and I do thee to wit, O God of the Earth, that I pledge my troth to this woman, the Sun-beam of the Kindred of the Wolf, to beget my offspring on her, and to live with her, and to die with her: so help me, thou God of the Earth, and the Warrior and the God of the Face!"

Then spake the Sun-beam: "I, the Sun-beam of the Children of the Wolf, pledge my troth to Face-of-god to lie in his bed and to bear his children and none other's, and to be his speech-friend till I die: so help me the Wolf and the Warrior and the God of the Earth!"

===Chinese===
于是金鬃取过那环，将右手穿了进去，又握住她的右手；那金环便卧在二人的手背之上，他便朗声说道：
"我是面神之宅（the House of the Face）的面神。地神啊，我在此告知于你：我向这位女子立誓订盟——她是狼之宗族（the Kindred of the Wolf）的日光，我要在她身上生养我的子嗣，与她同生，与她同死：愿地神、武神（the Warrior）与面之神（the God of the Face）助我！"

随后日光说道："我，狼之子民的日光，向面神立誓订盟：我要卧于他榻上，生养他的子女、而非任何别人的子女，做他的言友直到我死之日：愿狼、武神与地神助我！"

===Original===
Then they laid the Ring on the altar again, and they kissed each other long and sweetly, and then turned away from the altar and departed from the Doom-ring, going hand in hand together down the meadow, and as they went, the noise of the kine and the children grew nearer and nearer, and presently came the whole company of them round a ness of the rock-wall; there were some thirty little lads and lasses driving on the milch-kine, with half a score of older maids and grown women, one of whom was Bow-may, who was lightly and scantily clad, as one who heeds not the weather, or deems all months midsummer.

===Chinese===
随后他们将金环重新安放于祭坛之上，彼此长久而甜蜜地一吻，这才转身离开祭坛，走出判决环，携手下了草甸；他们一路走去，牛群与孩童的喧声愈来愈近，不多时那一群人便从岩壁的一处岬角后转了出来：约有三十个小童男女驱赶着奶牛群，另有十来个年长些的少女和成年的妇人，其中一人正是弓娥（Bow-may），她衣衫轻薄单少，仿佛全不在意天时，又仿佛把一年十二月都当作仲夏。

===Original===
The children came running up merrily when they saw the Sun-beam, but stopped short shyly when they noted the tall fair stranger with her. They were all strong and sturdy children, and some very fair, but brown with the weather, if not with the sun. Bow-may came up to Gold-mane and took his hand and greeted him kindly and said:
"So here thou art at last in Shadowy Vale; and I hope that thou art content therewith, and as happy as I would wish thee to be. Well, this is the first time; and when thou comest the second time it may well be that the world shall be growing better."
She held the distaff which she bore in her hand (for she had been spinning) as if it were a spear; her limbs were goodly and shapely, and she trod the thick grass of the Vale with a kind of wary firmness, as though foemen might be lurking nearby. The Sun-beam smiled upon her kindly and said:
"That shall not fail to be, Bow-may: ye have won a new friend today. But tell me, when dost thou look to see the men here, for I was down by the water when they went away yesterday?"
"They shall come into the Dale a little after sunset," said Bow-may.
"Shall I abide them, my friend?" said Gold-mane, turning to the Sun-beam.
"Yea," she said; "for what else art thou come hither? or art thou so pressed to depart from us? Last time we met thou wert not so hasty to sunder."
They smiled on each other; and Bow-may looked on them and laughed outright; then a flush showed in her cheeks through the tan of them, and she turned toward the children and the other women who were busied about the milking of the kine.

===Chinese===
那些孩童一见日光，都欢欢喜喜地跑上前来，可一瞧见她身旁那个高大的俊美生人，又怯生生地收住脚步。这些孩童个个壮实健硕，有几个生得极俊美，只是即便不因日晒、也为风霜所染，肤色黝褐。弓娥走上前来，握住金鬃的手，亲热地与他见礼，说道：
"你到底还是来了幽谷（Shadowy Vale）；我盼你对此心满意足，也盼你如我所愿的那般欢喜。也罢，这是头一回；待你第二回来时，这世道多半已比从前好些了。"
她手持手中那根纺杆（她方才正在纺线），擎得有如一柄长枪；她肢体美好匀称，踩着谷中厚厚的青草，步子带着一种警觉的沉稳，仿佛四下里或有仇敌埋伏。日光对她和蔼地一笑，说道：
"那定然不会落空，弓娥：你们今日已得了一位新朋友。可你告诉我，你估量那些男子何时到此？昨日他们离去时，我正在水边呢。"
"他们将于日落之后不久入谷。"弓娥道。
"我在此等他们么，我的朋友？"金鬃转向日光道。
"等。"她道，"否则你为何到此来？还是你这么急着要离开我们？上回我们相遇，你可不这么急着分手。"
二人相视而笑；弓娥瞧着他们，竟放声大笑起来；随即双颊透过那日晒的黝色浮起一阵红晕，她便转向那些孩童和别的正忙着挤奶的妇人。

===Original===
But those two sat down together on a bank amidst the plain meadow, facing the river and the eastern rock-wall, and the Sun-beam said:
"I am fain to speak to thee and to see thine eyes watching me while I speak; and now, my friend, I will tell thee something unasked which has to do with what e'en now thou didst ask me; for I would have thee trust me wholly, and know me for what I am. Time was I schemed and planned for this day of betrothal; but now I tell thee it has become no longer needful for bringing to pass our fellowship in arms with thy people. Yea yesterday, ere he went on a hunt, whereof he shall tell thee, Folk-might was against it, in words at least; and yet as one who would have it done if he might have no part in it. So, in good sooth, this hand that lieth in thine is the hand of a wilful woman, who desireth a man, and would keep him for her speech-friend. Now art thou fond and happy; yet bear in mind that there are deeds to be done, and the troth we have just plighted must be paid for. So hearken, I bid thee. Dost thou care to know why the wheedling of thee is no longer needful to us?"

===Chinese===
那二人却在一处草岸上并肩坐下，那草岸正在平坦的草甸之中，面朝河水与东面的岩壁，日光说道：
