"我乐得与你说话，也乐得看见你一面说话一面拿眼睛瞧着我；如今，我的朋友，有一桩你不曾问的事我也要告诉你，这事与你方才所问的有关；因为我要你完完全全信我，认得我本是个什么样的人。曾有一阵子，我为今日这订盟之日苦心筹算；可现在我告诉你：要促成你族人马与我们并肩作战，这事已不再必要了。就在昨日，他出去打猎之前——那猎事他自会讲给你听——民强还口头上反对此事；可他那种反对，活像一个人巴不得这事做成、只可惜自己不能与闻其事的模样。所以说句实在话，此刻这只卧于你掌中的手，乃是一个任性女子的手，她恋慕一个男子，要把他留作自己的言友。你这会儿正痴爱欢喜；可你须记住，还有事业待做，我们方才所订的盟誓是要付出代价来偿的。所以我劝你听着。你可愿意知道，为何我们对你再无须诱哄了？"

===Original===
He said: "A little while ago I should have said, Yea, If thy lips say the words. But now, O friend, it seemeth as if thine heart were already become a part of mine, and I feel as if the chieftain were growing up in me and the longing for deeds: so I say, Tell me, for I were fain to hear what toucheth the welfare of thy Folk and their fellowship with my Folk; for on that also have I set my heart?"

===Chinese===
他道："若是方才，我本会答：愿听，若你口中说出来。可如今，朋友，仿佛你的心已成为我心的一部分；我又觉得首领之气正在我心头滋长，对功业的渴望也油然而生：所以我说，告诉我吧，因为我乐闻一切关涉你族福祉、以及你族与我族结盟之事；这一层我也已倾心在意了。"

===Original===
She said gravely and with solemn eyes:
"What thou sayest is good: full glad am I that I have not plighted my troth to a mere goodly lad, but rather to a chieftain and a warrior. Now then hearken! Since I saw thee first in the autumn this hath happened, that the Dusky Men, increasing both in numbers and insolence, have it in their hearts to win more than Silverdale, and it is years since they have fallen upon Rosedale and conquered it, rather by murder than by battle, and made all men thralls there, for feeble were the Folk thereof; and doubt it not but that they will look into Burgdale before long. They are already abroad in the woods, and were it not for the fear of the Wolf they would be thicker therein, and faring wider; for we have slain many of them, coming upon them unawares; and they know not where we dwell, nor who we be: so they fear to spread about overmuch and pry into unknown places lest the Wolf howl on them. Yet beware! for they will gather in numbers that we may not meet, and then will they swarm into the Dale; and if ye would live your happy life that ye love so well, ye must now fight for it; and in that battle must ye needs join yourselves to us, that we may help each other. Herein have ye nought to choose, for now with you it is no longer a thing to talk of whether ye will help certain strangers and guests and thereby win some gain to yourselves, but whether ye have the hearts to fight for yourselves, and the wits to be the fellows of tall men and stout warriors who have pledged their lives to win or die for it."

===Chinese===
她庄容说道，目光肃穆：
"你说的极好：我满心欢喜，我所订盟的不是区区一个俊俏少年，而是一位首领、一名战士。那么听着！自入秋我初见你以来，出了这样的事：黝暗人于人数上、于骄横上都日见其盛，他们心存图谋，要吞下的不止银谷（Silverdale）一地；数年之前他们已侵攻玫瑰谷（Rosedale），将之征服——所凭的与其说是交战，不如说是屠戮——并把那里所有的人都贬作奴隶，因为那里的人丁软弱无力；切勿怀疑，他们不久便要觊觎堡谷（Burgdale）了。他们早已在林中出没，要不是畏惧狼族，他们在林子里还要更密、行迹还要更远；因为我们常出其不意地掩杀他们、诛戮甚众；他们既不知我们住在哪里，也不知我们是谁：所以他们不敢过分四散，不敢到生疏的地方窥探，生怕狼嚎落到他们头上。然而小心！他们一旦聚成我们难以匹敌的人数，便会蜂拥而入这山谷；你们若要继续过你们所钟爱的那种快活日子，此刻便非为之而战不可；那一战之中，你们势必要与我们合兵，彼此相援。这事由不得你们挑选，因为如今在你们，已不再是'要不要帮几个异乡客、借此为自己谋些好处'这种可商议之事，而是你们可有为自己而战的心肠，可有与那些高壮大汉、那些矢志不胜即死的壮士们结为同袍的智识。"

===Original===
She was silent a little and then turned and looked fondly on Face-of-god and said:
"Therefore, Gold-mane, we need thee no longer; for thou must needs fight in our battle. I have no longer aught to do to wheedle thee to love me. Yet if thou wilt love me, then am I a glad woman."
He said: "Thou wottest well that thou hast all my love, neither will I fail thee in the battle. I am not little-hearted, though I would have given myself to thee for no reward."
"It is well," said the Sun-beam; "nought is undone by that which I have done. Moreover, it is good that we have plighted troth today. For Folk-might will presently hear thereof, and he must needs abide the thing which is done. Hearken! he cometh."
For as she spoke there came a glad cry from the women and children, and those two stood up and turned toward the west and beheld the warriors of the Wolf coming down into the Dale by the way that Gold-mane had come.
"Come," said the Sun-beam, "here are your brethren in arms, let us go greet them; they will rejoice in thee."
So they went thither, and there stood eighty and seven men on the grass below the scree and Folk-might their captain; and besides some valiant women, and a few carles who were on watch on the waste, and a half score who had been left in the Dale, these were all the warriors of the Wolf. They were clad in no holiday raiment, not even Folk-might, but were in sheep-brown gear of the coarsest, like to husbandmen late come from the plough, but armed well and goodly.

===Chinese===
她沉默片刻，转过身来，深情地望着面神，说道：
"所以，金鬃，我们不再需要你了；因为你势必要在我们的战事中出力。我再也不必用尽心思哄你来爱我。可你若肯爱我，我便是个欢欣的女子了。"
他道："你明知你已尽得我的爱；沙场之上我也不会弃你于不顾。我并非怯懦之辈，纵然我本会不要半点酬报、将我自己交付于你。"
"这就好。"日光道，"我所做的，并不曾弄糟什么事。再者，我们今日订了盟，原是好的。因为民强不久便会听闻此事，他不得不承认这既成之事实。听！他来了。"
原来她正说话之间，妇孺之中发出一阵欢呼；那二人起身向西一望，只见狼族的武士们正顺着金鬃当日来的那条路走入谷中。
"来。"日光道，"你们的同袍在此，我们去迎接他们吧；他们见了你，定然欢喜。"
于是二人走过去，只见碎石坡下方的青草地上立着八十七名汉子，为首的便是他们的首领民强；除开几名勇健的妇人、几名在荒原上值守的汉子、以及留在谷中的十来个人之外，这些便是狼族全部的武士了。他们身上并不着节庆之服，便连民强也不着；所穿的都是最粗的羊褐衣裳，仿佛方才扶犁下地的庄稼汉，然而兵甲精良、气宇堂堂。

===Original===
But when the twain drew near, the men clashed their spears on their shields, and cried out for joy of them, for they all knew what Face-of-god's presence there betokened of fellowship with the kindreds; but Folk-might came forward and took Face-of-god's hand and greeted him and said:
"Hail, son of the Alderman! Here hast thou come into the ancient abode of chieftains and warriors, and belike deeds await thee also."
Yet his brow was knitted as he said these words, and he spake slowly, as one that constraineth himself; but presently his face cleared somewhat and he said:
"Dalesman, it behoveth thy people to bestir them if ye would live and see good days. Hath my sister told thee what is toward? Or what sayest thou?"
"Hail to thee, son of the Wolf!" said Face-of-god. "Thy sister hath told me all; and even if these Dusky Felons were not our foemen also, yet could I have my way, we should have given thee all help, and should have brought back peace and good days to thy folk."
Then Folk-might flushed red and spake, as he cast out his hand towards the warriors and up and down toward the Dale:
"These be my folk, and these only: and as to peace, only those of us know of it who are old men. Yet is it well; and if we and ye together be strong enough to bring back good days to the feeble men whom the Dusky Ones torment in Silverdale it shall be better yet."
Then he turned about to his sister, and looked keenly into her eyes till she reddened, and took her hand and looked at the wrist and said:
"O sister, see I not the mark on thy wrist of the Ring of the God of the Earth? Have not oaths been sworn since yesterday?"
"True it is," she said, "that this man and I have plighted troth together at the altar of the Doom-ring."

===Chinese===
但当那二人走近，众汉子便将长枪往盾牌上敲得铮铮作响，为他们放声欢呼，因为他们都明白面神到此所预示的、与诸族结盟之意；民强却走上前来，握住面神的手，与他见礼，说道：
"幸会，长老（the Alderman）之子！你来到这首领与武士的世居故地，料来也自有功业在此相候。"
他说这话时眉头紧锁，语速迟缓，像是极力克己的模样；但不久他的面色稍霁，又说道：
"谷民兄弟，你们若要活命、要过好日子，你族人可该振作起来了。我妹妹可曾把眼下的情势告诉你了？你又有何话说？"
面神道："幸会，狼之子！你妹妹已尽告我；纵使这些黝暗恶徒不是我族的仇敌，只要由得我做主，我们也定当全力相助，为你族人带回太平与好日子。"
民强闻言，脸涨得通红，向着那些武士挥了挥手，又向山谷上下指了一圈，说道：
"这些才是我族人，唯独这些；至于太平么，我们之中唯有那些上了年纪的人才见识过。不过也好；若你我两族合力，足以替银谷里那些被黝暗人所荼毒的软弱之人带回好日子，那就更好了。"
说罢他转向妹妹，目光炯炯地直视她的眼睛，看得她双颊泛红，又拉起她的手，看着手腕，说道：
"妹妹啊，我岂不见你腕上地神之环的印痕？自昨日以来，莫非有盟誓起了？"
她道："正是。此人与我已在判决环的祭坛前彼此订了盟誓。"

===Original===
Said Folk-might: "Thou wilt have thy will, and I may not amend it." Therewith he turned about to Face-of-god and said:
"Thou must look to it to keep this oath, whatever other one thou hast failed in."
Said Face-of-god somewhat wrathfully: "I shall keep it, whether thou biddest me to keep it or break it."
"That is well," said Folk-might, "and then for all that hath gone before thou mayest in a manner pay, if thou art dauntless before the foe."
"I look to be no blencher in the battle," said Face-of-god; "that is not the fashion of our kindred, whosoever may be before us. Yea, and even were it thy blade, O mighty warrior of the Wolf, I would do my best to meet it in manly fashion."
As he spake he half drew forth Dale-warden from his sheath, looking steadily into the eyes of Folk-might; and the Sun-beam looked upon him happily. But Folk-might laughed and said:
"Thy sword is good, and I deem that thine heart will not fail thee; but it is by my side and not in face of me that thou shalt redden the good blade: I see not the day when we twain shall hew at each other."

===Chinese===
民强道："你向来要怎样便怎样，我也无可挽回。"说罢他转向面神，说道：
"这一道誓，你可得用心守着，不管你从前失信过哪一道。"
面神带几分怒意地答道："无论你叫我守也好、叫我毁也好，我都会守住它。"
"这就好。"民强道，"如此一来，从前种种你也能算略作抵偿了，只要你临阵不惧。"
面神道："沙场之上我断不做畏缩之辈；这是我们一族的风骨，无论对手是谁。便是你这狼族的盖世武士的刀锋，我也要竭力以丈夫之姿相迎。"
他一面说，一面将谷卫（Dale-warden）从鞘中抽出一半，目不转睛地直视民强的眼睛；日光则欣然望着他。民强却大笑道：
"你这把剑是好剑，我也料你这颗心不会教你丢脸；只是这把好剑要饮血，须在我身侧，而非当着我的面：我瞧不见你我二人有互砍的那一天。"

===Original===
Then in a while he spake again:
"Thou must pardon us if our words are rough; for we have stood in rough places, where we had to speak both short and loud, whereas there was much to do. But now will we twain talk of matters that concern chieftains who are going on a hard adventure. And ye women, do ye dight the Hall for the evening feast, which shall be the feast of the troth-plight for you twain. This indeed we owe thee, O guest; for little shall be thine heritage which thou shalt have with my sister, over and above that thy sword winneth for thee."
But the Sun-beam said: "Hast thou any tonight?"
"Yea," he said; "Spear-god, how many was it?"
There came forward a tall man bearing an axe in his right hand, and carrying over his shoulder by his left hand a bundle of silver arm-rings just such as Gold-mane had seen on the felons who were slain by Wood-grey's house. The carle cast them on the ground and then knelt down and fell to telling them over; and then looked up and said: "Twelve yesterday in the wood where the battle was going on; and this morning seven by the tarn in the pinewood and six near this eastern edge of the wood: one score and five all told. But, Folk-might, they are coming nigh to Shadowy Vale."
"Sooth is that," said Folk-might; "but it shall be looked to. Come now apart with me, Face-of-god."

===Chinese===
过了一会儿，他又说道：
"我们说话粗鲁，你须见谅；因为我们所处的都是粗莽之地，在那里话不得不说得短、不得不说得响，因为要做的事太多了。但如今你我二人要谈一谈将赴艰险之功的首领们所当议的事了。你们这些妇人，去把大厅收拾出来备晚宴吧，这晚宴便是为你二人办的订盟之宴。客人，这一遭我们确是欠你的；因为你要从我妹妹那里得的遗产，除了你那把剑自己赢来的之外，本来不多。"
日光却问道："你今夜可有斩获？"
"有。"他道，"枪神（Spear-god），是多少来着？"
走上前来一名高大汉子，右手执一柄斧，左肩上扛着一捆银质臂环——正与金鬃当日在林灰（Wood-grey）屋前所见那些被诛恶徒身上的臂环一模一样。那汉子将臂环往地上一掷，跪下数了起来；数罢抬头道："昨日，在那交战正酣的林中，十二个；今晨，松林里那山潭边，七个；再就是这林子东缘附近，六个：共计二十五个。可是，民强，他们离幽谷越来越近了。"
"这话不假。"民强道，"但自有办法应付。面神，你随我到一边来。"

===Original===
So the others went their ways toward the Hall, while Folk-might led the Burgdaler to a sheltered nook under the sheer rocks, and there they sat down to talk, and Folk-might asked Gold-mane closely of the muster of the Dalesmen and the Shepherds and the Woodland Caries, and he was well pleased when Face-of-god told him of how many could march to a stricken field, and of their archery, and of their weapons and their goodness.
All this took some time in the telling, and now night was coming on apace, and Folk-might said:
"Now will it be time to go to the Hall; but keep in thy mind that these Dusky Men will overrun you unless ye deal with them betimes. These are of the kind that ye must cast fear into their hearts by falling on them; for if ye abide till they fall upon you, they are like the winter wolves that swarm on and on, how many soever ye slay. And this above all things shall help you, that we shall bring you whereas ye shall fall on them unawares and destroy them as boys do with a wasp's nest. Yet shall many a mother's son bite the dust.
"Is it not so that in four weeks' time is your spring-feast and market at Burgstead, and thereafter the great Folk-mote?"
"So it is," said Gold-mane.

===Chinese===
旁人便各自往大厅去了，民强却领着这位堡谷人走到绝壁之下的一处背风角落，二人坐下来谈；民强细问谷民、牧羊之民（the Shepherds）和林中汉子（the Woodland-Carles）的人马点校情形，面神告诉他能开赴战阵的有多少、弓弩如何、兵器如何、利钝如何，民强听了甚是欢喜。
这番话费了好些时候，此时夜色已急急上来，民强说道：
"也该去大厅了；可你须牢记，这些黝暗人若不趁早料理，定要犯境肆虐。他们这种人，非得你先下手为强、把恐惧打进他们心里不可；若等他们来犯，他们便如冬日的狼群，源源不断地涌来，任你杀多少都杀不尽。而最能助你们一臂之力的，是这一点：我们能领你们到一处地方，出其不意地掩杀他们，像孩子们端马蜂窝那样把他们剿灭。只是慈母之子，也必有许多要喋血黄沙。
"你们堡镇（Burgstead）的春节与集市，再过四周便要到了，其后便是民众大会，可不是么？"
"正是。"金鬃道。

===Original===
"Thither shall I come then," said Folk-might, "and give myself out for the slayer of Rusty and the ransacker of Harts-bane and Penny-thumb; and therefor shall I offer good blood-wite and theft-wite; and thy father shall take that; for he is a just man. Then shall I tell my tale. Yet it may be thou shalt see us before if battle betide. And now fair befall this new year; for soon shall the scabbards be empty and the white swords be dancing in the air, and spears and axes shall be the growth of this spring-tide."
And he leaped up from his seat and walked to and fro before Gold-mane, and now was it grown quite dark. Then Folk-might turned to Face-of-god and said:
"Come, guest, the windows of the Hall are yellow; let us to the feast. Tomorrow shalt thou get thee to the beginning of this work. I hope of thee that thou art a good sword; else have I done a folly and my sister a worse one. But now forget that, and feast."

===Chinese===
"到那时我便要去，"民强道，"自称是杀锈皮（Rusty）的凶手、又是劫夺害鹿（Harts-bane）与铜拇（Penny-thumb）之人；为此我要献上丰厚的血金（blood-wite）与盗金（theft-wite）；你父亲会收下的，因为他是个公正之人。那时我再细说原委。不过，若有战事，也许在那之前你便能见到我们。愿这新年行好运吧；因为不久刀鞘便要空了，雪白的刀剑要在空中飞舞，枪斧将是这一春时（spring-tide）的收成。"
他从座上一跃而起，在金鬃面前来回踱步，此时天色已全然黑了。民强这才转向面神，说道：
"来吧，客人，大厅的窗子已映出黄光；我们去赴宴吧。明日你便要着手这桩事业的开头了。我盼你是一把好剑；否则我便做了一桩蠢事，我妹妹做的蠢事更甚于此。可此刻把这话忘了，只管宴饮。"

===Original===
Gold-mane arose, not very well at ease, for the man seemed overbearing; yet how might he fall upon the Sun-beam's kindred, and the captain of these new brethren in arms? So he spake not. But Folk-might said to him:
"Yet I would not have thee forget that I was wroth with thee when I saw thee today; and had it not been for the coming battle I had drawn sword upon thee."
Then Face-of-god's wrath was stirred, and he said:
"There is yet time for that! but why art thou wroth with me? And I shall tell thee that there is little manliness in thy chiding. For how may I fight with thee, thou the brother of my plighted speech-friend and my captain in this battle?"
"Therein thou sayest sooth," said Folk-might; "but hard it was to see you two standing together; and thou canst not give the Bride to me as I give my sister to thee. For I have seen her, and I have seen her looking at thee; and I know that she will not have it so."
Then they went on together toward the Hall, and Face-of-god was silent and somewhat troubled; and as they drew near to the Hall, Folk-might spake again:
"Yet time may amend it; and if not, there is the battle, and maybe the end. Now be we merry!"

===Chinese===
金鬃起身，心中不甚自在，因为这汉子气焰逼人；然而他怎能向日光的族人、向这些新结的同袍之首领动手呢？于是他一言不发。民强却对他说：
"可有一样，我不愿叫你忘了我今日见你时动了怒；若不是大战在即，我早拔剑相向了。"
面神的怒气被激起，说道：
"那也还来得及！可你为何对我动怒？我且告诉你，你这般责难，实在没什么丈夫气概。我怎能与你相斗——你是我所订盟的言友之兄、又是这一战的统领？"
"这话你说得对。"民强道，"可要瞧见你二人并肩而立，实在难忍；你又不能像我把妹妹许你那样，把新娘许我。因为我见过她，也见过她望着你时的神情；我知道她是断不肯依的。"
于是二人一同往大厅走去，面神默然，颇有几分烦乱；走近大厅时，民强又说道：
"可时间也许能补救；若不然，还有战事，也许还有个了断。此刻且快活吧！"

===Original===
So they went into the Hall together, and there was the Sun-beam gloriously arrayed, as erst in the woodland bower, and Face-of-god sat on the dais beside her, and the uttermost sweetness of desire entered into his soul as he noted her eyes and her mouth, that were grown so kind to him, and her hand that strayed toward his.
The Hall was full of folk, and all those warriors were there with Wood-father and his sons, and Wood-mother, and Bow-may and many other women; and Gold-mane looked down the Hall and deemed that he had never seen such stalwarth bodies of men, or so bold and meet for battle: as for the women he had seen fairer in Burgdale, but these were fair of their own fashion, shapely and well-knit, and strong-armed and large-limbed, yet sweet-voiced and gentle withal. Nay, the very lads of fifteen winters or so, whereof a few were there, seemed bold and bright-eyed and keen of wit, and it seemed like that if the warriors fared afield these would be with them.

===Chinese===
于是二人一同走进大厅；只见日光盛装华服，一如当初林中幽阁之时。面神在高台上她身旁落座，留心看她那双眼睛和那张嘴——它们已变得待他如此温柔——又看见她的手有意无意地伸向自己手边，那一刻，渴慕之极的甘美便浸透了他的心。
大厅里人头攒动，那些武士悉数在座，还有林父（Wood-father）和他的儿子们、林母（Wood-mother）、弓娥以及许多别的妇人；金鬃放眼扫过整座大厅，心想自己从未见过这般魁梧的汉子，也从未见过这般胆壮、这般宜于上阵的人：至于女子，他在堡谷见过更美的，但这些妇人自有她们的美法，身段匀称、筋骨结实，臂壮肢大，却又嗓音甜美、性情温婉。便是那几个在场、十五岁上下的少年，也都一副胆大、目亮、机敏的模样，看那架势，武士若出征，他们也要相随而去。

===Original===
So wore the feast; and Folk-might as aforetime amongst the healths called on men to drink to the Jaws of the Wolf, and the Red Hand, and the Silver Arm, and the Golden Bushel, and the Ragged Sword. But now had Face-of-god no need to ask what these meant, since he knew that they were the names of the kindreds of the Wolf. They drank also to the troth-plight and to those twain, and shouted aloud over the health and clashed their weapons: and Gold-mane wondered what echo of that shout would reach to Burgstead.
Then sang men songs of old time, and amongst them Wood-wont stood with his fiddle amidst the Hall and Bow-may beside him, and they sang in turn to it sweetly and clearly; and this is some of what they sang:

===Chinese===
宴饮这般进行；民强又如前番那样，在轮番敬酒之间，叫众人同饮狼之颚（the Jaws of the Wolf）、赤手（the Red Hand）、银臂（the Silver Arm）、金斗（the Golden Bushel）、残锋剑（the Ragged Sword）——如今面神已不消问这些是什么意思了，因为他知道这些便是狼族诸支族的名字。众人又敬这订盟之事，敬这一对璧人，高声欢呼，将兵刃敲得铮铮作响：金鬃暗暗寻思，这一阵欢呼声能传到堡镇、激起怎样的回响。
众人又唱起古时的歌谣；其中林习（Wood-wont）抱着他的提琴立在厅中央，弓娥立在他身旁，二人轮流伴着琴声，婉转清亮地唱了起来；他们所唱的，有几句是这样的：

===Original===
Then the Sun-beam spake to Gold-mane softly, and told him how this song was made by a minstrel concerning a foray in the early days of their first abode in Shadowy Vale, and how in good sooth a maiden led the fray and was the captain of the warriors:
"Erst," she said, "this was counted as a wonder; but now we are so few that it is no wonder though the women will do whatsoever they may."
So they talked, and Gold-mane was very happy; but ere the good night cup was drunk, Folk-might spake to Face-of-god and said:
"It were well that ye rose betimes in the morning: but thou shalt not go back by the way thou camest. Wood-wise and another shall go with thee, and show thee a way across the necks and the heaths, which is rough enough as far as toil goes, but where thy life shall be safer; and thereby shalt thou hit the ghyll of the Weltering Water, and so come down safely into Burgdale. Now that we are friends and fellows, it is no hurt for thee to know the shortest way to Shadowy Vale. What thou shalt tell concerning us in Burgdale I leave the tale thereof to thee; yet belike thou wilt not tell everything till I come to Burgstead at the spring market-tide. Now must I presently to bed; for before daylight tomorrow must I be following the hunt along with two score good men of ours."
"What beast is afield then?" said Gold-mane.

===Chinese===
日光轻声对金鬃说话，告诉他这首歌是一位吟游诗人的手笔，所咏的是他们初居幽谷之时早年的一次劫掠；据说当真是一位少女领的头，做了那一队武士的首领：
"从前，"她道，"这被人当作一桩奇事；可如今我们人少到这步田地，妇人们但凡能做什么便去做什么，也就不算奇事了。"
二人这般闲话，金鬃心中甚是欢畅；然而在饮临睡那一杯酒之前，民强对面神说道：
"明日清早你们宜早起身：可你不要从来时那条路回去。林智（Wood-wise）和另一个人随你同去，领你走一条横穿山脊与荒原的路，论辛苦倒也够辛苦的，可性命要安稳得多；由此你便能寻到翻滚河（the Weltering Water）的那道涧，从而安然下到堡谷。如今你我既已是朋友和同伴，知道一条去幽谷的近路，于你并无妨害。你在堡谷如何说起我们，这说辞由你自己定夺；不过在春市之时我亲到堡镇之前，你大概不会把什么都抖搂出来。如今我得赶紧睡了；因为明日天亮之前，我必须带着咱们四十名好汉去追猎。"
"追的是什么猎物？"金鬃道。

===Original===
Said Folk-might: "The beasts that beset our lives, the Dusky Men. In these days we have learned how to find companies of them; and forsooth every week they draw nigher to this Dale; and some day they should happen upon us if we were not to look to it, and then would there be a murder great and grim; therefore we scour the heaths round about, and the skirts of the woodland, and we fall upon these felons in divers guises, so that they may not know us for the same men; whiles are we clad in homespun, as today, and seem like to field-working carles; whiles in scarlet and gold, like knights of the Westland; whiles in wolf-skins; whiles in white glittering gear, like the Wights of the Waste: and in all guises these felons, for all their fierce hearts, fear us, and flee from us, and we follow and slay them, and so minish their numbers somewhat against the great day of battle."

===Chinese===
民强道："是那些威胁我们性命的野兽——黝暗人。这些时日我们已摸到门道，能寻见他们的伙党；他们确乎每周都离这山谷更近一些；有朝一日我们要是不加提防，他们就会撞见我们，那时便要有一场惨绝的大屠杀；所以我们四出扫荡周围的荒原和林子边沿，以各种装扮掩杀这些恶徒，叫他们认不出我们是同一伙人；有时我们着土布粗衣，如今日这般，仿佛田里做工的庄稼汉；有时着绯衣金饰，仿佛西土（the Westland）的骑士；有时披狼皮；有时着一身白亮晃晃的装束，仿佛荒原之灵（the Wights of the Waste）：无论何种装扮，这些恶徒空有凶狠的心肠，却畏惧我们、逃避我们，我们则随后追杀，借以略略削减他们的人数，以待那决战之日。"

===Original===
"Tell me," said Gold-mane; "when we fall upon Silverdale shall their thralls, the old Dale-dwellers, fight for them or for us?"
Said Folk-might: "The Dusky Men will not dare to put weapons into the hands of their thralls. Nay, the thralls shall help us; for though they have but small stomach for the fight, yet joyfully when the fight is over shall they cut their masters' throats."
"How is it with these thralls?" said Gold-mane. "I have never seen a thrall."
"But I," said Folk-might, "have seen a many down in the Cities. And there were thralls who were the tyrants of thralls, and held the whip over them; and of the others there were some who were not very hardly entreated. But with these it is otherwise, and they all bear grievous pains daily; for the Dusky Men are as hogs in a garden of lilies. Whatsoever is fair there have they defiled and deflowered, and they wallow in our fair halls as swine strayed from the dunghill. No delight in life, no sweet days do they have for themselves, and they begrudge the delight of others therein. Therefore their thralls know no rest or solace; their reward of toil is many stripes, and the healing of their stripes grievous toil. To many have they appointed to dig and mine in the silver-yielding cliffs, and of all the tasks is that the sorest, and there do stripes abound the most. Such thralls art thou happy not to behold till thou hast set them free; as we shall do."

===Chinese===
金鬃道："告诉我，我们进攻银谷之时，他们的奴隶——那些旧日的谷中之民——会替他们作战，还是替我们作战？"
民强道："黝暗人不敢把兵器放到奴隶手里。不，那些奴隶会帮我们；因为他们虽然并无多少作战的胃口，可一旦战罢，割起主子的喉咙来却绝不含糊。"
"这些奴隶过的是什么日子？"金鬃道，"我从未见过奴隶。"
"可我，"民强道，"在平原诸城（the Cities of the Plain）那边见过许多。那里的奴隶中有的是欺压奴隶的小主子，手持鞭子辖管同伴；其余的人里，也有几个所受的待遇并不算太苛。但银谷这些却不然，他们人人每日都受着痛楚；因为黝暗人之于百合花圃，就像闯进园子的野猪。凡是那里美好的东西，他们都已玷污、都已蹂躏；他们在我们美好的厅堂里打滚，如同一群从粪堆里跑出来的猪。他们自己既不享受生之欢悦、甜美岁月，也嫉妒别人享受这些。所以他们的奴隶不得休息、不得慰藉；他们劳作的报酬是无数鞭笞，而医这些鞭伤的，又是繁重的苦役。他们叫许多奴隶去银砂石崖上挖凿开采，诸般苦差之中以这一桩最为酷烈，鞭子也以那里下得最密。这样的奴隶，你没见着、直到把他们解放之日才见着，是你的福气；我们将要解放他们。"

===Original===
"Tell me again," said Face-of-god; "Is there no mixed folk between these Dusky Men and the Dalesmen, since they have no women of their own, but lie with the women of the Dale? Moreover, do not the poor folk of the Dale beget and bear children, so that there are thralls born of thralls?"
"Wisely thou askest this," said Folk-might, "but thereof shall I tell thee, that when a Dusky Carle mingles with a woman of the Dale, the child which she beareth shall oftenest favour his race and not hers; or else shall it be witless, a fool natural. But as for the children of these poor thralls; yea, the masters cause them to breed if so their masterships will, and when the children are born, they keep them or slay them as they will, as they would with whelps or calves. To be short, year by year these vile wretches grow fiercer and more beastly, and their thralls more hapless and downtrodden; and now at last is come the time either to do or to die, as ye men of Burgdale shall speedily find out. But now must I go sleep if I am to be where I look to be at sunrise tomorrow."
Therewith he called for the sleeping-cup, and it was drunk, and all men fared to bed. But the Sun-beam took Gold-mane's hand ere they parted, and said:
"I shall arise betimes on the morrow; so I say not farewell tonight; yea, and after tomorrow it shall not be long ere we meet again."

===Chinese===
面神又道："再告诉我一桩，黝暗人和谷民之间，可有什么混血的人么？既然他们自己没有妇人，专与谷中的女子同床？再者，谷中那些可怜人不也生儿育女么，岂不是有奴隶生奴隶？"
"你问得在理。"民强道，"可这一层我告诉你：黝暗汉子与谷中女子交合，那女子所生的孩子，多半肖其父之族而不肖其母；不然便是痴傻，天生一个白痴。至于那些可怜奴隶所生的孩子；是啊，主子若有意便叫他们配种，孩子一生下来，主子或留或杀，全凭其意，犹如对待小狗小牛一般。长话短说，年复一年，这些恶徒愈凶残愈近兽性，他们的奴隶则愈无告、愈遭践踏；如今终于到了不做便死的关头，这一点你们堡谷的人不久便会明白。可此刻我非去睡不可了，否则明日日出之时，我便到不了我该到的地方。"
说罢他要了临睡的那一杯酒，众人饮罢，都去就寝。然而临别之际，日光握住金鬃的手，说道：
"明日清早我会早起的；所以今夜我不与你道别；是啊，过了明日，你我再相见之日起也不远了。"

===Original===
So Gold-mane lay down in that ancient hall, and it seemed to him ere he slept as if his own kindred were slipping away from him and he were becoming a child of the Wolf. "And yet," said he to himself, "I am become a man; for my Friend, now she no longer telleth me to do or forbear, and I tremble. Nay, rather she is fain to take the word from me; and this great warrior and ripe man, he talketh with me as if I were a chieftain meet for converse with chieftains. Even so it is and shall be."
And soon thereafter he fell asleep in the Hall in Shadowy Vale.

===Chinese===
于是金鬃在那古老的厅堂中躺下；将睡未睡之际，他仿佛觉得自己的族人正离他远去，而他自己正变成狼族的孩子。"然而，"他暗自想道，"我才真正长成了一个男子汉；因为我的"朋友"——她如今已不再吩咐我做或不做，叫我心中为之震颤。不，倒不如说，她倒乐得由我来拿主意；而这位盖世的武士、这位成熟的男人，他与我说话，竟仿佛我已是一位堪与首领们分庭抗礼的首领。事情正是如此，也将永远如此。"
不久，他便在幽谷这大厅中沉沉睡去。

## LIV Tidings of Dallach: A Folk-Mote in Silverdale / 五十四 达拉赫之音：银谷民众大会

===Original===
Three days thereafter came two swift runners from Rosedale with tidings of Dallach. In all wise had he thriven, and had slain many of the runaways, and had come happily to Rosedale: therein by the mere shaking of their swords had they all their will; for there were but a few of the Dusky Warriors in the Dale, since the more part had fared to the slaughter in Silverstead. Now therefore had Dallach been made Alderman of Rosedale; and the Burgdalers who had gone with him should abide the coming thither of the rest of the Burgdale Host, and meantime of their coming should uphold the new Alderman in Rosedale. Howbeit Dallach sent word that it was not to be doubted but that many of the Dusky Men had escaped to the woods, and should yet be the death of many a mother’s son, unless it were well looked to.

===Chinese===
三日之后，自玫瑰谷（Rosedale）来了两名腿脚飞快的信使，带来达拉赫（Dallach）的消息。他事事顺遂、斩获甚丰：杀了许多逃窜之徒，安然抵达玫瑰谷。在那里，他们仅凭挥剑一吓，便已遂了心意；因为谷中黝暗武士（the Dusky Warriors）所余无几，大半已奔赴银镇（Silverstead）就戮。于是达拉赫被推举为玫瑰谷之长老（the Alderman）；随他同去的堡谷人须留守彼处，等候堡谷大军余部的到来；在彼等到临之前，应当扶持这位新长老坐镇玫瑰谷。然而达拉赫传话道：毫无疑问，许多黝暗人（the Dusky Men）已逃入林莽，日后仍将是许多母亲之子的死因，除非严加防范。

===Original===
And now the more part of the Burgdale men and the Shepherds began to look toward home, albeit some amongst them had not been ill-pleased to abide there yet a while; for life was exceeding soft to them there, though they helped the poor folk gladly in their husbandry. For especially the women of the Dale, of whom many were very goodly, hankered after the fair-faced tall Burgdalers, and were as kind to them as might be. Forsooth not a few, both carles and queens, of the old thrall-folk prayed them of Burgdale to take them home thither, that they might see new things and forget their old torments once for all, yea, even in dreams. The Burgdalers would not gainsay them, and there was no one else to hinder; so that there went with the Burgdale men at their departure hard on five score of the Silverdale folk who were not of the kindreds.

===Chinese===
此时堡谷人与牧羊之民（the Shepherds）中的大半，都已归心似箭；纵然其中若干人，再多留些时日亦未尝不愿。因为彼处的日子极其安逸，虽然他们也很乐意帮扶那些可怜人务农。尤以谷中的妇人——其中颇有几位极其姣好——对那些面目俊朗、身躯挺拔的堡谷人心生倾慕，待他们千般殷勤。更有原属奴籍的旧人，无论男女，不少都恳求堡谷人将他们带回堡谷去，好见识一番新天地，将旧日的苦楚彻底忘却——哪怕在梦里也好。堡谷人不忍回绝，旁人也无阻拦者；于是堡谷人启程之日，随他们同去的银谷（Silverdale）人——凡非其诸氏族所属者——将近百名。

===Original===
And now was a great Folk-mote holden in Silverdale, whereto the Burgdale men and the Shepherds were bidden; and thereat the War-leader gave out the morrow of the morrow for the day of the departure of the Host. There also were the matters of Silverdale duly ordered: the Men of the Wolf would have had the Woodlanders dwell with them in the fair-builded stead, and take to them of the goodly stone houses there what they would; but this they naysaid, choosing rather to dwell in scattered houses, which they built for themselves at the utmost limit of the tillage.

Indeed, the most abode not even there a long while; for they loved the wood and its deeds. So they went forth into the wood, and cleared them space to dwell in, and builded them halls such as they loved, and fell to their old woodland crafts of charcoal-burning and hunting, wherein they throve well. And good for Silverdale was their abiding there, since they became a sure defence and stout outpost against all foemen. For the rest, wheresoever they dwelt, they were guest-cherishing and blithe, and were well beloved by all people; and they wedded with the other Houses of the Children of the Wolf.

===Chinese===
此时银谷召开了一场盛大的民众大会（the Folk-mote），堡谷人与牧羊之民皆受邀赴会；会上战帅（War-leader）宣告：大军启程之日定在后日。银谷的诸般事务也在会上一一议定：狼之男儿（Men of the Wolf）本欲请林中之民（the Woodlanders）与他们同住于那营建华美之城，任其随意选取其中精美的石屋而居；然而林中之民婉言谢绝，宁可散居于各处，自行在田亩耕作之极界筑屋而处。

说实在的，他们中大多数人连那里也没久住；因为他们钟爱的是林莽与林中营生。于是他们步入林莽，辟出栖身之地，筑起他们所钟爱的厅堂，重操烧炭与狩猎的旧业，很是兴旺。他们留驻于此，于银谷大有裨益，因为由此添了一道可靠的屏藩、一座抵御一切来敌的坚固前哨。至于其余，无论他们何处落脚，皆好客乐天，深受众人爱戴；他们并与狼之子弟（the Children of the Wolf）的其余诸氏通婚。

===Original===
As to the other matters whereof they took rede at this Folk-mote, they had mostly to do with the warding of the Dale, and the learning of the delivered thralls to handle weapons duly. For men deemed it most like that they would have to meet other men of the kindred of the Felons; which indeed fell out as the years wore.

Moreover, Folk-might (by the rede of Stone-face) sent messengers to the Plain and the Cities, unto men whom he knew there, doing them to wit of the tidings of Silverdale, and how that a peaceful and guest-loving people, having good store of wares, now dwelt therein, so that chapmen might have recourse thither.

===Chinese===
至于此次民众大会上所议的其他事项，多半关乎谷中的防御，以及教导那些获释的奴仆按规矩操练兵器。因为众人以为，日后多半要对付凶徒（the Felons）同族之人；后来岁月推移，果真应验。

此外，民强（Folk-might）依石面（Stone-face）之谋，遣使前往平原及诸城，访他素来相识之人，将银谷的消息告知他们：说如今有一支爱好和平、好客之民定居其间，家底殷实、货物充盈，商贾可前往通商。

===Original===
Lastly spake Folk-might and said:

“Guests and brothers-in-arms, we have been looking about our new house, which was our old one, and therein we find great store of wares which we need not, and which we can but use if ye use them. Of your kindness therefore we pray you to take of those things what ye can easily carry. And if ye say the way is long, as indeed it is, since ye are bent on going through the wood to Rosedale, and so on to Burgdale, yet shall we furnish you with beasts to bear your goods, and with such wains as may pass through the woodland ways.”

===Chinese===
末了，民强开口说道：

“诸位贵客、并肩作战的弟兄们，我们这新宅——本是旧宅——我们已经四处查看过了，其中所藏货物甚丰，我们自己用之不尽，唯有你们也来用，方能尽其用。因此恳请诸位看在情分上，能带走的尽管带去。倘若你们嫌路途遥远——确实也遥远，因为你们打定主意要穿过林莽前往玫瑰谷，再赶赴堡谷（Burgdale）——我们也会为你们备下驮货的牲口，以及那些能在林间小路上通行的车辆。”

===Original===
Then rose up Fox of Upton and said: “O Folk-might, and ye men of the Wolf, be it known unto you, that if we have done anything for your help in the winning of Silverdale, we have thus done that we might help ourselves also, so that we might live in peace henceforward, and that we might have your friendship and fellowship therewithal, so that here in Silverdale might wax a mighty folk who joined unto us should be strong enough to face the whole world. Such are the redes of wise men when they go a-warring. But we have no will to go back home again made rich with your wealth; this hath been far from our thought in this matter.”

And there went up a murmur from all the Burgdalers yea-saying his word.

===Chinese===
于是上屯之狐（Fox of Upton）起身说道：“民强啊，还有你们狼之男儿，请听我一言：倘若我们在夺取银谷一事上于你们有所助力，我们之所以如此，也是为自助之计，好使今后得以安居乐业，并与你们结为友盟伙伴；如此一来，银谷这里便能孕育出一支强族，与我们联手，便足以直面整个天下。智者出兵征伐，所谋便是如此。但我们无意揣着你们的财富衣锦还乡；此事我们从未作此想。”

全体堡谷人齐声附和，响起一片赞同之声。

===Original===
But Folk-might took up the word again and spake:

“Men of Burgdale and the Sheepcotes, what ye say is both manly and friendly; yet, since we look to see a road made plain through the woodland betwixt Burgdale and Silverdale, and that often ye shall face us in the feast-hall, and whiles stand beside us in the fray, we must needs pray you not to shame us by departing empty-handed; for how then may we look upon your faces again? Stone-face, my friend, thou art old and wise; therefore I bid thee to help us herein, and speak for us to thy kindred, that they naysay us not in this matter.”

===Chinese===
民强又接过话头，说道：

“堡谷与羊栏（the Sheepcotes）之民啊，你们这番话既见豪气，又见情谊；然而，我们盼望堡谷与银谷之间的林中之路能被开辟通畅，你们日后会常在宴厅与我们相聚，有时还会在战阵之中与我们并肩而立，因此我们不得不恳请诸位：莫要空手而去，使我们蒙羞；否则日后我们有何面目再见你们？石面，我的朋友，你年高德劭、识见深远；因此我请你在这件事上助我们一臂之力，替我们向你本族之人进言，莫让他们在这件事上回绝我们。”

===Original===
Then stood up Stone-face and said: “Forsooth, friends, Folk-might is in the right herein; for he may look for anger from the wights that come and go betwixt his kindred and the Gods, if they see us faring back giftless through the woods. Moreover, now that ye have seen Silverdale, ye may wot how rich a land it is of all good things, and able to bring forth enough and to spare. And now meseemeth the Gods love this Folk that shall dwell here; and they shall become a mighty Folk, and a part of our very selves. Therefore let us take the gifts of our friends, and thank them blithely. For surely, as saith Folk-might, henceforth the wood shall become a road betwixt us, and the thicket a halting-place for friends bearing goodwill in their hands.”

When he had spoken, men yeasaid his words and forbore the gifts no longer; and the Folk-mote sundered in all loving-kindness.

===Chinese===
于是石面起身说道：“诸位朋友，实不相瞒，这件事上民强说得在理；因为倘若他本族与诸神之间那些来来往往的神灵，看见我们空手穿过林莽而归，他便要招致他们的怒火了。再者，你们既已见识了银谷，便可知这是一片何等丰饶的土地，所有美好之物无不具备，出产足以生生有余。如今在我看来，诸神是眷爱将居于此地的这一族人的；他们必将壮大为一支强族，成为我们血肉的一部分。因此，让我们收下朋友的馈赠，欣然道谢吧。因为诚如民强所言：从此往后，林莽将化作我们之间的大道，灌丛将化作手捧善意的友人歇脚之处。”

他话音既落，众人皆附和其言，不再推辞馈赠；民众大会遂在一片友爱之情中散去。
